530: A speedy front-runner, best in dirt sprints. He won the JRA-local Cluster C. and Tokyo Hai, but was beaten in double figures in the Negishi S., and all 5 races until his retirement were double-figure defeats.
533: An early-maturing speedster who ran well around a mile on turf or dirt at 2 and 3. Winning in her 4th start, she then won 3 straight to reach open class, won the Flower C., and was 2nd in the NZT Yonsai S. and 3rd in the NHK Mile C.
534: She won the Elfin S. and was 3rd in the Tulip Sho, but 17th in the Oka Sho and 9th in the Oaks. Older, she was transformed, winning a tight Kyoto Himba S. as 8th choice for her first graded win, and later 2nd in the Aichi Hai, Mermaid S. and Lord Derby CT. As a dam she produced Meguro Kinen winner Cryptogram (12: King Kamehameha).
535: The 1969 Oaks winner. Her crop held stars like future Tenno Sho and Arima Kinen winner Tomei and Oka Sho winner Hide Kotobuki; overshadowed, she ran the race of her life in the Oaks. At 2 (old system) she won her debut and 2 more, a fine start, but slumped from year's end into early 3, missing the Oka Sho. She improved with a 3rd in the Flower C. and 2nd in the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu, and was 5th choice for the Oaks. In the straight she passed Tomei and won a duel with Light Palais by a nose for the Oaks title. Winless after, she retired after an open win at 4. Of her 10 foals, her 9th, Dyna Artemis, won the Himba Tokyo Times Hai (now Fuchu Himba S.), and her 5th, Dyna Turkin, produced Tenno Sho winner Let's Go Turkin; with her other daughters her family flourished.
527: She raced at around a mile on turf or dirt, so erratic she might finish in double figures then suddenly run well. After 5 JRA wins from 41, she moved at 7 to Southern Kanto, where she won the JRA-local Empress Hai.
532: She won 3 at 2, including the Fukushima 2yo S., and classic success was hoped for, but she was 12th in the Oka Sho. Skipping the Oaks, she targeted sprints of 1200m or less, finishing 3rd in the Ibis Summer Dash and winning the Keeneland C., her first graded race. Little followed but an open-special 2nd, and she retired in spring '09.
536: He won the Arlington C. but was crushed in the Satsuki Sho, then finished in double figures in the NHK Mile C. and Ibis Summer Dash. But as 10th choice in the Keisei Hai Autumn H., his stock fallen, he ran a stunning race for his second graded win. Troubles then kept him out nearly a year. In spring at 5 he won an open race, his first win in 18 months, but slumped again and retired, then went to stud in the Czech Republic.
517: 8th in the Oka Sho and 5th in a trial, she was 10th choice for the Oaks. Prone to drifting, she was taken widest by her jockey - and it worked: she swooped on favorite Shadai Kagura for a huge upset.
518: Right after winning his debut he was 2nd in the Shinzan Kinen and 3rd in the Kisaragi Sho, but injuries held him back. He won the Diamond S. at 6, but after a 7th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) a tendon injury forced retirement.
520: Steadily winning dirt allowance races, she reached open class, and at 5 ran down Limitless Bid and others in her first graded race, the Garnet S.
528: Won the Himba Tokyo Times Hai at 5 and was 4th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn).
531: All her wins, from her 3rd start on, came on dirt. In JRA graded races her best was 2nd in the Unicorn S., but she loved Kawasaki: Empress Hai wins at 4 and 5 and a 2nd in the Sparking Lady C.
537: With just one win at 2, she romped by 5 lengths in the Hanshin Sansai Himba S. At 3, as if venting her frustration at being barred from the classics as a foreign-bred, she won 5 straight graded races, then went to the Queen Elizabeth II Cup as heavy favorite. Oaks winner Chokai Carol fought back, and after a fiery duel in the straight Hishi Amazon won by a nose. In the Arima Kinen she was a fine 2nd to Triple Crown winner Narita Brian, a 3yo filly. Her long-awaited trip abroad came the next spring, but injury just before the race sent her home. Seeking redemption in the Japan Cup, she was best of the Japanese but beaten into 2nd by foreign raider Lando. She never won again, retiring after a 5th in the Arima Kinen at 5 to breed in America.
538: The 1982 Satsuki Sho winner, pouncing when heavy favorite Hagino Kamui O faded after leading. Heavy favorite himself for the Derby, he was 3rd behind Bamboo Atlas. In autumn, after a 2nd in the St. Lite Kinen and 8th in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, he was injured during the Kikuka Sho, finishing 13th, and retired.
539: Out of Mejiro Farm's treasure Mejiro Chaser, sister of Mejiro Ryan (87: Amber Shadai). Often 2nd, she suddenly bloomed in winter at 3: 3rd in the American JCC against older horses, she beat Derby winner Merry Nice in the Meguro Kinen and won the Nikkei Sho. But after a 9th in the Takarazuka Kinen she ran poorly and retired.
541: He won his dirt debut as 4th choice, then the Hokkaido 2yo Yushun as 7th choice with the fastest finish. He never won again and retired at 4, but Special Week, late in his stud career, often produced dirt stars like him, Roman Legend and Gold Blitz.
542: Winner of the 2010 Derby and Arc, famous for beating Japan's Nakayama Festa by a head in the Arc, crushing Japan's hopes. He won his debut at 2, then after a 2nd in the Dante S. (G2) went straight to the Derby. In just his 3rd start, not highly rated, he won by 7 lengths in 2:31.33, nearly a second under the record. Favorite for the King George, he was 5th, but went straight to the Arc and won a fierce duel with Nakayama Festa by a head. At 4 he was 2nd in the Eclipse S. and King George, then 12th in the Arc, and retired. At stud in Japan he sired Stayers S. winner Divine Force.
543: Apart from one early race, he ran only in 1200m and 1400m turf sprints, steadily winning, but went winless from autumn at 4 to winter at 6. Then at 7, with Mikio Matsunaga riding his final day as a jockey, he ran a shock race to win the Hankyu Hai, his first graded win - in his 47th start. Racing on at 8 in '07 he lacked sparkle; switched to jumps in November he was 5th, then crushed in flat open races and retired.
546: Racing in allowance company until spring at 5, he won the Epsom C. in June as 5th choice. At 6 he beat Admire Aura in the Kyoto Kimpai, then in a strong Osaka Hai was 2nd to Daiwa Scarlet, ahead of stars like Asakusa Kings and Meisho Samson, becoming a middle-distance star. He led all the way to win the Kinko Sho easily, then held off Meisho Samson and others in the Takarazuka Kinen to become a G1 winner. Big things were hoped for in autumn, but a suspensory injury and slow recovery sent him on a long break. He returned in autumn '09 without success and went to stud.
547: He won the Keisei Hai at 3, then was 8th in the Spring S. Only 15th choice for the Satsuki Sho, he ran a stunning 2nd, and a strong 4th in the Derby. But in autumn he was 9th in the All Comers, 14th in the Kikuka Sho and 15th in the Arima Kinen. Favorite for the first time in the '08 Shirafuji S., he was 13th. He tried jumping without success and retired after a 12th in the '09 American JCC.
548: By Sunday Silence out of a Danzig mare, and highly rated for natural talent, she drew attention before her debut. But after winning her debut she was erratic and missed the classics. In summer at 4 her sprinting talent bloomed: she won 4 straight from the 16-million class, her first graded race the Centaur S., then the Sprinters S. - Sunday Silence's first sprint G1, a sire said to be weak at sprints. The next year she won the Takamatsunomiya Kinen to top the sprint division, and retired after a 2nd trying to repeat in the Sprinters S. As a dam she produced sprint-mile runner Faridat (05: Kingmambo) and Daily Hai 2yo S. winner Gendarme.
549: She won her debut by 5 lengths and the Kobai Sho by 3, but was demoted to 13th for veering, and sore shins wrecked her classics. In autumn she won a 5-million race, then beat Scarlet Bouquet in the Rose S. for her first graded win. Favorite for the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, she brushed aside the spring stars to win easily, giving the late jockey Junichiro Oka his first and only G1. But right after the race an injury was found, and her career ended suddenly - so intense and fleeting, as if born for that one day. She died in '08, before that year's Oaks. As a dam she produced Fillies' Revue winner Yamakatsu Lily.
550: By unbeaten US Triple Crown winner Seattle Slew, she starred at middle distances. As a foreign-bred she missed the spring classics, but won the Flower C. and, as a 3yo filly, ran 4th in the Takarazuka Kinen. She won the Kokura Kinen and Rose S. and was 2nd choice for the Shuka Sho, but finished 11th, and was unplaced in the Japan Cup. Still, she won the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu at year's end, proving her ability.
553: She won the Daily Hai Sansai S. and Pegasus S. (then G3, 1700m turf), then as 2nd choice was 3rd to Sister Tosho in the Oka Sho and a close 4th in the Oaks - just short each time. As a late-developing Northern Taste filly, autumn growth was hoped for, but injury ended her career after the NZT Yonsai S. She produced no notable offspring.
554: Full sister of '82 Oaks winner Shadai Ivor. She spent most of her 2-4yo years in the 4-million class, only blooming at 5 to reach open class. She won the Azumakofuji Sho and Niigata Kinen, the latter a rout in record time. 4 of her 8 wins came at 5 - a late bloomer. As a dam she produced '96 Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (East) winner Center Rising (93: Hector Protector).
555: She won her first graded race, the Queen C., but was 12th in the Oka Sho. In the Oaks, as 13th choice, she ran a fine 2nd. Later she won only the Turquoise S. and kept losing, even against fillies, before retiring. As a dam she produced dirt mare graded star Trois Bonheur (10: Bago).
556: She won in her 2nd start and the Queen C. in her 4th, then beat Mejiro Dober in the Tulip Sho, an upset that made her a classic contender. 5th in the Oka Sho, she won the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (East) as favorite but was 5th again in the Oaks. 4th in the Shuka Sho in autumn, she later managed only an open-special 2nd. As a dam she produced TCK Jo-o Hai winner Rapid Orange (03: El Condor Pasa).
558: A top sprinter whose speed made for nimble front-running. His only graded win was the Lord Derby Challenge T., but in the Keeneland C., then a Sapporo open special, he set a course record for 1000m on turf - G1-class speed.
559: At 4 she led all the way to win the Kitakyushu Kinen over Daitaku Teio and Shori no Megami. She was 2nd in the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu and won the TV Aichi Open at 5, starring at middle distances, and retired at 6 to breed.
562: Debuting late, in February at 3, she spent spring winning lower races with no shot at the classics. In autumn she went straight from a break to the Queen Elizabeth II Cup. Her first G1, off a layoff, she was ignored at 17th choice of 18, but once the race began she left the other 17 hopefuls far behind with a powerful stride, winning alone by three and a half lengths - a stunning upset paying a 70,000-yen quinella. Called a fluke, she then crushed older colts in the Naruo Kinen, and was 2nd in the next Hanshin Daishoten, proving her ability.
563: She won her debut by 8 lengths, was 5th in the Icho Tokubetsu, then won a 4-million special by 6 and the TV Tokyo Sho Sansai Himba S., earning champion 2yo filly. At 3 she was narrowly 2nd to Nakami Julian in the Queen C., then won the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (West) with a sharp kick. The classics looked like a duel with Max Beauty, but Max Beauty won both. Older, she won the Tanabata Sho and Nakayama Kinen, but never a G1.
564: The first foal of Tenno Sho (Autumn)-winning mare Air Groove, by Sunday Silence - watched from before her debut. After winning her debut and the Erica Sho, she took on top colts in the Wakaba S., winning a duel by a nose with her dam's grit. In the classics she was a good 3rd in the Oka Sho, but sulked and was crushed in the Oaks. In the Shuka Sho she closed from behind but fell three-quarters of a length short, 2nd, as Still in Love won the Triple Crown - a humiliation. But in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup she beat Still in Love by a nose for her first G1. The next year, against colts at middle distances, she struggled, but won the Mermaid S., was 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), and won the Queen Elizabeth II Cup again - Yutaka Take's 4th straight win in that G1. Off form the next year, she was 3rd in her favorite race, then won her farewell, the Hanshin Himba S. She died suddenly in 2012, but her son Duramente (12: King Kamehameha) won two classics in 2015, carrying on one of Japan's finest families, founded by Dyna Carl.
565: After 3 wins from 4 at local Iwate, she moved to the JRA. Winning her JRA debut, the Crocus S., easily, she went into the fillies' classics, finishing 2nd to Vega in both the Oka Sho and Oaks - just short of a crown, but proving her ability. In autumn she won the Queen S., her first graded race, then was 10th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, ending her career on a high with the Turquoise S. at year's end.
566: With blazing speed she won her debut and the Hakodate Sansai S., becoming a classic contender. But from spring at 3, distance and her early-maturing blood held her back, and she never won again. Still, 3 graded wins prove her speed was real.
540: She won twice on dirt and tried the classics without success, then turned to dirt and bloomed, winning the Kanto Oaks and Sparking Lady C. From '04 she ran only 3 of 31 races in the JRA, winning JRA-local races like the Empress Hai, Hakusan Daishoten and Queen Sho.
544: From her second maiden she won 3 straight - the Hopeful S. and Flower C. - but was crushed in the Oka Sho and Oaks. After 11 months off she showed grit with a 2nd in the Fukushima Himba S., but then ran poorly and retired at the end of her 5yo year.
545: A familiar runner for trainer Hashiguchi. Early to shine, he won the Daily Hai 2yo S. and was 3rd in the NHK Mile C. at 3. A Tokyo specialist, he won the Fuji S., Tokyo Shimbun Hai and Epsom C., plus the Sekiya Kinen and Keisei Hai AH at left-handed Niigata - 6 graded wins. At 6, as 12th choice, he held on for 3rd behind Maurice in the Yasuda Kinen, and later placed as a double-figure outsider in the Milers C. at 7 and Keio Hai Spring C. at 8. He retired after the Yasuda Kinen at 8.
551: She won the Rose S. and was favorite for the Queen Elizabeth II Cup over Vega, but finished 9th. As a dam she produced '01 Chunichi Shimbun Hai winner Grand Pas de Deux (97: Fuji Kiseki) and '04 Tokai S. winner En Dehors (99: Brian's Time).
552: A late riser, she reached open class with 2 wins at the end of her 3yo year, then alternated good and bad runs until winning the Himba Tokyo Times Hai in autumn at 4. As a dam her best was 4-time winner Tsukiakari (94: Northern Taste).
560: The Anemone S. made her a classic contender, but she finished in double figures in both the Oka Sho and Oaks. In autumn she won the Negishi S. and then starred in dirt sprints, a close 2nd in the JRA-local Cluster C.
561: Strong or poor, she needed 7 starts to reach open class. At 3, with a 2nd in the Kobai Sho and 3rd in the Elfin S., she steadied and took off, winning the Oka Sho trial Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (West). 4th in the Oka Sho, she won the Oaks over hot favorite Agnes Flora and blueblood Daiichi Ruby. Little followed, and she retired after the Meguro Kinen in February at 4. As a dam, her best was 5-time winner A Shin Harimao (98: Tokai Teio).
557: A foreign-bred hope, he ran steadily at 1400-1800m on turf from 3 to 5. 3rd in his first graded try, the Nakayama Himba S. in spring at 4, he won the Keio Hai Autumn H. and Fuchu Himba S. in autumn. Never in a G1, he still ran well, 3rd in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and Nakayama Himba S.
570: Her style was to race forward and hang on, with first-class grit. Apart from her debut, all her wins were by a length or less - never a rout. When she got her pattern, her tenacity showed, as when she held on for 2nd to Admire Groove in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup at 4. She was 2nd in it again in '05 - proven quality. As a dam she produced Diolite Kinen winner Osumi Ichiban (09: Agnes Tachyon).
571: Running well in the mile division, he won his long-sought first graded race, the Tokyo Shimbun Hai, at 5. 3rd in the Hankyu Hai, he won the Takamatsunomiya Kinen as favorite, a G1 winner. After that he kept losing G1s as a fancied runner, and retired to stud after the '08 Mile Championship. Always producing a sharp finish, usually from the back, he was rarely beaten badly, but his style may explain the races he let slip. His first crop's Meiner Hoo won the NHK Mile C. with a brilliant finish from last, recalling his sire.
572: She improved fast as an older mare, winning two graded races for fillies and mares, the Nakayama Himba S. and Fuchu Himba S. Always fiery, she was so bad loading for the Tomoe Sho at 5 that she was banned for 3 months, then failed her gate retest and sadly had to retire.
573: She missed the classics, but as an older mare was 2nd in both the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu and Nakayama Himba S., then won the Mermaid S. as favorite in summer. After a 3rd in the Kitakyushu Kinen, she beat colts by 3 lengths in the Asahi Challenge C., and was 2nd in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, ahead of Air Groove. As a dam she produced '10 Oka Sho runner-up Oken Sakura (07: Bago) and '03 Hakodate 2yo S. winner Fille de Reve (01: Sunday Silence).
576: She debuted at local Kasamatsu and won 10 straight with overwhelming ability. Lucky to turn 3 just as JRA-local exchange began in earnest, she ran in the Oka Sho trial Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (West) to try the newly opened classics. 10 straight wins, but at local tracks - would that ability work on JRA turf? She stunned JRA fans with an astonishing finish to win and earn her Oka Sho spot. Ridden by Katsumi Ando, then a Kasamatsu jockey, the local filly won huge support: favorite for the Oka Sho, she was 4th on soft going. Favorite again for the Oaks, she hit the distance wall in 13th. The dream of a local classic winner in year one of exchange didn't come true. Fans still backed her, making her favorite a third time in the Rose S., but she was 3rd in a battle of finishes, then 13th as 6th choice in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup. No title, but in exchange's first year she pried open the trials' heavy door herself and ran in all three classics - a feat worth celebrating.
577: Strong from her debut, she won a fillies' maiden by 6 lengths, then the Kaede Sho easily and the Fantasy S. dominantly. As heavy 1.5 favorite in the Hanshin JF she came from the back of midfield to win, 2yo queen unbeaten in 4. But a fracture was found afterwards; after a long break she went straight to the Oaks, finishing 13th, then 4th in the Shuka Sho. Never regaining her 2yo shine, she retired in spring at 4.
578: With a sharp kick she won the Kobai Sho (5M) and Flower C., a graded win in her 5th start. In the Oka Sho a slow start left her 6th despite closing. In the Oaks she charged from last, diving to the rail at the final turn - a surprise tactic that worked perfectly - and her explosive finish won it, the one shining moment of her career. She never won again. She produced no notable offspring and died at 18 in summer, in foal to Daiwa Major.
579: Based in Hokkaido local racing, she was 3rd in the JRA-local Suzuran Sho, then moved to the JRA. Straight away she was a fine 2nd in the Hanshin JF, and the next spring won the Oka Sho as an outsider. She never won again and retired.
580: Winner of the Breeders' Cup Classic and Dubai World Cup, and Eclipse Horse of the Year in 2007 and 2008. Debuting late, in February at 3, he was 3rd in the Kentucky Derby, then won the Preakness S. for his first G1. In the Belmont he was 2nd to Rags to Riches, the first filly winner in 102 years. In autumn he won the Jockey Club Gold C. and romped in the Breeders' Cup Classic by four and a half lengths - 6 wins from 9 and Horse of the Year. At 4 he won the Dubai World Cup and 3 more G1s at home, including the Jockey Club Gold C. Going for another Breeders' Cup Classic, now on synthetic, he was 4th behind two lightly-regarded Europeans; his owner fumed, "He'll never run on plastic again." Still Horse of the Year again, he retired to stud. His first crop included Belmont S. winner Palace Malice, then Breeders' Cup Classic winner Vino Rosso and many G1 winners; 2nd on the 2016 North American sire list, he has been a top regular since.
581: He won his debut by 6 lengths, then the Fairy S. in a 2yo record that still stands. After a break he won the Crystal C. too, but lost the NZ Trophy by a head to Taiki Lion. Illness ruled out his goal, the NHK Mile C. He won the Akikaze S. in his 3rd race back, but never recovered, retiring after the Takamatsunomiya Kinen at 5.
583: He led all the way to win his debut at Niigata in July at 2 as 8th choice. After winning the Kaede Sho in his 4th start he reached open class, and was 5th to A Shin Apollon in the Keio Hai 2yo S. After a break he led at a perfect pace to win the Arlington C. 7th in the NZ Trophy and 11th in the NHK Mile C., he tried dirt in the Unicorn S. He lost his rider at the start but, with his speed, crossed the line first riderless. Trying more dirt against older horses, he was 16th in the Procyon S. Back on turf at a mile, he was 3rd as 15th choice in the Yasuda Kinen and won the New Year S. (OP) twice. He met crop-mate Garbo in over 10 races, and in 2012 they finished 1-2 in both the New Year S. and Tokyo Shimbun Hai.
586: Her close relatives include Broad Appeal, a 13-time winner including the Silk Road S. She won her first graded race, the Fillies' Revue, an Oka Sho trial, at 3, but was a non-factor 16th in both the Oka Sho and Oaks. Back after about six months, she kept finishing in double figures without any sign of improvement and left the turf. As a dam she produced Success Brocken, winner of the February S. and Tokyo Daishoten.
590: Winner of the 2010 Japanese Derby and 2012 Tenno Sho (Autumn), with just 6 wins from 25 - no glamorous path. Not highly rated in the classics, he was 3rd in the Satsuki Sho as 11th choice, and only 7th choice for the Derby, where an astonishing 32.7 finish won him the crown. A long slump followed, 2.5 years without a win. He bounced back in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) at 5: as 5th choice, he waited at the back in a fast race and slipped out perfectly to win. It was an imperial-attended race, and jockey M. Demuro's dismounting after his victory lap, removing his helmet and bowing deeply to the Emperor and Empress, became a moving talking point. He raced until the end of his 6yo year, retiring on Arima Kinen day 2013.
591: At 3, teamed with Mirco Demuro, she stole the Tulip Sho from the front, outfoxing favorite Osumi Cosmo. In the Oka Sho she tracked in 2nd and showed amazing grit, a fine 5th, 0.4 seconds back. She did little after and retired.
593: As 11th choice on debut she won with a stunning late charge. In spring at 3, ridden by Funabashi's jockey Sakai, she charged again to win the Flora S., her first graded title. Those were her only 2 wins.
594: After a 2nd in the Queen C., she ran steadily: 7th in the Oka Sho, 4th in the Oaks. In the Queen S., a Shuka Sho trial, as 3rd choice she won from the front. She was 12th in the Shuka Sho and won only once more, the BSN Open at 5, though she ran a close 4th in her last Queen Elizabeth II Cup. As a dam she produced Admire Main (03: Sunday Silence), '06 Aoba Sho and Mainichi Hai winner and Derby runner-up.
595: His brother Risk Me won the Grand Prix de Paris and starred at middle distances in France. Mainly on dirt, he raced tough until 7, consistent against stars: 2nd to Hokuto Vega in the Teio Sho and February S. (G2) at 6, 2nd to Kyoto City in the Winter S. at 5. He won 7 of 32; 6 of 26 on dirt and just 1 of 6 on turf - but that 1 was his only graded win, the Kabutoyama Kinen.
596: She won the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (East), but injury kept her out of the Oaks. In autumn she won the Rose S. but did nothing in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, 7th. She ran well in middle-distance graded races without winning, and retired at the end of her 4yo year. Silent Melody, by Symboli Kris S., won the March S.
567: At first a plain front-runner relying only on speed, she needed 6 starts to win. But once she learned to settle, she unleashed a fearsome kick, winning the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (East) and charging into 3rd in the Oaks. Outclassed against colts, she was astonishing when things fell right, winning the Tokyo Shimbun Hai with a furious finish. Retired in spring at 4, she produced Derby 4th Kyowa Splendor (01: Sunday Silence).
569: She won an Oka Sho shared at the top of the betting with Admire Groove, then in the Oaks, 2nd choice behind her rival, unleashed the field's fastest 33.5 finish for a double. In autumn, as heavy favorite, she was 5th in the Rose S., clouding her Triple Crown path. But in the last leg, the Shuka Sho, she won a tight duel with Admire Groove by three-quarters of a length - only the second fillies' Triple Crown winner, after Mejiro Ramonu. Going for a 4th crown in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, she ran superbly but lost to Admire Groove's grit by a nose. As an older mare she struggled, and the Shuka Sho was her last win. She died in August '07, leaving just one colt (by King Kamehameha), Judah. He debuted as favorite in March '10 but was 4th; he won twice after moving to local racing, then was crushed on returning to the JRA and retired.
574: She held off Air Deja Vu in the Queen C. for her first graded win, but was 6th as 2nd choice in the Oka Sho. Skipping the Oaks, she never won again, but was strong against fillies: 2nd in the Nakayama Himba S. and Queen S., 3rd in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup.
575: 2 wins from 13, but one was the graded Queen S. In the classics she ran well in every race: 3rd in the Oka Sho, 2nd in the Oaks, 3rd in the Shuka Sho. As a dam she produced American JCC winner Air Shady and Shuka Sho winner Air Messiah. Her half-brother is Air Shakur, 2000 Satsuki Sho and Kikuka Sho winner.
582: She won her debut as favorite, then the TV Tokyo Sho Sansai Himba S. and Queen C., 3 straight. But she fractured a leg during the Queen C., losing the spring. Back, she was 13th as 3rd choice in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, then won the Christmas S. Going for a third graded win in the next Tokyo Shimbun Hai, she fractured again on sloppy going. She won 2 open races later, but never regained her old burst. No notable offspring.
584: Debuting late, in April at 3, she won in her 2nd start and, after one race, won 4 straight. She was 3rd in the Niigata Kinen and 2nd in the Himba Tokyo Times Hai. Her talent then bloomed over long distances: 3rd to Kashima Wing in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai at 4, she won the Diamond S. early the next year, her first graded race. In the Nakayama Kinen she was 9th, her first finish outside the top five, and retired.
585: She won in her 3rd start, then ran the next week in the Kokura 2yo S. Last in the betting, over 100 to 1, she charged from the back in the straight to win her first graded race. She was crushed in the Fantasy S., but as 7th choice in the Hanshin JF she again swooped down the straight to win. From 3 she slumped badly, finishing in double figures in the classics and almost every race - an early bloomer who shone for a moment at 2.
588: She won the Tulip Sho and Rose S. and ran well in the classics: 2nd in the Oka Sho, 4th in the Oaks, 4th in the Shuka Sho, 5th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, then won the Aichi Hai against older mares. At 4 she was 4th in the Yasuda Kinen and 5th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup. In '08 she won the Kyoto Himba S., her first win in about a year but fractured a leg. While resting she developed colic, and thrashing in pain suffered a new open fracture. Beyond saving, she was put down, to much regret.
589: From the first crop of double classic winner Neo Universe, he won the 2009 Japanese Derby like his sire. Unbeaten in 4 from his debut, including the Yayoi Sho, he was clear Satsuki Sho favorite but finished 14th as the fast pace collapsed the leaders, him included - a shock. Seeking redemption in the Derby, he raced forward on heavy going and pulled away in the straight to win by 4 lengths. Leg trouble then kept him from racing properly; 2nd in the Sapporo Kinen at 4, he rested again, and after 2 more years off was 14th in the Sapporo Kinen, his last race. He went to stud from 2014.
592: With early speed typical of a Danzig x Mr. Prospector cross, and versatility, she came from behind to win a 5-million race as 8th choice, then led all the way to win the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun despite a loose horse pestering her. At 3 she aimed for the Oka Sho via the Fillies' Revue, but was last in both, then raced only on dirt. She won the Cluster C. in August at 4 and raced until August at 5.
568: A late-maturing sprinter, stuck in allowance races until spring at 5. From June she won twice and was 3rd in the Centaur S., and at 6 beat favorites like Scarlet Bouquet in the Swan S. for her first graded win.
587: Unbeaten in her first 4, including the Edelweiss Sho and Hokkaido 2yo Yushun, she then lost race after race as if a different horse. Moving to local Oi at 4 and America at 5, she won the Dahlia H., her first win in 3 years.
597: A highly rated foreign-bred by Mr. Prospector. 7th in the Fairy S. in her 2nd start, she won the Kobushi Sho and Elfin S. to reach open class. Two races later came the NZT Yonsai S. Against Yamanin Paradise, unbeaten in 3 in record times through the Hanshin Sansai Himba S., graded winner Go Go Nakayama and Kokuto Julian, she held firm and beat the charging Presto Symboli by a neck.
599: After winning her debut she was expected to star in the classics but couldn't win. In summer she won again, then 3 straight including the Sapphire S., and was 2nd to Sakura Candle by three-quarters of a length in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup. Back after 7 months in local summer racing, she won the Hakodate Kinen. In autumn she ran in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, newly open to older mares, but finished 12th and retired.
600: Her granddam Talented Girl denied Max Beauty the 1987 fillies' Triple Crown in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup. She debuted on dirt at Hanshin in June at 2, 4th as favorite, then won on turf next time and was 2nd in the Phoenix Sho. She stalled in 3 graded races, best 7th, but in the Falcon S., as 4th choice, she waited at the back and powered home to win. On the classic sprint route she was 11th in the NZ Trophy and 6th in the NHK Mile C., and a fracture of her right radius followed. Back in sprints she won the Shunrai S. (OP), and at 7 switched to jumping, winning graded races like the Niigata Jump S.
601: She won both the Oka Sho and Oaks trials, and in the Oaks ran a fine 2nd, three-quarters of a length behind Chokai Carol. A one-paced closer, she still reliably finished near the top whatever the race, winning many fans. Retiring in spring at 6, her first foal Sidewinder (98: Tony Bin) won 3 graded races including the Keihan Hai - a decent record as a dam.
602: Not top class, but blessed with a sharp kick, tough speed, a cool head in traffic and versatility. 5th in the Oka Sho and Oaks and 6th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, she was no classic star, but won 4 graded races, 3 against colts, 2 as an older mare - no ordinary filly. Her Kimpai (West) at 4 became a legend of handicapping: 9 horses abreast at the line. She won by three-quarters of a length with her grit, but 3rd was a dead heat by a nose, and every place down to 8th was decided by a nose - an unprecedented blanket finish.
604: Winning a semi-open race at 5, she went to the Epsom C. as 3rd choice and won, jockey Tsunoda's first graded win. In autumn she was 3rd in the Mile Championship. As a dam she produced Tabatha Tosho (93: Dancing Brave), dam of Sweep Tosho.
606: She won the Queen C. at 3, then was 3rd in the Oka Sho and 5th in the Oaks - real talent. Her form dipped from autumn at 3, but she won a semi-open race in spring '04 and the Oro C. open special that autumn. After a heavy loss in the Hanshin Himba S. at year's end she slumped and retired without results.
607: She won her debut and was never out of the top two in 1 win and three 2nds before the Oka Sho. Her speed was rare, especially early, and she often ended up leading on superior ability. Her temperament played a part: as when she was crushed from an inside draw in the Oka Sho, she often couldn't show her ability in big fields. She won the Centaur S. in a record 1:22.1 at the end of her 4yo year and retired. Passing her speed on, she produced 3 graded winners: '00 Yayoi Sho winner Fusaichi Zenon (97: Sunday Silence), '01 Spring S. and Kisaragi Sho winner Agnes Gold (98: Sunday Silence) and 7-time dirt graded winner Limitless Bid (99: Sunday Silence).
608: Crushed in the Yayoi Sho and NZ Trophy, he stalled at 3 despite high hopes. Maturing at 4, he won the Amethyst S. (semi-open) and Chukyo Kinen, but just as things took off, he went on a year-long break. Back, he ran well in open specials for a long career, his last race the Miyakooji S. (3rd) in May '09.
611: She won her debut and a 5-million race and aimed for the classics at 3, but lost momentum, 5th in both the Queen C. and Flora S., and missed the spring classics. She then won the JRA-local Kanto Oaks. After a summer break she was even better: 3rd in the Queen S., then 2nd to Fine Motion in both the Rose S. and Shuka Sho. Big things were hoped for, but after a 6th in the next Kyoto Himba S. she retired to breed.
613: He debuted in autumn at 2 over 1600m at Tokyo and won in a decent 1:35.4, then in the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. closed in 33.7 for a close 3rd behind Nakayama Festa and Break Run Out. As favorite in the Hiiragi Sho and Junior C. his late charges fell short, 3rd both times. Prone to lugging in, he ran with his tongue tied in the Crocus S., his 5th start, and won well. 4th to Unrivaled in the Spring S., he went to the NZ Trophy, prep for his spring goal, the NHK Mile C., and powered past Falcon S. winner Joe Cappuccino and the rest to win - a new sprint star. But in the NHK Mile C. he wobbled in the straight and hampered others; finishing 8th, he was demoted to 18th. As an older horse he was 4th, 2nd, 2nd and 9th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and 3rd, 7th, 6th and 8th in the Sprinters S. - just short of a G1 - but ran in the Hanshin C. 6 years running, winning it in '11 and '12, lighting up recent sprinting.
614: She won 1 of 3 on dirt with two 2nds, then in her first turf race, the Flower C., won by two and a half lengths as 8th choice. She ran above her odds in the spring classics: 3rd in the Oka Sho, 4th in the Oaks. After a summer break she won the Queen S. as favorite in autumn, but was injured. As a Real Shadai filly her best was still to come, but she had to retire. As a dam she produced Sing Like Talk (92: Northern Taste).
615: Rated a speedster, she was favorite for the Hanshin Sansai Himba S. but 3rd behind Biwa Heidi and Air Groove. She won the Queen C. at 3 and sought revenge in the Oka Sho, but lost to Fight Gulliver by half a length. She never won again.
617: His gleaming black coat recalled his sire Symboli Kris S. On debut in autumn at 2 at Tokyo, he swooped from the back to beat future Tenno Sho winner Hiruno d'Amour. In the Hopeful S. he pulled away from a good spot like a star, 2 for 2 and the East's top classic hope. In his first graded race, the Kyodo News Hai, he was a close 3rd to Hansode Band and Danon Chantilly, his first loss, but in the Spring S. he led alone and shut out 2yo champion Rose Kingdom and the rest. 3rd choice for the Satsuki Sho, he lacked a final kick and was 5th. Down to 6th choice for the Derby, he led at a slow pace but couldn't match the astonishing finishes, 13th. He later won the Mainichi Okan, among the best of his crop, but leg trouble led to retirement in autumn at 5.
624: Winning her debut by 9 lengths, she was hailed as a big foreign-bred star. After some stumbles she teamed with Yutaka Take to lead all the way in the Kyoto Yonsai Tokubetsu - her 2nd win, a graded one. Brushing aside colts in what was then the last big Derby trial was impressive, but she then stopped improving, her form slipping until her later years brought heavy defeats far from her star image. As a dam she produced Diamond S. winner Monte Kris S (05: Symboli Kris S.).
625: One-paced, needing the race to suit, she still won 2 local graded races at 5, the Niigata Daishoten and Niigata Kinen. As a broodmare, her 5th foal Heart's Cry (01: Sunday Silence) won the '05 Arima Kinen and '06 Dubai Sheema Classic.
626: Debuting late, she missed the fillies' classics, winning 3 of 11 at 3. She reached open class at 4 but couldn't win. Maturing at 5, she was 2nd in the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu, won the Kinko Sho for her first graded win, then the Fuchu Himba S. The year-end Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu drew four G1 winners: Hokuto Vega, Dance Partner, Wonder Perfume and Sakura Candle. Having walked the back roads, Samani Beppin was only 6th choice. But she unleashed a 34.7 finish, swooping widest of all to cut down the glamorous G1 winners together - surely a win worth a G1 to her and her connections.
598: She won her first 2 but was 10th in the Oka Sho. A romp in the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (East) kept her Oaks dream alive, but injury ended it. 4th in the Rose S. and 9th in the Shuka Sho, she retired to breed.
605: Beaten in every fillies' classic - 11th, 14th and 7th - she later raced around a mile, winning the Sekiya Kinen at 4, then the Nakayama Himba S. and Fukushima Himba S. for 3 graded wins.
609: She won in her 2nd start but was crushed in the TV Tokyo Sho Sansai Himba S. After winning a 4-million race in April and the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (East), she was 5th as 2nd choice in the Oaks. In autumn she won the Queen S. but was 7th as 2nd choice in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup. Older, she bloomed, beating colts in 3 graded races: the Kimpai (East), Argentina Kyowakoku Hai and American JCC.
610: Half-sister of Katsuragi Ace. Steady in allowance races, she won an open race at 5. After early struggles she was 2nd in the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu at 6, then won the Nakayama Himba S. for her first graded win. No notable offspring.
612: She won her debut by over 3 lengths, then the Niigata Sansai S. and Keisei Hai Sansai S. unbeaten. 3rd to Elpus in the TV Tokyo Sho Sansai Himba S., she was then found to have a fracture and lost a year. She ran well in graded races without winning, until the Tanabata Sho at 5, her first win in 2 years 8 months.
616: Tough, she raced until 6, winning 6 of 43, never badly beaten in any conditions, and at 5 won her first graded race, the Kokura Kinen. As a dam she produced '03 Nikkei Shinshun Hai winner Bamboo Juventus (99: Mayano Top Gun).
618: She beat Dance Partner by a nose in the Tulip Sho, then was 5th in the Oka Sho and 2nd in the Oaks. 13th in the Rose S., she was less fancied in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup but boldly raced forward for 5th.
619: Just 2 wins, her debut and the Daily Hai Sansai S., but out of the top five only in her last race, with a 3rd in the Shuka Sho. Her first foal Rose Bud (98: Sunday Silence) was 2nd in the Oaks, Shuka Sho and Queen Elizabeth II Cup, and Rosenkreuz (02: Sunday Silence) won 3 graded races including the Kinko Sho - a great broodmare like her dam Rosa Nay.
621: Her sire Buzen Dai O was a teaser stallion with just 2 foals that year. Yet in the Oaks, unexpected even by her connections, she won with apprentice Shigefumi Kumazawa, and later ran well in older graded races like the Kyoto Daishoten.
622: Tamamo Cross's sister. With Oaks winner Cosmo Dream injured and Oka Sho winner Arahoutoku off form, she won the Queen Elizabeth II Cup by a nose from Shiyono Roman, two weeks after her brother won the Tenno Sho (Autumn).
623: She beat the colts in the Shinzan Kinen and was 3rd in the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (West). 7th in the Oka Sho, she won the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (East) and was 4th in the Oaks. With a plain pedigree, she was never favorite in 25 starts - a long-shot fans' idol. Tough and injury-free, she livened up graded races, winning the Asahi Challenge C. at Chukyo at 4. As a dam she produced 8-time winner Fundori Ryoma (93: Mogami).
603: She won the Hanshin Sansai Himba S. as 9th choice, part of a 120,000-yen quinella, but did nothing after and retired after the next Queen Elizabeth II Cup. She produced Suehiro Commander (95: Commander in Chief), '99 Kokura Daishoten and Naruo Kinen winner.
620: In a chaotic year, Arahoutoku was 2nd in the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (West), then won the Oka Sho as 5th choice and the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (East). Oaks favorite, she was 7th behind Cosmo Dream, and retired after a 4th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup.
627: Won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai by a neck at 5, his first graded try, then ran poorly and retired.
628: She was crushed in the Oka Sho, 14th, and only 17th choice for the NHK Mile C. But from the back she unleashed a powerful finish, crushing colts like Laurel Guerreiro to win a G1. She was a fine 5th in the Oaks, but after a 14th in the Shuka Sho slumped for a long time. Switching to forward tactics at 5, she was 2nd in the Nakayama Himba S. and 4th in the Fukushima Himba S., but retired that August to breed.
629: He won a dirt maiden in his 4th start. In his first turf race, the Crocus Sho, heavy going blunted his speed and he was 7th, but on good-to-soft he led all the way in the Moegi Sho. In his first graded race, the Falcon S., he missed the break but charged to win, becoming a top turf sprint contender. Over 200m more in the NZ Trophy he was 3rd behind Sun Carlo's finish, and as 10th choice in the NHK Mile C. he tracked in 2nd and pulled 2 lengths clear. His 1:32.4 beat King Kamehameha's 2004 race record of 1:32.5 and gave his sire his first G1. Following Deep Sky, he tried the NHK Mile-Derby double, but blasted off in front on heavy going and collapsed, last of 18. After over a year off he returned to win the Silk Road S. and light up the sprint division.
631: In his second graded try, the Winter S. at the end of his 3yo year, he won a shock victory, brushing aside top runners like last year's champion dirt horse Narita Hayabusa. But after a 2nd in the Garnet S. he did little.
632: He won his turf debut over 1600m, then finished 4th or worse in his next 4. In his 6th start, his first on dirt, he won with the field's fastest 34.8 finish, then beat older horses in a special for 2 straight, and went to the Japan Dirt Derby for a third. Despite stepping up 800m from 1200m, he beat Silk Mobius and the rest. He did nothing in 2 autumn races, then rested for throat surgery. Back with a good 3rd in the Kawasaki Kinen and 2nd in the February S., he showed his class, but a fracture was found. It was mild, and he won the March S. as 7th choice. At 6, in the February S. as 7th choice, jockey Iwata's strong hands drove him to a second G1. He kept running well in JRA-local races, winning the Sakitama Hai, and went to stud in Korea.
633: She won her debut in June at 2 and the Cosmos Sho, raising classic hopes. Quiet for a few races, she won the Oka Sho decisively, breaking clear from up front. Hopes rose for the Oaks, but Silk Prima Donna just ran her down, denying her a double. Off form in autumn, she was 4th in the Shuka Sho, then leg trouble led to retirement. Her daughter Cheers Goddess (03: French Deputy) won in '05.
634: He won his debut over 1800m at Hanshin from up front. In the Kyoto 2yo S. two months later he tried the same but, perhaps short of experience, was caught in the straight, 4th. In the Kantake Sho at Nakayama he switched to waiting tactics and won by 2 lengths, showing versatility. In his first graded race, the Kisaragi Sho, he was no match for the speedy Reach the Crown, 4th, but he won the Wakaba S., outdueling Triumph March for a Satsuki Sho spot. He closed for a fair 5th behind Unrivaled, then won the Kyoto Shimbun Hai from up front, holding off Delphoi for his first graded win. He became a Derby contender - only for fractures of both forelegs to be found after the race. He ran well in graded races later, but repeated long breaks followed, and he retired without racing at 5.
635: Half-sister of Pilsudski, who beat top mare Air Groove by a neck in the 1997 Japan Cup. By great sire Danehill, she carried big hopes, and once she raced she far exceeded them, winning her first 5 including the Shuka Sho. She then won the Queen Elizabeth II Cup with ease, 6 straight, reigning as champion filly. But as an older mare her perfect running began to fade, with heavy defeats in big races against colts. She won 2 graded races, the Hanshin Himba S. and Sapporo Kinen, but without her old fire, and retired after the Mile Championship at the end of her 5yo year.
636: She shone only briefly, from her debut at 3 to the Oaks. Winning her first 2, she was 2nd in the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (West) and 3rd in the Oka Sho, then Oaks favorite. Living up to it, she surged in the straight and caught front-running Oka Sho winner Cheers Grace by a neck - a perfect race for the Oaks crown. But she seemed spent: 10th in the Shuka Sho, 5th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, then never placed again.
637: On debut at Chukyo in January at 3, he raced forward and pulled away to win by 9 lengths, then won the Viola Sho by three and a half lengths 3 weeks later, races of real scale. In the Spring S. against classic contenders, his inexperience showed: 4th as 3rd choice, his first loss. But in the NZ Trophy, despite a slow start, he pushed up to lead at the final turn and pulled away - a stunning performance. Fancied for the NHK Mile C., he raced forward at a fast pace and faded but still held 4th. A tendon injury in his right foreleg ended his Derby plans; after over 2 years off, he retired after a 3rd in the 2013 New Year S. (OP).
638: His sire Admire Boss, full brother of Derby winner Admire Vega, won the St. Lite Kinen; his dam Luca Dance was by 1991 classic star Dance Dance Dance - hardly fashionable. But he made a flashy debut at Kokura in February at 3, winning by 7 lengths. With Yutaka Take aboard in the Arlington C., he missed the break but closed for a close 4th, then in the Mainichi Hai swooped to beat Golden Ticket and the rest, with future Aoba Sho winner Apres Un Reve 3rd - proof his ability was real. As 2nd choice in the NHK Mile C. he was hampered in the straight, 8th, and in the Derby the sodden heavy going drained him to 17th of 18. A tendon injury then forced a long break, and he never regained his kick before retiring.
639: Out of French G1 winner Reve d'Oscar, sister of Hanshin JF runner-up Reve d'Amour - a blueblood whose name is French for "after a dream." 4th on debut at the end of his 2yo year, he won his next 2, then closed for 3rd behind Iron Look in the Mainichi Hai, his first graded race. Short of earnings, he couldn't get into the Satsuki Sho. Aiming for his big goal, the Derby, he won the Aoba Sho as favorite, bursting clear in the straight. In the Derby, on heavy going that hurt closers, he gradually came on for 5th. But in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, as 4th choice, he was 9th, and a tendon injury led to his retirement.
641: Unlike most of Amber Shadai's late bloomers, she showed full talent from the start and livened up the classics. She won the Fuyo S. at 2 to reach open class, then the Flower C. the next spring, beating future Oaks winner Chokai Carol.
642: Half-sister of Fuji Kiseki. Very consistent, but with a soft finish, she lost many close races and rose slowly. Her first graded title, the Mermaid S., came more than a year after her brother retired; already past her peak, it was her only graded win. As a dam she produced '02 Queen C. winner Shinin' Ruby (99: Sunday Silence).
643: After a string of 2nds she broke her maiden, then won the Flower C. In the Oka Sho she came from behind to beat Admire Kiss and others. Going for a double in the Oaks she was 6th behind Kawakami Princess. In autumn she ran 5th against colts in the St. Lite Kinen, but was 6th in the Shuka Sho and 10th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup. She kept trying G1s and even went to America without results, and seemed finished, but won the '08 Keisei Hai AH, her first win in 2 years 5 months, then her farewell, the '09 Nakayama Himba S., a fine send-off to breeding.
644: Out of the great mare Dyna Actress, she won her debut, then the Sapporo Sansai S. in her second start - Sunday Silence's first graded winner. She won the Fairy S. too and was the top classic contender, but at 3 her temper showed: she couldn't win the Queen C. or Tulip Sho, and was 3rd in the Oka Sho and 5th in the Oaks. Her temper kept her erratic, and she never won after 3. As a dam she produced 2-time mile graded winner Absolute (by Tanino Gimlet).
645: A fillies' classic star. She won in her 2nd start, then the Kobai Sho, and as favorite in her first graded race, the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (West). 9th in the Oka Sho, she showed her ability with a 3rd in the Oaks.
648: In the Sapphire S., moved to Chukyo, she led at her own pace and shut out good horses like Chokai Carol and Golden Jack. She later led all the way in the Aichi Hai over the same 2000m at Chukyo too - a perfect match for that course.
650: A front-runner suited to speed duels at middle distances. Leading in her first races, she was 2nd 3 times, unable to hold on before she matured. In summer she rose fast, leading all the way to win the Sapphire S., her first graded try. 4th choice for the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, she lost the lead to Kei Woman and finished 16th. She kept leading after that, but lacked the skill to vary her pace, and stalled.
652: 5 wins from 14. At 3 she beat strong older horses like Wako Chikako in the Asahi Challenge C. for her first graded win. As a broodmare she produced steady stars, led by '04 Yasuda Kinen winner Turu Maru Boy (98: Dance in the Dark), plus Turu Maru Fighter (99: Forty Niner) and Turu Maru Sister (01: Dance in the Dark). But she caught pneumonia in autumn '04 and died suddenly.
655: She won her debut by 7 lengths and 4 straight, including the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (West). Heavy Oka Sho favorite, she sank to 4th, then 6th in the Oaks. Back after 15 months, she was crushed in the Queen S., then a tendon injury ended her career.
656: In his 5th start he led all the way to win a JRA maiden exchange race over 1600m on dirt at local Funabashi. As 12th choice in the Mainichi Hai he raced forward and held on for 2nd behind Iron Look. In the Satsuki Sho the classic proved too much: he led and finished 11th. Seeking redemption in the Hyogo Championship, he showed grit to win a duel by a neck with sand king Suni - 2 for 2 on dirt. Back on turf for the Derby, he faded on the hill, 7th. He then ran well in dirt graded races, 3rd in the Japan Dirt Derby, and as 12th choice in the Japan Cup Dirt closed with the fastest finish for a surprising 3rd. But he couldn't race regularly after and retired.
640: 3 wins from 42. At 3 she was 2nd to Mejiro Ramonu by two and a half lengths in the Oaks, but did little after. In autumn at 4 she finally won a graded race, the Kabutoyama Kinen, then retired. She produced top jumper Gokai (93: Judge Angelucci).
646: She won her debut by 9 lengths, then a 4-million special and the Tulip Sho by 2, 3 straight. 4th choice for the Oka Sho, she broke clear from a good spot, but stablemate Arahoutoku's sharp finish beat her into 2nd. After a 5th in the Oaks a fracture was found, but she came back to win the Rose S. Favorite for the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, she lost by a nose to outsider Miyama Poppy's late run. G1 class, short only on luck.
647: Breaking her maiden in her 3rd start, she won once more before the Oaks (7th). After summer she won the Queen S. and met Max Beauty in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, 5th behind Talented Girl, and became a regular in fillies' graded races.
651: Unusually for a Sakura Yutaka O runner, she rose on dirt, 5 of her 8 wins coming there. Late on, on turf, she was 3rd in the Epsom C. and Tanabata Sho and 2nd in the Sekiya Kinen. In her farewell, the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu, she won as favorite, her first graded win. As a dam she produced '02 Nakayama Kimpai runner-up Tough Grace (96: Tony Bin).
653: She won her debut and the Kokura Sansai S., then went winless until 5. Switched to front-running, typical of "A Shin" horses, she won 2 allowance races in a row and led for 3rd in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup.
654: 6th in the Oka Sho and 11th in the Oaks, she bloomed in winter, winning the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu, Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu and Nakayama Himba S. in a row, then the Kyoto race again the next year - transformed against fillies.
630: From a top family, full sister of Scarlet Bouquet. She beat Arahoutoku in the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (West) and was Oka Sho favorite, but finished 12th, and injury cost her the classics. She later ran well at sprint-mile trips without winning.
649: Half-sister of Satsuki Sho winner Narita Taishin. After 3 allowance wins she was 5th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, won the Golden Whip T., and placed in the Hanshin and Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu. She later won the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu at 5.
657: 4th in his first graded race, the Unicorn S., he won the Japan Dirt Derby by 3 lengths. He was 12th in the Tokyo Daishoten, then won 3 dirt open specials, ran a strong 4th in the '06 Tokyo Daishoten, and in '07 was 4th in the February S. and 3rd in the Nambu Hai - a steady dirt force. From '08, apart from a 2nd in the Aldebaran S., he ran poorly, retiring to stud in January 2010.
658: 7 wins, two 2nds and nine 3rds from 32 - as the 3rds show, often good but rarely winning, needing 27 starts to leave the lower classes. She won her first graded race, the Mermaid S., at 6, but was 3rd again in the Queen S., and after the Sapporo Kinen, Queen Elizabeth II Cup and Aichi Hai retired.
659: With chronic leg trouble, not much was expected, but she was a fine 2nd to Nishino Flower in the Sapporo Sansai S. Raced carefully around her legs, she won 2 graded races and was an Oka Sho contender, but finished 9th and retired.
660: She won her heavy-ground debut by 4 lengths and beat colts by two and a half in the Niigata Sansai S., raising classic hopes. But always plagued by leg trouble, she was injured after a 6th in the Queen C. and never returned.
661: A tough runner who matched her rivals. In G1s, apart from a 14th in the Oka Sho, she was 3rd in the Hanshin JF, 2nd in the Oaks and 3rd in the Shuka Sho. In the Queen Elizabeth II Cup she crossed the line 2nd to Kawakami Princess but was promoted to the win when the winner was demoted - a title that clearly belonged to Kawakami Princess on the day. As an older mare she won the Sapporo Kinen, a graded win "on merit," surely late for her ability. Trying dirt in the Elm S. she was 11th, then 2nd by three-quarters of a length to front-running Daiwa Scarlet in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup. After a 9th in the Japan Cup she hurt her left hind and was scratched from her farewell Arima Kinen, retiring to breed. Her early foals did little, but her 7th was none other than Almond Eye (15: Lord Kanaloa), the greatest mare all fans know.
662: Behind in her preparation, she was a narrow 5th in the Oaks and 5th in the Shuka Sho, then fell back to the 10-million class. But at the end of her 4yo year she stepped up for the Chunichi Shimbun Hai and led all the way to win a graded race. As a dam she produced 2012 Summer Sprint champion Pas de Trois (07: Swept Overboard).
664: A strong front-runner, rare nowadays. Unable to lead in the Kisaragi Sho, he was 5th and missed the Satsuki Sho, but led to win the Mainichi Hai and Aoba Sho, then led happily in the Derby before Meisho Samson's kick beat him. In autumn, unable to lead, he was 7th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, but leading freely he held on for 3rd in the Kikuka Sho. He then lost his spark: 9th leading in the Arima Kinen, 10th sitting 2nd in the Kinko Sho, 17th in the Takarazuka Kinen. After a 5th in an open special in autumn '08 he retired, stood a season in Japan and was traded to South Africa.
665: An early-maturing speedster who won the Daily Hai Sansai S. but did little after. As a dam she produced '92 Niigata Kinen winner Tanino Bolero (88: Trebolo) and '95 Kobe Shimbun Hai winner Tanino Create (92: Creator).
666: 3rd in the Hanshin Sansai Himba S., she won the Shinzan Kinen and Tulip Sho, the top classic contender. But as Oka Sho favorite she was 11th, then fractured a leg training for the Oaks and retired with no chance at revenge.
667: 2nd on debut, he won his maiden and the Daily Hai 2yo S., his 1:33.3 a 2yo record for 1600m at Kyoto. He seemed headed for stardom, but was 7th in the Asahi Hai FS, 4th in the Satsuki Sho and 6th in the Derby, repelled by the G1 wall. As an older horse he had a long career at middle distances in lower classes.
668: Based at local Funabashi. Unbeaten in 4, all routs, he won the Tokyo Derby, then was 4th in the Japan Dirt Derby. After near misses he won the year-end Tokyo Daishoten, and made news with a trip to the Dubai World Cup (6th). He won the Tokyo Daishoten again at the end of '05 and the Kawasaki Kinen, but was 7th trying for a JRA G1 in the February S. He then beat strong JRA horses in the Kashiwa Kinen and Teio Sho. Going for a third Tokyo Daishoten at the end of '06 he was 5th, then 2nd in the '07 Kawasaki Kinen but 14th in the February S. Unable to break through in the JRA and hit by leg trouble, he ran once in '08 and 3 times in '09, retiring after a 10th in the Teio Sho to stud.
669: He won his debut over 2000m at Tokyo in autumn at 2, then a 5-million race in February at 3 despite the layoff, and outdueled future Tenno Sho winner Hiruno d'Amour in the Wakaba S. - 3 straight and classic-class ability. With a Satsuki Sho spot earned, his camp aimed only for the Derby, running in the Aoba Sho: he exploded in the straight to win by 4 lengths, with the fastest 33.8 finish and an excellent 2:24.3, emerging as the rival to Satsuki Sho winner Victoire Pisa. 2nd choice for the Derby, he missed the break and, in a sprint finish, could only reach 6th, ending his 4-race streak. He was 2nd to Buena Vista in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) at 3, and 3rd to Tosen Jordan in it the next year - top-class potential, but he just couldn't win. In the Shirafuji S. (OP), 1.4 favorite, he closed in 33.7 from hopelessly last at the final turn but fell short, 2nd. Trying the mile G1 Yasuda Kinen, he showed no will to run and was last. Then came an 18-month break; back, his slow starts worsened and he kept finishing in double figures. But in August 2015, in his first run at Sapporo, the Sapporo Nikkei OP, he led all the way to win - his first win in 5 years, since the Aoba Sho at 3, to fans' delight. His name comes from the nickname of Argentine soccer legend Diego Maradona.
672: From the first crop of big new sire King Kamehameha, he won his debut at Hakodate, his sire's first JRA winner. He swooped to win the Hakodate 2yo S., rising jockey Kosei Miura's first graded win. After a break he was 2nd in the Keio Hai 2yo S., then in the Asahi Hai FS closed faster than winner Seiun Wonder but fell a neck short. At 3 he was a good 3rd to Unrivaled in the Spring S., but then 7th in the Satsuki Sho, 5th in the NHK Mile C. and 11th in the Derby. In autumn, against older milers, he was 8th in both the Swan S. and Mile CS. At 4 he won the Kochi S. and Geshi S. (both OP), then the Keisei Hai AH for his second graded win in 3 years. After a 6th in the Sprinters S., as 11th choice in the Mile CS he used gate 1 to race forward and break clear. As others struggled on good-to-soft ground a G1 looked within reach, but soft-ground lover A Shin Apollon caught him, 2nd by a neck. He ran on for a long time in sprint-mile races, but died after a training injury in 2013.
676: A speedster who won the NZ Trophy. After indecisive runs he came back to win the '07 Kyoto Kimpai, and later, without graded wins, livened up the mile scene racing forward and holding on.
679: A US-bred by Smart Strike, sire of 2-time US Horse of the Year Curlin. He debuted at Niigata in summer and beat future graded runner Mikki Petra by 4 lengths. 4th in the Icho S. after a break, he was 2nd in the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. and 3rd in the Asahi Hai FS, then won the Kyodo News Hai at 3 with the fastest 33.6 finish for his first graded win. Skipping the Satsuki Sho for the NHK Mile C. at Tokyo, where his kick would count, he was favorite but, after 3 months off, did nothing, 9th, then a dismal 15th in the Derby. Like many Smart Strike runners he grew over summer, 2nd against older horses in the Asahi Challenge C., but trailed home 16th in the Kikuka Sho. A year later he was a good 5th in the Fuji S., but was injured in the race and retired.
680: She won in her 3rd start, then 3 straight to the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (West). 5th in the Oka Sho, she won the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (East), but was 9th as 3rd choice in the Oaks - a classic trial horse.
682: Southern-Hemisphere-bred in September, he debuted late, in March at 3, but won easily, then the Macau Jockey Club T., and in only his 3rd start the Radio Nikkei Sho, a graded winner. He won the St. Lite Kinen in autumn and went into the Kikuka Sho unbeaten in 4, but was 3rd behind Asakusa Kings and Alnasr Alwasheek, his first loss. In his first race against older horses, the Arima Kinen, he was 4th. In '08 he was 3rd in the Meguro Kinen, but in the Takarazuka Kinen dropped back in the straight to 12th, having ruptured a suspensory ligament in his left hind. He retired and went to stud in New Zealand from 2010.
683: He won his debut and was expected to go far, but couldn't win and missed the classics. Maturing from the end of his 3yo year, he won his first graded race, the American JCC, at 4 in '07, was 3rd in the Nikkei Sho, and won the All Comers in autumn. In G1s he was a dismal 11th and 15th in the Tenno Sho races, but in the '07 Arima Kinen beat stars like Meisho Samson, Daiwa Major, Vodka and Daiwa Scarlet for his long-sought G1. In '08 he won the Nikkei Sho, went to Hong Kong (6th in the QE2 Cup), lost the Sapporo Kinen to Tuscata Sorte's finish, then won the All Comers again. After the Japan Cup, he was 12th as 2nd choice trying to repeat in the Arima Kinen. In '09 he ran poorly in the Osaka Hai and Sapporo Kinen, but crushed Dream Journey and others in the All Comers for a third straight win. His farewell Arima Kinen brought nothing, but 8 of his 10 wins came on Nakayama turf - a true Nakayama specialist. At stud his first crop included Radio Nikkei Sho winner Win Marellei, his second Asahi Hai FS runner-up Arma Waioli and Fantasy S. winner Cool Hotarubi, and his third Lord Quest, who romped in the Niigata 2yo S. to become a 2016 classic contender.
685: At 3 he ran well, 2nd in the Radio Tampa Sho and 6th in the Kikuka Sho, but injury cost him over a year. Back at 5 he was steady in graded races, 2nd in the Niigata Kinen and 3rd in the Kyoto Daishoten, and won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai, but a tendon injury afterwards ended his career.
687: She won in her 2nd start, then beat colts in the Kigiku Sho. 2nd choice for the Hanshin JF, she spent energy getting a good spot from a wide draw and faded to 6th behind Buena Vista. She won the Fairy S. easily early the next year, but was then 5th in the Tulip Sho, 3rd in the Oka Sho and 3rd in the Oaks, beaten by Buena Vista every time. She never regained her spring shine and retired with a tendon injury.
688: She won her debut by 5 lengths and the Fantasy S. by 4, her race sense and sharp kick far beyond a 2yo's. Naturally a heavy favorite for the Hanshin JF, her kick misfired and she lost by a head and a nose - a shock. At 3 she won the Fillies' Revue, and in the Oka Sho, though Cesario was favorite, she raced forward and held off Cesario's finish to win a classic. Choosing the NHK Mile C. over the Oaks for her distance aptitude was a shrewd call: showing strong mile ability, she brushed aside the colts to win - a unique double. In autumn she was 2nd in the Rose S. and Shuka Sho, then 3rd in the Mile Championship, running well without winning. The next year, after a 2nd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, she was favorite for the new fillies' mile G1, the Victoria Mile, but finished 9th. While being rebuilt for revenge, she died of heart failure at pasture.
690: The second unbeaten Triple Crown winner ever, with 7 G1 wins, then equal most; leading sire 11 years running, with classic winners in all 13 crops - a modern legend who rewrote Japanese racing history. He won his debut with an astonishing 33.1 finish and romped by 5 lengths in the Wakakoma S. with a furious kick, quickly becoming the classic favorite. In the Yayoi Sho he had trouble catching the forward-running contenders, but caught Admire Japan by a neck at the line for his first graded win; his ability was now beyond doubt. In the Satsuki Sho he stumbled right after the start and lost a lot of ground, but powered home through the worst of situations, two and a half lengths clear at the line. From that moment the Derby was all but assured: he won it by 5 lengths in record-equaling time, then ran down front-running Admire Japan in the Kikuka Sho for an unbeaten Triple Crown. In his last race at 3, the Arima Kinen, he was 2nd to Heart's Cry, ending his unbeaten run, but at 4 he won the Hanshin Daishoten, Tenno Sho (Spring) and Takarazuka Kinen in a class of his own. In autumn he went straight to the Arc, but his kick misfired, a disappointing 3rd. Then a mistaken use of a banned substance came to light and he was disqualified from the Arc, casting a dark cloud. It was Deep Impact himself who blew it away, winning the Japan Cup and Arima Kinen with overwhelming power - truly "the best run," silencing all noise with ability. With 7 G1s, equal with Symboli Rudolf and T.M. Opera O for the JRA record, he retired at the end of 2006 to stud. His first crop gave Yasuda Kinen winner Real Impact and Oka Sho winner Marcellina. In 2012 his second crop's Deep Brillante won the Derby and Gentildonna the fillies' Triple Crown; after just 3 crops he was leading sire, and he reigned unchallenged, siring many G1 winners every year. Then in July 2019 he died young, at 17, news reported not only in Japan but abroad. In honor of his great achievements, the Yayoi Sho was renamed the "Hochi Hai Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen." His JRA wins as a sire passed his sire Sunday Silence's for No. 1 all-time, and his 71 JRA G1 wins (end of 2024) tie Sunday Silence's record. He sired 7 Japanese Derby winners, and his last crop even produced Irish-born Auguste Rodin, winner of the Derby and Irish Derby. His "impact" will carry on to the next generation and beyond.
670: Her first win came in her 3rd start and her first special in her 7th, but she improved with every race, and in her 8th start, the Queen C., she raced forward and overpowered Danon Velvet and the rest. Going for a second graded win in the Flower C., she was caught out by Viva Vodka's runaway and lost by a neck. Skipping the Oka Sho, she won the Flora S. from up front and challenged queen Buena Vista as Kanto's hope. But in the Oaks, against the Oka Sho stars she met for the first time - winner Buena Vista and runner-up Red Desire - she was well beaten in 5th.
671: Debuting fairly late, in February at 3, she ran tough until 6, winning 5 of 31, including 2 graded races, the Kabutoyama Kinen and Kokura Daishoten. All her wins came at local meetings; she loved tight, flat tracks but struggled on hills.
673: A speedy front-runner. She won her second maiden by 7 lengths and the Sapporo Sansai S. by 4, becoming a classic contender, and ran a good 4th in the Oka Sho. But leading boldly in the Oaks she was 13th, lost form and retired without another win.
674: At 2 he was 2nd in the Hyogo Junior Grand Prix and 3rd in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun on dirt, but then kept finishing unplaced, and switched to jumps in autumn at 4. It paid off: he won a maiden hurdle in his 2nd start, and the next year won the Nakayama Grand Jump, one of jumping's top races. He then won the Kokura Summer Jump and Nakayama Daishogai too. But from 6 his great rival Oju Chosan emerged, taking both the Nakayama Daishogai and Grand Jump two years running, leaving Up to Date 2nd or 3rd each time. He fought back, winning the Hanshin Jump S. twice, but fell at the last fence in the 2018 Nakayama Daishogai. He aimed to return after treatment but couldn't, and retired.
681: Debuting in Hokkaido local racing, he won once and moved to the JRA. He won the Kusunoki Sho, was 2nd in the Kyodo News Hai, and as 9th choice won the Mainichi Hai. After the Derby, injuries disrupted him, and at 6 he moved to local Kasamatsu, then Kanazawa the next year, without a win.
686: He won his debut at Kyoto in January at 3 as favorite, then made the top five twice in 5-million specials. In the Spring S., his first graded race, as 10th choice he raced forward and held on for 2nd, ahead of 2yo champion Rose Kingdom. He was a fair 7th in the Satsuki Sho, then won the Kyoto Shimbun Hai for his first graded win, and was a good 4th in the Derby, 2 lengths behind Eishin Flash in a sprint finish. He kept running well in turf graded races without winning.
689: At 3 he ran fairly well, 4th in the Aoba Sho, but from 4 alternated wins and losses in lower classes, reaching open class only in September at 5. In his first older-horse graded race, the Mainichi Okan, he unleashed a stunning kick, sweeping past Daiwa Major, A Shin Deputy and the rest in a record 1:44.2. He was 8th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 6th in the Japan Cup and 13th in the Arima Kinen, but his ability was real, until he broke a leg in training in winter '08 and was put down.
675: She had the speed of her dam, sprinter Tennessee Girl. After leading all the way in an allowance race as 12th choice, she went to the Aichi Hai and, slowing the pace to 64.5 for 1000m, led all the way as 7th choice.
677: Half-sister of That's the Plenty. Won the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (East) but was crushed in the Oaks.
678: Won his first 2 incl. the Niigata Sansai S., then raced in sprints, winning the Sekiya Kinen at 3.
684: Won the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (East) with rare race sense, but broke down fatally in the Oaks as 5th choice.
663: Nephew of Silence Suzuka. He won the Keisei Hai in his 4th start and was 3rd in the Mainichi Hai, but missed the Satsuki Sho and was crushed in the Aoba Sho and Derby. After a tendon injury, he broke a leg training in March '05 and was put down.
692: She won a soft Flora S. but was 13th in the Oaks. She kept running in graded races, making the top five only once (5th, Aichi Hai), but in the Tokai S., back on dirt, she caused an upset as 13th choice for her second graded title. She went on to win JRA-local races like the '08 Queen Sho and '09 TCK Jo-o Hai.
693: A foreign-bred by Giant's Causeway. He won in his 2nd start and was 2nd to Riddill in the Daily Hai 2yo S., then won the Keio Hai 2yo S. as 3rd choice. 2nd choice for the Asahi Hai FS, he led in the straight but was caught by Rose Kingdom, 2nd. At 3 he was a close 2nd to Victoire Pisa in the Yayoi Sho, but 11th in the Satsuki Sho and 9th in the NHK Mile C. Winless at 3, in autumn at 4 he won the Fuji S., his first win in about 2 years, then the G1 Mile Championship. He retired to stud at the end of his 5yo year.
694: A 1970s British speedster unbeaten in his first 15 starts. Unbeatable at a mile - 11 of 11, including the 2000 Guineas - he became a British hero. Overshadowed by crop-mate Mill Reef, the European Triple Crown winner, he beat him in the 2000 Guineas. He also won the 10-furlong Champion S. and 12-furlong King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S., and was Britain's Horse of the Year at 4. Timeform rated him 144 lbs, above Mill Reef, and 3rd in its "100 Greatest Racehorses" behind Sea-Bird and Secretariat. He retired at the end of his 4yo year with 17 wins from 18, his only loss a 2nd in the Benson & Hedges Gold C. At stud he sired Champion S. winner Vayrann, but his blood survives only faintly today.
695: By Agnes Tachyon out of Erimo Pixie. 7th on debut in August at 2, he won next time, then as favorite in the Daily Hai 2yo S. held off Danon Passion and caught A Shin Apollon at the line for his first graded win. A fracture at pasture needing a year to heal cost him the classics. Back in the mile division, he won the Swan S., but as 2nd choice in the Mile Championship couldn't quicken, 14th, and retired after an 11th in the Hanshin C.
697: She won her debut, then the Elfin S. after a duel with Wide Sapphire and Charm Pot. In her 3rd start, the Oka Sho, she led in the straight but was beaten by Buena Vista's powerful finish, 2nd. In the Oaks she seemed to have won, but Buena Vista caught her again by a nose. In the Rose S. Broad Street swooped, 2nd again. But in the Shuka Sho, as Buena Vista and Broad Street waited behind, she broke clear early to win her first G1. Riding that momentum she was 3rd in the Japan Cup, superb for a 3yo filly. The next year she won a G2 Dubai prep with a wide charge, but was 11th in the Dubai World Cup. She was 4th in the Victoria Mile and 4th again abroad in the BC Filly & Mare Turf, but after a 3rd in the Sapporo Kinen she bled from the nose before the Queen Elizabeth II Cup and retired to breed.
698: A great sire of Oceania, champion sire 6 times in Australia and once in New Zealand in the 1980s. His 45 G1 winners were then a world record, earning him the name "the Northern Dancer of the Southern Hemisphere." He raced in France, winning just 2 allowance races from 19. But his build and pedigree caught the eye of New Zealand breeder Sir Patrick Hogan, and he went to stud there. His first crop produced G1 winner Sovereign Red, and G1 winners followed almost every year, making him Oceania's great sire. His son Zabeel became nearly as great a sire, and his heirs flourished. In Japan, son Yamanin Vital was 2nd in the Naruo Kinen and later sired 2 G1 winners back in New Zealand. A rare carrier of the now uncommon Sir Gaylord line.
699: Debuting at local Oi, she won twice and moved to the JRA. Missing the classics, she found her way on dirt and became the first champion of the new dirt graded Negishi S. With few dirt sprint graded races then, wins were scarce.
701: 3rd on debut, she won with speedy front-running, then led all the way in the Hanshin Sansai Himba S., a leading classic contender. But a 9-month layoff cost her the spring classics. Back in autumn at 3, she held on for 2nd to Tico Tico Tac in the Shuka Sho. As an older mare she starred in fillies' and JRA-local races, winning 3 G3s: the Queen S., Mermaid S. and Zen-Nihon Thoroughbred C.
702: 3rd on debut, he then won by wide margins, 5 straight up to the Antares S., beating the runners-up by 21 lengths combined. After a 2-year break he won an open special in his 2nd race back, and ran well in dirt graded races, but after a 6th in the '08 Topaz S. a tendon injury ended his career.
703: 3rd in the Oka Sho and 2nd in the Oaks, she raced boldly forward as an older mare, a core figure in the fillies' division, winning the Queen S., Fuchu Himba S. and Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu. At 5 she suddenly tried the dirt G1 February S., 3rd on her first dirt run, then the Dubai World Cup, dirt's summit. It seemed reckless, but she ran a superb 2nd to Captain Steve. Back home after a break she won the Queen Elizabeth II Cup in autumn, a G1 - top class on turf or dirt. The next year she chose the Dubai World Cup as her farewell; 11th, but her record and reputation shine undimmed. As a broodmare her 3rd foal Dinashi sold for 600 million yen, a Japanese sale record, and To the Glory, To the World and Tosen Victory won graded races - a fine dam too.
704: Debuting in February at 3, too late for the Oka Sho, she won her debut, the Kunshiran Sho and Sweet Pea S., then the Oaks - an unbeaten Oaks winner. Her preparation disrupted, she went straight to the Shuka Sho in autumn and won again, an unbeaten double. In the Queen Elizabeth II Cup she crossed the line first with a brilliant kick but was demoted to 12th for veering - still a race that showed her power. When jockey Masaru Honda, her rider since debut, retired, Koshiro Take took over, but she was 10th in the Victoria Mile and 6th in the Takarazuka Kinen, then fractured a leg in late July. Retirement was rumored, but she returned after 11 months in the '08 Kinko Sho, a close 3rd against colts, and was 2nd in both the Fuchu Himba S. and Queen Elizabeth II Cup in autumn, hinting at a revival. But winless in '09, she retired to breed after the Queen Elizabeth II Cup.
705: 3rd in the Keisei Hai at 3, he struggled to win, scraping into the Kikuka Sho with his 3rd win, then did nothing (10th). At 4 he won a 16-million special and an open race, then the Nikkei Sho. After more near misses he was 2nd in the Stayers S. and won the American JCC. Erratic and struggling in G1s, he won the American JCC again in '10, proving his ability at middle-to-long distances.
706: Half-sister of Symboli Sword. Won the 2000 Crystal C. and was a fine 5th in the NHK Mile C.
707: His debut opponent was Deep Impact: he led at a slow pace and closed in 34.1, but Deep Impact ran him down with 33.1. He then won his maiden, romped in the Kusunoki Sho and won the Kisaragi Sho for his first graded win, but flopped in the Satsuki Sho and Derby. Moving to dirt for the Japan Dirt Derby and Derby Grand Prix brought nothing. Back on turf at 4 he came into his own, winning the Kinko Sho and running 2nd in the Tanabata Sho and Asahi Challenge C., a popular middle-distance force. In '07 he tried a mile, winning the Milers C. and running 2nd in the Yasuda Kinen. After a winless year, back on dirt he led all the way in the Kakitsubata Kinen. His form faded again and he retired in autumn '09, having thrilled fans by boldly taking the lead.
709: With colt-like power she won 13 of 49 in the JRA and local racing, including 8 JRA-local dirt graded races like the Kanto Oaks and Urawa Kinen. In the '02 JBC Classic she was a confident favorite despite being a mare, but was 2nd to monster Admire Don, missing her long-sought G1. She kept running steadily, and at 7 was a good 5th in the US G1 Santa Maria H. She retired to breed in America, covered by sires like Giant's Causeway and Medaglia d'Oro.
710: A speedy son of Taiki Shuttle with 2 mile graded wins. Talented from his debut, he came close at 3 with 2nds in the Spring S. and NHK Mile C. At 4 in 2010 he finally won the Tokyo Shimbun Hai. Leg trouble and throat surgery kept him out most of 5 and 6, but after the long break he won the Sekiya Kinen in summer at 7 - a 3.5-year gap between graded wins, 5th longest ever. Lightly raced, at 8 in 2014 he was 3rd in the Ocean S. as 9th choice and won the Keio Hai Spring C. as 10th choice, stunning everyone.
712: He won his debut at Sapporo in June at 2, then the Clover Sho, and as 3rd choice behind Danon Passion and Lordship won the Sapporo 2yo S. easily from up front. 4th to Rose Kingdom in the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S., his first loss, he rested. At 3 he ran in the Spring S., Satsuki Sho, Derby and Kikuka Sho, crushed in every classic, and later won the Capital S. (OP).
713: Poor on turf, he bloomed on dirt: 2nd in the JRA-local Hyogo Championship, then a clear Japan Dirt Derby win. Strong in orthodox forward races. After over a year off he was 15th on his return, kept finishing in double figures and retired in '08.
715: Two long injury breaks limited her to 3 wins from 5 at 3-4, and she only truly returned in January at 5. On turf she took off, winning the Sakuranbo Tokubetsu (10M) and Sapporo Nikkan Sports Hai (OP), then her first graded race, the CBC Sho.
