She won the Silk Road S. early the next year and was Takamatsunomiya Kinen favorite, but it wasn't that easy: 3rd. She then slumped and retired in January '07.
718: A middle-distance specialist: every win, debut included, came at 2000-2400m on turf. After winning the Kyoto Shimbun Hai and Chunichi Shimbun Hai, leg trouble forced a long break. He won the '08 Kyoto Daishoten, his first win in 2 years, but after more long breaks retired.
719: Based at local Oi. A runaway queen who lit up Southern Kanto sprints with her speed. Just 3 wins, but in the Tokyo Hai at 5 she rocketed to the lead and set her own pace. A Shin Lagrange drew level at the top of the straight, but after a fierce duel she pulled clear again near the line for her long-sought first JRA-local graded win. Her brilliant run earned her NAR champion sprinter that year.
720: Emerging at the end of his 3yo year, he was very consistent. He won the Naruo Kinen at the end of his 4yo year and the Nikkei Shinshun Hai at 5, then was 4th in the Hanshin Daishoten. Training for the Tenno Sho (Spring) he fractured a leg. Back, he was 6th in the Asahi Challenge C. and 5th in the Kyoto Daishoten, then won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. 3rd in the Stayers S. and 2nd in the Kyoto Kinen, he then had a tendon injury and over 18 months off. On his return in the '07 Naruo Kinen he broke down and had to be put down.
721: As 9th choice she won the Flower C. decisively from up front. Crushed in the NHK Mile C., she was 2nd in both the Radio Tampa Sho and Rose S., but last in the Shuka Sho. Then, remarkably, she went to the BC Filly & Mare Turf and stayed in America about 2 years, winning 2 of 13 and running 2nd in the G3 Arlington Matron H. Back home she ran poorly and retired at 6.
722: He won his debut, was 2nd in a 5-million race, then rested nearly a year. Back, he won right away and kept winning through the classes, taking the '06 Niigata Daishoten, his first graded race. Then he went 2 years without a win, until the '08 Osakajo S.; after a 9th in the Milers C., he won the Niigata Daishoten again with a powerful 31.9 final 600m. He retired in March 2010 to live as a riding horse.
724: By South Vigorous, sire of dirt stars like Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun winner Love Me Chan. Debuting late, in May at 3, he won 6 straight to draw attention. 3rd in his first graded race, the Procyon S., his first loss, he then lost 7 in a row, though always close, finally winning a graded race in the Musashino S. at 5. He later ran well in middle-distance dirt races.
691: Always in the top five, she rose through the classes, then won her first graded try, the Fukushima Himba S. at 4, from up front as 7th choice. A regular in fillies' graded races, her best after was 2nd in the Hakodate Kinen; she retired at the end of '07.
696: Debuting very late, in September at 4, he bloomed at once with 4 straight turf sprint wins. A last-to-first closer, he won the Silk Road S. at 6 and the Negishi S. on dirt that year. At 7 he won the Kakitsubata Kinen, Procyon S. and Sirius S., and at 8 the Garnet S. - a top sprinter on turf or dirt for years. In his farewell, his only race abroad, he was a fine 5th of 13 in the Dubai Golden Shaheen.
700: Stuck in the lower classes, she finally won her 3rd race in a September special. With no graded record and no late-improver form, 10th choice for the Shuka Sho was fair. But she broke clear from up front, beating the 2yo queen, Oka Sho winner and Oaks winner together - top of her crop. Called a fluke, she then ran 2nd twice in fillies' graded races and 3rd in the next Queen Elizabeth II Cup, silencing doubters.
711: Her dam Ski Paradise was a French star who won the Prix du Moulin. Air Thule won the Hanshin Himba S., was 3rd in a Singapore G3, then a fine 2nd in Europe's G1 Prix Maurice de Gheest. As a dam she excelled: first foal Ultima Thule won 2 graded races, and second foal Captain Thule the '08 Satsuki Sho.
714: At 2 she led to win the Fantasy S. by 3 lengths and was 5th in the Hanshin Sansai Himba S. At 4 she led all the way in the Centaur S. against Sprinters S. winner Daitaku Yamato. As a dam she produced A Shin Memphis (08: Medaglia d'Oro), who led all the way in the Aichi Hai as 7th choice.
716: A dogged front-runner. Hurt after debut, he rested 19 months, then won 2 JRA-local graded races.
723: Unlike his name, his legs weren't tough, and injuries often sidelined him. But he was talented, with 5 wins and five 2nds from a sharp late charge. At 4 he won the Kabutoyama Kinen in good time, closing from last in 33.0.
708: By NHK Mile-Derby double winner King Kamehameha out of queen Air Groove - one of the finest bluebloods in modern Japanese racing. He won his debut at the end of his 2yo year by 3 lengths as 1.5 favorite, already tipped for the classics. But in the Wakakoma S. (OP) he couldn't catch Hiruno d'Amour, who broke out on the inside, 2nd. In the Armeria Sho (5M) he was bumped badly but surged in the straight for his 2nd win. Boxed in on the inside in the Mainichi Hai, he was 5th, and lacking earnings missed the Satsuki Sho. He won the Principal S. by 4 lengths, then was 5th in the Derby. Hoof trouble followed, delaying his return to December's Naruo Kinen, which he won for his first graded title, then a good 6th behind Victoire Pisa in the Arima Kinen. At 4 he won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai by 2 lengths and went to the Dubai Sheema Classic, but fought his rider and was 6th. Back home, in the Kinko Sho he missed the break badly, yet with an astonishing kick that made others look still, won his 3rd graded race. 2nd choice for the Takarazuka Kinen, he couldn't close from behind, 5th. Leg trouble then sent him straight to the Arima Kinen; down to 11th choice, he closed fastest for 4th. At 5 he won the American JCC, was 3rd in the Nikkei Sho, then went to Hong Kong's QE2 Cup, racing forward and powering clear to win his long-sought first G1 abroad. Back home he developed a bad habit of missing the break badly in 4 straight G1s: 2nd in the Takarazuka Kinen, 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), Japan Cup and Arima Kinen. He went to stud that year, and his pedigree free of Sunday Silence blood made him instantly popular. His first crop gave Kikuka Sho winner Kiseki and Danburite; in 2019 Mer de Glace won the Australian G1 Caulfield C. on a 6-race streak; in 2022 Dolce More won the Asahi Hai FS; and Soul Rush won the 2024 Mile CS and 2025 Dubai Turf. He remains near the top of the sire rankings.
717: Good in allowance races but poor in graded ones, until the Hanshin Himba S. at the end of her 4yo year, where she swooped past Oaks winner Daiwa El Cielo and others. After a dip she was 2nd in the Queen S. the next summer, then won the Sapporo Kinen. In the Tenno Sho (Autumn) her astonishing finish caught Zenno Rob Roy and others - only the 3rd filly or mare to win the Tenno Sho, after Air Groove. Jockey Mikio Matsunaga bowed to the attending Emperor. She ran well against colts, 7th in the Japan Cup and 6th in the Arima Kinen, and retired at the end of 2005. As a dam she produced JBC Classic winner Awardee (10: Jungle Pocket), 5-time local dirt graded winner Amour Briller (11: Smart Strike) and UAE Derby winner Lani (13: Tapit).
725: Called the best Japanese runner by Dancing Brave, Europe's greatest horse of the '80s. Fast from the start, she won 3 of 4 at 2, including the Hanshin Sansai Himba S. At 3 she grew stronger, winning the Tulip Sho by 4 lengths and the Oka Sho as 1.3 favorite. Beaten by Lady Pastel's late charge in the Oaks, she gained revenge in the Shuka Sho for a fillies' double. Then older rivals proved tough: she won only the next year's Sapporo Kinen, losing big titles, and retired after a fracture in autumn at 5.
726: He moved from local Kawasaki to the JRA after 5 straight wins. After early struggles, once he won in the JRA he ran well on turf or dirt, rarely out of the top five. He won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai at the end of his 4yo year. The next year, 2nd in the March S., 4th in the Mainichi Okan and 5th in the Mile CS, he won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai again at year's end. Steady after, he won the '06 Swan S. and the '07 Hankyu Hai, was 3rd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and 2nd on dirt in the JBC Sprint. In '08 results faded and he retired.
727: She beat Lady Pastel, Rosebud and others in the Flora S., her first graded win and sire Dance in the Dark's first graded title. 5th in the Oaks, she suffered a tendon injury training for the Shuka Sho and retired.
728: His dam Home Sweet Home was a full sister of BC Distaff winner Pleasant Home. 6th on turf debut in November at 2, he then ran 4 times on dirt: 3 wins, incl. the Hyacinth S., and a 2nd. Back on turf for the classics he was 11th in the Spring S. and 12th in the Satsuki Sho, so returned to dirt. Favorite for the Hyogo Championship, he took the lead early and won by 5 lengths, then won the Unicorn S. comfortably - top 3yo dirt horse. After that he was 3rd in the Tokyo Daishoten, February S. and Teio Sho without winning, until the Akhal-Teke S. (OP), his first win in 2 years. After a nose 2nd to Grand City in the March S., he retired to stud.
729: Unbeaten in 3 including the Fairy S., she was a classic contender, but injury before the Oka Sho cost her the classics. Back in autumn, she beat older horses in the Andromeda S. The next year she won the Shunpu S. and Kokura Nikkei OP, but only won a 2nd graded race in the Centaur S. in autumn at 5. She ran in G1s without winning and left the turf after an 8th in the '04 Takamatsunomiya Kinen.
730: A Kansai horse, he debuted at Tokyo, 2nd to future graded winner Alyzeo. He won his maiden and was 4th to Victoire Pisa in the Radio Nikkei Hai. In the Wakakoma S. (OP) at 3, Air Groove's son Rulership was favored, but he slipped through on the inside to win with his experience. In the Wakaba S. (OP) he lost narrowly to Kanto hope Perusa, 2nd. In the Satsuki Sho, as 6th choice, he closed fastest for 2nd to Victoire Pisa. 3rd choice for the Derby, his kick misfired, 9th. He was 4th in the Sapporo Kinen and 7th in the Kikuka Sho, then as favorite in the Naruo Kinen was 2nd to Rulership. At 4 he kept racing in graded races, beaten by crop-mates Rulership in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai and To the Glory in the Kyoto Kinen. Then in the Osaka Hai he held off Derby winner Eishin Flash and NHK Mile C. winner Danon Chantilly - amazingly, his first graded win. In the Tenno Sho (Spring) he won a duel with Eishin Flash in the straight for his first G1. His camp went for the Arc: 2nd in the Prix Foy prep, he raised hopes, but got worked up in the paddock and was 10th. Back home he was 6th in the Arima Kinen. He raced on at 5 but had lost his old power, retiring to stud after a 3rd in the Sapporo Kinen.
731: At 3 she won the Uguisu Sho and Flower C., her first graded win. Like many Mejiro McQueen runners she grew stronger over longer trips, but perhaps lacking growth, her form collapsed in autumn and she never won again.
732: An unusual Australian-born son of Fuji Kiseki. He won his debut and an open special and was 3rd in the NHK Mile C., then always contended in sprint-mile graded races. He won the '08 Hakodate Sprint S. and that year was 2nd in both sprint G1s, the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and Sprinters S. After a dull '09, he won the Swan S. in autumn, then the Hanshin C. and the '10 Ocean S., and on that run the Takamatsunomiya Kinen - 4 straight. Consistent in sprints after, he won the Takamatsunomiya Kinen again the next year and retired to stud. His 2nd crop's Shuji won the Kokura 2yo S. and Hanshin C. His runners have long careers in sprints and on dirt, and in 2025 Shuji's foals debuted too.
733: In the JRA he did little beyond winning his first 2, incl. the Cosmos Sho, but a move to local Funabashi in autumn at 4 changed everything. He won his first race there by 4 lengths, emerging as queen of the sand. The next year she won the TCK Jo-o Hai, her first JRA-local graded race, and the Teio Sho, ruling Southern Kanto within a year of the move - a stunning rise.
735: He showed promise at 3, running in the St. Lite Kinen, but often couldn't win. Hampered by leg trouble, he came good in spring at 5, winning 3 straight from the 5-million class, then the Meguro Kinen by a neck from Eye Popper. He went to Australia with stablemate Delta Blues, running in 2 G1s and finishing 2nd to him in the Melbourne Cup. Back home he was 2nd to Deep Impact in the Arima Kinen. He never won a G1, but in '07 won the Meguro Kinen again and was 2nd in the Japan Cup and 3rd in the Takarazuka Kinen, always a presence on big days. After a 12th in the '08 Tenno Sho (Spring) he slumped, and after the '10 Diamond S. (11th) moved to Ireland. He won his first race there, retired with leg trouble and went to stud in the Czech Republic.
736: From summer at 3 he ran only at 2000m+. Often closing too late, with eight 2nds, he still won his first graded try, the Diamond S., from the 10-million class. Good in graded races after, he had a long injury break. Back in '07 he did little and retired after a 14th in the Tenno Sho (Spring).
737: Leading boldly like his dam, he won his debut and the Arlington C., but led and collapsed to 13th in the Satsuki Sho. Many more fades followed, until he led all the way in the '06 Kyoto Kimpai. Unable to race steadily after, he retired after a 17th in the '07 Mainichi Okan.
738: Rose Color's first foal. Won the Fillies' Revue, then missed the Oka Sho with a fever, and was 2nd by a neck in the Oaks, by 3/4 length in the Shuka Sho and by a nose in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup - always just short. As a dam she produced Japan Cup winner Rose Kingdom, passing on the "Rose family" blood.
739: Raced mainly in dirt sprints, she won her first turf race, the Ibis Summer Dash, after reaching open class. She then won the Centaur S. to be Summer Sprint Series queen, closed well for 2nd on heavy ground in the Sprinters S. and won the Keihan Hai - a top sprinter in no time. But in '08, the year of "G1 at last," she died of heart failure, far too soon.
741: Unbeaten in 3, incl. the Nanohana Sho and Tulip Sho, she was 6th in the Oka Sho and 4th in the Oaks, unable to break the wall of Cesario and co. After a 7th in the Shuka Sho, injury kept her out. Back in October '06, leg trouble struck again and she retired.
742: With a furious late charge he won the Kyoto Kimpai at 4, then the Tokyo Shimbun Hai as heavy favorite with an astonishing 32.9, suddenly a star of the mile division. But he was 9th in the Milers C. and 15th in the Yasuda Kinen, and flopped in the Mainichi Okan and Tenno Sho (Autumn). Sharpened by racing, his kick returned in the Mile Championship, winning his first G1 in good time, then the Hong Kong Mile. After that his form dipped, and he retired after a 6th in the '07 Milers C. He went to stud at famous Walmac Farm in the US; his son Dabirsim won French G1s, the Prix Morny and Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere.
743: As a daughter of great mare Rosita, much was hoped for, but she won only 2 of 10, best a 2nd in the Elfin S. As a dam she produced Regular Member (97: Commander in Chief), winner of 3 JRA-local G1s.
744: At 3 he ran in the Kyodo News Hai and Arlington C. without success and was long stuck in the lower classes. At 6 he finally settled in open class and won the Negishi S., then was 3rd in the February S. - a self-made dirt horse. His form faded in autumn and he moved to local Oi.
745: 3rd in the Spring S. to make the Satsuki Sho, he was 10th, and after a 13th in the St. Lite Kinen missed the Kikuka Sho. He improved steadily but wins were scarce, until the Epsom C. at 4, where he beat Grass Bomber and others from a good position. He then won the Niigata Kinen, a horse to watch for the autumn G1s. But he hurt a ligament, and back after a year in autumn '07 had lost his form, retiring after an 8th in the '09 Nakayama Kinen.
746: He won the Spring S. with a sharp finish, the classics' dark horse, but was crushed in the Satsuki Sho (8th) and Derby (14th). After near misses, he won the '07 New Year S., his first win since the Spring S., and was 3rd in the Nakayama Kinen. Hopes rose, but slow starts ruined him, then a tendon injury forced a long break. He struggled after his return, but at the end of his 8yo year won the Fukushima Kinen as 12th choice with an eye-opening charge from last.
747: 15th on debut, he won his 3rd start and 3 straight more. After a long break he reached open class at the end of his 5yo year, won the Shirafuji S. at 6, then the Niigata Kinen and Epsom C. In autumn he lost the All Comers to Matsurida Gogh but fought Dream Journey hard for 2nd. After a 5th in the Tenno Sho a fracture was found. Back after a year, he beat Dream Journey in the All Comers - clearly talented - but more long breaks followed and he retired without the results he deserved.
748: Half-sister of 10-time winner Shinko Lovely, a Mile CS winner. By Sunday Silence, she was a classic hope, but was 4th in the Oka Sho and 7th in the Oaks. Switched to miles and sprints when older, she slowly emerged, winning the Kyoto Himba S. at 5. As a dam, her 3rd foal Codino (10: King Kamehameha) was 2nd in the Asahi Hai FS and 3rd in the Satsuki Sho, and his full sister Cecchino 2nd in the Oaks.
749: He won his debut but was crushed in the Kyodo News Hai in only his 2nd start. Building up in his own class, he reached open class only in autumn at 5. He kept trying graded races, 3rd in the American JCC at 7, then slumped. But at 8 in '05, after 3rds in the New Year S., American JCC and Shirafuji S., his honed kick finally exploded in the Nikkei Sho - his first win in 2.5 years and first graded win.
750: Based at local Funabashi. After winning the Kanto Oaks and more, she raced in the JRA's Shion S. but was 14th. Dull from 4, she retired and became a broodmare from '08.
751: With light early speed and a quick kick, she starred in middle-distance fillies' races. Master jockey Yukio Okabe often rode her early on, but later she had no regular rider - 11 jockeys in 23 races. Oddly unlucky with G1s, she first tried one in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup at 4 and, ridden by Peslier, was 2nd to Fine Motion. With 3 fillies' graded wins that year, she was named JRA Best Older Filly or Mare.
752: Debuting late, in January at 3, and slow to win, she missed the Oka Sho, but 2nd in the Flora S. earned an Oaks spot. In the Oaks she swept past T.M. Ocean, the crop's empress, to win. Just as strong when older, she won the Nakayama Himba S. and Fuchu Himba S., and never once finished out of the top five, thrilling fans with her consistency.
753: Talented enough to be favored over Mihono Bourbon in the Spring S. at 3. With then-rookie Shinji Fujita, their first ride together, he won the Radio Tampa Hai 3yo S. with a powerful charge, a first graded win for both.
755: 2nd in his first 3, he then won 3 straight, including the Kisaragi Sho. Dull after a big Satsuki Sho loss, he regained form at 5, and after a long break won the Kokura Daishoten at 7. Age caught up and he retired in '08.
757: In the Arlington C. he lived up to his name, leading from the start at his own pace to win by 4 lengths. But after a long break and more, he never won again, racing until 5.
758: He won his first 2, incl. the Kokura 3yo S., but a fractured right radius cost him 15 months. After 5 more starts, periostitis forced another long break - 2 wins from 7 up to 4. But back at 5, he won 4 straight, then the G2 Keio Hai Spring C. over Takara Steel - 5 in a row. He kept starring in graded races, winning the CBC Sho at the end of his 7yo year - a moving long career.
759: Injured in summer at 3, he rose late, getting a 3rd win only at 5. Then his talent bloomed: after a 3rd, he won 4 straight, including the Sekiya Kinen. He didn't win again but was 2nd in the Mainichi Okan.
760: He won his 1200m dirt debut, then a 5-million race, the Violet S. and Hyacinth S. - all on dirt. In May he won the JRA-local Hyogo Championship for 5 straight, then the Unicorn S., but was 3rd to Kane Hekili, ending his streak. He won the '06 Nagoya Daishoten, but was 5th in the Japan Dirt Derby, 3rd in the Derby Grand Prix, 4th in the Kashiwa Kinen, 6th in the Japan Cup Dirt and 3rd in the Kawasaki Kinen - always just short at the top level.
734: From the widest draw in the Fairy S., she swooped from 2nd-last to win, and won the Canna S. (OP) at the same Nakayama 1200m. From 3, bar a 3rd in the Falcon S., she kept finishing in double figures - an early bloomer - and went to stud after a race at 5.
740: Romping in the Unicorn S. made him a core dirt horse, but he was 4th in the Japan Dirt Derby and 6th in the Derby Grand Prix, then moved to Masayuki Kawashima's Funabashi stable. Still unable to win (3rd Diolite Kinen, 6th Kashiwa Kinen), he retired.
756: Debuting in June at 3, he led doggedly to 3 wins and two 2nds by autumn, livened up the Kikuka Sho from the front (6th), then won the Aichi Hai and Kimpai (West). He went to stud for his Takeshiba O blood.
764: A sprinter unbeatable at summer local meetings, winning the straight-course Ibis Summer Dash and the Hakodate Sprint S. In G1s his best was a neck 2nd to Trot Star in the Sprinters S. at 5 - just short.
766: He won the Shinzan Kinen and Violet S., but was 9th in the Satsuki Sho and never won again.
771: With strong early speed and a sure finish, she won 3 straight up to the Flower C., becoming the classics' leading lady. Oka Sho favorite, she couldn't use her speed and failed to catch Rhein Kraft, 2nd. With Rhein Kraft heading to the NHK Mile C., she was a heavy Oaks favorite, but a slow start forced her to race behind. The early pace was slow, favoring the leaders, and she was still 12th at the final turn. Just when it seemed hopeless, her kick exploded - a staggering 33.3 final 600m - catching Air Messiah by a neck. Undisputed queen of her crop, she went to America for the American Oaks, where Dance in the Mood had been 2nd the year before. Racing in a good spot, she took the lead at the final turn and won by 4 lengths, conquering "the world" with ease - the first US G1 win by a Japanese horse. But leg trouble made it her last race. That this feat came not from a foreign-bred or a Sunday Silence runner, but from his Japan-sired grandchild, was the best possible news for Japanese racing. As a dam she produced 3 G1 winners - Epiphaneia (10: Symboli Kris S), Leontes (13: King Kamehameha) and Saturnalia (16: Lord Kanaloa) - a first in Japanese racing history. She died in 2021, aged 19.
773: Won 5 on any going, but finished in double figures 6 times - extreme form. Won the TCK Jo-o Hai at 4.
774: 2nd on debut, he won 11 straight, then after a 2nd won 7 more. Though at local Mizusawa and Morioka, word of his run spread nationwide early. He made the top two in 22 straight races until a 4th in the Oi Kinen at 4. From 4 he toured the Tokai and Southern Kanto areas, collecting graded wins everywhere. At 5 he tried the JRA in the All Comers, 7th - a pity we never saw him face JRA horses on dirt.
777: In 2007 she became the first filly in 102 years to win the Belmont S. 4th on debut at 2, she rested 6 months, then took off at 3: after a maiden win, she won the G1 Las Virgenes S. and Santa Anita Oaks in a row. Favorite for the Kentucky Oaks, she sat in a good spot and won with a champion's authority. Instead of the fillies' Triple Crown, she took on colts in the Belmont S. 2nd choice behind Preakness winner Curlin, she fought him fiercely down the straight and edged ahead by a head - the 3rd filly ever to win the Belmont, the first since Tanya in 1905. In autumn she started in the Gazelle S. but, with a fracture, lacked her usual kick, 2nd. Training continued until 4, but the injury worsened and she retired. Her first foal, Opulence (2009), was imported to Japan unraced as a broodmare.
778: A late-blooming stayer who came good when older, winning the Stayers S. and Niigata Daishoten. He left the lower classes in autumn at 4, already known for his stamina, and was favorite in the Stayers S., his first open race, winning it. At 6 (old age system) he was 2nd in the Nikkei Sho and won the Niigata Daishoten as favorite. He kept running well in graded races, retiring after a 10th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) at 7. His sire Pitcairn, champion sire in Ireland, was imported to Japan and also sired 2-time graded winner Soshin Hoju.
779: Seen as a horse who couldn't win until autumn at 3, he came good from year's end into 4. Winning a 14-million special to reach open class, he won the Kimpai (West) by half a length from Riujin Fuji, his first graded win. In the Kyoto Kinen he came from behind to beat Shinsei Kan by a nose. After a quiet year, at 5 he was 2nd in both the Tenno Sho (Spring) and Takarazuka Kinen, but retired with leg trouble after the latter.
780: Stuck in the lower classes until autumn at 3, he was 2nd in the year-end Stayers S. and then focused on long races. It paid off: at 4 he won the Diamond S. and Stayers S., a true stayer. His brother Hokkai Noble won the '76 Stayers S., and his nephew Hokkai Rousseau the '96 Nikkei Sho. His sire was from a tiny German stayer line - pure long-distance blood.
782: Debuting late, in January at 3, he won his debut and the Anemone Sho. Aiming for the Derby, he was 3rd in the Kyoto Yonsai Tokubetsu and missed out. In autumn he was 6th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, missing the Kikuka Sho too. But still in the lower classes, he won the Aichi Hai to reach open class, and won it again at 4. Winless after, he moved to Kochi at 7 and retired without a win.
783: Needing 26 starts to leave the lower classes, he was a hard worker. In his first graded race, the Silk Road S. at 6, he beat Tamamo Hot Play, Amber Jack and others. 3rd choice for the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, he was 7th, then kept running poorly and retired after the '09 Ibis Summer Dash to stud.
786: After the Kisaragi Sho he was 7th in the Satsuki Sho and 11th in the NHK Mile C., but led and held on for 2nd to Vodka in the Derby, then won the Kikuka Sho in autumn. Winless at 4, at 5 he suddenly won 2 G2s, the Kyoto Kinen and Hanshin Daishoten, and became Tenno Sho (Spring) favorite. But he disappointed, 9th, and never won again. Very tough in a duel, he also often sank tamely - an erratic horse.
787: The best son of Haiseiko, who sparked a racing boom in Japan, and the 1979 Derby winner; he also won the Tenno Sho (Spring) at 6 (old age system). Winning 3 straight at 4, he became a classic contender. 2nd in the Spring S. and Satsuki Sho, then 3rd in the NHK Hai trial, he went to the Derby. Fans hoped he would win the Derby his sire never could, making him favorite over Satsuki Sho winner Bingo Garoo and NHK Hai winner Teruten Ryu. Racing in a good spot, he repelled both in the straight and held off Lindo Purbun by a nose - a rare Japan-sired Derby winner in an era ruled by imported sires. Behind in training, he skipped the Kikuka Sho and returned a year later. He won the Meguro Kinen and was Tenno Sho (Autumn) favorite but, letting Pretty Cast run away, was 6th. In the Arima Kinen he redeemed himself, a nose 2nd to Hoyo Boy. At 6 he won the Tenno Sho (Spring) after a fierce match race with Katsu Al, a strong recruit from Oi, winning by a neck. 2nd to Katsu Al in the Takarazuka Kinen, he then retired. At stud he sired Kabutoyama Kinen winner Yu Miroku and local winners Tetsuno Sengoku O and Kane Yutaka O.
788: He won the Asahi Challenge C. at 5 in record time, his first graded win. He kept missing the top five, but at 6 won the Kita-Kyushu Kinen by 2 lengths, his first win in 11 months. With 7 wins in all, he was talented but erratic.
789: A sharp horse raced only at a mile or less since his debut. 3rd in the NHK Mile C., he had the ability for a mile, but all his wins came at 1400m or less, mainly 1200m. Fractures and more forced 2 long breaks from autumn at 3, limiting his wins. But in '07 he won a 16-million race to return to open class, won the Ocean S. for his first graded title and was 3rd in the Sprinters S., showing top sprint ability.
795: A Neo Universe colt based at Monbetsu. Debuting in May at 2, he won his 2nd start. After near misses, he won the Breeders' Gold Junior C. by 4 lengths over favorite Ono Yu, then the Sunrise C., and as favorite won the Hokkaido 2yo Yushun. Moving to the JRA at 3, he has struggled.
796: Half-brother of Mercy Atra. A 4-race streak, including a record Mainichi Hai, beat strong rivals and made him a leading classic hope. His success even brought his sire State Jaguar, already retired, back to stud. But that was the high point: 13th in the Satsuki Sho and 17th in the Derby, his spark gone, he raced until 6 without another win.
754: Full sister of QE II Cup winner To the Victory. Won Funabashi's Queen Sho under Yutaka Take.
761: Beaten by Sakkah Boy in his first graded race, the Chunichi Sports Sho, he won in his class and ran in the Kikuka Sho (11th). After a break he won the Niigata Daishoten as 2nd choice. Steady in open class.
762: By Kentucky Derby winner Fusaichi Pegasus, he sold for 100 million yen as a foal. 7th on his turf debut in February at 3, he blossomed on dirt, reaching open class in his 5th dirt start. In his first graded race, the JRA-local Diolite Kinen, he raced forward and held on, an easy graded winner. All expected him to rise to the top on dirt, but since then his best are two graded 3rds.
763: Running above her class, she was 3rd in the Rose S. As 12th choice in the Shuka Sho, she moved early from behind and held on to win. Winless after, she switched to jumps - almost unheard of for a G1-winning mare - and won her 4th jump race. Back on the flat she ran 4 graded races, all unplaced, and retired.
765: With a reliable late kick, at 3-4 she had a near-perfect 7 wins, two 2nds and two 3rds from 13. From 5 she faced top colts and ran poorly more often, but still added 2 graded wins, incl. the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu at 6.
767: A late bloomer, she won the Himba Tokyo Times Hai with a sharp charge in autumn at 4.
768: Winning the Tulip Sho made her a classic hope, but she was 9th in the Oka Sho and crushed in the Oaks and Shuka Sho. Often beaten when older, she won the Nakayama Himba S. at 5.
769: With crop-mates King Haiseiko and State Jaguar, he lit up Southern Kanto racing. At first he trailed them, 2nd in the Tokyo Derby. Then he won 6 straight, incl. the Tokyo Okansho and Diolite Kinen, and took the Teio Sho. In that autumn's Japan Cup, as local racing's representative, he beat world stars to finish 2nd to Rudolf - a famous feat.
770: She won her debut, the Marigold Sho and the Niigata 2yo S. After a 13th in the Keio Hai 2yo S. and 17th in the Hanshin JF she looked an early bloomer, but as an outsider was a narrow 2nd in the Oka Sho and Oaks and a close 5th in the Shuka Sho.
772: She won her debut in June at 3 and the Queen S. in her 4th start. 6th in the Shuka Sho and 12th in the Fuji S., she then had leg trouble and retired after just 6 starts.
775: He won his debut, was 3rd in the Radio Tampa Hai 2yo S. and won the Keisei Hai. In the Yayoi Sho he used his early speed to trouble heavy favorite Deep Impact, caught by a neck at the very end. In the Satsuki Sho Deep Impact and Six Sense swept past, 3rd. In the "third time lucky" Derby he was swallowed by the pack, 10th. In the Kikuka Sho his camp led boldly to blunt Deep Impact's kick, and just before he escaped, Deep's power overwhelmed him. Still, 2nd from the front in the Kikuka Sho was impressive. After 2 poor runs, a tendon injury ended his career early. At stud he had no notable runners, but as a broodmare sire produced Hanshin JF winner Circle of Life. He retired from stud in 2018 and appeared in a 2022 Yogibo commercial.
776: From the crop of Derby winner Bamboo Atlas and record-priced Hagino Kamui O. In 1984, the first year of graded races, he won the Chukyo Kinen and Naruo Kinen, beating later Japan Cup winner Katsuragi Ace and Suzuka Koban in the latter. He then kept running unplaced and retired at 7.
781: He won 4 straight up to the Hanshin Sansai S., champion 2yo colt. A classic clash with Symboli Rudolf was awaited, but shin trouble cost him 10 months. At 4 he won the Heian S.; after another break he won the Milers C., was 3rd in the Yasuda Kinen and won the Hankyu Hai.
784: She won her debut but was crushed in the Wakatake Sho. As 6th choice in the Queen C. she beat champion filly Shino Cross and others, but a leg injury ended her career. As a dam she produced miler Bell Winner (92: Nihon Pillow Winner).
785: 2nd to Mejiro Ramonu in the Oka Sho. At 4, with jockey Minai aboard, she won the Kita-Kyushu Kinen, then the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu the next year. She retired after a 7th in the Yasuda Kinen.
790: A part-bred with Arab blood, yet brilliantly fast, she won 7 incl. the Sapphire S. and Fukushima Kinen - "star of part-breds." As a dam, only Narita Meister (93: Sunday Silence) raced in the JRA.
791: His 2 turf runs - 16th on his late debut in April at 3, 15th in a maiden - were a model of mediocrity. But after winning on dirt at Monbetsu in his 3rd start, he was a new horse. He won 4 straight to reach open class, was 2nd in the JRA-local Hokkaido Sprint C., Procyon S. and Tokyo Hai, then won the Musashino S. for his first graded title. On dirt, local and overseas included, he had 9 wins and seven 2nds from 20.
792: The mare who made jockey Koichi Sumida "Sumida of the mares." As 9th choice at 6 she upset the Kinko Sho, his 2nd graded win in 2 weeks. She held her own against colts at middle distances.
793: Slow away, she always raced from behind. Stuck in the 9-million class until 4, she bloomed at 5, winning the Hakodate Kinen, and at 7 won the Tokyo Shimbun Hai, moved to dirt due to snow.
794: After starring at local Oi and Kasamatsu, he joined the JRA at 4. He was 2nd to top miler Nihon Pillow Winner in the Milers C., then in the Osaka Hai beat Triple Crown winner Mr. C.B. by a nose after a straight-long duel. 4th in the Takarazuka Kinen, he was caught up in a doping scandal and retired.
797: Many horses improve at tight, flat local tracks, but Maillot Jaune was extreme: she only ran big at Niigata. Of her 7 wins from 39, 4 came from 6 starts at Niigata - 3 of them graded - and her 2 losses there were by just 0.2s. She even won the Fukushima Kinen when it was moved to Niigata for rebuilding.
798: Half-brother of Admire Hope (2 graded wins incl. the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun) and Admire Fuji (3 graded wins incl. the Nikkei Shinshun Hai). 2nd on debut, he moved to local Nagoya, won twice, returned to the JRA and won 5 straight up to the Fukushima Kinen. But in the Nakayama Kimpai he fractured his right 3rd metacarpal. Retired to stud, his condition worsened at the farm and he was put down.
799: He kept trying graded races at 2 without success, but at 3 was a nose 2nd in the Shinzan Kinen. 8th over further in the Wakaba S., he won the NZ Trophy. After that he mostly ran poorly, as if burnt out, though he was 3rd in the Lord Derby Challenge T. at 5. He broke down in the '09 Aurora C. and was put down.
800: A mare who won 2 graded races as an outsider. First, the Fairy S. at 3, edging past the favorites in the straight. 2nd in the Flower C. and Fukushima Himba S., she went a long time without a win. Then at 6, as 10th choice in the Niigata Kinen, she stayed on as the favorites faded and won by a neck - her first win in 3.5 years.
801: Close but winless at 3, he won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai and the Kabutoyama Kinen as an older horse. He then lost form, moved to Hokkaido racing and retired without another win.
802: A talented horse always near the top in graded races. He won the Heian S. at 5, then the March S. and Elm S. at 6. But after a 2nd in the Nambu Hai he developed hemangiosarcoma and was put down - a shocking end.
803: 2nd in the Radio Tampa Hai 2yo S., he won the Mainichi Hai, but was 9th in the Satsuki Sho and 8th in the Derby. He was 3rd in the Kikuka Sho and a popular force in older graded races. At 5 he won the Chukyo Kinen, his first win since the Mainichi Hai, and the Kinko Sho, showing the "Rose family" strength of granddam Rosa Nay. Going for a repeat in the '08 Kinko Sho, he broke down and was put down - he shone at Chukyo and fell there.
804: He won 3 straight, incl. the Kisaragi Sho and Mainichi Hai, but then fractured a leg. Back after 9 months, he never regained his form, and moved to local Funabashi at 6 without a win.
805: Close but winless on turf, he suffered repeated injuries - 1 win from 7 by spring at 5. Back on dirt he won 4 straight and the Heian S. at 6, and despite leg trouble won 2 more graded races. He moved to Iwate at 9, racing until the end of '06.
807: Not overwhelming in ability, nor blessed with rare race sense - but undeniably strong. Her Oaks run, pushing Cesario to a neck, and her neck win in the Shuka Sho showed Air Messiah at her best: "strong without being overwhelming." Her straight 2nds in the Hanshin Himba S. and Victoria Mile reflected that too, if less kindly. As a dam she produced Air One Piece (08: Rock of Gibraltar), and her 4th foal Air Spinel (13: King Kamehameha) won 3 graded races, while his full brother Air Windsor won 4 straight up to the Challenge C.
808: Often close but winless at 3, he came good after injury in summer at 4, winning 4 straight to the Nikkei Shinshun Hai, then the Kyoto Kinen - 5 in a row. His late surge recalled his sire, "late-blooming star" Marvelous Sunday. In G1s he was 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Spring), 2nd in the Takarazuka Kinen and 3rd in the Arima Kinen. He won the '06 American JCC but, racing on until 10, never won again.
809: A head 2nd to Rhein Kraft in the Fillies' Revue and 3rd in the Oka Sho, she beat colts for 2nd in the NHK Mile C., a contender with just 1 win. After a 12th in the Shuka Sho she slumped, but at 4 was 6th in the Victoria Mile and 4th against colts in the Epsom C. In autumn she won the Queen S. and Fuchu Himba S. She was 3rd in the Victoria Mile and won the Fuchu Himba S. again, a leader among mares. She retired to breed after a 7th in the '08 February S.
810: A regular in low-class dirt races, with surprisingly many fans. His partnership with jockey Takashi Hirame, as low-key as the horse, was a hidden favorite: Hirame rode him in 50 of his 55 flat races. Slowly adding wins, at 6, in his 44th start, he tried his first graded race, the March S. A perfect start let him lead, and as 14th choice of 14 he pulled off a huge upset - Hirame's first graded win too.
811: Beaten badly in 2 turf races, he won his 3rd start on dirt like a new horse. Racing only on dirt after, he won the March S. in spring at 5, then the Tokai S. over Time Paradox and others - he had come good. He was 5th in the Teio Sho and JBC Classic, but a fracture was found. Back in June '05, he was 3rd in the Onuma S. but had lost his old strength. He finally won again in the Shiwasu S. at the end of '06. Still racing at 9 in '08, aiming for a full comeback, he was retired without running.
812: Half-sister of graded favorite Columbus Circle. She won her debut over a mile at Tokyo in November at 2 in a good 1:34.7. 2nd choice in the Fairy S., she broke clear early but was caught by a neck by 11th choice Cosmo Mnemosyne. As favorite she won the Queen C. with authority, an Eastern classic hope with 2yo queen Apapane. But 2nd choice in the Oka Sho, she faded to 5th behind Apapane, then was dull in the Oaks, 6th. In summer she beat older mares in the Queen S., but was 3rd behind Apapane again in the Shuka Sho. Older, she was 2nd in both the Keisei Hai AH and Fuji S. and won the Capital S. (OP).
813: By autumn triple crown winner Zenno Rob Roy out of Motek, a French middle-distance graded winner. She won her debut and a special. 1.6 favorite for the Flower C., she couldn't quicken, 3rd to Oken Sakura. Aiming only for the Oaks, she won the Flora S. as 1.9 favorite. 5th choice in the Oaks, she dueled Oka Sho winner Apapane to the line, noses level; after a long photo, it was the first dead heat in classic history. She didn't win again and went to stud in 2013.
814: She beat older mares in the Mermaid S. and was 3rd in the Aichi Hai. A closer, not consistent, she was still 3rd in the Mermaid S. at 4 and 5. She retired to breed in February '09.
815: Winner of 11 US G1s from 2002 to 2004; in 2002 at 4 she was only the 3rd female Eclipse Horse of the Year. Debuting late, in November at 3, she won her first G1, the Santa Margarita Invitational H., in spring at 4 and went on a winning run, taking 5 G1s that year incl. the BC Distaff - the first female Horse of the Year since Lady's Secret in 1986. At 5 she won 4 more G1s on the same path, but after a 2nd in September's Lady's Secret H., a tendon injury forced a long break. Back, she won less often but took 3 more G1s, incl. a 3rd straight Apple Blossom H., retiring with 11. At stud she produced graded winner Wine Princess, and from 2010 lived in Japan, bred to Deep Impact and Heart's Cry without notable success.
816: Winner of the 2004 Breeders' Cup Classic by a dominant margin, one of the best horses of the 2000s. He raced as a sprinter until 3: 3rd in his first G1, the King's Bishop S., he won the Vosburgh S. by 6 lengths. At 4 he stretched out with the BC Classic in mind, winning a 9-furlong G3 by over 10 lengths and the G1 Woodward S. as favorite. In the 10-furlong BC Classic, against stars like Pleasantly Perfect, then rated the world's best, and dual classic winner Funny Cide, he led all the way and won easily, earning Eclipse Horse of the Year. Racing on at 5, he won the Metropolitan H. but then hurt a leg and retired. At stud he sired many top fillies like Contested, Judy the Beauty and Goodnight Olive, plus colts like 2021 Dubai World Cup winner Mystic Guide and 2024 Santa Anita Derby winner Stronghold. As a broodmare sire he gave 2018 US Triple Crown winner Justify and Drefong, now a sire in Japan.
817: 6 wins, three 2nds and three 3rds from 15. Never out of the top five in 5 graded races incl. the Nikkei Sho and Kyoto Daishoten, he won a graded race in his final start, the Kokura Daishoten. At stud he sired steady runners like Kokura Kinen winner Sunrey Jasper.
818: Close but winless in lower classes, at 4 she ran above her class for a 2nd in the Mermaid S. She was 4th in the Kokura Kinen, 2nd in the Niigata Kinen and Fuchu Himba S., but 7th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup. She broke through in summer at 5: 2nd in the Mermaid S., then beat colts in the Kokura Kinen. Flu and hoof trouble halted her, and after her return she ran poorly, but had a long career.
819: Beaten in the trials (4th Spring S., 7th Aoba Sho), he missed the classics but won the Radio Nikkei Sho, unfazed by heavy ground. After an 11th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai he rested, returning in the Niigata Daishoten at 4. Struggling in older graded races, he won the Capital S. in autumn '08, then beat Admire Aura, Fallichat and others in the Kyoto Kimpai, his first graded win in 2.5 years. But he never made the top five in 8 more starts and retired after the '10 Niigata Daishoten.
820: After 2nds and 3rds, he won in his 5th start, then was 2nd in the Radio Nikkei Sho. 3rd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai in autumn, but graded-winless, he was 8th choice for the Kikuka Sho. In the race he ran down front-running Admire Main near the line with a powerful finish - a brilliant first G1. After a 4th in the Hong Kong Vase, a tendon injury ended his career. At stud he sired Hanshin JF 3rd Rice Terrace and others.
821: At 4 he was 2nd in the Kimpai (West), Kyoto Kinen, Osakajo S. and May S., but winless. The next year he won the Kimpai (West), catching later G1 winners Marvelous Crown and Nehai Caesar. A broodmare after retiring, she died in a pasture accident in '08.
823: Raced on dirt from his 2nd start, he was 2nd in the Japan Dirt Derby and Derby Grand Prix at 3. He won his 2nd open special in the Ritto S. at 4 but fractured his left knee and was out over a year. Back in July at 5, he was 4th in the Procyon S., then won 4 straight to the JBC Sprint - suddenly the ace of dirt sprints. At 6 he was 4th in the Dubai Golden Shaheen, the best yet by a Japan-trained horse. In autumn he won the Cluster C. and Tokyo Hai, but a tendon injury ruined his JBC Sprint repeat, and he retired to stud.
824: He led all the way in his first dirt race, the Poinsettia Sho (5M), then again in the big Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun. Invited to the UAE Derby, he went and was 8th. Back home he was beaten badly, his limits exposed, and after the Topaz S. at 3 moved to Sonoda.
825: By modest sire Carista Glory, but with top speed. At 3 he focused on turf sprints and won 3 straight incl. the Ibis Summer Dash. Struggling after, he switched to dirt and won the Keiyo S. (OP), then was 2nd in the JRA-local Kakitsubata Kinen. Winless in sprints on any surface after, he moved to Arao after the '09 Ibis Summer Dash, and won his first race there from the front.
827: 3rd in the Kokura 2yo S., she showed promise but missed the classics and was 15th in the NHK Mile C. After a long break, she focused on sprints of 1200m or less and won the Kita-Kyushu Kinen in summer at 4. After a 9th in the Centaur S. she lost her rhythm, finishing in double figures, and went to stud in '08.
828: He romped on debut and won the Niigata Sansai S. easily in record time, but a fracture kept him off the turf for 19 months. Back in April at 4, he beat Hokuto Helios, Material and others in the Paradise S., then was 3rd in the Tanabata Sho. Another injury cost him a year, and after one more race he retired. Everyone wondered what he could have been without injuries.
829: With just 1 win, he ran above his class to win the St. Lite Kinen, but was 16th in the Kikuka Sho. He then ran in the Japan Cup, Arima Kinen and February S. without making the top five. A tendon injury followed, and after a comeback the next summer he retired.
830: Bred at US Dell Ridge Farm, like Capella S. winner Victory Tetsuny. After 2 turf losses in summer at 2, she returned in a Kyoto 1400m dirt race and won by 4 lengths, then romped against colts in the Poinsettia Sho, a dirt contender. 3rd in the Hyacinth S. and 6th in the Fillies' Revue aiming for the Oka Sho, she went back to dirt and crushed colts in the Shoryu S. In the Kanto Oaks she raced forward and won by 5 lengths - top 3yo dirt filly. As jockey Yasunari Iwata said, she was a match for colts: dominant in fillies' JRA-local races, 2nd against colts in the Kashiwa Kinen. After duels with Miracle Legend, a year younger, she was 4th to Transcend in the Japan Cup Dirt as 10th choice, then retired to breed.
831: Raced on dirt from debut, he beat older horses in the Taisetsu H. (10M), then won the G1 Derby Grand Prix by a neck. He never ran well again, crushed even in open specials, and moved to Southern Kanto in '08.
832: A true miler who ran almost only at 1400-1600m on turf. Crushed in the NZ Trophy and NHK Mile C. at 3, he slowly improved, and at 7 won the Fuji S. as 16th choice, holding on against the odds.
806: Debuting in Hokkaido racing, he won 4 straight by wide margins incl. the Hokkaido 2yo Yushun. Moved to Futoshi Kojima's JRA stable, he was crushed in the Keisei Hai and returned to local racing.
822: In his 27th start, at 5, he tried his first graded race, the Hakodate Sprint S., and as 13th choice blew away See Is Tosho and others with a storming finish. A flat-track lover, he was also 3rd in the Keeneland C.
826: Too late for the Oka Sho, she won the Sweet Pea S., ran in the Oaks and Shuka Sho, and won the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu as 10th choice. As a dam she produced '05 Nakayama Himba S. winner Winglet (01: Taiki Shuttle).
833: At 3 he led all the way in the Kisaragi Sho as 11th choice. But in the classics Narita Brian dominated, he was nowhere: 17th of 18 in the Satsuki Sho, 18th of 18 in the Derby, 15th of 15 in the Kikuka Sho. Had Trust Kankan not been last in the Satsuki Sho, he would have achieved a "reverse Triple Crown" - last in all three - as Narita Brian swept them.
834: 2nd in both the Kyoto Kinen and Nikkei Sho at 4, he drew attention, then kept finishing 4th-6th. In autumn at 5 he won the Sapporo Nikkei OP, was 3rd in the Kyoto Daishoten and won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. Steady in graded races, he was 2nd in the '08 Nikkei Sho but fractured a leg training for the Tenno Sho (Spring) and died, deeply missed.
835: A late-maturing stayer who won the Stayers S. at 4. 2nd in the Epsom C., Kyoto Daishoten and Meguro Kinen, he had graded ability but was often beaten badly - simply never running when unfancied.
836: Winner of 9 dirt G1/JpnI races, one of the best dirt horses of recent years. 2nd in his first graded race, the Heian S., at 4, he was 4th against top horses in the February S. Then he swept the big races: Kashiwa Kinen, Mile CS Nambu Hai, Japan Cup Dirt, the next February S. and Kashiwa Kinen - undisputed dirt king. On his long-awaited trip abroad he was 10th in the BC Classic, but at 7 won the Kashiwa Kinen and Nambu Hai, and at 8 the Nambu Hai and JBC Sprint. He retired to stud after a 7th in that year's Japan Cup Dirt. His first crop debuted in 2017, making him the leading first-season sire in local racing, and his 3rd crop produced Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun winner Vacation (Kawasaki), his first JpnI winner.
837: A late bloomer, he debuted in April at 3 and needed 2 starts to win. Then he won 3 straight and was 3rd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, earning a Kikuka Sho spot. That Kikuka Sho was wide open, without Derby winner Deep Sky, Black Shell or Satsuki Sho winner Captain Thule. He was favorite and delivered. In the Japan Cup he was a close 5th to Screen Hero, proving he could match top older horses. Skipping the Arima Kinen, he returned at 4 in the Hanshin Daishoten as favorite over Asakusa Kings and Screen Hero, but was 7th and missed the spring with leg trouble. In autumn he won the Kyoto Daishoten with a burst, was 4th behind stablemate Company in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) despite the trip, and in the Japan Cup chased Vodka down the straight, failing by a nose. He ran in the Kyoto Daishoten 4 years running (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 2nd), a middle-to-long distance favorite, but never won another G1 and retired to stud.
838: He won his debut and the '08 Tokyo Sports Hai, a classic hope. In spring he was a bit-player, 8th in the Satsuki Sho and 4th in the Derby, but won the St. Lite Kinen in autumn. 4th choice for the Kikuka Sho, he was 12th, then 13th in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai, perhaps hurt by travel. At 4 he won the Metropolitan S. with authority and boldly tried the Takarazuka Kinen. Arriving at Ritto early to avoid travel stress paid off: as 8th choice he ran down Buena Vista to win - a huge upset. In autumn he went with Satsuki Sho winner Victoire Pisa to the Arc. 2nd in the Prix Foy, he was badly hampered in the race, but surged in the straight and, after a fierce duel with Derby winner Workforce, was 2nd - equal with El Condor Pasa ('99) as the best Arc finish by a Japanese horse. Back home he was 14th in the Japan Cup, but was named Best Older Male. The next year he tried the Arc again, 11th, and retired to stud. Quirky - stopping in training and dumping jockeys after the line - but a fierce fighter.
839: A tough horse who matured by racing a lot: 11 starts at 4 (old system), 19 at 5, 12 at 6. In the lower classes until spring at 5, after winning the Maya S. (14M) he was 6th to Green Grass in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and 6th to Erimo George in the Takarazuka Kinen. That autumn he won the Asahi Challenge C., Kyoto Kinen (Autumn) and Aichi Hai in a row. Winless after, he retired after a 10th in the Asahi Challenge C. at 7.
840: Winner of the 1973 Derby and Kikuka Sho. Known as Haiseiko's great rival, he was dominant at 2400m and beyond. After winning his debut he struggled, only winning again at 4 (old system), and another win in late April just got him into the Derby. Haiseiko, unbeaten in 10 after moving from Oi and the Satsuki Sho winner, was a heavy favorite; Take Hope was 9th choice. But he swept past Haiseiko in the straight, showing the crowds who had come for Haiseiko who he was. In autumn he was 8th in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai and only 6th choice for the Kikuka Sho, but again beat Haiseiko by a nose after a duel, a double winner and now his lifelong rival. At 5 he beat Haiseiko in the American JCC and lost in the Nakayama Kinen. In the Tenno Sho (Spring) they met again; Haiseiko moved too early and faded, and Take Hope won his 3rd big race. Their farewell clash came in the Arima Kinen: Tanino Chikara won, Haiseiko 2nd, Take Hope 3rd. At stud Haiseiko sired stars like Katsurano Haiseiko, but Take Hope sired no graded winner, falling far behind.
841: Slowly building in his own class, he entered graded racing in autumn at 5. He won the Fukushima Kinen on soft ground and the '07 Tanabata Sho. A graded regular, he retired with a tendon injury in '08 - a local graded race specialist.
842: Winning twice on dirt, he tried the classics, but was 16th in the Satsuki Sho. Back on dirt he won the JRA-local Hyogo Championship and was 2nd in the Unicorn S., then rested with a fracture. Back in December, he was 2nd in the Shiwasu S., and ran well in open races until he won the '08 Elm S., then the Negishi S. He was 5th in the February S. and 3rd in the Kashiwa Kinen, contending at the top. After a 2nd in the Nippon TV Hai, he was injured preparing for the JBC Sprint and had a long break. Back after 2 years in the 2011 Capella S., he was 12th, then 15th in the Negishi S., and retired.
843: With 2 wins, he ran above his class in the Kikuka Sho (8th). He added 3 wins at middle-to-long distances on turf and joined older graded racing at 6. 17th in the Meguro Kinen, he beat Kongo Rikishio and others in the Asahi Challenge C. Winless in '07, he retired after a maiden hurdle in autumn and became a riding horse.
844: The first foal of great mare Shinko Lovely, but often close without winning; his first graded win came at 6 in the Chukyo Kinen. After that his best was 2nd in the Tanabata Sho.
845: She won her debut but showed a difficult temper for a 3rd in the Niigata Sansai S., then won the Daily Hai Sansai S. At 3 she won 3 straight graded races - Shinzan Kinen, Flower C. and NZ Trophy - then the NHK Mile C. as heavy favorite, top speedster of her crop. Older, she raced in Europe and, ahead of Taiki Shuttle, won the French sprint G1 Prix Maurice de Gheest - the first G1 win abroad by a Japan-trained horse. At 5 she tried the US dirt G1 Santa Monica H., a creditable 4th of 8 on her first dirt run. Sold to a US owner, she bred in America. Her first foal Seeking the Dia (01: Storm Cat) won 5 graded races on any surface and was 2nd 9 times in G1s, raising hopes for her as a dam, but she was struck by lightning and died on June 10, 2005 - a tragic early loss.
846: He won in his 2nd start, then was 2nd in the Keisei Hai and 4th in the Kisaragi Sho and Wakaba S. In the classics he was 2nd in the Satsuki Sho and 3rd in the Derby, then 2nd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai and 4th in the Kikuka Sho, and 2nd in the Hong Kong Vase. Graded class but winless, "the best 1-win horse," he finally won the Kyoto Kinen at 4 with Yutaka Take. But a tendon injury right after forced his retirement.
847: Gelded before his debut, he started late, in June at 3. Winning steadily through the classes, he reached open class in spring at 4, dropped back, and returned by winning the Osakajo S. at 5. 3rd in the Hakodate Kinen and Fukushima Kinen, he won the Nakayama Kimpai at 6 by 3.5 lengths. His reliable kick lasted: at 9 in '07 he was 2nd in the Nakayama Kimpai and won the Kokura Daishoten as 10th choice. At 10 in '08 he won the Kokura Daishoten again - the oldest JRA flat winner ever - and ran in the Takarazuka Kinen, the oldest turf G1 runner. He retired after the Feb '09 Kokura Daishoten to be a riding horse at his birthplace.
848: Injured at 4 and out for a year, he won the Silk Road S. on return and was 3rd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, a sprint regular. The next year he beat Sprinters S. winner Calstone Light O in the Hankyu Hai and was 2nd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen. He tried English G1s but, perhaps disliking the ground, was unplaced twice. Declining after, he switched to jumps at the end of '06, winless in 3, then went back to the flat for a 16th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen. After more jump and local moves, he won at Kasamatsu in '08.
849: By Meisho Homura out of Meisho Hagoromo - the essence of the Meisho brand. At 4 he won the Kokura Daishoten by 5 lengths, starring on middle-distance turf. Injured at the end of 4, he switched to dirt after a long break and won 3 graded races in a row: Procyon S., Summer Champion and Sirius S. In '07, with Yutaka Take, he won 4 JRA-local G3s in a row: Kakitsubata Kinen, Sakitama Hai, Sparking Lady C. and Cluster C. From 8 he won the Marine C. twice and was 2nd in the Nambu Hai - a long-running dirt force.
850: He won his 7th start but couldn't win his way into the spring classics. 3rd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, he was 10th in the Kikuka Sho. A late-blooming stayer, he improved from autumn at 4 and won the Diamond S. at 5.
851: 3rd in the Aoba Sho, he was 9th in the Derby. He won through his class and took the Hakodate Kinen at 4. Back from 5 months off, he won the Nakayama Kimpai and American JCC, then fell ill. After another long break he was always beaten and retired.
852: He won his debut by 3.5 lengths, was 2nd in the Daily Hai 2yo S. and won the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. A year off cost him the classics, but older he recovered, 2nd in the Kinko Sho, then won the Sekiya Kinen.
853: 2nd in the TV Tokyo Sho Sansai Himba S. at 2, she then struggled, winning just once at 3 and not at all at 4. At 5 she won a 9-million race and 3 straight, up to the Nakayama Himba S.
855: Needing 8 starts to win, he was clearly short of class until spring at 3. Then he became consistent, always fancied in allowance races. At 5 he won the Wangan S. by 5 lengths, but injury kept him out over a year. In his 5th race back he won the Niigata Kinen, was 2nd in the All Comers and 3rd in his farewell, the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. One more year would have been nice.
856: After narrowly winning the Shoryu S., he was 3rd in his first graded race, the Unicorn S., then beat older horses in the Elm S. He won the G1 Derby Grand Prix by 9 lengths, a future dirt star, and boldly went to America for the BC Classic (6th). Tired from the trip, he ran poorly in the Tokyo Daishoten and was 12th in the February S., then won the Diolite Kinen and Elm S. Hopes of a revival faded as he never won again, moving to local Oi at 6. Winless in 6 and failing a gate test, he sat out about a year and went to stud in '09.
857: He won the Centaur S. at 4 as favorite, his first graded title. After poor runs, he won it again the next year, his first win in a year. He added 2 more wins but was very erratic, with some shocking runs. By '07 he had lost his power and moved to local Sonoda after a losing streak.
859: She won her July debut and went straight to the Hakodate 2yo S., winning it. Going straight to the Hanshin JF, she was 2nd. But after a 14th in the Oka Sho, she kept finishing in double figures. In spring at 5 she won the Stork S., her first win in 3 years, improved, and won the Final S. at year's end. She aimed for another graded win but fell short and retired to breed in '08.
860: Debuting at Kyoto in autumn at 2, she won in her 3rd start. Stepping up for the Tulip Sho, despite drifting in, she caught 2yo queen Apapane to win - a big upset and sudden classic hope. In the Oka Sho she was blocked in the straight but finished 4th. 2nd choice for the Oaks, on soft going and down in weight, she faded from the front to 17th, second-last. After mostly mid-field runs, she won the Kyoto Himba S. with a sharp 33.3 finish, and at 5 won the Asahi Challenge C., a blanket finish with the whole field within 0.6s. She went to stud in 2013 - a hot-and-cold mare.
861: He won his debut, the Dahlia Sho and Niigata 2yo S. 5th in the Keio Hai 2yo S., he won the Asahi Hai FS in a stunning record 1:33.4 to be 2yo champion. A classic favorite, he was 3rd in the Yayoi Sho behind the overwhelming monster Deep Impact, then a steady 4th in the Satsuki Sho and 5th in the Derby. After that his form faded; from January '06 he rested 14 months, and after his return did little and retired.
862: He led all the way in the Sapporo 2yo S. and held on for 2nd leading in the Asahi Hai FS. At 3 he led all the way in the Kyodo News Hai, but then broke a leg, missing the spring classics. Back in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, he led and faded to 8th, then was well beaten in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Japan Cup. After another long break he ran poorly and retired in autumn '08.
863: By US Horse of the Year Mineshaft out of Better Than Honour, dam of 2 US classic winners, he was bought for $950,000 at a US yearling sale. Delays in training put back his debut to February at 3, a Kyoto 1800m dirt race, which he won by 2.3 seconds. His camp then announced their plan for the Belmont S., the US Triple Crown's final leg. He won the Peter Pan S. easily as a prep, aiming for a 3rd straight Belmont for his family after brother Jazil and sister Rags to Riches, but a stone bruise forced his scratch on race morning. After returning home, he went to the BC Classic, led boldly from a good start but tired to finish last, 12th. Back home he won an allowance race easily, then in the February S. lost a fierce straight duel to Success Brocken by a neck, beating Kane Hekili and Vermilion - clearly top class. Representing Japan in the Dubai World Cup, he ran out of stamina, 8th. Back home a severe tendon injury forced a long break; returning after 2 years, he didn't win again and retired to stud. He covered 200 mares in his first year, with high hopes, but stopped breeding from 2017 and died young in 2019. After his death, Casino Fountain led all the way to win the 2021 Kawasaki Kinen, his first JpnI winner.
864: He won the Daily Hai 2yo S. and Shinzan Kinen, but lost form after a 6th in the Spring S. He was 6th in the Satsuki Sho, 4th as NHK Mile C. favorite behind fillies, and worst of all 15th in the Derby. Struggling at a mile to middle distances, he switched to sprints and in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen charged to 2nd as 13th choice. He kept racing at 1200-1400m but never escaped his slump, retiring at the end of '08 to stand in France.
865: By 2-time Arima Kinen winner Symboli Kris S out of '02 Fillies' Revue winner Success Beauty - a fine pedigree. He won his debut by 3.1 seconds and kept winning big on dirt, beating later Unicorn S. winner Ubiquitous by 0.9s in the Tango S. Boldly trying the Derby, his first turf race, he was 3rd choice but finished last. He bounced back to win the Japan Dirt Derby by 0.6s - notably, runner-up Smart Falcon had been last in the Satsuki Sho, so the two classic last-placers finished 1-2. After summer he was narrowly 2nd to champion Vermilion in the JBC Classic, ahead of Meisho Tokon and Furioso. He was 8th in the Japan Cup Dirt and 3rd in the Tokyo Daishoten and Kawasaki Kinen, no match for Kane Hekili or Vermilion, but at his peak in spring at 4 beat both in the February S. Favorite for the Nambu Hai, he was beaten 4 lengths by crop-mate Espoir City, and lost to him again in the Japan Cup Dirt. He beat Vermilion by a nose in the Tokyo Daishoten, but was then blocked by Espoir City, Furioso and others, retiring after a 13th in the Negishi S. at 6. He now works as a lead pony at Tokyo Racecourse.
866: He won his debut in January at 3, the Kobushi Sho and the Arlington C., unbeaten in 3. But a fracture cost him the classics. Back, he often fell just short, until the '08 Hakodate Kinen, his first win in 18 months.
867: He won a 10-million special in autumn at 3 and rode the momentum into the Kikuka Sho. Rated only 8th choice, he showed his staying power and won - his first graded win a classic. He kept running well, 3rd in the Japan Cup and 5th in the Arima Kinen, but missed spring '05 with back trouble. He won the Stayers S. in his 2nd race back, then went winless until he went to Australia and won the Melbourne Cup, the Southern Hemisphere's biggest race - a true stayer. From '07 he slumped and retired in June '09.
854: His first win came in his 10th start, but at 4 he won 3 straight, and at 5 won the Kokura Kinen. A Kokura specialist, in '05 he won the Kokura Daishoten, Kita-Kyushu Kinen and Kokura Kinen again - the "Kokura Triple Crown." In '06 he won the Tanabata Sho, but was 6th in the Kokura Kinen, 11th after a year off, and retired after a 10th in the Asahi Challenge C.
858: Debuting in March at 3, she missed the spring classics, but won a 5-million race and the Rose S. 3rd choice for the Shuka Sho, she was 6th, then 7th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup. She won the Queen S. at 4 but was inconsistent. As a dam she produced Keisei Hai winner Beruf (12: Harbinger).
869: He won his dirt debut and a turf open race, but was outclassed in turf graded races and, after finishing last in the Satsuki Sho, returned to dirt. 2nd in his first race back, the Japan Dirt Derby, he won the '08 Hakusan Daishoten. After a 2nd to Bamboo Ere in the JBC Sprint, he won 6 straight JRA-local graded races nationwide, incl. the Urawa Kinen. Winning his first G1, the JBC Classic, in autumn at 5, he swept aside rivals Furioso, Espoir City and Transcend for 9 straight wins. Some criticized his policy of racing only in JRA-local races, never in JRA graded races, but when he beat Transcend in a duel in the 2011 JBC Classic, Yutaka Take said "local racing made this horse strong," and the winner's circle roared. In the Tokyo Daishoten, as 1.0 favorite, he held off Wonder Acute only by a nose, stirring the crowd, but won the Kawasaki Kinen easily at 7. On a 9-race streak he went to the Dubai World Cup, but hit his head in the gate and stumbled after the start, unable to lead, 10th. He never fully recovered, and injury led to his retirement and stud career. Leading at a fast pace and pulling away, he was called "the Silence Suzuka of the sand" - one of recent dirt racing's stars.
870: At first his huge, nearly 550kg frame was a burden, but winning a dirt maiden in his 4th start, he breezed through the 5, 10 and 16-million classes and went straight to the Japan Cup Dirt against strong older horses. In his first graded race, let alone G1, he was only 7th choice, but closed from midfield to win - 5 straight up to a G1. Then leg trouble at pasture kept him out 10 months, and on his return in the Sirius S. he fractured a pastern. Back in the '09 Jinsen S. he was 8th, and though 2nd in a graded race, he never won again and retired after a long break.
872: Granddaughter of Lady's Secret, US Horse of the Year. After narrow losses from up front in her first 4 starts, she switched to closing in her 5th and won. She boldly tried the Elfin S., a classic gateway, but a slow pace left her 9th. Less fancied in the Fillies' Revue, the race suited her and she swept past Ranunculus to win an Oka Sho spot. But the Oka Sho's slow, fast-finishing race didn't suit her, 16th. In the NHK Mile C. the fast pace suited her, but racing forward she couldn't handle the speed, 13th.
873: Debuting in October at 2, he was winless in 4 entering his 3yo year. He won a maiden in late January, was 2nd in a 5-million race and 3rd in the Arlington C., then as 6th choice won the Mainichi Hai over later Aoba Sho winner Admire Command. Skipping the Satsuki Sho for the NHK Mile C., he was favorite, sat handy and burst through on the inside to win. That earned him favoritism in the Derby too: he settled behind and swept down the wide outside to win - the first NHK Mile C.-Derby double since King Kamehameha. In autumn he won the Kobe Shimbun Hai against his crop, then chose the Tenno Sho (Autumn) over the Kikuka Sho; in that historic race he was a close 3rd to Vodka and Daiwa Scarlet. After a 2nd in the Japan Cup he rested, returning at 4 with a fine 2nd in the Osaka Hai. In the Yasuda Kinen he seemed to have won, but Vodka's amazing burst beat him, 2nd. 3rd in the Takarazuka Kinen, he then suffered a tendon injury at pasture. With his sire Agnes Tachyon dead that year, he retired to stud as his heir. In 2015 Sound Sky won the Hyogo Junior GP, his first graded winner.
874: After winning her debut, she was 2nd to Meiner Recolte in the Niigata 2yo S., then swept past Rhein Kraft and others in the Hanshin JF to be 2yo queen. But at 3 she was out of form, crushed in the Oka Sho and Oaks, best a 2nd in the Shion S., and retired. As a dam she produced NZ Trophy winner Shonan Achieve (11: Shonan Kampf).
875: He ran well without winning, lost form, ran poorly, and repeated - suddenly he was 7. In the March S., his first graded race in a while, he won as 9th choice. It looked like he'd come good, but he slumped again. Yet at 8 in '08, as 6th choice, he beat Meisho Tokon, Bonneville Record and others. After a good 6th in the February S. he fractured a leg and retired to stud.
876: He won a maiden, then in the Sapporo 2yo S. closed to within half a length of front-running Stormy Cafe. At 3 he won a weak Sumire S., then held off Nishino Dokomademo in the Aoba Sho. With "the ultimate Derby pedigree" - his dam line bred to Derby-siring stallions for 7 generations - he was 3rd choice for the Derby as a threat to Deep Impact, but did nothing, 13th, and retired.
877: A consistent model student who rarely ran badly, but with too many 2nds and few wins. So his rise was slow; his first G1 was the Tenno Sho (Spring) at 5, where he was 3rd, then 2nd in Australia's G1 Caulfield Cup. After more near misses - 4th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), 2nd in the Meguro Kinen and Argentina Kyowakoku Hai - he won the '06 Stayers S. He won the '07 Hanshin Daishoten and was Tenno Sho (Spring) favorite, but 4th again. 2nd in the '08 Hanshin Daishoten, he never won a G1, and a 3rd in the '08 Kyoto Daishoten was his last.
878: She had brilliant front-running speed, shown in the Flower C., but her fiery temper, like her sire's, left her 10th in the Oka Sho. She was 4th in the Oaks but faded to 15th in the Rose S., and a recovery seemed unlikely. But in the Shuka Sho, as the favorites faded, she slipped through on the inside to win as 11th choice; with 8th and 16th choices 2nd and 3rd, the trifecta paid a G1-record 10.98 million yen. At 4 she went to Dubai for the Cape Verdi S., but bled in training. Barred from racing for 20 days, she switched to the Balanchine S. but bled again in the race, last of 9. She aimed for a summer return but retired to breed. Her foals include Sapporo 2yo S. winner Bright Emblem (12: Neo Universe) and Flora S. winner Victoria (16: Victoire Pisa).
879: Raced only on dirt, she won the JRA-local Diolite Kinen right after reaching open class. Winless after but 2nd in the Antares S., she then ran poorly and moved to Sonoda in '09.
880: In the open '08 colts' classics, the only one with 2 graded wins before the Satsuki Sho. Unmatched in his crop at Nakayama 2000m, he was Satsuki Sho favorite but 3rd to Captain Thule. He led his crop through the Derby (4th) and Kikuka Sho (5th) but lacked a final push. Expected to shine when older, he had a mild tendon injury, and after repeated breaks never regained his form and retired.
881: Needing 6 starts to win, he was slow to win, but won 3 at 5 to reach open class. His first graded race was the Tenno Sho (Spring), 15th. He then won the Fukushima TV OP, was 3rd in the Tanabata Sho and led safely to win the Niigata Kinen. Big things were expected in autumn, but fetlock trouble forced a long break; moved to local racing for a comeback, he broke a leg in pool training and was put down.
882: He won his debut and a 5-million race, but was 15th in the Asahi Hai FS. Focusing on 1200m, he won the Falcon S., but lost form from summer at 3 and moved to Iwate in autumn '09.
883: She won the Queen C. as favorite, but was 12th in the Oka Sho. She won the Sweet Pea S., then was 12th again in the Oaks. 5th in the Shuka Sho and 6th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, she lacked class for big races. Racing mainly in fillies' graded races on any surface until 5, her best was a 2nd in the Fukushima Himba S.
884: First noticed as a white horse, she drew more hopes with each step: winning, reaching open class, running in graded races. In the '08 Kanto Oaks she became the world's first white graded winner. 2nd in the Queen Sho and TCK Jo-o Hai, she moved to Kawasaki for race entry reasons. 3rd in her first race there, she then won the Queen Sho and TCK Jo-o Hai, and retired to breed.
885: After a 13th in the Daily Hai 2yo S., he won the Hyogo Junior Grand Prix, then the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun by 4 lengths over Funabashi star Sea Chariot. He seemed set for dirt, but his camp chose the Spring S., a Satsuki Sho trial: outclassed on turf, 15th. Back on dirt he never won again and moved to local Funabashi.
886: 4th as 3rd choice in the Asahi Hai FS, he won the Spring S. and, though foreign-bred, ran in the classics: 12th in the Satsuki Sho and 10th in the Derby. After over a year off, he returned in autumn '08, did little in 3 starts and rested again. From the summer '09 Tomoe Sho he raced more steadily, a long-time regular in open specials.
887: 2nd in the Mainichi Hai, he won the Aoba Sho but was 16th in the Derby. 7th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, 10th in the Kikuka Sho and 16th in the Japan Cup, he stalled - but won his first jump race by 7 lengths.
888: 2nd in the Shinzan Kinen, 3rd in the Kisaragi Sho and 2nd in the Wakaba S., he ran in the Satsuki Sho with just 1 win (11th). 2nd again in the Principal S., he was 9th in the Derby and 13th in the Kikuka Sho. He won the Welcome S. in late November and the Nakayama Kimpai at 4. He then went cold, just 1 win by 7. But in '05 he won the Osakajo S. and Osaka-Hamburg C., then as 14th choice in the Tenno Sho (Spring) led and held on for 2nd, part of an 80,000-yen quinella. He later moved to local Kanazawa.
889: After 2 wins she was a fine 4th against colts in the Keisei Hai, then won the Queen C. 2nd choice for the Oka Sho and favorite for the Oaks, she was 5th and 7th, and, after a break, out of the top five in the Shuka Sho. Yet never beaten badly, her finishes were always among the fastest. Proving it, she beat seasoned older mares in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, switching from her late charge to a forward position - promising more as an older mare. But apart from the Aichi Hai, she never won another G1.
890: From Shadai's famed Scarlet Ink family, he drew attention before his debut. He won it, then was 2nd twice, before winning the Radio Tampa Hai 2yo S. Dull in the spring classics at 3, he switched to dirt in autumn - a perfect fit. He won the Enif S. and Urawa Kinen and became a dirt mainstay in JRA and local graded races. In '07, though 4th in the Dubai World Cup, he won the Kawasaki Kinen, JBC Classic, Japan Cup Dirt and Tokyo Daishoten - the first to win 4 dirt G1s in a year. In '08 he silenced distance doubts to win the February S. In his second Dubai World Cup a shoe problem left him last, 12th, but on return he beat rising star Success Brocken in the JBC Classic. Then he lost twice to revived crop-mate Kane Hekili in the Japan Cup Dirt and Tokyo Daishoten. After a 6th in the '09 February S. he seemed in decline, but won the Teio Sho and JBC Classic. At 8 in '10 he won the Kawasaki Kinen in record time - the first graded winner 7 years running - for 9 G1s in all. At stud, his first crop's Not Formal won the Fairy S. as 11th choice. May he pass on precious El Condor Pasa blood.
891: Favorite on debut in September, she was 10th, but won a maiden at month's end and then a 5-million race as 8th choice of 9. A close 3rd in the Fillies' Revue earned an Oka Sho spot, and as 12th choice she won it by half a length from FT Maia. She was 3rd in the Oaks despite trouble and 2nd as favorite against older mares in the Queen S., proving the Oka Sho no fluke. 3rd in the Rose S., she was 8th as 2nd choice in the Shuka Sho. Her reputation then fell with runs unworthy of a classic winner, but at 5 she won the Fukushima Himba S., her first win in about 2 years.
892: After winning Uruguay's Triple Crown he moved to America, won 6 G1s in a row including the BC Classic, and was 2006 Eclipse Horse of the Year. In Uruguay he won his first 5, including the Triple Crown, and was Horse of the Year by far. Moving to America, he was 4th in the UAE Derby, then won the Pimlico Special H., Suburban H. and Whitney H., and beat Bernardini, Lava Man and others in the BC Classic - the first South American-bred Eclipse Horse of the Year. The next year he won the Donn H. and the Dubai World Cup: 6 wins and 6 G1s from 7 after moving. A fracture ended his career. Little success at stud; he returned to Uruguay in 2015.
893: Raced only on dirt, rarely beaten badly but rarely winning, with many 2nds and 3rds; he needed 27 starts to reach open class. In open class he kept finishing in double figures, but in the JRA-local Nagoya Daishoten ran the race of his life to beat Blue Concorde and others. Back to double figures, he moved to local Sonoda.
894: At 3 he ran well in graded races: 4th in the NZ Trophy, 6th in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai and Radio Tampa Sho. At 4 he went to France and was 2nd in the G2 Prix Daniel Wildenstein. At 5, back in JRA graded racing, he won the Lord Derby Challenge T. In double figures in graded races after, he was 2nd in the '08 Kokura Nikkei OP, then retired.
895: 2nd in the Keio Hai 2yo S., he fractured a leg. Back after a long break he won the St. Lite Kinen, but ran poorly in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). He then shone at a mile, 2nd to Great Journey in the '06 Lord Derby Challenge T. Racing with breaks, in autumn at 5 he won the Kochi S. and Keisei Hai AH, was 4th in the Sprinters S. and 6th in the Mile CS, and stayed competitive in graded races from 6.
896: Always strong, he fully bloomed at 5, winning the Antares S. and Procyon S., then 2nd in the G1 Nambu Hai and Musashino S. and a strong 5th in the Japan Cup Dirt. In '08 he won the Negishi S. and placed in all 3 G1s - February S., Kashiwa Kinen and Nambu Hai. After that year's Japan Cup Dirt he had leg trouble, did little on return and retired to stud after a 12th in an open special at 8.
897: He won the NZ Trophy as 11th choice; with 16th and 8th choices 2nd and 3rd, the trifecta paid 4,904,740 yen, then 5th highest in JRA history. 5th in the NHK Mile C., he was 4th in the Unicorn S., fracturing a leg in the race. He returned in the Heian S. the next January, rested again, and came back in June the following year to win an open special.
898: At 3 he won the Wakaba S., was 3rd in the Kisaragi Sho and Kyoto Shimbun Hai, 5th in the Satsuki Sho and 4th in the Derby - consistent. 4th in the St. Lite Kinen and 6th in the Kikuka Sho, he won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai at 4. Leg trouble disrupted him after, but he won the '08 Nakayama Kimpai and, under top weight, again in '09. He later moved to local racing.
899: 3rd on his turf debut in autumn at 2, he rested with sore shins. Back on dirt over 1700m in spring at 3, he won 5 straight from maiden to open class with the speed of his sire War Emblem - a new dirt star. In his first graded race, the Antares S., he easily held off Wonder Speed in 1:47.8, a Kyoto 1800m dirt course record. Going for more in the Tokai S., he was jostled, lost heart and finished last of 16 - his first loss in 7 dirt starts. Perhaps shaken by it, he never shone again and retired.
901: From the first crop of 2004 Arc winner Bago, out of Run for the Dream, winner of 2 graded races incl. the Asahi Challenge C. Unlike her late-blooming dam, she won in her 3rd start in January at 3, then beat Gestalt, later a classic colt, in the Kobushi Sho. 2nd choice behind 2yo queen Apapane in the Tulip Sho, she struggled on heavy ground, 4th.
