In the straight he dueled Real Birthday and won by half a length - the first Ibaraki-bred and first grey Derby winner. He fractured a leg in the Kikuka Sho and retired.
1209: At 2 he fractured a leg after winning his 3rd start. Back, he skipped the classics, was 3rd in the NZ Trophy Yonsai S. and won the Chunichi Sports Sho Yonsai S. In autumn he won the Kobe Shimbun Hai and was 2nd to Bamboo Begin in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, but was 12th as 3rd choice in the Kikuka Sho. Rested until the new year, he won the Kimpai (West) and Chukyo Kinen, a true top horse, then was 2nd in the Osaka Hai and 3rd in the Yasuda Kinen. In the Takarazuka Kinen, Oguri Cap was 1.2 favorite; Osaichi George, with 7 wins, four 2nds, two 3rds and only one unplaced run (Kikuka Sho), was 3rd choice. He took the lead at the final turn and easily held off Oguri's charge for his long-sought G1. He then lost form and never placed again in 8 starts before retiring.
1210: He won his turf debut, then raced mainly on dirt, winning 3 straight from autumn at 3, and the February H. (G3) as 2.8 favorite - champion dirt horse that year. He then switched to turf, winning the Kimpai (East) and Meguro Kinen at 5, 2nd in the American JCC and Nikkei Sho, and 2nd to Pre Classny in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), overshadowed by Mejiro McQueen's demotion. Winning graded races on turf and dirt and staying at the top is rare, and fans loved him as an all-rounder. At 8, after winning the Breeders' Gold C., his first win in a while, he died of a sudden heart attack in training.
1211: Debuted in the JRA, then moved to local racing at 6 and shone, winning 28, incl. the Nambu Hai.
1212: Debuting at Obihiro in Hokkaido, he won his 3rd start and 4 straight, incl. the Hokkaido Sansai Yushun in record time. Moving to the JRA, he won the Keisei Hai Sansai S. After a break for the classics, he was 3rd to Narcisse Noir and others in the Spring S., then went to the Satsuki Sho as a leading contender. Down 16kg from his last race, on heavy ground - the worst conditions - he raced forward and held off Winner's Circle's charge by half a length, a classic winner. Older, he won the Stayers S. in record time.
1213: Steady on dirt, he won the Breeders' Gold C. easily in autumn at 4, then switched to turf, 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). The next year he won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai, then was 2nd 4 races running, 3 of them G1s: Hanshin Daishoten and Tenno Sho (Spring) behind Mejiro McQueen, Yasuda Kinen behind Yamanin Zephyr, Takarazuka Kinen behind Mejiro Palmer. Good at any distance, he never beat the specialists - a jack of all trades.
1214: At 3 he was 2nd in the Pegasus S. (G3: 1600m) and Spring S., but 12th in the Satsuki Sho, and kept struggling in turf graded races. At year's end he switched to dirt and won the Winter S. in record time, his first win since his debut, then the February H. (G3) in record time too, suddenly a dirt star. At 4 he lowered the Winter S. record again, and the next year dead-heated with Russian Gold in Oi's Teio Sho. Next, in the Musashino S. (OP), he set yet another record under 60.5kg - a monster. Weights over 60kg then held him back, and at 6 he moved to local Niigata, winning 3 straight before breaking down in his 5th race and retiring.
1215: He won the Epsom C. in spring at 4, then the Mainichi Okan after a break, and went to the Tenno Sho (Autumn). Beaten 6 lengths by champion Mejiro McQueen, he was promoted to the win when McQueen was demoted for veering.
1181: Many think of her when they hear "one-hit wonder." She barely won an allowance race before the Oaks and went in as 21st choice of 28. The pace was fast, and Noano Hakobune, slow away, was last at the 3rd turn. Her move came so late her connections had given up - then she slipped through in the straight and beat favorite Mistategami and Oka Sho winner Elps - one of racing's great upsets.
1183: 2nd to Scrum Dyna in the Asahi Hai Sansai S. at 2, he drew notice. At 3 he was 11th in the Satsuki Sho and 10th in the Derby, winless. He struggled when older but won the Meguro Kinen, racing mainly in graded races - erratic.
1188: He won his debut and an allowance, but lacking a kick, he was an ordinary allowance horse until spring at 5. Winning a special at Niigata that summer, he bloomed: 2 allowance wins at Fukushima, then the Fukushima Kinen. In the Arima Kinen, as an outsider, he was 5th to Mejiro Durren. At 7 he won the Sekiya Kinen as 14th choice after 8 months off - a summer local specialist.
1200: He won the Asahi Hai Sansai S., but at 3 was beaten badly by Material in the Spring S. and Sakura Star O in the Satsuki Sho. With Star O absent, he won the Derby by 6 lengths, the widest margin ever. But he was well beaten by Star O in the Kikuka Sho, and in the Arima Kinen, meant to settle their rivalry, he lost his rider at the start. At 4 he was 2nd but well beaten by Mejiro Fulmar in the Meguro Kinen and 14th in the Tenno Sho (Spring). In his last race, the Hakodate Kinen, he was 2nd, 5 lengths behind 3yo Sakkah Boy - his shine never returned.
1202: With 2 wins and two 2nds from 5, he was 9th in the Satsuki Sho. After a 4th in the Aoba Sho, he won the NZ Trophy Yonsai S., then was 3rd in the Kikuka Sho and 2nd in the Arima Kinen, but never won again, retiring at 4.
1205: He won the Satsuki Sho in only his 4th start, but having been toyed with by Oguri Cap in the Mainichi Hai, he wasn't seen as the best. He was 4th to Sakura Chiyono O in the Derby and lost to Sakkah Boy in the Chunichi Sports Sho Yonsai S. In autumn he won the Kyoto Shimbun Hai but was 10th as Kikuka Sho favorite behind Super Creek. His misfortune was a crop packed with great rivals. He kept winning G2s like the Naruo Kinen and Osaka Hai, but in G1s against Oguri Cap, Super Creek and Inari One he only placed. Then at 5, in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he finally beat Oguri Cap for his 2nd G1.
1206: Half-brother of fillies' Triple Crown winner Mejiro Ramonu. Debuting late, in March at 3, he showed his blood, winning his debut and the Yamafuji Sho (4M), then 2nd in the NHK Hai (G2: 2000m). In the Derby, his 4th start, he defied 6th choice for 2nd, but was injured and rested a year. He won the May S. off the break and the Takamatsunomiya Hai (G2: 2000m) by 2.5 lengths from Bamboo Memory, seen as the next star after the Big Three. He was 3rd behind Oguri and Inari in the Mainichi Okan and 3rd behind Creek and Oguri in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), but injury forced another long break. Back, apart from a 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he ran poorly and went to stud after the Japan Cup at 6. His best foal in Japan was BSN Open winner Mejiro Steed, but exported to China in 2001, he sired Wu Di, who won 27 races there and went to stud, carrying on Northern Taste's sire line, now gone in Japan.
1216: He caught front-running Daitaku Helios by a head in the Hanshin Sansai S. 4th in the Satsuki Sho and 10th in the Derby, he broke a leg, went 3 years winless, and switched to jumps.
1217: Debuting late, in June at 3, he suffered a tendon injury right after his 2nd win. Back after 16 months of treatment, he grew rapidly into a powerful stayer, typical of Real Shadai's runners. In autumn at 5 he ran above his class to win the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. The next year he was narrowly beaten by Biwa Hayahide and Narita Taishin in the Tenno Sho (Spring) - impressive given his leg trouble.
1218: On turf his best was a 3rd on heavy ground, but on dirt he was in the top three every time: 7 wins, a 2nd and four 3rds from 12. In the '92 February H. (G3), doubted for lack of graded form and the trip, he was 10th choice, but brushed aside stars like Manjuden Kabuto and Narita Hayabusa - a new dirt king. He won the Keiyo S., then dead-heated with Narita Hayabusa in Oi's Teio Sho.
1219: Another masterpiece by the late trainer Tameo Toyama, who made Mihono Bourbon. His temper kept him from showing his ability; he couldn't even win a maiden at 2. Resting with a fracture, Legacy World was gelded to cure his temper - a great decision. Back, he rose steadily: 3 months later he won the St. Lite Kinen, then was 4th in the Japan Cup and 2nd in the Arima Kinen - transformed. Another fracture brought 9 months off, during which Toyama fell ill and died. Moving to Hideyuki Mori's stable, he returned in autumn, 2nd to Mejiro McQueen's powerful finish in the Kyoto Daishoten, then in the Japan Cup raced boldly forward and held off foreign stars Kotashaan, White Muzzle, Star of Cozzene and others. On the international G1 stage he had dreamed of with his late trainer, he gave everything and beat the world. A 3rd injury then cost him over a year. Back, perhaps to spare his legs, he ran in local graded races like the Kawasaki Kinen and Diolite Kinen, without winning.
1220: After Tokai Teio, Emperor Rudolf's best son. Debuting late, in May at 3, he won his 2nd start, then ran only at 2000m+. In autumn he won 2 allowances, then the Stayers S., his first graded race. At 4 he often fell short, but won the Stayers S. again at year's end. A classic stayer with a sharp kick, he was also 2nd in the Takarazuka Kinen and 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), top class at middle distances too.
1221: Called the last big runner by US Triple Crown winner Secretariat, he drew notice before his debut. His fiery finishing kick thrilled fans and terrified his crop rivals. But for all his talent, his early-maturing blood and a tendon injury beat him, and he retired with just 3 graded wins. The name Hishi Masaru first belonged to the 1959 Yasuda Kinen winner; he was the second, so his official racing name is Hishi Masaru II.
1222: Debuting fairly late, in January at 3, she won the Flower C. in her 4th start - "the first star of the East" - and headed to the spring classics, but was no match for heavy favorite Vega: 5th in the Oka Sho, 6th in the Oaks. In the Queen Elizabeth Cup, the last leg, the tables turned: she swept aside double winner Vega for her first G1. As the race caller cried, "Vega, yes - but Hokuto Vega!" - an upset as 9th choice. Winless after the Sapporo Kinen in summer at 4, her camp even tried jump training to find a new path. Then, almost by chance, she ran in the JRA-local Empress Hai at Kawasaki and won by 18 lengths - the start of the "Queen of the Sand" legend. Still struggling on turf, from 6 she switched fully to dirt, winning 9 of 9 dirt graded races, beating every star, JRA and local, and sweeping the major titles. In '97 she went to the Dubai World Cup as Japan's representative. It was the world's top race, but her strength was extraordinary, and fans hoped for a close fight. Having toured all of Japan to reach her dream stage, she was caught in a tragic accident in the race and died on foreign sand. But her role in lighting up JRA-local racing and her record as "the greatest dirt horse" in Japanese history will never fade.
1223: In his first G1, the Japan Cup, he beat US turf champion Paradise Creek - only the 5th Japanese winner of the Japan Cup and the 2nd gelding to win a G1 in Japan. Then leg trouble kept him from his best, and he retired. As a gelding, a local-racing comeback was tried, but he pulled up in his 2nd race and retired.
1224: The first foal of great mare Dyna Actress, much noticed before his debut, but he did little in the spring classics. 2nd to Biwa Hayahide in the Kikuka Sho, he showed his stamina and, older, focused on long races, winning the Nikkei Sho in spring at 4. In the Tenno Sho (Spring) at 5 he charged at front-running Rice Shower, failing by a nose. He kept running well in long graded races and won the Stayers S. at the end of 5.
1225: Unbeaten in 2, he beat Biwa Hayahide by a nose in the Asahi Hai Sansai S. after a fierce duel, unbeaten 2yo champion. Leg trouble dulled him after, but at 6 he won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai - his first graded win in 3 years 11 months.
1226: Debuting late, in March at 3, he raced steadily and won a 16-million race the next January. Inconsistent, he was slow to win, but at 5 he came good and became reliable, winning Saga's JRA-local Kaisetsu Kinen and KBC Hai, then beating a star field incl. Lively Mount and Amazon Opera in the Tokyo Daishoten - a Grand Prix win. He won the Heian S. the next year but was crushed in the February S., missing his dream Dubai World Cup. Inconsistent again, he switched to jumps without winning.
1227: Half-brother of Derby winner Dr Devious, a hyped foreign-bred. But his debut was delayed to July at 3, and he stayed in allowances until autumn at 4. After about 10 months off, he won an open special in his 2nd race back and was 3rd in the Sprinters S., repeatedly just missing a graded title. At 6 he finally did it in the Takamatsunomiya Hai (now Takamatsunomiya Kinen) - his first graded win, a G1.
1228: The dirt champion who symbolized "Year One of interchange," when JRA and local racing opened up to each other. He won the Winter S. at the end of 3, then went seeking new rivals in local racing, winning 7 straight to rule Japanese dirt racing. The next year he was Japan's representative in the first Dubai World Cup, against the world's best. He was 6th behind Cigar, then America's best - more than enough to show the spirit of Lively Mount as Japan's champion in the world's top race.
1229: Apart from his debut, all his wins came at 2000m+, incl. 2 graded races over 3000m - a stayer. At 3 he won the Aoba Sho, was 2nd to champion Narita Brian in the Derby and 3rd in the Kikuka Sho. In the Stayers S. he brushed aside older horses in his first meeting with them, setting a Japanese record of 3:41.6 that still stands. The next year he won the Diamond S., but in G1s was 5th to Rice Shower in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and 3rd to Dantsu Seattle in the Takarazuka Kinen. Valued for his pedigree at stud, he was popular for a while but sired no stars and was exported to Korea at the end of '02.
1230: A son of great sire Danzig, then rare in Japan, he drew notice early and, with his sire's speed, had a long career in sprints. At about 430kg he was small for a colt, but charmed fans with a powerful late charge. In an era packed with top horses, and with his extreme style at the mercy of the pace, he ran 14 G1s with three 2nds. But in his graded wins - the Keisei Hai, beating 2yo queen Hishi Amazon by 2 lengths, and the Centaur S. with a tremendous kick - he made a huge impression. A colorful supporting star.
1231: He won the Radio Tampa Hai Sansai S., then the Shinzan Kinen as 1.5 favorite by 7 lengths, rising to Narita Brian's top challenger. But a mild tendon injury ruled out the Satsuki Sho, and in the Derby, the trip too long, he couldn't get near Narita Brian, 6th. The tendon injury recurred twice, and at 6 he moved to Kochi. From his debut in September 1993 to retiring in December 2005, he raced for over 12 years.
1232: 3rd in the Derby, he won the Radio Tampa Sho over future G1 winners Taiki Blizzard and Offside Trap. Skipping the autumn trials, he won an open race against older horses in record time - suddenly Narita Brian's main challenger. He ran well in the Kikuka Sho but was 2nd to Brian's overwhelming run. After that he slumped, racing until 6 with only a 2nd in the All Comers in graded races and 2 open special wins.
1233: He won the Radio Tampa Hai Sansai S. at 2, a leading classic hope. 2nd in the Kyodo News Hai and 5th on heavy ground in the Wakaba S., he chased Genuine for 2nd in the Satsuki Sho, then won the Derby easily as favorite - the first Derby winner from Sunday Silence's first crop, cementing his sire's fame. He lost form, and after a 6th in the Kikuka Sho retired with leg trouble to stud. His best was Derby Grand Prix winner Man of Purser. In '08 he broke his right femur in a pasture accident and was put down.
1234: Of his 28 races, only one, his 2nd, was on turf - a big loss that set his course. Slow to win at 3, he won his 2nd race at 4 and then 5 straight. At 5 he won the Nambu Hai, a long-sought G1. Racing mainly in JRA-local graded races, he was 2nd going for a repeat in the Nambu Hai, then won the Urawa Kinen. He stood as heir to sire Jade Robbery and is now retired as a pensioner.
1235: Winless in 7 on turf, he won 12 on dirt, mainly at middle distances. Oddly, he did nothing in JRA-local G1s like the Teio Sho, Tokyo Daishoten and Nambu Hai, but was strong at graded level, especially over 2100m at Tokyo, winning the Musashino S. at 6 and 7. Had the Japan Cup Dirt existed then, he would surely have been a contender. He retired after a loss in the Teio Sho at 7 and went to stud.
1236: Brother of Ski Paradise, whose Prix du Moulin win gave Yutaka Take his first G1 abroad. Tipped for greatness from the start, he won his debut and the Kyoto Sansai S. His duel with fellow unbeaten Fuji Kiseki in the Asahi Hai Sansai S. is still talked about: in the dim dusk, his white body charged to catch Fuji Kiseki but fell a neck short. At 3 he won the Kisaragi Sho, then was 14th in the Kentucky Derby.
1240: A pure sprinter: every win at 1200m. Debuting late, in February at 3, and set back by injury, he got going at 4: winning a 16-million race, then the Hankyu Hai, and 3rd in the Takamatsunomiya Hai (now Kinen). The next year, in his 2nd Takamatsunomiya Kinen, on rain-soaked good-to-soft ground, he broke clear from 2nd and held on for his long-sought first G1. Racing only in sprints, he won 9 in all. At stud in Europe and Oceania he sired many graded winners, but died at his Irish farm in '07. His half-brother New Approach was Europe's champion 2yo colt in '07.
1241: After his debut win he struggled, but in his 13th start, on dirt, his blood suddenly bloomed: 3 straight wins incl. 2 graded races - a dirt star. He kept shining in graded races and won the Tokyo Daishoten at 4, reaching the top.
1242: Brother of Winning Ticket, by Sunday Silence - a prized blueblood. He debuted the same day as Dance in the Dark and beat him in the Radio Tampa Hai Sansai S. and Kisaragi Sho. But in the classics he was 2nd in the Satsuki Sho and 4th in the Derby, and in the Kikuka Sho was beaten by rival Dance in the Dark's powerful finish, 2nd - always close, never crowned. He kept running well in G1s and G2s but lacked the final punch and never won again. At stud he sired '07 Queen S. winner Asahi Rising (03: Asahi Mercury).
1243: That year the NHK Hai (G2: 2000m), formerly a Derby trial, was reborn as the NHK Mile C., a spring 3yo mile championship open to foreign-breds. In its first running, 14 of the 18 runners were foreign-bred - a festival of imports. Taiki Fortune, who won the Mainichi Hai but had no classic eligibility, naturally chose it. Against strong imports like Fabulous la Fouine, Sugino Hayakaze and Generalist, he won in a stunning 1:32.6, the first champion. Strong and fast, but fragile too: of his 15 races, apart from his 4 wins he made the top five just once.
1245: He beat Mejiro Bright in the Spring S. but was crushed in the Satsuki Sho and Derby, so switched to shorter races. It worked: older, he won the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and Milers C. and was 2nd in the Mile Championship.
1247: Winning his 2nd race at 4, he kept adding wins and took the Epsom C. as 11th choice. A middle-distance regular, he ran in 25 graded races, winning the Epsom C. again, the American JCC and Nakayama Kinen - 4 graded wins. Short of G1 class, he still burst into 2nd behind Manhattan Cafe in the Arima Kinen at 6, setting up huge payouts. It was the year of the 9/11 attacks, and the Manhattan-American combination was called a "coded bet."
1249: At 2 he was 3rd in the Sapporo Sansai S. and Daily Hai Sansai S. without winning, so switched to dirt - a perfect fit. At 4 he won a 9-million race and 3 straight up to the Elm S. Unstoppable, he then beat stars like Kyoei March and Wing Arrow in the JRA-local G1 Nambu Hai, seemingly set to rule dirt. But leg trouble forced a break, and he broke a leg training for his comeback and was put down.
1250: He ran all 38 races on dirt, winning 8. A close 3rd in the Derby Grand Prix at 3, he won the Tokai Winter S. at the end of 4, then the Diolite Kinen and Oguri Cap Kinen the next year, strong around 2400m. But at 5, at his peak, injury forced a long break. Back in spring at 6, a shadow of his best, he was beaten badly every time and retired at the end of 7 without another win.
1251: 2nd to Grass Wonder in the Asahi Hai Sansai S. and 3rd to El Condor Pasa in the NZ Trophy Yonsai S. - in the greatest crop, his rivals were tough, and his spring at 3 brought only near misses. In autumn he beat older horses in the Centaur S., then in the year-end Sprinters S. shockingly beat Taiki Shuttle, who was meant to crown his retirement ceremony after the race. Injuries followed, and apart from the Silk Road S. at 4 he never won again, retiring at the end of 5. At stud his first crop gave NZ Trophy winner Meiner Hearty (02: Civil Suite) and others.
1237: Crossing the line 3rd in the Wakaba S., a Satsuki Sho trial, he got in when winner Louisiana Boy was demoted. He led boldly in the Satsuki Sho (7th), then outdueled Meiner Garbe to win the NHK Hai (G2: 2000m). He starred mainly at local meetings, winning the Fukushima Kinen and Tanabata Sho. In the Arima Kinen at 4 he was a superb 3rd, ahead of Mayano Top Gun, Hishi Amazon and others - one of 6 graded 3rds.
1238: As 4th choice he held off Royal Touch to win the Satsuki Sho. 6th in the Derby and beaten in both trials, his camp made the unusual call to skip the Kikuka Sho for JRA-local dirt racing, and he won the Derby Grand Prix. He then boldly tried G1s of every kind: Kawasaki Kinen, February S., Tenno Sho (Spring), Yasuda Kinen.
1239: His G1 at 6 and late debut make him seem a late bloomer, but he showed promise early, 3rd in the Swan S. and CBC Sho at 3. He won the Hakodate Sprint S. at 4 and the Hankyu Hai, but fell short in G1s - "a second-rate sprinter." But at 6, as 8th choice in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, Masa Lucky beat Seeking the Pearl by over a length - proof of first-class quality.
1244: He won the St. Lite Kinen but was 11th in the Kikuka Sho. Older, he won the American JCC and Nikkei Sho, then was 5th in the Tenno Sho (Spring). With 4 graded wins but short of G1 class - mid-ranking among Sunday Silence's stars.
1246: The first G1 winner for Thoroughbred Club Ruffian ("Meiner"). He won the Hakodate Sansai S., Keisei Hai Sansai S. and Asahi Hai Sansai S., champion 2yo colt. At 3, behind in training, he was 13th in the NHK Mile C. and 15th in the Derby, and kept running poorly. At 5 he won the Christmas S., his first win in 3 years, and the Milers C. at 6, racing until 7. He died young in '08 as his stud career began.
1248: Several breaks slowed his rise, but he won the Asahi Challenge C. in autumn at 4, then beat Mejiro Bright in the Kyoto Daishoten. 8th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he was a superb 4th, half a length behind T.M. Opera O, in the Arima Kinen. Injury cost him 10 months, and in his 2nd race back, the Arima Kinen, he pulled up; saved, he was forced to retire.
1252: Set back by injury, he missed the spring classics. 2nd to Biwa Takehide in the Radio Tampa Sho, he was injured again after the Kobe Shimbun Hai. After 11 months off, he was 2nd in the Asahi Challenge C. and lost a nose duel to Grass Wonder in the Mainichi Okan. He won the Osaka Hai at 5 and Naruo Kinen at 6.
1254: Winning the January S. at 5 to reach open class, he won the Negishi S. on heavy ground, then the February S. by 1.25 lengths from Wing Arrow, going for a repeat - 3 straight and the dirt crown. He then raced in JRA-local races nationwide and abroad: of 88 starts, 39 in the JRA and 48 at local tracks, winning 4 JRA-local graded races - the Tochigi Marronnier C. twice, Sakitama Hai and Hyogo Gold T. Still racing at 12 in '08, even in G1s, he had lost his old power and retired to stud.
1255: By Park Regent out of a Goodly mare - a minor pedigree - yet a dirt specialist who starred in JRA-local races. Slow to win at first, with below-average results, he climbed the classes slowly and showed his ability at 5, winning the Diolite Kinen, and the next year the Kawasaki Kinen, a G1. At 8 he ran in the Dubai World Cup as part of Japan's team (9th).
1257: He won his first 3, up to the Daily Hai Sansai S., was 2nd in the Asahi Hai Sansai S. and Kisaragi Sho, then won the Arlington C. That was the end of his run: after a 7th in the NZ Trophy Yonsai S. he never won again.
1258: Won the NZ Trophy Yonsai S. by half a length and was 2nd in the NHK Mile C., then ran dismally and retired.
1261: Beaten in the trials, he missed the classics and raced mainly on dirt, often placing without breaking through. Reaching open class in autumn at 4, he matured: the next year he won the Procyon S. and Sirius S., then raced at local tracks. Beaten in the Nambu Hai, he outdueled Novo True in the JBC Sprint for a G1. He kept running in graded races, JRA and local, winning the Procyon S. again and running well in dirt sprints.
1262: With Novo True, a year older, he formed the "Novo-Novo" duo of JRA-local racing. From his first JRA-local race, Kochi's Kurofune Sho, he won 6 straight across Japan - Takasaki, Hokkaido, Morioka, Oi - capped by the JBC Sprint, one of local racing's top races. He kept touring: Utsunomiya, Kasamatsu, Nagoya, Funabashi, Urawa, Sonoda. In the '03 Kurofune Sho, Novo True was 2nd - a same-prefix 1-2. At stud from '05, his best was Kurofune Sho winner Blason d'Iris (Kochi).
1264: With 1 win and two 2nds from 3, he won the Principal S. and was a fine 4th in the Derby. A close 2nd in the St. Lite Kinen raised Kikuka Sho hopes; over 3000m he broke clear from a good spot but was narrowly beaten by Air Shakur, 2nd. A fracture after his 3yo season cost him over a year, and chronic hoof heat limited him to the Nakayama Kimpai and an open special when older. He raced until 8.
1265: By Wild Rush, sire of dirt king Transcend. Raced only on dirt from his debut in autumn at 2, he reached open class in summer at 4. He won 4 open specials and was 2nd in 3 graded races like the Capella S., a steady dirt sprinter, finally winning the Hyogo Gold T. at 6 and the Kakitsubata Kinen at 7.
1267: At 3 he alternated wins and losses like Othello pieces. At 4 he was 2nd twice in 4 starts, incl. the Yasuda Kinen, then injured. Back in summer at 5, he won the Keisei Hai Autumn H. easily, then ran poorly with leg trouble, before winning it again in good time the next year. A 4th long break followed. Talented as a sprinter, his career fell a bit short due to leg trouble.
1268: Won the Japan Dirt Derby, beating Agnes Digital, but never won again and moved to jumps.
1270: Versatile in any company, pace, distance or tactics, he lit up JRA-local dirt racing. In 30 dirt races he finished worse than 5th only 3 times - remarkably consistent. His graded wins were just the Kakitsubata Kinen and Tochigi Marronnier C., but he was 2nd in G1s - Tokyo Daishoten, February S. and Teio Sho. Valued for his ability, he went to stud.
1271: He won the Komakusa Sho (OP) on Derby day and the Tomoe Sho easily, then beat older horses and Derby winner Jungle Pocket in the Sapporo Kinen. In the Kobe Shimbun Hai he beat future G1 winners Kurofune and Dantsu Flame for 4 straight, but was 3rd to Manhattan Cafe in the Kikuka Sho. After a year off injured, he won the Hakodate Kinen and All Comers, but leg trouble persisted, and he retired without a G1 to stud, later exported to France.
1272: Half-brother of Mejiro Bright. By Sunday Silence instead, he was a speedier type. He needed 4 starts to win a maiden, but next, in the Asahi Hai Sansai S., easily defied 10th choice of 16 to win a G1. But soon after becoming 2yo champion, injury cost him 14 months. Back at 4 for just 2 races, he rested again over 2 years and retired without returning.
1273: With 2 wins from 3 on dirt, he ran in the Kisaragi Sho but, perhaps unsuited to turf, was 6th. Back on dirt, he won the Hyacinth S. and Fukuryu S., then the Hyogo Championship. He won the Nagoya Yushun, then beat Utopia by a nose in the Japan Dirt Derby, a G1 against the nation's best. He stalled after, moved to Sonoda in '05, and broke a leg in a race at the end of '05 and was put down.
1274: Winner of 7 US G1s incl. the Woodward S. and Jockey Club Gold C. twice each; 58th in The Blood-Horse's "Top 100 US Racehorses of the 20th Century." He won his first G1, the Wood Memorial S., in spring at 3, was 4th in the Kentucky Derby and 2nd in the Belmont S. In autumn he won the Woodward and Jockey Club Gold C. At 4, after an allowance win, he won 4 G1s in a row: Whitney H., Woodward, Marlboro Cup Invitational H. and Jockey Club Gold C. In the first BC Classic that year he was 2nd to Wild Again, but was Eclipse champion older male. He then retired to stud, siring Awe Inspiring, Golden Opinion, Thirty Six Red and others; Awe Inspiring was imported to Japan as a sire.
1275: One of Northern Dancer's most successful sire sons. He sired Galileo, Montjeu, Opera House and many more, and was champion sire in Britain and Ireland a record 14 times. His runners excel worldwide, founding the Sadler's Wells line. A fine racehorse too, he won the Irish 2000 Guineas and Phoenix Champion S. and was 2nd in the King George VI & Queen Elizabeth Diamond S. His first crop gave G1 winners Old Vic and In the Wings, followed every year by stars like Salsabil and Opera House. Galileo sired Frankel and Montjeu Hurricane Run - his family swept Europe's great races. Thought unsuited to Japanese turf, he still has many successful descendants there, like T.M. Opera O, Meisho Samson, Logotype, Mozu Ascot and Soul Stirring. His dam Fairy Bridge was a half-sister of Nureyev, making Nureyev his uncle.
1276: Winner of the 2000 Guineas and Irish Derby, with 7 wins and a 2nd from 8. In 1984, at 3, he was rated the world's best at 138 lbs. His crop, packed with stars like future Arc winner Rainbow Quest, great sire Sadler's Wells and 2-time G1 winner Chief Singer, was called one of the strongest ever. He lost the Derby to Secreto by a short head, but beat all those rivals, earning the world's top rating. He was to run in the King George and the Arc after the Irish Derby, but leg trouble forced his retirement. At stud he sired King George winner Belmez and Rodrigo de Triano, winner of the English and Irish 2000 Guineas and a sire in Japan. A good record, but next to Sadler's Wells and Rainbow Quest, the tables had turned.
1277: Winner of the Kentucky Derby and Preakness and 13 US G1s. Called the last great horse of the 1970s, he was rated "better than Secretariat up to 10 furlongs." Winning his 5th start by 15 lengths, he went on a streak, champion 2yo colt, and won all the way through the Kentucky Derby and Preakness at 3 - 12 straight. He was injured on Belmont day and finished 3rd, and in autumn was outfought by previous Triple Crown winner Affirmed in the Jockey Club Gold C., 2nd. But he then won his last 10 races until retiring at 4. So dominant was he that no one challenged him in the Woodward S. at 4, making it a walkover. 26 wins from 30, 8 records, and 10th in The Blood-Horse's "Top 100 US Racehorses of the 20th Century." At stud he sired Futurity S. (then G1) winner Spectacular Love and others, but no great success.
1278: An American horse who made his name beating Japan's aces Tamamo Cross and Oguri Cap in the 8th Japan Cup. He began in France as an ordinary horse, winning just a Listed race and an allowance from 17. Moving to America in spring at 4, he won a G2 at once and was 2nd in the G1 Bowling Green H. and Man o' War S. After 2 big losses, his camp aimed for the Japan Cup instead of the Breeders' Cup. All eyes were on the grey duo Tamamo Cross and Oguri Cap and Arc winner Tony Bin, but 9th choice Pay the Butler beat them all. Jockey McCarron's tactic - steering away from Tamamo Cross in the straight so the gritty grey couldn't fight him - shone. Back the next year, he was 3rd behind Horlicks and Oguri Cap's duel. After one more allowance win, he retired at the end of 6. At stud in Japan, he died in an accident after just one crop.
1279: One of Danzig's best, a dominant European sprinter. After winning his 1200m debut and losing badly at 1400m, he was kept to 1000-1200m. In August at 3 he won the Nunthorpe S., his first G1, then the Sprint C. and France's Prix de l'Abbaye, quickly top of Europe's sprinters. In America for the BC Sprint, unfazed by his first dirt race, he broke clear with previous Eclipse champion sprinter Safely Kept, but near the line shied at the grandstand's shadow and lost narrowly. Still, he was Europe's Horse of the Year and rated 133 lbs, the highest ever for a turf sprinter. At stud he sired occasional graded winners, incl. Shinko Splendor in Japan (Keisei Hai Autumn H., Elm S.), but was a slight disappointment as Danzig's heir.
1280: A mare bred in Japan who raced in Britain and won a G1. English broodmare Lingerie was boarded at Japan's Shadai Farm and bred to Hector Protector, producing her. Sent to Britain to race, she won the 1999 Tattersalls Gold C. (G1) at 4 - the first Japanese-bred to win a G1 abroad. But the year before, US-bred, Japan-trained Seeking the Pearl and Taiki Shuttle had won G1s abroad, drawing the headlines, and 1999 was also the year US-bred El Condor Pasa took on the Arc, so her feat got little attention. She also won 2 G3s and retired to breed in America, bred to top sires like Kingmambo and Storm Cat, without notable foals.
1282: The best son of Arc winner Urban Sea and half-brother of Galileo. Winner of 6 G1s incl. the Arc and an English double, and a fixture near the top of Europe's sire table. 4th on debut, he won 3 straight to the 2000 Guineas, then the Derby - the first double since Nashwan 20 years earlier. Meeting older horses in the Eclipse S., he beat Conduit and other stars, then won the International S. and Irish Champion S., going into the Arc on a 7-race streak. Against Conduit, Youmzain, crop-mates Fame and Glory and Stacelita and more, he was odds-on favorite, and from midfield went up the inside in the straight to win almost easily. He retired after it. His first crop included King George winner Taghrooda, followed by English and Irish Derby winner Harzand, 6-time mile G1 winner Baaeed and many more. In 2021 he was 2nd only to Frankel on Europe's sire list, and he remains near the top.
1283: Fragile and slow to mature, he came good from summer at 5, running well against top dirt horses, and won the March S. at 6. A closer, often with the fastest finish.
1284: A filly with a sharp kick. With just 2 wins and no graded win, she was a fine 4th in the Oka Sho. In the Oaks, without crop aces Daiwa Scarlet and Vodka, she seized her chance, running down favorite Bella Leia by a nose to win. She was 5th in the American Oaks, then 10th in the Shuka Sho without a prep. Struggling in graded races after, she retired after a 10th in the '08 Fuchu Himba S.
1287: Winner of the Fukushima Kinen in 2012 and 2013. No match for the elite in G1s, he was reliably top class in G3s on flat tracks: he won easily as favorite at 5 in 2012 and in record time as 3rd choice at 6 in 2013. He was also 2nd in many G2s and G3s like the All Comers and Nakayama Kinen.
1288: A graded winner from the first crop of Horse of the Year Zenno Rob Roy. Starring at 2, she won the Saffron Sho and was 2nd to Apapane in the Hanshin JF. In spring at 3 she trailed Apapane again in the Oka Sho (8th) and Oaks (4th), but won the Rose S. in autumn. In the Shuka Sho she was 2nd to her nemesis Apapane again. At 4 she was 2nd in the Fuchu Himba S. and 3rd in the Queen S. and Tanabata Sho, fair results in graded races, but from winter at 4 lost her spark, retiring to breed after her 5yo season.
1253: Winning 5 straight in autumn at 4, he took the Tokyo Daishoten, then was 6th for Japan in the Dubai World Cup. He never regained form and moved to local racing at 7.
1256: Debuting at Morioka, he moved to the JRA and was stuck in allowances, but gelded at 5, he won the HTB Sho and October S. and was 2nd in the Kabutoyama Kinen. At 6 he won the Nakayama Kinen and, in autumn, beat Eishin Preston, Telegnosis and others in a blanket finish for the Mile Championship - a 3rd-generation G1 winner after Rudolf and Teio. He pulled up in the next Nakayama Kinen and became a riding horse.
1259: A middle-distance dirt horse who emerged at 5. He won the Tokai S. twice and the Antares S., and was 2nd in the Kawasaki Kinen. After 2 injuries and long breaks, he returned in autumn '04 but retired winless.
1260: He won the Keisei Hai, split T.M. Opera O and Narita Top Road for 2nd in the Satsuki Sho, was 4th in the Derby and won the Kobe Shimbun Hai, but did little after the Kikuka Sho. He tried jumps at 7 and retired at 8.
1263: 3rd in the Spring S., he was crushed in the Satsuki Sho, missed the Derby and switched to dirt. Stalled in allowances, he became consistent once he mastered front-running. At 5 he won the JRA-local Teio Sho, and the next year the Kawasaki Kinen - a race his dam Rosita had won. 4th in the February S., he then won the Diolite Kinen and Oguri Cap Kinen in record time. He retired to stud in '04.
1266: Unstoppable from his debut, he was too late for 2yo races but won the Yayoi Sho over Air Shakur, the Derby favorite. But injury just before the classics forced a long layoff. He went to America, 4th in the G1 Man o' War S. in his 2nd start there, and retired to stud there - the 3rd Sunday Silence son at stud in North America, after Austin Powers and Eishin Masamune. Breeding from '04, he has had no notable runners.
1269: First foal of Tsurumaru Girl, who won the Asahi Challenge C. at 3. Like his dam, a closer dependent on the pace, but expected to be even stronger. He won his debut, then lost 6 straight, missing the classics. Older, he bloomed: 2nd in the Takarazuka Kinen at 4 and 5, and 2nd to Symboli Kris S in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) at 5. At 6 he beat a star-studded field in the Yasuda Kinen with a brilliant charge, his long-sought G1. In autumn he was 4th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) without a prep, and retired after the Arima Kinen to stud.
1281: She won the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu at 5. Racing 32 times until 6, she won 5 open specials against colts like the UHB Hai - a "summer girl" of local meetings. As a dam she produced '94 champion dirt horse Fujino Makken O (91: Bravest Roman).
1285: A blueblood whose brother was 2-time champion sprinter Daiwa Major and half-sister Arima Kinen winner Daiwa Scarlet. She led all the way to win her debut by 9 lengths, then won the Niigata Sansai S. 2nd to T.M. Ocean in the Hanshin Sansai Himba S., she was a classic contender. She won the Anemone S. at 3 and was 2nd choice for the Oka Sho, where she held back instead of racing forward, closing only to 3rd. Her form slumped, and she retired to breed after the '03 Fukushima Minpo Hai. As a dam she produced 2-time Fukushima Kinen winner Daiwa Falcon (07: Jungle Pocket).
1286: A great mare of Kasamatsu, called "the female Oguri" for her toughness and grey coat. Ordinary at first, she shone once Katsumi Ando took over, winning 6 straight, then the Tokai Kikkasho and Zen-Nihon Thoroughbred C. At 4 she was 9th as 2nd choice in Oi's Teio Sho. She retired to breed, producing Miracle Opera (97: Opera House), winner of the '01 Hakusan Daishoten and 3rd in the Japan Cup Dirt.
1290: The 1977 Derby winner. Always in the top three from his debut, he was 2nd in his first graded race, the Keisei Hai, then won the Yayoi Sho over Kane Minobu and Press Tosho, a leading Satsuki Sho contender. There he led and looked the winner, but Hard Barge caught him, 2nd. 4th to Press Tosho in the NHK Hai trial, he was only 9th choice for the Derby. But he raced up front throughout, kicked on in the straight and beat Satsuki Sho winner Hard Barge by a head in a duel for the Derby. Kikuka Sho favorite in autumn, he was 2nd in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, then swallowed by the fast pace in the Kikuka Sho, 15th. Injury kept him out for about 2 years; back, he won only the Sapporo Nikkei Sho at 7 (old age system) and retired. At stud he sired Kisaragi Sho winner Tochino Ruler and steady local dirt runners like Daikatsu Jeanne.
1291: Winning twice, he was 4th in the Satsuki Sho, 2nd in the Kyoto Yonsai Tokubetsu, 12th in the Derby and 11th in the Kikuka Sho - all 3 classics, no results. Older, he won the Hanshin Daishoten and Nikkei Sho, a Tenno Sho (Spring) contender. He was well beaten, 6th, behind Super Creek and Inari One, but 3rd in the race the next year.
1292: Crushed in the Satsuki Sho (13th) and Derby (18th), he was transformed after a break, winning the Kobe Shimbun Hai and Kyoto Shimbun Hai. 2nd choice for the Kikuka Sho, he was 5th on heavy ground, then never won again.
1293: Slow to win until spring at 3, he won a 9-million race in autumn and was 10th in the Kikuka Sho, then won the Hanshin Daishoten and was 4th to crop-mate Dyna Gulliver in the Arima Kinen, proving his staying power.
1294: 14th in the Derby, he won an allowance and the St. Lite Kinen in autumn, then was 17th in the Kikuka Sho. Older, at middle-to-long trips, he raced powerfully forward to win the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. In 3 Tenno Sho (Autumn) runs he was 2nd to Nippo Teio at 4 and 3rd to Tamamo Cross at 5.
1295: Crushed in the classics, he came good at 4, winning the Chunichi Shimbun Hai and Hakodate Kinen, and lost a head duel to Dyna Actress in the Mainichi Okan. 5th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he won the Lord Derby Challenge T. twice and went to stud.
1296: He won the Spring S. and Aoba Sho (OP), but was 11th in the Derby. Improving, he was 3rd in the St. Lite Kinen and 2nd in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, but as 4th choice in the Kikuka Sho he was brought down after contact and put down.
1297: After 2 starts at 2 and a long break, he won 3 straight from a maiden the next August. A neck 2nd in the Aichi Hai, he often fell short, then won the Asahi Challenge C. at 4 and Kokura Kinen at 5.
1298: Winning 3 straight to the Queen C., she was 11th in the Oaks. After an 8th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai and 3rd in the Rose S., she was 7th choice for the Queen Elizabeth Cup, but closed sharply for a narrow 2nd to Mejiro Ramonu.
1299: He won 3 straight from summer at 3, but was 9th in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai and stayed in allowances until 5. After the Ohara S., he was a nose 2nd to Yaeno Muteki in the Naruo Kinen, then won the Asahi Challenge C.
1300: Slow to win at 3, he won the Meguro Kinen at 4, then focused on staying races, winning the Stayers S., and was 4th to Tamamo Cross in the next Tenno Sho (Spring). No more graded wins; best a 2nd going for a repeat in the '88 Stayers S.
1301: He won a maiden and the Daily Hai Sansai S., then as 2nd choice in the Hanshin Sansai S. closed on Katsuragi Haiden but was 4th, 0.4s back. Injured after, this great prospect never returned.
1302: A famed stayer who won the Stayers S. and Diamond S., both over 3000m, 2 years running. Favorite in his first G1, the '89 Tenno Sho (Spring), he was 3rd to Inari One, and retired without a G1.
1303: 4th in the Satsuki Sho, he won the NHK Hai, but injury cost him the Derby and even the Kikuka Sho. He returned the next spring in the Nakayama Kinen and, after about 10 months off, won powerfully. But injured again, he rested over a year; back, he ran twice on dirt, 15th and 14th - his legs no longer fit for turf. He retired to stud, a talent hampered by injury.
1304: He won his debut, the Nojigiku Sho and Daily Hai Sansai S. with overwhelming power, but injury ended his career after 3 starts. That an unbeaten horse with one 2yo graded win went to stud owed much to his appeal as a son of Northern Taste. With many Northern Taste sons at stud, his fee was cheap, but he sired "tragic filly" San Ei Thank You (89: Glory Sakura), drawing notice.
1306: Missing the spring classics, he won the Radio Tampa Sho and the Kyoto Shimbun Hai in autumn, a Kikuka Sho dark horse, but faded in the straight, 6th to Sakura Star O. He ran once more and retired to stud.
1308: Good at middle-distance dirt races but slow to win, an allowance horse until 5. At 6 he ran in the Teio Sho, then dominated by local horses, and became its first JRA winner. He never won a JRA graded race.
1309: He won a debut race and the Kokura Sansai S., then as favorite was 2nd in the Hanshin Sansai S., raising classic hopes. But an accident kept him out of the spring classics. Back after 10 months against older horses, he was crushed in the Swan S. and Mile CS, then 3rd in the CBC Sho. At 4 he won the Hankyu Hai and Centaur S. in a row, seemingly coming good, but then ran poorly and never won again.
1310: She won a debut race, then as 4th choice beat Max Beauty in the Radio Tampa Hai Sansai Himba S., sharing champion 2yo filly with Kosei. Dull in the classics, she found her best on dirt, winning the Heian S. (OP) twice. But dirt racing then wasn't developed enough to focus on, so she raced on turf too, winning the Chunichi Shimbun Hai at 6. Of 7 wins, 3 were on turf, 4 on dirt.
1311: A Symboli Farm-bred owned by Tomohiro Wada, deliberately named without the "Symboli" prefix - a big hope. He won the Spring S. with a fierce kick, then was 3rd as Satsuki Sho favorite and 18th in the Derby. At 4 and 5 he rarely made the top five, and all thought he was finished. In the Keio Hai Autumn H. at 5, Okabe, back aboard after a long gap, sealed away his usual last-to-first charge and raced from a good position. It worked, and he won - a miracle revival. But right after the line he broke down and had to be put down - a sudden tragedy.
1312: At 2 he led all the way to win the Hakodate Sansai S. 7th in the Mainichi Hai at 3, he lost favor, but as an outsider in the Satsuki Sho charged from the back for 2nd to Yaeno Muteki. 18th in the Derby, he was 13th as 2nd choice in the Kikuka Sho. He was 3rd in the Kokura Daishoten and Hakodate Kinen but never won another graded race, just 2 open races.
1313: He won his debut and the Nojigiku Sho but couldn't break through a deep crop; his 3rd win came in a 9-million race in November at 3. The next year he was 2nd in the Kimpai (West) and Kyoto Kinen, then 2nd to Inari One in the Tenno Sho (Spring) as 16th choice of 18, and 3rd in the Takarazuka Kinen. Starring over long trips, he won the Naruo Kinen (G2: 2500m) at 4 and the Diamond S. in his farewell at 7 - a fitting end for a stayer.
1314: He won a debut race by 2.5 lengths, the Wakatake Sho by 5, and the Kyodo News Hai Yonsai S. in record time over later Derby winner Sakura Chiyono O. A classic star, but injury ended his career after that race, and he went to stud.
1315: At 2 she won the Keisei Hai Sansai S. and TV Tokyo Sho Sansai Himba S., champion 2yo filly and a classic favorite, but was 7th in the Oka Sho, 18th in the Oaks and 16th in the Queen Elizabeth Cup. She never won again after 2.
1316: Beaten badly on debut, he won a maiden in April at 3 after a break, a 4-million race in 2 starts, and the Shakunage Sho (9M) as 8th choice. He won the St. Lite Kinen after summer but broke a leg. His comeback was the next Yasuda Kinen: straight into a G1 off the break, he was 12th choice but charged into 2nd. Another leg injury brought a 3rd break; back, he was 7th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and retired.
1317: Brother of stars like Eighty Tosho and Tosho Pegasus, much hoped for, but 2nd on debut, 9 lengths behind Sakkah Boy. After a maiden win he took the Keisei Hai, then was 2nd in the Yayoi Sho and 5th in the Satsuki Sho. Switching to miles, he was 7th to Sakkah Boy in the Mile CS at 3, then won the Christmas S. and the Tokyo Shimbun Hai in February, but after that barely made the top five and never won again.
1319: He won his debut by 7 lengths, tipped as a star. After a setback, he won the NHK Hai (G2: 2000m) by a head, but was 20th in the Derby, never won again and retired at 4. Despite a modest pedigree and record, he went to stud.
1321: He won the Hanshin Sansai S. but injury cost him the classics. Back after a year, in summer at 4 he won the Hakodate Kinen and Mainichi Okan. 17th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he ran tough, placing in 7 graded races, racing until 7.
1322: He won his 3rd start, then was 15th in the Yayoi Sho. Back in his own class he won the Yamazakura Sho, then as 11th choice led all the way to win the NHK Hai (G2: 2000m). 4th in the Derby, he broke a leg in the race and rested long. Back at year's end, he won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai the next year, but was injured again and retired after that year's Takarazuka Kinen - an unlucky talent always hampered by his legs.
1323: A tough supporting player who ran on dirt, turf and over jumps until 8. Often just short, he came good at the Hokkaido meeting in summer at 4: in his 3rd race after dropping to the 5-million class, the Oshima Tokubetsu, he beat none other than Mejiro McQueen, then won the Esan Tokubetsu over 1700m on Hakodate dirt in 1:43.9 - a course record by an astonishing 2.7 seconds. At 6 he won open specials but not graded races, and switched to jumps at 7. At 8 he went back to the flat - never quite finding his path.
1289: From Dandy Route's first crop, he gave his sire his first graded title. In spring at 4 (old age system) he was 2nd in the Keisei Hai and Tokyo Yonsai S., won the Yayoi Sho and was Satsuki Sho favorite, but broke down in the race and rested long. After struggling, he revived to win the Lord Derby Challenge T. at 6 and Meguro Kinen (Spring) at 7, racing until 8. He left few foals, but they included Nuevo Tosho, winner of 5 graded races like the Asahi Challenge C. and Aichi Hai.
1305: Everything on a fierce straight-long charge - fans loved his style. He won the Hakodate Sansai S. and Keisei Hai Sansai S. and was 2nd in the Asahi Hai Sansai S., but finished in double figures in the Satsuki Sho and Derby. Racing mainly at 2000m or less, he often closed too late: four 2nds and eight 3rds. He won the Keio Hai Autumn H. at 4 and the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and Nakayama Kinen at 6.
1318: He needed 10 starts to win a maiden and 13 to leave the 4-million class, but switching to long turf races in September at 3 unlocked his ability. After a 16-million win, he beat Inari One, Sururi O Dyna and others in the Hanshin Daishoten, but was 15th in the Tenno Sho (Spring). He then switched to jumps and won the Kyoto Daishogai (Spring) at 6.
1324: A local-track king, with 6 of 9 wins at Chukyo and Kokura, often by wide margins thanks to a sharp kick. At 5 he won the Kinko Sho and Kita-Kyushu Kinen. At 6 he won the Chukyo Kinen and was 3rd in the Yasuda Kinen, then closed fiercely for 2nd to Let's Go Tarquin in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), part of an upset. At 7 he swept past Sister Tosho, Yamanin Zephyr and others with a 34-second finish to win the Nakayama Kinen.
1325: He won his debut by 3 lengths, then the Kigiku Sho and Daily Hai Sansai S., the top classic favorite - until a fracture was found. Over a year off cost him the classics; his rider Yutaka Take lamented, "We've lost next year's classics." He returned in January at 4 with a bolt still in his leg and won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai and Meguro Kinen. Everyone mourned what might have been had he stayed sound.
1326: A son of great sire Nijinsky. As a foreign-bred he couldn't run in the classics, but won his first graded race, the NZ Trophy Yonsai S. A fracture then cost him a year. Back, he won the December S. (OP), but was 13th in the Arima Kinen and never won again. At stud he sired Surprise Power (94: Shinobu Mochizuri), winner of the '97 Tokyo Derby and Tokyo Okansho and the '99 Nippon TV Hai.
1328: A gifted sprinter who came within a step of the top before his fragile end. Debuting late, in April at 3, he rose quickly, and 6 months later won the Swan S., beating sprint queen Daiichi Ruby in a Japanese record 1:20.6 - a superb win. But as favorite in the Sprinters S., on the verge of the top, he broke down in the race and was put down.
1329: He won the Kyoto Yonsai Tokubetsu with a swoop from behind, was 4th to Tokai Teio in the Derby, and won the Chunichi Sports Sho Yonsai S. easily, then fractured a leg. Back at 4, he hurt a ligament and retired after one race.
1330: A fine miler with G1 talent, kept from his best by repeated leg trouble. A fracture cost him the classics, but back he won the Nakayama Kinen and Keio Hai Spring C., heading to the Yasuda Kinen as the mile leader, where he was below par, 5th. Leg trouble then forced another long break; after 2.5 years he finally returned, a shadow of himself, and retired after one race.
1331: In the shock '92 Takarazuka Kinen he was 3rd behind Mejiro Palmer and Kamino Cresse, then beat strong rivals in the Takamatsunomiya Hai (G2: 2000m). Strong in form, but inconsistent.
1332: Running above his class in the February S., he beat the established stars to win - a new dirt star. Leg trouble then plagued him, and he retired after winning the Tokai S., his first win in 18 months.
1333: Debuting late, in May at 3, he won the Andromeda S. and Winter S. the next winter - his first graded win and a father-son Winter S. double with sire Andrea Mon. Injuries followed, and he moved to local Kaminoyama.
1334: He reached open class only at 6, after 30 races. He then ran mainly in dirt graded races, also trying long turf races, 5th in the Hanshin Daishoten. Truly "stronger with age," he won his first graded race, the Musashino S., at 7. At 6 he was 2nd to Lively Mount in the Breeders' Gold C. and to Admire Bosatsu in the Tokyo Daishoten; at 7, 3rd to Hokuto Vega in the Teio Sho; and at 8 he beat dirt star Kyoto City in the Oguri Cap Kinen - a fixture of dirt racing's transition era, battling its successive kings.
1335: He won the Wakana Sho and Wakagoma S., was 3rd in the Wakaba S., then 2nd to Mihono Bourbon in the Satsuki Sho. He won the NHK Hai (G2: 2000m) and went to the Derby primed, but did nothing, 7th. In autumn he was 10th in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, then injury cost him over a year. Back, he was 14th in the Sirius S. and quietly retired.
1336: He won the Momiji S. and Keisei Hai Sansai S., then met Mihono Bourbon in the Asahi Hai Sansai S. Bourbon was 1.5 favorite, Yamanin Miracle a distant 2nd choice. Against expectations it became one of the closest finishes ever: as Bourbon tried to break clear, Miracle clung on desperately. They hit the line together; Bourbon won by a nose, but it was Miracle's finest hour.
1337: Running above his class, he was crushed in the Kikuka Sho. After a year off, a switch to dirt unlocked his talent: 3 straight wins to open class, then the March S. Big things were expected, but he died young in a training accident.
1338: With a sharp kick he won the Chukyo Sansai S. and Shinzan Kinen, but in the classics was 5th in the Satsuki Sho and 3rd in the Derby. Injured after the Derby, he retired and became a lead pony at Kyoto Racecourse.
1339: At 2 he won 1 of 4, an ordinary 6th in the Icho S. But at 3 he improved rapidly, winning the Hyacinth S. and the Yayoi Sho with speed and a sharp kick. 2nd choice for the Satsuki Sho, he charged into 3rd behind Mihono Bourbon, the leading Kanto hope against strong Kansai horses for the Derby. But he broke a leg in his final workout before the Derby - 2 bolts were needed - and had to retire.
1340: Gifted with speed, he often weakened late when young. At 4 he matured, learning to settle and race from behind. In open class he won the Kinko Sho and Asahi Challenge C. and was 3rd to Yamanin Zephyr in the Tenno Sho (Autumn).
1341: 6 wins from 30, racing until 6. In the JRA-local Breeders' Gold C. he beat stars like Heisei Silver and Laurier Andre for his first graded title. At 4 he set a 1:42.5 record over 1700m on Sapporo dirt.
1342: He won a debut race in January at 3 but stalled, a late-blooming stayer who emerged when older. At 5 he swept past later Tenno Sho winner Sakura Laurel to win the Meguro Kinen. That year he was 3rd behind Rice Shower and Stage Champ in the Tenno Sho (Spring), part of a rare Real Shadai 1-2-3. He won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai at 6 and raced tough until 8.
1343: Despite chronic leg trouble, he lived up to his name with steady results. Spending over half his career resting, he ran just 21 times though racing until 7. Still, he won 10 - surely G1 class at heart. At 7 he won the Kyoto Kinen, his long-sought graded title, and that autumn won the Cassiopeia S. under 60kg. Valued for his talent, he went to stud.
1345: The best son of Tamamo Cross, giving his sire his first graded title. From a slow-maturing family, he steadily built strength in allowances away from the classics, winning the Epsom C. in spring at 4. Then that winter he won the Naruo Kinen and American JCC, for a time the leader of the Kanto older horses. But in 7 G1 tries he never made the top five.
1346: At 3 he was 3rd in the Satsuki Sho, 4th in the Derby, and 3rd against older horses in the Mile CS. Versatile on dirt too, he won the Negishi S. at 3, champion dirt horse that year. Racing mainly at a mile on turf and dirt, incl. JRA-local races, he won 2 graded races on turf and 1 on dirt. He moved to Iwate at 7, winless, then to Arao, racing until 9.
1347: One of Derby winner Dyna Gulliver's best runners. A powerful runner unfazed by soft ground, at 4 he used heavy going to beat Tenno Sho winner Rice Shower in the Nikkei Sho. A middle-to-long distance regular after, he couldn't win, declined with age, and left the JRA at 6. At Kochi he found a new stage, winning 8.
1348: Half-brother of English and Irish Derby winner Generous. With leg trouble he worked steadily through the classes, reaching open class late at 4, but graded wins were hard. In March at 6, he won the Milers C. under rookie Koshiro Take, who had debuted the day before - his first win, and a graded win on just his 2nd day, a record. With Koshiro Take aboard he also won the Centaur S.
1349: Debuting late and needing 7 starts to win, he then rose quickly to open class and won the Kyoto Kimpai easily, then crushed Oaks winner Dance Partner in the Kyoto Kinen. His brother Shin Chest also won the Kyoto Kinen. But he fought his rider in the Tenno Sho (Spring), 15th, then lost form and retired at 6 without another win.
1350: Of his 26 races, he was worse than 3rd choice only 4 times - remarkably well backed, fitting his over-50% top-two rate, though he only became consistent from 5. At 6, his 3 straight graded wins (the Diolite Kinen before unified grading) hinted at a new dirt king, but a long injury break meant he never quite reshaped the field.
1351: Known as dam of Soul Stirring. A French racehorse, she won her first 6, incl. 3 G1s: the Prix Saint-Alary, French Oaks and Prix Vermeille. In the Arc she was 3rd choice but 7th to Sea the Stars. At 4 she won a G3, then the Prix Jean Romanet, her 4th G1, but then stopped winning, and at 5 moved to America. She won her first race there, the Beverly D. S., then the Flower Bowl Invitational S. - 2 straight G1s. 10th in the BC Filly & Mare Turf, she was still Eclipse champion turf female, and retired that year. Bought by the Shadai group, she had her first foal in Britain, then came to Japan in foal to Frankel - that foal became Oaks winner Soul Stirring. She also produced Artemis S. winner Schon Glanz, and her first foal, Southern Stars, became a broodmare in Japan, producing double classic filly Stars on Earth - her family is flourishing in Japan.
1352: Full brother of BC Turf winner Prized, much hoped for. But he was 2nd on debut against 3 other blueblood imports, and slow to get going. His 2nd to Hishi Amazon in the NZ Trophy Yonsai S. sparked a rise worthy of his pedigree, and he beat veterans like Airton Symboli and Stage Champ in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. After a 10th in the Arima Kinen he developed leg trouble and retired, his limits unknown. At stud his runners disappointed; exported to Korea, he died in an accident in transit.
1353: His first win came late at 4, but he made up for lost time, rising quickly to open class. He raced eagerly in JRA-local races, winning the Breeders' Gold C. twice among other successes.
1354: Steady in Hokkaido racing, he moved to Oi at 3. 2nd in the Keihin Hai and Haneda Hai, he won the Tokyo Derby from a good position and was 2nd to Furioso in the Japan Dirt Derby.
1355: After winning his 2nd start, he was 2nd in 3 straight graded/open races, then won the Kyodo News Hai Yonsai S. by 3 lengths from Tayasu Tsuyoshi and the Spring S., Satsuki Sho favorite. Scratched lame in his right shoulder, his luck turned: straight into the Derby he was 11th. In autumn he won the Kyoto Shimbun Hai trial but was 7th in the Kikuka Sho. Still short on big days, he moved to local Funabashi.
1356: Winless in 3 on turf, he won 7 on dirt: the Antares S. at 4, then the JRA-local Sakitama Hai and Kurofune Sho easily as favorite. Outclassed in deep dirt G1s, his best was 5th in the Nambu Hai.
1357: At 2 he was 3rd to Fuji Kiseki and Ski Captain in the Asahi Hai Sansai S., then used his speed in sprints, winning the Crystal C. at 3. Short of class in older graded races (best 3rd in the CBC Sho), he ran well on flat local tracks, winning the Marine S. and Seikan S. at 4 and running two close 2nds at 6. Never top class, he raced steadily until 7 - a popular supporting player.
1358: By Shin Chest out of Shin Miss Brown - the culmination of the "Shin" prefix. He won 2 graded races, the Asahi Challenge C. and Chunichi Shimbun Hai, at middle distances on turf. 8 wins from 27 but never 2nd - win or lose, nothing in between. After 4 straight double-figure finishes from late 7 to the Kyoto Kimpai at 8, he tried jumps, but broke down in his first race and was put down.
1359: He won his first 3, incl. the Shinzan Kinen, but was last in the Derby. In autumn at 3 he was 2nd in the Mile CS, setting up a huge payout - a one-off fluke, as he never made the top five again.
1360: With just 1 win, a 2nd in the Anemone S. got her into the Oka Sho. Favorite was Kasamatsu's Raiden Reader, in a strong field, but from 8th at the final turn she unleashed a fierce kick to beat Dance Partner. 3rd in the Oaks proved it no fluke. But she slumped in autumn, 16th in the Queen Elizabeth Cup, and in her comeback race, the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu at 4, she fractured a leg and was put down.
1361: With 2 wins from 3, he was narrowly 2nd to Bubble Gum Fellow in the Asahi Hai Sansai S. and 8th in the NHK Mile C. He then won the Bodaiju S. and Sekiya Kinen, and the next year's Sekiya Kinen with a 33.7 finish.
1362: Despite injuries he ran steadily at a mile to middle distances, finally winning a graded race, the Tokyo Shimbun Hai, in his 23rd start. At 7 he won the Sapporo Kinen and Fuji S., but never won again.
1363: 4 wins from 26, the Epsom C. his best, but with eight 2nds he was known for consistency. He never won a G1, but had near misses, above all the NHK Mile C., reborn that year as the spring 3yo mile championship: 2nd choice behind Fabulous la Fouine, he closed fastest in 34.7 but fell 3/4 of a length short. His half-brother Yeats (01: Sadler's Wells) was Europe's champion stayer 4 years running.
1364: A sharp miler. He won the Lord Derby Challenge T. at 4, was 10th in the Yasuda Kinen, then 3rd in the Swan S. and 4th in the Mile CS. At 5 he ran down front-running Eishin Berlin to win the Swan S.
1307: A speedster who held the Hakodate 1200m record until One Carat broke it in 2010. She won her debut at 3 as 9th choice, but injury delayed her return to autumn. After a 4-million win she went straight to the Queen Elizabeth Cup, beaten badly, then kept adding wins, ridden by top jockeys like Yutaka Take and Katsumi Minai. Racing until 7, she won 2 G2s, the Swan S. and Keio Hai Spring C., and ran well in the Asahi Challenge C. and Takamatsunomiya Hai (G2: 2000m) - more than a sprinter.
1320: 2nd as 5th choice in the Kyodo News Hai, he won the Yayoi Sho on muddy ground. 2nd in the Kikuka Sho, he retired with leg trouble.
1327: He won a debut race and 3 straight, incl. the Wakakusa S. by 2.5 lengths. 5th choice for the Derby without graded experience, he was 11th. After a 4th in the Chunichi Sports Sho Yonsai S. and a win in the Seaside S., he was 3rd in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai and 4th in the Kikuka Sho. He won the next Nikkei Shinshun Hai over Mejiro Ardan, but broke down in the Osaka Hai and was put down.
1344: He won his debut in February at 3, then the Mainichi Hai in his 2nd start. 4th choice in the Satsuki Sho, he was 3rd, ahead of Winning Ticket. 14th in the Derby, he rested with leg trouble and retired after just 6 starts.
1365: Winless in 5 on turf, he found his way in dirt sprints, winning 4 straight at 3-4 incl. the Negishi S. and Garnet S., then a neck 2nd in the February S. He kept shining in JRA-local races.
1367: A late-maturing stayer who reached open class at 5. He won the Diamond S. (then 3200m) twice, and won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai from last with a stunning 33.8 finish.
1368: His fierce temper cost him wins, so he was gelded at 3. At 5 he won the Hakodate Sprint S. as favorite. Until an injury at 6 he had 9 wins and ten 2nds from 31 - very consistent - but after his return he lost his shine.
1369: Maturing at 5, he mastered fast front-running, winning 3 straight up to the Niigata Daishoten. At 6 he won the Nakayama Kimpai and Osaka Hai, and at 8 the Niigata Daishoten again - 4 graded wins from the front.
1370: Lacking a finishing punch, he often just lost, but kept adding wins and reached open class at 5. A graded regular, he won the Meguro Kinen and Fukushima Kinen, placed in others and raced until 10.
1371: A speedy middle-distance horse who set a Japanese 2000m turf record of 1:57.5 in the Australia T. Hot-tempered, he was demoted for veering in his 2nd start and injured jockey Mikio Matsunaga by acting up in training. At 3 he won the Shinzan Kinen and was 3rd to Taiki Fortune in the NHK Mile C. He won the Kinko Sho at 4, then slumped, running poorly in the Naruo Kinen, Takarazuka Kinen and Kyoto Daishoten, and retired. Prized for his pedigree and speed at stud, he sired no good runners.
1372: Half-brother of 4-time US G1 winner Thunder Gulch. He won 9 on dirt. In the Unicorn S. he crossed the line first but was demoted to 10th. At 4 he won the Procyon S. and Kashiwa Kinen, adding 2 more graded wins later.
1373: Winner of 14 G1s, a European record, and the BC Mile 3 years running. Beaten by later French fillies' Triple Crown winner Zarkava in the French 1000 Guineas and Oaks, she then focused on miles, winning the Prix Rothschild, Prix du Moulin and more. At 3 she won the BC Mile in America; at 4 she won the Jacques le Marois by 6 lengths and the BC Mile again. At 5 she won 5 G1s incl. a 3rd BC Mile, Cartier Horse of the Year. Racing on at 6, she won the Prix d'Ispahan and Prix Rothschild for her 14th G1, but going for an unprecedented 4th BC Mile was 3rd to Court Vision, and retired. 17 wins from 27; jockey Olivier Peslier, her rider throughout, named her among the best he ever rode. Of her 6 foals, Terrakova won the French G3 Prix Cleopatre.
1374: Unable to win on dirt early, he shone after switching to turf at a mile to middle distances. 3rd in the Mile CS at 3, he won the Sirius S. on dirt, and the Chukyo Kinen on turf at 4.
1375: 2nd to Mejiro Bright in the Radio Tampa Hai Sansai S., he won the Arlington C., then was 2nd in the NZ Trophy Yonsai S. and NHK Mile C. Winless after, he switched to jumps at 6, winning 4 open races.
1376: A foreign-bred sprinter on turf or dirt. He won the Crystal C. at 3, but was crushed in the NZ Trophy Yonsai S. and NHK Mile C., so dirt came into view. He won the Negishi S. in autumn and was 3rd to Taiki Shuttle in the Sprinters S. on turf - top-class speed. The next year he won the Negishi S. again and was 2nd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, racing until 8 with 7 wins from 38.
1377: Always closing in 34 seconds, he relied entirely on his late charge. Under 400kg at his debut, he ran in all 3 classics without success. But after the Kikuka Sho he came from 10th at the final turn to beat older horses in the Keihan Hai, and the next year from 15th with a 34.6 finish in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai. He fractured a leg in the race, then died suddenly of a twisted intestine while resting - still mourned.
1378: He moved from local Niigata to the JRA at 3 and, still in the 9-million class, was 2nd in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. At 5 he won the JRA-local Gumma Kinen, then switched to dirt and won 4 straight JRA-local races from the Saga Kinen.
1379: A stayer with abundant stamina. Inconsistent at 3, he added wins steadily from 4, won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai at 5, and the next Nikkei Shinshun Hai by half a length from later G1 winner Meisho Doto.
1380: A late-blooming dirt horse who won the Tokai Winter S. at the end of 4, then the Hakusan Daishoten and Tokai Kikkasho at 5. Despite leg trouble, he won 8 with his late charge.
1381: Coming good in summer at 3, he won 5 straight incl. the Kyoto Kimpai and Kyoto Kinen, then the Hong Kong International C. After winning the next Kinko Sho, he faded fast.
1382: In the Yayoi Sho, Yutaka Take moved early and he led at the final turn to win easily, putting minor sire Running Free in the spotlight. Injuries followed, and at 6 he moved to Kawasaki, winless in 8.
1383: A dirt horse who shone in JRA-local races: 4 JRA races and 8 local ones after reaching open class. He won Asahikawa's Grand Chariot C. and Morioka's Derby Grand Prix, and was 2nd in the Kawasaki Kinen and Diolite Kinen.
1384: Crushed in the Yayoi Sho and NZ Trophy, he switched to dirt and won the Hokkaido Sprint C. at once, then the Super Dirt Derby, Nagoya Daishoten and Kakitsubata Kinen - 4 JRA-local graded wins.
1385: Owned by TV star Kinichi Hagimoto. Missing the classics, he starred on middle-distance turf, mainly at local tracks, leading all the way in the Kokura Kinen at 5. He won once over jumps at 8.
1386: A late-blooming middle-distance horse who came good at 4. In his first graded race, the Naruo Kinen, he beat Air Groove by 3 lengths. He was 3rd in the Asahi Challenge C., Mainichi Okan and Tenno Sho (Autumn) but never won again.
1387: Debuting late, in March at 3, he won 4 straight to the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. Older, injuries plagued him; 5 wins, two 2nds and two 3rds from 9, he retired unexposed. At stud until '05, he sired no stars.
1388: As a son of Oaks winner Adorable he drew notice early, and was 4th to Seiun Sky in the Satsuki Sho. He beat older horses in the Cassiopeia S. and was 3rd in the Kikuka Sho. The next year, 2nd in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai, he won the Kyoto Kinen, but was injured and rested about 2 years. Back at 6, past his best, he moved to local Funabashi.
1389: Running well but slow to win, he reached open class at 5. He won the Musashino S. in autumn, then was 2nd in the Japan Cup Dirt despite the trip. Winless after, he livened up dirt racing.
1390: Close but winless on dirt early, he blossomed on turf. He won the Hakodate Kinen at 4, the Nakayama Kimpai and Kokura Daishoten at 5, and was a close 3rd to T.M. Opera O and Meisho Doto in the Takarazuka Kinen.
1391: After winning the Antares S. at 5 he slumped, but won it again the next year by 6 lengths, then the Heian S. at 7 and 8 - 4 straight years of graded wins over 1800m at Kyoto. A true specialist.
1392: Needing 8 starts to win, he grew fast when older: the Kokura Daishoten by a neck, 2nd in the Kinko Sho, then the Naruo Kinen. Racing in long graded races until 8, he was 2nd in the Kyoto Daishoten and Stayers S.
1393: Brother of great Kasamatsu mare Max Fleet, he showed power on dirt. A neck 2nd in the Tokai Kikkasho, he beat later G1 winner Wing Arrow in the Derby Grand Prix, top dirt horse of his crop. 4th in the Kawasaki Kinen, he won the Oguri Cap Kinen by 1.5 lengths. He kept trying dirt graded races without winning, moved to Hokkaido at 8, then Arao, and ran his last race in March '06, aged 11.
1394: He won the Daily Hai Sansai S. and was 6th in the Satsuki Sho, but in the Derby charged to 2nd behind Special Week as 14th choice. 2nd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai and 7th in the Kikuka Sho, he retired with a tendon injury the next year.
1395: He won the St. Lite Kinen after a 5-million win. 9th in the Kikuka Sho, he struggled, but at 5, as second-last choice, beat Stay Gold, Meisho Doto, Grass Wonder and others in the Nikkei Sho - 19,390 yen to win, a huge upset.
1396: Full sister of '06 Takamatsunomiya Kinen winner Ore wa Matteruze. After the Sweet Pea S. she was crushed in the Oaks, 4th in the Shuka Sho, then won the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu, and the Milers C. the next year - a superb miler. She died in a fire at pasture at 5.
1397: A speedy sprinter. He won his debut, the Kurotake Sho and Nanohana S., then the Crystal C. by 5 lengths. 2nd choice in the NHK Mile C., he faded to 15th, then won the Chunichi Sports Sho Yonsai S. Winless in graded races after, he moved to Iwate at 7 and raced until 13.
1398: A late bloomer who won the All Comers at 6 in his 36th start. As half-brother of Manhattan Cafe (98: Sunday Silence), he went to stud, later standing in Korea, and died in autumn 2011.
1399: He won 2 graded races at 3, the Kobe Shimbun Hai and Aichi Hai, then lost badly and switched to jumps, winning the Tokyo High Jump and Hanshin Spring Jump with his speed - a fine jumper.
1400: Unbeaten in 2 to the Niigata Sansai S., he won the Spring S. too, but was 7th in the Satsuki Sho and 15th in the Derby. Winless after, he tried jumps, then local racing.
1401: Winless on turf, he won 5 dirt sprints. Highly talented, but several serious injuries limited his graded wins to the Negishi S. at 4.
1402: Unsuccessful on turf, he switched to dirt in his 9th start and won 7 straight to the March S., then 3 JRA-local races: Hakusan Daishoten, Sakuranbo Kinen and Kashiwa Kinen.
1403: He won a debut race, the Yurikamome Sho, Mainichi Hai and Kyoto Yonsai Tokubetsu - 4 straight, 2 graded. After leg trouble he ran poorly, left the JRA at 6 for Nagoya, and never won again.
1366: Half-brother of fillies' Triple Crown winner Still in Love. A bold front-runner, he won the Hosenka Sho by 6 lengths and led all the way in the Radio Tampa Sho. In the Kobe Shimbun Hai he led but broke down in the straight, 5th, and retired.
1404: His dam was a Japan Cup runner-up. His temper kept him winless at 3; gelded, he first won in a JRA-local dirt race at Morioka. Back on turf he blossomed, winning the Sekiya Kinen at 5. The next year he won the NST Open in a Japanese 1400m record, then the Sekiya Kinen and Mainichi Okan. He won the next American JCC, but injury cost him 6 months; after his return he did little and retired after a training injury.
1405: Highly rated before his debut, he underperformed at 2-3, graded-winless. Maturing at 4, he won the American JCC and Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. Most of his good graded runs came at 2200m+ - a stayer at heart.
1406: A very late bloomer, he reached open class at 6, then beat local star Mitsuaki Silence by 3 lengths in the Oguri Cap Kinen and won the Breeders' Gold C. by 9. He then slumped badly and retired at 8.
1407: After 3 dirt wins he tried the classics, was beaten badly, and returned to dirt, winning the Nagoya Yushun and the Derby Grand Prix, a G1. Injury-prone after, he switched to jumps at 7.
1408: Needing 6 starts to win, he won 2 open races and within 2 months was 6th choice for the Derby, a fine 5th. After a break he won the St. Lite Kinen, but was 14th in the Kikuka Sho. Injured, he ran poorly and retired to stud, siring Saga Kinen winner Chance Torai (Hyogo) and Kanto Oaks winner Asuka Libre (Funabashi).
1409: Perhaps from broodmare sire Real Shadai, he had stamina to burn. He won the 2400m Aoba Sho, was 7th in the Derby and Kikuka Sho, then in December's Stayers S. beat T.M. Opera O, who had come to win. He stood at stud in New Zealand, siring graded winners.
1410: Hot-tempered, he finished last in his first 2 races and was gelded at 2. He improved, but as a stayer had few races to choose from and rose slowly. At 4 he beat crop-mate Narita Top Road in the Stayers S., then won the next Meguro Kinen by 3.5 lengths and was 3rd in the Takarazuka Kinen. He tried the Dubai Sheema Classic (7th), won the Stayers S. again at 6 and raced until 8.
1411: Based in Hokkaido. Not dominant but very consistent, he won the JRA-local Breeders' Gold C. at 4.
1412: He won his debut and the Niigata Sansai S., then struggled, doing little in the classics. After the Kikuka Sho he beat older horses in the Keihan Hai, his first win since the Niigata race. Older, he starred at middle distances, often closing too late for 2nd or 3rd, but won the Kokura Kinen at 5, the All Comers in record time at 6 and the Kokura Kinen again at 7 - 5 of his 6 wins graded races. At stud he had few stars, but his last crop produced Crown Rose, who won her debut as 10th choice and the Fairy S. as 10th choice too - surely stunning even Rosado's fans.
1413: Steady from his debut, he bloomed once he tried JRA-local races when older: from the Kurofune Sho at 6 he won 6 straight dirt graded races, JRA and local. After a 2nd in the Tokyo Hai, he won the JBC Sprint, his long-sought G1, and retired. At stud, true to type, he sired many dirt sprinters like Toho Dolce, Love Me Chan and Namura Titan.
1415: In the Radio Tampa Sho he closed sharply from a hopeless 12th at the final turn for a neck 2nd. A graded win seemed a matter of time, but he slumped, finally winning the Epsom C. at 5.
1416: Outclassed in the Oka Sho, she then focused on sprints, running well in graded and open races until she won the '08 Ibis Summer Dash, then the Centaur S. She was 7th in the Sprinters S. In '09, after a big loss in the CBC Sho, she won the Ibis Summer Dash again and ran well in the Kita-Kyushu Kinen and Centaur S., winning the Summer Sprint Series a 2nd time. 3rd in the Sprinters S., she broke down going for a 3rd Ibis Summer Dash and was put down.
1417: Raced only on dirt, he was stuck in the lower classes. Then at 6 he won his first turf race, and next the Lord Derby Challenge T. He raced until 9 without another win.
1418: Debuting in February at 3, he won his 3rd start and 4 straight to open class. 2nd in the Osaka Hai, he won the Hakodate Kinen at 5, then injury cost him 2 years 8 months; back, he was always beaten badly.
1419: In his first graded race, the Kobe Shimbun Hai, he beat Satsuki Sho winner Air Shakur and Derby winner Agnes Flight - a summer improver in the spotlight. A tendon injury then ended his career before he could show his talent. At stud his best was open-class Dream Flight, 3rd in the Diamond S.
1422: Debuting late, in April at 3, he missed the classics entirely. A typical late-blooming stayer, he improved as an older horse and beat Tap Dance City in the Nikkei Sho in spring at 5. A fine supporting player at middle-to-long trips, he won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai at 6. He switched to jumps in autumn '04, won once, returned to the flat in '05 and was 17th in the Tenno Sho (Spring). He later served as a lead pony at Hanshin Racecourse.
1423: 4th in the Satsuki Sho, 6th in the Derby and 8th in the Kikuka Sho, he then switched to miles and shone: he won the Keihan Hai, was 2nd in the Nakayama Kinen and won the Milers C. in a record 1:32.8. He won the Epsom C. at 5, but leg trouble forced a long break; back after 16 months, he had declined and never won again. Fast, but held back by temper and fragility.
1424: Half-brother of Tokai Teio. At 4, still in allowances, he was 2nd in the Kokura Kinen and 4th in the Asahi Challenge C., then won the Hiei S. and the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. All his wins came at 2000-2500m.
1426: 3rd to Air Shakur in the Kikuka Sho, he showed great staying power, and at 4 won the Doncaster S. and Stayers S., both over 3000m, easily. But in G1s he fell short, beaten badly in 2 Tenno Sho (Spring) tries.
1427: Maturing late at 3, he rose quickly from the 5-million class to open. 5th in his first graded race, the Kyoto Kinen, he beat T.M. Opera O in the Osaka Hai. He won just once more and moved to Iwate at 6.
