1428: Leg trouble cost him the classics, but at 4, running above his class, he won the American JCC, proving his potential. 2nd in the Diamond S., he then slumped and raced until 7 without another win.
1429: His half-brothers Yamanin Miracle and Yamanin Ability were graded winners, so hopes were high. Leg trouble at 4 cost him over a year, but back he won the Hakodate Kinen.
1430: Unbeaten in 5 up to the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun, she was local racing's 2009 Horse of the Year - the first 2yo ever. At 3 she aimed for the JRA's Oka Sho, but was 12th on turf in the Fillies' Revue and returned to dirt. Winning steadily every year, at 5 she beat strong JRA horses in the Tokyo Hai, and at 6 in 2013 finished with 4 straight wins incl. the Tokyo Sprint and Cluster C.
1432: Half-brother of Daitaku Riva, 2nd in the Satsuki Sho and Mile CS. Unlike his speedy brother, by Kikuka Sho winner Dance in the Dark he was a pure stayer. Over 3000m+ he had 3 wins, a 2nd and two 3rds from 6, winning the Hanshin Daishoten and Stayers S. He was 4th in the '04 Arima Kinen, but ran poorly in 2 more starts.
1433: Never consistent, he thrilled fans with rare, brilliant sweeps around the 3rd turn. The perfect example: the '01 Derby Grand Prix. Off poor runs, he was 9th choice of 14, the least fancied JRA horse, but as if stung, he swept to the lead past the 3rd turn and ran away in the straight, winning by 9 lengths for his first title.
1434: A familiar supporting player in sprints. At 3 he won the CBC Sho, coming from the back off a fast pace to sweep past strong older horses. Older, his form was erratic and his kick often dulled, but two G1 3rds proved his class, and longshot punters loved him. He moved to local racing at the end of '08 and retired at 12.
1435: He won the Cyclamen S. at the end of 2, then the Crystal C. as 13th choice. 3rd in the Japan Dirt Derby, he switched to dirt and was 2nd in the Thoroughbred Challenge C. and Derby Grand Prix, drawing notice. Then an accident sidelined him; back after about 6 months, he never got back on track and won just once more.
1437: Real Shadai's last great stayer. Improving from summer at 4, he won 2 10-million specials in autumn, then ran above his class in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai, beating Tap Dance City and graded regulars with a performance far beyond an allowance horse. The next year he closed to half a length of Hishi Miracle in the Tenno Sho (Spring). Frustrating runs followed, and in the '06 Kokura Daishoten he dislocated a joint and was put down.
1438: A slow maturer who came good when older. He won the Milers C. in spring at 4 and was 3rd in the Yasuda Kinen against strong rivals. After about a year off, he won the Kita-Kyushu Kinen and Fuji S. Retired to stud, he was later exported to France.
1439: Unbeaten in 4 to the Spring S. Fans looked forward to an "Agnes showdown" in the Satsuki Sho with Agnes Tachyon, unbeaten in 3 to the Yayoi Sho, but injury just before the race made it a dream. Back after 6 months in the Kobe Shimbun Hai he was 8th, far from his best, then 8th in the Kikuka Sho. No longer the elite colt, he retired winless after 3 comeback starts.
1440: He chased favorite Agnes Gold for 2nd in the Spring S., then was 4th in the Satsuki Sho and 12th in the Derby. Improving in autumn, he won the St. Lite Kinen, but a stone bruise ruled out the Kikuka Sho. Back in the Arima Kinen (7th), he then had a long break with leg trouble. Never the same, he left the JRA after 3 starts for Southern Kanto, where after another year off he retired.
1441: With 1 win, he beat Daitaku Bertram, Millennium Bio and others in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai. 6th in the Derby and 9th in the Kikuka Sho, he then won the Keihan Hai. Older, he ran well but just couldn't win. Thought retired at the end of 6, he returned at local Kanazawa in '06 and won twice.
1442: Named "Born King" in hope, he was 5th to Agnes Tachyon on debut. He won the Keisei Hai at 3, was 2nd to Agnes Tachyon again in the Yayoi Sho, then 16th in the Satsuki Sho. Winless after, he rested long after the '02 Tenno Sho (Spring). He returned in June '05 after 3 years 2 months, but retired without a win.
1443: From local Oi, he was 3rd in the Japan Dirt Derby, 5th in the Teio Sho and 3rd in the JBC Classic there, then won the Teio Sho after moving to the JRA. He ran in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) on turf without success, then focused on dirt, winning the Kashiwa Kinen and more at the top level. Back at Oi at 8 in 2010, he placed in the Teio Sho 4 years running, a long-lasting partnership with jockey Fumio Matoba. He retired after the 2012 Tokyo Daishoten, sharing a retirement ceremony with Furioso, and became a lead pony at Oi.
1444: Fragile, and hurt below the hock as a foal, he debuted in a maiden in September at 3. Winning, he kept adding wins and, in his first graded race, the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai in autumn at 4, closed sharply for 2nd to Screen Hero, later Japan Cup winner. Racing only in graded races after, at 6 he won the Tenno Sho (Spring), his first graded win a G1. He was 4th in the Japan Cup and Hong Kong Vase. At 7, 4th as 2nd choice in the Kyoto Daishoten after a year off and 9th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he was thought past it, down to 14th choice in the Japan Cup, but closed in 34.0 for 3rd, stunning everyone. Steady in long races - 5th in the Hanshin Daishoten, 4th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) - he was 10th in the Japan Cup. "At 8, this must be it," people thought, but in his 4th Hong Kong Vase he ran on strongly for a close 2nd, surprising everyone again.
1414: Coming good in summer at 4, he won the Kokura Kinen and Asahi Challenge C., and the Kinko Sho the next year, then plateaued. In his 34th start, his first dirt race in a while, he broke down and was put down.
1420: Debuting late, he won a maiden in August at 3. 2nd in the Tokai S. at 4, he raced at local tracks, winning the Mercury C. and Hakusan Daishoten, and was 3rd in the Japan Cup Dirt. After an injury break he was 2nd to Kanetsu Fleuve in the Teio Sho, then rested again. In his next comeback, the Heian S., he broke down and was put down - Kronos City and Monopolizer were also injured in that race.
1421: By double classic winner Vega, full brother of Derby winner Admire Vega. Leg trouble delayed his debut to summer at 3. He won it, was 2nd in the Shiretoko Tokubetsu, then ran above his class to win the St. Lite Kinen from midfield - a graded winner in 3 starts. He was 5th in the Arima Kinen and Tenno Sho (Spring) and 6th in the Takarazuka Kinen, but leg trouble forced his retirement. With sound legs he could have matched his brother. At stud he sired dirt runners Admire Subaru (3rd, Japan Cup Dirt) and Kurino Star O (3 dirt graded wins), and Mainichi Hai winner Iron Look.
1425: Full brother of double classic winner Vega. Fragile and often below par, in his first graded race, the Kyoto Kinen at 4, he beat Agnes Flight and Narita Top Road. He ran well in the Tenno Sho (Spring), but still fragile, retired early to stud.
1431: His explosive late kick drew notice early. Running above his class, he was 2nd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai. Older, he won the Osakajo S., then swept past double classic winner Air Shakur in the Osaka Hai. 5th and 3rd in the spring and autumn Tenno Sho, he seemed to be coming good, but injury sidelined him. Back after a year for 2 races, he rested long again, but returning in '05 he won the Osaka Hai and Mainichi Okan.
1436: A Bubble Gum Fellow filly based at Monbetsu. Debuting in May at 2 over 1200m on dirt, she won 3 straight. 9th in the JRA's Lavender Sho, she then had a win and two 2nds, and in the JRA-local Edelweiss Sho, ridden for the first time by Yutaka Take, she won. Moving to Kawasaki, she was 2nd in the Tokyo 2yo Yushun Himba.
1445: A slow developer, he missed the classics, but emerged gradually as an older horse, winning the Fuji S. in autumn at 4. He broke down in the '03 Kyoto Kimpai and, after long treatment, retired to stud.
1446: In 2001, when foreign-breds were first allowed in the Derby (with conditions), he led all the way in the Aoba Sho trial to be the first one in. Fellow import Kurofune also ran: Kurofune was 5th, Ruzel 14th. Injury then forced a long break; back in early '04 after 2 years 8 months, he was a shadow of himself and retired after 3 races.
1447: He won his first 2 incl. the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S., showing great potential, but repeated setbacks slowed his rise. Unlike his early-peaking sister Hornet Pierce, he kept improving, his ability only growing as an older horse. Back from 10 months off in autumn at 5, he won the Fuji S. After poor runs in sprint graded races, as 4th choice in the '05 Takamatsunomiya Kinen he beat Precious Cafe, Calstone Light O and others for a G1. Called a fluke, he proved his class with a 3rd in the Sprinters S. that autumn. At stud he sired 2013 Negishi S. winner Meisho Mashu, Admire Cosmos, who won the Fukushima Kinen on a streak after returning from local racing, and Niigata 2yo S. winner Monstre.
1448: He won the Niigata 2yo S. by 5 lengths, was a close 4th to Admire Don in the Asahi Hai FS, then won a fiery duel with Roman Empire in the Yayoi Sho. In the classics, G1s proved a bit beyond him: 8th in the Satsuki Sho, 7th in the Derby, 5th in the Kikuka Sho. A comeback was expected when older, but after a record win in the Mainichi Okan in autumn at 4, he kept just falling short. He was still strong in middle-distance graded races, winning the Nakayama Kinen in '05 and '06 and the All Comers, but was injured training for the '06 Tenno Sho (Autumn) and could not race again.
1449: In the Daily Hai 2yo S. at 2, he came from last at the final turn and passed 15 horses in the straight alone, drawing notice with that crazy kick. Then he couldn't use his finish, beaten without a show in the spring classics. But in the Kikuka Sho, written off, he charged into 2nd behind Hishi Miracle, setting up a 90,000-yen quinella. He also charged into 2nd in the Sapporo Kinen as 12th choice and the Kyoto Daishoten as 7th choice - occasional big runs amid poor ones, "the ultimate erratic horse." Favorite just once in 55 races ('03 Stayers S.), he was 10th; of his 6 wins, only his first came when among the first 3 choices.
1450: He won the Radio Tampa Hai 2yo S. at 2, then was 5th in the Satsuki Sho, 4th in the Derby and 3rd in the Kikuka Sho, but suffered a tendon injury. Back at the end of '04 after 26 months, he won the next Chukyo Kinen, then retired with another tendon injury.
1451: Debuting in Hokkaido racing, he won the JRA-local Clover Sho and Sapporo 2yo S. Moving to Kazuo Fujisawa's Miho stable, he was 2nd to Admire Don in the Asahi Hai FS. At 3 he ran in all 3 classics without much success, and grew inconsistent. He won the April S. in spring at 5, his first win in 2.5 years, then struggled again, moving to Saga in '06.
1452: He won the Falcon S. at 3, then the Hakodate Sprint S. powerfully against strong older horses, and the CBC Sho at year's end - clearly superior in sprints. At 4 he was narrowly 2nd to Believe in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, then won it the next year, holding off Durandal by a neck for his long-sought G1 - top of the sprint division.
1453: A long break at 3 cost him the classics, but he came good at 4, winning the Mutsuki Sho and Asuka S. to reach open class, then led all the way in the Chukyo Kinen, and beat G1 regulars Hishi Miracle and Tsurumaru Boy in the Osaka Hai - 4 straight. 8th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he rested long, and after just 4 races back was sidelined again; when he returned, his old power was gone.
1454: Inconsistent at 3 and outclassed in graded races, he was transformed when older: he won the Diamond S. and Nikkei Sho, plus 2 JRA-local dirt graded races - good on any surface. At 5 he led boldly in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and won by 7 lengths, showing his stamina, then tried England's marathon Gold C., running poorly. Back home a tendon injury disrupted him, and he retired after 5 winless races.
1456: He won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai at 4, but injury struck just as more was expected. After 18 months of treatment he returned in summer at 5, a shadow of himself, and retired after 2 races.
1457: Talented, with 5 graded wins incl. the Kyoto Kinen, but so inconsistent that his good runs were very hard to predict. After the '04 Milers C. he kept losing badly, then shockingly won the '05 Hanshin Daishoten, a trip thought too long. He then raced in the main middle-to-long distance races without spark and retired injured at 8, becoming a lead pony at Kyoto.
1458: Winless in the JRA, he moved to local Nagoya and bloomed, winning 16 in about a year. Falling short at 5, he won the JRA-local Summer Champion, then raced long and well at tracks all over Japan.
1459: He won the NZ Trophy at 3 and was 2nd in the NHK Mile C. Clearly a talented sprinter, but with very fragile legs: 4 long breaks. Racing on in '07 hoping for a chance, he retired after a 17th in the Aurora C.
1462: He ran well in 2yo graded races but poorly in the trials, so skipped the classics for the NHK Mile C., a fine 3rd. Racing mainly at a mile, he won the Lord Derby Challenge T. at 4 and the Keisei Hai Autumn H. that autumn, a solid miler. He retired after the New Year S. at 7 and in '09 began a new career as a lead pony at Nakayama.
1464: Inconsistent, he slowly added wins and reached open class only in June at 5. He was then 3rd in the JRA-local Mercury C. and won the Musashino S. In his first G1, the Japan Cup Dirt, he was 13th, then plateaued, moving to Kasamatsu after the Tokai S. at 8.
1465: He raced in Southern Kanto local racing until 11, winning the 2007 JBC Sprint and 2008 Tokyo Hai. Debuting at Kasamatsu, he moved to Oi at 3. At 4 he won 7 straight of 8, and at 5 beat top JRA horses in the JBC Sprint. Racing on until 11, he won steadily every year.
1466: He won 2 10-million races, the Kirinzan Tokubetsu and Auckland RTC, then the Sirius S. - a new middle-distance dirt star. In his first G1, the Japan Cup Dirt, he was 2nd choice but 6th.
1467: She won a maiden easily, was 2nd in the Rindo Sho, then won the Fantasy S. from up front, a leading Hanshin JF fancy, but was 4th behind Tall Poppy and others - unable to avenge her dam's 2nd in the Hanshin Sansai Himba S. 3rd in the Tulip Sho at 3, she was 12th as 3rd choice in the Oka Sho. 5th as 11th choice in the Oaks, she was then 4th in the Rose S. and 9th in the Shuka Sho, lacking a finish. In '09 she won after dropping in class, but broke down in October's Dotonbori S. and was put down.
1468: A classic hope, he fractured his right hind hock at 3 and rested long. Back after 18 months, 40kg heavier, he still won, showing his class. In autumn, running above his class, he was 2nd choice in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai and beat Tokai Trick and other graded winners. At 5, heavy, he was 4th in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai, but after a break beat Pop Rock, Eye Popper and others in the Hanshin Daishoten. In the Tenno Sho (Spring) he missed the break, but won a historic straight duel with Meisho Samson for his first G1. An Arc plan was announced, but a stone bruise in training ended it. A comeback was awaited in autumn, but he was 9th as 2nd choice in the Kyoto Daishoten, a tendon injury was found, and he retired to stud, much missed.
1469: After 2 wins he was 6th in the Asahi Hai FS, then won the Junior C. at 3 and held on for 2nd in the Spring S. 10th in the Satsuki Sho and 8th in the NHK Mile C., he was 3rd against older horses in the Keisei Hai Autumn H., then won the Fuji S. from the front. Expected to rise as a miler, he did little more, suffered a tendon injury at 4 and retired after a heavy defeat on his return.
1470: Second foal of Air Thule, an international sprint star. Favorite on debut, he showed immaturity, even whinnying as he ran, and was 8th. He won his 2nd start, was 3rd in the Nojigiku S., then broke clear from 2nd to win the Daily Hai 2yo S. In the Asahi Hai FS he let Goshawk Ken lead all the way but held on for 3rd. 4th to Meiner Charles in the Yayoi Sho, in the Satsuki Sho he made a bold run from before the straight under Yuga Kawada, in their 4th race together, and won a classic. But soon after, a carpal fracture forced a long break. Back in '09, he won the Asahi Challenge C. 2 years running but no more G1s, and retired injured in autumn at 6 to stud.
1471: At 3 she was 4th in the Flora S. and 5th in the Rose S., just short against the best. At 4 she often closed too late in allowances, but reached open class in autumn, 5th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup upset by Queen Spumante and 3rd in the Aichi Hai. At 5 she won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai by 3 lengths against colts. Favorite over colts in the Hanshin Daishoten, she was a close 3rd, then 10th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and 6th in the Takarazuka Kinen. In autumn she beat Oken Bruce Lee in the Kyoto Daishoten, then went for a G1 in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup: she ran down triple crown filly Apapane, but British raider Snow Fairy was 4 lengths ahead - 2nd. She was 2nd to the strong 4yo crop in the Kyoto Kinen - a match for colts at her beloved Kyoto - but broke down on her return in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and retired to breed. Her grey son Meisho Tengen (16: Deep Impact) won the Yayoi Sho as 8th choice.
1472: An Australian star of 2001-2004 with 11 G1 wins, and champion sire in 2010/11 - an icon of early-21st-century Australian racing. He emerged at 3, unbeaten in 7 with 1 G1, champion 3yo. At 4 he won 9 of 13, incl. 5 G1s; at 5 another 5 G1s, Australian Horse of the Year. In the Cox Plate he was 6th and 3rd, but retired with 26 wins from 35, 11 G1s. His first crop gave G1 winner Beaded, and G1 winners followed steadily; when his 4th crop debuted in 2010/11 he was Australia's champion sire. He entered Australia's Racing Hall of Fame in 2014.
1473: A gelding hailed as Hong Kong's greatest sprinter, winner of 8 sprint G1s there incl. 2 Hong Kong Sprints, plus Japan's Sprinters S., making his name worldwide. Unbeaten in 7, he won the Hong Kong Sprint over previous winner All Thrills Too and Horse of the Year Grand Delight, then became only the 3rd Hong Kong Sprint Triple Crown winner, extending his streak to 10 and sweeping Horse of the Year and champion sprinter. The next season he won the Hong Kong Sprint and Triple Crown again, a world-record 17 straight. He then tried a mile, but lost the Champions Mile and Japan's Yasuda Kinen, so returned to sprints. At 6 he came to Japan for the Sprinters S. and beat Durandal, Calstone Light O and others as favorite. Winless after, he raced until 7 and retired with 18 wins from 29, 9 G1s.
1474: Emerging in summer at 3, she won the Shion S. 11th in the Shuka Sho, she then beat colts in the Fukushima Kinen with a bold charge from behind. After a long dry spell, she won the '08 Niigata Kinen as 16th choice of 18.
1476: Winner of the 1983 Arc, she then swept America's 3 big turf races, Horse of the Year in both France and America. A leading 3yo hope, she did little in spring but won the Prix Vermeille in autumn. 15th in the Arc, she was invited to the 2nd Japan Cup and ran 2nd to Half Iced. At 4 she again did little in spring, but after a 2nd in the Prix Foy won the Arc, coming from far back as an outsider. Right after, in America she won the Rothmans International, Turf Classic Invitational and Washington DC International - Eclipse Horse of the Year in America and Horse of the Year in France. Winless at 5, she was 3rd in the Arc and 2nd in the first BC Turf, retiring that year. Her best foal was Prix Greffulhe winner and sire Along All.
1477: He ran in the Mile CS every year from 4, finally winning in 2014 at 6. Emerging at 4 with a 2nd in the Kyoto Kimpai, he became a regular contender in graded races. At 5 in 2013 he won the Kyoto Kimpai, was 3rd in the Yasuda Kinen a length behind Lord Kanaloa, won the Fuji S. in autumn and was 3rd as Mile CS favorite. In 2014 he was 9th as favorite in the Hankyu Hai, 1400m perhaps too short, then 4th in the Yasuda Kinen, 2nd in the Sekiya Kinen and 7th in the Fuji S. In the Mile CS, only 8th choice, he waited at the back, split the field on the inside in the straight and beat Fiero by a nose after a duel for his long-sought first G1. He was 10th in it at 7. Racing on at 8, he was 2nd in the Milers C. and, in his 5th straight Mile CS, 4th as 14th choice.
1478: From the 2nd crop of Admire Max, a sprint graded star who won the Takamatsunomiya Kinen. Fragile, he rose slowly but closed fastest in almost every race. In his first graded race, the Negishi S. at 5, he swept past dirt sprint stars like Sei Crimson and Taisei Legend with the fastest 34.6 finish - but was found to have fractured his right knee in the race.
1479: His debut was the legendary race with Unrivaled, Reach the Crown and Buena Vista. 4th behind those three, unnoticed at the time, he won in his 3rd start. Spring at 3 brought just a 5-million win, but in autumn he won an allowance easily from up front with a 33.6 finish and went to the Kikuka Sho. A fancied outsider at 8th choice, helped by his Dance in the Dark blood, he broke clear early in the straight and held off Forgettable, another Dance in the Dark colt, for his first G1. Hoped to lead a long-distance division without stars, he partially ruptured a tendon in the Arima Kinen and pulled up, retiring to stud; with no standout runners, he retired from stud in 2015.
1480: Stronger from autumn at 3, he was always competitive, reaching open class a year later with the Koto S. In his first graded race, the Kinko Sho, he was 3rd behind Ocean Blue, next the Arima Kinen runner-up, then 3rd to Danon Ballade in the American JCC. In his first long race, the Diamond S., he easily beat Tenno Sho winner Jaguar Mail. 4th choice in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he closed from behind but couldn't catch Fenomeno and others, 4th. After 2nds in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai and Hanshin Daishoten, still not winning, his camp, rating him as a stayer, announced an Australian campaign in autumn at 6. In the G1 Caulfield Cup, under top weight 58kg, he surged from midfield to win a G1 far away in Australia. Favorite for the Melbourne Cup, Australia's greatest race, again under top weight, 58.5kg, he raced forward but dropped back at the final turn to finish last. Back in his stall he died, apparently of acute heart failure; his ashes are buried in Australia.
1481: A strong horse rated next behind the TTG trio (Tosho Boy, Ten Point, Green Grass). At 5 (old age system) he won the Tenno Sho (Autumn), beating Tosho Boy and Green Grass for a big-race win. A late bloomer, his first big race was the Kikuka Sho in autumn at 4, where he was 17th, nowhere near TTG. But he won the Hanshin Daishoten at year's end, and at 5 was 2nd in the Nihon Keizai Shinshun Hai and Sankei Osaka Hai, showing real middle-to-long distance ability. In the Tenno Sho (Spring), 10th choice, he was 3rd behind Ten Point and Crown Pillard. That autumn he won the Asahi Challenge C. and Kyoto Kinen, then the Tenno Sho (Autumn): as Tosho Boy and Green Grass wore each other out dueling, Hokuto Boy swooped from behind at just the right moment to win. Often fancied but short after, his only other graded win was the Swan S. at 7. At stud he sired graded winners like Hanshin Shogai S. winner Daiten Sparta and Wide Girl.
1482: An allowance horse at 3-4, he won 4 straight after a long break in autumn at 5, then the Milers C., a sprint-mile contender. Dull in G1s like the Yasuda Kinen and Takarazuka Kinen, he won the CBC Sho at the end of 6.
1455: Half-brother of NHK Mile C. winner Taiki Fortune. Won the NZ Trophy but ran poorly after, tried jumps and moved to Iwate in '07.
1460: He won the Radio Tampa Hai 2yo S., but at 3 was 6th in the Yayoi Sho and 8th in the Satsuki Sho. Over further he was 3rd in the Derby and 5th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai. In the 3000m Kikuka Sho his sire Dance in the Dark's blood awoke: he powered on from the final turn to win, denying Neo Universe the Triple Crown. 2nd in the Japan Cup, older he managed only a 2nd in the Hanshin Daishoten, and a tendon injury ended his career.
1461: He won the Shinzan Kinen but struggled in the classics and the Takarazuka Kinen, so switched to dirt, winning the Musashino S. and running 7th in the Japan Cup Dirt. The next year he was a close 2nd to Admire Don in the February S., but 12th in the Dubai World Cup. After a long tendon-injury break, he won 2 open races, was 3rd in the '06 Teio Sho, and won the '07 Saga Kinen. He retired to stud in '08, drawing interest as full brother of G1 winner To the Victory, but has sired no graded winner.
1463: A local graded regular, as his Kokura Daishoten win shows. Racing until 9, in his 51st race, the Epsom C., he had run in graded races at all 10 JRA tracks. He retired after the Tanabata Sho.
1475: He won his debut but rested a year with a fracture, then won 3 straight to open class. In autumn '07 he was 2nd 3 times running - Sapporo Kinen, Mainichi Okan, Tenno Sho (Autumn) - and 4th in the Mile CS, then a fracture was found. Back in the '09 Kinko Sho he was 16th and went to stud.
1483: In the Yaezakura Sho at 3 he beat Running Free, later a graded star, by 3/4 of a length. Dull after, he came good at the end of 3 and won the Sprinters S. (G2) at 4.
1484: A fast horse at short-to-middle trips on dirt or turf. A late bloomer, he reached open class at 5 and won the Sprinters S. (G2) at 6, but was crushed in the Yasuda Kinen (7th) and Mile CS (15th), retiring after the next June's CBC Sho.
1486: After winning the Manyo S. at 4, he dead-heated with champion Tamamo Cross in the Hanshin Daishoten. He won the Kyoto Kinen and was 4th in the Takarazuka Kinen, but oddly flopped in the Tenno Sho (Spring), finishing in double figures twice.
1487: Right after winning a maiden at 3, she was 2nd to later double classic winner Max Beauty in the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (East), earning an Oaks spot. In the Oaks, as 10th choice, she tracked only Max Beauty and finished 2nd, ahead of Kosei, Mejiro Fulmar and others. After poor runs, at 5 she was 3rd in the Kimpai (East) and 2nd in the Nakayama Himba S., then won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai.
1488: He just couldn't win. At 5 he won the Kimpai (East) as 6th choice, but then was 3rd in the Nakayama Kinen and Nikkei Sho - six 2nds and five 3rds from 25. No match in G1s, but a fine supporting player always running well in graded races.
1489: The last graded winner sired by great sire Partholon. He won a maiden in May at 3, then often fell short until September, when he won 3 straight to open class. 3rd in the American JCC at 4, he then won the Meguro Kinen, his only graded win.
1490: A supporting player who ran 47 times at short-to-middle trips. With 2 wins at 2-3, he was 2nd in the NZ Trophy Yonsai S. and Radio Tampa Sho. At 4-5 he won the Keio Hai Spring C. and was 2nd in the Epsom C. and Tokyo Shimbun Hai. With a sharp 34-second kick, he was 3rd to Bamboo Memory in the Sprinters S. From 6 a regular in sprint-mile graded races, he declined, rarely making the top five, and retired after finishing last in the Sprinters S. at 7.
1491: A tough horse who raced twice a month almost without a break, building strength steadily in allowances. In the All Comers at 5, as 11th choice, he beat Mejiro Ardan, Doctor Spurt and others - a graded win in his 32nd start.
1492: His temper was so bad that, despite real ability, he was never consistent - a pure closer. He had a sharp 34-second kick but often misfired, rarely running to the betting. Valued as a son of Tosho Boy, he went to stud.
1494: A speedy sprinter. He won the Spring S. and went to the Satsuki Sho, but the longer trip and heavy ground left him 9th, so he gave up the classics for sprints. He won the Shobu S. but ran badly in autumn. Struggling to win, he took the Swan S. at 4 and Tokyo Shimbun Hai at 6, and at the end of 5 ran 2nd in the Sprinters S. as 11th choice.
1495: He won his 2nd start and the Momiji S., then was 3rd in the Hanshin Sansai S., Kansai's 2yo championship, and won the Kisaragi Sho, a classic contender. But then injury cost him a year. Back at the end of 3, he lost twice, then won the Kyoto Kinen as 3rd choice. He kept running well in graded races without winning, raced until 6, and became a lead pony.
1496: Raced mainly on dirt early at 3 without success, he switched to turf and won 3 straight 5-million races, then 3 more to open class, a regular in turf sprint graded races. His first graded win, the Centaur S. at 6, came in record time. Then a long losing streak: at 8, 19 losses in a row, he was 13th choice, second-last, in the Sekiya Kinen - and with a furious charge won by a nose, setting up a 40,000-yen quinella.
1497: He won the Spring S. by 5 lengths and was 5th choice in a strong Satsuki Sho, but 11th. After an injury break, he was 5th in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai and 9th in the Kikuka Sho, then won the December S. (OP) by 3.5 lengths. Leg trouble forced another long break; he returned in the Yasuda Kinen 2 years later, 17th, and retired to stud. His first crop drew attention with debut wins, but little followed.
1498: Unlike his sire Green Grass's image, a sprint closer. At 5 he won a 9-million race, was 2nd in an open special, then won the Keio Hai Autumn H. In his farewell, the CBC Sho, he won in a then-astonishing record 1:07.9.
1499: He beat White Stone and others in the NHK Hai. After a 9th in the Derby he never won again in the JRA, but won 4 at Saga and Arao.
1500: He won the Wakaba S. at 3 but was crushed in the Aoba Sho and Derby. Racing mainly at middle distances, he ran in 31 graded races, winning 3 local ones: Fukushima Kinen, Kabutoyama Kinen, Niigata Daishoten - rarely placing otherwise.
1501: He won his debut by a stunning 9 lengths, then the Niigata Sansai S. and Keisei Hai Sansai S. - seemingly invincible, a star overnight. But he was 2nd to Lindo Shaver, who set a record, in the Asahi Hai Sansai S., 2nd again in the Keisei Hai, then 14th in the Satsuki Sho and 15th in the Derby. Focusing on a mile or less, he struggled to regain form, taking over 3 years to win a 4th race.
1502: A bit slow to win a maiden, he then used his speed to win the Kisaragi Sho and Spring S., a leading classic contender. With genius Yutaka Take aboard he ran in the Satsuki Sho and Derby, but was nowhere near Tokai Teio, crushed in double figures. Little after; at 6 he switched to jumps and, showing a flat graded winner's class, won a jump graded race in only his 2nd try.
1503: He starred before dirt racing was organized and before unified JRA-local graded races. 3rd in the Keisei Hai at 3, a classic hope, he was 6th in the Kyodo News Hai, then injury cost him the spring classics. Back, he won steadily, taking the Fuji S. and Christmas S. (OP) in autumn at 3. From the Ginrei S. at 5 he raced more on dirt, and the next year, after a 2nd in the March S., beat Calypso Song, Tomishino Porunga and others in the Teio Sho for a big title. He didn't win again even on dirt and retired at 7. Seen as a dirt horse, but half his 8 wins came on turf.
1504: He beat Leo Durban in the St. Lite Kinen, but not nominated for the classics, couldn't run in the Kikuka Sho. After a long injury break he did little and moved to local Niigata.
1505: Brilliantly fast, he won the Crystal C., but leg trouble ended his career early. As a son of great mare Star Roch's daughter, he went to stud; his best was '06 Ibis Summer Dash winner Sachino Sweetie (03: Per Favore).
1507: He won his debut at Niigata in May at 3, as the spring classics heated up. Apart from one 1800m race, he ran only at a mile or less, all 10 wins at 1400m or less, and never made the top five at 1600m - a pure sprinter. Perhaps due to temper, he was impossible to read: winning streaks, then heavy defeats, then sudden wins. At 5 he won the Hankyu Hai, then after a 3rd in the CBC Sho won the Sapporo Sprint S.
1508: A late bloomer who reached open class late at 4. He won the CBC Sho at 5, then ran in many mile graded races, winning the Milers C. at 7. At stud he sired no stars.
1509: In the Kikuka Sho, where Mihono Bourbon sought the Triple Crown, he fought for the lead and set a forceful pace - called "the horse who wrecked Bourbon's Triple Crown." But Bogan was himself a noted front-runner who had to lead, win or lose. Outclassed, perhaps, but a 2-time graded winner too, and that run showed his pride. It failed, but it was more truly Bogan than the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, where he let Bourbon lead. In his 4 races after, he never led again; tracking in 2nd as if out of deference, he never won again.
1510: Just 2 wins up to 3. Effective leading or racing forward, he grew much stronger as an older horse. Dropped to the 9-million class in summer at 4, he won easily, then held off Fujiyama Kenzan in the Sekiya Kinen and won the Keio Hai Autumn H. too, fully mature. But against the best he was 4th to Shinko Lovely in both the Mainichi Okan and Mile Championship. He faded after and retired at 6.
1511: Slow to win, he stalled after reaching open class. At 7 he tried jumps, winning 2 of 6, then oddly returned to the flat for the Nikkei Sho. Naturally last choice of 12, but ridden by longshot specialist Teruo Eda he ran the race of his life and won. 355.7 to win, and with 7th choice Cygnus Hero 2nd, the bracket quinella paid 59,000 yen and the quinella 213,370 yen - a historic upset.
1512: A flagship of Masaru Sayama's stable, called "Sayama of the sprints" with stablemates Gold Mountain, Yuki Top Run and Hishi Akebono. With the speed of his sire Nihon Pillow Winner he starred in sprints, winning 7 of 37, including the CBC Sho and Hankyu Hai. Short of G1 class, he was beaten badly in 2 tries. Winless late in his career, he retired at 7 to be a riding horse at the Equine Park in Setagaya, Tokyo.
1513: Steady in the spring classics, he finally won a graded race, the St. Lite Kinen, in autumn. He then plateaued and moved to Kochi at 5, winning 15 and becoming a star there.
1514: Debuting in November at 2, she won once but was twice 2nd in allowances. At 3 she won the Anemone S. and Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (West), but was 4th as 3rd choice in the Oka Sho. She won the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (East), but was 8th in the Oaks - a classic trial horse, playing support to double winner Vega. After a 7th in the Rose S. she had leg trouble and retired. Little success as a broodmare.
1515: His career peak was the Spring S. at 3, where his furious finish made him a classic contender. But he was 14th in the Satsuki Sho, and in the Derby threw jockey Katsumi Minai just after the start - his one big day over in seconds.
1516: A versatile miler on turf or dirt. He won the Milers C. at 4, but his form was erratic, and the big win his name promised never came. At 7 he moved to Kaminoyama, then Takasaki, winning 4 more.
1517: Gutsy but lacking a quick burst, she often couldn't hold on. With 2 wins, she was 2nd in the Yonsai Himba Tokubetsu (East), 4th in the Oaks and a close 4th in the Queen Elizabeth Cup, a match for Hishi Amazon and Chokai Carol, and won the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu at the end of 3. But the next spring she died suddenly in an accident at pasture.
1518: Tipped as a star before his debut, he was heavy favorite - but at the crucial final turn he bolted, crashed into the rail and pulled up, famous for the wrong reason. He later won the Yayoi Sho as hoped, but his temper cost him in the classics. "Run straight and he's G1 class," people said, but 2 accidents and long breaks disrupted him, and he retired after winning the Tanabata Sho at 5.
1519: Debuting late, he won through the classes to open. In his first graded race, the American JCC at 5, he was 3rd as favorite, then won the Nakayama Kinen as 2.5 favorite. Constant leg trouble then kept him from his best.
1520: A blueblood by Sunday Silence out of Dyna Fairy; full brother of American JCC and Nikkei Sho winner Rosen Cavalier (93: Sunday Silence). He won his 3rd start and, after a 3rd in a 5-million race, won the Aoba Sho with a bold charge from far back. That was his only big moment, but as a Sunday Silence son he went to stud, siring jumper Aiden Summer (97: Aiden Noble).
1521: He ran in the NHK Hai (G2: 2000m) and Kobe Shimbun Hai at 3 while still developing. Slowly gaining strength, at 4, still in allowances, he won the Diamond S. as 4th choice, then the Meguro Kinen, and the next year the Diamond S. again. All his open wins came at 2500m+ - a clear stayer, as shown by his half-brother Gokai and full brother Yu Fuyoho, both J-G1 winners.
1485: Until late at 4 he couldn't even win in the 4-million class. Winning his 3rd race at year's end, he ran above his class for 2nd in the Naruo Kinen - a fluke, it seemed, as he then couldn't win even in his own class. He tried the Tenno Sho (Spring), beaten badly. But in his last race, the Kyoto Daishoten, again above his class, he beat Cosmo Dream by 3 lengths - a graded winner at last.
1493: A flashy chestnut with 3 white socks, a blaze and a flaxen mane - and a stylish front-runner who glided at the head of the field, his golden mane flowing. He had many fans even in the lower classes. At first they came for his looks, but late in his career he bloomed, winning the Kimpai (East) and American JCC at 6. Then chronic hoof cracks forced a long break, and he retired after a 15th in that November's Tenno Sho (Autumn). Valued for his looks, he became a lead pony at Tokyo Racecourse.
1506: A modest pedigree and a small, frail-looking frame - yet she ran on without rest as a leading filly: 2nd in the Hanshin Sansai Himba S., 7th in the Oka Sho, 2nd in the Oaks, 5th in the Queen Elizabeth Cup. Amid criticism that she was overraced, she ran in the Arima Kinen, her 10th graded race that year, and broke down near the line. Spared euthanasia at her connections' wish, she never recovered and died 22 months later.
1522: With Sunday Silence runners dominant, he was hyped as a Japan-sired classic hope. He won the Keisei Hai and Kyodo News Hai Yonsai S., but was 7th as 2nd choice in the Satsuki Sho and 5th in the Derby. Switching to sprints, he won just one mile open race, moved to Funabashi at 6, and retired without success.
1523: A true stayer: 5 of his 8 wins came at 2400m+. 7th in the Kikuka Sho, his only graded win was the Stayers S.; in middle-distance graded races he was clearly outclassed. He moved to Iwate at 7.
1524: After winning his 2nd start he struggled, but in his 13th won a 5-million special, then the Aoba Sho. Crushed in the Derby and Kikuka Sho, he still ran well in middle-to-long graded races, racing until spring at 6.
1525: In the top five in his first 8 starts without a win, he won his 9th and then 4 straight to open class. After a 2nd in the Topaz S., he beat Hagino Real King and others in the Naruo Kinen.
1526: A bold closer whose kick often misfired. After winning the May S. at 4, he raced unusually handy in the Meguro Kinen and beat Tsukuba Symphony and others - but leg trouble ended his career after that race.
1528: A JRA-local racing star with 13 wins. Raced mainly on turf early, he ran well - 5th in the NHK Mile C. - but rarely won. Switching to dirt, his power came through: he won the Heian S. at 5, then ran in a graded race about once a month, JRA or local. Never a G1 winner, he won 7 graded races, incl. 2 Heian S. and 2 each of the JRA-local Nagoya Daishoten and Mercury C.
1529: Steady from his debut, he reached open class late at 4. After a jump win he returned to the flat and raced mainly in JRA-local races, winning the Sakitama Hai at 6, the Urawa Kinen at 7 and the Sakitama Hai again at 8. He went to stud in America, his birthplace.
1530: Known for light speed, he starred around a mile on turf or dirt. He won the Keisei Hai Autumn H. at 4 and the Elm S. at 6, and at 8 set a record over 1700m on Hakodate dirt in the Marine S.
1531: A handicapper who ran well on light weights, and a flat-track lover: 4 of 7 wins at Hakodate, 2 at Niigata - both graded. He moved to Iwate at 9 but retired winless there.
1532: With a razor-sharp kick, she starred at 2. Winning her 2nd start, she beat colts in the Nojigiku S. with the fastest finish, then won the Hanshin Sansai Himba S. by 1.25 lengths. She did little from the spring classics on.
1533: A miler with a sharp kick who ran well from 2 to 6. At 2-4, unlike his name, he often fell short, settling in open class only late at 4. At 6 he won the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and Lord Derby Challenge T., then died suddenly in training.
1536: A son of great mare Rosita, but last on debut, 9.6 seconds behind. After a break he was 3rd in a maiden and won his 3rd start. Slowly building, he won the Asahi Challenge C. at 5 and was 4th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). At 6 he was 2nd in the Kokura Kinen and Asahi Challenge C., then won the Naruo Kinen.
1537: Full brother of Oka Sho winner Wonder Perfume. Unlike his closer sister, he was best leading at his own pace. His finest hour was the Spring S. at 3: as 11th choice he led alone from the start and, helped by heavy ground, won by 2.5 lengths, earning a classic spot. Older, he switched to jumps but was killed in a racing accident.
1538: She led all the way to win her June debut at Hakodate. 13th in the Hakodate 2yo S., she then ran steadily and was 2nd in the Fillies' Revue, earning an Oka Sho spot - but was no factor in Buena Vista and Red Desire's battle, 6th. In autumn the big two beat her again in the Rose S. and Shuka Sho, so she tried sprints in the 1400m Aurora C. and crushed older horses incl. graded winner Urbanity - a natural sprinter. At 4 she won the Hanshin Himba S. by 2 lengths off a break, avenging half-siblings I Am Tsuyoshi and I Am Angel, who never won graded races. In the Victoria Mile, perhaps too far, she was 10th to Buena Vista. At 1400m or less: 4 wins and two 2nds from 9 on any surface.
1539: Set back by injuries, he was long in allowances. At 7 he won the Shinshun S. by a nose to reach open class, then the Silk Road S. 4th to Believe and Sunningdale in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen. At stud his first crop included Hyogo Junior Grand Prix winner Dear Yamato.
1540: Winning his 2nd start on dirt, he ran mainly on dirt, 2nd in the Hokkaido Sansai Yushun, then won the Zen-Nihon Sansai Yushun by a nose after a duel with Silver Sabre.
1541: He won a debut race by 4 lengths in July at 2, then often fell short, winning again only in autumn at 4 before rising to open class. In the next Nikkei Shinshun Hai he closed in 34.1 to beat Hot Secret and Tap Dance City.
1542: Unbeaten in 3, he was crushed in the NHK Mile C. and Derby and returned to dirt, winning Asahikawa's Grand Chariot C. by 3 lengths, then the JRA's Sirius S. and Takasaki's Gumma Kinen - graded wins JRA and local.
1544: A speedy sprinter on any surface. At 3 he lost a nose duel with later Takarazuka Kinen winner Dantsu Flame in the Arlington C., and won the NZ Trophy over Native Heart and others. Crushed in the NHK Mile C. and Derby, older he won only the Yonago S. At 6 he tried jumps, but after one race returned to the flat and retired.
1545: With the kick and grit of his dam Golden Jack, he ran above his class to win the Keihan Hai in autumn at 4, then the Kyoto Kimpai at 5. 2nd in the Nakayama Kinen, he was then injured. Back after a year in the '05 Yasuda Kinen (9th), he was 3rd in the Kita-Kyushu Kinen, then won the Sekiya Kinen with a powerful finish.
1546: A supporting player in so many graded races that people said "him again" at every race card - and a mudlark transformed on soft ground. At 3, with 1 win, he won the Shinzan Kinen as 14th choice, helped by soft going. Then he lost race after race, classics included, yet kept running monthly: at 5 he ran 11 races, 10 graded, from the Kyoto Kimpai to the Arima Kinen without a break. In the 8th, the Niigata Kinen - also on soft ground - he won his 2nd graded race. The next year, at the same pace, he broke down in the Sapporo Kinen in August, his 8th graded race of the year, and was put down - a tragedy of toughness.
1547: Unlike his sire Star of Cozzene, a middle-distance turf horse, Nihon Pillow Sart was a dirt sprinter: all 13 wins came on dirt at 1400m or less. Carefully placed, he was very consistent, with eleven 2nds - nearly 50% in the top two. He won 4 graded races in '04-'05, then went winless and retired after the '07 Tokyo Hai, much missed.
1548: A pure sprinter who led at a blistering pace with exceptional speed. A specialist on Niigata's straight 1000m, he won the Ibis Summer Dash there twice, once in a record 53.7. More than speed, he had rare grit for a front-runner, holding on astonishingly in tight finishes. In the '04 Sprinters S. he beat mile king Durandal by 4 lengths, finally winning his long-sought G1 at 6. He was 14th in Hong Kong at year's end. Going for a 3rd straight Ibis Summer Dash in '05 he was 4th, then 10th in the Sprinters S., and retired to stud.
1549: One of the most successful Japanese runners by imported sire Silver Deputy, spreading his sire's name. A dirt sprinter with 10 wins. In the '04 JBC Sprint he was a fine 4th against Meiner Select and others, then won the Zen-Nihon Thoroughbred C., his 4th graded title. Though JRA-based, he raced mainly in JRA-local races after, but faded with age.
1550: 2nd on debut, he ran above his class and won the Clover Sho in record time - a remarkable feat - but was 8th in the Asahi Hai Sansai S. Injury then sidelined him until autumn at 4. Starting again in the 5-million class, he worked his way up and won the Tokyo Shimbun Hai at 6, then the Keio Hai Spring C., finding his niche at sprint-mile trips, and the Fuji S. at 7.
1551: He ran in the Kikuka Sho at 3 but was slow to bloom. In autumn at 5, as 14th choice, he ran big on his beloved heavy ground to win the Keihan Hai, and the next year won the Tanabata Sho as an outsider on good-to-soft ground.
1552: With leg concerns, he raced mainly on dirt. Two long injury breaks delayed his rise, but his ability made him a true "late-arriving star." He won the Heian S. early at 6, his first graded race win, and 4 graded races by autumn. In the Japan Cup Dirt, the dirt summit, he beat reigning king Admire Don for his first G1. 4th in the Tokyo Daishoten, at 7 he grew stronger still, winning the Kawasaki Kinen, Teio Sho and, in autumn, the JBC Classic. Then age seemed to tell: often close but not winning. A year without a win, he was only 5th choice for the JBC Classic at 8 - but the old warrior ran big, racing forward and powering home for his 5th G1, his first win in a year.
1553: He gave his sire Bubble Gum Fellow his first graded title. Losing on turf early, he ran well on dirt. At 3 he tried the Mainichi Hai for the classics but was crushed on turf. Switching fully to dirt, he won 3 straight at the end of 3 up to the Nagoya Grand Prix. 4th in the Kawasaki Kinen and 3rd in the Oguri Cap Kinen, he was then injured; back in '05 after 27 months, his old power was gone.
1554: He won his first 3, incl. the Keisei Hai, and charged from last at the final turn for 2nd in the Yayoi Sho. But he was 14th in the Satsuki Sho, then rested long with a lame left shoulder. Back, he won the Osakajo S., his first win in about 2 years, but was outclassed in graded races. Still racing in '07 but no longer JRA class, he moved to Kanazawa.
1555: Lacking a finish, he was slow to win and missed the classics. Emerging as an older horse, he won the Lord Derby Challenge T. in spring, and the next year the American JCC, proving his range. He kept running in graded races without winning and retired after a 12th in the '07 Nikkei Shinshun Hai.
1556: Debuting late, he missed the classics but came good when older. After a 16-million win, a week later he ran down front-running Lohengrin from last to win the Tokyo Shimbun Hai. Back from a long break, he was 2nd in the Hakodate Sprint S.
1557: He shone in the warm spring: all 6 wins after his debut came in April-June, including the Epsom C. in '03 and '04 - a "spring horse." In other seasons he was inconsistent.
1558: Always running on under any conditions. At 3 he crossed the line first in the Kabutoyama Kinen but was demoted to 10th. In autumn at 4 he won a blanket finish in the Asahi Challenge C. by a neck, then was 5th to Symboli Kris S in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). Winless for over 2.5 years, he won the '06 Sekiya Kinen and was 2nd to King's Trail in the '07 Keisei Hai Autumn H. That was his peak; he faded and retired after a 16th in the '09 Tanabata Sho.
1559: Inconsistent at first, he changed: after winning the Thoroughbred Challenge C. in autumn at 3, he became a reliable dirt force at any distance or going. At 5 he won the Saga Kinen and Nagoya Daishoten; at 6 the Nagoya Daishoten again and March S.; at 7, showing age, still the Mercury C. and 2nd in the Tokyo Daishoten - dangerous even unfancied. Winless in '07, he was 2nd in the Saga Kinen, Diolite Kinen and Mercury C., and retired to stud after a 2nd in the '08 Saga Kinen. Top class until 9, he loved the Saga Kinen: 1 win and four 2nds.
1560: A speedy middle-distance dirt star. Emerging early, his first graded win came only in the Nippon TV Hai at 4. He was 2nd in the JBC Classic and 4th in the Japan Cup Dirt, then won the Tokyo Daishoten, his long-sought G1, and was 2nd in the Kawasaki Kinen. A fracture forced a long break; back, he was 3rd in the Japan Cup Dirt and ran in the Dubai World Cup (7th). He retired at the end of '07 to stud.
1561: First foal of Queen Elizabeth Cup 3rd See's Grace. He won twice on dirt early at 3, then struggled. At 5, still erratic, he won the Negishi S. and the JRA-local Cluster C., then plateaued, retiring after a maiden hurdle in '07.
1562: A dominant sprinter of 2003-2005. His last-to-first charge, scything through the field, was as sharp as the holy sword he was named after. Emerging in autumn at 4, after a 3rd in the Centaur S. he won the Sprinters S. and Mile Championship back to back, champion sprinter. At 5 he was 2nd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and Sprinters S., then won the Mile Championship again, champion sprinter once more. In Hong Kong he was a close 5th in the Hong Kong Mile. At 6 he was 2nd in the Sprinters S. on his return - top of the sprint world for 3 years. At stud he sired Oaks winner Erin Court and 2-time Chukyo Kinen winner Fragarach, and died in 2013.
1527: A late bloomer who reached open class in summer at 5. 16th as 3rd choice in his first graded race, the Kokura Kinen, he rested after more losses. At 6 he was 2nd to Tosen Crown on heavy ground in the Nakayama Kinen, then in the Osaka Hai broke clear from up front and held off Golden Dahlia and Dream Journey. He faded to 11th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), then injury forced a long break, and after heavy defeats on his return he retired.
1534: Half-sister of Satsuki Sho winner Captain Thule. She won her debut and kept winning after a long break. 10th as 2nd choice in her first graded race, the Hanshin Himba S., she reached open class, was 3rd in the Ibis Summer Dash and won the Centaur S. Favorite for the Sprinters S., she was 5th to Laurel Guerreiro. At 6 she won the Silk Road S. and retired to breed after a 5th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen.
1535: A late-blooming stayer. He won the Manyo S. at 5, then the Meguro Kinen at 6 after a 7th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), and the same double the next year. After the Kyoto Daishoten he partially ruptured a hind-leg ligament. First diagnosed as hopeless, he was treated at the wish of his owner, a vet, and recovered enough to become a riding horse.
1543: Always with a sharp kick: 9 wins, seven 2nds and three 3rds from 33 - superbly consistent, in graded races too. After a long break from the '04 Tenno Sho (Spring), he returned in the '05 Nakayama Kimpai and retired after 3 races.
1563: Repeated leg trouble slowed his rise. Back from his 2nd break in summer at 4, he won 3 straight up to the Sirius S., then lost the JBC Sprint by a nose. At 5 he won the Garnet S. easily, then was a fine 5th in the Dubai Golden Shaheen. In his 2nd race back home he won the Tokyo Hai, then the JBC Sprint, his long-sought G1. He won the Kurofune Sho at 6 for 3 straight graded wins, but with leg trouble persisting, retired to stud after it.
1564: Strong when breaking fast and leading. 2nd in the Crystal C. and NZ Trophy, he was unplaced in the NHK Mile C., then led all the way to win the Falcon S. In autumn he led all the way in the Swan S., then led boldly in the Mile CS for a superb 3rd behind Durandal and Fine Motion. Older he plateaued, often fading from the front, but at 6 in '06 led all the way again in the Yodo Tankyori S. Able only to lead, he slumped again; at 7 he was 18th, 16th and 17th in the Ibis Summer Dash, Kita-Kyushu Kinen and Swan S., and finally retired.
1565: 6th in both the Derby and Kikuka Sho - a durable stayer. He won the Stayers S. at the end of 3, was 4th in the next Tenno Sho (Spring) and won the Meguro Kinen in record time. He ran well in 3000m+ races like the Manyo S. and Diamond S. Poor in '07, he switched to jumps that summer and retired to stud in '08.
1566: He won the Kyoto Shimbun Hai but was crushed in the Derby and Kikuka Sho. After poor runs he suddenly ran 2nd in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai at 4, then again a year later - occasional surprise graded runs.
1567: A sharp kicker best sitting handy, he won the Wakagoma S. and Sumire S. that way. Throat surgery and more ruled out the Satsuki Sho; straight into the Derby off a break he was a dull 8th. 4th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, he closed from midfield for 2nd to That's the Plenty in the Kikuka Sho, and in the Arima Kinen, though 9 lengths behind Symboli Kris S, broke clear early for 2nd. He won the Hanshin Daishoten the next year, then slumped. Reviving in the '05 Kyoto Daishoten, he was 3rd in the Arima Kinen, won the Nikkei Sho and was 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Spring), but retired injured to stud.
1568: 3rd in his first 5 starts, he won only in his 8th, missing the spring classics. He won a 5-million race, the Radio Tampa Sho in July and the St. Lite Kinen, then was 7th in the Kikuka Sho. Older, he struggled with just an open win until the '06 Nakayama Kimpai. A graded regular without more wins, he retired in autumn '08 and went to stud in Britain.
1569: He beat later G1 winner Tall Poppy on debut, but injury meant he raced steadily only from autumn at 3. Reaching open class in just 5 starts, he was 4th in his first graded race, the Nikkei Sho. After dropping and rising again, he was 2nd in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai and won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai. At 5, delayed by injury, he started in the Kinko Sho and won powerfully despite the layoff, then was 3rd behind Nakayama Festa and Buena Vista in the Takarazuka Kinen. He beat Logi Universe in the Sapporo Kinen, but as 2nd choice was 3rd to Buena Vista and Perusa in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), then rested 6 months. After a 3rd in the Kinko Sho came the Takarazuka Kinen: 6th choice amid strong 4yos like Rulership and Eishin Flash, he led at the top of the straight and held off Buena Vista - equaling the Japanese record, and the race's first father-son double (sire Grass Wonder). Leg trouble ruled out the Sapporo Kinen; returning in the All Comers, he won as 1.4 favorite. In the Tenno Sho (Autumn), facing queen Buena Vista and the 4yos again, he drew the widest gate - fatal for a forward runner - and was 14th. Winless after, he retired to stud after an 11th in the 2012 Arima Kinen.
1570: By Dance in the Dark out of Air Groove - a superb blueblood. Heavy favorite on debut, he was 5th; he won next time but then ran dully. His turning point came in autumn: 3rd as 7th choice in the St. Lite Kinen earned a Kikuka Sho spot, where he was 2nd to fellow Dance in the Dark colt Three Rolls, his stamina awakening. Favorite against older horses in the Stayers S., he won it, then was 4th in the Arima Kinen. At 4 he won the Diamond S. and was favorite for the Tenno Sho (Spring), but a slow start left him in midfield and he lacked response in the straight, 6th, then 10th in the Takarazuka Kinen. Winless after, he retired in 2013.
1571: By Sakura President, 2nd to Neo Universe in the Satsuki Sho. Improving with racing, his first graded race was the G1 Takamatsunomiya Kinen at 4; 9th, but only 0.5s behind Curren Chan. Dropping a class in summer at 4, he won the Okutama S. and the Lapis Lazuli S. (OP), then the Ocean S. by half a length after a duel with Dasher Go Go - his sire's first JRA graded win. In the Takamatsunomiya Kinen he was 4th to champion Lord Kanaloa, ahead of veterans Dasher Go Go and Majin Prosper, and in the Yasuda Kinen, 16th choice, ran on for 5th. Quiet at 6, at 7 he rose again, winning the Ocean S. and Keio Hai Spring C., and was 2nd as an outsider in the Sprinters S., a step from a G1.
1572: Unbeaten in her first 19, a North American record, with 13 G1s - the most by a mare there - and the first female to win the BC Classic. Little noticed for her pedigree, a big, slow-maturing mare, she debuted only in November at 3. Then she kept winning, taking her first G1, the Apple Blossom H., early at 4 and the BC Ladies' Classic in autumn. At 5 she took on males in the BC Classic and beat Rip Van Winkle, Summer Bird and others - the first female to win it. Her retirement was announced, but at 6 she raced on, winning the Lady's Secret S. for a record 19th straight, and truly retired after a 2nd going for a repeat in the BC Classic. She was Eclipse Horse of the Year at 6. As a broodmare her foals have mostly failed to win so far.
1573: For trainer Kunihide Matsuda, the ultimate horse was one who could win both the NHK Mile C. and the Derby - the brutal 2-week route stablemates Kurofune and Tanino Gimlet had tried, each winning just one. Many said it was too much for a 3yo. But King Kamehameha won the NHK Mile C. by 5 lengths, then the Derby in a stunning record 2:23.3, far easier than the margin suggests - silencing all doubters for the double. He won the Kobe Shimbun Hai flawlessly in autumn, and was to run in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) instead of the Kikuka Sho, where, given his power and rivals, he seemed sure to follow Bubble Gum Fellow and Symboli Kris S as a 3yo winner. But just before, he suffered a tendon injury and retired to stud. At stud his majesty endured: his 2nd crop gave fillies' Triple Crown winner Apapane, Rose Kingdom, To the Glory, Rulership and more, and he was champion sire in 2010 and 2011. In 2012 Lord Kanaloa won a G1 abroad, and later came dirt king Hokko Tarumae, double classic winner Duramente, Rey de Oro and Lovely Day - a leading non-Sunday Silence sire. He retired from stud in 2019 with ill health and died that year, aged 18. Through many heirs like Lord Kanaloa, his blood will keep spreading.
1574: Daughter of Oka Sho runner-up London Bridge. She won the Queen C. but was a dull 7th in the Oka Sho. In the Oaks she took the lead around the 3rd turn and held on - the classic her dam missed. 7th in the Rose S., she beat older horses in the Keihan Hai and was 3rd in the Hanshin Himba S., but was crushed in the '05 Kyoto Kimpai. Struggling against colts, she won the Mermaid S. - strong against fillies.
1575: A 3rd in the Spring S. got him into the Satsuki Sho. With just a maiden win he was 10th choice, but he raced forward and closed in 33 seconds, beating favorite Cosmo Bulk with authority - a classic winner. Then came heavy defeats: 6th in the Derby, 9th in the All Comers, 17th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). The cause was a throat problem; after surgery he returned to win the Lord Derby Challenge T., then was 2nd in the Sekiya Kinen and Mile CS. In '06 he was 2nd in the Nakayama Kinen and won the Milers C. 4th in the Yasuda Kinen and Takarazuka Kinen, everyone knew his class. That autumn he won the Mainichi Okan in good time, then the Tenno Sho (Autumn), his first G1 in a while, and the Mile CS. 3rd in the Arima Kinen, he was 3rd behind Admire Moon in the Dubai Duty Free, then won the Yasuda Kinen back home and the Mile CS again in autumn - 5 G1s. In his last race, the Arima Kinen, despite the trip, he was 3rd for the 2nd year. At stud his first crop gave unbeaten NHK Mile C. winner Curren Black Hill and Takamatsunomiya Kinen winner Copano Richard; Admire Mars won 3 G1s incl. the Hong Kong Mile; and many mile G1 winners followed - Major Emblem, Reine Minoru, Resistencia, Serifos, Ascoli Piceno - passing on his speed.
1576: Full sister of Dance Partner and Dance in the Dark - a superb blueblood. She won her debut by 6 lengths, the Wakatake Sho and the Flower C. easily, and stayed unbeaten in the Oka Sho in a good 1:33.6, a classic winner like her siblings. In the Oaks her fiery temper surfaced; fighting her rider, she was 4th. Abroad she was a close 2nd in the American Oaks. In autumn her temper cost her again (4th in the Shuka Sho), but she took the unusual step for a 3yo filly of running in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), a fine 2nd to Zenno Rob Roy, and 2nd in a strong Mile CS. 13th in Hong Kong, she did nothing in spring '05 (9th Keio Hai Spring C., 18th Yasuda Kinen), but improved in autumn, 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 4th in the Mile CS. In '06, after a 2nd in the Milers C., she won the new G1 Victoria Mile, holding off Air Messiah - her first win in a long time. She also won the US CashCall Mile S. and was 2nd in the Mile CS, retiring at the end of '06. Her first foal Dance Fantasia (08: Falbrav) won a graded race at once - a fine broodmare.
1577: King Kamehameha and Zenno Rob Roy were arguably better, but the talk of racing was Bulk, a Hokkaido-based horse taking on the JRA classics. With a 2yo graded win and the Yayoi Sho, hopes were high, but he was 2nd in the Satsuki Sho, 8th in the Derby and 4th in the Kikuka Sho. Undaunted, he ran a gutsy 2nd in the Japan Cup. In the Arima Kinen fan vote, Zenno Rob Roy topped the poll, but almost as many invalid votes were cast for Bulk. He was 11th, and his hard times began: '05 brought 6th in the Nikkei Sho, 10th in Hong Kong's Champions Mile, 12th in the Takarazuka Kinen, 11th in the Mainichi Okan, 14th in the Japan Cup. Just when he seemed finished, he was 4th in the Arima Kinen, and the next year went to Singapore and won the Singapore Airlines International C., a G1 abroad - a truly dramatic horse. In '07 he was 2nd in the same race. Most remarkable was his first race at home in Hokkaido since the Hokkai Yushun at 3: heavy favorite, he was only 3rd, perhaps baffled by his first dirt race in 22 starts, as he then won Morioka's turf OROC Cup easily and was 5th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). In '08, after a 4th in the Nikkei Sho, he was 6th in Singapore after a slow start, then a fracture needed surgery. He returned in the Japan Cup and kept trying JRA G1s without success, broke a leg again after the '09 Arima Kinen, and retired in 2010. A comeback in Ireland was discussed but a tendon injury ended it.
1578: Beaten 3 times by Cosmo Bulk - Hyakunichiso Tokubetsu, Radio Tampa Hai 2yo S. and Yayoi Sho - he missed the Satsuki Sho. In the Aoba Sho, on his favored left-handed track and newly in blinkers, he won, then swept forward from the 3rd turn to hold 3rd in the Derby. 4th against older horses in the All Comers, he was 11th in the Kikuka Sho and 13th in the Japan Cup, outclassed. Struggling when older, after one open win he had a long tendon-injury break. Back in autumn '07, he won the Naruo Kinen in his 3rd start, but then barely made the top five, retiring to stud after a 6th in the '09 Naruo Kinen.
1579: Full brother of Deep Impact. 2nd in the Kisaragi Sho, he won the Spring S. by a length. But as 2nd choice in the Satsuki Sho he was a shock 16th, then a tendon injury kept him out of the Derby. Back in '06 after 2.5 years, he ran well in open races without big wins, retiring to stud in '08. Popular for his pedigree, his first crop's T.M. Inazuma won the Daily Hai 2yo S., his 2nd crop's Meiner Frost the Mainichi Hai, and in 2015 Kitasan Black won the Kikuka Sho - a G1 and graded winners 3 years running.
1580: After winning the Wakaba S. he was 14th in the Satsuki Sho, but won the Kyoto Shimbun Hai and in the Derby exploded from far back for 2nd to King Kamehameha. 3rd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, 7th in the Kikuka Sho, 10th in the Japan Cup and 9th in the Arima Kinen, he steadied in 2005: 2nd in the Osaka Hai, 5th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), 2nd in the Takarazuka Kinen. After a dull Tenno Sho (Autumn), he was a nose 2nd to Alkaased in the Japan Cup, in a Japanese record 2:22.1. Then in the Arima Kinen he beat unbeaten Triple Crown winner Deep Impact by half a length - a huge upset and his first G1. In 2006 he went abroad and won the Dubai Sheema Classic easily, then was a close 3rd to Arc winner Hurricane Run in the King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S. Back home a throat problem left him 10th in the Japan Cup, and he retired to stud. His first crop debuted in 2010, incl. Just a Way, world's top-rated horse after a crushing Dubai Duty Free win, and Oaks winner Nuovo Record. One and Only won the Derby, fulfilling the dream of his sire and of trainer Hashiguchi. Japanese-bred Yoshida won 2 G1s in America, and Lys Gracieux won the Arima Kinen - a father-daughter double - and was 2019 Horse of the Year. He retired from stud in 2020 (last crop debuting in 2023) and died in 2023 after being unable to stand. In 2024 Do Deuce won the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Japan Cup with extraordinary finishes, Horse of the Year - his blood still shining after his death.
1581: He won the Crocus S., Arlington C. and NZ Trophy, and was 2nd choice for the NHK Mile C. as King Kamehameha's main rival, but faded to 7th. Beaten badly in England and France, he switched to dirt back home, mainly in JRA-local races. But in G1s - Kawasaki Kinen, February S., Nambu Hai, Japan Cup Dirt, Tokyo Daishoten - he was always 2nd. Undoubtedly talented, by his retirement at 6 he had nine 2nds from 16 dirt G1s, never winning one.
1582: She won her debut by 9 lengths, her 2nd start easily from a handy spot, and the Fillies' Revue by 1.25 lengths, then was 4th in the Oka Sho. Dull after, she retired.
1584: He won the Hiiragi Sho late at 2, then the Kyodo News Hai with a 33.3 finish. But he was 12th in the Satsuki Sho and 13th in the Derby, then had a tendon injury and a long break. Back, he struggled even in allowances and retired without a 4th win.
1585: He won the Shinzan Kinen but was crushed in all 3 classics and 13th in the Arima Kinen. Gradually recovering, he ran well at times and won the '06 Lord Derby Challenge T. He kept running in graded races, barely making the top five, and retired without a big title.
1586: He won his debut with a straight-long charge, his 2nd race by 2.5 lengths on heavy ground, and led all the way in the Crystal C., unbeaten in 3. Crushed in the NHK Mile C., he lost form and rested after a 7th in the Cluster C. He returned briefly, rested long again and retired.
1587: Raced only on dirt from his debut - a sand specialist. In the Unicorn S. he outdueled Personal Rush and others in the straight, then was 2nd in the Derby Grand Prix, but ran dully after. Tried once on turf in the Capital S., he was 12th, and back on dirt retired without notable results.
1588: With a brilliant burst, her finishing kick was second to none. But that meant she could only race from behind, at the mercy of the pace, so her results were inconsistent. In the Shuka Sho she swept past them all from the back for her first G1, but in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, with the leaders getting an easy run, she closed fastest in 33.2 yet barely made the top five. In the '05 Yasuda Kinen she charged down the long straight for a near-miss 2nd, then came the Takarazuka Kinen. With Tap Dance City and Zenno Rob Roy as anchors, and her last run seen as a fluke, Sweep was 11th choice. But 2 minutes 11 seconds after the start, the crowd learned her kick was real. Closing as ever, she won the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, then rested long with a fracture. Back after a year, she beat colts in the Kyoto Daishoten and was 2nd in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup. Then her kick dulled; she placed in G1s but couldn't break through, and in her farewell, the '07 Queen Elizabeth II Cup, was 3rd.
1590: All her wins came on dirt. She won the Kanto Oaks at Kawasaki on heavy ground, the Marine C. and Sparking Lady C. After a slump she moved to Funabashi, was 2nd in the Queen Sho and TCK Jo-o Hai, then won the Empress Hai and Marine C.
1591: After winning the Kikyo S., he won the Keio Hai 2yo S. easily in a record 1:21.8, then as 4th choice beat Meisho Bowler by a neck in the Asahi Hai FS - JRA champion 2yo colt of '03. At 3 he was 5th in the Spring S., 4th in the Satsuki Sho and 2nd in the NHK Mile C., but broke down in the Derby (12th). Dull after a long break, he won the Swan S., but died of acute heart failure during the next race, the Hankyu Hai.
1583: Won the Flora S. narrowly at 3. In '05 she was 2nd in the Nakayama Himba S., then won the Fukushima Himba S.
1589: After winning a 5-million race and the Fukuryu S., winless on turf, he went to the Satsuki Sho (15th). He won the Hyogo Championship narrowly, then ran poorly in the Derby. On dirt after, apart from a 3rd in the Derby Grand Prix, he did little.
1592: Only 6th choice for the Hanshin JF, she swept down the outside with a 34.5 finish to beat Yamanin Alcyone by a neck - her first graded win a G1. At 3 she was steady: 3rd in the Oka Sho, 5th in the Oaks, 2nd in the Shuka Sho. A closer best at the awkward 1800m, she often fell short, but was strong when things suited: 3 of her 4 wins, incl. the Nakayama Himba S. at 5, came at 1800m.
1593: He won his debut, the Phoenix Sho, Kokura 2yo S. and Daily Hai 2yo S. by wide margins, but as heavy favorite was narrowly 2nd in the Asahi Hai FS. 3rd in the Satsuki Sho, he was judged best at a mile, but was 3rd in the NHK Mile C. and 11th against older horses in the Yasuda Kinen. Running well but not winning in graded races, he tried dirt in the Garnet S. and won by 3 lengths, then the Negishi S. by 7 and the February S. - suddenly top of the dirt world. Then he kept falling short, even in JRA-local races. Back on turf, he was 2nd to Takeover Target in the '06 Sprinters S. At stud he sired Hyogo Junior GP winner Nishiken Mononofu and Hyogo CS winner Ekimae.
1594: Winning in his 4th start, he missed the spring classics and was 12th in the Aoba Sho. In summer he won the Akanko Tokubetsu, a stepping stone to stardom, and with his stamina was a Kikuka Sho dark horse, 6th. Winning in his own class early the next year, he reached open class. In the Tenno Sho (Spring), eyes were on a 4-generation Tenno Sho line from Mejiro Asama, but he led and held on only to 4th behind Admire Jupiter. He then led all the way in the '08 Meguro Kinen. After a long break he returned in the '09 Nikkei Sho without another win, and late in his career switched to jumps, breaking down in a race and having to be put down.
1595: She won her 1600m turf debut and a 5-million race, but was 4th in the Tulip Sho, missing an Oka Sho spot. Aiming for the Oaks, she won the Sweet Pea S., but was 4th, well behind Buena Vista and Red Desire. In the Rose S. she ran down Red Desire, becoming a leading contender. In the Shuka Sho she was hampered at the final turn but crossed the line 3rd behind Red Desire and Buena Vista, promoted to 2nd when Buena Vista was demoted for veering - some said she would have won unimpeded. She was 6th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup. Older, she was 2nd in 3 graded races without winning, proving her ability.
1596: Winning her 3rd start, her first on dirt, she won the Hokkaido 2yo Yushun easily and the year-end Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun. From 3 she kept finishing in double figures, until the '05 Yonago S., her first win in 18 months. Switching to jumps, she won the Yodo Jump S., then moved to Saga and was 9th in her first race there.
1598: He ran in the Satsuki Sho and Derby at 3 without success, but won the Asahi Challenge C. against older horses in autumn. 6th in the Kikuka Sho, he was 2nd in the Naruo Kinen and 3rd in the Osaka-Hamburg C., then ran in an open Tenno Sho (Spring) as 13th choice and unleashed a furious finish to win by 1.5 lengths - a G1 winner. Leg trouble followed, and he retired after 4 winless races. At stud, his 3rd crop's Meisho Mambo won the Oaks as 9th choice, then the Shuka Sho and Queen Elizabeth II Cup, and in 2015 Sunbista won the Champions C. as 12th choice - like their sire, big runs at long odds.
1599: 2nd in the Flower C., she was 9th in the Oka Sho, but 3rd in the Oaks and 5th in the Shuka Sho. After a slump, at 4 she won the Niigata Kinen and Fuchu Himba S., starring in fillies' graded races until a ligament injury cost her a year. Back, she was 3rd against colts in the Niigata Kinen and 5th in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai, surely too far. Racing on at 7 in '08 without her old spark, she retired to breed.
1600: He won his debut, the Phoenix Sho (OP) and the Kokura 2yo S. from a good spot - 3 straight. Winless for a while, he won the Kita-Kyushu Tankyori S. (16M) at his beloved Kokura, his first win in 2 years.
1601: In 2004 he won the US double unbeaten, but was 2nd in the Belmont S., narrowly missing the Triple Crown. Winning his first 5 with ease, he won his first graded race, the Arkansas Derby, then the Kentucky Derby. Heavy favorite at 1.7 in the Preakness, he won by a record 11.5 lengths, hailed as "the second coming of Secretariat." In the Belmont the Triple Crown seemed certain at 1.35, but just as he looked the winner, outsider Birdstone caught him near the line. He retired after it, Eclipse champion 3yo colt, and went to stud, siring some stakes winners but no stars. Dance Partner famously went from Japan to be bred to him, but the foal, Smarty Dance, won just once.
1602: Up-and-down in form, but talented enough to beat later G1 winner Tall Poppy. Just short of classic class, he came good in winter at 3, winning an open special and then the Chunichi Shimbun Hai. At 4 he was 2nd in the Nakayama Kimpai, Kokura Daishoten and Chukyo Kinen, then beat double classic filly Buena Vista in the Sapporo Kinen, a G1 contender. Struggling after, he switched to dirt and won his first dirt race, the Sirius S., with authority from 2nd, and was a close 2nd in it the next year.
1603: A famous stayer who won the 4000m G1 Gold C. 4 times. Winning his first 3, he was an English Derby fancy, but injury cost him his 3yo season. Back in spring at 4, racing mainly over 12 furlongs+, he won his first G1, the Coronation C. After some losses, he won the Gold C. at 5, the Gold C. and Irish St. Leger at 6, the Gold C. and Prix Royal-Oak at 7, and the Gold C. again at 8 - the first to win it 4 times. Cartier champion stayer 4 years running, 5 to 8, he retired after a 3rd in the Prix du Cadran that autumn. At stud in Ireland, his first crop debuted in 2013, without notable runners yet.
1604: Winner of 7 G1s incl. the English and Irish Oaks and BC Filly & Mare Turf, and Cartier Horse of the Year in 2004 and 2006. She came to the Japan Cup twice and was 3rd to Deep Impact. At 3, in her first stakes race, she won the Oaks by 7 lengths, then the Irish Oaks in record time, was 3rd to Bago in the Arc, and won the BC Filly & Mare Turf in America - Horse of the Year. At 4 wins were scarce, 5th to Alkaased in the Japan Cup, but she won the year-end Hong Kong Vase. At 5 she won 3 middle-distance G1s - Prince of Wales's S., Nassau S. and BC Filly & Mare Turf - and was 3rd to Deep Impact in the Japan Cup, Horse of the Year again, retiring at year's end. As a broodmare she produced English and Irish Derby winner Australia.
1606: Named after a princess in Greek myth. A late bloomer, she ran in her first JRA-local race, Oi's TCK Jo-o Hai, in 2013 at 5, then swept the Marine C. (Funabashi), Sparking Lady C. (Kawasaki), Ladies' Prelude (Oi) and Ladies' Classic (Kanazawa), all as favorite - 5 of 5 in fillies' dirt graded races. She won the 2014 TCK Jo-o Hai easily under a heavy 57kg and retired to breed.
1607: A fast sprinter nicknamed "the Rising Sun Kamikaze." He led all the way to win his first 3, and at his peak at 5 won the Sprinters S. by a wide margin, plus the Keio Hai AH and open races at 1400-1800m - unbeatable at sprint-mile trips. He also ran in the Derby, Japan Cup and Arima Kinen, leading and holding on for 4th in the Derby. At stud he sired gritty middle-distance horses like Yuwa Beam and Nishiyama Sho.
1609: A star at a mile to middle distances, incl. the Kinko Sho and Milers C. Racing until 6 (old age system), he won 8 of 14, always in the top three. Leg trouble kept him out of the classics at 4, but he won the Kinko Sho instead. At 5 he won the Milers C. and Lord Derby Challenge T. and was 2nd in the long Kyoto Daishoten. He retired after a 3rd in the Milers C. at 6. At stud he steadily sired graded winners like Kokura Sansai S. winner Dandy Apollo and Daily Hai Sansai S. winner Idol Mary.
1610: A leading fancy in the 1977 classics. 2nd in the Yayoi Sho, he was 6th as 3rd choice in the Satsuki Sho, rallied for 3rd to Lucky Ruler in the Derby, then was 5th in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai and Kikuka Sho - no classic. Often short as an older horse, he came good from May at 5 (old age system), winning the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai and Nihon Keizai Sho, and was 2nd in the Mainichi Okan and Meguro Kinen in autumn. 5th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he then ran the race of his life in the Arima Kinen: in a field packed with stars like crop Kikuka Sho winner Press Tosho, Green Grass and Hokuto Boy, and Erimo George, Kane Minobu was only 9th choice, yet raced handy and left them all behind in record time. Later he won only the Meguro Kinen and Mainichi Okan at 7, but was out of the top five just twice. At stud he sired graded winners like Mainichi Hai winner Key Minobu and Arlington C. winner Grand Shingeki.
1611: The 1978 Kikuka Sho winner. Debuting early, in June at 3 (old age system), he ran 9 times that year - a heavy schedule. Graded-winless but always in the top five, he was 2nd to Bamboton Court in the Hanshin Sansai S. At 4 he ran in all 3 classics: 2nd to Fantast in the Satsuki Sho as 5th choice, then 6th to Sakura Shori in the Derby, his first time out of the top five. 2nd in an open race and 4th in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, he was 3rd choice for the Kikuka Sho behind Derby winner Sakura Shori and Kobe Shimbun Hai winner Bamboton Court, and broke clear from midfield to win. Older, he won the Kimpai (West), then leg trouble sidelined him; after one prep he was 13th in the Arima Kinen and retired. At stud he steadily sired winners like Kita-Kyushu Kinen winner Ibuki Five One and Chunichi Shimbun Hai winner Shori Tenyu.
1612: A colorful front-runner who livened up the classics. 2nd in the Niigata Sansai S., he won the Fuyo Tokubetsu. Crushed in the Keisei Hai, he won the Junior C. and Kisaragi Sho, but missed the top five in the Satsuki Sho and Derby.
1613: With 2 wins and two 2nds from 5, she was a fine 5th in the Oaks as 16th choice, then 3rd in the Rose S. and Queen Elizabeth Cup - no fluke. 2nd in the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu, she won her farewell, the Chukyo Kinen, at 4.
1614: 2nd in the Kokura Sansai S. and Keisei Hai Sansai S., she showed promise at 2. She won the Flower C. and, ridden by master Yukio Okabe as 5th choice, was 4th in the Oka Sho behind Max Beauty and Kosei.
1615: He won the Chunichi Sports Sho Yonsai S. in July at 3 as 8th choice, then was 2nd to Max Beauty in the Kobe Shimbun Hai. A front-runner like his sire, gritty when leading, he also did well from midfield when older - five G3 2nds.
1616: She missed the fillies' classics, but the next year won the Nakayama Himba S. as 7th choice, then as 12th choice beat Material in the Epsom C. - a classic longshot, winning unfancied and flopping when fancied.
1618: He won the Keihan Hai and Epsom C. at 4. No more wins but six 2nds, incl. the Kokura Daishoten and Nakayama Kinen. A namesake debuted in '04 - the owner loved the name.
