1619: Unbeaten in 3, a classic hope, he won the Spring S. and was Satsuki Sho favorite, but was hampered by veering from Meiner Frisse (Yutaka Take) and May Brave (Norihiro Yokoyama), 6th. He never shone again.
1620: He won the Daily Hai Sansai S. as 10th choice and was 2nd in the Hanshin Sansai S. An early bloomer, he kept finishing in double figures from 3, even after dropping in class, and retired at 7.
1621: 2nd to Sakura Chiyono O in the Asahi Hai Sansai S. A front-running sprinter, he skipped the classics for the Crystal C., winning by 4 lengths. Winless against older sprinters, he moved to Hokkaido at 5.
1622: After his debut win he was crushed in the Shinzan Kinen, Pegasus S. (G3: 1600m) and Mainichi Hai. Winning 3 straight in his own class, he rested over a year. Losing badly at first, he learned to race forward and won the Aichi Hai.
1623: He won the Mainichi Hai, "Kansai's last train to the classics," and went to the Satsuki Sho as Kansai's secret weapon, but was hampered by a fall and beaten badly. He won the Kyoto Yonsai Tokubetsu, but a fracture ended his career.
1624: He won the Keisei Hai early at 3, but was 14th in the Yayoi Sho, 6th in the Satsuki Sho and 8th in the Derby. He beat older horses in the Hakodate Kinen, then retired after a 9th in the Kikuka Sho.
1625: 2nd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai at 3, he was 7th in the Kikuka Sho, then won the Aichi Hai. Steady but often short, 4th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he won the Kimpai (West) at 5 and later became a lead pony.
1626: Missing the classics, she was 2nd in the Sapphire S., then won the Rose S. in record time as 7th choice over Daiichi Ruby. 10th in the Queen Elizabeth Cup, she kept finishing in double figures. No notable foals.
1627: With 1 win at 2 he ran in the Hanshin Sansai S., 7th to Ibuki Maikagura, then fractured a leg and rested about a year. Back at the end of 3, kept to dirt sprints, he gradually showed his ability: the February H. (G3) at 5, then 4 dirt open specials, '93 champion dirt horse - king of the dirt. But in that era, before dirt racing was organized, he won just one graded race. At stud, from few foals, he sired Meisho Butler, winner of 8 graded races on turf and dirt.
1628: A light, speedy sprinter and supporting player of early-'90s older sprints. Over 1200m on turf he had 6 wins and five 2nds; allowed his own pace up front, he was feared as unstoppable. But in 3 Sprinters S. he never got his pace: 8th, 5th, 14th. His misfortune was a sprint era too deep, with Sakura Bakushin O and Nishino Flower.
1629: Originally at local Kawasaki, he moved to the JRA in spring at 3 for his talent, but struggled to adapt to turf. He won the year-end Negishi S. on dirt, but was 12th in the Sprinters S. "Even 1200m is too far," they said of this extreme sprinter, yet he kept running in graded races, mainly over 1200m on turf, and won the Lord Derby Challenge T. in '92 and '93. Late in his career he was 14th in Hong Kong.
1631: A classic late-blooming stayer, he came good in autumn at 4 with 5- and 9-million wins, then was 2nd in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai and Stayers S. The next year he won the Diamond S. and was 2nd in the Hanshin Daishoten. 9th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he tried middle distances, 2nd in the Niigata Kinen. Pure white even while racing, he had many fans. He later served as a lead pony at Nakayama and died in 2008.
1597: Near the top in allowances, he used his light weight to lead all the way in the '08 Tanabata Sho, winning the Summer 2000 Series. Later he won the Meguro Kinen on heavy ground by 5 lengths over Jaguar Mail, then the Tanabata Sho again. After a big loss in the Sapporo Kinen, he won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. He retired after the Nikkei Sho at 8 and became a lead pony at Chukyo.
1605: Half-brother of Danon Velvet, 2nd to Buena Vista in the 2008 Hanshin JF. Unlike his early-peaking sister, he emerged in summer at 4, winning the Christmas C. 4th to Danon Ballade in his first graded race, the American JCC, he won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai with the fastest finish.
1608: Winner of the 1982 Tenno Sho (Spring) and Takarazuka Kinen. Up to 4 he was often favored but fell short - 2nd in the Derby, Kikuka Sho and Tenno Sho (Autumn), 3rd in the Arima Kinen - "the uncrowned emperor." At 5 he finally bloomed, winning both. He disliked heavy ground, so was also called "the Emperor of the Sun."
1630: Leading alone and controlling the pace, he won big; otherwise he lost big, regardless of odds or rivals - longshot fans loved him. In his first G1, the Takarazuka Kinen, he was last, over 5 seconds behind Mejiro McQueen; next, in the Takamatsunomiya Hai, he cruised to a record win over Narita Taishin, Machikane Tannhauser and others. Late in his career he raced in Iwate and Utsunomiya without winning.
1632: A foreign-bred by Mt. Livermore, a fast mid-level sprinter. Much like his sire, he used powerful early speed to shine in dirt sprints. An accident at 3 cost him nearly a year, but about 6 months after his return, in autumn at 4, he won the Negishi S. Just as he seemed to be coming good, he broke down in the next year's Kan'etsu S. and did not survive.
1633: Prominent early, 2nd in the Shinzan Kinen, but as a gelding he watched the classics from the sidelines. When he settled he had a sharp kick, winning the Fukushima Kinen and Chukyo Kinen. He moved to Kanazawa at 6.
1634: He won his first 2, then did little - strong in open specials but crushed in graded races. Then at 5 he suddenly ran big in the Osaka Hai, beating previous Tenno Sho winner Nehai Caesar and others at over 100 to 1.
1635: Hard to believe given his later fame, but he was last choice on debut. He led all the way to win by 7 lengths, then beat Rugger Champion and others in the Niigata Sansai S., a leading 2yo contender, but injury then cost him over 6 months. His comeback was the Satsuki Sho, straight off the break; a miracle was hoped for, but he was 16th, then 13th in the Derby. Never his old self, he ran big again as 10th choice to win the Fukushima Kinen. In 19 more races, double-figure finishes were common and 4th his best, and he retired after the Diamond S. at 7.
1637: A superb blueblood: granddaughter of Oaks winner Agnes Lady, niece of Oka Sho winner Agnes Flora, among other classic winners. In her 3rd start she beat Oguri Roman by half a length in the Tulip Sho, a classic leading lady, but was 8th in the Oka Sho and 3rd in the Oaks. 3rd in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, she was 2nd in the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu, Kimpai (West) and Chunichi Shimbun Hai, but never won another graded race.
1638: He needed 11 starts to win, but grew enough to run in the Kikuka Sho that autumn. Older, he won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai, then beat Agnes Parade and others with authority in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai.
1639: From the 2nd crop of Arima Kinen and Dubai Sheema Classic winner Heart's Cry, related to Horse of the Year Sakura Laurel. A classic hope from a foal, he debuted late and was 9th as 2nd choice in the Aoba Sho, giving up the spring classics. 9th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, he skipped the Kikuka Sho - perhaps for the best. Fresh from a 10-million win, he ran in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai and, helped by a light weight, raced forward and powered home to win. 2nd to Fenomeno in the Nikkei Sho, his talent was blooming, but after the Meguro Kinen he rested long, running just once in 2014.
1641: She rose on dirt, but late in her career was a fine turf sprinter, winning the Sapporo Sprint S. at 4 and 5. Her 2nd win gave jockey Tomio Yasuda the first-ever graded wins at all 10 JRA tracks, making headlines. She raced tough until the end of 6 without another win. As a dam, hopes of a sprinter beyond her have not yet been met.
1642: Suited to flat left-handed tracks, 5 of his 7 wins came at Chukyo. He clicked with jockey Jotaro Horai: from late at 4, with Horai his regular rider, he improved sharply, winning the Chunichi Shimbun Hai twice and the Aichi Hai - 3 graded races for Japan-sired horses at Chukyo. Injured at 6, he rested 8 months and returned in the next Chunichi Shimbun Hai, going for a 3rd straight win, but his old kick was gone - last all the way.
1643: Slow to leave the lower classes, he won the March S. at 5 and again the next year, then the Antares S. He tried the Teio Sho and Tokyo Daishoten, but the G1 wall was high; he never even made the top five.
1645: He starred around a mile on dirt. Often 2nd at 3, stuck in allowances, he came good at 4, winning 3 straight to the March S., then the Procyon S. - both with furious charges from the back at the final turn.
1646: Full brother of Oka Sho winner Cheers Grace, much hoped for from the start. At 3 he was 2nd by half a length to Tanino Gimlet in the Shinzan Kinen, then won the Kyodo News Hai and Mainichi Hai, a classic contender. But he was 12th in the Satsuki Sho and 16th in the Derby. Older, back from 8 months off, he was beaten badly, and in autumn '03 died suddenly on the way back to his stable from pasture.
1647: Coming good at 4, he quickly left the allowances and won the Kabutoyama Kinen, then the Sakuranbo Kinen in autumn at 4 and the Gumma Kinen easily in spring at 5. Oddly, all 3 graded races he won were abolished the following year. In '05 he broke the jinx by winning the Kashiwa Kinen, just promoted to G1, then was 2nd in the Teio Sho. Repeated long breaks with leg trouble followed, and he retired without regaining his form.
1648: He won the Keio Hai 2yo S. at 2. In the classics he was 4th in the Spring S. and 13th in the Satsuki Sho. Switching to dirt sprints in autumn, he won the Shimotsuki S., then struggled until the Galaxy S. late at 4. In form, he won the Procyon S. by 2.5 lengths, then the Sirius S. and JBC Sprint. In '06 he won the Kurofune Sho, Nambu Hai, JBC Mile and the big year-end Tokyo Daishoten. In '07 he won the Kashiwa Kinen and Nambu Hai and was 2nd in the February S. and Teio Sho, and in '08 the Nambu Hai again - his 7th G1, equal to Deep Impact and T.M. Opera O. Still going at 8, he kept trying G1s, barely making the top five, and retired after an 8th in the '09 JBC Classic without breaking the record.
1651: 15th on debut, he recovered to win a maiden next time. Missing the spring classics, he won the Shirayuri S., his first open win, then ran in the Kobe Shimbun Hai for a classic spot and swept past "Big Three" members Unrivaled and Reach the Crown down the wide outside with a powerful finish. So impressive was it that he was 2nd choice for the Kikuka Sho, but 4th, then 4th as favorite in his first race against older horses, the Naruo Kinen. Struggling after, he died after breaking down in a race.
1652: A Southern Kanto star who won the 1981 Tokyo Daishoten. Moving to the JRA early at 6, he was 14th in the Swan S. and then moved to Iwate, winning 9 there until summer at 8. He died suddenly after just one year at stud, but his foals included Toukei Nisei, a local legend with 39 wins from 43.
1654: Debuting at 4 (old age system), long stuck in allowances, he won the Sapporo Nikkei Sho above his class at 5, then in the Sapporo Kinen beat that year's Satsuki Sho winner Tosho Boy and Derby winner Climb Kaiser - no ordinary horse. In autumn he won the All Comers and ran in the Arima Kinen, 14th behind Tosho Boy over his first long trip. He won the Lord Derby Challenge T. at 6 and raced until 8.
1655: Debuting at local Mizusawa, he was ordinary at 2, with 2 wins from 6. At 3 he came good fast, winning Kaminoyama's Tohoku Yushun and Iwate's derby, the Kozukata Sho, and was 3rd against older horses in the Nambu Hai. He also won the big local Derby Grand Prix. Moving to the JRA at 4, he was 10th in the Nakayama Kinen, then injured; after a long break he moved to Hokkaido racing, raced until 9 (9 wins from 54) and went to stud.
1656: As a local horse in the All Comers at 5, he was 2nd to runaway leader Twin Turbo, part of an upset. Last in 2 straight Japan Cups, he left a poor impression on JRA fans, but his record at home in Southern Kanto was truly first-class. Moving to the JRA at 7, he chased a first JRA win in vain, switched to jumps, and broke down fatally in his 2nd jump race.
1658: Based at Oi. Much hoped for, but debuting late, in February at 3, he couldn't run in the Southern Kanto classics. Free of major setbacks, he raced steadily until 7: 15 wins and eight 2nds from 40. No big titles, but his consistency won many fans, and winning graded races at all 4 Southern Kanto tracks, incl. the Urawa Kinen and Tokyo Hai, made him a star.
1659: Debuting in Hokkaido racing (3 wins from 13), he blossomed after moving to Kiyomatsu Akama's stable at Oi, winning the Tokyo Kinen and Tokyo Daishoten at 4. The next year he tried JRA turf races, beaten badly.
1660: Debuting late, in April at 3, he won by 9 lengths. Shin trouble cost him 5 months; he won on return, but a fracture was found, costing 11 months. Back in autumn at 4, 5th first time, he won 2 more, then never got right and couldn't race until 6 - 5 wins from 6 - and moved to Hokkaido racing. There he raced steadily, winning 16 as a top local horse, incl. the Mizuho Sho 4 years running, from 9 to 12. He also raced in JRA-local graded races like the JRA's Elm S., winning his first, the Hokkaido Sprint C., at 12. At 13 he won Hokkaido's Etoile Sho, setting a new record as Japan's oldest graded winner.
1661: His sire San O I was an unbeaten Southern Kanto Triple Crown winner. Inheriting his talent, Tomishino Porunga starred at Kasamatsu, winning most of its major races. At 5 he tried JRA races: 3rd in the Heian S., then his first JRA win in the turf TV Aichi Open, and a fine 4th in the All Comers - NAR's best older horse that year. The next year he tried the Takarazuka Kinen, 10th to Dantsu Seattle.
1662: His name, similar to a great sire's, made him surprisingly well known. A local horse who ran 78 times across Niigata, Kasamatsu, Nagoya, Kanazawa and Saga, strong on heavy ground. No G1-class wins, but 21 wins is a fine record.
1663: A blueblood of the Star Roch family, but needing 7 starts to win and then stuck, with 1 win he moved to local Nagoya in summer at 3 - and was transformed. Winning powerfully, he swept the Tokai area's graded races and was NAR's best older horse in '95 and '96. Representing local racing, he fought great battles with JRA stars like Hokuto Vega and Kyoto City, lighting up JRA-local racing, and boldly tried JRA turf graded races like the Nikkei Sho and Kyoto Daishoten. With 19 wins from 35 locally, he retired at 6 and went to stud.
1664: Meant to debut in the JRA, leg trouble sent him to local Kanazawa, where he won and won, including the Derby Grand Prix in record time with a furious charge - called Kanazawa's greatest ever. Leg trouble plagued his later career.
1665: Based at local Funabashi. Winning his first 7, he drew attention and won the Kawasaki Kinen the next year. But JRA-local racing had begun, pitting him against JRA stars like Hokuto Vega and Lively Mount. He tried turf races like the All Comers without success, and never won a JRA-local graded race, but raced until 9 with 17 wins. Late on he moved to Hokkaido racing without more wins.
1668: Winner of the Tokyo Hai at 4 and 5. Racing at Oi, Kaminoyama and Hokkaido, he ran 73 times. Winless from 7, he won once more at 10, and his last race was over 1800m on Monbetsu dirt in autumn at 11.
1669: Based at local Niigata. From his 3rd start he won 12 straight and the JRA-local Gumma Kinen. A monster at home, he struggled against the JRA's wall in JRA-local races.
1670: Based at local Iwate. A fast horse on dirt and turf. At 2 he raced in the JRA, 2nd in the Dahlia Sho and 3rd in the Niigata Sansai S. At 6 he won Oi's Tokyo Hai, unbeatable in sprints. Moving to Kochi at 8, he raced 104 times until 10.
1671: Debuting in Hokkaido racing (4 wins from 6), he moved to Funabashi and won the Tokyo Okansho and Tokyo Derby. Older, he starred in JRA-local races, winning the Kashiwa Kinen and Nippon TV Hai, though never a G1.
1636: Beaten in the Wakaba S., his first middle-distance race, he gave up the classics and, the day before the Satsuki Sho, led all the way in the sprint Crystal C. - his only graded title. He later moved to Iwate.
1640: Debuting in Hokkaido racing, he won 7 of 17 and moved to the JRA, where he struggled at first. But on heavy ground he was 2nd in the Niigata Daishoten and Epsom C., then on a bog in the Mainichi Okan led all the way over a star field incl. Genuine and Sakura Chitose O. He also won the Kabutoyama Kinen on soft ground - a mudlark, "the horse with webbed feet." Injured at 7, he returned to Hokkaido racing and raced until 9.
1644: Improving from autumn at 4, he won the Kabutoyama Kinen and Fukushima Kinen and was 6th in the Arima Kinen. He later won the Kokura Kinen and was 2nd in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai - a local-track star.
1649: After 2 dirt wins he switched to turf in autumn at 3, won 2 allowances and was a nose 2nd in the American JCC, then beat Zenno Rob Roy by a neck in the Nikkei Sho. He then struggled, fractured a leg in the '06 Arima Kinen, was injured again in training, and retired to stud in '08. Blind in his right eye, yet battling on in graded races, he still has many fans.
1650: Won 3 in Southern Kanto, incl. the Kanto Oaks. Dam of Hokkaido Sansai Yushun winner Takino Special.
1653: Plagued by fractures, in only his 2nd graded race, the Asahi Challenge C. at 4, he won when Nishino Raiden, first past the post, was disqualified. 2nd in the Takamatsunomiya Hai (G2), he battled on at 5, then moved to local racing and shone: he won Kanazawa's Hakusan Daishoten, then Nagoya's Tokai Kikkasho and Nagoya Daishoten easily, and won at Kasamatsu too. He retired at 7 to stud.
1666: Based at Kawasaki. With fierce, explosive runs, he won the Tokyo Okansho and Tokyo Daishoten. Injured before a Hanshin Daishoten bid, he broke down fatally on his return.
1667: Based at Kasamatsu. He won the Tokai Derby, Thoroughbred Challenge C. and the Derby Grand Prix, making his name nationwide. At 4 he was 3rd behind Narita Brian and Mayano Top Gun in the JRA's Hanshin Daishoten.
1672: Based at Kasamatsu. Unbeaten in 5, he tried the JRA's Daily Hai Sansai S., 7th to Seeking the Pearl, but won Kasamatsu's Junior Grand Prix and more, NAR champion 2yo of '96. At 3 he won the JRA-local Nagoya Yushun.
1674: By minor sire Pekin Ryuen. Debuting at Funabashi, he won 21 with powerful runs, above all as an older horse: at 5 he won the Urawa Kinen by 3 lengths from Surprise Power, and at 6 the Teio Sho.
1675: Debuting in Hokkaido racing, he moved to Oi. Quiet at 2, he won the Tokyo Okansho at 3, joining the elite, then starred in JRA-local races, winning the Zen-Nihon Thoroughbred C. and Oguri Cap Kinen.
1677: Debuting in Hokkaido racing (4 wins from 6), he moved to Oi, won the Wakajishi Tokubetsu and Keihin Hai, then the Haneda Hai, the first classic. 3rd in the Tokyo Okansho, he won the Tokyo Derby for 2 Southern Kanto classics, then the Japan Dirt Derby against the nation's best - NAR champion 4yo of '99. At 4 he was beaten badly in the February S. and Japan Cup Dirt.
1678: Debuting at Funabashi, she won her first 5 incl. the Kanto Oaks, then after a 2nd won 4 more incl. the TCK Jo-o Hai. After winning the JRA-local Marine C. she was injured; back, she had lost her power and was always beaten badly.
1679: Based at Kasamatsu. Strong on dirt, even faster on turf. At 2 he led all the way to win the JRA's Daily Hai Sansai S. by 2.5 lengths over prospect Rugger Regulus, then was favorite in the Asahi Hai Sansai S. despite being a local horse, caught near the line by Eishin Preston for 2nd. Long injury breaks kept graded wins away, but at 6 he won the Zen-Nihon Thoroughbred C. and raced until retiring at 10 at the end of '07, with 26 wins.
1681: Based at Kasamatsu. After winning a JRA-certified debut, he twice ran in JRA races, beaten badly, then at 3 was 5th in the Wakaba S. NAR champion 4yo of 2000, he boldly kept taking on the JRA, running 3 times in the Hanshin Daishoten and in G1s like the Japan Cup Dirt and Takarazuka Kinen - 17 JRA races in all, without a win, until retiring at 9.
1682: Moved from Aichi to Funabashi. Won the Thoroughbred Challenge C. at 3 and kept trying JRA-local races.
1683: Debuting on turf at Morioka, which has a turf course, he won 3 straight, then tried the JRA: he won the Ivy S. easily, was 2nd by 0.1s in the Keio Hai Sansai S., and 3rd in the Asahi Hai Sansai S., the 2yo championship. The next spring he was 2nd in the NZ Trophy and 4th in the NHK Mile C. Moving to Oi when older, he kept running in the JRA, winning the TV Aichi Open and Ocean S. (OP). Of 52 races, 40 were in the JRA, and as a local horse he ran just 8 on dirt - hopeless there, 8th or worse in 6 - a truly unique local horse. In '06 he won the Ocean S., newly a G3 - his first graded win at 8. Racing on into '08, he was clearly past it and retired in July without running.
1684: Based at Funabashi. Half-brother of Tulip Sho winner Jodi Shiraoki. With 3 wins and a 2nd from 4, he went to the JRA's Unicorn S. and won as 7th choice. After the '03 Hochi Grand Prix C. he never ran again, retiring in April '05.
1685: Debuting in Hokkaido racing, he won the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun, NAR champion 2yo. At 3 he moved to Oi, won the Haneda Hai and was 3rd in the Japan Dirt Derby. Winless after moving to the JRA at 4, he went to Saga.
1687: Debuting at Kaminoyama, he moved to Kasamatsu. He tried the JRA at 3 without winning, but older regained his strength, winning the Diolite Kinen and Oguri Cap Kinen. After a long break he raced on until 9 and went to stud.
1688: A Tokai local star with 14 wins, he ran in the All Comers and broke clear from a good spot to win. In the Japan Cup he was 7th, a bold, creditable run. Moving to the JRA at 5, he made his mark again: in his 2nd race, the Nikkei Sho, well behind winner Mihoshinzan, he beat previous Derby winner Dyna Gulliver by a head in a straight duel for 2nd - a local horse's pride.
1689: Based at Takasaki, winner of many graded races like the Tango Sho and Kaisetsu Kinen. His short life peaked in '88 in the Nambu Hai at Mizusawa, a new East Japan dirt championship: representing Takasaki, he won, "the hero of Takasaki," famous nationwide. The next year, at his peak after winning Takasaki's Kaisetsu Kinen, he was brought down in a fall in the Teio Sho and, with a severe fracture, had to be put down. 22 wins from 58; many fans were captivated by his fighting runs, and he is remembered as "the ill-fated dirt king."
1690: Useless on turf, but after a 2nd in Chukyo's Winter S. to Life Tateyama, then the JRA's best dirt horse, he moved to Kasamatsu, as "the JRA has few dirt races." With Katsumi Ando aboard he was unbeatable at Kasamatsu and Nagoya. In the '88 Zen-Nihon Thoroughbred C. he beat Inari One (then at Oi), next year's JRA Horse of the Year - the top dirt horse. In '89 he went to Oi and won the Teio Sho easily. At home his winning was a given; the only question was by how many lengths. He won Sapporo's Breeders' Gold C., then returned home for the Zen-Nihon Thoroughbred C. - but pulled up after one lap, leaving the crowd stunned. Judged hopeless, he was too great to put down at once; after 3 weeks of treatment he died.
1693: Based at Oi. Emerging early with the Tokyo Sansai Yushun Himba, she won the first Derby Grand Prix despite being a filly. As a dam she produced decent runners Aquilone (93: Dancing Brave) and Tight Squeeze (95: Tight Spot).
1695: A top Oi filly who won the Tokyo Sansai Yushun Himba. In a strong era for local racing, she was consistent and won the Derby Grand Prix, a grand new local event, following Tomi Alco for an Oi double. Moving to the JRA at 4, she never made the top five in 3 starts and retired. As a dam she produced Back Gear (99: Jade Robbery), with 5 local wins incl. the Bluebird C.
1696: Debuting at Utsunomiya, he showed rare talent; he came good at Kaminoyama, then moved to Oi, winning big races like the Tokyo Daishoten, Kawasaki Kinen and Grand Champion 2000. NAR Horse of the Year in '90 and '91, he was then local racing's all-time top earner. Joining the JRA in '91, he disliked turf - 8th in the Osaka Hai, 16th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) - and returned to Oi after just 2 races.
1697: Debuting at Oi, he won the Tokyo Okansho, Kawasaki Kinen and Derby Grand Prix, then the Diamond Tokubetsu after moving to Kasamatsu. Joining the JRA with 11 wins from 20, his best in 3 open races was second-last.
1698: Based at Oi, he was 2nd in the All Comers at 5 and went to the Japan Cup, where he stayed at the back and finished last. The next year he won the All Comers, and in the Japan Cup led boldly - but was last again.
1701: The chief rival of Swift Seidai, Tohoku's monster, in fierce battles at Iwate. Long unable to beat him, "the foil," he finally did so in the Kitakamigawa Daishoten at 6.
1702: Debuting at Kasamatsu, he won 24, including the 2nd Oguri Cap Kinen.
1703: A big sprinter typical of Sakura Bakushin O. Debuting early in the year, he won 3 straight incl. an open race. 6th in the NHK Mile C., against older horses he was 3rd in the Centaur S. and Keihan Hai and 4th in the year-end Hanshin C., promising more. But he was beaten badly as favorite in the Silk Road S. and 9th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen. After 6 months off he won the Nagaokakyo S. (16M), then the Keihan Hai. The next year he kept disappointing; a 2nd in the Australia T. (OP) hinted at a revival, but he broke down fatally. His half-sister Curren Chan later won the Sprinters S., the sprint G1 he never managed.
1704: He won his debut and, after a 3rd in the Icho S., charged from midfield to win the Keio Hai 2yo S. 2nd choice in the Asahi Hai FS, he was 11th, perhaps hurt by a wide draw. After winning the Baden-Baden C. in summer at 3, he focused on sprints, a fair 5th in the Sprinters S., then struggled.
1705: A Brian's Time dirt horse. He won an open race at 3, but kept falling short in graded races. His turning point came at 5 in the Mercury C., beating Smart Falcon, then unbeatable in JRA-local races, by 4 lengths. He won the Nippon TV Hai too, and on that run met Vermilion in the JBC Classic, a narrow 2nd but proving his class. He never won a G1, but won the Nagoya GP, March S. and more.
1706: Strong on dirt early, she won the 2yo JRA-local Edelweiss Sho. After a 15th in the Oka Sho she focused on JRA-local races, winning the Hyogo Championship, but phlegmon forced a long break and she retired.
1707: He won his debut and the Icho S., then was 3rd as Asahi Hai favorite. He won the Keisei Hai but flopped in the Satsuki Sho and Derby. Never living up to his "superstar" billing, after a year off he officially retired in '08.
1708: After her debut and the Kaede Sho, she won the Hanshin JF as 8th choice, sweeping past Fusaichi Pandora and other favorites - 2yo queen. But she was 8th in the Oka Sho and 11th in the Oaks, then rested long. Back in the '07 Kyoto Kimpai she was 16th, then 12th on dirt in the TCK Jo-o Hai. After a long slump, her retirement was set for the '09 Nikkei Shinshun Hai - where she ran away in front and held them all off, her first win in about 3 years, so she raced on. Dull after, she was only 12th choice in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, also a Kyoto middle-distance race, but ran away in front with Queen Spumante and held off heavy favorite Buena Vista's charge for 2nd. After more heavy defeats from the front, she retired to breed.
1709: Top two in 11 straight dirt sprints from his debut, he was 13th in his first graded race, the Garnet S. Managed carefully with leg trouble, he seemed in decline, but led all the way to win the '08 Hokkaido Sprint C. After double-figure finishes, he retired after the May '09 Ritto S. to be a riding horse.
1711: Full sister of Fusaichi Ho O (3 graded wins incl. the Kyodo News Hai). 2nd on debut, she won a maiden, then was 2nd to colt Yamanin Kingly in the Kigiku Sho. With 1 win, she was still 3rd choice for the Hanshin JF, and won, holding off Reve d'Amour by a neck - 2yo queen. At 3 she was 2nd in the Tulip Sho and 8th as Oka Sho favorite. In the Oaks she surged from midfield in the straight to hold off FT Maia and Les Grenettes. After the Oaks she was 6th in the Rose S. and 10th in the Shuka Sho, then kept finishing in double figures, retiring to breed after a 17th in the 2010 Hanshin Himba S.
1617: Won a debut race and the Sapporo Sansai S., then never won again in the JRA; raced at Iwate etc.
1673: Debuting in Hokkaido racing, he moved to the JRA after a 2nd in the Zen-Nihon Sansai Yushun. In the classics he was 4th in the Kyodo News Hai, then crushed in the Spring S. and Crystal C., and struggled on dirt too. At 4 he moved to Southern Kanto, won 5 straight and 3 JRA-local graded races - Urawa Kinen, Kawasaki Kinen, Diolite Kinen - NAR's best older horse in 2000.
1676: Based at Iwate. Unbeaten in 9 from his debut, he beat Wing Arrow, Toshin Blizzard and others in the Tokyo Daishoten at 5, and won the Nambu Hai the next year - NAR Horse of the Year in '01 and '02.
1686: Based at Funabashi. He won the Haneda Hai and Tokyo Derby, both by 5 lengths, top of his crop. At 4 he won 2 unified G2s, and in '05 was 3rd in the Kashiwa Kinen and Teio Sho. Strong at local level but unable to beat JRA horses in unified graded races, he retired without a G1 in '08 and went to stud.
1691: Based at Oi. Apart from a 3rd at 2: 9 wins and three 2nds from 13 - always placed. Winning the Haneda Hai, Tokyo Derby, Tokyo Hai and Tokyo Okansho in a row, he became the 5th Southern Kanto Triple Crown winner.
1692: Based at Funabashi. Debuting late, in January at 3, he won 7 straight; up to his record win in the Diolite Kinen he had 12 wins and three 2nds from 15. But as heavy favorite in the Teio Sho he was 5th, and only 2nd in graded races after.
1700: 5 wins from 24 in Southern Kanto, incl. the Kanto Oaks and Keisei Hai.
1710: Needing 4 starts to win, he was 2nd to later Satsuki Sho winner Victory in the Wakaba S. and ran in the Satsuki Sho (13th). After a break he won 3 straight to the Chunichi Shimbun Hai. In '08 he won the Epsom C., then the next February's Kokura Daishoten, and was 4th in the Tenno Sho (Spring). He kept livening up middle-distance turf races with a reliable charge from last.
1712: A blueblood whose half-brothers were Tenno Sho runner-up Swift Current and Yasuda Kinen winner Asakusa Den'en. Favorite on debut in October at 2, he was narrowly 2nd to Rose Kingdom, later Asahi Hai FS winner. Two weeks later he won a maiden easily, then the Kyoto 2yo S. with a sharp kick, and the Radio Nikkei Hai 2yo S., a classic gateway, with a 34.2 finish - the top hope of his crop. At 3 he won the Yayoi Sho, then as favorite burst up the inside to win the Satsuki Sho, 5 straight. Heavy 2.1 favorite for the Derby, he closed in 33.4 but bowed to Eishin Flash's astonishing 32.7, 3rd. He then tried to become the first Japanese 3yo to win the Arc, but closed too late from behind, 7th. Back home, after a 2nd in the Japan Cup, he raced forward in the Arima Kinen and beat Buena Vista by a nose - champion 3yo colt of the strong 2007 crop. At 4 his camp announced the Dubai World Cup early. He won the Nakayama Kinen prep by 4 lengths, then in the World Cup, sensing a slow pace, swept from last to 2nd on the back straight behind Japanese front-runner Transcend, dueled him down the straight and won by half a length - 15 years after Lively Mount's first try in 1996, the first Japanese winner of the Dubai World Cup, a landmark in Japanese racing history. He announced another Arc bid and planned Hong Kong's QE2 Cup, but lameness ruled out the latter, and lameness again in France ruled out the Arc. Back in the Japan Cup he was 13th, at the back throughout, and in the Arima Kinen, briefly threatening to lead, he was 8th to Triple Crown winner Orfevre, then retired to stud. His runners include sharp-kicking fillies like Oka Sho winner Jeweller, Fuchu Himba S. winner Scarlet Color and Flora S. winner Victoria.
1713: Half-brother of 7-time graded winner Balance of Game, incl. the Mainichi Okan. He won his 3rd start, then the Keisei Hai as 7th choice with a sharp kick, and was 4th to 2yo champion Logotype in the Spring S. But he was 12th in the Satsuki Sho, and a fractured left foreleg was found. Back, he won the Diamond S., showing stamina. 6th in both the Tenno Sho (Spring) and Takarazuka Kinen, he won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai in autumn so impressively that people asked, "Was he really this good?" He won the Diamond S. again the next year and was 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Spring). He then went to Australia for the Caulfield Cup and Melbourne Cup; favorite in the latter, he was jostled in the pack, 13th. At 6 he was 2nd going for a 3rd straight Diamond S., then unplaced in the Tenno Sho (Spring), Takarazuka Kinen and Japan Cup. At 7, 6th in his 4th Diamond S., he seemed finished, but won the Meguro Kinen under top weight 58kg - a veteran's pride. At 8, in his 5th straight Diamond S., he won it again, his first win in 3 years.
1715: Debuting in Hokkaido racing in May at 2, he won the Hokkaido 2yo Yushun in his 6th start with a straight-long charge, the best local 2yo. In the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun he closed hard but couldn't catch fast JRA horse Iide Kenshin, 2nd, and moved to Southern Kanto. He won the Keihin Hai easily from behind, then as 1.2 favorite in the Haneda Hai was 2nd to 109.8 outsider Nick Banyan. In the Tokyo Derby, 1.4 favorite again, he was 4th, then had a tendon injury. Back in summer '09 he lost twice as favorite and retired.
1716: He won the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. easily and the Asahi Hai FS in a tight finish - a worthy 2yo champion. But 2nd in both the Kyodo News Hai and Spring S., he was 5th in the Satsuki Sho, 6th in the NHK Mile C. and 8th in the Derby. In autumn he followed his sire Kurofune's dirt route, Musashino S. to Japan Cup Dirt, but was 5th and 13th. Back on turf he won the Hanshin C., modest next to his 2yo promise. After more heavy graded defeats he retired in '08.
1717: He ran a huge 2nd in the Asahi Hai FS, then won 4 open specials (Cassiopeia S., Osakajo S., Miyakooji S., Port Island S.) but was useless in graded races - "the open-class boss." Then at 4 he won the Swan S., the first graded win for himself and trainer Yoshito Yahagi; runner-up was old rival Fusaichi Richard, who had beaten him in the Asahi Hai. Revenge seemed to transform him: in the Mile CS he nearly beat Daiwa Major, 2nd. In '08, after a 5th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, he won the Keio Hai Spring C. Favorite for the Yasuda Kinen, he was behind Vodka, but beat her in the Mainichi Okan. 2nd in the Mile CS and 5th in the Hong Kong Mile, he won the Milers C. at 6 and was 2nd in the Yasuda Kinen at 7, always lighting up the mile division, but never won a G1 and retired to stud at the end of 7. He is also known as Yusuke Fujioka's favorite mount.
1718: He won the Radio Tampa Hai 2yo S. but was dull in the classics, 6th in the Satsuki Sho and 10th in the Derby. Beaten badly in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he beat older horses in the Naruo Kinen. Older, he often fell short, finishing similarly in G1s and open races alike. He won the '08 Naruo Kinen, his first graded win in 2 years, then the Kinko Sho and more, and was 2nd in the Takarazuka Kinen. Going for a G1 in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he was 13th, then had a tendon injury and a long break, and retired.
1719: He won the Keio Hai 2yo S. by a nose, showing grit, but after a double-figure finish in the Asahi Hai FS lost his spark, winning just once more, on heavy ground in a 16-million race. With repeated heavy defeats, he switched to jumps in spring '08.
1720: She won the Fairy S. and Fillies' Revue, then was 16th in the Oka Sho and ran poorly after. Her foals did little at first, but her 5th, Epoca d'Oro (15: Orfevre), won the Satsuki Sho with her bold early speed, and led and held on for 2nd in the Derby too.
1723: He needed 12 starts to win and 9 more to win again, then bloomed, winning 4 straight from summer at 6 into 7, and his first graded race, the Naruo Kinen, at the end of 8 - the ultimate late bloomer, a true Mejiro character.
1724: Full brother of Tamamo Hot Play, winner of 2 sprint graded races incl. the Swan S. Unbeaten in 2, he was 3rd to A Shin Top in the Shinzan Kinen, then caught front-running Muzzle Fire near the line to win the Kisaragi Sho - avenging his brother, 10th as 2nd choice in the 2004 Kisaragi Sho. Despite distance doubts he was 2nd to 2yo champion Logotype in the Spring S. and 5th to him in the Satsuki Sho. Racing on in graded races, always in the top 8 but not winning, he won the Tancho S. (OP), his first win in 18 months, then was a neck 2nd to Last Impact in the Kyoto Daishoten - more versatile in distance than his brother.
1725: Winning 3 straight on dirt at 4, he became a dirt graded regular, winning the '05 Saga Kinen. Winless after, he switched to jumps at 6, winning 3, and retired in '08.
1726: Debuting in Hokkaido racing, he moved to Funabashi. Improving from summer at 4, he won steadily and took the Empress Hai at 6, retiring in '06 with 13 wins from 43.
1727: Based at Kawasaki. At 3 she won the Kanto Oaks and more with a strong late charge, but from 4 her kick dulled, and she retired without another win.
1728: After 2 turf races he switched to dirt and won his 4th start. With the sharp kick typical of Stay Gold's runners, he won a 5-million race, the Tango S. and Unicorn S. In the Japan Dirt Derby he was caught by Testa Matta's charge, 2nd. In autumn he was demoted to 10th in the Leopard S. and 8th in the Musashino S., but revived in the Topaz S. and was 2nd in the Japan Cup Dirt, a top dirt horse. At 4, slow away in the Antares S. (5th), his kick exploded to win the Tokai S. and Breeders' GC. More was expected, but in the JBC Classic, Japan Cup Dirt and Tokyo Daishoten he was well backed but only made the top five. At 5, 8th in the February S. and 3rd in the Tokai S., he left the JRA for Monbetsu.
1730: Debuting in spring at 3, she won 2 straight, but then bounced between the 10- and 16-million classes, reaching open class only in autumn at 4. 7th in her first graded race, the Ocean S. at 5, she was just 0.3s behind Kinshasa no Kiseki, and 10th but 0.6s back in the Hanshin Himba S. As 10th choice in the Keio Hai Spring C. she raced forward and held on in a course-record 1:19.8 - an upset, and the first filly or mare to win it since Stinger in 2001.
1731: 2nd in 2 G1s, the Asahi Hai FS and NHK Mile C., but winless after, he was called "the best 1-win horse." At 4 he improved fast, winning the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and Hankyu Hai, then 4th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and 5th in the Mile CS. The next year he won the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, holding off champion sprinter Sleepless Night, then the Sprinters S. too - champion sprinter. Winless after, he retired to stud.
1732: A British horse who won the 2005 Japan Cup - the last foreign winner, as Japanese horses have won every one since. At 2-3 he won just a maiden from 6, so his owner sold him, and at 4 he began anew with a new owner and stable. In his 3rd start he won a Listed race, then the Jockey Club S. (G2) early at 5 for his first graded win, and the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud for his first G1. In autumn he was 2nd in the Prix Foy and 5th in the Champion S., then went to America for the BC Turf but was ruled out after a vet check. So his camp chose the Japan Cup. Against Japan's best - Zenno Rob Roy, Heart's Cry, Tap Dance City - and strong raiders Ouija Board and Bago, he was 3rd choice. He broke clear in the straight and held off Heart's Cry by a nose, the first foreign winner in 3 years, in 2:22.1, 0.1s faster than Horlicks's 1989 record. He then went to stud in Japan. Much noticed as a son of Kingmambo, like El Condor Pasa and King Kamehameha, he sired no graded winner and was exported to Britain.
1733: He won his debut and the Niigata 2yo S. with a devastating kick. Then his kick dulled: 8th in the Asahi Hai FS, 14th in the NHK Mile C., 17th in the Derby, and losses in summer graded races. In August 2010 he won an allowance at beloved Niigata, his first win in 2 years, and in February 2011 a 16-million race at Nakayama with a devilish 33.2 finish.
1738: Highly rated early, she couldn't win graded races against strong crop-mates until the Queen C. 5th in the Oka Sho, she ran well without winning, and retired to breed after the '09 New Year S.
1739: Best around a mile on turf, he won 4 at 2-3. Struggling in graded races at 4, he won the CBC Sho as 10th choice and was 3rd in the Hakodate SS, then livened up local sprints. A beautiful black horse, he even appeared in a TV commercial.
1740: He won his first 2, a classic hope, but was 8th in the Kisaragi Sho and 9th in the Spring S., no match for Dream Passport, Meisho Samson and others. In shorter races he was 2nd in the NZ Trophy and NHK Mile C., but a fractured sesamoid was found after the latter. Back after a year, 6th in the Miyakooji S., he barely made the top five until early at 5, when he won the Yodo Tankyori S. from last - a natural sprinter - then the Silk Road S. and Takamatsunomiya Kinen, spring sprint champion overnight. After that his best was a 3rd in the Mile CS; he retired and went to stud in France.
1741: He won the Keio Hai 2yo S., then was 5th in the Asahi Hai FS and 3rd in the Arlington C. After a class drop, he came good in autumn at 4, winning an open special and the Swan S., then livened up the mile division by always leading.
1742: He won his debut, the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. and Radio Nikkei Hai 2yo S., the classic star. He won the Kyodo News Hai at 3 as expected, but was 3rd in the Satsuki Sho, beaten a nose and a nose. Losing form, he was 7th in the Derby, then 12th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai and 8th in the Kikuka Sho. Tried on dirt in the Japan Cup Dirt, he was 11th against the dirt stars, without his old spark, and retired in '08.
1744: She won the Hanshin JF powerfully, but was beaten by Daiwa Scarlet in the Oka Sho. Everyone expected revenge in the Oaks, but her camp chose the Derby. Seen as reckless, she crushed the colts with a 33.0 finish - the first filly to win the Derby in 64 years, since Kurifuji. In autumn, straight into the Shuka Sho, she was 3rd, then a fine 4th against top older horses in the Japan Cup. Disappointing at 4, incl. Dubai, she won the Yasuda Kinen by 3.5 lengths. In the Tenno Sho (Autumn), one of a Big Three with rival Daiwa Scarlet and double classic winner Deep Sky, she raced from midfield and hit the line with front-running Daiwa Scarlet in record time - winning that historic duel by just 2cm. Again no luck in Dubai the next year, but back home she won the Victoria Mile by 7 lengths, then in the Yasuda Kinen, blocked in the straight, charged once clear to catch Deep Sky near the line. Short in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), she won the Japan Cup from an early lead - the first filly or mare with 7 G1s. At 6 she aimed for the Dubai World Cup, newly on all-weather, but in the Maktoum Challenge R3 prep she bled from the nose, 8th - her last race. Sent to Ireland, she was bred to historic champion Sea the Stars, and in 2011 entered the JRA Hall of Fame.
1745: 3rd in the Shinzan Kinen, 2nd in the Arlington C. and 3rd in the NZ Trophy, often just short, he ran the race of his life to win the NHK Mile C., a G1, then was 5th in the Derby. From autumn he seemed a different horse, running poorly, his 3yo mile crown fading. He retired in summer '09 and became a lead pony at Kyoto.
1746: Small like his sire Stay Gold, but with a top-class engine, he won the Asahi Hai FS with a fierce kick. 8th in the Satsuki Sho and 5th in the Derby, he won the Kobe Shimbun Hai in autumn, but was 5th to Asakusa Kings in the Kikuka Sho. Favorite in his first race against older horses, the Naruo Kinen, he was 8th. At 4 he tried miles, poorly prepared, and lost badly. That summer he won 2 2000m graded races, the Kokura Kinen and Asahi Challenge C., an autumn contender. 10th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), badly placed despite the 3rd-fastest finish, he was 4th in the Arima Kinen ahead of Japan Cup winner Screen Hero, and 3rd in the next Tenno Sho (Spring). Then in the Takarazuka Kinen he surged in the straight for his long-sought big title, fulfilling the dream his sire Stay Gold missed in 4 tries. In the Arima Kinen he closed fastest from behind to catch Buena Vista - both Grand Prix races in a year. Going for a repeat in the 2010 Takarazuka Kinen, he was 4th, and retired winless after to stud.
1657: Kanazawa star with 23 wins, incl. the Hakusan Daishoten.
1680: Hokkaido-based. Unbeatable there; won the Hokkaido Sansai Yushun, 3rd in the Japan Dirt Derby.
1694: A strong Oi horse, 2-time Teio Sho winner. Twice in the All Comers, unplaced both times.
1699: Raced at Kochi, Kanazawa and Tokai: 9 wins incl. the Hakusan Daishoten.
1714: Winning the Karasuma S. (16M), he reached open class and boldly ran in the Takarazuka Kinen (10th). Repelled by graded races, he then won the Stayers S. as 7th choice with a sweeping charge - the first graded winner for his sire Mejiro Bright, who died young. All-or-nothing and often winning unfancied, he has many longshot fans.
1721: Running well in Hokkaido racing, he moved to the JRA for the classics, flopped in the trials and returned to local racing.
1722: Long in allowances, he came good early at 5 with 3 straight wins. 3rd in his first graded race, the Tanabata Sho, then 2nd in the Niigata Kinen and All Comers, he won the Fukushima Kinen. At 6 he ran well in middle-distance graded races, then had a long break with hoof trouble. Back, 5th in the '08 Nakayama Kimpai and twice 3rd in graded races, he retired in November '09.
1729: She won her first 3, but leg trouble kept her from racing steadily. Sound again late at 4, she was 2nd in the Mermaid S., Fuchu Himba S. and Hanshin Himba S., and won the Kyoto Himba S. at 6. In her last race, the Nakayama Himba S. at 7, she won with a kick that sliced through heavy ground.
1734: After winning the Kokura 2yo S. and Fantasy S., she was 2nd to Vodka as Hanshin JF favorite. She won the Fillies' Revue, then was 7th in the Oka Sho. In autumn she beat older males in the Sprinters S., proving her 3 graded wins in the "greatest fillies' crop" were real. But she kept finishing in double figures, and in April '08 died of heart failure while treated for colitis X.
1735: He won a maiden, the Cosmos Sho and Sapporo 2yo S., then was 2nd in the Kisaragi Sho and won the Mainichi Hai. Dull in the Satsuki Sho and Derby, he was then sidelined with leg trouble. In '08 he closed fastest for 2nd in the Naruo Kinen and Nikkei Shinshun Hai, hinting at a revival, but after repeated long breaks moved to Kanazawa.
1736: Debuting at Asahikawa, he moved to Kawasaki, winning 3 of 4 incl. the Tokyowan C. 8th in the Tokyo Derby and 11th in the Kuroshio Hai, he then won the Totsuka Kinen and Saitama Eikan Sho, and took on Smart Falcon in the Urawa Kinen. Expected to lose easily, he swept wide at the final turn and won comfortably. Hailed as local racing's next ace after Furioso, he seemed burnt out, beaten badly ever since.
1737: Funabashi-based, Hokkaido 2yo Yushun winner. He won the Keihin Hai and Haneda Hai at 3, and placed steadily in JRA-local races when older.
1747: Based at Funabashi. Famous as "the Prince's horse," he lived up to it by winning the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun. At 3 he tried the JRA classic path, but was 7th in the Kyodo News Hai and 11th in the Spring S. and never ran in the classics. Running well on dirt, he won the Japan Dirt Derby and was 2nd in the JBC Classic. 10th to Vermilion in the Japan Cup Dirt, he was 2nd in the Tokyo Daishoten and Kawasaki Kinen, proving his class, then won the Diolite Kinen and the Teio Sho again - his 3rd G1. As local racing's leader, he often led and held 2nd in JRA-local G1s, denying JRA horses 1-2 finishes. In the 2010 Teio Sho he beat JRA stars Kane Hekili, Vermilion and Success Brocken, easily breaking clear from 2nd in the straight - a champion's run. He then battled dirt kings Espoir City, Smart Falcon and Transcend, closing fastest for 2nd in the JRA's February S., and won 6 JRA-local G1s in all. He retired after the 2012 Tokyo Daishoten - truly a great of modern local racing.
1749: He won the Wakaba S. and, with 2 wins and a 2nd from 3, won the Satsuki Sho by a nose and a nose from Fusaichi Ho O, Sun Zeppelin and others - a classic winner. Then: 9th in the Derby, 3rd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, 16th in the Kikuka Sho, 18th in the Japan Cup. Older he tried dirt and miles without success, retiring to stud after the '09 Kinko Sho.
1750: A stayer consistent over 3000m+. At 4 he was 3rd in the Diamond S. and 2nd in the Hanshin Daishoten and Stayers S., just missing graded wins. Even better at 5, 2nd in the Manyo S., he won the Diamond S., then was 3rd in the Hanshin Daishoten and Tenno Sho (Spring), a leading stayer. At 8 in 2010 he won the Hanshin Daishoten. Amazingly, at 10 in 2012 he won the Stayers S., and at 11 in 2013 ran in his 8th straight Tenno Sho (Spring), a record, and was 3rd in the Stayers S. In 2014 he began with a 5th straight Manyo S. (4th), aiming for the Tenno Sho (Spring), but injury ended his career. Much loved, he was to become a lead pony at beloved Kyoto, but broke a leg and was put down. No G1, but surely one of the great characters among stayers.
1751: Coming good in autumn at 4 with 4 straight wins, he won the Saga Kinen at 5 and was 2nd in the Nagoya Daishoten and Tokai S. That was his peak; he ran poorly after and retired in '08.
1752: Half-brother of '07 Niigata Kinen winner Yume no Shirushi. At 3 his best in 3 graded races was a 4th in the Spring S. Until autumn at 4 he bounced between 16-million and open class, then in open class either won or finished unplaced. His rise began in the Nakayama Kinen at 6, closing from behind for 3rd, his first graded placing. After a 3rd in an open race, he raced forward and overpowered Meiner Falke in the straight to win the Lord Derby Challenge T. He then won 2 open specials and ran in his first G1, the Yasuda Kinen: an 8th-choice outsider, he surged from midfield to win in a race-record 1:31.7 - a big title and 3 generations of Tokyo G1 winners.
1753: Half-sister of Saga Kinen winner Marubutsu Top. Debuting late, in spring at 3, she won 2 straight on dirt and tried the Sweet Pea S. for the Oaks, but hating turf, was 16th. Back on dirt, 3rd in the Shoryu S., she won the Kanto Oaks as favorite. After a summer break, 8th in the Topaz S., she won the Queen Sho by 4 lengths from Meisho Butler. But after the next July's Onuma S. she had a tendon injury; back a year later in the KBC Hai (7th), she retired to breed.
1755: With just 1 win, he survived a 1-in-8 ballot to run in the Asahi Hai FS, broke well, led and held on to become 2yo champion. No soft lead either: he had the fastest finish and won in time just 0.1s off the record. More was expected, but apart from a 5th in the Hakodate Sprint S. he kept finishing in double figures and retired.
1756: Resting from June at 3, she came good in spring at 4: winning the Yamashiro S. (16M) from up front, then the Hanshin Himba S. up the inside, then the Hakodate Sprint S. and Keeneland C. - 3 graded wins in a row (narrowly missing the Summer Sprint title on points). In the Sprinters S., "Singapore's hero" Rocket Man was 1.5 favorite, but she ran on from midfield to beat Pas de Trois by 1.75 lengths - a G1 on a 4-graded-race (5-race) streak. In the Hong Kong Sprint, without a smooth run, she was 5th, ending the streak, and 4th in the Ocean S. early the next year, but in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen her speed returned and she beat rising stars Lord Kanaloa and Majin Prosper for a 2nd G1 - a "strong sprinter" Japan had long awaited. After a 2nd in the Sprinters S. and a hampered 7th in her farewell Hong Kong Sprint, she retired to breed.
1757: A star prospect for Dance in the Dark, whose status as Sunday Silence's heir had slipped behind Agnes Tachyon and Deep Impact. At 3 his best was a 5th in the St. Lite Kinen, but at 4 he matured: after a 2nd, he won the Chofu Tokubetsu (10M) by 3 lengths, the only horse to close in 33 seconds. In the Sankei Osaka Hai, against a superb field - 4yo crop-mates Derby winner Eishin Flash, NHK Mile C. winner Danon Chantilly and Satsuki Sho runner-up Hiruno d'Amour, plus Dream Journey and Captain Thule - he closed in 33 seconds as 8th choice for a nose 2nd. Skipping the Tenno Sho (Spring), he won the Epsom C. by 2.5 lengths from a handy spot, and fans began naming him a Kanto star. In the Mainichi Okan he closed fastest from a seemingly hopeless position for a 2nd straight graded win. 2nd choice behind queen Buena Vista in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), at a blistering pace set by Silport he ran on from midfield but was caught by Tosen Jordan, half a length 2nd, in a record 1:56.1. A G1 was expected in 2012, but he was 2nd to crop-mate Trailblazer in the Kyoto Kinen and 9th in the Dubai Duty Free. Back in the Sapporo Kinen as 1.7 favorite, he led at the final turn but was caught by outsider Fumino Imagine, 2nd. In the Tenno Sho (Autumn) he lost a finishing duel with crop-mates Eishin Flash and Rulership, 4th, then was 4th in the Japan Cup and 6th in the Arima Kinen - close in G1s but winless. With his beautiful chestnut coat, he aims to become a lead pony.
1758: A horse who flew in training, clocking under 50 seconds on Ritto's slope, even under 49. He won his debut, but was 2nd to Kokura specialist Jewel of Nile in the Kokura 2yo S. Repelled by graded races, he was 2nd against older horses in the CBC Sho, then won the Centaur S. in autumn at 3, holding off Hong Kong's Green Birdie. In the Sprinters S. he chased Hong Kong front-runner Ultra Fantasy to a nose, but was demoted from 2nd to 4th for interference. At 4 he won the Ocean S., then in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen was demoted from 4th to 11th for interference. He won the CBC Sho again, was 3rd in the Centaur S., but 11th as 2nd choice in the Sprinters S. In his first dirt race since his debut, the JBC Sprint, he was 3rd to Suni. He ran well in sprints after, even in Singapore at 6, but retired winless and went into equestrian sport.
1759: A superb blueblood, both parents G1 winners. Debuting late, in March at 3, he was 2nd in the Aoba Sho and ran in the Derby (7th). But he was 5th as favorite in the Radio Nikkei Sho and 7th as 4th choice in the Mile CS - clearly talented, but perhaps unable to handle his 520kg+ frame. He won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai in December, then as second-last choice raced boldly for a nose-and-neck 3rd in the Arima Kinen. At 4 he won the Kyoto Kinen and Nikkei Sho, beating crop-mates Perusa and Rose Kingdom by 2.5 lengths. Favorite in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he fought his rider, 13th, then slumped: 13th in the Takarazuka Kinen, 5th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 11th in the Japan Cup. Only 9th choice for the Arima Kinen despite his 3rd the year before, he ran on from midfield for 3rd behind Triple Crown winner Orfevre and crop Derby winner Eishin Flash. He won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai and Naruo Kinen in 2012 - top-class talent - but he hated the heat, running well in cold seasons, and was erratic. He retired after the 2014 Kinko Sho to stud.
1761: Her dam was a North American graded winner, related to great mare Miesque. Unable to win on turf, she won 3 straight on dirt, was 4th in the Japan Dirt Derby, then ran past colts with the fastest finish to win the Leopard S. She won the Queen Sho too, then in the TCK Jo-o Hai at 4, favorite under 2.0, she met her greatest rival, Lavelita, a year older, losing a duel by a neck, then was 3rd to her in the Empress Hai. After winning the Kan'etsu S. (OP), she beat Lavelita at the 3rd meeting in the Ladies' Prelude, and in the JBC Ladies' Classic won their duel again, 7 lengths clear of the rest - 2-2 against Lavelita. In the Japan Cup Dirt they were close again (Lavelita 4th, Miracle Legend 6th), and Lavelita retired after it. Miracle Legend then ruled fillies' JRA-local races, winning the JBC Ladies' Classic again, and was 5th in the Teio Sho and 6th in the Japan Cup Dirt twice - queen of the dirt. She won the 2013 Empress Hai and retired to breed.
1762: Highly rated from a foal, he sold for 170 million yen as a yearling despite having no Sunday Silence blood. 6th on debut, he won 3 straight from a maiden, then was 2nd in the Kyodo News Hai, swept past by Break Run Out. Hoof cracks kept him out of the spring classics, and back in autumn he didn't win at 3. After over 6 months off he was 5th on return, 22kg heavier, then won a 16-million race and an open race. In the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai, under top weight, he won with the fastest finish, then was 5th in a star-studded Arima Kinen with Victoire Pisa - coming good. At 5 he won the AJCC, but was scratched lame from the Hanshin Daishoten and 9th in the Takarazuka Kinen. He won the Sapporo Kinen, then as 7th choice in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), at Silport's blistering pace, he surged from behind for his first G1, in a stunning Japanese record 1:56.1. Perhaps feared tired, he was 6th choice in the Japan Cup but ran 2nd to Buena Vista, then 5th to Triple Crown winner Orfevre in the Arima Kinen. He was 2nd in the 2012 Tenno Sho (Spring) and 3rd as 11th choice in the 2013 Japan Cup, a star of middle-distance racing. Now at stud, from a distinguished family and free of Sunday Silence blood, he carries high hopes as a sire.
1763: One of recent dirt racing's greats, with fast-pace front-running and amazing grit to fight back. Winning his 3rd race in summer at 3 by a wide margin in record time, he beat Suni and others in the Leopard S. After graded losses, he skipped the Japan Cup Dirt to rest. At 4 he won the Aldebaran S. (OP) in record time but kept falling short, until leading became his style and he won the Miyako S. With dirt king Espoir City in America, he was favorite for the Japan Cup Dirt, led from a good start and held off Glorious Noah by a neck for his first G1. At 5 he won the February S. easily as favorite, then went to the Dubai World Cup, the world's top race where past dirt kings had failed. Leading as usual, he looked around, even turning his head (watching the camera car, it was said), and finished 2nd to Japan's Victoire Pisa; his grit in fighting back after Victoire Pisa drew level drew wide praise. After 6 months off, he met former king Espoir City in the Nambu Hai, passing him mid-straight and fighting off Danon Come On again to win. In the JBC Classic, billed as a 2-horse race with a 1.0 quinella, he chased Smart Falcon, on 6 straight dirt graded wins, closing but 2nd. Without Smart Falcon, he beat Espoir City again in the Japan Cup Dirt for his 4th dirt G1. That was his peak; winless after, he retired to stud.
1764: 2nd in the Arlington C. and NZ Trophy, he showed early mile aptitude, then slumped. A 3rd in the Dotonbori S. (16M) late at 4 turned things around: an allowance and an open win, then the Hankyu Hai and a 3rd to Kinshasa no Kiseki in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen. Then he kept failing as favorite, until the Mile CS as 13th choice: saving ground on the inside off Jo Cappuccino's fast pace, he won a blanket finish (first 4 on the same time) for his first G1, in a course-record 1:31.8 - a stunner.
1765: By top miler Taiki Shuttle out of Shin Wind, 2-time graded winner who raced against Oguri Cap and Bamboo Memory. Debuting in summer at 3, unable to win before maidens ended, he moved to Hokkaido racing, won 2 there by wide margins, returned to the JRA and won 3 allowances (5 straight). Favorite in his first graded race, the Negishi S., he was caught by 11th choice Glorious Noah, then won the Tennozan S. (OP) at 1.3. In the Procyon S. fast mare K. I. Gerbera beat him by 4 lengths, but he won the Cluster C. and Tokyo Hai, then the JBC Sprint as 1.2 favorite, leading all the way by 4 lengths - jockey Yusuke Fujioka's first G1 too. The next year he was 14th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, his first turf race since his maiden, and 6th to Suni going for a repeat in the JBC Sprint, and has slumped since.
1766: Winner of the 2011 Satsuki Sho, Derby and Kikuka Sho, the 7th Triple Crown winner. His dam was bred to Deep Impact at the trainer's urging but failed to conceive 3 times, so she was bred to Stay Gold instead. He emerged at 3, winning the Spring S. and the Satsuki Sho as 4th choice - the start of his run. He won the Derby on heavy ground, and with Triple Crown talk building, won the Kobe Shimbun Hai and Kikuka Sho to complete it. He then beat older horses in the Arima Kinen - 4 G1s and Horse of the Year. After winning the Takarazuka Kinen at 4, unrivaled at home, he took on the Arc: at 4 and 5 he won the Prix Foy prep but was 2nd in the Arc, narrowly missing Japan's first win. Back home he announced his retirement after the Arima Kinen at 5, and won it by 8 lengths as favorite - a perfect farewell. At stud his first crops produced Satsuki Sho winner Epoca d'Oro and 4-time G1 winner Lucky Lilac, incl. 2 Queen Elizabeth II Cups. His son Ushba Tesoro, 2023 Dubai World Cup winner, is No. 1 in earnings among Japanese horses (end of 2024).
1767: From Deep Impact's first crop, but unsold at auction as a foal. He won his debut as 1.3 favorite, then was 2nd in the Keio Hai 2yo S. and Asahi Hai FS - proof that Deep Impact, a middle-to-long distance star, sired speed for a mile too. 11th in the NZ Trophy at 3, he was 3rd in the NHK Mile C., then as 9th choice in the Yasuda Kinen, wary of older horses, he passed Jo Cappuccino in the straight and held off Strong Return by a neck - the first 3yo winner of the Yasuda Kinen. Back in the Mainichi Okan he was caught by a neck by improver Dark Shadow, 2nd. Favorite for the Mile CS, his first time since his debut, he was 5th, then 10th as favorite in the Hanshin C. At 4, after a 3rd in the Nakayama Kinen, he was last in the Milers C., perhaps upset by travel, then 6th in the Yasuda Kinen, 4th in the Mainichi Okan and 5th in the Mile CS. But in the 2013 Hanshin C., as 8th choice, he led all the way, and in 2014, again 8th choice, broke clear from up front to win it again. In 2015 he went to Australia, winning the George Ryder S. and running 2nd in the Doncaster Mile, the southern hemisphere's big mile. At stud his first crop included NHK Mile C. winner Laudacion.
1748: Daiwa Major's sister and queen of the greatest fillies' crop. She beat Vodka in the Oka Sho; a fever ruled out the Oaks, but in autumn she won the Rose S., Shuka Sho and Queen Elizabeth II Cup, racing forward and powering home - very consistent. Against Derby winner Vodka she lost only in the Tulip Sho and Tenno Sho (Autumn), beating her clearly in the Oka Sho, Shuka Sho and Arima Kinen. In her first race against older males, the Arima Kinen, she led in the straight but Matsurida Gogh came up the inside, 2nd - the first filly to place in it since Hishi Amazon - and was champion 3yo filly. In '08 a Dubai plan was scrapped after a wood chip hit her eye in training. Back in the Osaka Hai she beat Meisho Samson and Asakusa Kings, but shin trouble ruled out the spring. In autumn, in the Tenno Sho with Vodka and Deep Sky, she lost by 2cm after a 13-minute photo. Then in the Arima Kinen, without Vodka, she beat the colts with authority - the first filly to win it in 37 years. Leg trouble ended her career the next year. Always in G1s, never out of the top two - surely a candidate for the greatest mare ever.
1754: Racing in Hokkaido at 2, she won the Eikan Sho and the JRA-local Edelweiss Sho by 5 lengths, then sold for a high price. Moving to Southern Kanto, she was 12th in the Kanto Oaks and 13th in the Starlight C., and retired.
1760: By Bago, the French Arc winner who also ran in the Japan Cup. He needed 6 starts to win, then won 3 straight. Lacking a sharp kick, he raced forward and was 3rd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai. In the Kikuka Sho, as 7th choice, he raced forward and held off Rose Kingdom's charge for a G1. Then he slumped: meant to be the strong Kikuka Sho winner of a strong crop, he kept missing the top five, and late in his career switched to jumps.
1768: The 2011 Oka Sho winner. With heavy favorite Reve d'Essor out, the classics were wide open, and she was 2nd choice. Hampered and forced to race last, she produced an eye-opening late charge to win the first classic with the kick of her sire Deep Impact. Favorite for the Oaks, she couldn't quicken in the straight, 4th. In autumn she was 7th in the Shuka Sho and 6th in the Mile CS. At 4 she was 2nd in the Hanshin Himba S. and 3rd in the Victoria Mile, and at 5 won the Mermaid S., retiring at the end of 2013. Her son Last Draft (16: Novelist) won the 2019 Keisei Hai.
1769: By Durandal, 2-time Mile CS winner with an ultimate kick. She won a maiden in her 3rd start and a 5-million race in her 7th - rarely beaten badly but rarely winning - then won the Wasurenagusa Sho (OP). In the Oaks, run in pouring rain, amid the Marcellina-Whale Capture duel she ran on from midfield and outfought front-running Pure Breeze for the crown. Aiming for a 2nd classic in autumn, she was 10th in the Rose S., 14kg heavier, then 10th in the Shuka Sho and 12th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, and double-figure finishes became the norm.
1770: Her dam was French-born Reve de Scarlet, who ran in the Japan Cup, and her siblings include many good runners, so hopes were high; she won her debut, then the Daily Hai 2yo S. and the Hanshin JF easily - champion 2yo filly. With 3 straight wins, all with the fastest finish, people whispered "the Oka Sho is hers" and "she may reach stablemate queen Buena Vista's level." Confirming it, she won the Tulip Sho at 1.1, 10kg heavier, but a fracture ruled out the spring. Back, she couldn't show her old self, broke down again and retired to breed.
1771: Steady from her debut in August at 2, he won the Kyodo News Hai. 2nd choice for the Satsuki Sho, he was 5th to fellow Stay Gold colt Orfevre, then 4th to him in the Derby on heavy ground. In autumn he went to France as Nakayama Festa's companion, but Longchamp's ground didn't suit him: last of 6 in the Prix Niel, the 3yo Arc prep, and 10th in the Prix Dollar. Back home he won the December S., then was 2nd to Rulership in the American JCC at 4. Steady in graded races, he won the All Comers in autumn. He won the Nakayama Kinen at 5, but then slumped.
1772: Full sister of Fusaichi Ho O, who won 3 graded races in a row, and Tall Poppy, winner of the Hanshin JF and Oaks - a hyped blueblood. She won a 1600m turf debut on opening week, a race known for future stars. In the Sapporo 2yo S., a blueblood duel with Admire Scepter, out of 2-time G1 winner Admire Groove, she beat her rival but couldn't catch 3rd-choice colt All as One, 2nd. In the Hanshin JF, perhaps hurt by big weight loss, she closed from behind for 4th to Reve d'Essor, then fractured a leg, missing the spring classics. Back 28kg heavier, she won the Isaribi S. (16M) by 2.5 lengths, then beat older graded regulars like Lady Alba Rosa and Animate Bio in the Queen S. In the Shuka Sho, her first G1 since the Hanshin JF, she raced forward and held on to win. As the new 3yo queen in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, she was 2nd choice and ran on, but was beaten by previous winner Snow Fairy's other-worldly kick, 2nd - ahead of 5-crown queen Apapane and rival Whale Capture - champion 3yo filly. But after a fracture in that race, she broke down again preparing to return, and retired to breed.
1773: Improving rapidly as an older horse, he was 3rd in the Sprinters S. at 4. At 5 he won the Hankyu Hai and Keeneland C. and was a nose 2nd to Laurel Guerreiro in the Sprinters S., a step from a big title. In the Takamatsunomiya Kinen he was again a nose 2nd, to Kinshasa no Kiseki - always a leading sprinter. He raced until 7 and went to stud from 2012.
1774: A fast Falbrav sprinter. Coming good at 4, he won 3 straight up to the Ibis Summer Dash. After a 3rd in the Kita-Kyushu Kinen, he won the Centaur S. over Hong Kong's Lucky Nine and Green Birdie and 3-time graded winner Dasher Go Go - 2011 Summer Sprint Series champion. He was 3rd in the Sprinters S. behind Curren Chan, his rival for series points.
1775: Repelled by graded races from spring to autumn at 3, he was 3rd as 9th choice on a light 51kg in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai, then in the Stayers S., the longest flat graded race, won from up front like a true stayer. He was later 2nd to Cosmo Meadow in the Diamond S.
1776: His dam was a half-sister of Deep Impact. Well backed from his debut but unable to win, he moved to Hokkaido racing in autumn at 3 when maidens ended. Winning twice by 5 lengths, he returned to the JRA and won by 7, then was 7th in the Tokyo Daishoten - a dramatic 3yo season. At 4 he won 2 allowances as odds-on favorite, then in his first JRA graded race, the Antares S., held off dirt regulars Wonder Acute and Birdie Birdie from up front - 3 straight. He won the Mercury C., but was last in the Miyako S. after falling ill in the race and rested for the year. At 5 he won the Jinsen S. and Antares S., then the Teio Sho, beating Espoir City clearly - from an unusual path to the very top. Bigger things were expected in autumn, but he died of a twisted intestine at pasture.
1777: A rare filly star among Neo Universe's runners, mostly colts. Winning a maiden in summer at 3 and then a 5-million race, she won 3 straight from summer to autumn at 4, and at 5 the Tanabata Sho, Kokura Kinen and Fuchu Himba S. - 3 graded wins in a row and the 2011 Summer 2000 Series. Truly a "summer girl." She retired to breed after the Nakayama Himba S. at 6 (14th).
1778: Once a forward runner, he stalled in the 5-million class and switched to closing - a huge success, with a stunning 34-second finish on dirt. In the Procyon S. at 5 he swept past dirt regulars Danon Come On and K. I. Gerbera from last in a flash, winning as 9th choice. A pure closer, he also won the Negishi S. and Capella S. and was 2nd in the G1 February S. - a colorful dirt character always capable of a big run.
1779: A Falbrav sprinter. 2nd in the Fantasy S. at 2, she won the Fillies' Revue the next year. Coming good in summer at 4, she beat G1 runner-up BB Gardan by 2 lengths in the Hakodate Sprint S., then won the Keeneland C. - 2010 Summer Sprint Series champion. Also known as Yusuke Fujioka's favorite mount.
1780: Winner of the 2012 Victoria Mile. Prominent early, she was 2nd in the Hanshin JF at 2 and the classic leading lady at 3, but was 2nd as favorite in the Oka Sho, 3rd as 2nd choice in the Oaks and 3rd as favorite in the Shuka Sho - just short in all 3. At 4 she won the Victoria Mile, her first G1. After a slump, at 5 she was 2nd in the Victoria Mile and won the Fuchu Himba S. In her first race at 6, the Tokyo Shimbun Hai, 8th choice under a heavy 57kg, she surged from midfield to beat the colts. 2nd choice in the Victoria Mile, she couldn't catch front-running Verxina, 4th, then was 3rd in the Sapporo Kinen and Fuchu Himba S. She retired after the Hanshin Himba S. at 7 (9th). With her white coat and sweet face, she had many fans.
1781: From the first crop of Heart's Cry, who ended Deep Impact's unbeaten run in the Arima Kinen and won the Dubai Sheema Classic. He won his debut and the Nojigiku S. (OP), and was 3rd choice in the Radio Nikkei Hai 2yo S. but faded from the front to 4th. Beaten in the Kisaragi Sho and Yayoi Sho, he waited boldly at the back in the Aoba Sho and won with a 33.6 finish. In the Derby, as 10th choice, he made his move when Satsuki Sho winner Orfevre was squeezed on the inside, closing fastest, but Orfevre split the field and beat him by 1.75 lengths - though 7 lengths clear of the rest, he was the top threat to stop the Triple Crown. In the Kobe Shimbun Hai he started his run level with Orfevre but was quickly left behind, 2nd. In the Kikuka Sho, "this is the only way to win," he waited last for a straight-long charge, but couldn't catch Orfevre, who had learned to lead early - 2nd a 3rd time as his rival completed the Triple Crown. In the Japan Cup, without Orfevre but with Buena Vista and seasoned older horses, he launched a surprise sweep at the 3rd turn, but queen Buena Vista passed him at once, 5th. At 4 he was 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and 4th in the Takarazuka Kinen, then a tendon injury struck. Back in autumn at 5, he was 2nd in the Arima Kinen, but never got past the monster of his crop. Aiming again for the top, he won the Nikkei Sho and was 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Spring), but no G1 came; his dream passes to his foals.
1782: He won the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. by 3.5 lengths with a 33.7 finish, the best of his crop. But as 1.8 favorite in the Asahi Hai FS he couldn't quicken from behind, 4th to Grand Prix Boss. In a wide-open year for the colts' classics, he won the Yayoi Sho, the leading contender. The Satsuki Sho was held at Tokyo, and he was favorite, but was beaten 3 lengths by 4th choice Orfevre, full brother of 3-time G1 winner Dream Journey and fresh from his first graded win in the Spring S. - 2nd. He was 7th in the Derby, unable to quicken from midfield, and kept running well without winning. At 4, after 2 losses, he won the Keio Hai Spring C. with a kick like his best, then the Mile CS with a sharp finish for his first G1. After that, apart from a 3rd in the Swan S., he missed the top five, but at 6 won the Chukyo Kinen under top weight, surging from the back - his first win in 2 years.
1783: He won his debut despite getting loose in the warm-up, then showed his temper for 3rd in the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. - very talented, but needing to grow up. After a 3rd in the Hopeful S. (OP), he won the Keisei Hai, holding off Agnes Tachyon's talented colt Debonair by a nose. Crushed in the spring classics, he matured after a break and won the St. Lite Kinen with a long run, but was 7th in the Kikuka Sho. At 4 he was 8th in the Nikkei Sho and 13th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), and retired with leg trouble.
1784: A dirt specialist who won the 2011 Japan Dirt Derby and 2013 February S. Steady on dirt at 2, he won a 5-million race at 3 by 6 lengths as 1.5 favorite, then was 2nd in his first turf race, the Sumire S. (OP). Back on dirt he won the Ibuki Sho (OP), was 2nd in the Unicorn S., then won the Japan Dirt Derby as favorite, top of his crop on dirt. A fracture forced a break; back in spring at 4, he won the Aso S. (OP) in his 3rd race, then was 3rd in the Sirius S. and 5th in the Japan Cup Dirt. At 5 he beat later Teio Sho winner Hokko Tarumae and others in the Tokai S., then surged from a handy spot to win the February S., a JRA G1. He kept making the top five in dirt graded races, and at 8 went to Korea for a 3rd in the new international G1 Korea Sprint, racing until January at 9.
1785: With the fastest finishes in middle-distance dirt races, he was 3rd in the Unicorn S. and 2nd in the Japan Dirt Derby, then won the Leopard S. by 2 lengths - proof Deep Impact's runners can win on dirt. Winless after, he slumped.
1786: Sold for 30 million yen, he was rated highly before his debut. Beaten by later Shuka Sho winner Aventura on debut, he won a maiden at 1.2. Losing and learning, he won a 5-million race in December, then ran a fine 5th as 12th choice in the Spring S. 12th choice again in the NZ Trophy, he raced forward and held on to win. 4th in the NHK Mile C., he then rested long; back, he switched to jumps and won an open race.
1787: His sister was 2-time graded winner Apricot Fizz (by Jungle Pocket). Needing 4 starts to win, he then won the Moonee Valley RC Sho (5M), and as 3rd choice in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, guided skillfully by Yutaka Take on his first ride, won for 3 straight. In the Derby he ran on from midfield for 5th. Autumn hopes ended when an injury scratched him from the Kobe Shimbun Hai. Back the next spring, he was 5th in the year-end Kinko Sho, rested again and retired to stud.
1788: By Agnes Tachyon, related to Kikuka Sho winner Delta Blues - but gelded before his debut for his temper. He won a maiden in his 3rd start, but crossing the line first in an allowance he was demoted for interference - slow to get going. Then in the Shinzan Kinen he broke clear from up front and held off later Triple Crown winner Orfevre and Oka Sho winner Marcellina, and also won the Mainichi Hai. Ineligible for the classics as a gelding, he was still called "the best of his crop." But crushed as heavy favorite in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, he rested with a fracture. Back by December, 20kg heavier, he won the Naruo Kinen over classic crop-mates Sadamu Patek and Frere Jacques. With Yutaka Take aboard, seeking a G1 for 24 straight years, he was 9th in the Arima Kinen. Big things were expected at 4, but his form oddly faded; at 5 he won the Osaka-Hamburg C. (OP), his first win in a while.
1790: Hailed from a foal as "Agnes Tachyon's masterpiece." 2nd on debut, he won a maiden by 8 lengths at 1.1, then a week later the Sapporo 2yo S. safely from up front. In the Radio Nikkei Hai 2yo S. he led in the straight but lacked a final kick, 3rd. At 3 he swept past Deep Brillante in the Spring S., proving his class, and was Satsuki Sho favorite, but from the widest gate 18 he only ran on slowly, 5th. 4th choice in the Derby, he stopped on the hill, 10th, then had a tendon injury preparing for autumn and a long break. Back in January at 5 after 18 months, he was beaten badly twice, then in the Miyakooji S. raced boldly forward and drew away - a 5-length win, his first in 2 years, in a Japanese 1800m turf record 1:43.9. Beaten badly on soft ground in the Yasuda Kinen and 10th in the Hakodate Kinen, he was 5th lighter in the Mainichi Okan, then in the Mile CS, as the leaders collapsed, he alone held on for 3rd as 9th choice behind Danon Shark. At 6 he won the Tanabata Sho, but another injury ended his career - a great talent plagued by injuries.
1791: Winner of the 2011 Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun. His sire Malibu Moon, with 1 win from 2, went to stud in America for his pedigree. 6th in a 1800m turf debut, he won a dirt maiden by 7 lengths, then the Platanus Sho (5M) by 5 and the Hokkaido 2yo Yushun by 8 - 3 dominant wins. In the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun he stumbled at the start but swept forward and held on - a G1 on a 4-race streak. A Dubai trip was planned the next spring, but injury forced a long layoff. Back in spring at 5, he finished in double figures in every dirt open and G3 race, his old power gone.
1792: Like Triple Crown winner Orfevre and Dream Journey, he has the golden cross of Stay Gold out of a Mejiro McQueen mare, and a fierce kick that never tires. He won the Satsuki Sho and Kikuka Sho, was a fine 5th to Deep Brillante in the Derby, and won the year-end Arima Kinen - clearly the best of his crop. But unluckily, overshadowed by 3yo filly Gentildonna (fillies' Triple Crown and Japan Cup) and previous Triple Crown winner Orfevre, he wasn't Horse of the Year. At 4 he beat Gentildonna in the Takarazuka Kinen for his 4th G1, but went winless in autumn, perhaps out of sorts mentally. At 5 he announced plans abroad, won the Takarazuka Kinen again for his 5th G1, and went to the Arc. With Just a Way and Harp Star, Japan's 3 runners raised hopes, but he never got going from the start and was 14th, at the back throughout. At 6 he won the Tenno Sho (Spring), his 6th G1, and in autumn went for a 7th, then equaling the JRA record, but was 10th in the Japan Cup and 8th in the Arima Kinen, and retired. Wildly inconsistent, but undeniably strong - a beloved champion. At stud from 2016, his first crop debuted in 2019: in the Sapporo 2yo S. his Black Hole and Satono Gold ran 1-2 at once. His 2nd crop gave Oaks winner Uberleben, his first G1 winner; in 2023 Meiner Grand won the Nakayama Daishogai, and in 2025 Meisho Tabaru won the Takarazuka Kinen, a father-son double, raising hopes for more.
1793: He beat Gentildonna to win the 2013 Tenno Sho (Autumn).
