Unsuccessful in the spring classics at 3, he targeted the Tenno Sho against older horses in autumn: 2nd in the Mainichi Okan, a fair 6th in the Tenno Sho. At 4 he was again 2nd in the Mainichi Okan, then in the Tenno Sho, with previous triple crown filly Gentildonna favorite, at a fast pace that left others tired, he surged from midfield to win easily. In 2014 his camp announced Dubai: he won the Nakayama Kinen prep by slipping up the inside, then in the Dubai Duty Free swung wide and blew the field away in the straight to win by 6 lengths, beating the old record by over 2 seconds. That made him the first Japanese horse rated No. 1 in the world, drawing global attention. Back home, in the Yasuda Kinen he struggled on heavy ground but, with an eye-opening burst, caught 16th choice Grand Prix Boss by a nose for his 3rd G1. Skipping the Takarazuka Kinen, he went with 3yo filly Harp Star and Takarazuka winner Gold Ship for Japan's long-sought Arc, but, racing on the inside, was blocked for a long time and finished 8th behind previous winner Treve. In the Japan Cup he ran on from midfield but was 2nd to Epiphaneia's crushing win, and in his farewell Arima Kinen he charged in the straight but couldn't catch Gentildonna, 4th. With the astonishing late development inherited from his sire Heart's Cry, from autumn at 4 the whole world watched him - truly a star of modern Japanese racing. His first crop, debuting in 2018, included Velox (2nd, 3rd and 3rd in the classics), Lord My Way and Awill a Way, and Master Fencer was 6th in the Kentucky Derby and 5th in the Belmont S. His 2018 crop's Danon the Kid won the Hopeful S., and in 2024 Yamanin Ours won the Procyon S. (G3) - a steady presence.
1794: By Admire Max, who won the Takamatsunomiya Kinen with a late charge. He won his debut with the fastest finish, then burst down the middle to win the Niigata 2yo S., suddenly a classic hope. But as 1.6 favorite in the Keio Hai 2yo S. he couldn't quicken, 4th. Throat surgery followed, successfully, but back at 3 he was a well-beaten 6th in the Spring S., did nothing in the spring classics, and has stalled since.
1743: Won the Shinzan Kinen as an outsider, then was crushed in the Satsuki Sho and NHK Mile C. After a tendon injury a local comeback failed.
1789: From the first crop of NHK Mile C. winner Telegnosis. With her sire's kick, she won the Niigata 2yo S. as 9th choice. 9th in the Fantasy S. and 6th in the Hanshin JF, back to closing she was a close 2nd in the Queen C. Running well after - 2nd in the Rose S., 3rd in the Fukushima Kinen - she won the Fuchu Himba S. at 4. In 2013 she won the Nakayama Himba S., was 3rd in the Victoria Mile and 4th as 15th choice in the Yasuda Kinen. A rare member of the Propontis family.
1795: A star of the 2012 fillies' classics. She won the Fillies' Revue, then battled crop stars Gentildonna and Verxina: 3rd in the Oka Sho, 4th in the Oaks, 6th in the Shuka Sho. She won the Queen S. at 3 and 4 and retired after a 4th in the Sapporo Kinen. From Dyna Carle's family, she carries high hopes as a broodmare.
1796: From the first crop of 5-time G1 winner Daiwa Major, "the heavy tank." She won a mile maiden by 6 lengths and was entered in the Niigata 2yo S., but at risk of exclusion switched to the same day's Kokura 2yo S. Doubts about dropping to a sprint proved wrong: she ran on from midfield to win, her sire's first graded winner. Straight into the Hanshin JF, she was 8th. At 3 she was 2nd in the Tulip Sho, ahead of Gentildonna, raising classic hopes, but was crushed in the Oka Sho (15th) and Oaks (16th). Switching to sprints, in her 2nd race she beat the division's two stars, Lord Kanaloa and Curren Chan, in the Centaur S. - a huge upset - then was 4th in the Sprinters S. No more graded wins, but she often ran well in sprints.
1797: From the first crop of Admire Moon, a leading middle-distance horse. Using her early speed, she won her debut and the Hakodate 2yo S., her sire's first graded winner. After a break she was 3rd in the Fantasy S. and 11th to Joie de Vivre in the Hanshin JF. Seemingly an early bloomer, she was unbeatable at Hakodate, winning allowances there, and retired after the Keeneland C.
1798: Galileo's masterpiece: unbeaten in 14, mainly at a mile, with 10 G1s, most won by wide margins, he dominated European racing from 2010 to 2012. Brilliant at 2, he was Cartier champion 2yo; at 3 he won 4 G1s incl. the 2000 Guineas and St. James's Palace S., Cartier Horse of the Year. At 4 he won the Queen Anne S. by 11 lengths, then stepped up to 10 furlongs to win the International S. and Champion S. with ease - Horse of the Year again, rated 140 lbs, the highest ever in the World Thoroughbred Rankings. At stud he was just as superior: his first crop gave G1 winner Cracksman, and in Japan Soul Stirring and Mozu Ascot started a Frankel boom. In 2021 Adayar won the Derby and Hurricane Lane the Irish Derby, and he took the British and Irish sire title from his sire Galileo. In 2023 he sired a northern hemisphere record 11 G1 winners, and in 2024 his fee equaled Dubawi's as Europe's highest at 350,000 pounds. He also reached 100 graded winners in a record 3,144 days, faster than Galileo, Dubawi or Japan's Deep Impact.
1799: With an Agnes Tachyon kick, he charged home in the straight. Missing the spring classics, he was 2nd in the Principal S. and Radio Nikkei Sho, then in the St. Lite Kinen caught runaway leader Yamanin Elbe. Yamanin Elbe closed in 37.0, Quark Star in 34.0 - 3 seconds faster, making the others look still. After a 9th in the Kikuka Sho he had leg trouble and retired without returning.
1800: At 2-3 he was 2nd 4 times - Radio Nikkei Hai 2yo S., Kyoto Shimbun Hai, Japan Dirt Derby, Chunichi Shimbun Hai - a steady middle-distance graded runner. At 4 he won the Nakayama Kimpai, breaking clear from up front. More was expected, but he was well beaten by later Tenno Sho winner Tosen Jordan in the AJCC, 4th, then slumped, until as 11th choice he narrowly held on to win the year-end Chunichi Shimbun Hai.
1801: By King Kamehameha out of a Sunday Silence mare - today's fashionable cross. Winning his 3rd start, he was 2nd to Danon Chantilly in the Mainichi Hai over a strong field incl. Ril da Val, Rulership and Cosmo Helenos. A fracture ended his 3yo season. Back in spring at 4, dropped in class, he won 3 straight from the 10-million class to the Asahi Challenge C. No more graded wins, but he placed 3 times at double-figure odds.
1802: 3rd in the Fillies' Revue, she was beaten badly in the Oka Sho, but 5th as 15th choice in the Shuka Sho. After stalling, she won a wide-open Nakayama Himba S. (favorite at 4.7) as 10th choice, then was 3rd by a neck and a neck to stars Apapane and Buena Vista in the Victoria Mile. 3rd against colts in the Asahi Challenge C., she led all the way to win the 2012 Nakayama Himba S. as 8th choice - 2 wins in the race, both as an outsider.
1803: Debuting late at 2, he improved steadily, 4th as 12th choice in the Aoba Sho. Missing the Derby, he won the Radio Nikkei Sho 2 months later.
1804: From the first crop of autumn triple crown winner Zenno Rob Roy. Based at Funabashi, as 6th choice he led all the way in the Japan Dirt Derby over JRA stars like graded winner Birdie Birdie and Cosmo Phantom - the first local winner since Furioso 3 years earlier. Little success after; from 2014, at 7, he raced at Kasamatsu, then Sonoda at 8 - 34 races in those 2 years.
1805: From 3 he showed dirt class, 2nd in the Unicorn S. and winning the Enif S. (OP). Early at 4 he ran down favorite Summer Wind, on a 5-race streak since his local days, to win the Negishi S. as 11th choice. 5th in the February S., he boldly went to Dubai's Godolphin Mile, a fine 4th. Beaten badly back home, he won the Musashino S. with a powerful finish, then in the Japan Cup Dirt, as 8th choice, closed fastest to chase front-running favorite Transcend to a neck. Injury then forced a long break.
1806: She won the Hiiragi Sho (5M) at 2, then was 4th as 3rd choice to Whale Capture in the Queen C. In the Fillies' Revue she switched from racing forward to waiting behind, and kicked sharply in the straight to win. 9th in the Oka Sho, she tried dirt without success and retired to breed in autumn at 4.
1807: Winner of the 2013 Mile Championship. Originally a middle-to-long distance horse, he was 3rd to Orfevre in the Kikuka Sho at 3, and at 5 won the Kyoto Kinen and was 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Spring). But often falling short, his camp suddenly switched him to a mile that autumn. In the Mile CS he waited at the back and swept past them all with the fastest finish. Kyoto suited him, but a G1 win at an unfamiliar distance was remarkable - and it gave Yutaka Take an unprecedented 100th JRA G1 win. In 2014 he was 2nd in the Kyoto Kinen, 3rd in the Kyoto Daishoten and 4th in the Mile CS - superbly reliable at Kyoto - and retired after an 8th in the Arima Kinen to stud.
1808: Winner of the 2011 Kentucky Derby and 2013 Dubai World Cup. He raced on turf and all-weather early, winning the Spiral S. (G3) in March at 3, then tried dirt for the first time in the Kentucky Derby. Only 11th choice, he moved early from midfield to win clearly - the first horse to win the Kentucky Derby without a dirt race. 2nd in the Preakness and 6th in the Belmont, he then rested with a fracture. Aiming for the Dubai World Cup at 4, he broke down again and missed it, ending the year with a 2nd in the BC Mile. At 5 he finally went to Dubai and, racing forward, pulled clear in the straight to win the big title. He was 11th in England's Queen Anne S. and retired, standing as a shuttle sire in Australia and America with G1 winners in both, then in Japan from 2020; his first Japanese crop was born in 2021.
1809: By US dual classic winner Smarty Jones. Above all strong at 1400m on dirt, with 7 wins there. His wins were brilliant: sitting 2nd, he'd sprint clear in the straight to win by 2 lengths or more. He won 3 open races, the Procyon S. and, in his farewell, the Capella S. As a dam she produced NHK Mile C. winner K. I. Notek (15: Deep Impact).
1810: An unusual sprinter by Jungle Pocket, she won her debut and the Hakodate 2yo S. Fair at 3 (5th Falcon S., 7th Centaur S.), she slumped after.
1811: With the gleaming black coat of his sire Manhattan Cafe, he debuted in July at 2. Only placing in classic trials, he came good as an older horse. In the Osaka Hai, a springboard to stardom, he closed fastest to beat strong rivals Tosen Jordan, Rose Kingdom, Earnestly and Federalist. In the Naruo Kinen he closed in 32 seconds but was 2nd to veteran To the Glory. In a star-studded Takarazuka Kinen he was 3rd behind Orfevre and Rulership, proving himself. The next year he was 3rd in the Kyoto Kinen and 2nd in the Osaka Hai. Trying the mile G1 Yasuda Kinen, he closed in a devilish 32.8 but was a neck 2nd to sprint champion Lord Kanaloa. Disappointing as a favorite after, he was 10th choice for the next Yasuda Kinen but surged from nearly last for 3rd - then a fracture sidelined him. With one of the sharpest kicks in training, many fans await his return.
1812: Based at Oi. At 4 he held 4th chasing front-running Summer Wind in the Tokyo Hai, then as 6th choice beat 4 JRA horses for 2nd to Summer Wind in the JBC Sprint. He later won the Sakitama Hai and more.
1813: An Australian sprint mare, unbeaten in 25 with 15 G1s. Winning big from her debut, she missed time with injury at 3, won her first G1, the Patinack Farm Classic, at 4, and won it again at 5 for 16 straight, an Australian record. Unbeatable at home, she went to England for the Diamond Jubilee S.; tested for the first time, she beat Moonlight Cloud and others by a head for a G1 abroad. That year she was Australia's Horse of the Year and Cartier champion sprinter in Europe. She raced until 6 and retired, rated 130 lbs in the World Thoroughbred Rankings, equal to Arc winner Treve - the first Australian-trained horse rated world No. 1. Her foals from 2014 have done little. She died in 2024 of worsening laminitis.
1815: A speedster who won the 2012 Yasuda Kinen in record time. Stuck in the 16-million class until mid 5, he came good after winning the Keio Hai Spring C. and running 2nd in the Yasuda Kinen. At 6, after a 4th in the Keio Hai Spring C., he won the Yasuda Kinen in record time, closing from behind in 33.8 to sweep past them all in a stunning 1:31.3. A fracture in 2013 ended his career.
1816: A straight-long closer, he ran well in graded races, 2nd in the St. Lite Kinen, and won the Niigata Daishoten in spring at 5, racing mainly at long-straight Tokyo and Niigata.
1817: By Eishin Sunday, unraced yet a sire of many local graded winners like Mitsuaki Silence (Hyogo Championship). He won the Mikage S. (16M) late at 3 to reach open class, became a dirt sprint regular, and won the Capella S. at the end of 4 and the Negishi S. next. 2nd choice for the February S., perhaps too long, he was 14th. He won the Coral S. (OP) and Kakitsubata Kinen, then went winless; 2nd in the JBC Sprint, he was 15th in the February S. But he won the Kurofune Sho, his first win in a while, and 4 straight, including the Sakitama Hai over 1400m by 8 lengths. Winning the Kurofune Sho again, he has been very reliable in JRA-local graded races.
1818: His dam was a sister of Kikuka Sho winner Narita Top Road. Unlike his stamina-rich sire, a sharp-kicking miler. At 4 he won 4 straight to the Fuji S. and was Mile CS favorite, closing from last in a devilish 33.6 but failing to catch A Shin Forward, 2nd. No wins since.
1819: With just 1 win from 13 at 2-3, she came good at 4, winning 3 straight from up front, and was 3rd in her first graded race, the Mermaid S. After a break she won the Nishinomiya S. (16M), then led to win the Fuchu Himba S. 10th in her first G1, the Mile CS, she broke down in December's Aichi Hai and was put down.
1820: Steady in allowances on turf and dirt, she reached open class in summer at 4. Struggling after, she charged from a wide draw to win the Kita-Kyushu Kinen.
1823: A sharp-kicking Agnes Tachyon mare. At 4 she won the Kyoto Himba S. from last with a devilish 33.6 finish, then in the Victoria Mile raced forward instead for a neck 2nd to Buena Vista.
1824: Switching to closing at 5, she broke out: closing fastest, she was 2nd as 14th choice in the Nakayama Himba S., then won the Fukushima Himba S. as 9th choice, plus the Mermaid S. and Aichi Hai - 3 fillies' graded wins that year. In 2012 she raced boldly against males, slicing past top colts Dark Shadow and Hiruno d'Amour with a powerful finish in the Sapporo Kinen. With partner Keisuke Dazai she kept thrilling fans from the back, but broke down in the Victoria Mile at 7 and was put down.
1825: A dirt sprinter with a strong late kick. In the Hokkaido Sprint C. she caught local horse Yasaka Fine by a neck.
1826: His brother was Radio Nikkei Sho runner-up Not Alone, another brother Arlington C. winner Northern River, and a relative Derby winner Logi Universe, but he preferred dirt. Thriving at 5, he swept forward to win the Elm S. as favorite. 4th choice in the Nambu Hai, he was 6th to Transcend.
1827: A prospect admired for his build from a foal. Trained to his growth, he debuted late, in March at 3, and won by 7 lengths, a horse to watch. Favorite in his 2nd start, the Mainichi Hai, he was 2nd to Deep Sky, then won the Aoba Sho from a good spot with the fastest finish. After 3 starts he was a Derby contender, but couldn't quicken from a good position, 7th to Deep Sky. Aiming for autumn revenge, he suffered a tendon injury. Back after 18 months in the American JCC at 5, he was 12th, and never regained his dazzling spring-at-3 shine.
1829: From the first crop of Gold Allure, winner of 4 dirt G1s incl. the February S. Raced on turf at first, he won his first dirt race in June at 4 by 4 lengths and rose quickly to open class, but big wins eluded him, incl. a scratch from the February S. After a 2nd in the Elm S., in the Nambu Hai, Espoir City's send-off before America, he was 1.0 favorite, but this horse took the lead at the final turn and won by 3 lengths - a G1 title at last.
1831: By US dual classic winner War Emblem, brother of 9-time dirt G1 winner Vermilion and 4-time dirt graded winner Sakarart. Like Vermilion he raced on turf at first, then won his first dirt race in spring at 4. After nearly a year off and 2 heavy defeats, he won an allowance and the Sirius S. Well backed in dirt graded races, he kept falling short, but won the Betelgeuse S. (OP) by 5 lengths, showing his class.
1832: A Sapporo dirt specialist. He won 2 allowances there in summer at 4, then at 5 the Shirakaba S. (OP) and the Elm S.
1833: A late-blooming Agnes Tachyon colt. He won the Karasuma S. (16M) in spring at 5 with a 33.4 finish, then the Meguro Kinen. Leg trouble then forced a long break; back at 7, he was past his best and retired.
1834: A late-blooming dirt horse by US dual classic winner War Emblem. Always steady, but as a closer he often fell short. Coming good from summer at 6, he ran well against top dirt horses, winning 4 graded races incl. 2 Breeders' GC, and placed twice in the JBC Classic - a leading middle-distance dirt force.
1814: With his sire Marvelous Sunday's dogged early speed, he was a neck 2nd to Strong Garuda as 13th choice in the Radio Nikkei Sho, then won the Fukushima Kinen as 8th choice.
1828: An Admire Vega front-runner who won only when leading, incl. the Kokura Daishoten early at 5.
1830: Winning 4 straight in summer at 3, he won the Musashino S. over dirt king Kane Hekili, back after 2 years, crop-mate Ubiquitous, 7-length Unicorn S. winner, and G1 winner Sunrise Bacchus. Highly rated, he was still excluded from the Japan Cup Dirt for lack of earnings, causing controversy.
1835: One of the best front-runners in training. Reaching open class in spring at 5, he led and held on for a nose 2nd to Seiun Wonder in the Epsom C. He led all the way in the Final S., Kansai's last race of 2010, then won the Kyoto Kimpai as 7th choice, and the Milers C. as 7th choice too - "never let him lead unchallenged, however unfancied." His next show came in the Tenno Sho (Autumn): 12th choice, drawn gate 1, he blazed through 1000m in 56.5; he finished 16th but set up Tosen Jordan's Japanese record 1:56.1. He passed 1600m in 1:32.2, so as 7th choice in the Mile CS people thought "at that pace he can win," but he ran over 2 seconds slower, 8th. At 7 he won the Milers C. again and led to hold 4th in the Mile CS. In 2013 he held on for a dead-heat-time 3rd in the Nakayama Kinen, then retired to stud.
1836: At 2 he beat even Smart Falcon in a dirt race, then was 8th in the Asahi Hai FS. Racing mainly in dirt sprints, he won 3 JRA-local graded races - Tokyo Sprint, Hokkaido Sprint C., Summer Champion - and made the top five in 2 JBC Sprints, a fixture of the division until 9. He went to stud.
1837: From the first crop of versatile great Agnes Digital. Never in the top five on turf, he emerged on dirt, loving Kyoto's 1800m dirt course with 5 wins there, incl. the Antares S. and Heian S.
1839: First foal of Yamanin Paradise, unbeaten Hanshin JF winner. Unbeaten in 2, he met fellow unbeaten Roman Empire in the Keisei Hai - a rare graded-race dead heat. Winless after, he sired Hanshin Daishoten winner Namura Crescent.
1840: Debuting on turf, he found his best on dirt: 4th first time, then 3 straight wins to the Hyogo Championship and the Shirakaba S. (OP) against older horses. More was expected, but injury ended his career at the end of 3.
1841: By Daitaku Riva, a 5-time graded winner and one of Fuji Kiseki's early stars. With early speed, she ran a big 4th as 13th choice in the Shuka Sho and won the Mermaid S. at 5. Then, 8th at best in 6 starts, she retired after the Queen S. at 6 (11th) to breed.
1843: A small filly like her sire Stay Gold, sometimes under 400kg. With a sharp kick she won the Fillies' Revue as 11th choice and the Rose S. as 7th choice. Her best after were a 3rd in the Aichi Hai and 4th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup; winless, she retired to breed after her 5yo season.
1844: At 2 he ran well on dirt, 3rd in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun. In the Kisaragi Sho at 3, winless on turf, he was 8th choice but won with the sharp kick of Agnes Tachyon's runners. Plagued by injuries, at 6 he won the Asuka S. (OP), his first win in 3 years, then the Sekiya Kinen from up front. Mile success was expected, but a fracture sidelined him in autumn at 7.
1845: A late-arriving Deep Impact star. Winning a maiden in May at 3, he won 3 straight to the Radio Nikkei Sho. Unbeaten in 3, he was 3rd behind double classic winner Orfevre and Win Variation in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, then 10th in the Kikuka Sho and 4th behind 3 crop-mates incl. Red Davis in the Naruo Kinen. Stalling, he won only the Nishinomiya S. (16M) at 4. At 5 he was 2nd, 4th and 4th in open races, then broke down in the Chukyo Kinen and was put down.
1846: By King's Best, sire of Derby winner Eishin Flash and Arc winner Workforce. At 3 he won 2 allowances over 2600m on turf, showing stamina. At 4 he won the 3000m Manyo S. (OP), then the Diamond S. with the fastest finish - Cosmo Helenos 2nd, a Cosmo 1-2. 2nd to Namura Crescent in the Hanshin Daishoten, he was expected to star as a stayer, but broke down in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and was put down.
1848: A sprinter of 2011-2013 with 3 graded wins. 2nd in the 2011 Sprinters S., in 2012 he won the Ibis Summer Dash and Keeneland C., Summer Sprint Series champion, and in 2013 the Hakodate Sprint S. He went to Hong Kong late in 2011, 14th in the Hong Kong Sprint.
1849: By Miscast, son of mile queen North Flight and a 5-time winner incl. the Principal S. Not a standout as a foal, he improved steadily with racing, and in autumn at 3 defied 13th choice for 3rd in the Kikuka Sho, showing stamina. After a 2nd in the Kyoto Daishoten and more, in his 2nd Tenno Sho (Spring) he raced forward and burst clear in the straight, winning by 4 lengths from Tosen Jordan - his first graded win a big title. He kept running well over long trips, but after the Kyoto Kinen at 6 a tendon injury struck. Back in the 2014 Osaka Hai (8th), he retired after it and became a lead pony at beloved Kyoto.
1851: 2nd on debut to later Oka Sho winner Marcellina, she won a dirt maiden easily, then beat later Kanto Oaks winner Colorful Days. After an 11th in the Fillies' Revue she focused on dirt, winning the Shoryu S. (OP), then broke clear early in the Unicorn S. to beat Grape Brandy and Boreas, later 1-2 in the Japan Dirt Derby. Favorite against older horses in the Sparking Lady C., she was well beaten by queen Lavelita, 3rd. After dull runs, she retired to breed in summer at 4.
1852: By Deep Impact out of Biwa Heidi, half-brother of Buena Vista - the finest of Japanese bloodlines; he sold for 231 million yen, the top price at the 2008 foal sale. Delayed to a February debut at 3, he won 2 straight on talent alone, but as favorite in the Mainichi Hai and Aoba Sho lacked a finish, 3rd both times. Desperate for a Derby ticket, his camp ran him a week later in the Principal S., and he won, but as 5th choice in the Derby he struggled on heavy ground, 9th behind stablemate Orfevre. Given a gentler schedule after, his highlight was the Epsom C. at 4 - somewhat disappointing. He retired at 9 after 33 races, notable for being ridden mostly by foreign jockeys.
1854: His dam Kei Woman beat colts in the Kyoto Yonsai Tokubetsu (G3). Over 530kg from his debut, he was 3rd in the Aoba Sho at 3 and ran in the Derby (16th). At 4 he won the Diamond S., then was 3rd behind Alnasr Line and Meiner Kitz in the Nikkei Sho - the pair then ran 1-2 in the Tenno Sho (Spring), and the Nikkei Sho 4th was later G1 winner Earnestly, so his potential was clearly high, yet he kept falling short. In spring at 5 he won his first dirt race, the Jinsen S. (OP), as 7th choice, but was 4th in the March S. Growing past 550kg, he ran mostly in long races, closing fastest for 3rd in the Hanshin Daishoten at 6, but never won another graded race.
1855: First foal of great mare Dance in the Mood, winner of the Oka Sho and Victoria Mile. Closing fastest, she won her debut and the Akamatsu Sho (5M). In the Hanshin JF, billed as a 2-horse race, she fought her rider and was 9th to Reve d'Essor. Showing no fatigue, she won the Fairy S. by 2.5 lengths from midfield early the next year. Going for a mother-daughter Oka Sho, she was 7th. She later placed in allowances at double-figure odds, surprising many, but retired winless.
1857: A Special Week miler. After winning the Mukogawa S. (16M), he led all the way in his first graded race, the Lord Derby CT.
1858: From the first crop of Gold Allure, winner of 4 dirt G1s incl. the February S. After his debut win he was 6th, 2nd, 5th, 4th, 2nd and 3rd in graded races - never badly beaten. In the Satsuki Sho he charged past favorite Meiner Charles but couldn't catch front-running Captain Thule, 2nd. Running well in open races, he was repelled by graded ones until the Lord Derby Challenge T. - where he was favorite at a remarkable 6.7 in a wide-open race. He died suddenly of hemorrhagic colitis at 5.
1859: A foreign-bred sold for 48 million yen at a US sale. Living up to it, he won his debut with an other-worldly kick and was odds-on under 1.5 in his next 4 races. Favorite again in his first graded race, the Falcon S., he closed fastest from last to win. 7th in the NZ Trophy, closing too late, he was 14th choice for the NHK Mile C. amid distance doubts, but charged from behind for 3rd to later double winner Deep Sky. Leg trouble then forced a break; after one more race he went to stud.
1860: Unlike his brother Hokuto Sultan (by Mejiro McQueen), a middle-to-long distance horse who won the Meguro Kinen, he was a miler. 2nd as 12th choice in the Keio Hai 2yo S. and 4th to Goshawk Ken in the Asahi Hai FS, he won the Shinzan Kinen early the next year as favorite with a charge from last. His best after was a 4th in the NHK Mile C.; winless, he retired after an open special at 5.
1861: By Black Hawk, a long-lasting sprint-mile star. Her name is Italian for "fame." Charging from last, she was 2nd as 14th choice in the Aichi Hai at the end of 3, then won the Kyoto Himba S. early the next year under Yutaka Take. She placed in 3 more graded races, incl. 3rd in the Nakayama Himba S., but died of colic at pasture in summer at 5.
1862: At 5 he won the Asuka S. (16M) as 10th choice, but finished in double figures in 3 graded races. Only 11th choice in the Tanabata Sho, he came from 16th at the final turn - last - to win. He then stalled, moved to local racing without success, and his last race was the Oi Kinen at 7 (16th). His name means not "hopelessly weak horse" but "hopelessly naughty kid" in Tango dialect.
1863: After his 2nd win he ran well in graded races, 2nd in the Asahi Hai FS, but couldn't win. Switching to front-running at 4, he won the Rainbow S. (16M), his first win in 2 years, then the Sekiya Kinen the next year. Training for autumn, he had a tendon injury and a long break; back at 7, past his best, he retired after the Sekiya Kinen (17th).
1864: She won the Wasurenagusa Sho (OP) in spring at 3, then was 2nd in the Rose S. and Shuka Sho - near the top of her crop. Then she often closed too late, until her 33.7 kick exploded in the Fuchu Himba S. in October at 4, beating G1 mares like Kawakami Princess and Little Amapola. She then plateaued and retired at 5. As a dam she produced You Can Smile (15: King Kamehameha), a stayer with his dam's straight-long charge.
1865: Somewhat erratic, he reached open class in spring at 5. 15th in his first graded race, the Procyon S., he won the NST Sho (OP), then the Cluster C. by 6 lengths.
1866: Debuting very late, in mid-June at 3 after the Derby (14th), he won his first dirt race, a maiden, by 5 lengths, then 5 straight on dirt incl. 2 open specials. 10th in the Shirakaba S. (OP), he then won the Elm S., but hasn't won since. Clearly capable - he took on Transcend head-on in the February S. and held 5th - he needed a spark, and at 7 moved to Kawasaki for a fresh start.
1867: With the speed of his sire Sakura Bakushin O, he won the Kokura 2yo S. After a 2nd in the Falcon S. he missed the top five for nearly 2 years, but ran 3rd as 16th choice in the Ibis Summer Dash at 5, and retired at 6.
1868: A graded winner on turf and dirt: the 2011 Arlington C. and 2013 Capella S. After a fine Arlington C. win at 3, he was 15th in the Satsuki Sho and 17th in the Derby, then a fracture cost him 2 years and he switched to dirt. Steadily improving in open races, he won the Capella S. late at 5, his first dirt graded race. In 2014 he won 3 JRA-local graded races incl. the Sakitama Hai and Tokyo Hai, but as JBC Sprint favorite couldn't quicken, 5th.
1869: Not big, but well suited to dirt, she won the Kanto Oaks, was 3rd behind the dirt mares' Big Two, Miracle Legend and Lavelita, in the JBC Ladies' Classic, and 2nd in the TCK Jo-o Hai. She also did fairly well in turf sprints.
1870: Half-brother of local graded star Sunrise Max (by Stay Gold). Unlike his brother, suited to dirt, he won a maiden and the Platanus Sho. Narrowly 2nd to Hokkaido's Kanemasa Concord in the Hokkaido 2yo Yushun, he won the big Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun. At 3 he tried turf for the classics without success and returned to dirt.
1871: Raced mainly in turf sprints, she needed 5 starts to win, but in her first dirt race, the Edelweiss Sho, won by 3 lengths as 7th choice, then the Hyogo Junior Grand Prix, and was 2nd to Big Romance in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun. She then slumped and moved to Hokkaido racing.
1872: A small Stay Gold filly. A pure closer with the fastest finish, she was slow to win, but straight after a maiden win she won the Flora S. in light rain, closing fastest. 5th choice for the Oaks in pouring rain for her bad-weather record, she stayed at the back, 17th, and a chip fracture was found. Back after 6 months, she did little and retired to breed after her 4yo season.
1873: In the Sapporo 2yo S. he beat Aventura, sister of Oaks winner Tall Poppy, and Admire Groove's daughter Admire Scepter. 2nd in the Radio Nikkei Hai 2yo S., he struggled after and switched to jumps from 2014. His broodmare sire is Narita Brian.
1879: A sprinter by Dance in the Dark, known for stayers. Winning his 7th start, he won 3 straight allowances. In his 2nd graded race, the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, he was 9th but just 0.6s behind Fine Grain, good enough for sprint graded races. Steady after, twice placed, he won the Hanshin C. at the end of 4, holding off Fallichat. Up and down after, he won the Swan S. about 2 years later, then aimed for the Mile CS but had a tendon injury just before it, and retired after the Milers C. at 8.
1821: A regular in local middle-distance graded races: 2 Niigata Kinen wins and the Chukyo Kinen held at Kokura. Steady, rarely beaten badly.
1838: By Yamanin Seraphim, known for his Keisei Hai dead heat. Improving in summer at 3, he won 2 allowances, then was 3rd to Oken Bruce Lee in the Kikuka Sho as 9th choice. He ran well at long and middle distances alike, yet graded wins eluded him until he won the Hanshin Daishoten by 3.5 lengths at 6. In the Tenno Sho (Spring) he swept from 10th to the lead at the 3rd turn and held on for 3rd behind Hiruno d'Amour. At 7, 3rd in the Hanshin Daishoten, he was 8th to Beat Black in the Tenno Sho (Spring), then moved to local racing.
1842: At 2 he was 3rd as 11th choice in the Hagi S., and at 3 3rd as 11th choice in the Kyodo News Hai. In summer at 4 he won 3 straight to the Ireland T. (OP), and won the next Hakodate Kinen. With 2 wins at Hakodate and 5 at Sapporo, he loved Hokkaido's Western-style turf.
1847: A middle-distance Dance in the Dark colt. Closing from midfield, he won the Edelweiss S. and Radio Nikkei Sho.
1850: She won a maiden and a 5-million race on dirt, then her first turf race, the Flower C., with a straight-long charge. With 2yo queen Reve d'Essor out, the Oka Sho was wide open; 4th choice, she closed fastest from last at the final turn for 3rd. Raced mostly at middle distances, she was expected to shine in the Oaks, but injury forced her retirement.
1853: He won the Radio Nikkei Hai 2yo S. with the fastest finish - Deep Impact's first graded winner as a sire, with Yutaka Take aboard. A classic hope, he was 9th as favorite in the Kyodo News Hai, then straight into the Satsuki Sho as 8th choice slipped up the inside for 3rd. Hopes of a Derby for Deep Impact's first crop rose, but injury ruled him out. Back in middle-distance graded races, he was 2nd in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai and twice 3rd in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai. At 5 he won the AJCC despite a controversially forceful ride, then raced boldly for 2nd to Gold Ship in the Takarazuka Kinen, ahead of Gentildonna and Fenomeno.
1856: Sister of Maruka Schenk (by Sunday Silence), a Sekiya Kinen winner known for late charges after slow starts. She won the Wasurenagusa Sho (OP) at 3. At 4 she was 2nd to Admire Kiss in the Kyoto Himba S. as 9th choice, then had five 2nds and 3rds in fillies' graded races, finally winning the Keisei Hai AH at 5. She retired to breed after the Nakayama Himba S. at 6. Her 2nd foal Mickey Olivier (by King Kamehameha) won 4 straight from a maiden.
1874: After 3 wins in Hokkaido racing, she moved to Funabashi and won the Tokyo 2yo Yushun Himba at once. Then, as odds-on favorite, she kept winning - the first filly to win 2 Southern Kanto classics in 22 years, since Rosita. Going for the Triple Crown in the Japan Dirt Derby, she was 3rd to JRA horse Grape Brandy (later disqualified). 5th behind JRA dirt queens Miracle Legend and Lavelita in the Ladies' Prelude, she won the Rosita Kinen at 1.1 and the Queen Sho. At 4 she kept taking on Miracle Legend, but after her rival retired she seemed to lose her edge, only making the top five from 2013, and retired.
1875: Half-sister of Tenno Sho winner Meiner Kitz, a year older. In spring at 4 she was 2nd as 13th choice in the Nakayama Himba S., then held off Hello Speed by a nose in the Fukushima Himba S. Racing until 5, her best after was 5th in the Nakayama Himba S. and Queen S.
1876: A long-lasting middle-distance dirt horse who beat dirt star Wonder Speed in the Antares S. in autumn at 4. His full brother Meiner Charles won 2 graded races incl. the Yayoi Sho - 3 siblings were graded winners.
1877: By Mejiro McQueen out of Yamanin Arena, from Sunday Silence's first crop. A front-runner who won 2 fillies' graded races incl. the Nakayama Himba S.
1878: Small for a dirt horse at about 430kg, but with his sire Forty Niner's speed he starred at middle distances on dirt, winning the Summer Champion twice. Later a riding horse at the JRA school.
1880: His brothers include 5-time dirt graded winner Nihon Pillow Sart and Kokura Kinen runner Nihon Pillow Keith, and relatives include CBC Sho winner Nihon Pillow Prince and Nambu Hai winner Nihon Pillow Jupiter. With the powerful kick of Admire Vega's runners, he ran well in 2 Niigata Daishoten, then won the Kokura Kinen as 9th choice.
1881: Admire Vega's colts mostly excel at middle-to-long trips, but he was a sprint closer: he won the Ocean S. as 7th choice, the CBC Sho as 12th choice and the Keihan Hai as 7th choice, stunning everyone.
1882: Last foal of great broodmare Legacy of Strength, dam of Rose S. winner Silent Happiness (by Sunday Silence) and 5-time graded winner Stinger, incl. the Hanshin Sansai Himba S. (G1). Unable to win before maidens ended, he moved to local racing. Back in the JRA, at 5 he won the Korea Racing Authority Hai (16M) and Ocean S. At 7 he was 2nd as 14th choice in the Silk Road S. and 3rd as 11th choice behind Kinshasa no Kiseki in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, then plateaued and retired.
1883: From the first crop of Tanino Gimlet, like Vodka; his dam Prime Stage won 2 graded races and was known for her fiery temper. In autumn at 4 he ran well against Shingen, Showa Modern and others in the 16-million class, then won the Christmas C. (16M). Early at 5 he won the Tokyo Shimbun Hai on heavy ground with the fastest finish. 13th behind Vodka in his first G1, the Yasuda Kinen, he won the Fuji S. in autumn, then closed in an extreme 33.0 for 5th in the Mile CS. He then slumped, never making the top five, and retired at 8.
1884: He won a maiden in spring at 3. In the Radio Tampa Sho the favorite (him) was 5.2 - wide open. Sweeping forward from behind, he won a fierce duel. Winless for a long time after, he won the Geishun S. early at 6, his first win in 2.5 years, then was 2nd to Admire Monarch in the Diamond S., showing his graded class.
1885: Like other long-lasting Mayano Top Gun runners such as Precise Machine, Meisho Tokon and Chakra, he reached open class with the Namba S. (OP) at 5, then went nearly 3 years without a win. In spring at 8, last choice of 18 at 477 to 1, he charged to a neck 2nd behind Beat Black. Then as 7th choice he won the Meguro Kinen and the Hakodate Kinen, stunning everyone. He raced until 9 without regaining that shine.
1886: Fractured at 2 and unable to return before maidens ended, he moved to Sonoda, won 2, and returned to the JRA. Steadily improving in dirt sprints, he won the Capella S. in December at 5, then the Hokkaido Sprint C., and was 3rd to Summer Wind in the JBC Sprint - a dirt sprint regular until retiring after an open race at 8 (12th).
1887: A long-lasting middle-distance turf horse. In the Chukyo Kinen at 7, with Yamanin Kingly and Satsuki Sho winner Victory well backed, he ran on doggedly on heavy ground to win as 15th choice. That summer he won the Hakodate Kinen, and was 3rd behind Yamanin Kingly and 3yo queen Buena Vista in the G2 Sapporo Kinen. Like many El Condor Pasa runners, he loved heavy turf.
1888: From the first crop of wonder horse Grass Wonder. Late at 2 she won the G3 Fairy S. with an eye-opening kick. Straight into the Oka Sho she was last, but in the Falcon S. her kick earned 2nd to Kazusa Line against colts.
1889: Strong racing forward, he was 4th in the Unicorn S. at 3, then won allowances to reach open class. Running well in graded races, at 5 he won the Lord Derby CT and Fuji S. Aiming to be mile king, he was 14th to Blumenblatt in the Mile CS, and never won again.
1890: By Admire Boss, son of great mare Vega and an unfulfilled talent. He won the Shimotsuki S. (OP) in November at 4 and was 3rd in his first graded race, the Negishi S. After 3 open special wins, he led all the way in the Hakusan Daishoten at 6, his only graded win. Until retiring at 8 he lit up dirt G1s: 2nd in the JBC Sprint, 3rd in the Japan Cup Dirt, JBC Classic and Kashiwa Kinen.
1891: From the final crop of great sire Sunday Silence. Steady at middle distances on turf, he won the Yasaka S. (16M) in October at 6, then the Naruo Kinen as 7th choice, and the 2010 Nakayama Kimpai. Racing until summer at 9, he drew attention as the last Sunday Silence runner in the JRA.
1892: Winning a maiden in April at 3, he boldly tried the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, 3rd as 9th choice. Steady at local tracks, he won the Nihonkai S. (16M) at 5. In his 2nd graded race, the Niigata Kinen, he was 2nd, and ran well in middle-distance graded races. At 7 he won the Kokura Daishoten by a nose and a neck over crop-mate Battle Banyan and favorite Ril da Val. Sometimes beaten badly but still capable, he ran 2nd as 9th choice in the Niigata Kinen at 7. He retired after finishing last in the Tanabata Sho at 8.
1893: Her name means "angelic tomboy." She won the Aichi Hai at the end of 4 as 16th choice, then became a middle-distance graded regular. At 6 she was 2nd as 14th choice in both the Mermaid S. and Fuchu Himba S., then won the Aichi Hai again 2 years later. That was her last win; she retired to breed after her 7yo season.
1895: His brother was Grand Chariot C. winner Ecol Place and his younger brother Hyogo Junior GP runner-up Takara Stone (both by Grindstone) - a foreign family with a great aptitude for Japanese dirt. He too won the Hyogo Junior GP at 2, then was 2nd to Furioso from the front in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun, and livened up dirt open races.
1896: From the crop of 7-G1 queen Vodka, also by Tanino Gimlet. She won 3 straight in spring at 5 to reach open class and was 2nd in her first graded race, the Mermaid S. She won the next Nakayama Himba S., then charged for 3rd as 11th choice in the Victoria Mile. Favorite in the Mermaid S. and Fuchu Himba S., she was 4th and 9th, and retired.
1897: He led all the way to win his debut by 3 lengths, then was 9th choice in the Falcon S. off a 3-month break, but raced from midfield and won. Very erratic - win or out of the top five - but with 2 open wins, strong when things suited.
1898: From the first crop of Admire Moon, a G1 winner abroad. A colorful closer from the very back, he won the Keio Hai 2yo S. with a devilish 33.6. In the Asahi Hai FS, only 8th choice from the outside bracket, a handicap at Nakayama, he closed fastest from last for 3rd behind Alfredo. At 3 he aimed for the NHK Mile C., 4th in the Falcon S. and 2nd in the Marguerite S. (OP), but was 8th. After an open win against older horses, he won the Keisei Hai Autumn H. in 1:30.7 - a stunning Japanese record. Winless after, he kept showing his kick at sprint-mile trips.
1899: Full brother of Flower C. runner-up Hubble Bubble. Praised for his action before his debut, he won it by 5 lengths as heavy favorite, then the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. by 2 lengths on heavy ground. Much expected at 3, he was 2nd to Gold Ship in the Kyodo News Hai and 2nd to Grandezza in the Spring S. In the Satsuki Sho, on his beloved soft ground, he raced forward and held on for 3rd behind Gold Ship. In the Derby, billed as Gold Ship vs. World Ace, he broke clear from up front and held off Fenomeno by a nose - Deep Impact's first colt classic winner. He then went to England's King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S. against stars like Arc winner Danedream, 2-time hopeful Nathaniel and BC Turf winner St Nicholas Abbey, but Ascot's testing ground didn't suit him, 8th to Danedream. Preparing for the Kikuka Sho, he suffered a tendon injury days before and went to stud.
1900: By Precise End, sire of dirt open runners like 2-time graded winner Glorious Noah. Also a dirt type, she won her debut, a 5-million race and the Edelweiss Sho. After a long break she kept losing badly.
1901: A quick-maturing Sakura Bakushin O runner. 2nd in the Kikyo S. (OP) and Kaede Sho (5M), she won her first dirt race, the Hyogo Junior GP, by 3.5 lengths, then was 11th to Oblutiev in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun. Steady in dirt sprint allowances after.
1902: Debuting fairly late in December at 2, he caught the eye on the slope and won by 6 lengths as 1.2 favorite. From spring at 3 he kept winning, taking the Keihan Hai at the end of 3 on a 4-race streak and the Silk Road S. next. On 5 straight he was 3rd to G1 winner Curren Chan in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, then often fell short. In the Sprinters S. in autumn at 4 he switched from racing forward to closing and ran down Curren Chan for revenge and his first G1. Next his camp chose the Hong Kong Sprint, where Japanese horses had always been repelled (best: Curren Chan's 5th the year before); he broke clear from a handy spot to win, making his name worldwide, and was champion sprinter. At 5 he reached his peak: he won the Hankyu Hai, the Takamatsunomiya Kinen easily as 1.3 favorite, then his first mile, the Yasuda Kinen, for a 4th G1 despite distance doubts. In autumn front-running Haku San Moon held him off in the Centaur S., ending a 5-race streak, but he beat her to win the Sprinters S. again, then won the Hong Kong Sprint again by an astonishing 5 lengths. He retired to stud, the first sprinter named Horse of the Year since Taiki Shuttle. Out of the top two only once (3rd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen at 4), favorite in 17 of 19. Free of Sunday Silence blood, he suits Sunday Silence mares. His first crop gave 9-crown Almond Eye, a record, Mile CS winner Stelvio and Hong Kong Sprint winner Danon Smash, followed by G1 winners like Saturnalia, Danon Scorpion, Bellagio Opera, Red le Zele, Costa Nova and Satono Reve. Panthalassa won the 2022 Dubai Turf and in 2023 became the first Japanese winner of the Saudi Cup - his flair abroad passed on. 2nd on the sire list 5 years running from 2020, the great sprinter may soon be champion sire.
1903: Her name means "sound of the heart." Highly rated, she won a 1400m turf debut at Niigata by 4 lengths, then the Fuyo S. (OP) against colts. Favorite for the Hanshin JF, she broke clear but was beaten by Joie de Vivre's finish, 3rd - her first loss. She won the Kobai S. (OP) without a break, but after 3 months off was 4th to Gentildonna in the Oka Sho, and a fracture was found. Back after 8 months, she won the Turquoise S. (OP), fully recovered. 4th against colts in the Kyoto Kimpai, she won the Rakuyo S. (OP) by 2 lengths and the Hanshin Himba S. with a sharp kick, a graded winner at last. 3rd choice for the Victoria Mile, she broke down in the race and retired.
1904: He won 3 straight to the 2013 Japan Cup Dirt, reaching the top of dirt racing. At 3 he ran in the classics, a fine 3rd to Orfevre in the Derby. Injured at 4, he returned at 5 and switched to dirt to spare his legs; trainer Kunihide Matsuda, citing Kurofune in 2001, was sure a Derby placer would succeed on dirt. As favorite he won the Brazil C. and Musashino S., then the Japan Cup Dirt, dirt king. In 2014 he was 3rd as Copano Ricky led all the way in the February S., then announced a Dubai World Cup bid but was 11th. Injured while resting, he retired to stud.
1905: Running well at middle distances on turf, she reached open class in autumn at 5, then as 5th choice beat G1 winners Yamakatsu Suzuran and Tico Tico Tac in the G3 Fuchu Himba S. As a dam she produced Japan Cup Dirt winner Belshazzar (by King Kamehameha).
1907: A fast front-running sprinter. At 6 he held off 3yo Dasher Go Go to win the CBC Sho. The next year Dasher Go Go got revenge, but he was 2nd - a Sakura Bakushin O 1-2 two years running.
1908: Only placing in the 10-million class, she was last choice of 12, bottom weight 48kg, in her first graded race, the Mermaid S. Yet on rain-soaked ground she charged past front-running Piece of Love to win, and retired to breed that year with the prize.
1909: Winner of the 2012 English and Irish Derbies. Unbeaten, he was one race from the English Triple Crown but was 2nd in the St. Leger. At 2 he won his first races and the Racing Post T., his first G1, the top fancy for the next year's classics. At 3 he went straight to the 2000 Guineas and won, then the Derby as 1.62 favorite, from behind with a crushing straight run, and the Irish Derby at 1.2 with ease. In autumn he went straight to the St. Leger for the Triple Crown, but closing from behind fell just short, 2nd. In the Arc he was 7th, far behind Solemia and Orfevre. Still champion 3yo colt, his 2 autumn defeats hurt his standing. At 4 he won a G3, then was 2nd in the Tattersalls Gold C. and 4th in the Prince of Wales's S., and retired to stud. He sired Irish Derby winner Latrobe and Irish Oaks winner Even So, plus G1 winners in America and Australia, and in 2024 was Europe's champion sire thanks to Bluestocking (Arc) and Los Angeles (Irish Derby).
1910: After 5 G1s in Australia he moved to Ireland and won 5 more, incl. 2 Tattersalls Gold Cups - 10 G1s, 9 of them around 2000m, a middle-distance specialist. He won his first G1, the Cox Plate, in October at 3, and at 4 won the G2 Memsie S. and then 4 G1s in a row. That year he was bought by Coolmore and moved to Ireland, sparking protests at home over losing a star. He won a G3 by 10 lengths and the G1 Tattersalls Gold C. easily, proving himself, then the Eclipse S. and Irish Champion S. - 3 G1s that year. Beaten in the Arc, BC Classic and next Dubai World Cup, he added the Tattersalls Gold C. and Prince of Wales's S. and retired. Back home in Australia at stud, he sired Australian Derby winner Quick Thinker and others.
1911: He won the 2010 King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S. by a record 11 lengths, then sired stars like Persian Knight and Blast Onepiece in Japan. Debuting late, in April at 3, he won only the Gordon S. (G3) that year. Maturing at 4, he won 3 graded races in a row, then the King George, where record-breaking Derby winner Workforce was heavy favorite and he 2nd choice. Tracking the leaders, he burst clear in the straight and kept drawing away, winning by 11 lengths. His only G1, but rated 135 lbs in the World Thoroughbred Racehorse Rankings. Injury ended his career, and he went to stud in Japan. His first crop gave 3 G1 winners - Persian Knight, Mozu Katchan and Deirdre - followed by Blast Onepiece, Normcore, Namur, Cervinia and more. He was 5th on the JRA sire list in 2018 and has stayed consistent.
1912: Sixth foal of Oaks and Queen Elizabeth Cup winner Dance Partner. After debuting in the JRA, injury sent him to local racing; winning twice, he returned and won 3 straight from allowances up to the Nakayama Kimpai, then the Nakayama Kinen. He proved his dam, whose foals had disappointed, a fine broodmare after all. He went to stud in Korea.
1913: Half-brother of Vermilion, dirt king with 9 G1s. Much hoped for, he often fell short and reached open class only in autumn at 4. The next year he won the Tokai S. and Nippon TV Hai, seemingly blooming, but was 4th as 2nd choice in the JBC Classic and 13th in the Japan Cup Dirt. Always compared to his great brother, a bit unfairly, he won the Mercury C. at 6 and was 3rd in the Teio Sho and JBC Classic - clearly talented.
1914: Owned by a former pro baseball player. A leading sprinter with 3 graded wins: the Hankyu Hai and CBC Sho in 2012 and the CBC Sho in 2013 - both CBC wins in record time, racing forward and holding on with real speed. In G1s, the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and Sprinters S., his best was a 4th as 6th choice in the 2013 Sprinters S. at 6.
1915: Half-brother of Mile CS winner Company and Argentina Kyowakoku Hai winner Leningrad. He won a 2000m turf debut at Kyoto with a powerful finish, but lost the Erica Sho and Fukujuso Tokubetsu (both 5M) in sprint finishes. In the Kisaragi Sho he closed in a stunning 32.8 but couldn't catch hyped World Ace, 2nd. After a break he was favorite for the Mainichi Hai; boxed in at the back in the straight, he swung wide and exploded to catch Mount Shasta near the line. His only graded win, but he was a steady mile-to-middle-distance runner, winning the Osakajo S. and Ireland T. (both OP) at 6 and 2nd in the Challenge C. and Kokura Daishoten. He raced until November at 8 and went to stud.
1916: She finished 2nd in all 3 fillies' classics in 2012 - a rare record. That year Gentildonna became the 4th fillies' Triple Crown winner, and the same pair ran 1-2 in all three, a first. At 4, as if venting, she won the Victoria Mile as favorite - short of 2-time Japan Cup winner Gentildonna, but proving the crop's strength. Then she couldn't quicken from a handy spot or from behind, beaten badly. In the next Victoria Mile, though defending champion, she was 11th choice, but led and held off 3-time G1 queen Meisho Mambo to win it again. She also led and held 3rd behind Gold Ship in the Takarazuka Kinen. She retired after the Arima Kinen (14th), as did Gentildonna - their foals' rivalry is eagerly awaited.
1894: Debuting at Sapporo at 2, he won a maiden in late October and was 4th in the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S., but missed the classics. He reached open class with the Spica S. (16M) at 5, was 3rd as 12th choice in the Fukushima Kinen, and the next year moved from the 3rd turn to win the Nakayama Kinen as 13th choice, then 3rd as 7th choice in the Nikkei Sho, retiring at 7. In open class his placings came at 12th, 8th, 13th and 7th choice, ridden by longshot specialist Teruo Eda - longshot fans owed him plenty.
1906: Champion 2yo filly in Gentildonna's crop, from a superb family with many graded winners incl. Buena Vista and Admire Aura. She won her debut as favorite and got into the Hanshin JF by ballot. Only 4th choice, she won with something to spare - the 3rd Hanshin JF winner from one family after her dam Biwa Heidi and sister Buena Vista. Oka Sho favorite at 3, she closed too late, 6th, then a fracture kept her out for the year. The next year she was 4th to Verxina in the Victoria Mile, but broke a leg in training and was put down.
1917: A German mare who won 5 G1s, incl. the 2011 Arc and 2012 King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S. She came to the 2011 Japan Cup as favorite but was 6th to Buena Vista. Emerging at 3, she won 2 German G1s that summer, the Grosser Preis von Berlin and Grosser Preis von Baden, then went to France and won the Arc - only the 2nd German-trained winner, the first in 36 years. In the Japan Cup she closed well from the back but only to 6th. Cartier champion 3yo filly. At 4 she won the King George - the first female to win both it and the Arc. She won the Grosser Preis von Baden again and was preparing to defend the Arc, but an infectious disease at her training center banned travel, and she retired. A broodmare in England, then in Japan from 2021, she has had no notable foals.
1918: Champion dirt horse of 2012 at 5, the year he won the Japan Cup Dirt. That year he won the Nagoya Daishoten (Nagoya) and Hakusan Daishoten (Kanazawa), and was 2nd in the JRA's Tokai S. and Miyako S. - at the forefront of dirt racing. In the Japan Cup Dirt, as 6th choice, he sat handy throughout and broke clear early in the straight to win easily. With superb early speed he added graded titles like the Heian S., Tokai S. and Diolite Kinen, but no more G1s: 2nd in the Teio Sho, 3rd in the Tokyo Daishoten. At 8 in 2015 his best was a 2nd in the Nagoya Grand Prix.
1919: By King Kamehameha out of a Mejiro McQueen mare, he raced at middle-to-long distances on turf at first, without success, then switched to dirt sprints - with success: open class in autumn at 4. In the Cluster C. at 5 he led and pulled away in the straight to win by 6 lengths. Unable to lead in the Tokyo Hai, he was 2nd to Love Me Chan. In the JBC Sprint he boldly took the lead and beat Sei Crimson, Suni and others by 3 lengths for his first G1. He also tried the Dubai Golden Shaheen (12th), and kept starring in dirt sprints.
1920: A mare with a gritty but slow-building finish, who won the 2012 Queen Elizabeth II Cup on soft ground. 8th in the Shuka Sho and 5th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup at 4, she reached open class only late at 5. In her 2nd Queen Elizabeth II Cup, helped by the soft going, she kept on to beat favorite Verxina. She ran in it a 3rd straight year at 6, then retired.
1921: Unbeaten in 3, he won the 2011 Asahi Hai FS. Expected to be open, it was his show: breaking well, he waited, then burst clear in the straight to win easily. 12th by a wide margin on soft ground in the Spring S., he skipped the Satsuki Sho for the NHK Mile C., beaten clearly by Curren Black Hill but holding 2nd, keeping his 2yo champion's pride. In the Derby, perhaps beyond his trip, he was 13th, then a tendon injury at pasture cost him nearly 2 years. Back at 5, he ran gamely in graded races, 2nd in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and 3rd in the Niigata Daishoten. He was Symboli Kris S's first turf G1 winner.
1922: Winner of 4 graded races in 2013 incl. the Lord Derby Challenge T. and Sapporo Kinen. Unremarkable until 3, he stayed in allowances, then came good at 4: winning a 16-million race, then the Lord Derby Challenge T. In summer he won the Naruo Kinen, Hakodate Kinen and Sapporo Kinen in a row, joining the elite. 10th as 2nd choice in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he went to Hong Kong and was a narrow 2nd in the Hong Kong Cup. In 2014 he raced abroad eagerly: Dubai Duty Free (7th), Singapore International C. (4th).
1923: By Heart's Cry, who beat Deep Impact in the Arima Kinen, out of Fabulous la Fouine, Shuka Sho winner and close 2nd in the Japan Cup. Winning his 4th start and a 5-million race, he tried the Yayoi Sho (6th) and Aoba Sho (4th) and gave up the classics. Winning steadily at middle-to-long trips, he was 2nd as favorite in the Diamond S. at 4, then beat Triple Crown winner Orfevre, Tenno Sho winner Hiruno d'Amour and others in the Hanshin Daishoten, and was 5th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) despite trouble. Autumn hopes ended when, after a 6th in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai, he partially ruptured a tendon and retired. With Sunday Silence sires dominant, stud was hard even for a blueblood, and he became a riding horse.
1924: By Deep Impact out of Horse of the Year Air Groove - the ultimate blueblood, much noticed before her debut. She won it as 1.5 favorite, was 3rd to later Oka Sho winner Marcellina in the Elfin S., then won a 5-million special and ran in the Oaks: 3rd choice but 14th to Erin Court. Often 2nd in her own class, she was 14th in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup. In her 2nd race at 4, the Murasakino Tokubetsu, she won for the first time in a year, then the Hong Kong JCT with a superb run and the Mermaid S. easily. Autumn G1 success was expected, but a tendon injury struck, and she retired to breed at her birthplace.
1925: Half-brother of Miracle Legend (by Fuji Kiseki), queen of the dirt with 2 JBC Ladies' Classics. After 2 turf races he switched to dirt in his 3rd start and was transformed, leading all the way to win by 6 lengths, then kept winning on dirt. In his first graded race, the Elm S., he overpowered 6-time G1 winner Espoir City, proving himself, then won the Miyako S. after a duel with Nihon Pillow Ours and Hokko Tarumae. Favorite for the Japan Cup Dirt, he disappointed, 4th, but in the Tokyo Daishoten won a duel with Hatano Vainqueur and Wonder Acute for his first G1. In 2013, favorite in the Kashiwa Kinen, a mile perhaps too quick, he couldn't catch Hokko Tarumae and Espoir City, 3rd, then 6th in the Teio Sho, and went winless all year. At 6 in 2014 he won the Elm S. off a break, then was 3rd in the new G1 Champions C., and in 2015 3rd in the Heian S. and Miyako S.
1926: Half-brother of Tenno Sho (Autumn) winner Tosen Jordan (by Jungle Pocket); he sold for 162.75 million yen, 2nd-highest at the 2009 foal sale. Debuting at the end of 2, he was 2nd twice as a fancy before winning his 3rd start. After the Daikanzakura Sho he raced forward instead of holding back in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai and beat Veiled Impact and others for a Derby ticket. In the Derby he tracked in 2nd and held on doggedly for 3rd, raising autumn hopes, but a tendon injury while resting ended his career, and he went to stud.
1927: By Osumi Haruka, 4-time graded winner incl. 2 Queen S. and twice 2nd in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup. Beaten badly in 2 turf races, he switched to dirt and won a maiden by a wide margin in his 2nd dirt race, then a 5-million race and the Hyogo Championship. 2nd to Straw Hat in the Unicorn S. and 4th to Hatano Vainqueur in the Japan Dirt Derby, older he led all the way to win the Diolite Kinen as 6th choice.
1928: From Deep Impact's 2nd crop; his broodmare sire Singspiel was a British great who won the Dubai World Cup and Japan Cup. He won his debut by 2.5 lengths from 2nd. In the Radio Nikkei Hai 2yo S., with a Big Three of Erica Sho winner Trip and Sapporo 2yo S. 1-2 Grandezza and Gold Ship, he was 4th choice; saving ground among the leaders, he slipped up the inside of Grandezza in the straight to win by 1.5 lengths. Unbeaten in 2, a leading 2012 classic fancy, he then fell away: 8th in the Yayoi Sho, last (18th) in the Satsuki Sho. A tendon injury sidelined him; back in 2014, he won an allowance, his first win in 2.5 years.
1929: From the first crop of autumn triple crown winner Zenno Rob Roy. Like his sire, he bloomed when older; still in the 16-million class, he ran in the Takarazuka Kinen as last choice, 8th. After a 2nd in the Koto S. (16M), he held off Kikuka Sho winner Oken Bruce Lee in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai, 3 lengths clear of 3rd. In the Japan Cup, as 11th choice, he was 4th, best of his crop ahead of Derby winner Eishin Flash. Just 14 days later he was 6th of 13 in the Hong Kong Vase. At 5 he beat Dark Shadow and others in the Kyoto Kinen and eyed Dubai, but nosebleeds ended that plan; after a 9th in the Meguro Kinen and another nosebleed, he went to America, where Lasix is allowed. 2nd against West Coast's top milers in the Arroyo Seco Mile, he was a fine 4th in the BC Turf. Back home, tired and against stronger rivals, he was 13th in the Arima Kinen, and kept racing abroad. From summer at 6 he raced only in Japan, without success, retiring after a 15th in the Nikkei Sho. He became a riding horse in Minamisoma.
1930: Brother of 5-time dirt graded winner Wonder Speed, by US dual classic winner Charismatic, imported to Japan. Debuting in January at 3, he won 3 in 6 months, all at 7th choice or longer. 5th in the Japan Dirt Derby, he teamed up with Ryuji Wada that autumn, winning the Auckland RCT (16M), the Sirius S. and the Musashino S. 3rd choice for the Japan Cup Dirt, he was 6th. At 4 he was scratched from the Antares S. and rested; back after a year, he was 6th in the Miyako S., won the Betelgeuse S. (OP) and was 10th in the Tokyo Daishoten behind Smart Falcon's crushing win. Often falling short after, he won the Tokai S. in May at 5, then split the Transcend-Espoir City duel for 2nd in the Japan Cup Dirt and chased Smart Falcon to 3.5cm in the Tokyo Daishoten - 2 straight G1 2nds. At 6 he was 3rd in the February S., then rested after 2 poor runs. Refreshed, after 6 months off he led and drew away to win the JBC Classic by 5 lengths, his long-sought G1. He was 2nd to Nihon Pillow Ours in the Japan Cup Dirt and 3rd to Roman Legend in the Tokyo Daishoten. In 2014 he was 6th as Copano Ricky led all the way in the February S. and 3rd when Copano Ricky ran him down in the Kashiwa Kinen, then in the Teio Sho tracked Copano Ricky and passed him in the straight to win by 2 lengths - a 2nd G1. Racing on, he won the Kashiwa Kinen at 9, and in his farewell, the Tokyo Daishoten, was 3rd to Sound True.
1931: Debuting late, in spring at 3, she beat older horses in a 5-million race in autumn and ran in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup, outclassed while still developing, 15th to Snow Fairy. She then won the Sakaiminato Tokubetsu and Asuka S. to reach open class, was 2nd with the fastest finish in the Nakayama Himba S., and won the Fukushima Himba S. with a burst from midfield. Her name comes from a classic film that won the Palme d'Or at Cannes.
1932: A Deep Impact colt hyped before his debut. He won his debut in December at 2, then as 1.2 favorite in the Wakagoma S. was caught out by runaway leader Zeros, 2nd. He then won the Kisaragi Sho and Wakaba S., the leading classic contender. In the Satsuki Sho he clipped heels and stumbled after the start, yet finished 2nd to Gold Ship - impressive in defeat. In the Derby he closed fastest but the slow pace didn't suit him, 4th to Deep Brillante. Hoping for autumn revenge, he suffered a tendon injury and a long break. Back after 20 months, 5th in the Shirafuji S. (OP), he won the Milers C. over fellow Deep Impact stars like improver Fiero, on 3 straight, and Kyoto Kimpai winner Extra End. He showed his class around a mile - 5th in the Yasuda Kinen, 4th in the Hong Kong Mile - and went to Australia at 6, but didn't win again.
1933: At 3 he held his own against older horses in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Japan Cup, and at 4 in 2013 won the Tenno Sho (Spring). A classic hope in spring at 3, he disliked Nakayama, so skipped the Satsuki Sho for the Derby, losing by a nose to Deep Brillante. Ignoring the Kikuka Sho, he took on older horses in autumn: 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 5th in the Japan Cup. At 4 he won the Nikkei Sho, then beat favorite Gold Ship in the Tenno Sho (Spring) for a G1. Gold Ship turned the tables in the Takarazuka Kinen (4th). Missing the autumn injured, he was 5th as 2nd choice in the next Nikkei Sho, then in the Tenno Sho (Spring) took the lead early and held off Win Variation and others by a neck for back-to-back wins - a "monster," as his name says. Winless after, he retired injured to stud.
1934: Steady on turf, winning the Falcon S., he switched to dirt at 4 and reached the top. 3rd in the Elm S., he won the Miyako S. as 2nd choice, saving ground from an inside draw and holding on by a nose. He was 4th in the Japan Cup Dirt, 5th in the February S. and 5th in Dubai's Godolphin Mile, but didn't win again.
1935: Owned by Sheikh Mohammed, ruler of Dubai. With 1 win from 6 by spring at 3, she won the Kunshiran Sho by 3.5 lengths, an Oaks hope, then the Flora S. from midfield with the fastest finish, and was Oaks favorite. Closing as usual, she didn't quicken at all, 13th, far behind Gentildonna. Losing her rhythm, she was 3rd in the Queen S. on a light weight but never won again.
1936: Her dam Omega Island was a half-sister of Arima Kinen winner Heart's Cry, a year younger. Debuting in September at 2, she closed fastest in 3 straight races, with 2 wins and a 3rd. Favorite in the Fairy S., she was 4th, then 9th in a sprint-finish Queen C., but won the Flower C. on heavy ground with the fastest finish. In the fillies' classics she was 12th, 12th and 14th, seemingly an early bloomer, but in her last race at 3, the Turquoise S., she ran 2nd as last choice.
1937: A 2012-2013 dirt star who won the JRA-local Japan Dirt Derby and Kawasaki Kinen. JRA-based but a dirt specialist, at 3 he aimed for Oi's Japan Dirt Derby and won it as favorite with a fierce finish. 2nd in the year-end Tokyo Daishoten, at 4 he beat favored Wonder Acute in the Kawasaki Kinen. 2nd in the Diolite Kinen and Hakusan Daishoten, he had a tendon injury and retired at the end of 2013.
1938: Beaten badly in a turf debut, he won a dirt maiden by 6 lengths, then fought later G1 winner Hokko Tarumae to a neck in the Leopard S. in summer at 3. He won the Brazil C. by 5 lengths, but was caught in a collapse of the leaders in the Musashino S. After a long break, he won the Betelgeuse S. in his 3rd race back. Teamed with Koshiro Komaki in the Jinsen S. at 5, he won by 4 lengths, then swept forward from behind to win a blanket finish (first 4 on the same time) in the G3 Antares S. Winless after, he was 8th choice in the G1 Champions C. but charged to 2nd behind Hokko Tarumae, then kept closing too late.
1939: Related to Colorful Days, who starred in JRA-local races incl. the Kanto Oaks. After 2 dirt wins she tried the Fillies' Revue, an Oka Sho trial (7th). Giving up turf, she beat colts in the Shoryu S., but faded from the front to 11th in the Unicorn S. Against top older mares Miracle Legend, Clave Secreta and others in the Sparking Lady C., she was a good 4th. In the Queen Sho, her first race in 5 months, her rider let her set her own pace up front and she beat Clave Secreta by 4 lengths. She has been a steady force among dirt fillies.
1940: Full sister of fillies' Triple Crown winner Gentildonna, a year older. Compact but talented, she won her first 2. Favorite in the Shinzan Kinen over later classic winners Orfevre and Marcellina, she lost for the first time, 5th. Often closing too late after, she missed the spring classics. But in the Kyoto Himba S. she moved early to win, showing versatility. In her first G1, the Victoria Mile, she raced forward and held on for 2nd, won the Sekiya Kinen in summer, and was 3rd in the Mile CS with a sharp finish. Winless after, she was 5th in the next Mile CS, running well around a mile.
1941: A great mare of many G1s, hailed as the best in years. In 2012 she became the 4th fillies' Triple Crown winner, then won the Japan Cup in a clash of Triple Crown winners with previous colt Triple Crown winner Orfevre. Most favored the older colt, but after a fierce duel she won by a nose - the first 3yo filly named Horse of the Year. At 4, aiming for the Arc, she was 2nd in the Dubai Sheema Classic and 3rd in the Takarazuka Kinen, and the Arc plan was dropped. Venting her frustration, she won the Japan Cup as favorite in autumn - the first to win it twice. In 2014 she returned to the Dubai Sheema Classic for revenge: blocked in the straight, she regained balance and surged to win a G1 abroad. Back home, one of a Big Three with Gold Ship and Win Variation in the Takarazuka Kinen, she was 9th. In the Tenno Sho (Autumn) she won a duel with 3yo Isla Bonita but was beaten by Spielberg, bursting down the middle, 2nd. 4th going for a 3rd Japan Cup, her camp at once named the Arima Kinen as her last race. Amid doubts - "is she declining?" "does right-handed Nakayama suit her?" - she was 4th choice. But guided by jockey Tosaki, she raced boldly, pulled clear of Japan Cup winner Epiphaneia and held off Gold Ship and Just a Way to win her farewell. Her 7 turf G1s equaled her sire Deep Impact's record (as of 2014), and her earnings of over 1.7 billion yen were 2nd only to T.M. Opera O, ahead of Orfevre (as of 2014). A retirement ceremony followed, and the great mare left the turf to the cheers of a big crowd. As a broodmare, her 3rd foal Geraldina won the 2022 Queen Elizabeth II Cup - the "lady's" blood has crowned a new queen.
1942: From the first crop of Daiwa Major, speedy winner of 5 G1s incl. the Satsuki Sho and Tenno Sho (Autumn). With his sire's speed and power he won his debut and a 5-million race, the New Zealand T. by 2.5 lengths, then the NHK Mile C. by 3.5 lengths over 2yo champion Alfredo - unbeaten in 4, 3yo mile king. After a summer break he beat older horses like Eishin Flash and Real Impact in the Mainichi Okan for 5 straight. But in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), bidding to match his sire, perhaps beyond his trip, he was 5th to Eishin Flash, his first loss. At 4 he tried dirt in the February S. as favorite but was swallowed up, 15th. Perhaps shaken, he lost his 3yo brilliance, yet won the Lord Derby CT in spring at 5, his first win in 1.5 years, and the next year's Kokura Daishoten - tough at 1600-1800m. No more G1s; he retired at the end of 6 and went to stud.
1943: From Deep Impact's first crop, related to Dance in the Dark and Dance Partner. Winning his 3rd start, he led all the way in the Erica Sho, a classic hope, but missed the spring after poor trials. 4th from the front to Orfevre in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, he skipped the Kikuka Sho and beat older horses in the Hiei S. (16M). At 4 he was 5th to To the Glory in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai and 3rd in the Diamond S., won the Metropolitan S., then tracked in 2nd and burst clear to win the Meguro Kinen, his first graded title.
1944: Half-sister of Nagoya Grand Prix winner Wild Soldier and Nambu Hai runner-up Danon Come On. She won a dirt debut by 4 lengths in November at 2, but after 2 poor dirt runs switched to turf. Racing forward and overpowering rivals, she was a close 5th from the front in the Kyoto Himba S., then led all the way in the Hanshin Himba S. as 11th choice, beating Oka Sho winner Marcellina.
1946: Racing until 8, he won 3 middle-distance graded races. Often placed in graded races at 2 and 3, he won the Kyoto Kimpai early at 4. A fracture cost him a year; back at 5 he won the Tanabata Sho as favorite. At 6 he tried Hong Kong's Champions Mile (10th), and that autumn won the All Comers, held at Niigata. Another fracture meant over a year off; back at 8 in the Nakayama Kinen, he kept finishing far back and retired after a 13th in the Kinko Sho.
1947: From the 3rd crop of Dubai World Cup winner Roses in May. Needing 3 starts to win, he won the Habotan Sho on heavy ground. 5th to Gold Ship in the Kyodo News Hai, he was 9th choice in the Yayoi Sho but loved the soft going and beat the classic fancies. Soft ground made him a fancied outsider in the Satsuki Sho, 4th, then 6th in the Derby, 0.3s behind Deep Brillante. Chip fractures followed; he went straight to the Kikuka Sho and tired, 17th, and stayed out of form.
1948: 3rd foal of Commercante, a graded winner in Europe and America incl. the G1 E.P. Taylor S. After a debut win he was 4th to Grandezza in a strong Sapporo 2yo S., then won the Hyakunichiso Tokubetsu and Keisei Hai. Hind-leg trouble ruled out the Satsuki Sho and Derby. 11th on his return in the St. Lite Kinen, he stayed out of form. His name means "best deal."
1949: Very big for a Deep Impact colt. Debuting late in spring at 3, he reached open class in his 4th start, then in the Radio Nikkei Sho burst clear from 5th - a late-blooming star. 2nd to Clarente in the Fuji S., he was 3rd choice for the Mile CS but lost heart after trouble in the straight, 12th. He was 3rd to Sun Carlo in the Hanshin C., but never won again.
1950: Unsold until February at 2 and bought cheaply, she was from the first crop of Takamatsunomiya Kinen winner Ore wa Matteruze. With 2 wins from 4, she sensationally ran down Oka Sho favorites like Joie de Vivre and Gentildonna in the Tulip Sho. Mishap after a workout kept her out of the Oka Sho; 7th against colts in the NHK Mile C., she was 7th in the Oaks too. 4th against older horses in the Sapporo Kinen and 5th in the Keihan Hai, she beat Mount Shasta in the Rigel S. (OP). At 1.7 in the Kyoto Himba S., she closed in 34.1 for a 2nd graded win. Then, racing in her owner's native Australia, she charged from last to win the G1 All Aged S. - a horse who truly repaid her owner.
1951: From Daiwa Major's first crop, related to stayers Admire Monarch and Hagino Real King. Winning her 5th start and the Akamatsu Sho, she was 10th to Joie de Vivre in the Hanshin JF, then won a thrilling Fairy S. by a neck.
1952: 3rd foal of Whortleberry, a 3-time European graded winner incl. the Prix Jean Romanet, who ran in the Queen Elizabeth II Cup. 4th to Gold Ship in the Kyodo News Hai, he was 8th in the Spring S., then switched to dirt, winning a 5-million race by 3 lengths and the Unicorn S. easily. 7th as 2nd choice in the Japan Dirt Derby and winless against older horses, he broke down in the Negishi S. at 4 and was put down.
1953: First in Japan to win 10 G1s - king of the dirt. A top-level runner from 3, winning the Leopard S. and 3rd in the Japan Cup Dirt, he fully bloomed in 2013: from the Saga Kinen (Saga) he won 5 straight to the Kashiwa Kinen and Teio Sho. 2nd in the Nambu Hai and 3rd in the Japan Cup Dirt, he won the JBC Classic and Tokyo Daishoten - 4 G1s that year. In 2014 he won the Kawasaki Kinen, then let Copano Ricky escape in the February S. but beat Belshazzar for 2nd. His camp went for the Dubai World Cup, but on the all-weather he was 16th, with stress colitis after. Back after 6 months, he was 4th in the JBC Classic as Copano Ricky led all the way, then, with Copano Ricky slow away, raced boldly to win the new G1 Champions C., his first JRA dirt G1, and the Tokyo Daishoten easily - 7 G1s. In 2015 he won the Kawasaki Kinen at 1.0, was 5th in the Dubai World Cup, and won the Teio Sho for a 9th G1. After a 3rd, 5th and 2nd, he won the 2016 Kawasaki Kinen for a 10th G1. He was to retire after the Tokyo Daishoten, but injury a month before ended it early.
1954: As his name says, an eye-opening closer. An imported horse by Belmont S. winner Empire Maker, rare in Sunday Silence's heyday. After a turf debut (3rd) he raced only on dirt and soon emerged. Favorite in the Leopard S., he was 3rd after a rough trip, then won a 16-million race with a late rush. In the Musashino S. he missed the break badly yet closed in 35.3 to win.
1955: Debuting at Sonoda in June at 2, she won all 4 there incl. a stakes, moved to Southern Kanto and beat favorite Angel Tweet in the Tokyo Princess Sho. In the JRA-local Kanto Oaks she beat JRA fillies with ease - the first local winner since Charm Asleep in 2006. Beating colts in the Kuroshio Hai and Totsuka Kinen, she won 4 straight Southern Kanto stakes. 2nd to rival Emmy's Paradise in the Rosita Kinen, she beat her in the Queen Sho but was 9th behind older mares. She stayed a steady force among older local mares.
1956: His grand-dam Happy Trails produced his dam, Kyoto Himba S. winner Happy Path, and Mile CS winner Shinko Lovely. Hyped before his debut, he won it and the Sapporo 2yo S., then the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. in record time despite being blocked in the straight. At 1.3 in the Asahi Hai FS, he couldn't catch Logotype, who broke clear early, 2nd. 3rd in the Yayoi Sho and Satsuki Sho, he was 9th to Kizuna in the Derby. 7th in the Mainichi Okan with the fastest finish, he was 5th to Just a Way in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). At 4, 4th in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and 5th in the Lord Derby CT, he died of colic.
1957: The 2013 Derby winner, half-brother of 2-classic filly Phalaenopsis, a blueblood hyped before his debut. A top classic fancy, he skipped the Satsuki Sho, winning the Mainichi Hai and Kyoto Shimbun Hai and going straight to the Derby. Favorite at 2.9 among 4 fancied horses, he swept past the field from the back to win. He then aimed for the Arc, won France's Prix Niel, and ran alongside Orfevre, 2 years older, carrying Japan's hopes, 4th - promising. At 4 he met Kikuka Sho winner Epiphaneia in the Osaka Hai; 2nd choice after 6 months off, he closed fastest from last to win clearly. Heavy favorite in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he couldn't catch Fenomeno, 4th, and a fracture kept him out for 2014. In 2015 he ran well in the Kyoto Kinen and Osaka Hai without winning, was 7th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), and retired injured to stud. Hailed as Deep Impact's heir, his first crop gave QEII Cup winner Akaito and 2-time Hanshin Daishoten winner Deep Bond, then 2-time Yasuda Kinen winner Songline; in 2024 Justin Milano won the Satsuki Sho, and in 2025 Natural Rise won 2 dirt classics (as of June 2025). He was 2024 leading sire - the "Kizuna" impact goes on.
1958: The 2013 Kikuka Sho winner, out of Cesario, winner of the Japanese and American Oaks, much noticed from his debut. Unbeaten in 3 at 2, he won the Radio Nikkei Hai 2yo S. A classic fancy, his hot temper cost him: 2nd in the Satsuki Sho and Derby. In autumn he won the Kobe Shimbun Hai, then the Kikuka Sho as heavy favorite by 5 lengths over Satono Noblesse. In 2014 the Osaka Hai was a crop summit with Derby winner Kizuna and 3-G1 mare Meisho Mambo; favorite, he was 3rd to Kizuna. Skipping the Tenno Sho (Spring), he was 4th as 2nd choice in Hong Kong's QEII Cup. 6th after a slow start in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), his shine seemed to fade, but in the Japan Cup he raced boldly forward and pulled away to win by 4 lengths for a 2nd G1. 2nd choice in an Arima Kinen with 6-G1 Gold Ship, Just a Way and queen Gentildonna, he led at the 4th turn but was passed by Gentildonna, 4th. At 5 he tried the Dubai World Cup, hated the dirt, last (9th), and retired injured to stud. Fiery and keen in races, he was brilliant in his Kikuka Sho and Japan Cup wins. His first crop gave unbeaten fillies' Triple Crown winner Daring Tact and Kikuka Sho runner-up Aristoteles; the next, Efforia, who won the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen at 3 like his grandsire. In 2024 he sired 4 spring G1 winners: Stellenbosch, Ten Happy Rose, Danon Decile and Blow the Horn. Danon Decile won the Derby, avenging his sire, and the 2025 Dubai Sheema Classic. 3rd on the 2024 sire list, he has shown his class at stud.
1959: Half-brother of Fillies' Revue 3rd Prenotato. He won the Niigata 2yo S. from near last with a finish under 34s, then was beaten badly in the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. He keeps closing from last, without results.
1960: Named "stalk and ray," he swept past the leaders in the Hakodate 2yo S. to be his crop's first graded winner. Then 10th in the Fantasy S. and 15th in the Hanshin JF.
1961: Muscular and superb in work, hailed as the best of the Meiner team, entered for the next year's English Derby before he debuted. He won his debut at 1.4 and the Kokura 2yo S., then was 3rd in the Daily Hai 2yo S., 8th from the front in the Keio Hai 2yo S. and last (16th) in the Asahi Hai FS. Seemingly in a mental slump, he kept losing badly, but won the Baden-Baden C. (OP) from midfield in summer at 3.
