1962: A gelding twice named US Horse of the Year on turf in dirt-led America - the "Titan of the Turf." Racing mainly on dirt until 4, he won the G1 Clark H. From summer at 5 he raced only on turf, winning the Woodbine Mile, Shadwell Turf Mile and Breeders' Cup Mile - the first turf miler named Horse of the Year. At 6 he won 4 turf G1s incl. a 2nd BC Mile, Horse of the Year again. At 7 he won 3 G1s from the Maker's 46 Mile, but a fracture just before ended his bid for 3 BC Miles like Goldikova. He never returned, retiring at 8. Rated 129 lbs, top US-trained horse in the 2012 and 2013 World Thoroughbred Rankings.
1963: His name comes from his sire Macho Uno, the song "Macho Man" and his big frame; "Mucho" means "much" - "a very macho man." The best son of Macho Uno, a rare Himyar-line sire. Struggling until 3, he won a G2 but was 3rd in the Kentucky Derby, 6th in the Preakness and 7th in the Belmont. At 4 he won 2 G2s and was 2nd in the Woodward S. and Breeders' Cup Classic. At 5 he won the Awesome Again S., his first G1, then the BC Classic as 2nd choice, holding off Will Take Charge. He missed the Eclipse Award but won "Moment of the Year" and the Secretariat Vox Populi Award, a fan idol across the US. After 2 races at 6 he retired, going to stud in 2015 and siring G1 winner Mucho Gusto.
1964: By Black Tide, full brother of Deep Impact. Winning his 2nd start, he boldly tried the Daily Hai 2yo S. and led all the way as 6th choice under Ikezoe. Since, he has shown a sharp finish from behind.
1965: By Heart's Cry, winner of the Dubai Sheema Classic and Arima Kinen. After a debut win she closed from last for 4th in the Daily Hai 2yo S., then won the new Artemis S. as favorite, its first winner. 2nd was Ayusan - a Deep Impact foal chasing a Heart's Cry foal, like that old Arima Kinen.
1966: As hyped, he won his debut and the Chukyo 2yo S. from the front. 5th choice in the Keio Hai 2yo S., doubted on Tokyo's long straight, he won from 2nd in race-record time. In the Asahi Hai FS, billed as a clash with unbeaten Kodino, he was caught in a hot pace, 8th. At 3 he won the Shinzan Kinen and NZT narrowly, but was 7th in the NHK Mile C. Switching to dirt, he won the Shimotsuki S. (OP), was 5th as heavy favorite in the Hyogo Gold T. and last in the February S. Back on turf at 15th choice in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, he held 4th from the front on heavy ground.
1967: Winning her debut with the fastest finish, she was 9th choice in the Niigata 2yo S. after gaining 20kg, yet 3rd. After a 7th in the Daily Hai 2yo S., she raced forward to win the Fantasy S. by 3 lengths. 3rd choice in the Hanshin JF, she was 17th, and 9th in the Oka Sho. Switched to dirt in the Tango S. (OP), 4th choice, she surged from the back to win by 4 lengths, then was 2nd as favorite to Best Warrior in the Unicorn S.
1968: The 2013 Satsuki Sho winner, from the 2nd crop of Lohengrin, a miler in Japan, Europe and Hong Kong. After a tight debut win in June at 2, he was 4th, 3rd and 4th, then won the Begonia Sho in record time under Mirco Demuro. At 34.5 in the Asahi Hai FS, he led early in the straight and held off hot favorite Kodino by a neck - the G1 his sire never won - and was champion 2yo colt. At 3 he won the Spring S. as favorite, then the Satsuki Sho, beating Epiphaneia, Kodino and others. Near-joint favorite with Kizuna in the Derby, he was 5th, perhaps beyond his trip. He raced at mile-to-middle trips, 6th in the Dubai Duty Free at 4. Winless for 2 years, he won the Yasuda Kinen at 6 as 8th choice for a 3rd G1, then was 5th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Hong Kong Mile. The next year he led in the Yasuda Kinen but was caught near the line by Satono Aladdin, 2nd, and retired.
1969: By South Vigorous, ex-king of dirt sprints and sire of Namura Titan and Love Me Chan. Based in Hokkaido, she won the Edelweiss Sho as 5th choice, then beat one of 3 JRA fancies, Keiai Leone, for 3rd in the Hyogo Junior GP.
1822: Symboli Kris S dirt colt; won 3 straight, then the Hakusan Daishoten by 6 lengths on heavy going.
1945: By South Vigorous, winner of 8 dirt sprint graded races incl. the JBC Sprint; her dam Haruwaka is related to Ten Point. Based at Funabashi, she was a close 4th to Manierisme in the Tokyo Princess Sho, 4th to JRA filly Colorful Days in the Kanto Oaks, and steady in Southern Kanto races. In the TCK Jo-o Hai at 4 she charged from wide to beat Colorful Days and others.
1970: A long-lasting Oi horse. At 5 he won 7 of 8 open races, and at 6 was 2nd in the G1 Kashiwa Kinen. Still without a graded title, he then won the Sakitama Hai, breaking well to lead and winning by 1.5 lengths.
1971: US-bred, by "Iron Horse" Giant's Causeway. Racing tough with his early speed from 2, he reached open class at 6 and led all the way in the Kokura Daishoten, his 8th graded try. Later he won over jumps too, incl. 2 jump open races late at 9.
1972: 4th in the Kikuka Sho at 3 and 2nd in the Kyoto Daishoten at 4. A closer who often fell short, winless after spring at 4, he won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai at 7 on his 18th graded try. At 8 he still ran in the Takarazuka Kinen and Japan Cup.
1973: Fiery-tempered, he improved steadily once gelded, winning the Hakodate Kinen at 7 with the fastest finish, then the Niigata Kinen over Touch Me Not, 2012 Summer 2000 Series champion. In the Tenno Sho (Autumn) he was 17th to Eishin Flash.
1974: By Silent Happiness, 2-time graded winner incl. the Rose S. Stuck in allowances on turf until March at 4, he switched to dirt, reaching open class in his 4th dirt race and winning the March S. in his 7th. Since: Tokai S. 3rd, Shirakaba S. (OP) 1st, Nippon TV Hai 2nd.
1975: Half-brother of Spring S. winner Flying Apple (by Rahy), sold for over 100 million yen at the 2007 foal sale. On turf until 4, his best was 4th in the Radio Nikkei Sho. Switched to dirt at 5, he won the Sirius S. in only his 6th dirt race - helped by the weights, but beating Yamanin Kingly and Grape Brandy. In 2014 he won the Mercury C., then a tendon injury ended his career.
1976: Half-sister of 2011 Flower C. winner and Oka Sho 3rd Trend Hunter (by Manhattan Cafe). A late bloomer, she came good in spring at 5. Raced mainly on dirt, she won her first graded race, the Sparking Lady C., beating Miracle Legend, Clave Secreta and Red Claudia.
1977: 4-time graded winner incl. the 2013 Kyoto Daishoten. Needing nearly a year to win, he reached open class at 4 and won the Niigata Daishoten, then the Kokura Daishoten at 5. That autumn he upset Gold Ship and Verxina in the Kyoto Daishoten. At 6 he was 4th in the Takarazuka Kinen and 5th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), and at 7 won the Meguro Kinen.
1978: By Silver Deputy, sire of 2-time US champion Silverbulletday. Raced on dirt after his 3rd start, a graded regular from 5, he peaked at 7 in 2012: 2 JRA-local graded wins incl. the Urawa Kinen, 2nd in the Diolite Kinen, 5th in the Kashiwa Kinen. A fracture after the Urawa Kinen ended his career; he became a riding horse.
1979: Reaching open class in autumn at 4, he won the December S. and Metropolitan S. After failing in graded races, he led at a slow pace to win the Diamond S. at 6 - at 190 to 1.
1980: Bred at Odo Farm, home of 1994 Tenno Sho (Autumn) winner Nehai Caesar. In open class from summer at 5, he finished far back in graded races. 12th choice at 167 to 1 in the Nikkei Sho at 6, he set off far clear and it worked, stunning Win Variation, Rulership and other stars. His owner named him after a wild cat that killed a viper with a punch. A fan favorite, he became a lead pony at Tokyo.
1981: Never out of the top five from his debut in January at 3, in his 2nd graded try, the Heian S. at 5, he beat Espoir City - a new dirt star. Leg trouble then held him back.
1982: By Meiner Love, who beat world-class miler Taiki Shuttle. She won 2 from debut incl. the Kokura 2yo S., then retired injured. As a dam she passed on early maturity and speed: JBC Sprint winner Dream Valentino, Hakodate 2yo S. runner-up Meiner Schokolade.
1983: From the first crop of 2005 Dubai World Cup winner Roses in May. Maturing like his sire, he beat Lord Kanaloa in the Hakodate Sprint S. at 5 for his first graded win, then was 3rd to Lord Kanaloa and Curren Chan in the Sprinters S. The next year he won the Silk Road S. in a blanket finish and closed for 2nd to Lord Kanaloa in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen. After a 6th in the Sprinters S. he switched to dirt sprints, at once 2nd in the JBC Sprint, then won the Hyogo Gold T. and others, and in November 2014 won the JBC Sprint for his long-sought G1. Winless in 2015, he was 2nd in the Kurofune Sho, Tokyo Hai and Hyogo Gold T., then won the Tokyo Hai at 9 in 2016.
1984: A late bloomer at 5, winner of the 2012 Tanabata Sho and 2013 Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. Open class only at the end of 4, in his 3rd graded try he won the Tanabata Sho by a nose as 14th choice. 3rd in the Niigata Kinen and 2nd in the Sapporo Kinen, he won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai (G2) at 6, then was 7th in the Hong Kong Vase.
1985: By great sprinter Durandal and, like him, a sprint-mile horse. His sire was named for Roland's holy sword in a medieval French epic, he for a sword of Celtic myth. He won the Chukyo Kinen in 2012 and 2013, both times sweeping past all from the back with Durandal's sharp kick.
1986: A summer horse, with most wins at Kokura. Debuting late in summer at 3, he rose steadily to open class by summer at 4 and won the Kokura Kinen at 5.
1987: A closer who rarely lost badly but often fell short, he reached open class in the Yasaka S. in autumn at 4, and was 2nd in the Fukushima Kinen with the fastest finish. Struggling against stronger rivals, he won the Kyoto Daishoten at 5 in a fast race, beating Oken Bruce Lee by a neck.
1988: After 4 JRA races he moved to Saga, won 9, and returned. Unable to run his race unless alone in front, he reached open class in spring at 6. 12th choice in his first graded race, the Procyon S., he boldly led and held on - at 119 to 1.
1989: Running well from 2, 3rd in the Kokura 2yo S., not just early-maturing: 2nd in the Falcon S. at 3, and at 4 he beat sprint stars A Shin Virgo and Epice Arome in the Kitakyushu Kinen. A "sprint closer," charging from last.
1990: Highly rated in training, carefully raced as he grew, with only 9 starts by summer at 4. 4th to Nakayama Knight in the All Comers, he beat Tenno Sho winner Beat Black and later Arima Kinen runner-up Ocean Blue in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. Since then, 2nd in the Meguro Kinen and 3rd in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai, but a long break and no wins.
1991: A true Sakura Bakushin O, fast and forward on dirt. He led to win the Yoshun S. (16M) by 6 lengths in spring at 4, then the Summer Champion by 4 lengths. Kept waiting in the gate, he missed the break badly for 6th in the Tokyo Hai, then retired injured.
1992: A pure sprinter at 1200m or less, winner of the 2012 Keihan Hai and 2013 Ibis Summer Dash and Centaur S., and 2013 Summer Sprint Series champion. In G1s he was 3rd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and 2nd in the Sprinters S. With Lord Kanaloa retired, 2014 seemed his chance, but he was 13th as heavy favorite in the Ocean S., 5th as 2nd choice in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, 2nd in the Centaur S. and 13th as favorite in the Sprinters S. At 6 he led in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen straight but was caught near the line by Hong Kong's Aerovelocity, 2nd. Winless in 4 more races at 7, he retired to stud. Famous for spinning wildly in the post parade, many fans longed to see him win a G1.
1993: He won the Ohara S. (16M) with the fastest finish, was 5th in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai, then won the Kinko Sho from midfield. In the Arima Kinen, untested at top level, he was 10th choice, but under a perfect ride led briefly; Gold Ship swept past, but he was 2nd in his first G1. Like Silence Suzuka, he was immature and circled in his stall - eased by a big mirror, which went with him to Nakayama for the Arima Kinen. Hard to keep sound, he won the 2014 Nakayama Kimpai under top weight, with 9 horses within 0.5s.
1994: Winner of the 2013 Sirius S. At 2 he won 3 straight incl. the Hyogo Junior GP (Sonoda) easily. At 3 he was 3rd in the Unicorn S., Japan Dirt Derby and Leopard S., then won the Sirius S., waiting at the back and closing fastest. In spring at 3 he went to Dubai but didn't settle, 10th in the UAE Derby.
1995: Winning a Tokyo 1400m turf debut as favorite, she charged wide in the Artemis S. but lost by half a length to Collector Item. 4th choice in the Hanshin JF, she closed wide but faded, 7th. At 3 she raced forward in the Tulip Sho but couldn't catch Crofne Surprise, 3rd. In the Oka Sho, passed by Red Oval in the straight, she fought back to win - her first graded win a classic. With Deep Impact's kick, she seemed a possible heir to Gentildonna, but injury ended her 3yo season, and after returning short of her best she retired at the end of 2014.
1996: 2nd G1 winner by US dual classic winner War Emblem. After a debut win at Hakodate in July, she was rested until autumn; 2nd to Sound Riana in the Fantasy S., she closed fastest among the leaders. In the Hanshin JF, with fancies collapsing, she ran down Crofne Surprise near the line from a handy spot - champion 2yo filly. At 3 she was 9th in the Tulip Sho, 5th in the Oka Sho, 9th in the Oaks and 11th in the Shuka Sho. At 4 she turned to sprints: close 3rd in the Hanshin Himba S., close 2nd in the Hakodate Sprint S., then held off Red Oval by a neck in the Keeneland C. After being whipped by a handler at the gate in the Keihan Hai, she lost form, retiring to breed after the Swan S. at 5.
1997: He won a Hanshin 1600m turf debut, weaving through the pack. Heavy favorite at 2.0 in the Daily Hai 2yo S., he pulled hard and was 11th. 3rd in the Wakagoma S., still keen, he then raced forward and burst clear to win the Kyodo News Hai in race-record time. Favorite in the Wakaba S., his temper struck again, 8th; in the Satsuki Sho he closed fastest from last but was only 9th.
1998: Best US foal of Henny Hughes before his import to Japan. 11 G1s incl. 2 Breeders' Cup Distaffs and 3 Zenyatta S. - a US star of the 2010s. At 2 she won the BC Juvenile Fillies; at 3 she won 4 G1s incl. the Santa Anita Oaks and BC Distaff, Eclipse champion 3yo filly. At 4 her only G1 was the Zenyatta S., but at 5 she was unbeaten in 5 with 3 G1s, champion older mare - the first to win G1s at 2, 3, 4 and 5, and the 2nd after Zenyatta herself to win the Zenyatta S. 3 times. At 6 she won the Vanity Mile, then after close 2nds won a 2nd BC Distaff and retired. Her first foal (by Uncle Mo) came in 2018.
1999: A bold front-runner who won the 2014 Takamatsunomiya Kinen. 13th in the Satsuki Sho at 3, he turned to sprints, winning the Swan S. well in autumn and holding 4th from the front in the Mile CS. At 4 he led all the way in the Hankyu Hai, then in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen beat later Sprinters S. winner Snow Dragon and favorite Straight Girl by 3 lengths for his first G1. 3rd choice in the Sprinters S., he raced from the back, 12th. 2nd in the Hanshin C. when able to race forward, he never won again.
2000: Full brother of Leopard S. winner Boreas and Mainichi Hai runner-up Mount Shasta. A closer with the fastest finish in each of his first 3 races from a Tokyo 2000m turf debut, he ran down the classic fancies in the Yayoi Sho. 4th choice in the Satsuki Sho behind the Big Three - Logotype, Kodino and Epiphaneia - he closed from the back for 4th, proving his win no fluke. A Derby run was hoped for, but a tendon injury ruled him out.
2001: His uncle was 1990 Hanshin 3yo S. winner Ibuki Maikagura. 2nd in a Niigata debut at 2, he won 3 straight incl. the Falcon S., then closed for 2nd, on the same time as Meiner Hoouh, in the NHK Mile C. Mostly beaten badly after, he was 3rd in the Lord Derby CT at 5. Switched to jumps at 7, he was pulled up in his 3rd start and retired.
2002: Winner of the 2013 NHK Mile C. Racing only at 1600-1800m, at 3 he passed up a Satsuki Sho spot for the NHK Mile C. and won it as 10th choice, closing brilliantly wide. He tried the Derby, but at 15th the trip was too far, failing the NHK-Derby double of King Kamehameha and Deep Sky. A tendon injury cost him nearly 2 years; back at 5, his best was 2nd in the Port Island S. (OP). Winless to 7, he retired that November.
2003: Winner of the 2015 Milers C. and Sekiya Kinen, brother of sprint-mile stars like Ridill and Clarente - a pure miler with nearly all wins at a mile. 8th choice in the Milers C., he sat 3rd and ran down leader Sunrise Major. 2nd choice in the Sekiya Kinen, he led all the way for a 2nd graded win. Mostly far back in graded and G1 races after, he retired after the Takamatsunomiya Kinen at 7.
2004: With Espoir City and Smart Falcon, a flagship son of Gold Allure. Little noticed in 2014 with 1 graded win, he led all the way in his first G1, the February S., at 16th choice, upsetting Belshazzar and Hokko Tarumae. He won the Kashiwa Kinen by 2 lengths, proving himself, but was 2nd as favorite to Wonder Acute in the Teio Sho. In autumn he won the JBC Classic in record time, then stumbled at the start as favorite in the Champions C., 12th. At 5 he won the February S. and JBC Classic for a 5th dirt G1, but was 7th in a hot pace in the Champions C. and 4th to Sound True in the Tokyo Daishoten; still champion dirt horse. In 2016 he won 3 G1s in a row - Kashiwa Kinen, Teio Sho, Mile CS Nambu Hai - then was 5th as favorite in the JBC Classic and far back in the Champions C. At 7 he was 14th in the February S., seemingly past his peak, but won the Kashiwa Kinen with a new waiting style, then the Mile CS Nambu Hai. Going for an 11th JRA-local G1, beyond Hokko Tarumae, he was 2nd in the JBC Sprint and 3rd in the Champions C.
2005: From the 6th crop of Rosado, 5-time graded winner incl. the All Comers. She won a Tokyo 1600m debut as 10th choice, then the Fairy S. at 83.3 to 1, fighting back from up front - her sire's first JRA graded win. 2nd choice in the Anemone S., she held back and won a straight duel, unbeaten in 3. In the Oka Sho, on soft ground, she tracked handy but found nothing, 16th, far behind Ayusan.
2006: By On Fire, Deep Impact's younger brother; her uncles and aunts include Hanshin Himba S. winner Queen's Burn and Nagoya GP winner Wild Soldier. At 50.7 to 1 in her debut in November at 2, she won from midfield, then broke clear early to win the Daily Hai Queen C. at 3. After a long break she restarted at 4 in the 16-million class, won the Keeneland C. at 5 and was 3rd in the Sprinters S. Out of form at 6, she won the Fukushima Himba S. at 7. After finishing last in the QEII Cup she retired to breed.
2007: Winning her 2nd start at Kokura, she was 9th in the Kokura 2yo S. after a hot pace and trouble. She led to win the Rindo Sho, then at 89.9 to 1 in the Hanshin JF tracked in 2nd and held on for 2nd to Robe Tissage - a classic hope. In the Tulip Sho, ridden by Yutaka Take, she led all the way. Oka Sho favorite, she tried to pull clear again but tired, 4th.
2008: The standout 3yo filly of 2013. 10th in the Oka Sho, she won the Oaks easily as 9th choice in 2:25.2, 2nd-fastest ever after Gentildonna. In autumn, 4th in the Rose S., she beat fancied Denim and Ruby and Smart Layer in the Shuka Sho - 2 classics - then beat older mares in the QEII Cup from midfield for a 3rd G1. Against top colts when older she kept finishing far back; 2nd in the Victoria Mile was her last good run. Fans still await her revival.
2009: From the "Sakura" family; her uncle was Tenno Sho winner Sakura Chitose O and aunt QEII Cup winner Sakura Candle. She won a Tokyo 1600m debut, then the Flower C. by a nose over Ever Blossom. 6th choice in the Oaks, she was 14th to Meisho Mambo, and kept losing badly.
2010: 2nd in the Tulip Sho at 3, she ran in the Oka Sho. A miler moving between open and allowance races, she won the Kyoto Kimpai at 6 from 3rd, then was 3rd in the Kyoto Himba S. and Hanshin Himba S. After a 12th in the Mile CS she retired to breed.
2011: A 2013 filly star. After the Flora S. she was 3rd in the Oaks, and after the Rose S. 4th in the Shuka Sho - G1 glory eluded her. 5th in the QEII Cup, she was 7th choice in the Japan Cup but closed in a devilish 33.2 to lose by a nose to Gentildonna. At 4 she was 3rd choice for the Dubai Sheema Classic, but was forced to lead and was 10th, as Gentildonna made history. Often closing too late after, at 5 she ran 2nd to Gold Ship in the 3000m Hanshin Daishoten, then closed fastest for 2nd on the same time in the Takarazuka Kinen.
2012: Foreign-bred half-brother of Argentina Kyowakoku Hai winner Taiki Eldorado, related to Mile CS winners Shinko Lovely and Taiki Marshal and Happy Path. A steady sprint-miler who loved Hakodate and Sapporo: in 4 Hakodate Sprint S. he won once and was 2nd twice, and won the UHB Hai and Sapporo Nikkan Sports Hai (OP). In the Mile CS at 5 he was 3rd to Zenno El Cid as 10th choice.
2013: A Warning sprinter who set up many longshots: 2nd as 11th choice in the Fuji S. at 5, he led to win the UHB Hai (OP) at 7 as 8th of 9, and was 3rd as 11th choice at 8. Best of all, as last choice of 16 he beat Bibi Garudan and Kinshasa no Kiseki in the Keeneland C. At 9 he was 2nd as 8th choice in the Hakodate Sprint S.
2014: A long-lasting mile-to-middle horse; ran 14 times at Kokura and won the 1995 Kokura Daishoten under Yutaka Take.
2015: Winning 3 straight from his 2nd start, he was 2nd to Shake Hands in the NZT, then won the Radio Tampa Sho by 2.5 lengths over classic runner Meiner Bridge and graded winner Go Go Nakayama. Unreliable with his temper, he was gelded; never winning a graded race again, he often ran well at a mile.
2016: A mile-to-middle horse with 5 open wins. In the February 1992 Kokura Daishoten he held off Nihon Pillow Brave and Mr. Spain.
2017: By Yamanin Ski, a stud on his pedigree. He won the 1994 Chunichi Shimbun Hai by a nose and was 2nd 3 years running in the Aichi Hai (then for home-bred sires).
2018: A gritty front-runner at local tracks who won the 2008 Fukushima Kinen. Very tough: 68 career races.
2019: A crop-mate of Narita Brian. He beat Derby runner-up Air Dublin in the St. Lite Kinen and was 4th in the Kikuka Sho. Older, his speed served him in graded races on any going.
2020: Needing 10 starts to win, he rose steadily to open class at 6, then won a blanket-finish 2009 Niigata Kinen at 7.
2021: 49 career starts; he won the 1997 Kokura Daishoten in his 42nd race, then was 3rd as 9th choice in the Lord Derby CT and 2nd as 12th choice in the Keio Hai Spring C. His half-brother Osumi Jet won 7 dirt graded races in 51 starts.
2022: Racing mostly at a mile, he ran 47 times from 2. He won 4 open races and the 2002 Kitakyushu Kinen.
2023: Foreign-bred by Singspiel. Running in miles everywhere, he won the 2010 Kyoto Kimpai and was 2nd as 14th choice in the Fuji S.
2024: Crop-mate of Mejiro McQueen and Ines Fujin. At 7 he won the 1994 Niigata Daishoten over later Japan Cup winner Marvelous Crown.
2025: After 37 local races he joined the JRA, 5th in the 1990 Takarazuka Kinen and winner of the 1991 Chunichi Shimbun Hai at 7.
2026: A Tokai Teio colt and gritty front-runner. 2nd in the Asahi Challenge C. at 5, he won the Aichi Hai at 6.
2027: Peaking at 5, he won the 1997 Saga Kinen.
2028: A late bloomer, debuting in January at 3, he needed 4 starts to win and 9 more for a 2nd. Leaving the 16-million class in autumn at 5, he won the Kitakyushu Kinen, then ran 2nd in the Kokura Kinen, 4th in the Asahi Challenge C. and 2nd in the Kabutoyama Kinen, but was fatally injured in the Aichi Hai - a cruel end just as he bloomed.
2029: A sprinter who loved Kokura, winning the 2009 Kitakyushu Kinen and the Encore S. (OP) twice. A longshot specialist, with 4 wins at 8th choice or longer.
2030: Half-sister of Mile CS winner Shinko Lovely and Kyoto Himba S. winner Happy Path. She was top two in her first 11 starts - near Taiki Shuttle and Hishi Amazon's 12. Won the Epsom C. at 5.
2031: At home on any going, 3rd in the Milers C. at 4 and Procyon S. at 5, then mostly minor placings. In the Chukyo Kinen at 7, Shinichiro Akiyama sent him to the front for the first time, and he led all the way as last choice of 16.
2032: A 2000m turf specialist; at 5 he won the Chukyo Kinen and Hakodate Kinen, and was 3rd to queen Air Groove in the Sapporo Kinen ahead of Genuine. His entry for the Tenno Sho (Autumn) was forgotten, and he never won again.
2033: By versatile great Agnes Digital. Under longshot jockey Shigefumi Kumazawa at 3 he won as 10th and 11th choice, then was 3rd as 13th choice in the NHK Mile C. under another rider. With Kumazawa back and 51kg, he won the Hakodate Sprint S., and ran well in sprints after.
2034: A versatile 3-time graded winner incl. the Chukyo Kinen, but 6-1-1-26: win or out. Later a lead pony at Chukyo.
2035: A long-lasting middle-distance turf horse, 67 starts. His only graded win was the 2001 Fukushima Kinen, often at long odds.
2036: By Derby winner Sakura Chiyono O. Switched from sprints to middle trips, he became a local graded expert, winning the 1997 Aichi Hai.
2037: A front-running dirt sprint mare who took on males too, 2nd 4 times in graded races. She held off queen Lavelita by a nose in the 2010 Marine C.
2038: Improving steadily, he won the Aichi Hai late at 4. His rider Shigefumi Kumazawa then won the Winter S. and, with Daiyu Saku, the Arima Kinen - 3 straight weeks.
2039: After a 3rd win in autumn at 3, she held 4th from the front in the QEII Cup as 11th choice. In the All Comers at 4, billed as Mayano Top Gun vs. Sakura Laurel, she led at the 4th turn and held 2nd to Sakura Laurel. On her first dirt try she won the Marine C., and raced 10+ times a year on any surface.
2040: Half-brother of Hanshin 3yo S. winner Gold City. Unlike his flashy chestnut brother, this big bay rose quietly, reaching open class at 6. 5th as 2nd choice in the Sekiya Kinen, he beat 3yo stars Sakura Speed O and Yashima Captain in the Keio Hai AH. He raced 53 times, until 8.
2041: With Toyo Rifaar, the best Japanese runner by US sire Relaunch. After 5th on turf in the Tanabata Sho at 4, he raced only on turf, and the next summer won the Kitakyushu Kinen as 8th choice, catching leader Unbras More. He also won twice over jumps.
2042: By Hard to Beat, French Derby winner and the first European classic winner for a Japanese owner. She won 3 straight in summer at 4, and 3 more at 5 incl. the Niigata Kinen; 2nd in it the next year - a summer mare.
2043: Fractured in his 3rd start, he returned with a bolt in his leg, won, and ran in the Derby (14th). Maturing at 4, he was 2nd as 7th choice in the Kokura Daishoten. After a long break, he was 10th in the New Year S. (OP); then, 2 years on and 11th choice in the Kokura Daishoten, he led at the 4th turn and held on.
2044: Won the 1996 Nakayama Himba S. as 11th choice; a match for males in open turf races, winning 3.
2045: The best Japanese runner of US sire Proud Debonair. He won the Marine S. (OP) and Elm S. by 4 lengths each at 4. At 8 he was 2nd as last choice in the Garnet S., then won the Cluster C., catching Divine Silver.
2046: Steady at middle trips on turf. In his first graded race, the Niigata Daishoten at 5, he was 3rd on the same time; 3rd in the 1400m Hankyu Hai, he won the Sapporo Kinen under Yutaka Take, then went to Hong Kong, rare then (7th).
2047: Best foal of Kiyo Hidaka, still Nakayama's dirt 1800m record holder - one of only 2 in his first crop. He won the Kabutoyama Kinen as 8th choice at 3, then led all the way in the Nakayama Kimpai at 7 as 10th choice and the Kabutoyama Kinen again.
2048: Best Japanese runner of US sire Sadden Saw; won the Tanabata Sho at 7.
2049: Ridden by Hiroaki Kiyoyama, he led all the way as 15th choice in the Naruo Kinen at 5, beating later Japan Cup winner Marvelous Crown, then was 2nd to Biwa Hayahide in the Kyoto Kinen.
2050: An Adjudicating runner on turf, unlike his dirt siblings. 2nd in the Sekiya Kinen, Keisei Hai AH and Fuji S. at 5, he was 9th in the Mile CS, then won the Tanabata Sho over a longer trip.
2051: 8th choice in the Kokura Daishoten at 6, in pouring rain she closed as if the others had stopped, winning by 2 lengths. She ran 65 times on middle-distance turf.
2052: Winner of the 1997 Cluster C., a front-running sprinter with 71 starts. Half-brother of 2-time Meguro Kinen winner Toshi the V.
2053: He won the Hakodate Kinen at 5 as 14th choice, then was 2nd as 10th choice in the Nakayama Kimpai and as 14th in the Hakodate Kinen - a handicap longshot. His half-brother Craftwork later won the Hakodate Kinen too.
2054: Ran well in middle-distance graded races at 3. Older, he went from the Kanmonkyo S. (OP) to the Kokura Daishoten 3 years running, winning it in 1989.
2055: He won his debut in December at 2, then was 3rd on the same time in the Radio Nikkei Hai on muddy ground. After a slow start at 3, he won the Kyoto Shimbun Hai by a head and a head on soft ground. On any going, he loved stamina tests on Western-style turf, running well each year in Hokkaido's 2600m open races. He was fatally injured in the Stayers S. at 7.
2056: Crop-mate of Special Week, El Condor Pasa and Grass Wonder. With 1 win he made the Kikuka Sho via a trial (13th). Winning 2, he was 3rd in the Diamond S. at 4, then won the Osaka-Hamburg C. (OP) as heavy favorite and the Niigata Daishoten at 5. He went to stud in Korea.
2057: A dirt sprinter who stepped up in trip, 3rd in the March S. at 5, then won the Saga Kinen at 6 and was 3rd in the Nagoya Daishoten - but collapsed after the line in the Saudi Arabia C. (OP) and died of heart failure.
2058: Gelded after his debut, he kept losing by over a second, winning a maiden at 3 by a neck. Finding his trip in Sapporo stayers' races, he won 3 straight; next to last in the AR Kyowakoku Hai, he caught Kikuka Sho runner-up Flotation by a neck in the Stayers S. He won the Sapporo Nikkei OP as 9th choice and was 5th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) at 7 - a late-blooming stayer.
2059: A front-runner from the T.M. Opera O team of Wada and the Iwamoto stable. Moving up to middle trips when older, he led all the way in the Osaka-Hamburg C. (OP) and, as 5th choice, the Fukushima Kinen. He also led to win the next year's Australia T. (OP).
2060: Plodding through allowances, he reached open class at 6, was 4th in the Sekiya Kinen, then won the Kokura Kinen and was 2nd in the Asahi Challenge C.
2061: By "white lightning" Tamamo Cross. In open class in autumn at 5, 2nd in the Fukushima Minpo Hai, he won the Kabutoyama Kinen and was 3rd as last choice in the next Fukushima Kinen.
2062: Best foal of Derby winner Tayasu Tsuyoshi. From Hokkaido racing, he was 2nd as 13th choice, won the Fukuryu S. (OP) and was 3rd in the Unicorn S. At 5 he won the Brilliant S. (OP) as heavy favorite and the Mercury C., beating Biwa Shinseiki. 5th in the Japan Cup Dirt, he was fatally injured in the Kawasaki Kinen.
2063: By Bizen Nishiki, Symboli Rudolf's 3yo rival. Raced hard - 10 starts at 2, 15 at 3 - he won the Saga Kinen at 4, running 63 times.
2064: Crop-mate of Vodka and Dream Journey; half-brother of Kikuka Sho runner-up Sky Dignity. Debuting in January at 3, he won the Principal S. (OP) as favorite and was 6th in the Derby. 2nd in the St. Lite Kinen with the fastest finish, he was injured for 2 years. Back, he won under top weight and ran well in open races; at 6 he was 2nd as 9th choice in the Osaka Hai ahead of Dream Journey, then won the Niigata Kinen. Injured again, he retired in 2013.
2065: By Mejiro Titan from a Mejiro family, and grey - favorite in 15 of 21 starts. Peaking in autumn at 4, he won 4 straight and was 5th as favorite in the Kyoto Kinen, then won the Hakodate Kinen at 6 by a nose and a neck. His last race was the 1991 Tenno Sho (Autumn), famous for Mejiro McQueen's demotion.
2066: A big Cozzene colt. After an 11th in the Kyodo News Hai he turned to miles, winning 2 in autumn at 3. Placed in the Swan S. and Kyoto Kimpai, he led all the way in the Keio Hai SC as 11th choice; 1400m suited him best.
2067: From the T.M. Opera O team of T.M. owner, Iwamoto stable and Wada. Placed in graded races from his debut, he won the Mainichi Hai over Hidaka Brian and later Derby runner-up Silk Justice, plus 2 open miles.
2068: By front-running dual classic winner Sunny Brian. A closer until 5, he then raced forward like his sire, 2nd by a neck in the Epsom C. and winner of the Chunichi Shimbun Hai. He ran 58 times.
2069: By Air Jihad, who beat Grass Wonder in the Yasuda Kinen; his dam Nanayo Wing was 2nd to Mejiro Dober in the Oaks as 13th choice. On dirt he won steadily, and at 7 in the March S. swept past heavy favorite Fifty Oner. A male, despite his cute name.
2070: Debuting at Funabashi with 6 wins at 3, he moved to the JRA when older. After a long slump he reached the 16-million class at 6 and blossomed in JRA-local races: the Cluster C. by 4 lengths, twice 2nd in the Empress Hai, winning from 1200m to 2100m. Tough too: 18 starts at 4, 68 in all.
2071: Winning on dirt at first, his Sadler's Wells blood came out with age on long turf trips. With stamina and a light 51kg he won the Stayers S. late at 5. Trainer Ichizo Iwamoto laughed: "The longer the better. Give me a 5000m race!"
2072: A gelding with a US-record 16 G1s, the only star by minor sire Ole Bob Bowers. Sold for just $1,100, he earned a then-world-record $6.6 million - the American dream. Poor at 2 and 3, he emerged at 4, won 3 graded races in a row at 5, then 4 turf G1s from the San Luis Rey S., Eclipse champion turf horse. At 6 he won 5 G1s on turf and dirt, Horse of the Year. At 7 he came to the 2nd Japan Cup as favorite but was 13th. At 9 he won 4 G1s, Horse of the Year again, retiring at 10 with 39 wins from 83.
2073: The American mare who won the first Japan Cup. Lightly regarded, she easily beat Japan's best like Monte Prince and Hoyo Boy, showing the gap with the world. Winning her 4th start and 3 allowances at 3, she won her first stakes, the Yerba Buena H. (G3), in May at 4. At 5, G1 tries brought a 7th, 2nd and 5th, but she then won 3 graded races in a row from a 2nd Yerba Buena H. and was invited to the Japan Cup. The Very One, the only foreign G1 winner, was favorite, followed by Monte Prince, Hoyo Boy and Gold Spencer; she was 5th choice. Waiting at the back, she swept past in the straight to win, with foreign horses taking the first 4 places - a shock for Japanese fans. She retired to breed; her sons Mairzy Dancer and High Bridge Thru were imported to Japan as sires.
2074: Winner of the 1975 English and Irish Derbies and the King George VI & Queen Elizabeth Diamond S. Imported to Japan as a sire, he disappointed. Unbeaten in 4 incl. the G1 Dewhurst S. at 2, he was the classic favorite. 2nd in the 2000 Guineas, he won the Irish 2000 Guineas, the Derby by 3 lengths and the Irish Derby by 2. In the King George he and older star Bustino broke clear in a fierce duel, and he won by half a length in a record 2:26.98, over 2 seconds faster - the "Race of the Century." Perhaps burnt out, he was 4th next time and retired. Siring 3 G1 winners, he came to Japan as Europe's best, but had no G1 or even graded winners here.
2075: In 1980 she became only the 2nd filly to win the Kentucky Derby, and was 2nd in the Preakness and Belmont - a match for colts. Unbeaten in 4 at 2 incl. the Demoiselle S. (G2), at 3 she was sent down the colts' classic path: 3rd in the Wood Memorial, then 6th choice in the Derby, the first filly in 21 years. Leading at the 4th turn, she held on - the first filly winner since Regret in 1915. Placing in all 3 Triple Crown races was a first for a filly. In autumn she won the Ruffian H., a 2nd G1. After 2 wins at 4 she retired. As a broodmare she had only 2 live foals, at 16 and 19; neither raced, and her line ended.
2076: Fragile, he debuted only after maidens ended at 3, then after 3 races and a year off restarted in Hokkaido. Stronger with age, he raced 12 times at 6 and reached graded level, then won a 4-way photo in the Kokura Kinen at 8.
2077: Known as a front-running sprinter, in the Centaur S. in autumn at 6 he raced from the back and closed in a then-unheard-of 33.4, passing heavy favorite Senryo Yakusha in a flash.
2078: A late-blooming Sunday Silence colt. Peaking in autumn at 6, he won the Newmarket C. (16M) by 7 lengths and the Opal S. (OP), then a wide-open Fukushima Kinen. Racing to 8, 5th in the Kokura Daishoten, he was fatally injured in the Osakajo S. (OP).
2079: By Sakura Shingeki, the "Rising Sun kamikaze" who led boldly in the first Japan Cup. A front-runner too, he loved Fukushima, winning 4 there incl. the Kabutoyama Kinen.
2080: The best Japanese runner by US sire Fappiano. Often odds-on at 2, he was 3rd to Mihono Bourbon in the Asahi Hai 3yo S., then won the Keisei Hai in a blanket finish at 3. Running well at sprints and miles, he faded after a 3rd in the Lord Derby CT at 4, retiring at 7. He often raced with his mouth open. Related to sire Gone West, he went to stud in his native US and was New York's leading sire in 2005. In 2006 he fought a fellow stallion, Gold Token, in a paddock and was badly hurt; his rival hit a tree and died.
2081: A sprinter with a strong finish who won the Chunichi Sports Sho 4yo S. at 3. A steady sprinter, short of G1 class. Full brother of 3-G1 sprinter Durandal, the "famed sword."
2082: A sprint closer at 1200-1600m, swooping from the back. At his best in the Keisei Hai AH at 5: on perfect opening-week turf, Hikoki Gumo set a hot 57.0 for 1000m, and he ran down mile stars like Black Hawk and Speed World.
2083: A front-runner at 1600-1800m on turf. In the Kisaragi Sho, his 3rd start, he dropped to 2nd at the 4th turn but fought back to win. Gritty, and popular for a quirky name inspired by his sire Keen. Later a riding horse at Baji Koen.
2084: Raced only on dirt, 8 wins from 1200m to 1800m, but 6 at 1400m or less - a speed horse. Best in the Tokyo Sprint at 7: from 3rd he burst clear, beating Gavrin and Fujino Wave.
2085: A local specialist with all 7 wins at 1800-2000m on turf, 5 at Chukyo and Kokura. All his first 6 wins came from the front, but in the Kokura Daishoten at 6 he raced wide from the outside draw, made a long run from the 3rd turn and won from behind for the first time - a stunning upset.
2086: In the Hankyu Hai, a tricky handicap where favorites had lost 18 straight, he won as favorite from the outside draw - a new sprint star. But 2 year-long breaks for leg trouble limited him to 1 graded win. Sound, he'd surely have been the "star" of his name.
2087: A classic wide-closing sprinter. In the Hankyu Hai, from gate 1, he dropped back by design, swung wide and exploded in the straight. Still in the 16-million class on a light 53kg, but 2nd in the Kitakyushu Kinen and 3rd in the Centaur S. proved it no fluke.
2088: Hiroo Toyama's stable of the early 1990s, led by dual classic winner Mihono Bourbon, was full of stars like Fujiyama Kenzan and Legacy World; he was one. He won the Niigata Kinen and the 3200m Bloodstone S. His half-brother Tanino Create won the Kobe Shimbun Hai, and his nephew Big Week the Kikuka Sho.
2089: After 2 wins at Niigata 1600m he closed for 3rd, 0.1s behind Meiner Max, in the Asahi Hai 3yo S., and won the Radio Tampa Sho in June at 3. From Mejiro Ryan's first crop, he, Mejiro Dober and Mejiro Bright made his sire's name, racing until 6.
2090: She won 3 straight at 1600m in spring at 5, then in the Queen S., off 3.5 months, took the lead early at the 4th turn and held on against Diamond Bico, champion older mare that year, and G1 winners Tico Tico Tac and Lady Pastel - a real upset.
2091: Mainly at 1800-2100m on dirt. Unlike most sprint-bred Twining runners he had stamina, from a family incl. Derby winner Tayasu Tsuyoshi. 3rd, 0.3s behind Success Brocken, in the Tokyo Daishoten late at 4, he won the Heian S. up the inside.
2092: His only graded win, the Hakodate 3yo S., suggests an early bloomer, but he won 2 open races when older and was 3rd in the Sekiya Kinen at 6, at 1200-1800m. That Hakodate 3yo S. was rich in hindsight: 2nd Samson Big and 4th Bodyguard became graded winners, and 6th was later Triple Crown winner Narita Brian.
2093: Winning on talent when young, he pulled hard as he rose, so raced only in fast sprints - fine for a dual-surface Mill George runner. He won the dirt 1200m Negishi S. in November at 6, then closed from the back for 5th in the G1 Sprinters S. on turf - a sprint character.
2094: 446kg at his debut in January at 3, he grew as his frailty faded: 464kg winning a 16-million race at 4, and 486kg winning the Chunichi Shimbun Hai at 5. All 7 wins came at 1800-2000m on turf, and he handled the rough ground in that race.
2095: 2nd in the Chukyo Kinen and 3rd in the Nakayama Kinen at 4, then leg trouble cost him 2 long breaks. Back on track in summer at 6, he won Kokura's Summer S. and the Niigata Kinen over Air Smap and Daiwa Texas, but tendon trouble returned and he retired. Sound, he might have fought for G1s.
2096: All 6 wins came at 2000m on turf. A front-runner, but no tearaway: he won from the front only at slow paces (61s+ for 1000m). Often off with fractures, he won the Niigata Kinen at 6 in just his 10th race.
2097: From 450kg at her debut to 498kg at 6, she grew tough and powerful, rising in fillies' dirt races. Her first graded win came at 7, in the Empress Hai - a true late bloomer. 5 of her 7 wins came under ex-local jockeys Futoshi Komaki, Katsumi Ando and Yasunari Iwata, strong riders who suited her.
2098: Mainly at 2000m on turf, racing until spring at 6. Small but brave, always fighting for a place: only twice out of the top five in 25 starts. Hard to pass once level, she won a fierce duel with Top Coat by a nose in the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu.
2099: Placing but never winning in 6 turf races, he switched to dirt and won at once by 8 lengths. In July at 5 he led all the way to win the Mercury C. at Morioka by 9 lengths over Coolinger - power, and the speed shown on turf too.
2100: At 2 and 3 he won the Erica Sho and Keisei Hai, a classic contender, then late at 4 switched to dirt sprints and revived as a front-runner, winning the Subaru S. and Uzumasa S. He tried jumps, then in spring at 7 moved to Masayuki Kawashima's stable at Funabashi.
2101: JRA-based, yet his first 3 wins came in JRA-local races at Sonoda. A dirt sprinter at first, he ran well on turf from 4, reaching open class at 6. In the Ibis Summer Dash he closed in an amazing 31.6 - a turf sprint closer.
2102: Debuting at Niigata (local) with 8 wins from 13 at 3, he moved to the JRA. Racing at 1600-1800m, he was 3rd in his first 2500m race late at 5, then focused on long turf races, winning the Geishun S. and Nikkei Sho at Nakayama 2500m. In the Nikkei Sho on heavy ground he split Calypso Song and Chokai Ace in the straight - real grit.
2103: 2nd in the Aoba Sho and a Derby runner, he bloomed at 4. His first graded win, the Chukyo Kinen, was dominant: tracking 5th in a hot 57.8 pace, he led before the 4th turn and pulled away to win by 5 lengths under "pro" Yoshiyasu Tajima.
2104: Held back at 3 by frailty and leg trouble, he grew fast when older and emerged at middle trips on turf. In the Kyoto Kinen at 5 he led, dropped to 2nd at the 3rd turn, then fought back to win. His sire Hurry was a British long-distance graded winner, the source of his stamina and calm.
2105: Every summer an improver wins race after race; in 2004 it was him. From a Hakodate 1800m 5-million race in July, he won 4 straight in Hokkaido incl. the Hoyo Boy Memorial, TVh Sho and HTB Sho, then the Fukushima Kinen that autumn - a local graded regular.
2106: He led to win his first 2 at Sapporo 1200m, then struggled. When trainer Masatoshi Ando retired in autumn 2007, he moved to Yoshito Yahagi's stable; he won the Fruit Line C. (Fukushima dirt 1150m) by 5 lengths and the Kibune S., then the Garnet S. - a dirt sprint front-runner.
2107: He missed the classics, but his early promise - beating colts as favorite in the Yamafuji Sho at 3 - bloomed in summer at 4. After beating later open horse Keiwan and later graded winner Yuwa Beam in the Akanko Tokubetsu, he won the Hakodate Kinen as 13th of 14 on a light 51kg, teaming with Hitoshi Matoba.
2108: His sire Long Fast, 2nd in the Derby and Kikuka Sho, won 8 but only 1 graded race, the Swan S. He inherited that: 3rd in the Kokura Daishoten and Chunichi Shimbun Hai, 2nd in the Chukyo Kinen. On his 15th graded try, at 6, he won the Keihan Hai - dreams come true.
2109: He won the Hokkaido 3yo Yushun while still a maiden - a rare graded race as a first win. Dropping to the 9-million class, he won 3 to return to open class at 7, and raced in Australia at 9. His full brothers Win Marvelous, Royal Cancer and Win Duel were open horses too.
2110: All 7 wins at 1200-1400m on dirt, charging wide from the back - a rare closer among dirt sprinters. In the Capella S. late at 4, on fast wet ground behind a blistering 32.7 first 600m, he set a JRA record of 1:08.7.
2111: Winning the Mikuni Tokubetsu in September at 4, he won 5 in 7 months to the Sobu S., then struggled in open class. 3rd in the Azuma Kofuji OP at 6, he won the Tanabata Sho by racing wide on the better ground. Like his half-sister Nifty Niece, he kept improving.
2112: His sire Grindstone (1996) and grandsire Unbridled (1990) both won the Kentucky Derby. With that power and speed he shone early on dirt; in summer at 3 he led all the way in Asahikawa's Grand Chariot C. by 6 lengths, the 3rd another 7 back.
2113: Related to Tenno Sho winner Hokuto Boy, she showed early promise but, nervous, stalled for a while. Maturing in summer at 4, she was 2nd in the Hakodate Kinen, won the UHB Hai by 3.5 lengths over Legacy World, then charged wide to win the Fuchu Himba S.
2114: 11th choice in the Mainichi Hai at 3, he ran 2nd from the front and raced boldly in the Derby. At 4 he went up the muddy rail to win the Hankyu Hai, and led for 2nd as 14th choice in the Takamatsunomiya Hai - dangerous when forgotten.
2115: His dam Solo Singer ran in the Oka Sho. Under trainer Yamauchi, who also trained his dam, he won the Kyodo News Hai and was 4th in the Satsuki Sho. From 4 he turned to dirt like his sire Brian's Time, 2nd in 2 open races, and raced at Kasamatsu until 8.
2116: Crop-mate of Tokai Teio. He won the Kyodo News Hai 4yo S. and ran in all 3 classics, 3rd in the Satsuki Sho and Derby. A sharp closer but tricky; if he pulled, his kick misfired, so he tested his riders. Tough too: 22 starts in 17 months.
2117: At 3 and 4 he regularly closed fastest from the back. Slow to win but rock-steady, top five 16 straight. 4th in a 10-million race, he ran again a week later in the Aichi Hai (home-bred sires only) and, under Aichi jockey Minoru Yoshida, won by a nose - a 2-class jump to a graded win.
2118: With the JRA until June at 5, he won 5 on dirt. Moving to local racing, he won stakes at Morioka, Kaminoyama and Mizusawa, beating later G1 winner Toho Emperor. Moving to Kochi at 9, he raced 20+ times a year from 10 to 15: 27 wins from 233.
2119: By Rodrigo de Triano, a 2000 Guineas winner, out of a Southern Kanto Oka Sho winner - but via his broodmare sire Alanas, 3rd in the 3100m Grand Prix de Paris, 5 of his 7 wins came at 2400m+. In the Diamond S. at 6, under Olivier Peslier, he raced handy on the rail and won like a stayer.
2120: "Bakushin O for sprints, Sekai O for middle trips." Same owner, age and sire as Sakura Bakushin O, debuting a day apart. Long outshone, he was then 3rd in the Yayoi Sho and NHK Hai and won the Valentine S. (OP) from the 9-million class.
2121: A local specialist at 1800-2000m on turf, he won the Fukushima Minpo Hai at 4, then blossomed at 6 with Shoichi Osaki. He won the Joetsu S., was 2nd in the Toki S., then avoided the rain-damaged rail to win the Niigata Kinen from wide.
2122: Debuting at Sapporo at 2, 6th at best in 4 turf races, he switched to dirt in December and won at once. All 5 wins came at 1600-1800m on dirt. In the Grand Chariot C. at 3 he beat Kasamatsu's Fujino Condor and later G1 winner Mugamuchu.
2123: Around 1990 Mill George runners like Inari One, Rosita and Osaichi George shone. Winning his debut in autumn at 2, he emerged at 3 and won the Kobe Shimbun Hai. Older, he often placed in graded races: 2nd as 10th choice in the Keihan Hai, 2nd as 11th in the Kinko Sho - a longshot favorite.
2124: He won a Fukushima 1000m turf debut in June at 2 in record time, by 4 lengths. A turf sprinter at 2 and 3, after winning the dirt Happy End C. late at 3 he starred in dirt sprints, winning the Hokkaido Sprint C. at Sapporo as favorite over Nobo True and Shadow Scape.
2125: Her first 4 wins came on dry dirt, but from summer at 5 she handled turf sprints and gained speed with age. At 6, after an 18th as favorite in the Ibis Summer Dash, she closed powerfully to win the Kitakyushu Kinen. As a dam, by Deep Impact she produced graded winners Mikki Glory and Katsuji.
2126: Placed from 3, e.g. 3rd on the same time as Silva Cockpit in the Kisaragi Sho, but often lacked a kick. A 2600m win at Kokura at 4 turned him into a stayer: in the Good Luck H. he matched the Arima Kinen time on the same day and course, then won the Diamond S.
2127: 5th, 0.5s behind Dance in the Dark, in the Kikuka Sho, a prized talent, but after the Naruo Kinen (8th) a fracture cost him 2 years 10 months. Back, he was 4th as 14th choice in the Meguro Kinen at 7, then won the Tanabata Sho, held at Tokyo that year.
2128: A powerful closer at 1800-2000m on turf, best on long straights - Tokyo, and old Niigata's outer course. In the Niigata Kinen at 6 he closed fastest in 34.4, rare then - a striking run.
2129: Tough from June at 2: 12 starts at 3, 11 at 4, 10 at 5. A middle-distance front-runner, at 6 she led all the way in the Mermaid S. over Bella Leia and Little Amapola.
2130: Early-maturing, she won her June debut at 2 by 4 lengths over later classic runner-up Dantsu Flame. Beaten by Tenzan Desert in the Lavender Sho, she held off Gary Mucho in the Hakodate 3yo S.
2131: She won her first 4 incl. the Fantasy S. Favorite in the Hanshin JF, she was 4th to Tamuro Cherry in a blanket finish, then 3rd in the Fillies' Revue. Injured, she returned after 1.5 years to win the Niigata Nippo Sho, but retired after another injury. She was ridden by Naosuke Sugai, later trainer of Just a Way and Gold Ship.
2132: A Special Week front-running miler. In open class in autumn at 4, he held off Kyoei Storm by a nose in the Keisei Hai AH. He raced on locally after.
2133: He ran down $1.1-million buy Star El Dorado in the Hakodate 2yo S. Often placing in turf sprints without winning, he won the Rokko Island S. (16M) late at 4, 2 years on.
2134: He led to win a dirt allowance by 5 lengths as 11th choice, then the Chunichi Sports Sho 4yo S. by 3 lengths as 13th choice - both under front-running master Nakadate. A sprint front-runner, he also won the Fukushima Minyu C. (OP).
2135: Winning first in local racing, she returned to the JRA and turned to long turf races at 4, running on gamely. After a 4th in the Keihan Hai at 5, she won the Shinshun S. (16M) from last and the Kyoto Himba S.
2136: He beat later graded winner Sunrise Jaeger in the Kyushu Sports Hai at 5, then went early to win the Kokura Kinen on 52kg. His half-brother Aratama Summons was 3rd in it, and his nephew Aratama Universe 2nd in the Kokura Summer Jump.
2137: By Kingmambo, sire of El Condor Pasa and American Boss. He led to win at 4, then was 4th as favorite to later G1 winner Tsurumaru Boy in the Chukyo Kinen, the only front-runner in the top five. 6th choice in the Niigata Daishoten, he led and held everyone off.
2138: 5th on debut, he ran twice more at 2-week gaps, winning his 3rd start, then again 2 weeks later ran in the Hakodate 2yo S. As 9th choice he caught leader Toho Asuka - his camp's will to win it. At 3 he won the Fukushima Minyu C. (OP), on turf or dirt.
2139: A late-blooming dirt closer. In his first graded race, the Sirius S. at 5, he was 2nd, then won the Musashino S. A handsome grey, he became a lead pony after retiring.
2140: A very late bloomer: 13 starts to win, a 2nd win in his 43rd. After a 4th win in his 52nd, he won the Kabutoyama Kinen as 9th choice on 50kg. He ran 62 times.
2141: Half-brother of Flower C. winner Shonan Talent. Winning his 2nd start, he used his speed to win 3 straight incl. the Kyodo News Hai. 3rd in the Spring S., he was 3rd choice in the Satsuki Sho but missed the break and finished far back. Losing form, he became a closer and won a 16-million race at 5, 2 years on, then was 2nd as 9th choice in the Swan S. with the fastest finish.
2142: Without a classic despite a 2nd, 4th and 2nd, he made up for it by winning the Dubai Turf the next year, his first G1. Highly rated from his debut, a top classic fancy, he was 2nd to Duramente's charge in the Satsuki Sho. In the Derby he chased Duramente from behind but was 4th, also passed by Satono Rasen and Satono Crown. 2nd choice in the Kikuka Sho without Duramente, he lost by a neck to Kitasan Black. In the Dubai Turf he raced handy and broke clear in the straight, held off all under star jockey Ryan Moore. 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 5th in the Japan Cup, the next year he won the Mainichi Okan but was 4th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). At 7, 3rd in the Dubai Turf, he was beaten badly in the Yasuda Kinen and retired injured to stud. He has sired Leben Stil, Chikappa and Forever Young, who won 3 local G1s and raced abroad: 3rd in the Kentucky Derby and BC Classic, and in 2025 winner of the Saudi Cup, his earnings 2nd all-time, ahead of Equinox and 9-crown Almond Eye (as of June 2025). Expect his foals to shine on turf and dirt.
2143: By Sunday Silence, then all-conquering. 3rd with the fastest finish on debut, he won 3 straight incl. 2 open races. Out of form in spring, he won the Radio Tampa Sho in July with his old kick, and was 2nd to Tokai Point in the Nakayama Kinen in 33.9.
2144: Winner of the 1980 Tenno Sho (Spring). Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Chukyo 3yo S. (old age system), injury then kept him out long. Back in autumn at 4, he was 5th as favorite in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, 8th in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai and 6th in the Kikuka Sho. At 5 he won an open race by 8 lengths, then as 3rd choice won a duel with Mejiro Transam in the Tenno Sho (Spring). After a 10th in the Takarazuka Kinen he retired; his best foal was Shinzan Kinen winner Nichido Thunder.
2145: Winner of the 2009 Procyon S. Fragile, with only 6 starts by the end of 5, he won his way up to open class in January at 6, then won the Procyon S. - Agnes Tachyon's first dirt graded winner. Leg trouble kept him from big races, and he retired in May at 7.
2146: Winner of the 2008 Keihan Hai. Raced on dirt due to leg trouble, she emerged on turf in autumn at 4: 2nd in the Kyoraku S., then won the Keihan Hai as 4th choice. 15th as favorite in the Silk Road S., she mostly finished far back in turf sprints after, and became a broodmare in 2011.
2147: Early to shine, she won her 2nd start, was 3rd in the Phoenix Sho (OP), then won the Kokura 3yo S. (old name) and the TV Tokyo 3yo Himba S. (now Fairy S.). Overtaken by rivals, she was 14th in the Oka Sho and 18th in the Oaks, then 2nd in the Opal S. (OP) as a sprinter. Her daughter Meisho Sabato carries on her line.
2148: Debuting at Kasamatsu, he won 5 straight incl. the 2000 Daily Hai 3yo S. Still at Kasamatsu, he tried the JRA classics (14th in the Spring S., 8th in the NHK Mile C.), then moved to the JRA and was 2nd in the Unicorn S. Mostly beaten badly after, he went to Funabashi, won the Chiba Nippo Sho, and returned to Kasamatsu at 6: 13 wins from 71, racing until 9.
2149: Won the 2004 Keisei Hai, beating heavy favorite and later Derby winner King Kamehameha - a win many still rate. Favorite in the Yayoi Sho, he was 5th to Cosmo Bulk, then flopped in the Satsuki Sho and Derby. A crop with Daiwa Major, Company and Heart's Cry was hard luck.
2150: A late star by Tosho Boy. He won his debut by a huge margin as favorite, then the Daily Hai 3yo S., beating later Triple Crown winner Narita Brian. 7th in the Asahi Hai 3yo S., he rested from spring. Back when older, he won the Hankyu Hai over defending winner Gold Mountain, then after another long break moved to Urawa and retired.
2151: Won the 2003 Fairy S., then a 2yo race. A classic fancy, she won the Elfin S. and was 2nd in the Fillies' Revue, but 11th in the Oka Sho, and never won on the flat again. She won once over jumps at 5, retired in 2007 and produced front-running 3-time graded winner Maltese Apogee (12: Goshawk Ken).
2152: Winner of the 2001 Nakayama Kimpai. 2nd in the 4yo Himba Tokubetsu at 3, she was 13th in the Oaks and Shuka Sho, then improved in open races and won the Nakayama Kimpai at 4 - longshots filled the top 3 in a rare upset. Little in 15 more races; a broodmare from 2003.
2153: Winner of the 2008 Flora S. 2nd on the same time to later Shuka Sho winner Black Emblem in the Flower C., she won the Flora S. as favorite and was 2nd choice in the Oaks, 6th to Tall Poppy. Rarely placed after, she retired at the end of 5 with 2 wins from 33: a maiden and the Flora S. As a dam she produced Red Genial (16: King Kamehameha), who won the Kyoto Shimbun Hai as 11th choice.
2154: Winner of the 1981 QEII Cup. Overshadowed by Brocade and Tenmon in spring, she grew fast in autumn, winning the Sapphire S. and Kobe Shimbun Hai, then the QEII Cup, sharing champion 3yo filly with Tenmon. She tried the Arima Kinen, Tenno Sho (Spring) and Takarazuka Kinen without success, retiring at 4.
2155: The 1981 Oaks winner. Though she retired after it, she beat 2-classic colt Katsu Top Ace and classic regular San'ei Solon - hailed as the best filly since Tesco Gaby. Debuting in July at 3 (old age system), she beat San'ei Solon in the Shiragiku Sho, then Katsu Top Ace and others in the Asahi Hai 3yo S. At 4 she beat colts in the Keisei Hai, but struggled on heavy ground for 2nd to Brocade in the Oka Sho. Her camp said "the Oaks is hers," and from midfield she burst clear to win easily. Badly injured in a typhoon while resting that summer, she retired, and the injury limited her as a broodmare.
2156: The 1981 Oka Sho winner, who also won the Sprinters S. at 5 (old age system). Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, she was Oka Sho favorite; on a quagmire, she broke clear from a handy spot to win easily, having won on heavy ground before. 13th to Tenmon in the Oaks, beyond her trip, she then fought a classic duel with older Oka Sho winner Hagino Top Lady in the Tomoe Sho, losing a photo. Turning to sprints, 2nd in the CBC Sho, she beat defending champion Sakura Shingeki in the Sprinters S. At 6 she was 2nd in the Milers C., Yasuda Kinen and Hakodate Kinen. No notable foals.
2157: A Southern Kanto star who won the 1981 Takarazuka Kinen. At 4 he won 5 straight: Diolite Kinen, Teio Sho, Oi Kinen, the JRA Invitational and Sapphire Tokubetsu. Moving to the JRA at 5, he was 2nd to Katsurano Haiseiko in the Tenno Sho (Spring), then beat him as 3rd choice in the Takarazuka Kinen - local grit. 2nd in it again at 6, he retired in summer at 7.
2158: His half-brother Riki Ai O won the Yayoi Sho and Spring S. Winning early, he was 6th in the Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system). Blooming at 5, he won 4 straight: an open race, the Meguro Kinen, Nakayama Kinen and Sapporo Kinen. 13th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 15th in the Arima Kinen, he won the Sapporo Nikkei Sho at 6 and retired after a 3rd in the All Comers.
2159: Unbeatable at 2 in 1979: she won her debut by 10 lengths and 5 straight to the Hanshin 3yo S. (old name), beating later Derby winner Opec Horse and Kikuka Sho winner North Gust. A slump followed for 1.5 years, but in summer at 4 she won the Kokura Nikkei Sho, Kitakyushu Kinen, Kokura Kinen and Asahi Challenge C. - champion older mare.
2160: Winner of the 1980 and 1981 Kawasaki Kinen in Southern Kanto. Moving to the JRA late at 5, he was 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 5th in the Japan Cup, best of the Japanese. Winless in the JRA until retiring at 6, he often made the top five in big races.
2162: Winning a maiden at 4 (old age system), she rose steadily to summer at 5. After the Iide Tokubetsu, as 7th choice she ran away with the Niigata Kinen, then beat heavy favorite Hoyo Boy in the All Comers. Beaten by Hoyo Boy in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen, she stood up to seasoned males. No notable foals.
2163: Winner of the Shinzan Kinen and Kisaragi Sho, then the Keihan Hai twice - jockey Tadashi Kayo's first graded wins. At 4 (old age system), 4th as favorite in the Spring S., he rested; his only classic was an 8th in the Kikuka Sho. After a 3rd in the Kyoto Kinen (Autumn), he won the Keihan Hai at 5 and again at 6. Switched to jumps at 8, he won a maiden and retired.
2164: Winner of the Nakayama Himba S. at 6 and 7 (old age system), and at 8 the Chunichi Shimbun Hai - the first graded win by an 8yo mare. Blooming at 5 with the Kabutoyama Kinen, she won the Nakayama Himba S. and Fukushima Kinen at 6. Out of the top five only 3 times at 2000m or less, and top three in all but one race on soft or heavy ground. No notable foals.
2165: The best runner by little-known sire Yellapa. 13th in the Derby and 6th in the Kikuka Sho at 4 (old age system), he was 3rd in the Hanshin Daishoten, 2nd in the Sankei Osaka Hai and won the Kinko Sho at 5. He won the Sapporo Kinen (then on dirt) at 6 and 7. After an 11th in the Takarazuka Kinen at 8 he moved to local racing, racing until 10.
2166: Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Hokkaido 3yo S. (old age system; now Sapporo 2yo S.), then 3rd and 5th, he won the Shinzan Kinen at 4. 18th in the Derby and 13th in the Kikuka Sho, he won the Sapporo Kinen (then on dirt) and Tanchori S., a dirt force. At 5 he was 2nd in the Sankei Osaka Hai and won the Hankyu Hai; at 6, 2nd in the Sapporo Kinen and won the Tanchori S. He later raced locally.
2167: Winner of the 1982 QEII Cup. A super blueblood given a treasured name by Chiyoda Farm and trained by filly specialist Yukio Inaba. Injured in spring at 3 while unbeaten, she missed the Oka Sho and Oaks. Back in autumn she won the QEII Cup easily, then was 5th to Hikari Duel in the Arima Kinen, champion 4yo filly (old name). Called the "phantom Triple Crown filly."
2168: Winner of the 1981 Hanshin 3yo S. (old name). With heavy favorite Saruno King scratched, she won by 2.5 lengths as 5th choice. Injured the next year, she came back in the CBC Sho late at 3, 14th, and retired.
2169: The 1982 Oaks winner. Debuting late at 3, no fancy, she won 2 in spring and squeezed into the Oaks, then beat favorite and Oka Sho winner Riesengross by half a length in a straight duel. A tendon injury cost a year, and she retired after her comeback. Her foals include open horses Galleon and Steppenwolf.
2170: Debuting at 4 (old age system), she won her way up, never out of the top five. In her first open race she won the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu, then was 2nd to Victoria Crown in the QEII Cup, and won the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu and Kimpai (West). That autumn she won the Asahi Challenge C., unplaced in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), Japan Cup and Arima Kinen. Her foals incl. Miss Casablanca, 6th to Mejiro Dober in the Shuka Sho.
2171: Founder of the famed "Glorious Family." Modest on the track, she produced Itto, from whom came Hagino Top Lady and Dai Ichi Ruby. She won allowances early but was 18th in the Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu and 12th in the Oka Sho, then won 8 in all by the end of 5. When her half-sister, Oaks winner Yamapit, died after her first foal, she was retired to breed in her place. Her first foal was Itto, winner of the Takamatsunomiya Hai and Swan S.; others incl. Yasuda Kinen winner Nippo King and Shinzan Kinen winner Silk Tenzan O.
2172: Half-brother of Derby winner Dyna Gulliver. Placed in local stakes, he moved to the JRA in spring at 6 (old age system) and won the Milers C. at once. He won the Takamatsunomiya Hai and Hakodate Kinen, was 2nd in the Kyoto Daishoten, and 6th in the 2nd Japan Cup, 2nd-best Japanese behind fellow ex-local Hikari Duel. At 7 he was 2nd to Hagino Kamui O in the Takarazuka Kinen.
2173: A late-blooming mare who won the Yasuda Kinen at 6 (old age system). Often falling short at 4-5, she caught favorite Brocade in the last 100m of the Yasuda Kinen, then won the Tanabata Sho and Himba Tokyo Times Hai. She retired after an 11th in the 2nd Japan Cup.
2174: Winner of the 1982 Asahi Hai 3yo S. After a debut win as favorite, he won it as 7th choice - one of Maruzensky's speedy sons. Little in the next year's classics, he couldn't trouble Mr. C.B.'s Triple Crown. Turning to sprints at 4, he was 15th in the Yasuda Kinen and retired.
2175: Top two in every start, he won the Hanshin 3yo S. in his 5th race, beating later stars Nihon Pillow Winner, Shadai Sophia and Mejiro Monsuny - next year's classic favorite. But he was 17th in the Satsuki Sho and 5th in the Kikuka Sho, retiring as fellow Tosho Boy son Mr. C.B. won the Triple Crown.
2176: Winner of the 1983 Sprinters S. A sprinter from his debut, he set a record over Kyoto 1200m. After 4 wins at 1200m, he won the Sprinters S. as 3rd choice. Moving to local racing after 6, he went to stud in Kyushu, whose foals often starred in the Himawari Sho for Kyushu-breds.
2177: Eastern 2yo champion of Symboli Rudolf's crop. Despite sore shins, he won the Keisei Hai 3yo S. (old name) and Asahi Hai 3yo S. A classic fancy with Symboli Rudolf and Bizen Nishiki, he was injured and never raced again, never meeting them.
2178: Debuting at Oi, he won steadily there until spring at 6 (old age system), then won Kanazawa's Hakusan Daishoten and moved to the JRA at 7, winning the Milers C. 15th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he was 2nd in the Sapporo Nikkei Sho and won the Sapporo Kinen (then on dirt). He retired after a 5th in the AJCC at 9.
2179: Unbeaten in 5 up to the Keisei Hai 3yo S. (old age system), 6th to Miho Ranzan in the Asahi Hai 3yo S., he won the Tokyo 4yo S. (now Kyodo News Hai) and Yayoi Sho, classic favorite. A fracture kept him out of all 3 classics. Back late at 4, 6th in the Arima Kinen, he won the Meguro Kinen at 5 and was 2nd to Fujino Perseus in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). He retired after the Tenno Sho (Autumn) at 7.
2180: A mare who won the 1971 Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen, Horse of the Year. Small and plain as a foal - "like a mouse" - she sold for half the average price and struggled to find a stable. But she kept winning, took the Kyoto 4yo Tokubetsu at 4 (old age system) and was Oka Sho favorite. 2nd in the Oka Sho and 3rd in the Oaks, she kept placing, then a bad split hoof meant a long break at 5. Back at 6 she peaked: the Milers C. and Hankyu Hai in spring, and the Himba Tokyo Times Hai (now Fuchu Himba S.) under top weight - "queen of the mile." Doubted at the trip, she beat Akane Tenryu and Dai Symbol Guard in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). In the Arima Kinen, with only 6 runners due to equine flu, she closed from the back - the first mare to win in 11 years. She retired as Horse of the Year; her son Tenmei won the Tenno Sho, the first mother-son Tenno Sho double.
2181: Winner of the 2008 Radio Nikkei Sho. After a 5-million win at 2 he struggled in open class at 3 and dropped to the 10-million class, then stepped up to win the Radio Nikkei Sho as a longshot, moving early and holding off favorite Diversity. Little noticed after, his best in local graded races was 5th in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai.
2182: The 1977 Satsuki Sho winner, best son of French import Faberge. Debuting in July at 3 (old age system), he needed 8 starts to win. Stumbling in allowances, he won the Mainichi Hai, the last route to the Satsuki Sho, as 10th choice. 8th choice in the Satsuki Sho, with favorites Hishi Speed and Kane Minobu stalling, he shot up the inside to win - a stunner. Derby favorite next, he charged from the back but just missed Satsuki runner-up Lucky Ruler, 2nd. A tendon injury and 3 years of treatment ended his career. He sired little, failed as a riding horse, and died young after hard years in horse shows.
2183: The 1977 Oaks winner. Debuting at 4 (old age system), she won her debut and the Tsukushi Sho, then was 3rd to Inter Gloria in the Oka Sho as 8th choice. After a runaway win, she was Oaks favorite, helped by Inter Gloria's 9th in the trial, and led early to win easily. In autumn, 2nd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai and 5th in the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu, she closed well but just missed Inter Gloria in the QEII Cup, who also took champion 4yo filly. At 5 she won the Kimpai (West), then was 5th against Tenno Sho winners Hokuto Boy and Erimo George in the Kyoto Kinen (Spring), and retired injured. Only 1 foal won, a maiden.
2184: The 1978 Oka Sho winner. Winning 2 at 4 (old age system), 3rd in the 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, she shared Oka Sho favoritism with Dark Road and Sanem Joo, and held off Sanem Joo's charge by a nose. 6th as 3rd choice in the Oaks and 7th as 2nd choice in the QEII Cup, she retired winless in spring at 5. 12 foals, none notable.
2185: Noticed early in 2003, she won the Hakodate 2yo S. 2nd choice in the Hanshin JF, she was 12th in a chaotic race (trio paid 370,000 yen). 3rd in the Fillies' Revue at 3, she was 13th in the Oka Sho and never won again, retiring at 5 in 2006. Of 3 foals, O Soleil won 3.
2186: Debuting at Oi, he raced against Haiseiko, then led Southern Kanto after Haiseiko left. Via Nagoya, he joined the JRA at 7 (old age system): 2nd to Silver Land in the Milers C., then at 8 won the Sankei Osaka Hai and Milers C. 3rd choice behind Ten Point and Green Grass in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he was last (14th) and retired. No notable foals.
2187: 5th in the Satsuki Sho, 11th in the Derby and 5th in the Kikuka Sho at 4 (old age system), he won the Kumohata Kinen (a December Nakayama 1800m handicap until 1980), then the Kimpai (East) and Nakayama Kinen - strong at middle trips. 2nd in the Nikkei Sho, he was 12th in the Tenno Sho (Spring). His best foals: Sprinters S. runner-up I'll Be There and Kokura Daishoten runner-up Banri Ryuho.
2188: She won the 2008 Tulip Sho from the front, holding off favorites incl. later Oaks winner Tall Poppy. 9th in the Oka Sho and 17th in the Oaks, she never placed again as a sprinter. A broodmare from 2010.
2189: Winning early, he was 24th in the Derby at 4 (old age system). Winless for a while, he rose from autumn at 5, led all the way in the Nihon Keizai Sho at 6 as 10th choice, then won the Mainichi Okan as 7th choice. Last in the Arima Kinen, he won the AJCC and Nihon Keizai Sho at 7 - no fluke.
2190: Winner of the 2004 Falcon S. Often fancied but beaten, she won a maiden in her 7th start, then a 5-million race, and the Falcon S. as 10th of 16 in her 3rd open race. Far back in sprint graded races and the Takamatsunomiya Kinen after, she retired to breed in 2006.
2191: Winner of the 2000 Queen C. After a debut win at 3, she stepped up as 10th choice and closed sharply to win by 1.5 lengths. 15th in the Oka Sho, 9th in the Oaks, 14th in the Shuka Sho, she later won only a 16-million race, but at 6 ran 13 times, 3rd in Kawasaki's Sparking Lady C. - tough.
2192: A 2004 classic hope. He beat Heart's Cry and Black Tide in the Kisaragi Sho, then was 8th in the Satsuki Sho, and fractured a leg in the Derby and was put down. Having beaten later Arima Kinen winner Heart's Cry, many rate his talent highly.
2193: A late bloomer at 6: winning a maiden at 3, then a race each year, he stepped up to win the Ibis Summer Dash at 6, blazing to the front. A pure sprinter (all races at 1200m or less) who loved Niigata: 4 of his 5 wins.
2194: Best foal of French great Sea-Bird, she won 8 G1s incl. the French fillies' Triple Crown and the Arc - the first mare to earn $1 million. At 3 she beat rival Dahlia to the Triple Crown, then was 2nd in the Arc and Champion S., top-rated French 3yo. At 4 she won the Prix Ganay and Prix d'Ispahan among 4 straight, then the Arc as favorite, French Horse of the Year. At 5 she won the Ganay again for an 8th G1 and retired. She beat Dahlia, 2-time King George winner, in all 8 meetings - but as a broodmare had only 1 graded winner to Dahlia's 4 G1 winners.
2195: Winner of the 1970 Tenno Sho (Autumn); with son Mejiro Titan and grandson Mejiro McQueen, 3 generations of Tenno Sho winners. Emerging at 5 (old age system), he won the Yasuda Kinen and Hakodate Kinen, then after a 2nd in the Meguro Kinen (Autumn) won the Tenno Sho (Autumn), beating doubts about a Partholon son's stamina. At 6 he won the Argentina JCC and Hollywood Turf Club Sho (now Kyoto Daishoten), 2nd in the Meguro Kinen (Spring) and Takarazuka Kinen. At 7 he won the AJCC and was 2nd to Ishino Hikaru in the Arima Kinen. Perhaps due to flu antibiotics, his fertility was very low - only 19 foals, yet they incl. Tenno Sho winner Mejiro Titan and Kyoto Daishoten winner Mejiro Cara.
2196: Winner of the 2000 Radio Tampa Sho. Debuting at 3, he led all the way, then won in May and June and went straight to the Radio Tampa Sho, run at Tokyo 1800m that year - 2 for 2 there. He beat the fancies to win. Little after; he won once over jumps at 6.
2197: A 2006 2yo star: debut by 5 lengths, an open race as favorite, then the Daily Hai 2yo S. as heavy favorite, unbeaten in 3. In the Asahi Hai FS he lacked his usual kick, 3rd. Troubled by leg injuries, he raced 22 times until 7.
2198: She won the 1975 Swan S. and Takamatsunomiya Hai at 5 (old age system). As a broodmare she produced 2-classic filly Hagino Top Lady and Takarazuka Kinen winner Hagino Kamui O. Hagino Top Lady produced 2-G1 mare Dai Ichi Ruby - the "Glorious Family," Itto to Hagino Top Lady to Dai Ichi Ruby.
2199: A Southern Kanto mare with many wins incl. the 1982 Teio Sho - its only female winner until Hokuto Vega in 1996. 12 wins from 24, retiring at 4; her foals incl. local star Tsuki no Maruzen.
2200: A Southern Kanto star who won the 1984 Teio Sho and 1985 Tokyo Daishoten. Tough: Teio Sho 4 years running from 4, 70 starts. In his only JRA race, the Local Invitational, he was 4th.
2201: Winner of the 1982 and 1984 Kawasaki Kinen in Southern Kanto. In 1983 he was the first local horse in the Japan Cup (10th). 2 years later local Rocky Tiger was 2nd, proving local strength.
2202: A Southern Kanto star who won the 1982 Tokyo Kinen and Tokyo Daishoten and 1983 Teio Sho: 11 wins from 26, retiring at 7. No notable foals.
2203: Winner of the 1981 Teio Sho and Tokyo Daishoten, a long-striding stayer; he beat Toukei Hope in the Teio Sho in record time. He moved to the JRA with crop-mate Hikari Duel but disliked turf; while Hikari Duel became Horse of the Year, he retired winless there.
2204: A dirt force who won the 2013 Procyon S. Struggling on turf until 3, he was transformed on dirt at 4, rising quickly: 3rd in the Musashino S., 2nd in the Procyon S. At 6 he won the Procyon S. in record time. He ran in Morioka's Mile CS Nambu Hai 4 years running.
2205: At 5 in 2013 he stepped up to win the Kokura Kinen on a light weight, leading at the 4th turn in record time, then was 2nd in the All Comers. But as favorite he was 14th in both the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai and Kinko Sho. In 2014, racing mainly locally, he led all the way in the Tanabata Sho.
2206: Winner of the 2013 Elm S. Unbeaten in 3 on dirt, he flopped in the Japan Dirt Derby and Leopard S. at 3 and restarted in allowances at 4. Winning 2 to return to open class, he won the Elm S. as 3rd choice in record time. 4th in the Hakusan Daishoten (Kanazawa), he was scratched before the Galaxy S.
2207: A long-lasting mare: no G1, but 2 Hanshin Himba S. and, at 7, the Kyoto Daishoten. Debuting late, in April at 3, she won her first 2; after a 10-million win she was 2nd to Meisho Mambo in the Shuka Sho. In 2014 she won the Osakajo S. (OP) and Hanshin Himba S., closing powerfully after a slow start. At 5 she won only the Yonago S. (OP); at 6 she won the Hanshin Himba S. again and was 4th in the Victoria Mile, her best. At 7 she beat males incl. favored Cheval Grand in the Kyoto Daishoten, then was 5th in the Hong Kong Cup. At 8 she fell away.
2208: A Neo Universe stayer who won the 2013 Stayers S. 3rd in it at 4, 2nd to Gold Ship in the Hanshin Daishoten at 5, he then lost several before winning the Stayers S. easily as favorite. In 2014 he raced boldly to win the Kyoto Kinen over Gentildonna, Tosen Ra and Lachesis. 5th choice in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he was far back; after more defeats, he won the Stayers S. again under Norihiro Yokoyama - an Arima Kinen dark horse - but retired injured to stud.
2209: Winner of the 2014 QEII Cup. At 3 she was 2nd to Meisho Mambo in it, her first G1. At 4, 2nd in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai and All Comers, she beat Oaks winner Nuovo Record and defending champion Meisho Mambo to win the QEII Cup, then was 6th as 11th choice in the Arima Kinen. At 5 she swept past Kizuna in the Osaka Hai. 2nd choice in a 3rd QEII Cup, she was 11th, and retired to breed.
2210: Winner of the 2013 Keeneland C. Unplaced in G1s like the Hanshin JF and Oka Sho, she switched to sprints at 4. At 5 she was 3rd in the Hakodate Sprint S. and 2nd in the Ibis Summer Dash, then led all the way to win the Keeneland C. over favorite Straight Girl. 16th to Lord Kanaloa in the Sprinters S.
2211: Winner of the 2013 Keisei Hai Autumn H. Highly rated but slow to win, he came good at 4, winning 4 straight from allowances to the Keisei Hai AH. A fracture then sidelined him for 2013, and he never won again.
2212: Winner of the 2013 St. Lite Kinen. Fresh from a 5-million win, he was 3rd choice and split the field to win by a nose. Fancied in the Kikuka Sho, he was 15th on heavy ground. He won the 2014 Niigata Daishoten.
2213: A romantic pedigree: sire and broodmare sire won the Derby, grand-dam was Oaks winner Umeno Fiber. Long stuck in allowances, he won 3 straight at 5 to reach open class and won the All Comers. 8th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 10th in the Arima Kinen, he won the 2014 AJCC over the same course, but after finishing last in the Takarazuka Kinen died of cancer.
2214: Winner of the 2015 Fukushima Himba S. 2nd in the Queen C. at 3, she ran in the Oaks, then was 3rd in the Fuchu Himba S. and Aichi Hai. In the Fukushima Himba S. at 5, as the fancies collapsed, she alone of the top 3 choices made the top five, and won. She retired at the end of 5.
2215: With only 3 wins by the end of 4, he blossomed in 2015, winning the Takarazuka Kinen and Tenno Sho (Autumn) to top the older ranks. 4th choice in the Asahi Hai FS after 2 wins, he then slumped: 15th in the Satsuki Sho and 7th in the Derby, both as 17th choice. He came good winning the Metropolitan S. at 4, then placed in graded races. At 5 he won the Nakayama Kimpai and Kyoto Kinen; 8th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), doubtful at the trip, he won the Naruo Kinen and Takarazuka Kinen. In autumn he won the Kyoto Daishoten, then the Tenno Sho (Autumn) as favorite, alone holding on from the front as the pace-setters collapsed. 3rd in the Japan Cup and 5th in the Arima Kinen, he was champion older colt. At 6 he was 4th in Hong Kong's QEII Cup, 4th in the Takarazuka Kinen, 3rd in the Kyoto Daishoten and 9th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn).
2216: Winner of the 2015 Hakodate Kinen. In graded races early, 2nd in the St. Lite Kinen at 3, he then stayed in allowances, returning to open class at 5. 6th as 2nd choice in the Meguro Kinen, he won the Hakodate Kinen from midfield, holding off Hagino Hybrid by a head. Unplaced in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), Japan Cup and Arima Kinen.
2217: Winner of the 2013 Meguro Kinen. In open class late at 4, he was 2nd in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai and Nikkei Shinshun Hai, 3rd in the Nikkei Sho. Outclassed in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he split the field to win the Meguro Kinen in a record 2:29.6. Winless after, he tried dirt in the 2014 Kawasaki Kinen, 2nd by half a length to Hokko Tarumae.
