Racing on turf and sometimes dirt (Teio Sho, Procyon S.), he retired in May at 9 after 39 races.
2218: A 2013 classic runner who won the Aoba Sho and ran in the Derby, 5th choice behind Kizuna, Logotype, Epiphaneia and Kodino. 13th, but only about 4 lengths behind Kizuna. Far back in the St. Lite Kinen and Kikuka Sho, often injured, he won the Tancho S. (OP) in autumn at 5, and retired to stud at 7.
2219: Winner of the 2014 Kyoto Himba S. Slow to win at 3, she improved after a 3rd in the Rose S., won a 10-million race as favorite, then the Kyoto Himba S. at 4 and 2nd in the Hanshin Himba S. 16th in the Victoria Mile, she won the CBC Sho at 5, then was 2nd in the Centaur S. and 5th in the Sprinters S.
2220: A long-lasting middle-to-long distance horse with 4 graded wins. 3rd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai and 2nd in the Kikuka Sho, he won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai and Kokura Kinen at 4, then the Chunichi Shimbun Hai and Naruo Kinen at 6. Unplaced in G1s like the Tenno Sho (Spring) and Arima Kinen.
2221: He blossomed at 4 in 2014: a 16-million win, the Kokura Daishoten by 2 lengths as favorite, the Kyoto Daishoten in a tight finish, and the Kinko Sho in record time. At 5, 4th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he was 7th choice in the Japan Cup but, with Ryan Moore saving ground, lost by a neck to Shonan Pandora. At 6 he was 3rd in the Dubai Sheema Classic, behind Duramente's 2nd.
2222: A Niigata specialist: all 3 open wins were Niigata graded races. A handsome blueblood bought for 94.5 million yen as a foal, he reached open class at 3, but leg trouble cost a year. Back at 5 he placed often, won the Niigata Daishoten, then the Niigata Kinen at 7 and Niigata Daishoten at 8.
2223: A 2013 sprint star. In open class late at 3, he was 2nd in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and Lord Derby CT at 4, then won the Keio Hai SC as favorite. Beaten badly in the Yasuda Kinen, he was 2nd in the Swan S. and 2nd to Tosen Ra by a length in the Mile CS. Favorite in the Hanshin C., he was 7th, then slumped, but was 3rd to Real Impact in the 2014 Hanshin C. and won the 2015 Hankyu Hai, his first win in 2 years. No wins since.
2224: US-bred, a 2014-2015 dirt star, all-American dirt blood: by Majestic Warrior out of a Mr. Greeley mare. 2nd in the Hyogo Championship (Sonoda), he won the Unicorn S., top 3yo dirt horse, then was 5th in the Japan Dirt Derby and 3rd in the Musashino S. In 2014 he won the Subaru S. (OP), and was 3rd choice in the February S. but 13th. He won the Oasis S. (OP) as heavy favorite, was 2nd in the Akhal-Teke S. (OP), and won the Procyon S. At 1.2 in the Nambu Hai, he raced boldly and won by 4 lengths, his first G1. The next year he was 3rd in the February S., 2nd in the Kashiwa Kinen, and won the Nambu Hai again. At 6, winless, he was 3rd in the Kashiwa Kinen, 2nd in the Nambu Hai and 2nd in the JBC Sprint.
2225: Winner of the 2013 Radio Nikkei Sho. Improving late in spring, he stepped up to win it as a longshot (trifecta 910,000 yen). 5th in the St. Lite Kinen, he ran in the Kikuka Sho, won the 2 previous years by Stay Gold sons Orfevre and Gold Ship; this Stay Gold son was 5th.
2226: A 6-time dirt graded winner. He won the Leopard S. at 3 easily as favorite, fresh into open class. At 4 he won the BSN Sho and Radio Nippon Sho (both OP), then the Miyako S., sweeping from the back. At 5 he was 3rd in the Tokai S., 2nd in the February S. and won the Heian S., but a fracture before the Teio Sho cost a long break. At 6, 11th in the Tokai S., another fracture before the February S. followed. At 7 he won the March S., was 2nd to Copano Ricky in the Kashiwa Kinen, then won the Hakusan Daishoten and Musashino S. for a 6th graded win. At 8, winless, he was 3rd in the February S. and Kashiwa Kinen.
2227: A rare Heart's Cry sprinter who won the 2013 Kitakyushu Kinen, closing strongly as a longshot. Leg trouble followed; he retired after the 2014 Kitakyushu Kinen (10th), a year later.
2228: Winner of the 1991 Nambu Hai. Debuting in the JRA, after 2 maidens he moved to Niigata (local). At 5 he beat Iwate star Great Hope in the Nambu Hai: 27 wins from 57.
2229: A Southern Kanto mare who won the 1990 Diolite Kinen and Kashiwa Kinen, best foal of Oguri Cap's sire Dancing Cap. At 3 she won the Tokyo Princess Sho, a Southern Kanto fillies' classic. She won the new Kashiwa Kinen at 4 and was 3rd at 5.
2230: A Southern Kanto star who won the 1994 Kawasaki Kinen. JRA-based but stuck in the 15-million class, he moved to local racing at 5, won his first 2 and was 2nd as favorite in the Kashiwa Kinen. At 6 he won the Kawasaki Kinen as 9th choice, then the Tokyo Hai twice and the Grand Champion 2000.
2231: A Southern Kanto star who won the 1992 Kawasaki Kinen. Winning 6 of 11 from 3, he beat heavy favorite Daiko Garudan in the Kawasaki Kinen at 4. Fading after, he slumped in the JRA at 5, then moved to Kochi, racing until 9. He ran in the Kawasaki Kinen 4 years running.
2232: Winner of the 1993 Tokyo Daishoten in Southern Kanto. Hot-tempered, he barely won until 3, improving from 4. Invited to the JRA's All Comers in autumn at 5, he was beaten badly, then ran as if transformed: he beat top older horses in the Grand Champion 2000 and Tokyo Kinen, then won the Tokyo Daishoten easily.
2233: A Hokkaido local who won the 1991 Derby Grand Prix, a local 3yo championship (6th running), by a nose after a straight duel with favorite Keiwan Heart. Winless after, retired at 6.
2234: A Hokkaido local with 96 starts. Debuting at Obihiro, he moved to Southern Kanto at 4 and won the 1995 Kashiwa Kinen, then returned to Hokkaido, racing until 9: 25 wins from 96.
2235: A Southern Kanto star who won the 1995 Haneda Hai and 1996 Kashiwa Kinen. Unbeaten in 5 from debut, one of a Big Three with George Taisei and Concert Boy, he won the Haneda Hai, first leg of the local Triple Crown. Steady, he won the Kashiwa Kinen at 4. In his only JRA race he was 12th to Hokuto Vega in the February S.
2236: A Nagoya horse who also won the JRA's Tokai S. Winning 8 of 9 until early 4, he was 3rd in his first G1, the Kawasaki Kinen, 2nd in the All-Japan Thoroughbred C. and Nagoya Daishoten. At 8 he raced handy to win the JRA's Tokai S., proving himself there. Racing until 9 in 2004: 16 wins from 54.
2237: A 2007 2yo hope: a debut win as favorite, a close 2nd as favorite in the Sapporo 2yo S., 13th in the Asahi Hai FS, then 2 weeks later the Radio Nikkei Hai 2yo S. Out of form at 3, he switched to dirt and was 3rd at Kawasaki at 5.
2238: A 1980 Tenno Sho winner. A jinx then said a mare won the Tenno Sho (Autumn) every 9 years; 9 years after Tomei in 1971, she kept it alive. Tricky and erratic, she needed 8 starts to win, yet stepped up for 4th in the QEII Cup in autumn at 4 (old age system). At 5 she lost badly in open races, nearly retiring, then suddenly ran well in allowances. At 6 came her day: in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), with Derby winner Katsurano Haiseiko, Tenno Sho winner Hoyo Boy and mare Silk Ski fancied, she was 8th choice. As the fancies watched each other, she raced far clear and nobody could catch her - an astonishing wire-to-wire win. After a heavy defeat in the Arima Kinen she retired. Her daughter Steel Cast thrilled fans with a runaway lead, like her dam, in the Kikuka Sho Narita Brian won for the Triple Crown.
2239: A 2004-2009 star on turf and dirt. On turf until 4, he won the Crystal C., was 3rd in the Hakodate Sprint S. and 2nd in the Yodo Tankyori S. Switched to dirt at 5 in 2007, he was at once 3rd in Funabashi's Kashiwa Kinen, then won the Funabashi Kinen and Oi's After 5 Star Sho, racing until 7.
2240: The best of Fuji Kiseki's first crop, his only JRA graded winner. Winning a 9-million race only in his 26th start at 4, he won his first graded race, the Chunichi Shimbun Hai, narrowly over fancied Frontal Attack and Grand Pas de Deux. Never better than 5th after, he moved to Iwate at 7 and Arao at 8.
2241: A speedy 2002 2yo flash. She won her debut by 3 lengths, then the Niigata 2yo S. from last in record time. 4th in the Fantasy S. and 10th in the Hanshin JF, she was far back in the Fillies' Revue and Oka Sho, retiring at 4 after 9 starts.
2242: Winner of the 1977 Hanshin 3yo S. (old age system), champion 3yo colt with 6 wins and a 3rd from 7. Derby favorite at 4, he lost the straight duel, 4th to Sakura Shori. He won the Kobe Shimbun Hai but was 7th to Inter Gushiken in the Kikuka Sho. At 5 he won the Milers C. and Asahi Challenge C., 2nd in the Takarazuka Kinen and Takamatsunomiya Hai. 13th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 11th in the Arima Kinen, he won the Tomoe Sho at 6 and retired. Few notable foals.
2243: The 1979 Oka Sho winner. After winning her debut and the Erica Sho, she kept losing, 7th in the Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu (old age system), and was 15th choice in the Oka Sho. On a quagmire, as the fancies floundered, she led all the way - a stunning win. 21st in the Oaks, her only later placing was 2nd in the Tomoe Sho. 16 foals, none notable.
2244: An older sprinter who won the 2009 Silk Road S. Winning 3 classes at 1200m on turf, he tried the Silk Road S. at 5 as 7th choice and swept past the whole field from the back. Racing until 8 via Funabashi, Hokkaido and Iwate: 7 wins from 59.
2245: A 2004 summer-autumn 3yo star. After a runaway 10-million win, he was favorite in his first graded race, the Radio Tampa Sho, and held off Company and others from a handy spot. 2nd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, he was 16th in the Kikuka Sho. Older, he was 3rd in the Mainichi Okan and Asahi Challenge C., and 2nd on dirt at Oi.
2246: Winner of the 1972 Tenno Sho (Spring). 11th in the Satsuki Sho and 6th in the Derby at 4 (old age system), he improved in autumn, winning the St. Lite Kinen and 4th in the Kikuka Sho. At 5, after an open win, he won the Tenno Sho (Spring) as favorite, a Big Eight race. At 6 he won an open race and the Meguro Kinen (Autumn), racing until the Arima Kinen at 7. No notable foals.
2247: A 2000 2yo hope fatally injured in the Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old name). He fought later Derby winner Jungle Pocket closely in his debut and the Sapporo 3yo S., then won the Tokyo Sports Hai 3yo S. In the Asahi Hai 3yo S. he broke down in the straight yet finished 2nd. Jockey Fujita said, "sound, he'd have won by a mile" - a phantom star.
2248: Winner of the 2013 Keihan Hai. Struggling in open races until early 4, he improved by autumn and won the Keihan Hai, his 2nd graded try, as 7th choice by a neck - 3 longshots dueling to the line, trifecta 460,000 yen.
2249: Winner of the 2014 Naruo Kinen and Mainichi Okan. After 4 open wins when older, he was Naruo Kinen favorite at 5 and closed from the back to win a blanket finish. He won the Mainichi Okan in another tight finish as 8th choice. Skipping G1s, he was 3rd in the Kinko Sho, and kept running well without winning.
2250: Winner of the 2015 Negishi S. A dirt mile specialist, almost never out of the top five and always fancied, he was Negishi S. favorite without a graded win, and split the field from midfield to win. Injury ruled out the February S.; back in autumn, he was 14th in the Procyon S.
2251: The 2014 Satsuki Sho winner. Catching the eye in training, he won his debut, then was 2nd in the Niigata 2yo S., 3 lengths clear of 3rd but no match for later Oka Sho winner Harp Star. He won the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S., then, skipping the Asahi Hai FS, the Kyodo News Hai, then the Satsuki Sho as planned, unfazed by Nakayama. In the Derby he lost a duel with One and Only, 2nd - jockey Ebina's long Derby dream unfulfilled. After the St. Lite Kinen he chose the Tenno Sho (Autumn) over the Kikuka Sho, 3rd, best of the 3yos. At 4 he was 3rd in the Mainichi Okan, Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Mile CS; at 5, 5th in the Yasuda Kinen, 2nd in the Fuji S. and Mile CS. At 6 he won the Milers C. and Hanshin C., a force around a mile for years.
2252: A filly who boldly ran in the 2013 Asahi Hai FS. 2nd in the Kokura 2yo S. and winner of the Fantasy S., she skipped the Hanshin JF for the open 2yo championship, with Yutaka Take bidding to win every JRA G1. 3rd choice, a hope for the first filly winner in 33 years, she faded to 10th. At 3 she won the Fillies' Revue, was 10th in the Oka Sho, then turned to sprints, 5th in the Sprinters S. The next year she won the Ibis Summer Dash and Kitakyushu Kinen, Summer Sprint champion, but was 13th as 2nd choice in the Sprinters S. The year after, same route: she won the Ibis Summer Dash again, then was 10th in the Sprinters S.
2253: Winner of the 2013 Keio Hai 2yo S. Winning his debut in a canter a week before, he ran again at once as 5th choice and, in a slow race, burst clear from a handy spot in the last 50m. Bound for the Asahi Hai FS, he was rested with leg trouble, and has struggled since.
2254: A 2014 classic star: Yayoi Sho winner, 2nd in the Satsuki Sho. 2nd on debut, he won 4 straight to the Yayoi Sho, then lost a duel with Isla Bonita in the Satsuki Sho and was 5th to One and Only in the Derby. 2nd in the St. Lite Kinen and 16th in the Kikuka Sho, he was 2nd as 9th choice in the Arima Kinen. At 4 he went to Australia with stablemates like World Ace: 2nd in The BMW, then beaten badly in the Queen Elizabeth S. Back home, injury ended his career.
2255: A 2014 3yo sprinter who won the New Zealand T. Fancied from his debut, he was 2nd to Asia Express in the Asahi Hai FS. At 3 he won the NZT as favorite, then was 6th in a 6-horse blanket finish in the NHK Mile C. Unplaced in the Sekiya Kinen and Keisei Hai AH.
2256: Blooming from autumn at 4, a force among older milers. In open class in spring at 4, he was 2nd in the Epsom C. and Fuji S., then 4th as 3rd choice in the Mile CS. At 5 he won the Keio Hai SC and Swan S., Mile CS favorite, but trouble in the straight left him 5th. 7th in the Hong Kong Mile and 9th in the Keio Hai SC, he was 7th choice for the Yasuda Kinen - and ran his best: as defending champion Logotype tried to hold on, he swept wide and won by a neck, his first G1, in a hot-paced, wide-open race. 2nd in the Mainichi Okan that autumn, he was far back in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), Mile CS and Hong Kong Mile.
2161: A mare who won graded races incl. the Mainichi Okan and Niigata Daishoten. At 4 (old age system) she won the Flower C., was 2nd in the 4yo Himba Tokubetsu and 4th in the Oaks; in autumn she won the Himba Tokyo Times Hai (now Fuchu Himba S.), 4th in the QEII Cup. At 5 she won the Niigata Daishoten and Mainichi Okan, unplaced in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), Japan Cup and Arima Kinen. Retired after the Kabutoyama Kinen at 6; son Tosho Arrow won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai.
2257: A dirt sprint star who became a G1 winner in the JBC Sprint at 6. Debuting at Mombetsu, he won 2 open races there, moved to the JRA and won a 5-million race and the Hyogo Junior GP at once. Without big wins for a while, he won the Polaris S. and Subaru S. (both OP) and was 4th in the Musashino S. Late at 5 he was 2nd in the Procyon S. and Capella S., then won the Hyogo Gold T. At 6 he was 5th as 14th choice in the G1 February S., then won the Hokkaido Sprint C. as favorite. In the JBC Sprint he raced forward and held off favored Copano Ricky by a head for his long-sought G1. Never out of the top five at 5 and 6, he declined sharply at 7; his only top-five finish was a 4th in the Hokkaido Sprint C.
2258: Bought for 262.5 million yen at the Select Sale, he won his first 3 incl. the Kisaragi Sho. A classic fancy, he was 11th as 3rd choice in the Satsuki Sho and 16th as 5th choice in the Derby, then 7th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai and 8th in the Kikuka Sho. In the Challenge C. he charged from the back to win. At 4 he went to Australia, 2nd in the G1 Ranvet S. Back home he won the Cassiopeia S. (OP) but struggled in graded races, and moved to Australia in April at 5, winning 2 G1s there at 6: the Toorak H. and Emirates S.
2259: Winner of the 2013 Asahi Hai FS, a US-bred son of Henny Hughes. After easy dirt wins in his debut and a 5-million race, he was balloted out of Kawasaki's Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun, so ran in the Asahi Hai FS - his first turf race - and won as 4th choice, champion 2yo colt. 2nd in the Spring S., he was 6th in the Satsuki Sho, and returned to dirt. Beaten in the Unicorn S., he won the Leopard S. easily. After a fracture, at 4 he was 2nd in the Nagoya Daishoten and Antares S.
2260: A 2014 fillies' classic fancy. A close 3rd behind Red Rivere and Harp Star in the Hanshin JF at 2, she won the Queen C. as favorite at 3. 3rd choice in the Oka Sho rematch, she was 8th, then 11th in the Oaks.
2261: A filly noted for an otherworldly finish recalling her sire Deep Impact. She won her debut and the Niigata 2yo S. with straight-long charges, the top 2yo filly of 2013. Heavy favorite in the Hanshin JF, she charged from the back but lost by a nose to Red Rivere. In 2014 she won the Tulip Sho at 1.1, the others seeming to stop, then caught Red Rivere by a neck in the Oka Sho for her G1. With Red Rivere going to the Derby, a 2nd classic looked sure in the Oaks; she closed in under 34s, the only one to do so, but failed by a neck to catch Oka Sho 3rd Nuovo Record under Iwata, 2nd. Following stable star Buena Vista, her camp aimed for the Arc. In the Sapporo Kinen she beat Gold Ship, Takarazuka Kinen winner with 5 G1s, by 3/4 length in a match race, albeit with a 5kg weight edge. In the Arc, the first by a Japanese 3yo filly, with a light 54.5kg like previous winner Treve, she joined world top-rated Just a Way and Gold Ship; racing near last, she closed like an arrow but was 6th. 5th as 2nd choice after interference in the Japan Cup, she ended 2014. At 4, aiming at the world, she was 5th as heavy favorite in the Kyoto Kinen and beaten badly in the Dubai Sheema Classic, then retired injured. Bred to King Kamehameha, her dream passes to her foals.
2262: A front-running 2013 2yo filly who won 3 straight: her debut, the Kokura 2yo S. and Daily Hai 2yo S. 2nd choice in the Hanshin JF against favorite Harp Star's fierce kick, she was 7th. At 3 she was 5th as favorite in the Fillies' Revue, 4th in the Oka Sho and 5th in the NHK Mile C., then last in the Mile CS against older horses after a long break.
2263: She won the 2013 Artemis S., a Hanshin JF fancy. Keen early, she learned to wait in midfield and won the Fuyo S. and Artemis S. 4th choice in the Hanshin JF, she won the tight battle for 5th. In 2014 she ran in all 3 fillies' classics, 7th, 6th and 16th, then was 2nd in the Turquoise S. (OP) in December.
2264: Unbeaten in 3 from debut, she won the 2013 Hanshin JF, all close finishes and never favorite - Stay Gold's first G1-winning filly. At 3 she went straight to the Oka Sho, 2nd by a neck to favorite Harp Star. Her camp then chose the Derby over the Oaks, the first filly since Vodka; 4th choice, perhaps hurt by weight loss, she finished far back for the first time. With Harp Star in France, she was expected to lead the autumn fillies, but was out of the top five in the Shuka Sho and QEII Cup. At 4 under Lemaire she was 4th in the Victoria Mile and 2nd in the Queen S., but faded after.
2265: She won her 2013 debut by 7 lengths in record time in a canter, then the Hakodate 2yo S. easily as favorite. A Hanshin JF fancy, she flopped in the Artemis S., then switched to waiting tactics in the Hanshin JF and charged to 4th. Winless in 2014, she was 3rd on the same time in the Hakodate Sprint S. on 50kg, closing fastest. Older, she won the UHB Sho (OP) at 5 and was 3rd in the Ocean S. at 6, then moved to Funabashi and retired after 1 race.
2266: She ran in the Oaks at 3, but a mile suited her best. Racing at 1400-1600m, 2nd in the Kyoto Himba S., she won the Lord Derby CT from midfield up the inside, catching leader Logotype - the only filly in the field. 3rd in the Sekiya Kinen and 2nd in the Fuchu Himba S., she has yet to win a G1.
2267: Out of Biwa Heidi, from a blue-blooded family incl. siblings Buena Vista, Joie de Vivre and Admire Aura. With only a debut win, she got into the 2014 Flora S. by ballot and won as 4th choice, earning an Oaks ticket. 7th in the Oaks after losing 14kg, she was 5th as a longshot in the Shuka Sho, then 14th in the QEII Cup. At 4, 8th in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai and 10th in the Hanshin Himba S., she dropped to the 16-million class.
2268: Winner of the 2015 Kyoto Kimpai. 3rd in the Asahi Hai FS, a classic fancy, he was 3rd in the Satsuki Sho but scratched 2 days before the Derby with injury. Back in autumn, racing around a mile, he won the Cassiopeia S. (OP), then the Kyoto Kimpai at 4. Injured again, he has been out long.
2269: The star of 2014's Southern Kanto 3yos. From Hokkaido racing, at 2 he easily won the Hokkaido 2yo Yushun and Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun. Moving to Oi at 3, he won the Haneda Hai and Tokyo Derby easily, but lost the Triple Crown by a nose in the Japan Dirt Derby. Placing in dirt G1s like the Tokyo Daishoten and Teio Sho, he won the G2 Urawa Kinen in autumn at 4.
2270: A local horse who won the 2014 Keisei Hai. Unbeaten in 2, he tried the JRA's Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. as 4th choice and lost by a neck to Isla Bonita. 7th in the Asahi Hai FS, he won the Keisei Hai easily at 3 and aimed at the classics, but a leg injury that wouldn't heal ended his career.
2271: A French mare who won the 2013 and 2014 Arcs. In 2013 she crushed Japan's Orfevre, making her name in Japan as Europe's best mare. Small and modestly bred, she was little rated young, but won her first 3 incl. the Prix de Diane easily, then the Prix Vermeille, and in the Arc beat favorite Orfevre, 2nd the year before, by 5 lengths - unbeaten. Cartier Horse of the Year. At 4 she often fell short but won the Arc again. At 5 she won the Prix Corrida (G2), Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud and Prix Vermeille, going for a historic 3rd Arc, but lacked her usual burst and was 4th, unable to catch Derby winner Golden Horn. Her first foal Qous (2017) won in summer at 3.
2272: A German horse who won the 2013 King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S., following Danedream for a 2nd straight German-trained win. 4 G1s incl. the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud and Grosser Preis von Baden - a German great. Unbeaten in 4, he was hot favorite for the German Derby but lost by half a length, then was 4th to Danedream in the Grosser Preis von Baden. He won Italy's G1 Gran Premio del Jockey Club. At 4 he won the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud, then the King George by 5 lengths in 2:24.60, over 2 seconds under the record. After winning the Grosser Preis von Baden he aimed for the Arc, but a fever the day before ruled him out. Already bound for stud in Japan, he retired. His foals debuted in 2017; Last Draft won the Keisei Hai, his first graded winner, and in 2022 Breakup won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai.
2273: A speedster who won the NHK Mile C. at 3 and Mile CS at 5. 2nd on debut, he won 3 straight incl. the Shinzan Kinen, then the Arlington C. as favorite and the NHK Mile C. 16th in the Yasuda Kinen and 13th in the Mile CS, he slumped, but revived at 5 with the Hankyu Hai, 2nd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and Sprinters S., then led all the way in the Mile CS for a 2nd G1. At stud he sired temperamental 6-time graded winner Meikei Yell and 5-time graded sprinter Namura Clair; a first G1 winner is eagerly awaited.
2274: Raced only on dirt, he won the 2013 Japan Dirt Derby at Oi. Never out of the top two before, he won it by 7 lengths as favorite - like his sire Gold Allure. 5th in the JBC Classic at Kanazawa and 15th in the Japan Cup Dirt, he ended 2013. Beaten badly early at 4, he was 2nd from the front in the Mercury C. in July, then won the Nippon TV Hai by 7 lengths as heavy favorite. Favorite in the JBC Classic over Teio Sho winner Wonder Acute and February S./Kashiwa Kinen winner Copano Ricky, he couldn't quicken and let Copano Ricky lead all the way, 2nd. He let fans down in the Champions C. and Tokyo Daishoten too. His next G1 came at 6 in Korea: in the new Korea Cup, the country's richest race, he pulled far clear. At 7 he won the Diolite Kinen for a 3rd straight time, was 2nd in the Teio Sho and 2nd in the Korea Cup. At 8 he was 3rd in the Urawa Kinen.
2275: A gelding who won the 2013 Kinko Sho. A late bloomer in open class only in June at 5, he won his first graded race, the Kinko Sho, as 3rd choice, then was 6th choice in the Arima Kinen - like Kinko Sho longshot Ocean Blue, 2nd the year before. 6th behind Orfevre's crushing win, with 4th-7th close, he looked G1-capable. In 2014 he was 14th in the Nakayama Kinen, 4th in the Osaka Hai and Naruo Kinen, and 9th choice in the Takarazuka Kinen. Racing boldly, 3 lengths behind Gold Ship, he held off Win Variation, Gentildonna and others for 2nd. 5th in the Hong Kong Vase after 6 months off, he was 3rd to Gold Ship in the Tenno Sho (Spring) at 7 and 2nd to Kitasan Black at 8 - gritty when he got a good early position.
2276: A mare who won the 2013 Aichi Hai as 12th choice. Stuck in 5-million dirt races until summer at 4, she was transformed on turf, winning 2 straight, then the Aichi Hai on a light 50kg. With 14th and 13th choices 2nd and 3rd, the trifecta paid a record 4.71 million yen. In 2014 she was 3rd against males in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai, won the Nakayama Himba S., and was 4th to Lachesis as 10th choice in the QEII Cup. 2nd in the next Nikkei Shinshun Hai, she ran well with a tireless late run.
2277: Named after a great ancient mathematician. Stuck in allowances until 3, he bloomed at 4 in 2013, winning 3 straight to open class, then the Asahi Challenge C. as favorite, from midfield. 2nd to Just a Way in the 2014 Nakayama Kinen, after a long break he was 7th in the Hong Kong Cup.
2278: The 2014 Derby winner. Almost unknown before his debut, he won the Radio Nikkei Hai at 2 as 7th choice, closing from midfield past blue-bloods like Deep Impact's son Satono Aladdin and brother Mont Charmant. In 2014 he was 2nd by a nose to To the World in the Yayoi Sho, then 4th to Isla Bonita in the Satsuki Sho despite the fastest finish from last. 3rd choice in the Derby, from gate 2 he raced forward for once, saved ground on the rail and won a straight duel with Isla Bonita. Trainer Hashiguchi, 4 times 2nd in the Derby incl. with Dance in the Dark, won it just before retiring. In autumn he won the Kobe Shimbun Hai; favorite in the Kikuka Sho, he was 9th, then flopped in the Japan Cup and Arima Kinen. At 4 he was 3rd in the Dubai Sheema Classic ahead of favorite Harp Star, but unplaced in the Takarazuka Kinen, Tenno Sho (Autumn), Japan Cup and Arima Kinen. Still slumping, his best was 5th in the Dubai Sheema Classic at 5 and AJCC at 6; he retired after the Japan Cup at 6 and went to stud.
2279: A speedster named after the new Tokyo-Osaka express Kodama (forerunner of the Shinkansen Kodama). He won the 1960 Satsuki Sho and Derby; trainer Takeda, who later had Shinzan, famously said, "Kodama cuts like a razor, Shinzan like a hatchet." Unbeaten in 3 at 3 (old age system) incl. the Hanshin 3yo S., at 4 he won an open race and the Spring S., then the Satsuki Sho by 6 lengths over 3yo champion Matsukaze O. His fame soared; the Derby drew record crowds and betting, and he won it easily as hot favorite, unbeaten in 2 classics. In autumn he lost 2 preps, was 5th in the Kikuka Sho and 6th in the Arima Kinen, winless that season, yet Horse of the Year. At 5 he stuck to 2000m or less, won 2 open races and the Takarazuka Kinen, and retired in glory. He sired Oka Sho winner Hide Kotobuki and some graded winners, and died at 20.
2280: The 1965 Derby winner. Fatally injured in the Hanshin Daishoten in autumn at 6 (old age system), he is remembered for staying beside his fallen jockey Yamamoto. At 3 he won his debut by 10 lengths and 5 straight, then the Yayoi Sho at 4, a classic hope. 2nd to rival Daikoter in the Spring S. and 14th in the Satsuki Sho, he made amends in the Derby: 2nd choice behind Satsuki winner Daikoter, he led all the way and held him off. Daikoter turned the tables in the Kikuka Sho, 2nd. With 7 wins from 10, mostly around a mile, he was champion sprinter. At 5 he won the Kimpai (West), was 5th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and rested. Back at 6 he won 4 straight, then fell and broke a leg in the Hanshin Daishoten.
2281: Winner of the 1963 Satsuki Sho and Derby. 6th in the Kikuka Sho but 2nd in the Arima Kinen, Horse of the Year. His farm wanted a late developer, so he trained through 3 (old age system) and debuted at 4, winning 3 easily, a classic fancy. Against stablemate and 3yo champion Great Yoruka, he won the Satsuki Sho, then the Derby by 7 lengths over him in record time. A Triple Crown seemed certain; in the Kikuka Sho he was backed at an astonishing 83.2% of win bets, but swept along by the pace he raced 30 lengths clear, then tired to 6th. Top of the fan vote, he was 2nd to Ryu Forel in the Arima Kinen, sharing Horse of the Year with him. At 5, aiming at the Tenno Sho, he was 2nd (Spring) and 8th (Autumn), 3rd in the Arima Kinen, and retired at 6. A home-bred hope at stud, he sired no stars.
2282: Blooming in autumn at 4 (old age system), he won the 1963 Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen at 5 - the first Kansai horse to win the Arima Kinen, in its 8th year. Below top level in spring at 4 (Satsuki Sho 8th, NHK Hai 7th, Derby 8th), he improved after summer: Kobe Hai (now Kobe Shimbun Hai) 1st, Kyoto Hai (now Kyoto Shimbun Hai) 2nd, and a neck 2nd to Hiro Kimi in the Kikuka Sho as 8th of 23. At 5 he was 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Spring), won the Takarazuka Kinen, and as favorite won a fierce duel with Hikaru Polar in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). He then beat younger dual classic winner Meizui in the Arima Kinen, sharing Horse of the Year with him. At 6, with no races at fair weights, he went to the Washington DC International, but tired from the trip finished last of 8 and retired. Little success at stud.
2283: The 1972 Satsuki Sho winner, in a great crop with Long Ace, Ishino Hikaru and Tai Teem. He beat all 3 in the Satsuki Sho, was a narrow 2nd to Long Ace in the Derby and 4th behind Ishino Hikaru and Tai Teem in the Kikuka Sho. Older he faded: 5th and 13th behind Tai Teem in the Milers C. and Tenno Sho (Spring). Unlike Long Ace and Tai Teem, he sired no notable foals.
2284: Winner of the 1972 Kikuka Sho and Arima Kinen, a classic star with Long Ace, Tai Teem and Land Prince. Winning late at 3 (old age system), he won 4 straight into spring at 4. The "Kansai Big Three" were the focus; he was the Kanto ace. 2nd to Land Prince in the Satsuki Sho and 6th to Long Ace in the Derby, he couldn't break the Kansai hold in spring. In autumn, after an open win, he ran again a week later and swept past to win the Kikuka Sho. Favorite over older stars like Mejiro Asama and Mejiro Musashi in the Arima Kinen, he won from midfield - the first 4yo colt (old age system) to win it. Worn out, he rested over 10 months, then was last of 7 on his return and retired. Few foals, no stars.
2285: Blooming when older, he won the 1966 Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen at 5 (old age system). Half-brother of Tenno Sho (Spring) winner Korehisa. Debuting at 4, he won lesser races but flopped in graded ones (Yayoi Sho 7th, Spring S. 10th), and was 17th in the Derby and 8th in the Kikuka Sho. At 5 he won the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and Argentina JCC, then the Tenno Sho (Autumn). 2nd choice in the Arima Kinen, he held off Kabuto Shiro and Speed Symboli - Horse of the Year. At 6, 2nd in the Argentina JCC, he won the Diamond S. for a 5th graded win, then retired injured. No notable foals.
2286: A sprinter who won the 2001 Falcon S. Winning a maiden and 5-million race, she struggled in open class at 2. Back in May at 3, she was 3rd as 15th choice in the Aoi S., then beat favorites like Carston Light O by half a length in the Falcon S. Perhaps her peak; little after, retiring at 5.
2287: Winner of the 2000 Tulip Sho. With 3 wins in Hokkaido at 2, she moved to JRA races at 3. 12th in the Elfin S., she led all the way on heavy ground to win the Tulip Sho as a longshot. Overlooked in the classics, beaten badly in the Oka Sho and Oaks, she raced to 6: 5 wins from 41.
2288: Winner of the 2014 Kyoto Kimpai. Debuting at 3 and reaching open class mid-4, he won the Kyoto Kimpai in January at 5, closing from the back with favorite Osumi Nine and winning by 1.5 lengths. He ran well in mile graded races after.
2289: Winner of the 2014 Chunichi Shimbun Hai and Niigata Kinen. A late bloomer in open class at 5, he loved flat, tight local tracks (3 of 5 wins at Kokura). In his first graded race, the Chunichi Shimbun Hai, he upset as 10th choice, then was 2nd in the Kokura Kinen and won the Niigata Kinen. In the Tenno Sho (Autumn) Tokyo's hill beat him, 13th.
2290: Switched to dirt at 6, he won the 2014 Negishi S. On turf he was 3rd in the Mile CS in his first open race at 3 and 3rd in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai at 4, then slumped. The switch worked: 2 open wins, then the Negishi S., and 4th in Funabashi's Kashiwa Kinen that spring.
2291: A rare graded winner on the flat and over jumps. Struggling on turf, he soared on dirt, reaching open class late at 3; at 4 he won the Pollux S. (OP) and the March S. 2nd in the Heian S. and winner of the Marine S. (OP) at 5, he switched to jumps in autumn at 6, won his jump debut, then the Kokura Summer Jump as 6th choice. Injured in the Hanshin Jump S., he retired.
2292: A late bloomer who won the 2015 and 2016 Victoria Mile - 3 G1s in all. Peaking late at 4, she won the Silk Road S. at 5 in 2014, then was 3rd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and Victoria Mile, a rising sprinter. 2nd as 2nd choice in the Sprinters S., she was 3rd in the Hong Kong Sprint. At 6, 13th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, she won the Victoria Mile, then the Sprinters S. as favorite. At 7 she beat Mikki Queen, Shonan Pandora and others in the Victoria Mile for a 3rd G1, and retired.
2293: A sprinter at 1200-1800m who won the Ocean S. and Chukyo Kinen. Improving from summer at 3, he won 4 straight classes; in his first open race at 4, the G3 Ocean S., he won from a handy spot as 3rd choice. After poor runs, he won the Chukyo Kinen at 5 by a neck in a 7-horse blanket finish. Winless after, briefly over jumps, he raced until summer at 7, then moved to Macau.
2294: Winner of the 2014 CBC Sho. A miler at first, she soared once switched to sprints mid-3, winning through the classes and taking the CBC Sho at 4 from midfield with the fastest finish. Prized for speed on flat tracks, she was a hope in the Sprinters S. at Niigata but was 14th.
2295: A late-blooming sprinter who won the Ibis Summer Dash at 7. Placing in graded races in open class at 4, he had a tendon injury and over 2 years off. Back at 6, he never gave up: winning at 7, he won the Ibis Summer Dash as favorite that summer. At 8 he was 3rd as 12th choice in the Silk Road S. with the fastest finish.
2296: Blooming at 5 in 2014, he won the Kitakyushu Kinen and Centaur S. Top five in 3 of 4 graded tries, he won the Kitakyushu Kinen by a nose, then the Centaur S. easily. A Sprinters S. fancy, he was scratched with leg trouble; back late in the year, he was 14th in the Hong Kong Sprint.
2297: 2nd in the 2014 Takamatsunomiya Kinen and winner of the Sprinters S. Mainly a dirt runner, 2nd in the Capella S., he tried turf graded races at 6 in 2014: 2nd in the Ocean S. and Takamatsunomiya Kinen. Still overlooked, 13th choice in the Sprinters S., he won it, proving himself. After an 8th in the Hong Kong Sprint, leg trouble meant a long break. Back after over a year at 8, he never won again but was 3rd in the Ocean S. and 3rd in the Hokkaido Sprint C. 3 years running. Racing until 11, he retired after a 17th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen.
2298: Winner of the 2014 Fukushima Himba S. A late bloomer in open class at 5, she was 2nd as a longshot in the Nakayama Himba S., then won the Fukushima Himba S. as 5th choice, leading throughout and just holding on. 6th in the Victoria Mile, at 6 she led all the way in the Kyoto Himba S. and stunned with 2nd from the front in the Victoria Mile.
2299: Winner of 2 dirt graded races in 2014. In open class late at 3, at 4 he won the Heian S. as a longshot, was 2nd in the Elm S., then won the Sirius S. as favorite. He led boldly but was 8th in the Champions C. At 5 he won the Antares S., a steady middle-distance dirt force. At 6 he ran in Korea's G1 Korea Cup, 2nd to fellow Japanese Chrysolite - a Japanese 1-2.
2300: Winner of the 2014 Meguro Kinen. Long stuck in allowances, he reached open class at 6 and won his first graded race, the Meguro Kinen, closing from the back in a 4-way finish. A true stayer, racing mostly at 2400m+.
2301: He won the Epsom C. at 5. Improving mid-4, he won race after race to open class that autumn, placing in graded races (4th Fukushima Kinen, 3rd Nakayama Kimpai). 2nd choice in the Epsom C., he won from midfield. At 6 he won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai and Sapporo Kinen, 2nd in the Mainichi Okan and Kinko Sho, and at 7 the AJCC for a 4th graded win.
2302: A sharp closer who won the Mermaid S., Fuchu Himba S. and Aichi Hai. Blooming at 4 in 2014, she won the Mermaid S. easily as favorite, then beat Smart Layer, Whale Capture and others in the Fuchu Himba S. 3rd in the QEII Cup, she won the Aichi Hai as favorite.
2303: A middle-to-long trip horse, 2nd in the 2014 Meguro Kinen and winner of the Hakodate Kinen. A maiden until the end of 3, he won race after race at 4 and was 4th in Orfevre's farewell Arima Kinen. At 5 he was 2nd as a longshot in the Meguro Kinen and won the Hakodate Kinen, then 4th in the Sapporo Kinen and Tenno Sho (Autumn).
2304: A mare who bloomed at 5 and won the Champions C., by Tenno Sho (Spring) winner Suzuka Mambo out of 2002 Fairy S. winner White Carnival - turf parents, yet she was a dirt horse. 3rd in her first graded race, the Empress Hai, she won the Breeders' Gold C. by passing hot favorite Wild Flapper, then the JBC Ladies' Classic, her first G1. At 6 she won the TCK Jo-o Hai, Marine C. and Ladies' Prelude, then the Champions C.: 12th choice without form against males, she broke clear in the straight to beat Copano Ricky, Hokko Tarumae and others - dirt champion. She retired after it.
2305: Winner of the 2002 Fairy S. Noticed early, she ran 6 times at 2 incl. the Hanshin JF, then won the Fairy S. at 3 and was 3rd in the Queen C. 11th in the Oka Sho, she never won again and retired at 4. She produced Sambista, the first mare to win the Champions C.
2306: Winner of the 2014 Queen S. 2nd in the Aichi Hai late at 4, at 5 she was 2nd in the Nakayama Himba S. and Fukushima Himba S. - 3 straight 2nds - then 5th to Verxina in the Victoria Mile as 13th choice. She won the Queen S. in a 3-way finish, was 5th in the QEII Cup and 2nd again in the Aichi Hai.
2307: A 2014 classic fancy after winning the Spring S., holding off 2yo champion Asia Express by 1 1/4 lengths. 10th in the Satsuki Sho, he went for the NHK Mile C. and, despite a slow start, was 4th. Around a mile he kept falling short, then won the Auro C. (OP) in November at 4, his first win in 1.5 years, and the Hanshin C. At 5, 3rd in the Keio Hai SC, then little.
2308: A 2014 classic runner. After many graded tries, he won the Mainichi Hai under Daichi Shibata. Skipping the Satsuki Sho for the Derby, at 12th choice he closed from midfield for 3rd to One and Only. Rarely beaten badly, he won the Fukushima Minpo Hai (OP) in spring at 4, then went abroad, 4th in the Singapore Airlines International C.
2309: Winner of the 2014 Falcon S. After a 3rd in the Shinzan Kinen and 2nd in the Arlington C., he won the Falcon S. as favorite, charging from the back by a neck. 4th in the Derby, 3rd in the St. Lite Kinen and 4th in the Kikuka Sho, he made news by going from the 3000m Kikuka Sho to the 1600m Mile CS (10th).
2310: Winner of the 2014 Aoba Sho. Stuck in the 5-million class, he stepped up as 10th choice and charged from the back to win. 6th in the Derby closing the same way, 8th in the St. Lite Kinen, he closed sharply for 5th to Toho Jackal in the Kikuka Sho.
2311: Winner of the 2014 Kyoto Shimbun Hai. Struggling in allowances, he won a 5-million race only the week after the Satsuki Sho, then rushed into the Kyoto Shimbun Hai 2 weeks later for a Derby ticket and swept wide from the back to win. Overlooked in the Derby, he was 13th.
2312: Winner of the 2014 Radio Nikkei Sho. A classic hope but keen, he flopped in the Keisei Hai and Spring S., and lacked stamina in the Aoba Sho. In the Radio Nikkei Sho, the "consolation Derby," he held off favorite Clarity City, also out of the classics, for a graded win.
2313: Classic-class, yet in autumn at 3 he turned to the mile Fuji S. and won. In spring, still in the 5-million class, he was 3rd in the Mainichi Hai and 5th in the Satsuki Sho as 15th choice, but missed the Derby; 4th in the St. Lite Kinen, he passed on the Kikuka Sho. In the Fuji S. he closed strongly from the back to beat older horses. At 4 he was 2nd in Hong Kong's QEII Cup and, as 10th choice, closed fastest for 2nd to Lovely Day in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). At 5, 2nd in the Naruo Kinen, top five in the Takarazuka Kinen and Mainichi Okan, he was 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). At 6 he was 2nd in the Osaka Hai, newly a G1, and 2nd in the All Comers, but 10th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn); at 7, 4th in the Mainichi Okan and 9th of 12 in the Tenno Sho (Autumn).
2314: A 2015 middle-distance star. Debuting late in spring at 3, he won 5 straight to open class and was favorite at 1.9 in his first graded race, the Challenge C. At 4 he won the Epsom C. and Mainichi Okan as favorite; 9th as 2nd choice in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he went to Hong Kong and won the Hong Kong Cup, his first G1. At 5 in Europe he won France's Prix d'Ispahan by a huge margin, cruising clear on heavy ground. Back home, 2nd choice again in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he led from a fine start but faded to 12th.
2315: The 2014 Oaks winner. Harp Star drew all the attention, and she was little noticed in spring at 3. 2nd in the Tulip Sho though well beaten by Harp Star, she was 3rd as 5th choice in the Oka Sho, a length behind. Seen as needing more distance, she was 2nd choice in the Oaks, went clear early and held off Harp Star's kick for a G1. With Harp Star at the Arc, she was the autumn star: she won the Rose S. and, as heavy favorite in the Shuka Sho, closed but just missed, 2nd. Favorite in the QEII Cup, she was a close 2nd against older mares. At 4 she won the Nakayama Kinen and was 5th in the Takarazuka Kinen, among the top older horses; 2nd in the All Comers and QEII Cup, she was 2nd in the Hong Kong Cup, unable to catch leader A Shin Hikari. At 5 she was 6th in Hong Kong's QEII Cup and won America's Red Carpet H. - a globetrotter.
2316: Winner of the 2014 Fairy S. Highly rated, she went straight from her debut to the Fairy S. as favorite and edged clear from midfield in a 7-horse blanket finish. A fracture meant a long break; rated near Harp Star when sound, she has lost badly since returning.
2317: Winner of 3 fillies' graded races. After the Flower C., she skipped the Oka Sho for the Satsuki Sho, middle trips suiting her (11th). 3rd choice in the Oaks, she was a close 3rd to Nuovo Record and Harp Star. At 4 she won the Nakayama Himba S. Beaten badly after, she won the Aichi Hai at 5.
2318: A great mare who won the 2014 Shuka Sho and 2015 Japan Cup. Winning her 2nd start, she was favorite every time in open races but kept falling short, missing both the Oka Sho and Oaks. Restarting in allowances, she won in August and was a close 2nd in the Shion S., earning a Shuka Sho spot. 3rd choice behind heavy favorite Nuovo Record, she slipped through on the inside and held on - a perfect ride by Hamanaka, her jockey from the start. 6th against older mares in the QEII Cup, at 4 she matched the males, 3rd to Lovely Day in the Takarazuka Kinen. She won the All Comers and was 4th to Lovely Day from the back in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), then beat him in the Japan Cup - the best of all, mare or not. At 5 she was 3rd in the Osaka Hai and Victoria Mile, then retired injured while preparing for the Takarazuka Kinen.
2319: Winner of the 2014 Unicorn S., a leading son of dirt sire Gold Allure. Struggling on turf, he soared on dirt, winning his way up; 3rd choice in his first graded race, the Unicorn S., he went early from midfield and pulled away. He won 2 open races incl. the Subaru S., but no more graded races.
2320: Winner of the 2014 Japan Dirt Derby. Struggling as a maiden, he was transformed on dirt at 3, winning a 5-million and open race, then beat favorite Happy Sprint in Oi's Japan Dirt Derby. A dirt G1 regular, he was 2nd to Hokko Tarumae in the Kawasaki Kinen, later 2nd in the Miyako S. and 3rd in the Nagoya GP, but didn't win again, retiring at the end of 8.
2321: A super blueblood by Galileo out of 7-G1 mare Ouija Board. His owner, with farms in Australia, saved the name for a horse who could be Australia's leading sire. Debuting in June at 2, he won his 2nd start and a G3, then rested and went straight to the 2000 Guineas, a close 3rd. Hot favorite in the Derby, he won from midfield with a perfect run, then the Irish Derby at 1.125 - "like a morning canter." He beat older horses in the International S. easily, but was caught by The Grey Gatsby, beaten last time, in the Irish Champion S., 2nd, and retired. At stud he soon sired BC Mile winner Order of Australia.
2322: He ruled European miles in 2014 with 4 G1s incl. the Sussex S. and Prix Jacques le Marois: 7 wins from 8, his only loss a 2nd in the 2000 Guineas. After an easy debut and 2 graded wins, he was caught near the line in the Guineas by Night of Thunder, beaten last time. Taking the mile route, he won the Irish 2000 Guineas easily and ran down Night of Thunder in the St James's Palace S., then beat older horses incl. defending champion Toronado in the Sussex S. and won the Jacques le Marois - 4 straight G1s. An infection forced his retirement. At stud from 2015, his first crop gave 3-G1 winner Persian King, and in Japan Schnell Meister won the NHK Mile C.
2323: Winner of 7 G1s incl. 2 US classics and the Dubai World Cup, US Horse of the Year at 3 in 2014 and at 5 in 2016. California-bred, rare in the US, a standout by sire Lucky Pulpit. Emerging at home, he won the Santa Anita Derby, then the Kentucky Derby from a handy spot - the first California-bred winner in 52 years - and the Preakness, the first for a California-bred. 4th in the Belmont, he won the turf G1 Hollywood Derby, Horse of the Year. At 4 he was 2nd in the Dubai World Cup, then injured; at 5 he won it. Back home he won the Pacific Classic and Awesome Again S. for 7 G1s, then lost the BC Classic by half a length to younger star Arrogate, still Horse of the Year. Retiring at 6, he was later imported to Japan; his first foals debuted in 2023.
2324: Winner of 7 G1s incl. the King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S. and BC Turf, a flagship son of Galileo. At 3, 6th in the French 2000 Guineas, 2nd in the French Derby and 5th in the Irish Derby, he won the Secretariat S. in America and the Hong Kong Vase. At 4 he won the King George, was 2nd to Found in the Arc, then led all the way to beat her in the BC Turf. Going for a 2nd Hong Kong Vase, he led but was caught by Satono Crown, 2nd. At 5 he won the Coronation C. and Prince of Wales's S., then a 3rd Hong Kong Vase and retired. At stud from 2018; first foals in 2021.
2325: In 2015 he won the US Triple Crown, the first since Affirmed 37 years earlier, then the BC Classic - America's first "Grand Slam." 5th on debut, still a maiden he won the G1 Del Mar Futurity easily, then the FrontRunner S., champion 2yo colt. At 3 he won the Rebel S. by 6 1/4 lengths and Arkansas Derby by 8. A narrow Kentucky Derby win was followed by easy wins in the Preakness and Belmont - the 12th Triple Crown winner. Then, at 1.7 in the BC Classic, he won by 6.5 lengths, retired, and was Horse of the Year. He sired G1 winners American Theorem and Harvey's Lil Goil, and in Japan Cafe Pharoah and Danon Pharaoh won G1s.
2326: At 5 in 2014, he won a Tenno Sho (Autumn) packed with stars like Isla Bonita and Gentildonna, as 5th choice. With no graded win before, his best was 3rd in the Kyodo News Hai and Mainichi Hai at 3; 14th in the Derby. After over a year off with leg trouble, he restarted in autumn at 4, stronger with age, and won 3 straight. 3rd in the Mainichi Okan with a sharp late charge, he unleashed it in the Tenno Sho (Autumn): as Isla Bonita and Gentildonna dueled, he flew past on the outside. 3rd to Epiphaneia in the Japan Cup, closing again, he proved it no fluke. At 6, 4th in the Osaka Hai, he was 6th in England's Prince of Wales's S.
2327: The 2014 Kikuka Sho winner. Colitis at 2 delayed his debut until the week after the Derby - then the fastest-ever rise to a Kikuka Sho win, a miracle horse. Winning his 3rd start and a 5-million race, he got into the Kobe Shimbun Hai by ballot; 9th choice and blocked in the straight, he was 3rd on the same time as the winner. Not entered for the classics, his camp paid a late fee. 3rd choice in the Kikuka Sho, he raced handy, led early in the straight and won a fierce duel with Sounds of Earth in record time, far clear of 3rd. At 4, delayed, he was 4th as 7th choice in the Takarazuka Kinen, ran in the Sapporo Kinen and rested. At 5, from the Hanshin Daishoten, he was 5th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and 11th in the Takarazuka Kinen.
2328: In 2015 he won 3 straight to his first graded win, then the Arima Kinen as 8th choice - no fluke, a mainstay of older middle-to-long races since. At 3, after 2 wins, he was 3rd to Toho Jackal in the Kikuka Sho. Resting until summer at 4, he won 3 straight to the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. Overshadowed by stars as 8th choice in the Arima Kinen, he raced handy and won - a Grand Prix winner. In 2016 he won the Nikkei Sho and All Comers, but was 12th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and 4th as 3rd choice in the Japan Cup. Defending the Arima Kinen, he was 3rd after a fierce duel with Satono Diamond and Kitasan Black.
2329: Winner of the Nikkei Shinshun Hai and Nikkei Sho, strong at long trips. 9th in the Satsuki Sho and 7th in the Derby, after a long break he won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai as 6th choice from up front as favorites like Satono Noblesse faltered. He won the Nikkei Sho dominantly and was a Tenno Sho (Spring) fancy, but lacked his kick, 15th; that autumn his best was 7th in the Arima Kinen. At 5, winless, he was 3rd in the Kyoto Kinen and Hanshin Daishoten and 2nd in the Kyoto Daishoten. At 6 he was 4th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), steady to the end. Moving to Australia after retiring, he injured a ligament in training.
2330: Winner of the 2015 Kokura Kinen, on his 10th graded try. 2nd to One and Only in the Radio Nikkei Hai at 2, he then bounced between open and 16-million races. At 4 he stepped up for the Kokura Kinen under 2nd-year jockey Matsuwaka and closed from behind midfield to win by 1 1/4 lengths.
2331: Often placing in fillies' graded races, she finally won the Mermaid S. at 5. At 3 she was 3rd in the Tulip Sho and Rose S., at 4 2nd in the Fukushima Himba S. In the Mermaid S. at 6th choice, she went clear early from the leaders, was passed, but fought back to win.
2332: She ran in the Oka Sho at 3, then turned to dirt, 2nd in the Unicorn S. Improving at 4, she won 2 straight incl. the Kakitsubata Kinen, then was 2nd in the Procyon S. and 3rd in the Tokyo Hai. In the JBC Sprint she led from the start and held on by 3/4 length. The next year she won the Tokyo Sprint, 2nd in the Tokyo Hai and 3rd in the JBC Sprint.
2333: Bought for 75 million yen as a yearling, he won his debut with a sharp kick, then as 3rd choice held off hyped Deep Impact colt Avenir Marche in the Niigata 2yo S. in a course-record 1:33.4. A fracture found after the race dimmed his rise, but in his 2nd race back he was 3rd in the NHK Mile C.
2334: His grand-dam was Crystal C. winner Taiki Diamond and his half-brother graded placer Clarity City. Winning a maiden in his 3rd start, he led to win the new Icho S. by 2 lengths in record time. 3rd choice in the Asahi Hai FS, moved to Hanshin, he was 3rd to Danon Platina. Growing at 3, he was 5th as a longshot in the Satsuki Sho, then won the NHK Mile C. as 3rd choice, breaking clear from up front. He then slumped, 12th in the Mile CS; at 4 his best was 3rd in the Ireland T. (OP), but at 5 he was 2nd in the Nakayama Kimpai and 3rd in the Kokura Daishoten.
2335: His dam Black Emblem won the Shuka Sho as 11th choice, sparking a 10-million-yen trifecta. Winning a Tokyo debut in June at 2, he closed powerfully from the back like a Neo Universe in the Sapporo 2yo S. on tiring ground. Straight into the Asahi Hai FS as 2nd choice, he couldn't quicken, 7th. At 3 he was 2nd in the Yayoi Sho and 4th in the Satsuki Sho, but faded from autumn.
2336: He led all the way in the Hakodate 2yo S., unbeaten in 2. 3rd choice in the Keio Hai 2yo S. after 3.5 months off, he couldn't lead and was 6th. 9th choice in the Asahi Hai FS, he led and held 5th as the pace-setters collapsed. A sprinter at 3, he won the Centaur S. as 10th choice, then was 9th in the Sprinters S. - dangerous if allowed to lead.
2337: A 2014 debut winner who won the Kokura 2yo S. too. 15th choice and last into the straight, she charged wide with by far the fastest finish to pass the field. Straight into the Hanshin JF after a rest, she closed from the back again but only to 9th.
2338: A 2014 debut winner who won the Artemis S. despite a slow start and pulling her way to the lead - she still kept on in the straight. In the Hanshin JF she settled handy and held 3rd. She won the Tulip Sho at 3, but was 10th as 2nd choice in the Oka Sho, and flopped in the Oaks and Shuka Sho. The only surviving line of her great-grand-dam Max Beauty, via Max Jolie and Beauty Song - a first G1 since Max Beauty is hoped for.
2339: The 2015 Oka Sho winner. 2nd in the Artemis S. and Hanshin JF at 2, she was 5th choice in the Oka Sho, led from the start at a slow pace and won by 4 lengths with plenty left. Fancied but far back in the Oaks and Shuka Sho, she turned to sprints, 3rd in the Hakodate Sprint S. and Keeneland C., and 2nd in the JBC Ladies' Classic at Kawasaki on dirt. Back on turf at 5 she won the Kyoto Himba S. at once, then was 2nd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and Sprinters S. At 6 she was still 2nd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and 5th in the Sprinters S., and 5th in the February S. and JBC Sprint on dirt. Fading at 7, she was 5th in the Sprinters S. and 4th in the Hanshin C. In 2020 she went to Ireland to breed.
2340: Unbeaten in 2, she won the Kisaragi Sho so powerfully she was called a monster - the first filly to win it since it moved to turf. Favorite in the Oka Sho and Oaks, her best was 2nd in the Oaks, but her potential was clear. Straight into the QEII Cup in autumn, 4th; voted into the Arima Kinen, she was 10th. At 4 she took on males, winning the Epsom C. and Mainichi Okan, 3rd choice in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). Without a G1, she won the All Comers in autumn at 5, a match for any male.
2341: Winner of the 2014 Fantasy S. After a debut win she was beaten badly in the Hakodate and Kokura 2yo S., and was last choice of 14 in the Fantasy S. Racing handy, she surged in the straight to beat favored Danon Gracias and others. A longshot again in the Hanshin JF, she was 14th.
2342: A super blueblood out of G1 winner To the Victory, with graded-winning siblings. Missing the spring classics, she won 2 in summer and was 3rd in the Rose S. A bit short in G1s like the Shuka Sho and Victoria Mile, she won the Nakayama Himba S. at 5, racing forward and holding on.
2343: Winner of the 2015 AJCC. Blooming at 5, he was 3rd in the All Comers, 2nd in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai and 3rd in the Stayers S. In the AJCC at 6, as 4th choice, he fought for the lead, turned for home in front and held off Gold Ship and others. 10th in the Nikkei Sho and 16th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) after.
2344: A 2014 debut winner who won the Keio Hai 2yo S. 7th in the Kokura 2yo S., he was 11th of 12 in the Keio Hai 2yo S., but led, settled and pulled away in the straight - a stunning win. 14th as 11th choice in the Asahi Hai FS. Winless at 3 in sprint G3s and open races, he won the Kurama S. (OP) at 4 and placed in other open races, on the upswing.
2345: With Mirco Demuro aboard he won the Satsuki Sho and Derby with overwhelming power, ranked with Deep Impact and Orfevre. A late foal of Admire Groove, from a G1 line - grand-dam Air Groove, great-grand-dam Dyna Carl. Slow away and 2nd on debut, he won next by nearly a second, then lost narrowly in the Kyodo News Hai. 3rd choice in the Satsuki Sho, he swung wide from the back at the 4th turn and blew past favorites Satono Crown and Real Steel. Heavy Derby favorite, he burst clear from midfield to win in a race-record 2:23.2. A fracture found while resting sidelined him. Undaunted, he targeted the Dubai Sheema Classic and Arc, won the Nakayama Kinen on return, and was 2nd in Dubai despite losing a shoe at the start. Back home he was a close 2nd to Marialite in the Takarazuka Kinen, but injury struck again and he retired to stud. He sired G1 winners Titleholder, Stars on Earth, Liberty Island, Dura Erede, Lugal and Durezza, but died in 2021 at just 9 with only 5 crops. In 2023 those foals made him leading sire.
2346: Unbeaten in 2, he won the Hopeful S. A classic fancy at 3, he was 7th as heavy favorite in the Yayoi Sho and missed the Satsuki Sho with leg trouble, then a tendon injury meant 2 years off. Back at 5 in the Jinsen S. (OP), he switched to sprints, winning the Azuchijo S. (OP) and CBC Sho - the latter from the back for once.
2347: A 2014 2yo dirt star who won Kawasaki's Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun and Mombetsu's Hokkaido 2yo Yushun. Beaten badly in 2 turf races, he won on dirt by 5 lengths, then the Hokkaido 2yo Yushun by 4, and a duel with favorite Tap That in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun. Unplaced in the UAE Derby and Japan Dirt Derby, he was pulled up in the Leopard S. Back after 10 months in the 16-million class, less fancied, he won the Alexandrite S. in his 6th race to reach open class, and has run well in local open races like the Katsushima Okan.
2348: An Oi mare who won the JBC Ladies' Classic at 5 for a G1. Top five from her debut at 2, always fancied, she was 4th as 6th choice in her first graded race, the Ladies' Prelude at 4. Scratched at the start of the JBC Ladies' Classic with a leg issue, she was 10th in the Queen Sho. Stronger at 5, 2nd in the Marine C. and Sparking Lady C., she tracked in 2nd-3rd in the JBC Ladies' Classic and passed leader Princia Cometa - the first local winner, and her first graded win a G1.
2349: A dominant 2002 2yo: a debut win by 9 lengths, the Canna S. (OP) as favorite, then the Daily Hai 2yo S. by 2.5 lengths as heavy favorite. Leg trouble ruled out the Asahi Hai FS and the classics; back at 5 without his old power, he never won again.
2350: The 1969 Oka Sho winner. Winning her debut easily, 2nd and 3rd on Sapporo dirt, she won again at Kyoto in autumn, then closed sharply from the back for 2nd to Riki Eikan as a longshot in the Hanshin 3yo S. (old age system). At 4 she won the Kobai Sho and Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, 3rd choice in the Oka Sho behind dominant Tomei and Shinzan Kinen winner Fine Happy; she won a straight duel with Tomei by half a length. Leg trouble ruled out the Oaks and cost nearly a year. Back at 5, she was 3rd in the Sankei Osaka Hai but didn't win again. Her 6th foal, Sankyo Shori, raced locally and went to stud.
2351: Gelded early, he fought frailty to win 2 graded races. Rising slowly at 3 and 4, he won the Paradise S. (OP) at 5 as favorite, then leg trouble cost over a year. Back at 6, 3rd in the Keisei Hai AH, he won his first 2000m race, the Fukushima Kinen. At 7, steady in graded races, he won the Kinko Sho in December. An Arima Kinen surprise was hoped for, but leg trouble ruled him out, and he retired the next April without racing.
2352: Rated on dirt from his debut but often falling short, he reached open class only at 5, then improved fast and won the Musashino S. as 7th choice. His only graded win, but 6th in the Champions C. and February S. showed his depth. A tendon injury at 8 ended his career; he was exported to China as a sire.
2353: A 2014 debut winner who won the Daily Hai 2yo S. After winning his 3rd start, he started from the back, pulled up to the leaders, then broke clear early in the straight and held off Ash Gold. At 3 he was 3rd in the Yayoi Sho as 10th of 11. Long-lasting, he switched to jumps in spring at 7, and at 10 won the Kyoto High Jump, a 3rd jump graded win, in his farewell.
2354: A 2014 debut winner who won the Kyoto 2yo S., newly a G3 that year. Two weeks after a 5-million win, fresh and well, he settled handy and burst clear mid-straight to win as 6th of 8. At 3, 9th in the Yayoi Sho, he was 14th in the Satsuki Sho and 15th in the Derby. In the 16-million class from summer at 4, he retired without another win.
2355: Winner of the 2015 Flora S. and Turquoise S. After a 5-million win, she raced forward and held off favorite Dear My Darling in the Flora S. 17th to Mikki Queen in the Oaks, she was 14th in the Rose S. and 10th in the Shuka Sho. Then in the new Turquoise S. she won from the front as 11th choice (quinella 54,690 yen, trifecta 2,954,680 yen). The next year, after a 15th and 7th, she was 12th choice in the QEII Cup but held 2nd from a handy spot - another shock.
2356: Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Yayoi Sho, a top 2015 classic fancy. Slow into stride in the Satsuki Sho, 6th; 3rd in the Derby with the fastest finish, but no title. Skipping the Kikuka Sho, he was 17th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). He won the Kyoto Kinen, then was 12th in Hong Kong's QEII Cup, 6th in the Takarazuka Kinen and 14th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). Then came a stunning Hong Kong Vase: world champion Highland Reel, King George and BC Turf winner, was hot favorite and seemed to have it won from the front, but he charged from the back to win by half a length - his first G1. At 5 he won the Kyoto Kinen again, then beat Kitasan Black, rated the best in training, in the Takarazuka Kinen for a home G1. In the Tenno Sho (Autumn) he was 2nd to Kitasan Black on the same time. At 6, 7th in the Dubai Sheema Classic, 12th in the Takarazuka Kinen and 9th in the Japan Cup, he retired. His first crop included Derby winner Tastiera.
2357: Winner of the 2014 Keihan Hai, her first graded win in autumn at 5. A sprinter throughout from a debut at 3, she reached open class in spring at 5, struggled in graded races, then made the top five in the Kitakyushu Kinen. Blooming, 5th choice in the Keihan Hai, she led and won by 1 1/4 lengths. She won the Silk Road S. the next year, but died of colic while resting that summer.
2358: Switched to dirt at 4 in 2014, she won Funabashi's Queen Sho. Struggling on turf, she soared on dirt, reached open class and was at once 2nd in the G1 JBC Ladies' Classic at Morioka, then won the Queen Sho easily as favorite. She won the Sparking Lady C. at 5 and the Queen Sho again at 6, always in the top five in fillies' graded races - very consistent, if short of a G1.
2359: The 1962 Oaks winner. As a broodmare she produced World Hayabusa, whose line gave Nippo Teio, Talented Girl and Victoria Crown. Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Fukushima 3yo S. (old age system), she won the Keisei Hai at 4, was 4th to Kenho in the Oka Sho and 12th in the 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, then won the Oaks as 8th choice. Winless at 5, she won an open race at 6, her first win in 1 year 8 months, and retired. Of 11 foals, none starred, but World Hayabusa was a hugely successful broodmare: QEII Cup winner Victoria Crown, and descendants incl. Chiyoda Masako, dam of Nippo Teio and Talented Girl, whose line gave Victoria Mile winner Whale Capture.
2360: 2014's 2yo queen. Beaten by Navion's charge on debut, she won a maiden and a 5-million race, then was 5th choice in the Hanshin JF, untested in graded races. Unable to race forward, she seemed short of experience, but driven hard by Ebina she closed as if the others had stopped, champion 2yo filly. A fracture, then another, cost her the whole 3yo season; back at 4, she was 16th in the Victoria Mile and 6th in the Fukushima TV OP. Leg surgery meant another long break; last in the Lord Derby CT the next year, she retired with leg trouble.
2361: By BC Juvenile winner Macho Uno, of the rare Himyar line. A dirt front-runner who reached open class in October at 4. 3rd choice in the Autumn Leaf S. (OP), he was 5th, a second behind. 12th choice in his first graded race, the G3 Capella S., he led as usual and won by 5 lengths - a shock. Awakened, he won 4 JRA-local graded races in 2015; hot favorite in the JBC Sprint, he couldn't catch leader Colin Berry, 2nd. In 2016 he won the Kurofune Sho, Hokkaido Sprint C. and Cluster C., then led all the way in the JBC Sprint for his G1 revenge.
2362: Winner of the 2015 Leopard S. Winning his way up, he went to the Hyogo Championship in spring at 3 and won as favorite by 9 lengths over Liar Fail. 2nd in the Japan Dirt Derby, he won the Leopard S. back in the JRA. Resting for the autumn, he died suddenly of colitis.
2363: A super horse, introduced in Winning Post 8 2016. Bred from the fastest (53.7s, sire) and 2nd-fastest (53.8s, dam) winners over Niigata's 1000m straight. Blazing speed: he can lead like his sire or sit handy like his dam. Favorite course: the 1000m straight, of course. Earn too much prize money young and the weights may make the Ibis Summer Dash hard to enter.
2364: 2nd on debut, he won a maiden and the Begonia Sho, then the Asahi Hai FS, moved to Hanshin from 2014. Racing from the back for once, he unleashed an extraordinary finish to win 3 straight, 2yo champion. It was Ebina's 2nd G1 in 2 weeks after the Hanshin JF, the only Deep Impact runner in the field, and his sire's 2nd grey graded winner after Smart Layer. At 3, 3rd in the Spring S., he was 11th in the Satsuki Sho, then turned to shorter trips and won the Fuji S.; 7th as 8th choice in the Hong Kong Mile. Older, at a mile, he was 3rd in the Keisei Hai AH and Fuji S., then after 10 months off was 5th in the Sekiya Kinen.
2365: A Hokkaido-raced filly who won the 2015 Hokkaido 2yo Yushun, then joined the JRA. At home she won the Floral Cup by 2.5 seconds, a star in the making, then crushed JRA fillies in the Edelweiss Sho. 5th choice behind JRA fancies in the Hokkaido 2yo Yushun, she won it, with local Steel King 2nd - a local 1-2. Moving to the JRA, she won Kawasaki's Kanto Oaks, then was 3rd in the Sparking Lady C., 2nd in the Breeders' Gold C. and Queen Sho. Steady in JRA-local races at 4, she retired without another win.
2366: Switched to dirt at 5 in 2015, he won the Sirius S. It took him over 2 years to pass the 10-million class, often a close 2nd or 3rd. After finally winning it in spring at 5, he switched to dirt, won a 16-million race easily, and as 3rd choice in the Sirius S. moved up at the 4th turn and swept past favorite Danon Liberty. At 6 he won 4 straight: Nagoya Daishoten, Antares S., Nippon TV Hai and JBC Classic. Hot favorite in the Champions C., he seemed to have it won but was caught near the line by Sound True, 2nd. 2nd in the Tokyo Daishoten, at 7 he was 5th in the Dubai World Cup and 3rd in the Teio Sho - close but no title. Favorite to defend the JBC Classic, he couldn't quicken, 4th.
2367: After winning 2 classes late at 3, she won the Empress Hai, moving to the front at the 4th turn and pulling away from favorite Wild Flapper. She won the Breeders' Gold C. next. 4th in the JBC Ladies' Classic, she won the Nagoya GP from the front with the fastest finish. The next year she won all 3 again - 6 graded wins - but no G1: her best was 3rd in the Kawasaki Kinen.
2368: The 2015 Derby runner-up. A late bloomer needing 8 starts to win a 5-million race, he won the Kyoto Shimbun Hai from a handy spot, earning a Derby ticket, then closed from Duramente's position for 2nd. With Duramente out in autumn, he was a lead player, but was 7th as favorite in the St. Lite Kinen and 5th as 3rd choice in the Kikuka Sho. Beaten badly in graded races, he switched to sprint-to-middle open races from autumn at 4: 2nd in the Rigel S. and Yonago S. (OP) - always fancied in open races.
2369: Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Niigata 2yo S., noticed early. 8th in the Satsuki Sho and 11th in the Derby, he was 2nd in the NHK Mile C. between them, suited to shorter trips. Turning to miles, he won the Keisei Hai AH against older horses as favorite, but was 9th as favorite in the Fuji S. and 9th in the Mile CS. A long slump followed, with only open-race placings, but late at 5 he made the top five in the Sekiya Kinen and Keisei Hai AH, then 2nd choice in the Swan S. behind Yasuda Kinen winner Mozu Ascot, he won their straight duel for a 3rd graded win.
2370: Winner of the 2015 Falcon S. Erratic - 3 wins, mostly unplaced otherwise - he was 14th of 18 in the Falcon S. Racing forward on the rail, he won a long duel with Active Minoru by a nose - even jockey Matsuda was surprised. Beaten badly in the NHK Mile C. and Hakodate Sprint S. after.
2371: He won Saga's Summer Champion in 2015. After a long time in allowances, he bloomed at 5, winning a 16-million and open race, then dirt graded races: the Summer Champion as favorite by 2.5 lengths from the front, 3rd in the Teletama Hai Oval Sprint, 2nd in the Nambu Hai, and 2nd in the JRA's Musashino S. In 2016 he was 6th in the February S. and won the Musashino S. in course-record time, his first JRA graded win. A Champions C. hope, he fractured a leg in training and was put down.
2372: The first winner of the Saudi Arabia Royal C., renamed from the Icho S. in 2015. After a maiden win as favorite, he broke clear early from midfield and held off favorite Immortal and others. At 3, 2nd in the Falcon S., he was 8th in the NHK Mile C. and 18th in the Derby. Falling short in open and G3 races, he moved to Australia at 4 - and thrived, 3rd in The Everest, the world's richest race.
2373: A mare who won the JBC Ladies' Classic in 2015 and 2016, a dirt specialist like her sire Kurofune. After the Tango S., she won the Kanto Oaks by 2.3 seconds, leading all the way and pulling away with by far the fastest finish. 3rd in the Breeders' Gold C. and Ladies' Prelude, she overpowered defending champion and favorite Sambista to win the JBC Ladies' Classic by 5 lengths. At 4 she won the TCK Jo-o Hai and Sparking Lady C., 2nd in the Ladies' Prelude, then won the JBC Ladies' Classic again as favorite from a handy spot. At 5 she won the Marine C. and Sakitama Hai, then was a career-best 1.8 favorite for a 3rd JBC Ladies' Classic, but faded in the straight, 11th.
2374: Winner of the 2015 Mainichi Hai. 4th in the Sapporo 2yo S. and Kyodo News Hai, he raced forward and held on as 7th choice in the Mainichi Hai, earning classic starts: 7th in the Satsuki Sho, 10th in the Derby. 2nd to Kitasan Black in the St. Lite Kinen, he was 8th in the Kikuka Sho; by pedigree he should thrive at longer trips.
2375: Winner of the 2015 Keisei Hai AH, his first graded win at 7. Stuck in the 16-million class from spring at 5, he reached open class in summer at 6 and was 2nd in the Fukushima Kinen. 13th choice in the Keisei Hai AH, he waited at the back, charged into a blanket finish (first 7 within half a length) and won by a nose.
2376: Winner of the 2015 Niigata Daishoten, his first graded win at 7. He won his debut, then placed often, reaching open class in summer at 4 - never out of the top five in 20 starts. Racing mainly in local graded races, he won the Niigata Daishoten at 7; in graded races, top five 10 times from 15.
2377: Raced only on dirt, mainly in JRA open races until 6, he toured local tracks at 7 in 2015 and won the Teletama Hai Oval Sprint on his 3rd trip, his first graded win. 4th in Oi's G1 JBC Sprint, he won the Hyogo Gold T. as favorite by 3/4 length. At 8, after a dry spell, he was 5th choice in the Teletama Hai Oval Sprint but defended his title.
2378: Winner of the 2015 Tokyo Shimbun Hai and Yasuda Kinen runner-up, a blueblood by Deep Impact out of Flower Park. After a fracture at 3 and tendon injury at 4, he returned in autumn at 5 and won 4 straight incl. the Tokyo Shimbun Hai. 3rd choice in the Yasuda Kinen, he closed powerfully to lose by a neck to Maurice. After that year's Mile CS the tendon injury returned, and he retired.
2379: Winner of the 2015 Nagoya Daishoten. Switched from turf to dirt in autumn at 3, he won his way to open class in spring at 5, then won the Hyogo Gold T. as favorite by 1.5 lengths. At 6 he led to win the Nagoya Daishoten, beating favorite Asia Express in a straight duel - 2 straight graded wins.
2380: Winner of the 2015 Hakusan Daishoten, his first graded win at 6 in his 32nd start. In 6 graded tries he had placed only in the Tokai S. (3rd, 4th). On his first local trip, to Kanazawa, he was 4th choice behind JRA fancies; defending champion A Shin More Over, 3rd choice Solitary King and he broke clear to duel, and he burst through to win. His only graded win, but just before retiring at 8 he was 3rd as 15th choice in the Heian S.
2381: A mare who won the 2015 Queen S., her first graded win at 6 in her 37th start. At 3 she ran all 3 fillies' classics: 5th, 9th, 18th. Restarting in the 10-million class, she reached open class in summer at 5, racing in G3s like the Kitakyushu Kinen and Kyoto Himba S. 7th of 10 in the Queen S., she ran down favorite Red Rivere in the straight to win.
2382: Won the 2015 Saga Kinen and March S. in a row. On turf and dirt without winning, he raced only on dirt from autumn at 3, blooming at 5. After a 16-million win, he won the Saga Kinen as favorite by a nose over Solitary King, then the March S. as 6th choice by a head in a tight finish - 2 straight graded wins.
2383: Winner of the 2015 Hakodate Sprint S. Open class at 2 and 5th in the Asahi Hai FS, he struggled when older, then at 5 won 2 classes strongly and the Hakodate Sprint S. from last with the fastest finish, by 2.5 lengths. 10th in the Sprinters S.
2384: A middle-distance dirt horse who won the 2015 Elm S. Raced only on dirt, he reached open class in autumn at 3 and was at once 2nd in the March S. at 4. Often fancied but beaten, he won the Elm S. at 5, closing from the back, joining the leaders at the 4th turn and coasting clear - stronger than the margin. From 6 he kept finishing out of the top five, 7th as 2nd choice in the Elm S., and retired after a 12th in the October S. (OP) at 7.
2385: Winner of the 2015 Hanshin Himba S., by Brian's Time out of a Caerleon mare - an old-school pedigree. Winning 2 classes late at 4, she raced handy in the Hanshin Himba S. and burst clear for her first graded win. She couldn't give her sire a long-awaited G1 in the Victoria Mile, but was 5th in a chaotic race.
2386: Winner of the 2015 Mermaid S. 2nd in the Rose S. at 3 and a Shuka Sho runner, she slumped and dropped to the 10-million class. Still there at 5, she stepped up as 8th choice in the Mermaid S. and closed brilliantly from the back past fancies incl. later QEII Cup winner Marialite. Unplaced in the Fuchu Himba S. and QEII Cup.
2387: In open class at 5, he won the July S. (OP) and Nippon TV Hai, then was 2nd in the JBC Classic and 3rd in the Champions C. In the Tokyo Daishoten, against 9-G1 Hokko Tarumae, 5-G1 Copano Ricky and others, he swept past the field to win by 1 3/4 lengths - a changing of the dirt guard. At 6 he was always placed in G1s - 2nd in the Kawasaki Kinen, 3rd in the Teio Sho and JBC Classic - then in the Champions C., from last, he swooped wide past favorite Awardee to win as 6th choice, a 2nd G1. At 7, 2nd in the Kawasaki Kinen and 4th in the Teio Sho, he won the JBC Classic as 4th choice for a 3rd G1, then was 11th as 2nd choice in the Champions C.
2388: Winner of the 2015 Hokkaido Sprint C. A pure sprinter who raced only at 1200-1400m. Winning up to the 16-million class on turf, he won the Chiba S. on dirt, was 2nd in the Tokyo Sprint, then led all the way in the Hokkaido Sprint C., holding off favorite Danon Legend. Effective on turf and dirt.
2389: A speedster who won the spring and autumn mile G1s of 2015. With only a 5-million win by the end of 3, he grew fast at 4: winning 2 classes, he won the Lord Derby CT by 3 lengths as favorite, then the Yasuda Kinen as favorite, sitting handy, drawing level in the straight, pulling clear on the bridle, then kicking on. Rested, he went straight to the Mile CS as 4th choice and dominated, outpacing favorites Isla Bonita and Fiero from midfield. In the Hong Kong Mile, 2nd choice among 3 Japanese runners, he ran down defending champion Able Friend - the first Japanese winner in 10 years. 2015 Horse of the Year. In 2016 he won Hong Kong's Champions Mile as favorite, a world-class miler, then the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and the Hong Kong Cup at 1.6 - a champion at middle trips too. Retiring to stud, his first crop gave 3 G1 winners: Pixie Knight, Geraldina and Jack d'Or, then graded winners like Lagerfeld, Knocking Point and Strauss. Shuttling to Australia, he sired Australian Derby winner Hitotsu and Doomben 10,000 winner Mazu.
2390: Winner of 7 G1s at middle to long trips, top three in every race except a beaten Derby and Takarazuka Kinen. Debuting at 3, little noticed, he won 3 straight to the Spring S., then was 3rd to Duramente and Real Steel in the Satsuki Sho as 4th choice. 14th in the Derby, he won the St. Lite Kinen, then the Kikuka Sho as 5th choice with Duramente out, beating Liar Fail and Real Steel. Voted 3rd for the Arima Kinen, he was 3rd, best of the 3yos. With Yutaka Take he won the Tenno Sho (Spring), beating favorite Gold Actor. In the Takarazuka Kinen, billed vs. Duramente, he was a close 3rd. In autumn he won the Kyoto Daishoten and led all the way in the Japan Cup as favorite - best in training. In the Arima Kinen he tracked in 2nd and led, but was caught near the line by Satono Diamond. At 5, at his peak, he won the Osaka Hai, newly a G1, then the Tenno Sho (Spring) in record time, crushing Satono Diamond. 9th in the Takarazuka Kinen, perhaps tired, he won the Tenno Sho (Autumn). 3rd in the Japan Cup behind crop-mate Cheval Grand, he led all the way in the Arima Kinen as fan-vote winner for a then JRA-record-equaling 7 G1s. At stud from 2020, his first crop gave 6-G1 Equinox and his 2nd Satsuki Sho winner Sol Oriens. His 2024 fee, 20 million yen, was the highest in Japan. In 2025 Croix du Nord won the Derby he had lost - still a giant as a sire.
2391: Winner of the 2015 Shinzan Kinen. 7th in the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. with a sharp finish, he bloomed at 3: 2nd choice in the Shinzan Kinen, he moved early from midfield, led and held on narrowly. Unplaced in the NHK Mile C. and Derby, he raced in open races, winning 2 when older, 2nd in the Milers C. and 4th in the Yasuda Kinen. His name means "salted pork cheek."
2392: Winner of 3 mile G3s. Winning his debut as 6th choice and 3rd in the Junior C. (OP), he stepped up for the Arlington C. as 9th choice. Handy at the 4th turn, he seemed to stall, then in the last 100m suddenly accelerated and shot clear. Raw but talented, he was 3rd in the Sekiya Kinen and Keisei Hai AH against older horses. Winless after, he dropped a class, then won 3 straight: a 16-million race, the Sekiya Kinen and Fuji S. A Mile CS fancy, he was 16th. 3rd in the Milers C. at 5, he faded and was retired after the Keisei Hai AH at 7.
2393: A 5-time graded winner at a mile to 2000m. His first was the NZT in spring at 3: 7th choice, he burst clear from midfield and held off favorite Gran Silk. He won the Fukushima Kinen that autumn, the Nakayama Kimpai and, late that year, the Kinko Sho. A G1 contender, he was 4th in the Arima Kinen and 3rd in the Osaka Hai. In 2017, with the Kinko Sho moved to March, he won it again - twice in 3 months, a rare record.
2394: A blueblood with graded-winning siblings like Reve d'Essor and Apres Midi.
