Winning 2 at 3, he won the Aoba Sho as favorite from midfield in a 3-way straight duel. 4th choice in the Derby, he was 9th behind Duramente's runaway. He won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai the next year, but was 10th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), and did little in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai and Hanshin Daishoten after.
2395: A 2015 dirt star who won the Japan Dirt Derby. Noticed on dirt in allowances, he won the Unicorn S. with a powerful finish, then swept past the field from midfield to win the Japan Dirt Derby by 2.5 lengths. Against older horses he won the Musashino S. and was 2nd in the Champions C. At 4 he fell short: 2nd in the February S., 4th in the Kashiwa Kinen, 2nd in the Teio Sho, then unplaced from autumn, and lost favor. At 6 he revived, winning the Negishi S. and February S. for a 2nd G1, then made the top five in the Kashiwa Kinen and Mile CS Nambu Hai. Far back at 7 in the February S. and Godolphin Mile, he moved to Oi - and it worked: closing steadily, he was 2nd to JRA stars in the Tokyo Daishoten. Still racing at 8, with more dirt graded success hoped for.
2396: A middle-distance horse who won the Osaka Hai (G2) and Radio Nikkei Sho. Unbeaten in 2, he was 3rd in the Kyodo News Hai and Mainichi Hai, then won the Principal S. for a Derby spot, but chose the Radio Nikkei Sho for his trip. Hot favorite, he spurted from midfield and pulled away. 5th against older horses in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), at 4 he won the Osaka Hai (G2), was 2nd in the Mainichi Okan and 4th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). The next year the Osaka Hai became a G1; he was 5th.
2397: He won the 2015 Kobe Shimbun Hai, rated top of his crop that autumn. Racing mainly on dirt at first, 2nd in the Hyogo Championship, he switched to turf in summer at 3, won a 16-million race easily under Christophe Lemaire, then led all the way in the Kobe Shimbun Hai. Kikuka Sho favorite, unable to lead, he was 3rd. More fancied than Kikuka winner Kitasan Black in the Arima Kinen, he broke down in the race and was last.
2398: Debuting in May at 3, he won 4 straight from his debut to the 16-million class. 3rd in his first graded race, the Musashino S., he won the Negishi S., then the February S. as 2nd choice, breaking clear mid-straight and holding off favorite Nonkono Yume - on the road to dirt kingship. Then a long drought: 2nd in the Nippon TV Hai and Sakitama Hai, but no win for 2 years until the Coral S. (OP) in March at 6. He then won the Korea Sprint, a G1 abroad, and was 4th in the JBC Sprint and February S. Trying turf at 7 in the Centaur S. and Swan S., unplaced in both, he retired.
2399: Rarely beaten badly from 2, he was 2nd in the Aoba Sho for a Derby spot. Steady in long graded races but never quite winning, he rested after a 4th in the Tenno Sho (Spring). After 9 months off, perhaps short of his trip, he closed strongly to win the AJCC. A spring G1 force was expected, but injuries kept him out.
2400: 2nd in the NZT and NHK Mile C. favorite, talented early, but stuck on 2nds and 3rds, always fancied. At 5, on his 10th graded try, he won the Keisei Hai AH, sweeping from midfield to overwhelm the leaders - sharing the Summer Mile Series title with Win Ganion.
2401: A mile-to-middle graded star who won the Kokura Daishoten and Tanabata Sho at 4. In open class in spring at 3, he was beaten badly in the Kobe Shimbun Hai and Kikuka Sho, then won the Kokura Daishoten. That summer he won the Tanabata Sho - the first 4yo winner in 17 years.
2402: Winner of the 2015 Fairy S. Struggling to win a 5-million race, she led for the first time in the Fairy S. and won easily as 11th choice. 16th choice in the Oka Sho, she led and held 5th, but was 13th in the Oaks and 15th in the Shuka Sho; her only later highlight was 4th in the Queen S.
2403: Winner of the 2015 Queen C. Winning her debut as 6th choice and a 5-million race, she was 2nd choice in the Queen C., swung wide at the 4th turn and beat later 2-classic winner Mikki Queen and favorite Roca. 7th in the Oka Sho and far back in the Oaks and Shuka Sho, she never came close to Mikki Queen again.
2404: A leading 3yo filly without a classic, she grew stronger and won the QEII Cup. Unbeaten in 2, she won the Fillies' Revue as favorite, 3 from 3. 3rd choice in the Oka Sho, she was 4th behind Let's Go Donki's runaway, best of the fancies. 9th in the Oaks, she was 2nd as 5th choice in the Shuka Sho, closing to a neck of Mikki Queen. Fancied but beaten in the QEII Cup and Victoria Mile, she bloomed in autumn at 4: winning the Fuchu Himba S., she beat Marialite, Mikki Queen and others as 3rd choice in the QEII Cup for a G1. Little at 5, but in her farewell Arima Kinen, ridden forward by Lemaire, she was 2nd to Kitasan Black as 8th choice.
2405: Winner of the 2015 Swan S. Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Flower C., a leading 3yo filly, her camp chose the NHK Mile C. over the fillies' classics; 2nd to Clarity Sky, she was exceptional for a filly. In autumn she beat older horses and colts in the Swan S., then was 5th as 5th choice in the Mile CS after a tight finish. Older she was 3rd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, then faded: 6th in the Swan S., 17th in the Kyoto Himba S., and retired to breed.
2406: Winner of the 2015 Oaks and Shuka Sho. By Deep Impact out of a 3-time French graded winner, sold for 100 million yen at the Select Sale. Lacking prize money, she was balloted out of the Oka Sho, won the Wasurenagusa Sho the same day, and in the Oaks crushed favorite Rouge Buck and Oka Sho winner Let's Go Donki, closing from midfield with her sire's power - the best of her crop. After the Rose S. she won the Shuka Sho as favorite, bursting clear of the pack. Skipping the QEII Cup for the Japan Cup, 3rd choice against older males, she was 8th; champion 3yo filly. At 4 she was 2nd in the Victoria Mile, 3rd in the QEII Cup and 5th to Satono Diamond in the Arima Kinen. At 5, a puzzling 7th in the Victoria Mile, she was 3rd in the Takarazuka Kinen, then in the QEII Cup, going for a 3rd G1, closed fastest but just missed, 3rd to 3yo Mozu Katchan - a changing of the guard.
2407: Winner of the 2015 Rose S. With Oaks winner Mikki Queen hot favorite, she was 7th choice, but charged from the back and outran Mikki Queen's late run. Joint favorite with her in the Shuka Sho, she was 6th, then 3rd in the QEII Cup, best of the 3yos. Older, 2nd in the Kyoto Kinen, she took on males, but was 9th in the Osaka Hai, 6th in the Meguro Kinen and 12th in the Takarazuka Kinen, then 8th in the QEII Cup. At 5, 9th in the Kinko Sho and 13th in the Hanshin Himba S., she retired after a 17th in the QEII Cup.
2408: A King Kamehameha filly with a sharp finish. 3rd in the Flora S. and Shuka Sho at 3, often at the mercy of the pace, she finally won the Aichi Hai at 5, then the Mermaid S. as 3rd choice, breaking clear from a handy spot past Tosen Victory and other fancies. 9th against males in the Kyoto Daishoten, but a force in fillies' graded races.
2409: Of Sakura Bakushin O's blood, he won the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and became sprint king. Debuting late, he won 5 straight to open class, then placed in sprint graded races (2nd in the Kitakyushu Kinen and Keihan Hai) before winning the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, tracking joint favorite Mikki Isle and running him down. In autumn he led all the way in the Centaur S., and a spring-autumn sprint double seemed sure, but from the rail he raced too cautiously, was swallowed up, 12th - a shock from a horse only twice out of the top two. Thrown off, he was 10th as favorite in the Hong Kong Sprint. Injured, he returned in the next Sprinters S., 6th as 8th choice, his old fire gone, and retired to stud.
2410: A middle-distance dirt star. In open class in summer at 4, he raced in graded races from 5, winning the Saga Kinen. After a 6th and 9th, he beat Oi star Keiai Leone in the Mercury C., tracking in 4th and alone finding a different gear as the leaders held on.
2411: A miler who won the Epsom C. at 5. 4th as favorite in the Shinzan Kinen at 3, talented but short of wins, he restarted in allowances, won 3 classes quickly, then the Rigel S. (OP). A fancy in 1400-1600m graded races, he finally won the Epsom C. at 5.
2412: Emerging at 4, he won 3 straight - a 16-million race, the Coral S. (OP) and Nagoya's Kakitsubata Kinen. That summer he won the Procyon S. as favorite, leading from 2nd at the top of the straight. After poor runs, he was 3rd choice in the Capella S. but led all the way to win by 1 3/4 lengths. From 5 he slumped, unplaced except a 2nd in the Nambu Hai, until 7, when he won the Ritto S. (L) and returned to the graded mix; at 8 in May he won the Sakitama Hai.
2413: She won the 2015 Fuchu Himba S. as a longshot. Winning the Shirayuri S. (OP) at 3, she then stayed in allowances until mid-5. 2nd in the Kokura Nikkei OP, she was 11th choice in the Fuchu Himba S., swung wide from midfield and flew past all as favorite Smart Layer and others dueled. With a priority spot in the QEII Cup, she was 12th.
2414: Winner of the 2015 Keisei Hai. Winning steadily from his debut, his first open race was the Keisei Hai, closing wide from midfield. Beaten at Nakayama in the Spring S. and Satsuki Sho, he was 2nd against older horses in the Kokura Kinen, 5th in the St. Lite Kinen, 6th in the Kikuka Sho and 6th in the Kinko Sho - close to another graded win.
2415: Dominant among US females in 2015-2017: 13 wins and 2 2nds from 15, 9 G1s. Most wins were runaways; her losses were by a nose and a neck. At 2 she won her debut, then the Del Mar Debutante S., Chandelier S. and BC Juvenile Fillies. At 3 she won the Santa Anita Oaks, missed the Kentucky Oaks with a fever, then romped in the CCA Oaks, Alabama S. and Cotillion S. Against older mares in the BC Distaff she lost by a nose to Beholder, her first defeat, yet was unanimous champion 3yo filly. At 4 she won 2 more G1s, then after a neck 2nd in the Personal Ensign S., leg trouble ended her career. A broodmare from 2018; her first foal (by Arrogate) came in 2019.
2416: A 2016 classic star behind the Big Three of Dee Majesty, Makahiki and Satono Diamond. A blueblood out of Air Messiah, ridden like his dam by Yutaka Take. He won his debut easily as favorite and the Daily Hai 2yo S. in a duel with fancied Shuji. In a star-studded crop, he was 4th in the Satsuki Sho and Derby, 3rd in the Kikuka Sho - close to the best. At 4 he turned to miles, winning the Kyoto Kimpai; 5th in the Yasuda Kinen, he won the Fuji S., then, with Moore replacing the injured Take, lost the Mile CS by a nose to Persian Knight. At 5, 3rd in the Milers C. and 4th in the Fuji S., he was 10th in the Mile CS. After a long break he turned to dirt at 7: 2nd in the Procyon S., 3rd in the Musashino S. At 8 he closed sharply for 2nd to Cafe Pharoah in the February S., then 2nd in the Sakitama Hai and Musashino S., as good on dirt as on turf. G1s proved hard: 9th in the Champions C. and February S.; after a 5th, 4th and 9th, he retired after a 10th in the Musashino S.
2417: He won his debut and a 5-million race as favorite, then a fracture kept him out until early 4. Back, he won the 10- and 16-million classes as his talent promised, then in his first graded race, the Miyako S. on sloppy ground in light rain, slipped up the rail at the 4th turn and held off Roman Legend and Kazenoko. The next year he was 3rd in the Tokai S. and 5th in the February S. Winless after but often in the top five, he raced until November at 6, then moved to Oi.
2418: A star from 3, top five in the Oaks and Shuka Sho. Restarting in allowances, she kept placing without winning until 6. Then, still in the 16-million class, she stepped up for the Mermaid S. and won as 10th choice from behind, and was 5th as 9th choice in the Queen S. - dangerous in fillies' graded races.
2419: Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Hakodate 2yo S., she was 3rd as 3rd choice in the Hanshin JF, a leading filly. At 3 she flopped in the Tulip Sho and was 8th in the Oka Sho. Turning to sprints, she was 6th in the NHK Mile C. as 15th choice, then won the Keeneland C. Winless in later sprint G1s and graded races, she retired after an 11th in the Keeneland C. at 4 and went to breed in the US.
2420: Winner of the Artemis S., talented early. 2nd choice in the Hanshin JF, she was 7th to Major Emblem. At 3 she flopped in all 3 fillies' classics (10th, 9th, 9th) and was 11th in the QEII Cup. Older she suddenly improved: 4th in the Fukushima Himba S., then 2nd as 11th choice in the Victoria Mile (trifecta 910,000 yen). A long slump followed, with a 3rd in a fillies' graded race. In spring at 6, as 4th of 10, she closed from the back to win the Fukushima Himba S., and at 7, when forgotten again, she won the Aichi Hai by a neck as 9th choice.
2421: A star of the 2015 debut crop, ridden throughout by Christophe Lemaire, who gained a full JRA license that year. She won her debut and a 5-million race as favorite, lost to Denko Ange's late charge in the Artemis S., then led all the way to win the Hanshin JF, top of her crop and champion 2yo filly. She won the Queen C. by 5 lengths, but was jostled in the Oka Sho, 4th. In the NHK Mile C., at her best trip, she held off Lord Quest and others for a G1. Injured after, she never recovered and retired at 4.
2422: The 2016 Oaks winner, hailed as the best of her crop, but injured just before the Shuka Sho. Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Tulip Sho, she was 2nd choice in the Oka Sho behind 2yo queen Major Emblem; it became a duel with 3rd choice Jeweler, who won by a nose. With Jeweler then injured, she was clear Oaks favorite and won. In the Rose S. she beat a returning Jeweler easily, Shuka Sho favorite, but a tendon injury before the race ended her career.
2423: Steady from 2, he beat later 3-time graded winner Smart Odin in the Hagi S., but missed the spring classics. Focusing on miles, he was 2nd to Air Spinel in the Kyoto Kimpai at 4, then beat him in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai for his first graded win. After the Milers C. he was last (18th) in the Yasuda Kinen, and 12th as 4th choice in the Keisei Hai AH.
2424: Leading all the way to win his debut and the Chukyo 2yo S., a star 2yo, he was 1.5 favorite in the Kokura 2yo S.; slightly slow away, he still burst clear with superb speed. 5th in the Asahi Hai FS and 12th in the NHK Mile C., from summer at 3 he was 2nd in the Hakodate Sprint S. and Keeneland C. and 4th in the Sprinters S. 7th choice against G1 winners like Isla Bonita in the Hanshin C., he shot clear for his first graded win since Kokura. At 6 he tried dirt in the Chiba S. (OP) and won, his first win in 2 years.
2425: Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Sapporo 2yo S. After an easy debut win as favorite, he was a fancy in the Sapporo 2yo S. and won a photo after a straight duel with favorite Prophet. 5th in the Hopeful S. and Yayoi Sho, little else. Missing 4 injured and dropping 2 classes, he won on his return at 5 as 7th choice, rose to open class again by year end and was 2nd in the Stayers S. Hopes were high at 6, but after poor runs in the Manyo S. and Hanshin Daishoten, he broke down in the Meguro Kinen and was put down - unusually precocious for a Heart's Cry.
2426: A rare Tochigi-bred. Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Keio Hai 2yo S.: 2nd choice, he led at the 4th turn and edged clear in a long straight drive to win by 1 1/4 lengths. That was his peak; 11th in the Asahi Hai FS, he did little after.
2427: A flagship of the 2016 crop, Kikuka Sho winner, one of a Big Three with Dee Majesty and Makahiki. Prized from a foal, he won his debut easily as favorite and was unbeaten in 3 to the Kisaragi Sho. Satsuki Sho favorite over Leondeux and Makahiki, he was hampered in the straight, 3rd. In the Derby he just failed to catch Makahiki, 2nd. With Makahiki in France, autumn was a duel with Dee Majesty: he won the Kobe Shimbun Hai and Kikuka Sho as favorite, dominant from a handy spot - Deep Impact's first Kikuka Sho winner. Favorite over Kitasan Black in the Arima Kinen, he caught leaders Kitasan Black and Gold Actor near the line for the Grand Prix. In 2017, aiming at the Arc, he won the Hanshin Daishoten, but in the Tenno Sho (Spring) rematch couldn't catch leader Kitasan Black, 3rd. In France, after the Prix Foy, he struggled on Chantilly's heavy turf in the Arc, 15th. Apart from the Kyoto Daishoten at 5 he never recaptured his best, and retired to stud.
2428: The 2016 Derby winner, one of a Big Three with Dee Majesty and Satono Diamond. Unbeaten in 3, he closed from last but couldn't catch Dee Majesty in the Satsuki Sho, 2nd; in the Derby, from midfield, he ran him down to win. In France from August, he won the Prix Niel, then in the Arc, with betting newly allowed in Japan, a hot pace drained him, 14th. Older he fell short: 4th in the Osaka Hai, 5th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 4th in the Japan Cup. As Rey de Oro's younger crop rose, he rarely made the top five at 5, and at 6, a Derby winner at double-figure odds at times, he still popped up with a 4th in the Osaka Hai and Japan Cup. At 7, rivals long retired, he kept running in G1s (11th Osaka Hai, 9th Japan Cup). At 8, 8th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he suddenly won the Kyoto Daishoten - his first win in 5 years - catching favorite Aristoteles near the line. Then the Japan Cup became a clash of 4 Derby winners with Wagnerian, Contrail and Shahryar; 14th, but ahead of Wagnerian. After 3 races at 9, all far back, he retired to stud.
2429: A talent hailed after Dee Majesty and Makahiki. Winning the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. in his 3rd start, at 3 he won the Mainichi Hai and Kyoto Shimbun Hai; 6th in the Derby. Turning to miles, he went winless against older horses until the Hankyu Hai at 4, a 4th graded win, charging powerfully from last.
2430: No G1, but 2nd in the QEII Cup 3 years running - a memorable mare. 3rd in the Sapporo 2yo S. and Artemis S. at 2, she missed the spring classics but was 2nd in the Rose S. and 6th in the Shuka Sho. At 4 she led all the way in the Fuchu Himba S. as 5th choice, holding off favorites Vivlos and Admire Lead. 9th choice in the QEII Cup, she nearly led all the way, 2nd. At 5 she was 2nd again as 9th choice; at 6, 3rd in the Victoria Mile as a longshot, and - as everyone half expected - 2nd in a 3rd QEII Cup. In her farewell, her first Arima Kinen, she tracked leader Aerolithe in 3rd but, perhaps beyond her trip, was last. Even among quirky Stay Gold runners she excelled in big races; may she produce a star.
2431: A great mare who won the QEII Cup at 4 and the Takarazuka Kinen against top males at 5. Blooming at 4, she won 2 allowances, was 2nd as favorite in the Mermaid S. and 5th in the All Comers. In the QEII Cup, against favorite Nuovo Record, defending champion Lachesis and 3yo star Rouge Buck, Ebina timed his move perfectly to win. 4th in the Arima Kinen, at 5 she was 2nd in the Meguro Kinen and 8th choice in a Takarazuka Kinen packed with G1 winners - Duramente, Kitasan Black, Lovely Day - but closed brilliantly from midfield to hold off Duramente for a 2nd G1. Favorite to defend the QEII Cup, she was 6th.
2432: Emerging early, 2nd in the Sapporo 2yo S., he won the Keisei Hai the next January, racing 4th-5th and pulling away. Overlooked in the classics: 11th as 10th choice in the Satsuki Sho, 17th as 18th in the Derby, unplaced in the St. Lite Kinen and Fukushima Kinen. At 4, 3rd in the Shirafuji S. (OP), he dropped to the 16-million class.
2433: Winner of the 2015 Hopeful S. Named after comet Hartley 2, observed by NASA's Deep Impact probe - fitting for a Deep Impact colt. After a debut win as favorite, he was 3rd choice in the Hopeful S. behind hot favorite Lord Quest, but drew level at the 4th turn and outkicked him. Beaten badly in the Kyodo News Hai at 3, leg trouble followed; he recovered enough to race but never regained his power, retiring at 6 after just 8 starts - a talent unfulfilled.
2434: Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Kyoto 2yo S., noticed early. He won as favorite on Kikuka Sho day, the "legendary debut" race that produced Buena Vista, Rose Kingdom and Victoire Pisa; Yutaka Take was excited. In the Kyoto 2yo S. he tracked in 2nd and won a straight duel with Respect Earth. A classic fancy, he was 7th in the Spring S. and 15th in the Satsuki Sho, then stayed in allowances, returning to open class in autumn at 5. Improving with 3 top-five runs in Hokkaido at 6, he won the Kyoto Daishoten as 11th choice, sitting 3rd and passing leader Danburite - his first graded win in 4 years.
2435: A super horse named by Maaya Morinaga, introduced in Winning Post 8 2016. By her beloved Kizuna out of 2-time Arc winner Treve, he storms home to win the Arc his sire couldn't - a son fulfilling his father's dream. The name "Mirai" (future) holds the wish to see that future.
2438: A super horse named by the University of Tokyo Horsemen Club, introduced in Winning Post 8 2016. Mejiro McQueen on the sire's side; Shinzan, Maruzensky and other greats of modern Japanese racing on the dam's. As her name suggests, she is flexible; early-normal maturity, a threat in the fillies' classics. The name is a double meaning: "UT + Rise" (University of Tokyo and her dam's name) and "utilize."
2439: A sprinter who bloomed in autumn at 4. Though he ran in the Derby once, he was best at 1600m or less. Reaching open class with a 16-million win in autumn at 4, he was 8th as 3rd choice in the Swan S., then won the Keihan Hai, leading mid-straight from a handy spot and holding off favorite Big Arthur by a head. A sprint graded regular the next year, unplaced in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and Sprinters S., he was 2nd as 8th choice in the Swan S.
2440: A rare star by Admire Don, 3-time winner of the Stayers S. and a fixture in long races. Struggling at a mile to middle trips, he soared once tried at long distances in summer at 4: 3 straight wins to open class, then the Stayers S. 6th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) at 5, he won the Stayers S. again after a duel with Fata Morgana. At 6 he won the Diamond S. and a 3rd Stayers S. - king of the stayers.
2441: Winner of the 2015 Challenge C. 2nd as 2nd choice in it at 3, he kept falling short: 3rd in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai, 4th in the Epsom C. In the Challenge C. at 4, Mirco Demuro rode with force: boxed in on the rail in midfield at the 4th turn, he split a narrow gap and burst clear to win as favorite.
2442: Winning his debut in summer at 2, he then spent years in allowances, rising and dropping, before an open win early at 5. Often closing too late, he won the Capella S. late at 6 for his first graded win. Winless at 7.
2443: Winner of the Asahi Hai FS, a 2016 classic hope. His dam Cesario won the Japanese and American Oaks and produced Kikuka Sho and Japan Cup winner Epiphaneia; much was expected of his brother. He won his debut as favorite by 1.5 lengths, then the Asahi Hai FS as 2nd choice, charging from last to beat favorite Air Spinel - 2yo champion. Classic favorite at 3, he lost for the first time to Makahiki's kick in the Yayoi Sho. 2nd choice in the Satsuki Sho, he ended up leading a hot pace, 5th; in the Derby he closed too late, 5th - no crown. A tendon injury while preparing for autumn ended his career. At stud, his first crop gave Tenno Sho (Spring) winner T O Royal (2024), and in 2025 Museum Mile won the Satsuki Sho - a bright future.
2444: The 2016 Satsuki Sho winner, in a classic billed as a Big Three with Makahiki and Satono Diamond. Despite winning the Kyodo News Hai, he was only 8th choice in the Satsuki Sho, but charged past Makahiki and Satono Diamond to become a lead player. Derby favorite, he closed powerfully again but just missed Makahiki and Satono Diamond, 3rd. In autumn he won the St. Lite Kinen as favorite; with Makahiki in France, the Kikuka Sho was a duel with Satono Diamond, but despite moving early he couldn't close in, 4th. 4th choice against older horses in the Japan Cup, he was 13th. Older, 6th in the Nikkei Sho and Tenno Sho (Spring), he retired to stud with leg trouble.
2445: Struggling long in allowances, he soared at 2400m+ - a true stayer. In open class in autumn at 4, he was at once 3rd in the Stayers S., then won the Diamond S. as 4th choice. 13th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he was 2nd in the Sapporo Nikkei OP. A tendon injury sidelined him; 9th in the same race a year later, he retired and moved to Nagoya.
2436: A super horse named by the University of Tokyo Horsemen Club, introduced in Winning Post 8 2016. Heir to his sire Durandal, whose kick was likened to Shinzan's "hatchet." His dam 1 Carat adds more sparkle. Late-normal maturity with lasting growth like his sire, he always makes players fear a charge from off the screen. His name is a 16th-century German greatsword (inspired by Durandal, a French holy sword).
2437: A super horse named by the University of Tokyo Horsemen Club, from Winning Post 8 2016. A dirt horse of North American blood, inbred 3x4 to Deputy Minister, he races forward and keeps going. After ruling Japan's dirt races he aims for the BC Classic his sire Casino Drive never won. His name means "Watch me, Father."
2446: Half-brother of Rose S. winner Animate Bio (07: Zenno Rob Roy). He won the Arlington C. and was 3rd in the NHK Mile C., then tried longer races: the Derby, and the Sapporo Kinen, a neck behind favorite Maurice in 3rd. In the Kikuka Sho he was 2nd to Satono Diamond as 9th choice, handling 3000m, then 6th in the Japan Cup, best of the 3yos. Older, he was 5th in the Takarazuka Kinen and 3rd as 13th choice in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). At 5 he won the Hanshin Daishoten, then the Tenno Sho (Spring) as 2nd choice, closing superbly from midfield for a G1. His jockey dismounted after the line - he was injured and retired to stud.
2447: Racing in local middle-distance graded races, he won the Kokura Kinen at 7. Always fancied, he won a 16-million race in summer at 5, then was 2nd in the Niigata Kinen in his first open race. Unplaced for a while, at 7, next-to-last choice in the Kokura Kinen, he led and held on - a big upset.
2448: Of Sakura Bakushin O's blood, a sprinter like him. Debuting in spring at 3 and slow to win, he came good at 5, winning 3 classes quickly, then raced in sprint graded races. Always overlooked, he closed brilliantly from last to win the Kitakyushu Kinen at 7. Little after; retired in August at 8.
2449: A turf G1 winner from Nikiya's famed dirt family. Winning with a sharp finish, he won the Arlington C. in his 5th start. 4th choice in the Satsuki Sho, he joined the leaders at the 4th turn and lost a duel with Al Ain, 2nd. 7th in the Derby, he turned to miles: 5th in the Fuji S., then 4th choice in the Mile CS, he split the field at the 4th turn and swept past all - the first 3yo winner since Agnes Digital in 2000, one of 3 G1 winners from his sire Harbinger's crop with Deirdre and Mozu Katchan. Older he was 2nd to Suave Richard in the Osaka Hai and a head 2nd defending the Mile CS, then 3rd to Indy Champ in it the next year. At 6, 2nd in the Sapporo Kinen, he was 7th in a 4th Mile CS, then 7th in the Arima Kinen, his first 2500m race. At 7, 10th in the Osaka Hai and 7th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), his best were 3rds in the Sapporo Kinen and Challenge C. He retired after the Arima Kinen and became a lead pony.
2450: Winner of the 2016 Hakodate Kinen on the middle-distance G3 circuit. Winning 2 allowances at 4, he placed in G3s (5th Kokura Daishoten, 3rd Chunichi Shimbun Hai) and at 6 won the Hakodate Kinen as 3rd choice, leading throughout and winning by 2 lengths.
2451: A dirt sprinter who won open races like the Green Channel C. and Polaris S., then Saga's Summer Champion at 6 as hot favorite at 1.8, leading all the way. After a dry spell he won Korea's G1 Korea Sprint, then the Hyogo Gold T. At 8 he led all the way in the Tokyo Sprint, was 2nd in the Sakitama Hai and Tokyo Hai, then won the JBC Sprint as 4th choice - Christophe Lemaire, on a run of 3 straight weekly G1 wins, delivered again with a perfect ride from up front.
2452: 2nd in the Mainichi Hai at 3, he flopped in the NHK Mile C. and turned to sprints, winning the Yodo Tankyori S. (OP) at 4 and the Ocean S. at 5 as 5th choice, closing sharply from behind midfield to catch leader Haku San Moon. In the Takamatsunomiya Kinen he closed for 5th.
2453: A speedster who bloomed at 5 and won the Sprinters S. twice. Disliking right-handed tracks, he raced mainly at Tokyo and Chukyo, switching between dirt and turf, and reached open class in autumn at 4. 10th in the Negishi S., he was 2nd and 1st in dirt open races, seemingly a dirt horse, but then won the turf CBC Sho from the back with the fastest finish. In the Sprinters S. off a break, 3rd choice behind hot favorite Big Arthur on a right-handed track he disliked, he charged from midfield past Mikki Isle and the leaders for his first G1. At 6 he was 3rd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, won the Keio Hai SC, 3rd in the Yasuda Kinen, then won the Sprinters S. again as favorite off a break, closing from the back.
2454: 3rd in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai at 3 with only 1 win, he restarted in the 5-million class. After many placings he won 3 straight at 4 to reach open class. Fancied but only top five in open races, he won the Chukyo Kinen at 5, closing fastest from last.
2455: He upset mile king Maurice in the Sapporo Kinen, and was 3rd in a wide-open Mile CS that autumn - real class. In allowances until the end of 4, he raced in graded races from 5. In the Sapporo Kinen, switching from waiting to leading, he beat favorite Maurice by 2 lengths. He tracked in 2nd for 2nd in the Mile CS, now a front-runner, and went to the Hong Kong Mile. The next year, after the Nakayama Kinen, he won Hong Kong's QEII Cup - a big title abroad - and was 3rd in the Hong Kong Cup, best of the Japanese.
2456: He won 3 straight at 5 from allowances to the G3 Sirius S. Winning a maiden early, a weak left foreleg limited him to 3-4 races a year, and it took 3 years to reach open class. After a 16-million race and the July S. (OP), he led from the start in the Sirius S. and won a 3-way duel with Pionero and Apollo Kentucky.
2457: A sprinter who won the Keihan Hai twice. Blooming mid-4, he won the Kyoraku S. and Opal S. (both OP); at 5, 2nd in the Ibis Summer Dash and Centaur S., he won the Keihan Hai as 2nd choice, leading from the start and pulling away. At 6 he suddenly lost form, then was 4th on dirt in the JBC Sprint and led all the way to win the Keihan Hai again as 9th choice. At 7, mainly on dirt, he was 3rd in the Tokyo Sprint and 2nd in the Cluster C. and Tokyo Hai.
2458: 3rd in the Keisei Hai at 3, a classic hope, he fractured and missed the classics. Restarting that summer, he reached open class the next year, was 6th in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai, then won the Milers C. in his first mile race, closing fastest from midfield past favorite Fiero. At 7 he raced 4 times in Australia, 2nd to great mare Winx in the G1 Queen Elizabeth S. At 8 he won the Lord Derby CT, his first win in 4 years.
2459: Won 3 straight: a 5-million race, an open race and the Falcon S., closing from behind midfield to win by 1 3/4 lengths. 5th as 5th choice in the NHK Mile C., he was unplaced in the Chukyo Kinen and Keisei Hai AH, then won the Shin'etsu S. (OP) in autumn.
2460: He lost a maiden by a neck to later Satsuki Sho winner Dee Majesty, then won 3 straight incl. the Spring S., passing leader Meiner Honey from a handy spot. But in the G1s - 6th in the Satsuki Sho, 7th in the Derby and Kikuka Sho - he couldn't break into the Big Three of Dee Majesty, Makahiki and Satono Diamond.
2461: From the late crops of great sire Brian's Time, noted as his last graded winner. 1st in the Junior C. (OP) and 2nd in the Arlington C., he won the NZT as 2nd choice, settling despite pulling and holding on with something in hand. 4th in the NHK Mile C., then unplaced in 2 open races.
2462: By Deep Impact out of a Galileo mare, a stout pedigree suited to long trips. Winning a 2000m maiden and a 2400m 5-million race, he won the Aoba Sho, leading in the straight from a handy spot. 13th in the Derby, perhaps worn out by long races, he suffered a tendon injury; preparing a return, it recurred the next July, and he retired to stud.
2463: A sharp closer, 3rd in his first open race, the Principal S., then winner of the Radio Nikkei Sho as favorite. 2nd in the St. Lite Kinen, he skipped the Kikuka Sho for the Fukushima Kinen at 2.1, but couldn't catch leader Maltese Apogee, 2nd. 2nd again in the AJCC at 4, he won the Tanabata Sho that summer, proving his strength at 2000m.
2464: Winning a 5-million race at 3, he won the Hosu S. (OP), then the Japan Dirt Derby, 3yo dirt champion. Billed as Gold Dream vs. Strong Barows, he burst clear from a handy spot and pulled away. Little in the Sirius S. and Miyako S.
2465: A 2016 3yo dirt star who won the Leopard S. Beaten on turf on debut, he won steadily on dirt and was 3rd as 3rd choice in the Unicorn S. In the Leopard S., joint favorite with Katy Brave, he spurted from a handy spot and caught the leader near the line. At 4 he won the Tokai S., then was 5th in the JBC Classic and 10th in the Champions C.
2466: 2nd to Satono Diamond on the same time in the Kobe Shimbun Hai and 5th in the Kikuka Sho, he won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai as favorite, beating crop-mate Shaketra in a duel. 4th in the Kyoto Kinen and Kyoto Daishoten, 2nd in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai, he was 4th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) at 5. In the Takarazuka Kinen, with Derby winner Rey de Oro and Osaka Hai winner Suave Richard absent, he was 7th choice in a wide-open race, raced boldly, led early in the straight and held off longshot Waarther by a neck for a G1. Jockey Wada's first JRA G1 in 17 years, since T.M. Opera O, who had died that May; his words, "Opera O pushed me," moved many fans.
2467: Winning the Saga Kinen easily at 4, he was 4th in the March S., 2nd in the Antares S., then won the Elm S. as 4th choice in record time, catching favorite T M Jinsoku. In Korea he led all the way to win the Korea Cup (Korean G1), with Chrysolite 2nd - a Japanese 1-2. He won it again the next year.
2468: Emerging early, he won the Saudi Arabia Royal C. as 3rd choice, charging wide from the back past Climb Major and others, then the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. by a neck in a 3-way duel with Move the World and Suave Richard as the leaders collapsed. A fracture meant a long break - cruel luck for a colt who had beaten later classic stars. Back in autumn at 3 straight into the Kikuka Sho, he was 12th, then 3rd in the Challenge C.
2469: A rare Japanese runner by US sire Pioneerof the Nile, sire of Triple Crown winner American Pharoah, and his first graded winner in Japan - the 2016 Hakodate 2yo S., breaking clear early from a handy spot and holding off favorite Mondo Cannon. Beaten badly in the Asahi Hai FS, he has struggled in sprints since.
2470: After winning a maiden, he was top three in 16 of 20 allowance races. Finally winning a 16-million race in summer at 5, he won his first graded race, the Elm S., as 7th choice, moving early from a handy spot past favorite Mondo Classe and holding off Kurino Star O.
2471: A Shuka Sho runner at 3, she slumped and restarted in the 16-million class. In open class the next year, she was 4th in the Kyoto Himba S. and 3rd in 2 open races. At 6 she suddenly won the Fukushima Himba S. as 15th choice, then the Queen S. as 9th choice - stunning back-to-back wins. Injured after, she retired.
2472: In open class in autumn at 4, she was 7th in the QEII Cup and 8th in the Aichi Hai, then won the Nakayama Himba S. as 4th choice, running down favorite Rouge Buck from midfield. 4th as favorite in the Mermaid S., she was 3rd against males in the Kinko Sho.
2473: Starting on turf and running in the Flower C. at 3, she switched to dirt at 4 and was steady. 2nd in the Empress Hai at 5, she won the Marine C. - hot favorite Buchiko was scratched at the gate; tracking in 2nd, she drew level 200m out and won by half a length.
2474: 3rd in the Leopard S. and TCK Jo-o Hai, she won the Ladies' Prelude in autumn at 4, moving up from behind midfield at the 4th turn and charging wide past favorite White Fugue to win by 1.5 lengths. White Fugue turned the tables in the JBC Ladies' Classic (4th).
2475: A late-blooming star of America's 2016 3yo crop. Too late for the classics, he won 4 G1s incl. the BC Classic and Dubai World Cup, top of the dirt world. Debuting in April at 3, he won his 2nd start and 3 more, then in August led all the way in the G1 Travers S. by 13.5 lengths over Preakness winner Exaggerator and Belmont winner Creator. 2nd choice in the BC Classic, he outdueled champion California Chrome, rated the world's best at 134 lbs. At 4 he won the new Pegasus World C. easily, then in the Dubai World Cup stumbled at the start, raced last, swept wide and passed them all. Winless in 3 more, he retired; his first crop gave Kentucky Oaks winner Secret Oath, but illness ended his life in June 2020, with only 3 crops.
2476: A mare who won 25 G1s in Australia from 2015 to 2019, world records for G1 wins and earnings. Mixed results until late at 3, she won the Queensland Oaks, her first G1, and then won 33 straight. At 4 she won 5 G1s, Australian Horse of the Year; at 5 she won 6, Horse of the Year again; at 6, 6 more - a world-record 18th international G1, and 25 straight wins, equaling Black Caviar. At 7 she won 7 G1s incl. a 4th Cox Plate and 3rd Queen Elizabeth S., retiring with 25 G1s. Dominant from 1400m to 2200m. Great things are hoped for from her foals.
2477: With just 1 win, she won the Fillies' Revue, an Oka Sho trial, at long odds, but was 17th of 18 in the Oka Sho. Perhaps 1600m was too far; turning to sprints, she won the Hakodate Sprint S. as 12th choice in record time, holding on from up front in a hot pace. 3rd in the Sprinters S. proved her no fluke. At 4 she won only the Opal S. (OP), but was 5th in the Victoria Mile back at a mile.
2478: Winner of the Flower C. as favorite, a classic hope, leading all the way. 3rd choice in the Oaks behind Sinhalite and Cecchino, she tired mid-straight, 10th - too far. In autumn she was 16th of 18 in both the Shion S. and Shuka Sho.
2479: She won the Oka Sho with a thrilling late charge. With 2yo queen Major Emblem dominant, she quietly rose: a debut win, 2nd in the Shinzan Kinen and to Sinhalite in the Tulip Sho. 3rd choice in the Oka Sho, she waited at the back, then swept past the field and caught Sinhalite by a nose. A chip fracture ruled out the Oaks. 11th in the Rose S., not at her best, she was 2nd choice in the Shuka Sho and closed powerfully for 4th.
2480: She won the Flora S. and stormed the fillies' classics, a hope to break into the Major Emblem, Jeweler and Sinhalite group. 2nd choice in the Oaks, she closed from the back to lose by a neck to favorite Sinhalite. A tendon injury meant 2 years off; back, she was 7th in the Yonago S. and Sekiya Kinen and retired. Her first foal, by Maurice, came in 2020.
2481: She won the Shion S. in autumn at 3, a Shuka Sho trial, then was Shuka Sho favorite. Debuting late at 3, she was soon 3rd in the Oaks and bloomed in autumn, but faded to 10th in the Shuka Sho, then 16th against older horses in the Japan Cup.
2482: Sister of 2-time Victoria Mile winner Verxina and Japan Cup winner Cheval Grand; like siblings Falster and Rangiroa, owned by ex-baseball player Kazuhiro Sasaki. Fancied on debut, she won once then faded, missing the spring classics. Switching from racing forward to closing, she improved dramatically: an easy 5-million win, 2nd to Bisch in the Shion S., then 3rd choice behind Bisch and Oka Sho winner Jeweler in a Shuka Sho without Oaks winner Sinhalite, she charged past them all - avenging Verxina, who was shut out by Gentildonna in the fillies' classics. At 4, 5th of 11 in the Nakayama Kinen after gaining 10kg, she won the Dubai Turf under "magic man" Moreira, proving the Shuka Sho no fluke. Favorite in the Fuchu Himba S. and QEII Cup, she was 2nd and 5th. At 5 she was 2nd defending the Dubai Turf, 4th in the Takarazuka Kinen (trifecta 490,000 yen), the only fancy in the top five, and 2nd in the Hong Kong Mile.
2483: She won the Niigata 2yo S. with a brilliant late run, recalling monster filly Harp Star, who won it 3 years earlier. Still raw and keen, she was handled by Fukunaga on their first ride and unleashed in the straight. 6th choice behind Soul Stirring and Lys Gracieux in the Hanshin JF, she was 5th. At 3 she was 10th in the Oka Sho and 11th in the Shuka Sho; her best was 4th in the Arlington C.
2484: He led as usual to finish 2nd in the Spring S. ahead of favored Lord Quest and Mikki Rocket. With a Satsuki Sho spot but no classic entry, he went the Aoba Sho-Derby route instead; 16th in the Derby, too far, he turned to middle trips, 2nd in the Ireland T. (OP), 4th in the Fukushima Kinen, then won the Challenge C.
2485: A talent noticed early, 2nd choice in the Asahi Hai FS. At 3 he was 3rd in the Satsuki Sho, 6th in the Derby, 5th in the Kikuka Sho. In his first race as an older horse, the AJCC, 2nd choice behind Mikki Swallow, he broke clear from up front for his first graded win. 7th in Hong Kong's QEII Cup, he was 5th in the Takarazuka Kinen, then 3rd to Rey de Oro and Al Ain in the All Comers - a crop 1-2-3. At 5 he won the Kyoto Kinen and was 2nd in the Kyoto Daishoten, strong in graded races without a G1. Gelded at 6, unplaced in 3 races, at 7 he was 3rd in the Kyoto Kinen and in the Nagoya GP on dirt, retiring after the Hanshin Daishoten at 8.
2486: He won his debut by 6 lengths and the Platanus Sho by 7, then went to the Hokkaido 2yo Yushun as 1.0 favorite under Lemaire and won by a huge margin. At 3 he won the Hyacinth S. and was 2nd to Thunder Snow in the UAE Derby after a duel. A Belmont S. plan was dropped with leg trouble; back, he was favorite in the Leopard S. and Miyako S. but won neither.
2487: A classic hope noticed early, unbeaten in 2, he was 1.4 favorite in the Kisaragi Sho but 2nd on heavy ground, and 2nd again at 1.2 in the Mainichi Hai. 10th in the Derby and 11th in the Kikuka Sho. Still rated, he shone when older at a mile to middle trips: after the Rakuyo S. (OP) he won the Epsom C. A ligament injury cost a year; back, he was 2nd in the Port Island S. (L), 3rd in the Osakajo S. (L), 2nd in the Rokko S. (L), then in the Sekiya Kinen closed from last with a superior finish to win easily. Winless after, he retired after the Milers C. at 8.
2488: Unbeaten in 2, he was 2nd in the Arlington C. and 4th in the NHK Mile C. at 3, then won the Rigel S. (OP), a sprint name to watch. Winless when older, he kept placing in the 16-million class until the Hikone S. in spring at 5, then won the CBC Sho from midfield. Focusing on sprints, he was 3rd in the next CBC Sho, then won the Kitakyushu Kinen as 8th choice, beating Takamatsunomiya Kinen winner Mozu Superflare. 4th choice in the Sprinters S., he was no match for champion Gran Alegria, 6th, then 14th as 2nd choice in the Keihan Hai. At 7, unplaced but for a 5th in the Kitakyushu Kinen, he retired after the Silk Road S. at 8.
2489: A flagship of Rey de Oro and Kiseki's crop. No classic, but 2nd to Rey de Oro in the Derby, and older he won the Osaka Hai and Japan Cup. At 3 he won the Kyodo News Hai, was 6th in the Satsuki Sho and 2nd in the Derby, then beat older horses in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai and was 4th in the Arima Kinen, best of the 3yos. At 4 he won the Kinko Sho, then the Osaka Hai for his first G1, with crop-mates Persian Knight and Satsuki winner Al Ain 2nd and 3rd, seeing off older star Satono Diamond. 3rd in the Yasuda Kinen at a mile, he was 10th as favorite in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), then 3rd in the Japan Cup. At 5, 3rd in the Dubai Sheema Classic and Takarazuka Kinen, unplaced again in the jinxed Tenno Sho (Autumn), he shared favoritism with Rey de Oro and Wagnerian in the Japan Cup and burst up the rail from a handy spot for a 2nd G1. His brother Bandwagon was a 2014 classic hope until injured. At stud from 2020 at 2 million yen; after first-crop Corazon Beat won the Keio Hai 2yo S., his fee jumped to 15 million.
2490: A sprinter who won his first graded race in summer at 5. Winner of 4 open races like the Carbuncle S., with graded best a 2nd, he was always fancied and 3rd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen. In his 3rd Keeneland C. - 5th at 3, 3rd at 4 - he won by 2.5 lengths. 2nd choice in the Sprinters S., he was 7th in a blanket finish (7 within 2 lengths).
2491: The 2017 Oka Sho winner. Hugely popular, she won her debut at 1.8 and the Kokura 2yo S. as favorite by 6 lengths, closing fastest from 2nd. 3rd choice in a strong Hanshin JF, she was 3rd behind favorite Soul Stirring and Lys Gracieux. 4th in the Queen C. behind Admire Miyabi, she tried midfield tactics in the Fillies' Revue and was caught by Karakurenai, 2nd - doubts grew that sprints suited her best. 8th choice in the Oka Sho, she raced forward and held on as rivals floundered on soft ground. The Oaks and Shuka Sho were too far (double-figure finishes), but she was 4th as 10th choice in the Mile CS. At 4, unplaced in the Ocean S. and Takamatsunomiya Kinen, she was far back in the Victoria Mile, Yasuda Kinen and Mile CS.
2492: Unbeaten in 4 incl. the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun. He won his debut and the Suzuran Sho (OP) on turf from up front, then the Edelweiss Sho on dirt by 5 lengths, and the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun at 2.0 by 3 lengths, alone finding another gear from 3rd-4th. At 3 he was 2nd in the NHK Mile C. on turf, then back on dirt was 7th in the Unicorn S. and 5th in the Oval Sprint.
2493: At 3 she was 2nd in the Queen C., 4th in the Flora S., and ran in the Oaks and Shuka Sho. Older, in fillies' graded races, she was 2nd in the Fukushima Himba S. and Turquoise S. at 4, and the Nakayama Himba S. and Queen S. at 5. At 6, in a Nakayama Himba S. with 8 horses in a blanket finish, she edged ahead - a graded winner at last. 2nd in the Fuchu Himba S. that year, she retired to breed.
2494: A late improver who won the Victoria Mile. She won a strong debut with a sharp kick, then struggled as her body caught up. 5th in the Oka Sho, 15th in the Oaks, 7th in the Rose S., she skipped the Shuka Sho and restarted in allowances, winning 2 to reach open class at 4. Much stronger, she was 2nd as 3rd choice in the Hanshin Himba S. In the Victoria Mile, with 5yos Mikki Queen and Rouge Buck fancied, she was 6th choice but split the field powerfully from midfield to win; with 11th choice Denko Ange 2nd and 7th choice Jour Polaire 3rd, the trifecta paid 910,000 yen. 3rd in the Fuchu Himba S., she was injured before the Mile CS. Back at 5, 4th in the Hanshin Himba S., she was 8th as 2nd choice defending the Victoria Mile. She won the December S. (OP) and retired to breed.
2495: A super blueblood by Frankel, 10-G1 monster, out of 6-G1 European mare Stacelita, ridden by star jockey Christophe Lemaire - hugely noticed from her debut. Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Hanshin JF, far more finished than her rivals, she broke clear from up front and won with ease. At 3 she won the Tulip Sho at 1.5, a classic seemingly assured, but on soft ground in the Oka Sho lacked her usual kick, 3rd. Amid doubts about power and stamina, fans still made her Oaks favorite; from the rail she raced handy and dispelled them all with a strong finish - queen. Skipping the Shuka Sho, she took on older horses but was out of the top five in the Mainichi Okan, Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Japan Cup. Older, her best was 3rd in the Queen S.
2496: Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Daily Hai 2yo S., talented early. 4th choice in the Hanshin JF, she was 11th; at 3, 4th in the Fillies' Revue and 9th in the Oka Sho. Dropped in trip for the Hakodate Sprint S., she won by 2.5 lengths - brilliant when conditions suit.
2497: A Manhattan Cafe colt unbeaten in 2 incl. the Nojigiku S. At 3 he won the Kisaragi Sho as 6th of 8, sitting handy and holding off Satono Arthur and Danburite. But he was 18th in the Satsuki Sho and 17th in the Derby. On miles in autumn: 10th in the Port Island S., 1st in the Cassiopeia S. (both OP), 16th in the Mile CS. At 4, 4th in the Rakuyo S. (OP) was his best; back at middle trips, 3rd in the Andromeda S. (OP), then the odd 4th or 5th. Winless as an older horse after racing until the Kan'etsu S. (OP) at 7, he switched to jumps.
2498: He won the Swan S. on 4 straight, a sprint name to watch. 3rd in the Daily Hai 2yo S. and 5th in the Hopeful S. without winning, he restarted in allowances at 3. Winning in May, he won 2 more classes strongly, then the G2 Swan S. as 2nd choice behind Let's Go Donki, closing brilliantly from the back. 3rd as 7th choice in the Mile CS, at 4 he won the Milers C., then the 2000m Sapporo Kinen, and was 2nd as 4th choice in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) - effective at middle trips too.
2499: The 2017 Derby winner. With Satsuki Sho winner Al Ain and Kikuka Sho winner Kiseki, he led racing in 2017-2019, proving his crop's strength. Unbeaten in 3 to the Hopeful S. as hot favorite, he was the classic focus. Straight into the Satsuki Sho, 5th, he then won the Derby, best of his crop. In autumn he won the Kobe Shimbun Hai easily, then skipped the Kikuka Sho for the Japan Cup, 2nd, ahead of champion Kitasan Black. Older he led his crop: 3rd in the Kyoto Kinen, 4th in the Dubai Sheema Classic, then the All Comers as favorite and the Tenno Sho (Autumn) over crop-mates Al Ain, Kiseki and others. 2nd to 3yo Blast Onepiece in the Arima Kinen, still a force. At 5 he faded: 6th in Dubai, 5th in the Takarazuka Kinen, 4th in the All Comers, 11th in the Japan Cup as crop-mate Suave Richard won. In his farewell Arima Kinen he was 7th as 9th choice, but the paddock was full of fan banners. Now a sire.
2500: Favorite in every allowance race, but often 2nd or 3rd, he reached open class only when older. In the Challenge C., 2nd choice in a 2-horse race with Rey Enda, he broke clear from a handy spot with the fastest finish and won easily.
2501: The 2017 Satsuki Sho winner, a flagship of the crop with Rey de Oro and Kiseki. Unbeaten in 2, he was 6th in the Shinzan Kinen on heavy ground, then won the Mainichi Hai from 2nd. 9th choice in the Satsuki Sho amid stamina doubts, he was swallowed up at the 4th turn, recovered, split the pack and won. 5th in the Derby, close up, 2nd in the St. Lite Kinen, he was 2nd choice behind Kiseki in the Kikuka Sho but, in a storm-soaked quagmire (final 600m near 40s), finished 7th. At 4, at middle trips, no G1 but 3rd in the Osaka Hai, 4th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 3rd in the Mile CS. At 5, 9th choice as Blast Onepiece and Wagnerian rose, he won the Osaka Hai in a tight finish with Kiseki 2nd - his crop's strength again. 4th in the Takarazuka Kinen, he was 14th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 16th in the Mile CS, then 11th in his farewell Arima Kinen, reunited with Satsuki rider Matsuyama.
2502: A Heart's Cry filly in the strong 2017 crop. Losing her debut narrowly, she won 3 straight incl. the Daily Hai Queen C., beating later Yayoi Sho winner Cadenas in the Hyakunichiso Tokubetsu and later NHK Mile C. winner Aerolithe in the Queen C. In the Oka Sho, billed vs. Hanshin JF winner Soul Stirring, she floundered on soft ground, 12th. Her camp's stated goal was always the Oaks; 2nd choice there, she was 3rd. A tendon injury before the Rose S. ended her career.
2503: The first mare to win both Grand Prix races in one year, 2019 JRA Horse of the Year ahead of younger star Almond Eye. Noticed early, she was 2nd in the Hanshin JF, Oka Sho and Shuka Sho, 5th in the Oaks - always short of a title until the QEII Cup at 4 shed her "silver collector" tag. At 5, 2nd in the Kinko Sho and 3rd in Hong Kong's QEII Cup, she won the Takarazuka Kinen, sweeping past Al Ain, Rey de Oro, Kiseki and Suave Richard. In Australia she won the Cox Plate. Her camp named the Arima Kinen as her last race - a showdown with Almond Eye, with the JRA specially allowing her Takarazuka and Cox Plate rider Damian Lane - and excitement peaked. As Aerolithe set a hot pace, she raced on the rail in midfield watching Almond Eye, then swung wide in the straight with superb agility, caught the leaders and won by 5 lengths from Saturnalia - the first mare to win both Grand Prix races. Horse of the Year and champion older mare, she retired. Her first foal Schwertlilie was fatally injured in a race, but much is hoped from foals by top sires.
2504: A dirt miler who won his first graded race at 6. Winning 3 straight at 5 to the Ritto S. (OP), he was 3rd in his first graded race, the Procyon S., then a top-five regular: 4th in the Musashino S. and Negishi S. 11th in the G1 February S., he won the Procyon S. on his 6th graded try, charging powerfully from the back. In autumn he was 3rd in the Nambu Hai and Miyako S.
2505: Debuting at Kawasaki, he won the Sapporo 2yo S. as a local horse. He won his debut at 1.1 by 4 lengths and the Wakakusa Tokubetsu by a huge margin, then in JRA races was 2nd in the Clover Sho and led all the way in the Sapporo 2yo S. Moving to the JRA, he placed in graded races: 5th in the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. and Asahi Hai FS, 4th in the Shinzan Kinen, 5th in the Mainichi Hai. In the G1s - 13th in the Satsuki Sho, 8th in the NHK Mile C. and Derby - he struggled.
2506: A rare pedigree: by Danzig's son Langfuhr. As of 2018 he was the sire's only runner in Japan and only graded winner. Emerging at 4, he won 3 straight - a 16-million race, the Jinsen S. and Brilliant S. (both OP). 3rd in the Sirius S., he won the Miyako S. in a tight finish, was 5th as 7th choice in the Champions C., then won the Tokyo Daishoten, a G1. 9th in the Dubai World Cup, 5th in the Teio Sho, he won the Nippon TV Hai, a 3rd graded win, then kept falling short despite a 2nd in the Kawasaki Kinen and 3rd in the Kashiwa Kinen.
2507: A pure sprint pedigree: by Kinshasa no Kiseki out of a Sakura Bakushin O mare. After a debut win, he was 1.8 favorite in the Hakodate 2yo S. but couldn't catch Levante Lion, 2nd. In the Keio Hai 2yo S. he beat him, swinging wide from behind midfield with a finish from another dimension. In the Asahi Hai FS he closed the same way but lost by half a length to Satono Ares. At 3 he faded: 10th in the Spring S., 9th in the NHK Mile C., 6th as favorite in the Keeneland C., 14th in the Sprinters S.
2508: Winner of the Kyoto 2yo S. at 2 and Yayoi Sho at 3, a 2017 classic fancy, but 9th as 3rd choice in the Satsuki Sho and 11th as 8th choice in the Derby. A 2-year slump followed until a 3rd in the Fukushima Minpo Hai (L) in spring at 5; that summer he was 2nd in the Kokura Kinen and 3rd in the Niigata Kinen. At 6 he won the Kokura Daishoten in February, his first graded win in 3 years, with an overwhelming late charge. 4th in the Osaka Hai and Mainichi Okan, he faded at 7 (10th Mainichi Okan, 16th Tenno Sho). At 8 he was 5th on his dirt debut in the Tokai S. and 3rd in the Kokura Daishoten, retiring to stud after the Tenno Sho (Autumn).
2509: From the first crop of Frankel, unbeaten in 14 with 10 G1s; she and Soul Stirring quickly won graded races, gifting their sire success in Japan. She won her debut at 1.3, then the Fantasy S. at 1.4, closing fastest from the back with ease. Choosing the Asahi Hai FS over the Hanshin JF, she was favorite - hope for the first filly winner in 36 years - but lacked her kick, 4th. Hard to get right, she went straight to the Oka Sho as 5th choice (11th), then was 7th in the NHK Mile C. and 15th in the Swan S. - her early brilliance gone.
2510: A filly who held her own with crop-mates Rey de Oro and Kiseki. Soul Stirring and Admire Miyabi drew the early attention, but her NHK Mile C. win changed that: 2nd choice in an open race, she broke clear from up front with authority. She won the Queen S. that summer. At 4 she was 2nd in the Nakayama Kinen, 4th in the Victoria Mile and 2nd in the Yasuda Kinen, then won the Mainichi Okan as favorite, a force against males. At 5, the year of younger star Almond Eye, she beat her for 2nd in the Yasuda Kinen and was 3rd behind her in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). In her farewell Arima Kinen, her longest race, she led boldly as always (14th).
2511: A character who blasts out of the gate and races far clear. 3rd in the Radio Nikkei Sho at 3, winless after, he restarted in allowances, won 2 classes in summer at 4, then the Fukushima Kinen, followed by the Kokura Daishoten and Sekiya Kinen - 3 graded wins. A fan favorite for his all-out front-running at middle trips on turf.
2512: Winning 3 straight in summer at 3 to open class, he was fancied in graded races but 5th in the Kokura Daishoten was his best. Falling short in open races, he finally won at that level at 5 in the Naruo Kinen, breaking clear from up front in a course-record 1:57.2.
2513: After 35 allowance races, he reached open class in autumn at 5 and won his first graded race, the March S., as 8th choice, leading all the way and laughing off favorite Buster Type. He won the Marine S. (OP) that summer.
2514: Improving at 5, 2nd in the CBC Sho and Hanshin C., he won the Silk Road S. the next year as 2nd choice, tracking in 3rd and passing leader Laurel Veloce to win by 1.5 lengths - a first graded win at 6 in only his 16th race, after injuries. Slow to win after, he won the Silk Road S. again at 7.
2515: Winner of the Teio Sho at 4, Kawasaki Kinen and JBC Classic at 5 - a 2016-2019 dirt star. He won his first graded race, the Hyogo Championship, in spring at 3, then was 2nd in the Japan Dirt Derby, Leopard S. and Radio Nippon Sho (OP), and won the Hakusan Daishoten and Urawa Kinen. At 4 he won the Nagoya Daishoten, then the Teio Sho as 6th choice behind Awardee, Apollo Kentucky and Sound True, charging from the back to crush them - a star born. 2nd in the JBC Classic and 4th in the Champions C., he led all the way in the Kawasaki Kinen at 5 for a 2nd G1. Favorite defending the Teio Sho, he was 2nd to Gold Dream, then won the Nippon TV Hai and the JBC Classic, beating Sunrise Soar and Omega Perfume for a 3rd G1. At 6, 2nd in the Kawasaki Kinen, he was scratched from the Dubai World Cup when unwell; back in autumn he won the Urawa Kinen easily. After an 8th and 6th, he was last choice of 16 in the February S. at 7, yet ran 2nd, then 2nd in the Kashiwa Kinen. 6th in the Teio Sho, after a break and stable move, his best was 5th in the JBC Classic at 8; injured after the February S. at 9, he retired to stud.
2516: He beat favorite Marialite in his first graded race, the Meguro Kinen. A stayer who won allowances at 2300-2400m, he won the Osaka-Hamburg C. (OP) as favorite, then was 3rd choice in the Meguro Kinen behind Marialite and Touching Speech; from midfield he swung wide and caught Marialite on the rail by a neck. A fracture meant a long break; back a year later in the same race, he was 4th and retired.
2517: An unusual record: at 3 he won the UAE Derby, then ran in the US Triple Crown - 9th in the Kentucky Derby, 5th of 6 in the Preakness, but 3rd in the Belmont. Back home he was 3rd in the Brazil C. (OP) and 9th in the Champions C. At 4, 8th in the Dubai World Cup, 4th in the Brilliant S. and 5th in the Brazil C. (both OP), he retired.
2518: He won the Shinzan Kinen early at 3, then a fracture cost him about 2 years. Back late at 4, he won a 16-million race and the Rokko S. (OP); late at 5 he was 2nd in the Chukyo Kinen and 3rd in the Keisei Hai AH, then won the Fuji S. as 2nd choice behind Air Spinel, tracking in 2nd and holding everyone off.
2519: Blooming at 5, he won the Tokai S., then was 3rd as 7th choice in the February S. 2nd in the Antares S., he won the Heian S., a dirt force; 3rd choice in the Teio Sho and Nambu Hai, he was 6th and 4th. In the Champions C. he held 3rd from up front as a longshot. From 6 he slumped, rarely in the top five, winless for over 2.5 years.
2520: Named after the Beatles song "A Day in the Life." 3rd in the Keisei Hai and Yayoi Sho, he was beaten badly in the Satsuki Sho and restarted in allowances. After a long struggle he won 2 classes at 5, back to open class, and won the Niigata Kinen, swinging wide from last and grinding down favorite Albert Dock.
2521: Winner of 5 dirt G1s by spring at 6, a leader of dirt racing in 2017-2019. Unbeaten in 3, 2nd in his first graded race, the Hyogo Championship, he won the Unicorn S., catching gritty leader and favorite Strong Barows. Favorite in the Japan Dirt Derby, he was 3rd; 2nd choice in the Champions C., he faded to 12th. But at 4, never out of the top two at Tokyo 1600m, he won the February S. from midfield, his long-sought G1. A dry spell ended with a surge from the Champions C. - the 3rd horse to sweep both JRA dirt G1s in a year. At 5 he won the Kashiwa Kinen and Teio Sho, 2nd in every other race. At 6, 2nd in the February S., he won the Kashiwa Kinen again, then lost narrowly to 3yo star Chrysoberyl in the Champions C., still the senior leader. At 7, fading with an unplaced run, he was 2nd to Chuwa Wizard in the Champions C., ahead of Chrysoberyl - revenge.
2522: Brother of 2-time Victoria Mile winner Verxina, sister of Shuka Sho winner Vivlos - a blue-blooded family owned by ex-baseball player Kazuhiro Sasaki. He won the Japan Cup at 5. Missing the classics, he won 3 allowances in autumn at 3, then the Hanshin Daishoten at 4, and was 3rd to Kitasan Black as 3rd choice in the Tenno Sho (Spring), his first G1. He won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai and was 3rd to Kitasan Black again in the Japan Cup. At 5, 2nd in the Hanshin Daishoten and to Kitasan Black in the Tenno Sho (Spring), ahead of Satono Diamond. In his 2nd Japan Cup, 5th choice behind Kitasan Black and younger Derby winner Rey de Oro, he tracked Kitasan Black and took over in the last 100m to win. 3rd in the Arima Kinen, at 6 he was 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and 3rd in the Arima Kinen again. At 7 he raced abroad: 2nd in the Dubai Sheema Classic, 6th in the King George like his sire Heart's Cry, and 8th in the International S., the first Japanese runner since Zenno Rob Roy. In a 4th Arima Kinen, at a career-long 135.4 to 1, he ran on under old partner Fukunaga for 6th and retired.
2523: Winner of the Fairy S., the first fillies' graded race of the year, leading all the way as 3rd choice. In a strong crop with Major Emblem and Jeweler, she was 9th in the Oka Sho, then turned to dirt, 2nd in the Onuma S. (OP) and 3rd behind Amour Briller in the Breeders' Gold C.
2524: A Roses in May runner from Mombetsu who won the Hyogo Junior GP, then was 3rd against JRA horses in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun.
2525: The 2016 2yo champion. 2nd on debut at Sapporo, he won a Nakayama maiden and the Begonia Sho, then as 6th choice in a strong Asahi Hai FS unleashed a Deep Impact-like kick to win - jockey Shii's first G1 since the 2010 Takamatsunomiya Kinen (Kinshasa no Kiseki). Favorite in the Spring S. at 3, he was 4th, then 11th in the Satsuki Sho. Winless in graded races since, he won the Tomoe Sho (OP) and was 2nd in the Capital S. (OP).
2526: Winning his 3rd start, steady, he won the Spring S. in his 6th race with a powerful finish from midfield. A "grey Stay Gold colt" like Gold Ship, he was expected to shine, but was 8th in the Satsuki Sho and 15th in the Derby. Jockey Matsuoka still rated him; in autumn he broke clear from up front to win the Fukushima Kinen. Older he won the Nakayama Kinen, but flopped in G1s like the Osaka Hai and Mile CS. At 5 he won the Nakayama Kimpai and Nakayama Kinen - 5 graded wins - then the QEII Cup in Hong Kong, beating crop-mates Lys Gracieux and Deirdre. Unplaced in the All Comers and Tenno Sho (Autumn), he won a fierce duel in the Hong Kong Cup - Hong Kong G1s in spring and autumn. At 6, defending the Hong Kong Cup, he burst clear from midfield but was caught by fellow Japanese Normcore, 2nd.
2527: Out of Fortune Word, a filly who ran in the Asahi Hai FS. Hoped to shine on turf, he stalled in 3 races, then won 5 straight on dirt and his first graded race, the Heian S. A chip fracture cost a year; back in the Antares S. at 2.2, he moved up at the 4th turn and pulled clear. Favorite in the Heian S. and Sirius S., he was 5th and 11th.
2528: A late-blooming Neo Universe colt: 6 starts to win, 20 to pass the 10-million class. Then he bloomed, winning 2 to open class and the Niigata Daishoten. A tendon injury cost 2 years; back at 7 he lost badly, and from 8 has raced on dirt, out of the top five but for a 2nd in the Azuma Kofuji Sho.
2529: A Manhattan Cafe colt with a sharp kick from up front; half-brother of Hanshin Himba S. winner Smart Layer. Emerging with a 4th in the Mainichi Hai, he was 2nd choice in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai and narrowly caught favorite Satono Chronicle from midfield, earning a Derby spot - but a fracture of the right radius was found, and he had to rest.
2530: He won 3 straight at 3 incl. the Aoba Sho, a Derby fancy. Winning a maiden only in March at 3 and a 5-million race easily, he was Aoba Sho favorite and surged from last through the 3rd-4th turns, leaving everyone behind. Derby favorite, he couldn't catch Rey de Oro and Suave Richard, 3rd. Leg trouble meant 2 years off; with a 2019 return planned, he broke his pelvis and retired without racing again.
2531: By imported sire Harbinger, she won the QEII Cup at 3 - with crop-mates Deirdre and Persian Knight, 3 G1 winners for Harbinger in a year. Winning a maiden at 3, she won a 5-million race and the Flora S. as 12th choice, charging from midfield. 6th choice in the Oaks, she was 2nd to Soul Stirring, well clear of 3rd. 7th in the Rose S. and 3rd in the Shuka Sho, she won a star-studded QEII Cup - Vivlos, Mikki Queen, Rouge Buck, Shuka Sho winner Deirdre - racing forward and holding off Mikki Queen. At 4 she was 6th in the Dubai Sheema Classic, 3rd in the Sapporo Kinen, then 3rd as favorite in the QEII Cup behind Lys Gracieux.
2532: A Deep Sky colt who won the 2017 Antares S. Slow to open class, he was 2nd as 12th choice in the Tokai S. at 5, won the Aldebaran S. (OP), was 4th in the Nagoya Daishoten, then won the Antares S.
2533: From the first crop of Jo Cappuccino, NHK Mile C. winner as 10th choice. 5th in the Arlington C. and 6th in the Falcon S., he won the NZT as 12th choice from a handy spot, with 8th choice Mason Junior 2nd from the front - a big upset. Bidding to match his sire in the NHK Mile C., he was 12th, then last in the Derby and Mile CS.
2534: A big colt, hyped from his debut and popular for his distinctive face, but slow to rise and missing the classics. Winning steadily when older, he reached open class, and at 5 in the Lord Derby CT tracked in 2nd and held off Campbell Junior by half a length - his first graded win.
2535: Needing 7 starts to win, he improved with each drop in trip, quickly reaching open class in turf sprints. 2nd in his first graded race, the Silk Road S., after leading briefly, he went to the Takamatsunomiya Kinen; with Oka Sho winner Let's Go Donki and Sprinters S. winner Red Falx fancied, he alone found another gear and won. Then he faded: 4th as favorite in the Hakodate Sprint S., 11th as 3rd choice in the Sprinters S., far back in the Swan S. At 5, 2nd in the Silk Road S., 6th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, he won the Hakodate Sprint S. At 6, 15th in the Silk Road S., he was 2nd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and 3rd in the CBC Sho, then unplaced. At 7 an occasional 5th; at 8, 3rd in the Keeneland C., he retired to stud after the Hanshin C.
2536: A blueblood named after a rare dessert wine. Unwell, he debuted only in June at 3, then rose steadily and was 2nd as 2nd choice in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai at 4, his first graded race. He won the Nikkei Sho over Arima Kinen winner Gold Actor and Satsuki winner Dee Majesty - a spring star. 9th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), tired, he was 4th as 2nd choice in the Takarazuka Kinen. Unplaced in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), Japan Cup and Arima Kinen, at 6 he won the AJCC and Hanshin Daishoten, but fractured a leg after a workout and was put down.
2537: A filly who ran in the Satsuki Sho as favorite - a unique record. Debuting in January at 3, she won her debut by 9 lengths, the Tsubaki Sho and the Flower C. by 5, all from up front with speed. Skipping the fillies' classics, she went for the Satsuki Sho, bidding to be the first filly winner in 69 years, but didn't quicken, 7th. 6th in the Rose S., she was 13th as 2nd choice in the Shuka Sho.
2538: A Victoire Pisa sprinter. After winning his debut and the Kurumi Sho, he was 4th as 2nd choice in the Keio Hai 2yo S. - a strong race, won by later Asahi Hai runner-up Mondo Cannon with later Oka Sho winner Reine Minoru 2nd - and won the Falcon S. the next year. Laminitis followed, and he died that November; the Falcon S. was his last race.
2539: A quirky Lohengrin filly with a sharp kick. She won the Fillies' Revue in her 4th start and closed for 4th in the Oka Sho, dispelling stamina doubts. Favorite in the NHK Mile C., she lacked her kick, 17th.
2540: A rare Fastnet Rock runner in Japan, with big weight swings. 502kg at his debut at 3, he grew to 522kg in summer at 4 and won fast to open class. +10kg, he was 14th in the Keihan Hai; -8kg the next year, he won the Ocean S. 3rd choice in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen at +14kg, he was 10th.
2541: Steady and versatile, but long breaks kept him from winning much. In his first graded race, the Hankyu Hai, his 21st start, he closed brilliantly to win as 7th choice.
2542: A dirt sprint closer with a brilliant finish. Often falling short from the back, he reached open class in summer at 4 and was 4th in the Champions C. He won the Negishi S. as favorite, then was 3rd as favorite in the February S. 5th in Dubai's Godolphin Mile, he has been 2nd in the Procyon S. and 4th in the Nambu Hai since.
2543: A Bago colt who won the Keisei Hai with a steady finish; 2nd to later Derby winner Rey de Oro in the Habotan Sho. 6th as 3rd choice in the Yayoi Sho and 14th as 16th choice in the Satsuki Sho, he suffered a suspensory injury and never returned, retired in summer at 4.
2544: A Black Tide filly like Kitasan Black. She won the Fairy S. in her 3rd start as 10th choice with the fastest finish, and the Anemone S. too, but her kick misfired in the Oka Sho.
2545: Named after the son of an acquaintance of his owner. A mudlark, he was 2nd to later Satsuki Sho winner Al Ain in the Senryo Sho, then won the Shinzan Kinen on heavy ground with a finish from another dimension - his sire Reach the Crown's first graded winner. 14th in the NHK Mile C. and 12th in the Derby, he ran steadily in open races without winning, then dropped to win the Tarumi S. (16M). 8th in the Kokura Kinen, he raced in open and listed races without a win, switched to dirt at 8, and moved to local racing after the Sobu S. (OP) at 9.
2546: Needing 21 starts to reach open class, he then blossomed, 3rd in a strong All Comers, and won the Nakayama Kimpai at 6. A true Stay Gold, he loved Nakayama.
2547: A 2017 3yo dirt force. Last (16th) in a turf debut, he switched to dirt and was nearly always top two, winning through the classes. In his first open race, the Hyogo Championship, he burst clear from a handy spot, then was 3rd in the G1 Japan Dirt Derby. Perhaps tired, he was 12th in the Leopard S., 4th in the Hakusan Daishoten and 11th in the Miyako S.
2548: Unable to pass the 10-million class with the JRA by 5, he blossomed after moving to Hyogo: 4 quick wins, 6th in the Kurofune Sho, the Tokai Oka Sho (OP), then the Kakitsubata Kinen. 2nd choice behind hot JRA favorite Chocolat Blanc, he led all the way and pulled away with the fastest finish.
2549: Owned, like Kitasan Black, by singer Saburo Kitajima (via his office, Ono Shoji). A dirt sprinter at 1200-1400m, he won allowances only at 5, then placed in open races, and won the Tokyo Sprint as favorite, leading and holding on by a head.
2550: A Normandy Thoroughbred Racing club horse at just 19,000 yen a share - 7.6 million yen for 400 shares - who earned over 100 million yen, winning the Kurofune Sho and Valentine S. (OP). Winning allowances in summer at 4, 12th in the Musashino S., he kept placing in open races, then at 5 won the Valentine S. and Kurofune Sho, and was 5th in the G1 Kashiwa Kinen.
2551: Slow through allowances, he then surged: fresh into open class, he went straight to the G1 Kawasaki Kinen and won as 5th choice, leading all the way and pulling clear in the straight. Winless for a while, at 6 he won the Urawa Kinen by 4 lengths over 3yo Grimm, on a graded winning streak, and stars Chrysolite and Apollo Kentucky.
2552: By Gold Allure, from a dirt family - her dam's brother Testa Matta won the February S. and Japan Dirt Derby. Improving late at 3, she won 2 allowances, then the TCK Jo-o Hai and Empress Hai early at 4. In autumn she was 4th as 3rd choice in the JBC Ladies' Classic.
2553: A record-setting mare: 2 Arcs, 3 King Georges, and the Arc and BC Turf in the same year. At 3 she won the English and Irish Oaks, romped in the King George and won the Arc as favorite, Cartier Horse of the Year. Injured at 4, she returned in the G3 September S., then won a 2nd Arc (7th horse to do so) and the BC Turf - the first to win both in a year. At 5 she won the King George and bid for a 3rd Arc, but was 2nd to Waldgeist. At 6 she won a 3rd King George, then in her farewell Arc finished 6th, her first time out of the top three. Her first foal (by Kingman) came in 2022, and a filly by Dubawi in 2023.
2554: A late-blooming sprinter in open class at 7, graded winner at 9 in the Keeneland C. After 2 wins from debut, leg trouble meant a long break; gelded, he returned in summer at 5, steadily placing in allowances. From 7 he ran in the Keeneland C. 3 years running and won at the 3rd try at 9, closing brilliantly from last as 12th of 13.
2555: He won the Ibis Summer Dash at 7, then was 2nd in the Centaur S. - Summer Sprint Series champion. Long in allowances, he won the 10-million class only at 7, then stepped up from the 16-million class to win the Ibis Summer Dash as 8th choice, unleashing a powerful late surge from midfield.
2556: He won the Naruo Kinen at 6. Debuting late in spring at 3, he reached open class in just 7 starts over 3 years, always fancied. 3rd choice in the Naruo Kinen, his 2nd open race, he led as usual, saved energy, and held off favorite Smart Layer by a neck.
2557: A late-blooming middle-distance horse who won the Hakodate Kinen at 6. Winning allowances at 5 so strongly that he was 2nd choice in his first open race, the Tanabata Sho (8th), he then placed steadily: 5th Niigata Kinen, 4th AJCC, 5th Kinko Sho. In the Hakodate Kinen he crept up from midfield on the back straight, joined the leaders at the 4th turn and burst clear.
2558: Blooming at 6, he was 2nd in his first graded race, the Nakayama Kinen, ahead of favored Ambitious and Real Steel. 13th in the G1 Osaka Hai and 9th in the Hakodate Kinen, he was transformed in the Sapporo Kinen, closing sharply from midfield. He tried the Tenno Sho (Autumn), won by his uncle Sakura Chitose O, raising "Sakura" hopes, but was 8th. 3rd in the Nikkei Sho 2 years running, he never won again and retired to stud at 8.
2559: After 45 starts, he became a graded winner at 6 in the Sirius S. Though he ran in the Sapporo 2yo S. and Kikuka Sho, he was a dirt specialist. Winning the Aso S. and Radio Nippon Sho (both OP) at 5, he moved to dirt graded races but never made the top five - until the Sirius S. (G3), where as 11th choice he swept past the leaders from midfield for a stunning upset.
2560: Debuting in graded races at 5 in summer 2017, he topped the Summer Mile Series at once. After 3 allowance wins at 4 he struggled in open class (14th in the Shin'etsu S.), then won the Tanigawadake S. (OP) when out of favor, the Paradise S. (OP), and the Chukyo Kinen by 2.5 lengths - 3 straight. 2nd in the Sekiya Kinen, he shared the series title with Gran Silk.
2561: A middle-distance horse at about 2000m who races forward and holds on. Winning the 10-million class at 5, he stepped up for the Tanabata Sho (6th), then won the Kokura Kinen as 4th choice on a light weight, beating favored Strong Titan and San Martin, and the Niigata Kinen next - 2017 Summer 2000 Series champion.
2562: After 23 allowance starts, he thrived in open class: 4th in his first graded race, the Sirius S., he won the Brazil C. and Betelgeuse S. (both OP), was 4th in the G1 Kawasaki Kinen, then won the Mercury C. as favorite, catching joint fancy Pionero by a neck. At 6 he won it again, pulling away from rival Phoenix Mark. At 7 he won the Kawasaki Kinen, beating G1 winners Katy Brave, All Blush and Apollo Kentucky for his long-sought G1.
2563: He won the Summer Champion in summer at 5. It took 2.5 years to reach open class, rising steadily and almost never out of the top five. 5th in the Akhal-Teke S. (OP), he won the Summer Champion as 2nd choice from up front, holding off Tamuro Miracle.
2564: At 5 he won the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and Sprinters S., ruling the sprints. In allowances at 3-4 but always fancied, he reached open class in summer at 4 and was favorite in the Kitakyushu Kinen (5th), then won the Centaur S. At 5 he won the Silk Road S. and Takamatsunomiya Kinen, then was 4th in Hong Kong's Chairman's Sprint Prize (G1). He won the Centaur S. as favorite, then the Sprinters S. as favorite from midfield, catching Love Kampu and Line Spirit - a spring-autumn sprint G1 double.
2565: He won 3 classes early at 4 and the Ritto S. (OP) - 4 straight - then was favorite in his first graded race, the Cluster C., 3rd behind local Bulldog Boss. In the Oval Sprint he led all the way, holding off Bulldog Boss for revenge.
2566: A dirt specialist of Gold Allure's line. Debuting late at 2, he won a 5-million race, made the top five in the Fukuryu S. and Hosu S. (both OP), then won the Unicorn S. as 2nd choice, charging wide from the back. Favorite in the G1 Japan Dirt Derby, he was 6th. Blooming at 4, he was 2nd in the Negishi S., 4th in the February S., then won 2 open races and the Musashino S. 6th in the Champions C. and 7th in the February S., he won the Nambu Hai at 5, breaking clear early from a handy spot past Gold Dream and Arctos. At 6, 3rd in the February S. and Kashiwa Kinen, he won the Procyon S. charging wide, was 4th defending the Nambu Hai, won the Musashino S., then was 12th in the Champions C. Fading at 7 (11th, 7th, 7th), he was 2nd in the JBC Sprint and closed sharply for 5th in the Champions C. Unplaced at 8, he went to stud after the Champions C.
2567: Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Radio Nikkei Sho, though with long gaps: a debut at 2, a 5-million win in May at 3, the Radio Nikkei Sho in July. Leg trouble scrapped his Kikuka Sho plan; back in November, 3rd choice in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai behind Suave Richard and Albert, he was 3rd from a handy spot. At 4 he won the Nakayama Kimpai, then injury; 7th in the Niigata Kinen after 8 months off, he rested long again. Back after 15 months, he won the December S. (L) at 5, then a tendon injury; returning at 7, he finished far back and retired with tendon trouble again - a horse plagued by injury.
2568: A 2017 3yo dirt star. Winning a 5-million race in spring, he won the Hosu S. (OP) as last choice of 10, in a tight finish over favored Sunrise Nova. 8th in the Japan Dirt Derby, he won the Leopard S. as 11th choice - another shock - with his gritty forward running. He won the Radio Nippon Sho (OP) at 5, and moved to local racing at 10.
2569: A 2017 Kikuka Sho fancy. Far from the classics in spring, he stepped up to win the St. Lite Kinen in autumn, swooping past Satsuki Sho winner Al Ain. 3rd choice in a Kikuka Sho without Derby winner Rey de Oro, he couldn't use his kick on rain-soaked ground, 6th. At 4 he was 2nd in the AJCC, 5th in the Osaka Hai and Japan Cup. At 5, on the G3 circuit, he won the Tanabata Sho, 2nd in the All Comers and 3rd in the Fukushima Kinen; at 6 he won the Nikkei Sho and was 3rd to Fierement in the Tenno Sho (Spring). 5th as favorite in the All Comers, he was 7th in the Japan Cup.
2570: A middle-distance dirt horse, 3rd in the Unicorn S. and 2nd in the Japan Dirt Derby at 3, and 2nd in the Musashino S. that autumn. At 5, after a 2nd in the Jinsen S.
