(OP), he led all the way in the Nagoya Daishoten as hot favorite, then won the Heian S., and was 3rd in the JBC Classic and Champions C.
2571: Her grand-dam was 1997 2-classic filly Cheers Grace; she was the family's first graded winner. Struggling in allowances, she blossomed mid-4, passing 3 classes in a row. Beaten badly in open class, she won the Breeders' Gold C. in her 4th try, leading early in the straight and holding off favorite Queen Mambo.
2572: Winning 3 classes in a row in summer at 4, he won the Kitakyushu Kinen, tracking in 2nd from a fine start and breaking clear - 4 straight wins and his first graded win, with longshots 2nd and 3rd for a trifecta over 1 million yen. 4th choice in the Sprinters S., he faded to 15th. At 5 he won the Hankyu Hai. After an 18th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and 9th in the Hakodate Sprint S., he was 3rd as 11th choice in the Keihan Hai, then led all the way on heavy ground in the Hanshin C. as 11th choice, a 3rd graded win. At 6, 6th defending the Hankyu Hai and 4th in the Hanshin Himba S., he retired.
2573: Without a graded win, she won the G1 Victoria Mile as 8th choice - a finish that works on testing ground. Her first graded race came when older: in the Hanshin Himba S. on heavy going she held 3rd from up front, well clear of 4th behind Mikki Queen. In the Victoria Mile on soft ground she held 3rd again; as favorites Mikki Queen and Rouge Buck sank, 3 longshots filled the places (trifecta 910,000 yen). A year later, in another rain-softened Victoria Mile, she won a straight duel with Red Avance from midfield and held off favorite Lys Gracieux by a nose - her first graded win a G1. 6th against males in the Mile CS.
2574: 3rd in the Fantasy S. at 2, talented early. 2nd in the Anemone S. (OP) at 3, she was 6th in the Oka Sho as 14th choice, closing fastest from the back, then 4th in the Oaks as 9th choice, again fastest. In autumn she won a 10-million race and the Shion S., then the Shuka Sho as 3rd choice with an otherworldly finish from the back - a G1. Older, 3rd in the Dubai Turf, she won the Queen S. and Fuchu Himba S., and was 2nd in the Hong Kong Cup. At 5 she toured: 4th in the Dubai Turf, 6th in Hong Kong's QEII Cup, 6th in England's Prince of Wales's S., then won the Nassau S., 4th in the Irish Champion S. and 3rd in the Champion S. In Hong Kong's Vase she closed too late, 4th. With Mozu Katchan and Persian Knight, a flagship of import sire Harbinger.
2575: A summer improver who won a 5-million race at 3, then the Rose S. as 8th choice, a Shuka Sho fancy. A sharp closer, she swept past Satsuki Sho runner Fandina and Oaks runner-up Mozu Katchan in the Rose S., then was 4th in the Shuka Sho. Struggling at 4, she soared after switching to dirt in summer: 3rd in the Sparking Lady C., then the Breeders' Gold C., and 2nd as favorite in the G1 JBC Ladies' Classic.
2576: Winner of the Kanto Oaks and Ladies' Prelude, a force among dirt fillies. Winning 2 to open class in spring at 3, she was 3rd in the Hyogo Championship, then won the Kanto Oaks as favorite by 4 lengths. 12th on turf in the Rose S., she won the Ladies' Prelude on dirt by 8 lengths. At 4 she was 2nd in the Marine C. and Heian S., 3rd in the Breeders' Gold C., and 4th as 2nd choice, a length behind Ange Desir, in the JBC Ladies' Classic.
2577: Very strong in fillies' dirt races: the JBC Ladies' Classic and 3 graded wins. On turf at first, she switched to dirt after a 13th in the Fillies' Revue at 3 and was 2nd at once in the Kanto Oaks. She won the Sparking Lady C. as 2nd choice from a handy spot, then was 3rd in the Ladies' Prelude and 2nd in the Queen Sho. At 4 she timed her run perfectly to win the Empress Hai, then led for the first time to win the Marine C. 4th in the Ladies' Prelude, she won the JBC Ladies' Classic as 6th choice by a head after a straight duel with favorite Rabbit Run.
2578: Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Asahi Hai FS, a leader of the 2017 2yo crop. He won his debut easily from a handy spot, then after 3.5 months off won the Saudi Arabia Royal C., 2nd choice behind Lemaire's Stelvio. Favorite in the Asahi Hai FS, from the rail he raced forward and closed fastest to beat Stelvio by 3.5 lengths in 1:33.3, the fastest since the race moved to Hanshin in 2014. Top classic fancy, he won the Yayoi Sho, then missed the Satsuki Sho with leg trouble. Hot Derby favorite over Satsuki winner Epoca d'Oro and unbeaten Blast Onepiece, he couldn't hold on from up front, 6th. Back at 4 in the Kinko Sho against G1 winners Al Ain, Persian Knight and Lys Gracieux, he won easily, then the Milers C. In the Yasuda Kinen, billed vs. Triple Crown filly Almond Eye, trouble left her 3rd and him last. He was 2nd to her in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 2nd in the Mile CS. At 5, 3rd in Hong Kong's QE S., 13th in the Yasuda Kinen, 4th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he was 4th in the Hong Kong Cup as fellow Japanese Normcore and Win Bright ran 1-2.
2579: He won the Hakodate 2yo S. as favorite, a 2017 2yo name. Ridden by Hamanaka from his debut, he won a maiden easily, then caught leader Win Gelbera from a handy spot in the Hakodate 2yo S. 2nd to Tower of London in the Keio Hai 2yo S., he raced forward like Danon Premium in the Asahi Hai FS but faded, perhaps at his limit, 7th.
2580: US-bred, by Stormy Atlantic. Winning his 3rd start by a distance, he won the Kokura 2yo S. under Yutaka Take, sitting 2nd-3rd and breaking clear early. 3rd to Tower of London in the Keio Hai 2yo S. He gave his sire a first graded win.
2581: The 2018 Derby winner, who gave Yuichi Fukunaga his long-sought Derby. Highly rated, he won his debut, the Nojigiku S. (OP) and Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. At 3 he was 2nd to 2yo champion Danon Premium in the Yayoi Sho; with Danon Premium out, he was Satsuki Sho favorite but was outmaneuvered by the leaders and closed in vain, 7th. With Danon Premium back for the Derby, he was 5th choice, but moved up early, broke clear and held off Satsuki winner Epoca d'Oro by half a length - Fukunaga's bold ride paid off. He won the Kobe Shimbun Hai, then rested, unwell, instead of the Tenno Sho (Autumn). At 4 he was 3rd in the Osaka Hai, 4th in the Sapporo Kinen, 5th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 3rd in the Japan Cup. At 5 he raced only twice; at 6, 5th in the Kyoto Kinen, then 12th, 6th and last (18th) in the Japan Cup. Falling ill, he was treated intensively but died suddenly of multiple organ failure at the end of the year.
2582: Brother of Derby and Tenno Sho (Autumn) winner Rey de Oro, said to be even more gifted. He won his debut at 1.2, but a fracture followed and a long break. Back in May at 3, he won 2 classes and was 2nd in his first graded race, the St. Lite Kinen. After a dry spell he won the Epsom C. at 4, then closed powerfully for 2nd in the Fuji S., but was 15th in the Mile CS. 3rd in the Lord Derby CT, then beaten badly, he retired.
2583: From Lord Kanaloa's first crop, his first male G1 winner. 2nd to Danon Premium in the Saudi Arabia Royal C. and Asahi Hai FS, he was among his crop's best. At 3 he won the Spring S.; 2nd choice in the Satsuki Sho, he couldn't catch the leaders, 4th, then 8th in the Derby, ending his classic bid. Against older horses he was 2nd in the Mainichi Okan with a sharp finish from midfield. In the Mile CS, with Yasuda Kinen winner Mozu Ascot, Mainichi Okan winner Aerolithe and defending champion Persian Knight, he was 5th choice, best of the 3yos, broke clear from up front and held off Persian Knight. Later 3rd in the Nakayama Kinen at 4 and 2nd in the Keio Hai SC and Swan S. at 5, he retired injured after the Kyoto Kimpai at 7; meant to be a riding horse, he later went to stud.
2584: A new dirt star who, under Mirco Demuro, won 3 straight G1s: Japan Dirt Derby, Mile CS Nambu Hai and Champions C. He won his debut easily as favorite, the Platanus Sho at 1.4, and, unbeaten, the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun at 1.8, moving up at the 4th turn and winning without the whip. At 3 he won the Unicorn S. easily, the Japan Dirt Derby and the Nambu Hai, beating veteran Gold Dream - dirt king at 3. Favorite at 1.9 in the Champions C., he won easily, following Almond Eye's Japan Cup the week before - the 3yo crop's strength. Leg trouble kept him out all of 2019; back in spring 2020, 5th in the Kashiwa Kinen and 10th in the Teio Sho, he retired.
2585: After a debut win he won the Kikyo S. (OP) and Keio Hai 2yo S., a crop leader, and was 2nd choice with Danon Premium in the Asahi Hai FS (3rd). At 3 he won the Arlington C., then was NHK Mile C. favorite but trapped in the straight, 12th. Stronger at 4, he turned to sprints: he won the Keio Hai SC, was 3rd in the Hakodate Sprint S. and 2nd in the Keeneland C., won the Centaur S. easily, then the Sprinters S., near joint favorite with Danon Smash, with a late swoop. At 5, 3rd in the Ocean S., he was 12th as favorite in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and 8th as favorite in the Keio Hai SC; in the Hong Kong Sprint, as Danon Smash won brilliantly, he was 13th of 14.
2586: From the first crop of Triple Crown winner Orfevre, she gave him a quick graded win. Ridden by Lemaire from her debut, she won it as heavy favorite, then the Sapporo 2yo S. as favorite at 3.0, creeping up wide through the 3rd-4th turns and catching Fast Approach. 9th as favorite in the Hanshin JF - can she spark an Orfevre boom?
2587: A hope from Orfevre's first crop, she won the Osaka Hai and became the 4th to win the QEII Cup twice, giving her sire big titles. After easy wins in her debut and the Artemis S., she won the Hanshin JF with an arrow-like finish, beating Orfevre's early star Rock This Town - the best filly of her crop. At 3 a stronger rival arrived: Almond Eye, from Lord Kanaloa's first crop. Favorite in the Oka Sho, she was 2nd to her, 3rd in the Oaks well beaten, and out of the top three in the Shuka Sho as Almond Eye won the Triple Crown. Still a crop leader, she was 2nd against males in the Nakayama Kinen at 4, 4th as favorite in the Victoria Mile, then won the QEII Cup over younger Oaks winner Loves Only You and Shuka Sho winner Chrono Genesis. 2nd in the Hong Kong Vase behind Glory Vase - a Japanese 1-2. At 5, 2nd in the Nakayama Kinen, she won the Osaka Hai over Chrono Genesis and Danon Kingly for a 3rd G1. 6th in the Takarazuka Kinen and 3rd in the Sapporo Kinen, she won the QEII Cup again as favorite for a 4th G1 - ridden by Lemaire, Almond Eye's regular jockey, who led early in the straight and, sure "she is strong," never let anyone past.
2588: Her name means "the ultimate normal." Unbeaten in 2 in summer at 2, a fracture then cost a long break. Back in spring at 3, 3rd in the Flower C. and Flora S., she won the Shion S. Skipping the Shuka Sho, tired, she was 2nd choice in the QEII Cup but faded from a handy spot, 5th. At 4, favorite in the Aichi Hai (2nd) and Nakayama Himba S. (7th), she was 5th choice in the Victoria Mile behind Lucky Lilac, Primo Scene, Aerolithe and Red Orca, then burst clear from midfield in a hot pace to win in a record 1:30.5. Another fracture; back in autumn she won the Fuji S., then was 4th in the Hong Kong Mile. At 5 she was 3rd to Almond Eye in the Victoria Mile, then won the Sapporo Kinen over Lucky Lilac and Persian Knight. In Hong Kong with Win Bright and Danon Premium, she charged wide from the back to win the Hong Kong Cup, a 2nd G1.
2589: The mare who dominated 2018-2020, hailed the best in training. At 3 she became the 5th fillies' Triple Crown winner, then raced only in G1s, winning a JRA-record 9 turf G1s - the star who sent her sire, new stallion Lord Kanaloa, soaring. She won the Shinzan Kinen in January at 3, then went straight to the Oka Sho; unbeaten 2yo queen Lucky Lilac was favored, but she charged from the back to steal the show. Oaks favorite at 1.7, she broke clear from handy and won with an otherworldly finish. Despite going straight to the Shuka Sho, she was 1.3 favorite and won from midfield as if the others had stopped - the Triple Crown. Skipping the QEII Cup for the Japan Cup, at 1.4 she crushed Kikuka winner Kiseki and Osaka Hai winner Suave Richard. In spring she won the Dubai Turf as favorite with the world watching, then, hampered at the start, was 3rd in the Yasuda Kinen with a stunning finish. In autumn she beat younger star Saturnalia easily in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), a 6th G1. A fever ruled out the Hong Kong Cup; in the Arima Kinen she faded, her first time out of the top three. Was she declining? At 5 she won the Victoria Mile by a street - 7 turf G1s, equaling the record - then was 2nd to sprint queen Gran Alegria in the Yasuda Kinen. That autumn she won the Tenno Sho (Autumn) again for an unprecedented 8th G1 - beyond Symboli Rudolf, Deep Impact and Gentildonna. With 2 unbeaten Triple Crown winners, Contrail and Daring Tact, set for the Japan Cup, she chose it as her farewell - the best in training vs. 2 unbeaten Triple Crown winners. The 3 fought out the finish as fans hoped, and the senior star won, setting records for G1 wins and earnings (as of 2020). Her first foal, by Epiphaneia, arrived in 2022, followed by foals by Maurice, Kitasan Black and Equinox - the last hailed as the "15-crown baby." Great things are awaited.
2590: Leg trouble delayed his debut and limited his starts, but he won 5 straight from allowances to the Kochi S. (OP), then was 4th as 6th choice in the G1 Yasuda Kinen and 3rd in the Mainichi Okan. Often fancied but struggling after, he finally won the Chukyo Kinen at 6 as favorite, charging from midfield.
2591: By Meisho Samson, of the Sadler's Wells line - his 3rd flat graded winner. In open class in autumn at 4, she toured fillies' graded races like the Fuchu Himba S. and Aichi Hai, rarely in the top five, then won the Fukushima Himba S. at 5 as 7th choice, charging from the back past fancied Kawakita Enka and Tosen Victory.
2592: Winning 2 allowances at 4 to open class, she kept finishing unplaced in fillies' graded races, then improved at 5: 2nd in the Mermaid S., 5th in the Tanabata Sho. At 6 she won the Aichi Hai as 8th choice from a handy spot, holding off favorite Normcore. 11th in the Nakayama Himba S., she retired.
2593: Running in miles until 3 without success, he turned to sprints, reaching open class at 4 and 2nd in the Hakodate Sprint S. Fancied but beaten, he fell to 10th choice in the Ocean S. at 5 and won, holding on from up front against favored Daimei Fuji and Nac Venus. Winless in the JRA until 9, he moved to local racing and broke a leg at 10, fatally - a tough, long-serving horse.
2594: Out of Kokura 2yo S. winner Cosmo Valenti; full brother of turf-and-dirt sprinter Dream Valentino. In open class in summer at 4, racing at 1400m on dirt, he won the Hyogo Gold T. late at 5. At 6, 4th in the Kakitsubata Kinen, he led all the way in the Sakitama Hai and pulled clear.
2595: The 2017 Kikuka Sho winner who built an era with Satsuki winner Al Ain and Derby winner Rey de Oro. A late summer improver at 3, he was 2nd to Rey de Oro in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, then won the Kikuka Sho by a street through a historic quagmire in torrential rain. After a lean spell, he grew strong late at 4: 3rd in the Mainichi Okan, 3rd to Rey de Oro in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) with Al Ain 4th - all 3 classic winners. 2nd to younger Triple Crown filly Almond Eye in the Japan Cup, at 5 he was 2nd in the Osaka Hai and Takarazuka Kinen, then in the Arc was best of the Japanese, handling Longchamp's tough turf. At 6, with Al Ain and Rey de Oro retired, the last of the trio, he was 2nd in the Takarazuka Kinen and Kyoto Daishoten, 5th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). At 7, 5th in the Kinko Sho, 4th in Hong Kong's QE S., 5th in the Takarazuka Kinen and 3rd in the Kyoto Daishoten, he retired to stud after 10th in the Japan Cup and Arima Kinen.
2596: Little noticed in the classics, he was 2nd in the Kikuka Sho in an upset, a crop leader with Rey de Oro and Kiseki. Older, he won the Kyoto Kinen over Derby winner Rey de Oro and Satsuki winner Al Ain. 3rd in the Hanshin Daishoten and Tenno Sho (Spring) behind Rainbow Line and Cheval Grand, a top stayer. In France he was well beaten in the Prix Foy and Arc, then lost form. Switched to dirt at 6, he was 2nd in the March S. and 3rd in the Antares S., then won the Miyako S. as favorite over Air Almas and Best Touchdown - JRA graded wins on turf and dirt. At 7 he won the Saga Kinen and Nagoya Daishoten, 3rd to T O Keynes in the G1 Teio Sho, and 2nd to Omega Perfume in the Tokyo Daishoten. At 8 he won the Nagoya Daishoten again, then after a 5th, 10th and 5th, retired.
2597: He won the Challenge C. late at 3. 2nd in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, missing the Derby, he was 6th as favorite in the Radio Nikkei Sho, 3rd in the St. Lite Kinen and 10th in the Kikuka Sho on a quagmire. In the Challenge C., under Mirco Demuro, he broke clear from a handy spot and won a duel with Denim and Ruby, ridden by Mirco's brother Cristian. Older, 2nd in the Hanshin Daishoten and Kokura Kinen, he retired without another win.
2598: Unbeaten in 2, he won the Principal S. (OP); 14th in the Derby, he was 4th against older horses in the Mainichi Okan. Falling short in graded races, he won open races like the Capital S., May S. and October S. (L), then the Epsom C. at 6. 2nd to 3yo Salios in the Mainichi Okan, he was 6th as 10th choice in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). Close at 7-8 (4th Milers C. and Mainichi Okan, 2nd Kyoto Kimpai), he retired after the Kyoto Kimpai at 9. All 8 wins came at Tokyo.
2599: 7th in the Oka Sho at 3, 2nd in the Rose S. and top five in the Shuka Sho, she won the Nakayama Himba S. when older, leading at a slow pace and holding off favorite Fronteer Queen. 2nd on the same time in the Fukushima Himba S., she was 14th in the Victoria Mile and last on dirt in the JBC Ladies' Classic.
2600: 2nd in the Tulip Sho, she flopped in the Oka Sho and Oaks and restarted in the 16-million class. In her first open race, the Turquoise S., she emerged from a blanket finish to win. Older, she won the Kyoto Himba S. as favorite and the Hanshin Himba S. - 3 straight graded wins. Little in the Victoria Mile and QEII Cup, she won the Turquoise S. again. At 5, 5th defending the Kyoto Himba S., she retired with a tendon injury to breed.
2601: A new dirt star unbeaten in 3 incl. the Hyogo Junior GP, ridden by Lemaire from the start. He led to win his debut by a huge margin and a 5-million race by 4 lengths, then at 1.1 led again in the Hyogo Junior GP, holding off Aster Sword by a neck. 2nd choice behind Le Vent Se Leve in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun, with 3rd choice Don Fortis, he tracked in 2nd but, perhaps disliking Kawasaki's deep sand or the trip, was 10th.
2602: A sprint leader from 2019 to 2021. A miler at first (5th Asahi Hai FS, 7th NHK Mile C.), he switched to sprints in summer at 3: 2nd in the Keeneland C., then won the Keihan Hai. At 4 he won the Silk Road S., was 4th as favorite in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, won the Keeneland C., and was 3rd as favorite in the Sprinters S. At 5 he won the Ocean S., Keio Hai SC and Centaur S.; 2nd to Gran Alegria's explosive finish in the Sprinters S., he won the Hong Kong Sprint - a G1 at last, abroad. At 6 he won the Takamatsunomiya Kinen in a tight finish, with crop-mate Indy Champ 3rd. 6th in Hong Kong's Chairman's Sprint Prize and 6th as favorite in the Sprinters S., he was 8th in the Hong Kong Sprint after being caught up in another horse's fall.
2603: He won 3 straight incl. the Hokkaido 2yo Yushun, a 2yo dirt force. 3rd on debut, he won a maiden easily under Mirco Demuro, then the Yamaboushi Sho under Yutaka Take. At 1.9 in the Hokkaido 2yo Yushun, he led early from midfield and pulled away. In a strong Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun he closed sharply on Le Vent Se Leve, who swept wide before the 4th turn, losing by a length.
2604: First winner of the Hopeful S., made a G1 in 2017. Winning his 2nd start, he won the Hagi S. with a brilliant late charge, then lost by a head to Grail in the Kyoto 2yo S. Favorite in the new G1, he closed from last with an extraordinary kick. A classic fancy, he was 5th as favorite in the Wakaba S., 10th in the Satsuki Sho, 11th in the Derby and 6th in the Kikuka Sho. At 4 he tried dirt in the Elm S. (6th), then was 2nd as 8th choice in the Musashino S. At 5, 5th in the February S., he won the Marine S. (OP), then the Elm S. as favorite, beating dirt convert Air Spinel and veteran Westerlund - his first graded win since the Hopeful S. 5th as favorite in the Musashino S. and 8th in the Champions C. At 6, 3rd in the Negishi S., then unplaced; at 7, 5th as 15th choice in the February S., he moved to local racing.
2605: A strong miler. She won the Fairy S. early at 3, flopped in the Oka Sho and NHK Mile C., then won the Sekiya Kinen as favorite. Older, she was 2nd in the Lord Derby CT and lost by a neck to Normcore in the Victoria Mile. After a 15th and 11th in autumn, she won the Tokyo Shimbun Hai at 5, then was 8th as 2nd choice in the Victoria Mile.
2606: A late bloomer who won the Miyako S. at 5 and was Champions C. favorite. Winning allowances in spring at 5, he won the Onuma S. and Marine S. (both OP) dominantly, then was 1.5 favorite in his first graded race, the Elm S., 2nd. He won the Miyako S. easily, then as Champions C. favorite lost by a neck to Gold Dream. At 6 he won the Tokai S., but was 12th as 2nd choice in the February S., kept finishing unplaced, and after a 14th in the JBC Classic was found injured.
2607: The first local horse in 7 years to beat JRA horses in the Japan Dirt Derby. Debuting at Mombetsu at 2, he won 3 and was 2nd as 5th choice to Epicharis in the Hokkaido 2yo Yushun, then 4th in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun. Moving to Funabashi, he won the New Year C., Keihin Hai and Tokyo Derby. 5th choice in the Japan Dirt Derby, the top local, he outdueled JRA favorites Sunrise Nova and Tagano Diguo from a handy spot - the first local winner since Magnifica in 2010. 2nd in the Urawa Kinen.
2608: A 2017 2yo name: his half-brother 12 years older was Dream Passport, his uncle Stay Gold. After a debut win as favorite, he won the Niigata 2yo S. as 3rd choice, tracking in 2nd and catching Cordierite. Favorite in the Daily Hai 2yo S., he lacked a kick, 4th; a 6th-choice fancy in a strong Asahi Hai FS, he followed stablemate Danon Premium from gate 2 but was 8th.
2609: A dirt sprinter who won 2 allowances late at 3, then the Uzumasa S. and Chiba S. (both OP). 4th in the Tokyo Sprint, 2nd in the Kakitsubata Kinen and Cluster C., he won the Cluster C. a year later over JRA star Saitas Three Red, with local Love Bullet 2nd - a local 1-2. Two years on, at 7, he won the JBC Sprint as 6th choice, closing fastest of all.
2610: A local horse owned by singer Saburo Kitajima (via Ono Shoji) who won the Tokyo Hai. Debuting in the JRA, he reached open class only at 6; after the Keiyo S. (OP) he kept losing, and moved to Oi at 7. He at once won the After 5 Star Sho, then the Tokyo Hai as 7th choice, and was 5th in his first G1, the JBC Sprint. At 8 he improved further: 2nd in the Tokyo Sprint and Sakitama Hai, 3 straight wins incl. the Tokyo Hai, 3rd in the JBC Sprint. At 9, 9th in the Negishi S., he won the Tokyo Sprint, was 5th in the Kashiwa Kinen and 3rd in the Sakitama Hai, and retired after winning the After 5 Star Sho.
2611: A Mombetsu filly who won the Edelweiss Sho. Winning her debut in summer at 2 and the local Lily Cup, she was narrowly 2nd in the Floral Cup, then won the Edelweiss Sho, tracking in 3rd, spurting early and winning a duel with fellow Hokkaido filly Graviola, far clear of the rest.
2612: An Oi dirt sprinter who raced almost only at Oi; his first graded win was a G1, the JBC Sprint. 4th as a longshot in the Tokyo Sprint at 4, 2nd in it 2 years later, he was 5th in the Tokyo Hai, then won the JBC Sprint as 8th choice with a sharp finish from midfield. In his first JRA race, the Capella S., a crushing 59kg left him 8th.
2613: Reaching open class in January at 4, he then had a long road: 5th Meguro Kinen, 4th Argentina Kyowakoku Hai, 3rd Stayers S. - close but no win, except the Sapporo Nikkei OP at 5. Fading from 6, late at 7 he won the Stayers S. as 6th choice, beating 2015-2017 winner Albert from a handy spot.
2614: By Spiecule, a minority Sunday Silence-line sire with 8 crops, in Korea since 2014 - his leading JRA-local graded winner. Winning allowances in autumn at 4, she was 2nd in the G1 JBC Ladies' Classic, then led all the way in the Queen Sho at 2.0. She won the Ladies' Prelude at 5 and Empress Hai at 6, and at 7 the Breeders' Gold C. and 3rd in the Ladies' Prelude.
2615: He won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai late at 4. 3rd in the Keisei Hai and Kyodo News Hai early, out of the top three only twice in his career, a graded win was expected, but he was 3rd as favorite in the Niigata Daishoten and 12th as favorite in the Sekiya Kinen. In the Chunichi Shimbun Hai, 2nd choice, he led 200m out from midfield and held off favorite Mikki Rocket.
2616: Emerging early, 2nd in the Yayoi Sho, 16th in the Satsuki Sho, he was 4th as 14th choice in the Derby. Winless for a while despite 2nds in the Fukushima Kinen and Kyoto Kimpai, he won the Hakodate Kinen in summer at 5, leading all the way under veteran Katsuharu Tanaka. Dropping in trip, he was 3rd in the Swan S. and 4th in the G1 Mile CS, then far back in the Hanshin C., Hankyu Hai and Lord Derby CT. After a break, 4th in the Lord Derby CT and Sekiya Kinen at 7, he retired after the Silk Road S. at 8.
2617: Winning a 5-million race at 3, she was 2nd in her first graded race, the Leopard S., then 3rd in the Empress Hai, 2nd in the Queen Sho and Sparking Lady C. Moving to Oi at 6, she led all the way to win the Marine C. by 2 lengths - a graded winner at last - and the Queen Sho. At 7 she won 3 straight: Sparking Lady C., Sparking Summer C. and Nippon TV Hai, but was 8th in the Kashiwa Kinen and 10th in the JBC Ladies' Classic. At 8 she won the Sakitama Hai, 2nd in the Empress Hai and Marine C.
2618: He won his debut easily, then was 2nd in the Koyamaki Sho and Kisaragi Sho. Fragile, he raced 4 times at 3, winning only a 16-million race. Stronger at 4, he won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai as favorite from midfield, then was 2nd to Fierement in the Tenno Sho (Spring). 6th as favorite in the Kyoto Daishoten, he skipped Japan's G1s and won the Hong Kong Vase, his first G1. At 5, 17th in the Takarazuka Kinen, his first heavy defeat, he won the Kyoto Daishoten, then was 5th, close behind 3 Triple Crown winners, in the Japan Cup. At 6, 4th in the Kinko Sho, he was 2nd to Loves Only You in Hong Kong's QEII Cup, Japanese runners 1st-4th; 3rd in the All Comers, he won the Hong Kong Vase again. At 7, 8th in the Dubai Sheema Classic, 6th in the Sapporo Kinen, 3rd defending the Vase, he retired to stud.
2619: A spring 3yo hope, 4th in the Kyodo News Hai and 7th in the Spring S., he was 6th choice in the Aoba Sho and finally showed his class, bursting clear from a handy spot and beating Etario by 2 lengths. 7th in the Derby, he was unplaced in the Sapporo Kinen and Kobe Shimbun Hai. Older, often top five but never top three, he retired after the Fukushima Minpo Hai at 7.
2620: The first graded winner by Scat Daddy, of the Storm Bird line. After dirt wins in his debut and a 5-million race, his first open race was the turf Falcon S.; 3rd choice, he burst clear from a handy spot. 7th choice in the NHK Mile C., he held 4th from 2nd. At 1200-1400m he was 2nd in the Hanshin C. late at 3. 7th as favorite in the Hankyu Hai at 4, he won the Takamatsunomiya Kinen as 3rd choice behind Danon Smash and Mozu Superflare, breaking clear early from 4th-5th and winning by half a length. 4th in the Sprinters S., he was 6th as favorite on dirt in the JBC Sprint. At 5 he was 11th in the Yasuda Kinen, 4th in the Sprinters S. and 12th in the JBC Sprint, and retired to stud, carrying a rare line.
2621: Out of famed sprinter Believe, bred in America to top sires each year - her first graded-winning foal. After an easy debut win, he won the Daily Hai 2yo S. under Atzeni, replacing the injured Yutaka Take, with a perfect late run - unbeaten in 2. With Take back, he was 2nd to Time Flyer in the Hopeful S. At 3 he faded: 3rd in the Yayoi Sho, 9th in the Satsuki Sho, 17th in the Derby. On shorter trips he won only listed races at 5 and 6, then at 7 won the Ocean S., and after defeats in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and Kitakyushu Kinen, won the Sprinters S. as 8th choice by a neck in a blanket finish - a G1, and a mother-son double with Believe. After a 12th in the Hong Kong Sprint he retired to stud.
2622: Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Fantasy S. Slow away on debut, she won from midfield with a brilliant kick, praised by jockey Moreira. In the Fantasy S. she broke well, waited at the back, then charged wide with a finish from another dimension. A fracture found after ruled out the Hanshin JF.
2623: After a long road, he won his first graded race, the Niigata Daishoten, at 7. 4th in the Stayers S. late at 3 and 2nd in the Kyoto Kinen, he slumped long, improving only at 6: 3rd in the Kinko Sho, 4th in the Naruo Kinen. In the Niigata Daishoten at 7, under a top weight, he closed sharply from midfield to win.
2624: In open class when older, he raced in mile graded races like the Fuji S., Kyoto Kimpai and Tokyo Shimbun Hai, and was Chukyo Kinen favorite at 5 (3rd to Win Ganion). At 6 he won the Kyoto Kimpai from the back past fancied Red Ansel and Kruger. Mostly unplaced after, incl. G1s, he switched to jumps at 9.
2625: Often top five as a longshot in fillies' graded races - "her day will come." 4th choice in the Turquoise S. late at 4, she was a close 5th to Miss Panthere, then won the Aichi Hai at 5 from a handy spot. Far back in the Victoria Mile and QEII Cup.
2626: Winning a maiden in his 2nd start, then 4th and 2nd in 5-million races, he was gelded. Back, he rose quickly, 5th to Satono Arthur in his first open race, the Rakuyo S., then won his first graded race, the Keio Hai SC, as 4th choice after a straight duel with Campbell Junior and Satono Ares.
2627: 2nd in the Daily Hai 2yo S. and 5th in the Kisaragi Sho, he won the NZT by a head over favorite K A Knotech. Overlooked as 8th choice in the NHK Mile C., NZT winners having flopped lately, he was 8th. 4th as 16th choice in the Mile CS, mostly unplaced after, he was forgotten - then in the next Swan S. he led for once and held off Admire Mars, Stelvio and others, a stunning 2nd graded win. 17th in the Mile CS, 5th in the Hakodate Sprint S. the next year, he went to jumps, then became a riding horse.
2628: Emerging early, 3rd in the Daily Hai 2yo S. and 4th in the Asahi Hai FS, he was NZT favorite at 3 but was caught by Katsuji's charge by a head. In the NHK Mile C., with Tower of London and Gibeon fancied and NZT horses overlooked, he raced last, swung wide in the straight and accelerated furiously 200m out to pass Gibeon and Red Veyron - a G1. Autumn disappointed: 5th in the Mainichi Okan, 11th in the Mile CS, far behind Katsuji. Unplaced all of 4, he revived at 5: 4th in the Lord Derby CT, 5th as 11th choice in the Yasuda Kinen, 3rd in the Fuji S.
2629: He faced Dee Majesty in the Satsuki Sho and Satono Diamond in the Kikuka Sho, racing until 7. At 4, 3rd in the AJCC and 2nd in the Nikkei Sho, he then slumped with a tendon injury. Near retirement at 7, as last choice of 16 in the Diamond S., he won by a nose over Meisho Tengen - also his sire Dream Journey's first graded winner. After the Tenno Sho (Spring) and Meguro Kinen, the tendon injury recurred and he retired.
2630: A dirt sprinter who won the Capella S. late at 3. In the UAE in spring at 3, he was 7th in the Mahab Al Shimaal (G3) and 11th in the Dubai Golden Shaheen. Restarting in allowances, he won a 16-million race in November, then the Capella S. as 4th choice, breaking clear from midfield and holding off 9yo Snow Dragon.
2631: A filly who beat later Kikuka Sho runner-up Etario in a 5-million race in spring at 3, then won the Flora S. as favorite, charging from the back with a finish from another dimension past Normcore and Pioneer Bio. 6th as 3rd choice in the Oaks, and 6th as favorite in the Rose S.
2632: He won the Urawa Kinen in autumn at 4. In graded races from spring at 3 without success (9th Unicorn S., 6th Leopard S.), he restarted in allowances and returned to open class at 4. 5th choice in the G2 Urawa Kinen, untested in open class, he raced forward, led in the straight and pulled away from Higashi Will Win to win by 6 lengths. From 5, a graded force, he was 3rd as 3rd choice in both the Saga Kinen and Diolite Kinen.
2633: A miler on turf or dirt who won the turf Yasuda Kinen and dirt February S. - with Soul Stirring, a flagship of Frankel's first crop in Japan. Fragile, he debuted only in June at 3, then won a maiden and 4 straight to open class. Placing but not winning in graded races (4th Hanshin C., 2nd Hankyu Hai and Milers C.), he lost the Azuchijo S. (OP) by a neck chasing prize money, then ran again a week later in the Yasuda Kinen. Against Osaka Hai winner Suave Richard, Mile CS winner Persian Knight and Milers C. winner Sungrazer, little noticed, he closed fastest from behind midfield - a huge upset, his first graded win a G1. Two winless years on, at 6 he tried dirt, winning the Negishi S., then the February S. as favorite over dirt stars like Inti, bursting clear from midfield - G1s on turf and dirt. 2nd in the Nambu Hai, he closed sharply for 5th in the Champions C.
2634: Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Kyoto 2yo S., a 2017 2yo name. A Heart's Cry stayer, he won a 2000m debut, then the 2000m Kyoto 2yo S. as 2nd choice, passing favorite Time Flyer from a handy spot. A classic hope, he was 7th in the Kyodo News Hai, 6th in the Satsuki Sho and 14th in the Derby. 3rd in the St. Lite Kinen, he was 10th in the Kikuka Sho.
2635: A great Hong Kong miler with 8 G1s from 2017 to 2020. Starting in Australia, placed in G1s without a graded win, he moved to Hong Kong late at 3. Winless for a while at 4, at 5 he won his first graded race and the Hong Kong Mile, then the Queen's Silver Jubilee C. and Champions Mile - Hong Kong Horse of the Year. At 6 he won 4 G1s incl. a 2nd Hong Kong Mile, unbeaten in 8 that season, 10 straight in all. At 7 his only G1 was a 3rd straight Queen's Silver Jubilee C. Racing until early 8, he retired to Australia - 8 G1s at 1400-1600m, ruling Hong Kong's miles for 4 years.
2636: Unbeaten in 2, 4th in the Yayoi Sho at 3, he then stalled in allowances, always fancied but often 2nd or 3rd, winning a 16-million race only at 7. In open class, he won the Hakodate Kinen, breaking clear from up front, and was Fukushima Kinen favorite - a middle-distance force.
2637: He won 3 straight from a maiden to the Keisei Hai, a classic dark horse. In the Satsuki Sho, as the fancies sank, he was 3rd behind Epoca d'Oro and Sanrival - 3 longshots, trifecta 370,000 yen. He won the St. Lite Kinen in autumn, holding on with stamina from up front, but in a slow, sprint-finish Kikuka Sho he lacked speed, 9th. 4th in the AJCC at 4, a tendon injury followed; back at 5, 7th in the All Comers, he faded from the front in later races and retired.
2638: In open class only late at 5, but always well regarded. After a 2500m 16-million win, he was favorite in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai and won from up front under Mirco Demuro. Favorite again in the Meguro Kinen, he was a close 3rd to Win Tendaness, then won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai - a top stayer. At 7, 4th in the Kyoto Kinen, he was 3rd as a longshot in the Tenno Sho (Spring). A fracture cost a long break; back at 8 in the Naruo Kinen, as 10th choice he beat hot favorite Loves Only You by a nose.
2639: A leading Zenno Rob Roy colt. After a debut win, he led with ease in the Kisaragi Sho, waited for the pack in the straight, then kicked clear of Glory Vase and Red Leon, holding off Glory Vase's late charge. Injured after, he missed his 3yo season. Back at 4, 3rd in the Rokko S., he ran well in open races and won the listed Rakuyo S. at 6, his first win in 3 years. From 8 he raced locally.
2640: Best foal of Oken Bruce Lee, a rare sire of the Tony Bin line, he gave him a first graded win in the Kyodo News Hai. After a maiden and 5-million win, he raced forward while favorites Grail and Stay Foolish waited, led 200m out and held on. Far back in all 3 classics.
2641: Named after an ancient Greek coin; a 2018 3yo filly hope. Unplaced as favorite in the Fairy S., she won the Queen C., holding on from 2nd as the leaders collapsed in a hot pace. 3rd choice in the NHK Mile C., she was 14th.
2642: The first graded winner by imported sire Turtle Bowl. Slow to win at 3, he won a 16-million race early at 4, then the Kokura Daishoten in his first open race. Favorite in the Niigata Daishoten, Naruo Kinen and Kokura Kinen, he lost the first 2 narrowly, then won the Kokura Kinen easily from a handy spot. After a tendon injury and long break, he won the Nakayama Kimpai, but the injury recurred and he retired.
2643: Still a maiden in the 5-million class, she ran in the Fillies' Revue for an Oka Sho ticket and beat the fancies - Kobai S. winner Molto Allegro, unbeaten Encore Plus and Fukushima 2yo S. winner Anvar - none decisive, edging clear by half a length from a pack. Little rated, 10th choice in the Oka Sho, she fought well for 6th from up front.
2644: Winner of the Flower C. at 3, she was 13th as 7th choice in the Oaks, then won the Rose S., a Shuka Sho fancy. Almond Eye won the Triple Crown, but she closed well for 3rd. Against older mares in the QEII Cup, she was 6th, 2nd-best 3yo behind Normcore.
2645: Placing often on turf but not winning, he finally won a maiden and 5-million race on dirt - nearly 2 years in all. Back on turf late at 4, he won a 10-million race at once, was 3rd stepping up in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai, then won the Nikkei Sho 2 months later. A strong stayer, he ran in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and Japan Cup, far back in both.
2646: Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Mainichi Hai, a classic fancy. Skipping the Satsuki Sho, he was 2nd choice in the Derby (5th), then beat older horses easily in the Niigata Kinen. Kikuka Sho favorite, with Derby winner Wagnerian absent and Satsuki winner Epoca d'Oro beaten in a trial, he couldn't match sharper finishers in a slow race, 4th. A great talent seemed set to end 3 without a crown, but as 3rd choice in the Arima Kinen he made a long run and held off older champion Rey de Oro by a neck for a G1. At 4, crop leader and Osaka Hai favorite, he was 6th, then 8th in the Meguro Kinen; he won the Sapporo Kinen, then was 11th of 12 in the Arc, and won the AJCC. Unplaced in the Osaka Hai, Takarazuka Kinen and Tenno Sho (Autumn), he was pulled up with atrial fibrillation in the Arima Kinen. At 7, 3rd in the Naruo Kinen and 5th in the Sapporo Kinen, he retired injured to become a riding horse - the first Arima Kinen winner, aside from deaths in training, not to go to stud.
2647: A steady performer in dirt open races, he won the Radio Nippon Sho in autumn at 5, then the March S. at 6 as 2nd choice, breaking clear from a handy spot and holding off Queen's Saturn by a nose.
2648: A specialist who raced only at a mile, a graded winner in spring at 5. Winning a 16-million race at 4, he dropped a class, won it again at 5, then in his first open race won the Lord Derby CT: boxed in at the top of the straight, he escaped through a narrow gap and passed gritty Campbell Junior. Unplaced in the Yasuda Kinen and Mile CS.
2649: Named after the Italian for "golden age." From Orfevre's first crop, his first male G1 winner. 2nd to Stelvio in the Spring S., he was 7th choice in the Satsuki Sho but led and held on for a G1, with longshots Sanrival and General Uno 2nd and 3rd (trifecta 370,000 yen). In the Derby he led and nearly won 2 classics, caught by Wagnerian, 2nd - clearly among his crop's best. 3rd choice in the Kikuka Sho, he raced forward but faded, 8th, blamed on the slow pace and the trip. At 4, troubled by nosebleeds, he raced only twice.
2650: 3rd in the new G1 Hopeful S. at 2, he was 2nd choice in the Kyodo News Hai at 3 but 10th after a big weight loss. Then, as 7th choice, he broke clear from up front to win the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, with 11th choice Admire Alba 2nd (trifecta about 270,000 yen). Far back in the Derby and Kikuka Sho, he was 3rd in the Challenge C. Older, he ran well but kept falling short: four 2nds and five 3rds at 4-5. At 6, 4th in the AJCC and 2nd in the Kyoto Kinen, he rested with phlegmon, then had atrial fibrillation in the Sapporo Kinen; back, 5th, 7th, 4th, and 5th in the Hong Kong Vase. At 7 he tried the Red Sea Turf H. - his first 3000m since the Kikuka Sho - led from the start and pulled away, his first win in 3 years 9 months, then won the 3200m Dubai Gold C. too. 9th in the Takarazuka Kinen, 2nd in the Grand Prix de Deauville and 14th in the Arc, he retired injured to become a riding horse.
2651: Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Phoenix Sho in summer at 2, she was 10th on dirt in the Shoryu S., then 3rd back on turf in the Tachibana S. (OP). 9th choice in the Aoi S., she led all the way; Love Kampu and Tour Vesoul dead-heated for 2nd. Beaten badly after, she switched to dirt in autumn at 3, won the Galaxy S., then the Kakitsubata Kinen, and later the Nagatsuki S. (OP) and 2nd in the JBC Ladies' Classic.
2652: In open class only at 5, after a 16-million win at Tokyo in a fast 2:22.9, he won his first open race, the G2 Meguro Kinen, as 9th choice, bursting clear from a handy spot. 8th in the Japan Cup, but very strong at long trips on left-handed tracks like Tokyo.
2653: He beat Kikuka Sho winner Fierement and runner-up Etario. He held off Etario by a nose from the front in a 5-million race in January at 3, then in the Radio Nikkei Sho broke clear from a handy spot and resisted Fierement's arrow-like charge. 14th as 5th choice in the Kikuka Sho, far behind both. Older, 9th in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai, he won the Nikkei Sho; 5th choice in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he faded from up front to 11th.
2654: Winning 4 straight at 4 to open class, he then struggled; his best was 5th in the Hankyu Hai at 6. Over a year later, at 7, he won the Tanabata Sho as 11th choice from midfield as favorites Sabre d'Or and Reiho Romance faded; with 4th choice Meiner Sage 2nd and 12th choice Power Pocket 3rd, the trifecta paid 2.56 million yen.
2655: A foreign-bred son of Speightstown, a dirt sprint star. Emerging at 4, he won 3 allowances around a trip to the Dubai Golden Shaheen, then the Procyon S. - Speightstown's first graded winner in Japan. Favorite at 2.0 in the JBC Sprint, he seemed to win from the front but was caught by Graceful Leap by a neck. At 5 he was 2nd in the Dubai Golden Shaheen and 8th in the BC Sprint; at 6, 2nd in Saudi Arabia, then won the Cluster C. and was 2nd in the JBC Sprint. At 7 he was 2nd to Copano Kicking in the Riyadh Dirt Sprint - a Japanese 1-2 - but 12th in the Golden Shaheen, and 5th in his 2nd BC Sprint, better than before.
2656: Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Hakodate 2yo S. - Giant's Causeway's 4th graded winner in Japan. Waiting at the back, he spurted in the straight as favorite Nanyo Izayoi, closing from the same spot, faltered, and ran down the leaders. 5th as 3rd choice in the Keio Hai 2yo S. and 7th in the Asahi Hai FS. A sprinter at 3, 2nd in the Aoi S., he was 2nd choice back at beloved Hakodate in the Hakodate Sprint S., 2nd to front-running longshot Kaiser Melange.
2657: A late-blooming sprinter who matured at 5. Winning the Idaten S. (OP), he raced in the CBC Sho, Ibis Summer Dash and Kitakyushu Kinen, winning the Ibis Summer Dash as favorite and 2nd in the Kitakyushu Kinen - 2nd in the Summer Sprint Series. 4th as 10th choice in the G1 Sprinters S. At 6, after a poor spring, he won the Kitakyushu Kinen.
2658: A 2018 dirt name. 9th as 2nd choice in the Unicorn S., he led all the way in the Leopard S., holding off Hirabo Kurtash. Against older horses he won the Hakusan Daishoten by 5 lengths. At 4 he won the Nagoya Daishoten, was 2nd in the Antares S., won the Mercury C. and the Hakusan Daishoten again. A tendon injury followed; winless after returning at 6, he moved to local racing.
2659: Winning 2 classes when older, he was favorite in his first graded race, the March S., but closed from the back too late, 9th. Back in open class after a summer 16-million win, he raced 3rd and broke clear to win the Elm S. as 2nd choice.
2660: From Lord Kanaloa's 2nd crop, its first graded winner. Beaten a nose by Admire Mars on debut, he won a maiden at 1.1, then the Niigata 2yo S. as favorite after a straight duel with Unbroken and Stillness from midfield. At 3, 4th in the Mainichi Hai, he was 2nd as 14th choice in the NHK Mile C. - perhaps a fluke, as he was 14th in the Sekiya Kinen and 17th in the Capital S. (L). Unplaced at 4 until a 5th in the Shin'etsu S. (L), he won the Kyoto Kimpai at 5 as 12th choice, was 2nd to Hishi Iguazu in the Nakayama Kinen and won the Milers C. as 2nd choice. Then 10th in the Yasuda Kinen, 9th in the Mainichi Okan, 10th in the Mile CS, and unplaced until retiring after the Musashino S. at 6.
2661: By Harbinger, sire of Deirdre and Persian Knight - the first graded winner of his 5th crop, 5 straight crops with a graded winner. Suited to longer trips, at 2 he won the Sapporo 2yo S. and Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. and was 3rd in the Hopeful S. 17th in the Satsuki Sho, he was 5th as a longshot in the Derby. 2nd choice in the Kikuka Sho after a 5th in the St. Lite Kinen, he closed too late from the back, 9th. Older he was unplaced in the AJCC, Meguro Kinen and others, and far back on dirt at 5. Switched to jumps at 6, he won the Nakayama Daishogai (J-G1) that December - a second career.
2662: A hope from Lord Kanaloa's 2nd crop. Unbeaten in 3 - debut, Kokura 2yo S., Keio Hai 2yo S. - he was 4th in the Asahi Hai FS. 2nd in the Spring S. at 3, he was 13th in the Satsuki Sho and NHK Mile C., then turned to sprints, 2nd in the Centaur S. In the Keihan Hai in November he died of acute heart failure mid-race - a career cut short.
2663: Nearly always top three, he reached open class in summer at 3, then was favorite in the Keisei Hai AH under Lemaire, swung wide at the 4th turn and burst clear. 8th choice in the G1 Mile CS, he closed fastest from last for 5th. A fracture the next year meant a long break; back after 9 months in the Sekiya Kinen as favorite, he charged from the back to win.
2664: A new dirt star of 2018. A sharp closer from midfield, he won his way up and was 2nd to Le Vent Se Leve in the Japan Dirt Derby. Against older horses he won the Sirius S. as 2nd choice over Great Pearl and Sunrise Soar, then was 2nd in the JBC Classic and 5th in the Champions C. In the Tokyo Daishoten, one of a Big Three with Gold Dream and JBC winner Katy Brave, he ran them both down for his first G1. At 4 he won the Teio Sho; 2nd in the JBC Classic and 6th in the Champions C., he won the Tokyo Daishoten again. At 5 he won the Heian S., then was 2nd to Chrysoberyl in the Teio Sho and JBC Classic. Favorite at 1.3 in the Tokyo Daishoten without Chrysoberyl, he swung wide from 5th at the 4th turn and held off Funabashi longshot Casino Fountain by a neck - the first 3-time winner. At 6, 2nd in the Kawasaki Kinen and JBC Classic, he won a 4th straight Tokyo Daishoten the same way, holding off Clincher - an unprecedented feat. At 7 he won the Antares S., was 3rd in the Teio Sho and Miyako S., and went to stud.
2665: A mare who won 5 mile and sprint G1s in 2020-2021, ruling short races - with Oaks winner Loves Only You and Shuka Sho winner Chrono Genesis, part of a golden crop. A star from 2, she won her debut and the Saudi Arabia Royal C., then took on colts in the Asahi Hai FS as 1.5 favorite but was marked by Admire Mars, 3rd. At 3 she went straight to the Oka Sho and won, breaking clear from up front ahead of slightly favored Danon Fantasy. NHK Mile C. favorite for revenge on Admire Mars, she lacked her kick and was demoted to 5th for interference. Hoof trouble ruled out the Sprinters S.; back in the Hanshin C., she won by 5 lengths. At 4 she was 2nd by a nose in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, then crushed Almond Eye, bidding for an 8th G1, in the Yasuda Kinen - a changing of the guard. She won the Sprinters S. by 2 lengths from last, then the Mile CS: boxed in hopelessly, she passed all the leaders in the last 200m. At 5, aiming for a 3rd division at 2000m, she was 4th to Rei Papale on heavy ground in the Osaka Hai, and 3rd to 3yo Efforia in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) - beyond her trip. But she won the Victoria Mile easily, was a close 2nd to Danon Kingly in the Yasuda Kinen, and beat 3yo star Schnell Meister in her farewell Mile CS. A broodmare from 2022.
2666: Unbeaten in 4 incl. the Asahi Hai FS. With filly Gran Alegria favored, he was 2nd choice, shadowed her from a handy spot, drew level at the 4th turn and edged clear - the colts' pride intact. A classic fancy at 3, he was 4th in the Satsuki Sho, then focused on miles. In the NHK Mile C. rematch with Oka Sho winner Gran Alegria, the favorite, he broke clear from a handy spot to win - mile king of his crop. 9th as favorite in the Fuji S., he won the Hong Kong Mile. Older, 6th in the Yasuda Kinen and 3rd in the Swan S., he met Gran Alegria a 4th time in the Mile CS - now sprint queen, but beaten by him twice; she won, but he held 3rd from up front. In a 2nd Hong Kong Mile he was 3rd.
2667: Unbeaten in 2 as hot favorite, then 2nd by a nose in the Keio Hai 2yo S., a classic fancy, but 7th in the Fillies' Revue and 10th in the Oka Sho. Turning to sprints, she won the Opal S. (L), then the Silk Road S. at 4. 11th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, she closed brilliantly for 3rd as 10th choice in the Sprinters S., then was 12th in the Mile CS.
2668: Emerging early, 3rd in the Daily Hai 2yo S., he was 5th in the Shinzan Kinen, then won the Falcon S., waiting at the back and sweeping past the field. 7th in the NHK Mile C., unplaced in the Keeneland C. and Sprinters S. Older he tried everything - dirt, 2000m - always unplaced, retiring after the Yodo Tankyori S. at 7.
2669: Unbeaten in 2, 11th in the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S., he was 2nd in the Arlington C. and 3rd to Admire Mars in the NHK Mile C. at 3. Little after but the Toki S. (L) at 4, he revived at 5: 2nd in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai, Lord Derby CT and Chukyo Kinen, then won the Keisei Hai AH. 9th in the Mile CS.
2670: 2nd on debut, she won 5 straight: a maiden, Canna S. (OP), Christmas Rose S. (OP), Marguerite S. (L) and the Aoi S. at 2.3, from a handy spot. 2nd against older horses in the Kitakyushu Kinen, she was 13th in the Sprinters S., then slumped (14th Silk Road S., 10th Kyoto Himba S.). At 5 she revived: 3rd as 12th choice in the Kokura Daishoten, a nose win in the Fukushima Himba S., and 4th to Gran Alegria from up front in the Victoria Mile. Unplaced until the next February, she retired to breed.
2671: 5th in the Artemis S. and 2nd in the Fairy S. early, she was 8th in the Oka Sho, 13th in the Rose S., and scratched lame from the Shuka Sho. Her chance came late at 4: 3rd in the Mermaid S., 2nd in the Queen S., then 4th choice in a Fuchu Himba S. with G1 stars Primo Scene, Lucky Lilac and Crocosmia, she closed from last with an overwhelming kick. Unplaced in the QEII Cup and Arima Kinen, at 5 she was 2nd in the Hanshin Himba S., 3rd in the Queen S., and 4th as 13th choice in the Mile CS.
2672: By sprint sire Swept Overboard, he raced around a mile at 2-3 without winning, then tried 2500m+ at 4 and won 2 classes quickly, 2nd in the Diamond S., his first JRA graded race. In the Stayers S., with 3-time winner Albert scratched on the day, he was favorite, tracked in 4th and pulled away. Never placing again in long graded races, he switched to jumps at 8, moved to local racing, and ran in the Japan Cup from there (last).
2673: Unbeaten in 2, a classic fancy, she was 11th in the Flower C. and restarted in allowances. Winning 2 classes, she was 2nd in the Kyoto Himba S. at 4, then won it at 5 as 9th choice, running on from a handy spot past favorite Miss Panthere and others. 3rd in the Shin'etsu S. (L) that autumn.
2674: 3rd in the Spring S., he was 13th to Epoca d'Oro in the Satsuki Sho. Winning 3 allowances by spring at 4, he was 2nd in the Hakodate Kinen at once, then mostly unplaced, his only placing a 2nd in the Tomoe Sho (OP) at 6. Two races later he won the Niigata Kinen as 12th choice, charging from the back by half a length.
2675: Debuting late, in December at 2, he won his debut and a 5-million race, then was 2nd to Blast Onepiece in the Mainichi Hai and to K A Knotech in the NHK Mile C., and rested instead of the Derby. 13th in the St. Lite Kinen, he won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai as favorite after a fierce duel. Older he mostly disappointed, top five only in the Lord Derby CT and Naruo Kinen. Then at 6, last choice of 10 in the February Kinko Sho, he led all the way and held off hot favorite Daring Tact by a neck - his first win in 2 years 4 months. At 7, 5th in the Kinko Sho and 4th in the Naruo Kinen, he retired after the Chunichi Shimbun Hai.
2676: A rising star of 2019 who won both mile G1s at 4. Noticed from his debut, he won it and a 5-million race, but was 3rd in the Mainichi Hai and 4th in the Arlington C., restarting in allowances. Talented, he soon won 2 classes, then the Tokyo Shimbun Hai as favorite at 4; Yuichi Fukunaga said he "still has room to grow." In the Yasuda Kinen, with Almond Eye (5 straight G1s) and Milers C. winner Danon Premium dominating the betting, he was 4th choice far behind, but spurted from a handy spot and passed leader Aerolithe for his first G1. In the Mile CS, 3rd choice behind Danon Premium and 3yo Danon Kingly, he sat handy and pulled away in the straight - the 7th to win both mile G1s in a year, the first since Maurice in 2015. Like Maurice he went for the Hong Kong Mile, 2nd choice behind local hero Beauty Generation, but was blocked in the straight, 7th. At 5 he won the Milers C., then was 2nd choice behind Almond Eye in the Yasuda Kinen; Gran Alegria split them, he was 3rd. Straight into the Mile CS, he seemed to have it won but was caught near the line by Gran Alegria, 2nd - ceding the mile crown to a new star. At 1.5 in the Hanshin C., his first 1400m turf race since his debut, he couldn't keep up early and closed fastest for 3rd.
2677: A miler who was 2nd in the Arlington C. at 3. 6th as 4th choice in the NHK Mile C., he grew in autumn, won the Rigel S. (OP) by 4 lengths, then the Kyoto Kimpai as favorite from a handy spot. 3rd in the Milers C., a fracture followed; 9th in the Sekiya Kinen after 2.5 years off, he retired but went to stud for his precious Kurofune blood.
2678: A sprinter who won the CBC Sho at 5. Top two in his first 6 starts, at 3 he was 2nd in the Ibis Summer Dash and Centaur S., and a neck 2nd to Fine Needle as 11th choice in the G1 Sprinters S. Then a slump with heavy defeats, until the CBC Sho at 5 as 13th choice: he led from a fine start and held everyone off, with 11th choice Anvar 2nd - quinella 138,600 yen. Perhaps a one-off; heavy defeats resumed.
2679: A top stayer: Kikuka Sho and 2 Tenno Sho (Spring). In a crop led by fillies like Almond Eye and Lucky Lilac, he and miler Indy Champ flew the colts' flag. Debuting at 3, unbeaten in 2, he skipped the classics with fragility and was 2nd as heavy favorite in the Radio Nikkei Sho. Straight into the Kikuka Sho, 7th choice after the break, he was given little chance - but Lemaire, fresh from a Shuka Sho win, was aboard. Settled in midfield, he spurted through the pack at the 4th turn and caught Etario by a nose - a classic in only his 4th start. At 4, 2nd in the AJCC, he became Tenno Sho (Spring) favorite after AJCC and Hanshin winner Shaketra's sudden death, broke clear early and beat Glory Vase by a neck. 3rd in the Sapporo Kinen, he was most fancied of 3 Japanese in the Arc but last on heavy ground. In an Arima Kinen with 11 G1 winners he was 4th to Lys Gracieux. At 5 he won the Tenno Sho (Spring) again as heavy favorite, by a nose over Stiffelio, then went straight to the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and was 2nd, half a length behind Almond Eye.
2680: A talent who stunned on debut. Favorite in the Sapporo 2yo S., he lost a tight finish, 3rd. In the Kyoto 2yo S. at 2.8 he waited at the back, moved up through the 3rd-4th turns, drew level at the top of the straight and won a duel with Breaking Dawn. At 3, 3rd in the Kyodo News Hai, he ran well as a longshot in the classics: 5th in the Satsuki Sho, 6th in the Derby.
2681: Steady in trials at 3 - 4th in the Tulip Sho and Flora S., 2nd in the Rose S. - she was 4th to Almond Eye in the Shuka Sho. Older, 2nd in the Epsom C. and top five in the Sekiya Kinen and Fukushima Himba S., she won the Fuchu Himba S. at 5 as 7th of 8, from a handy spot as favorites like Loves Only You collapsed. In the QEII Cup she lost by a head to Lucky Lilac, then in her farewell Arima Kinen, as 11th choice, charged wide with the fastest finish for 2nd - a devilish late kick fans won't forget.
2682: As crop-mate Duramente's first foals debuted, he raced on, a late bloomer who won his first graded race at 8. On turf until spring at 5, stuck in the 10-million class, he switched to dirt and won 2 classes quickly, then was 2nd in the Sirius S. and 2nd to Le Vent Se Leve in the Champions C. 3rd in the Miyako S., 2nd in the Diolite Kinen, he won the Antares S. at 8, then was 2nd in the Elm S., 3rd in the Urawa Kinen and Tokyo Daishoten. At 9: 2nd Sirius S., 3rd Tokyo Daishoten again. At 10, 7th in the Antares S., he retired when unwell before the Heian S.
2683: Winning 3 straight by wide margins in summer at 3, she was a Shuka Sho fancy and led boldly for 2nd to Almond Eye. Older, 14th in the Nakayama Himba S., she won the Hanshin Himba S., then the Queen S. as favorite from a handy spot.
2684: Winning only a maiden on dirt, he switched to turf when older and showed stamina at once: 3 wins to open class, then 2nd in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. After a 6th and 5th, he won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai at 5 as 2nd choice, racing forward and holding on. His later highlight was 4th in the Hanshin Daishoten at 6.
2685: Debuting late in February at 3, he won easily, then grew steadily, winning the Nagoya GP late at 3 over Grimm and Mitsuba. Blooming older, 2nd in the Tokai S., he won the Diolite Kinen and Heian S., was 2nd in the Teio Sho, then won the JBC Classic at 1.6, dueling Omega Perfume and edging him by a nose. Then rival Chrysoberyl arrived: 4th in the Champions C. behind him, he won the Kawasaki Kinen easily without him, but was 3rd to him in the Teio Sho and JBC Classic. In their 4th clash, the Champions C., as 4th choice he burst clear and beat Chrysoberyl at last - his first JRA G1. At 6 he went to the Saudi Cup and Dubai World Cup, 2nd to Mystic Guide. After a 6th in the Teio Sho and a fracture, he was 3rd in the JBC Classic and 2nd to younger T O Keynes defending the Champions C. At 7 he won the Kawasaki Kinen, was 3rd in the Dubai World Cup and 2nd to Meisho Hario in the Teio Sho, retiring a top horse.
2686: Winner of the 2019 Shuka Sho and 3 straight Grand Prix races. With crop-mates Gran Alegria and Loves Only You, she ruled 2019-2021 over the males. Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Ivy S. (OP), she lost narrowly to Danon Fantasy in the Hanshin JF after a thrilling duel from the back. At 3 she won the Queen C., but was 3rd to Gran Alegria in the Oka Sho and to late bloomer Loves Only You in the Oaks. In a Shuka Sho without either, 4th choice off a break, she led early in the straight and won easily - a G1. In the QEII Cup, sharing favoritism with Loves Only You, both lost to older mares. At 4 she won the Kyoto Kinen, with Curren Bouquet d'Or 2nd again, then was 2nd in the Osaka Hai. In the Takarazuka Kinen she crushed G1 winners incl. Saturnalia, Blast Onepiece and Lucky Lilac by 6 lengths. In the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 2nd choice behind Almond Eye going for an 8th G1, she was 3rd, a neck behind Fierement - impressive in defeat. Top of the fan vote and favorite in the Arima Kinen, she moved wide on the back straight, swept to 3rd at the 4th turn and ran down Fierement on heavy ground - jockey Yuichi Kitamura's first Arima ride and win. At 5, she was caught near the line by French Derby winner Mishriff in the Dubai Sheema Classic, 2nd, with Loves Only You 3rd. She won the Takarazuka Kinen again as hot favorite - the 3rd to win 3 Grand Prix races in a row, the first since Grass Wonder in 1999. In the Arc she faded to 7th. Bidding for a historic 4th, she was 3rd in the Arima Kinen behind 3yo leader Efforia and Deep Bond.
2687: A stayer from the start, blooming in autumn at 3: after the Aganogawa Tokubetsu he was 3rd to Fierement in the Kikuka Sho as a longshot. At 4 he won the Diamond S. as heavy favorite, was 5th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), then won the Niigata Kinen, 4th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 5th in the Japan Cup. At 5 he won the Hanshin Daishoten, 4th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), then 4th as heavy favorite in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai, 12th in the Japan Cup and 11th in the Arima Kinen. At 6, 2nd in the Hanshin Daishoten, he was unplaced in 3 G1s.
2688: Like her half-sister Soul Stirring, noticed from 2: she won a maiden and the Artemis S., 4th in the Hanshin JF. Fading at 3, 5th as 2nd choice in the Tulip Sho, 9th in the Oka Sho, 7th in the Oaks, 11th in the Shuka Sho; after an 8th in the Capital S. (L) a tendon injury ended her career, and she became a broodmare.
2689: A flagship of the 2019 classic crop. Posting workout times to rival older horses before his debut, he won it with ease, then the Hagi S. (OP) and the G1 Hopeful S., boxed in but splitting the field and bursting clear without the whip. Straight into the Satsuki Sho at 1.7, he won a tight finish. Even hotter Derby favorite, he missed the break and rallied to 4th, his first loss. In autumn he won the Kobe Shimbun Hai easily, then skipped the Kikuka Sho to face Almond Eye, winner of 5 straight G1s, in the Tenno Sho (Autumn); a little worked up, he was 6th. In the Arima Kinen he was 5 lengths behind Lys Gracieux but held off Kikuka winner World Premiere for 2nd. At 4 he won the Kinko Sho at 1.3; with Hong Kong called off due to COVID, he was favorite in a Takarazuka Kinen with 8 G1 winners incl. Lucky Lilac, Chrono Genesis, Kiseki and Blast Onepiece, but finished 4th, far behind crop-mate Chrono Genesis. He never raced again, retiring to stud. Out of Japanese and American Oaks winner Cesario; half-brother of Epiphaneia and Leondeux.
2690: 2nd on debut to crop star Gran Alegria, she won a maiden and the Fantasy S., then with Gran Alegria in the Asahi Hai FS, won the Hanshin JF as favorite. At 3 she won the Tulip Sho and was Oka Sho favorite, but was beaten clearly by Gran Alegria, 4th. 5th to Loves Only You in the Oaks, she won the Rose S. but was 8th as favorite to Chrono Genesis in the Shuka Sho. Older, 5th in the Hanshin Himba S. and Victoria Mile, 6th in the Fuchu Himba S., she revived in the Hanshin C., shooting up the inside past G1-winning males Indy Champ and Stelvio. At 5, after a 5th, 12th and 7th, she won the Swan S. from behind and was 3rd in the Hanshin C., then retired to breed.
2691: After a debut win she was top two every time. 9th in her first open race, the Ritto S., she was 3rd in her first graded race, a G1 - the JBC Ladies' Classic. The next year she won the Sparking Lady C. as favorite, tracking in 2nd and pulling clear, then was 2nd in the Ladies' Prelude and 3rd again in the JBC Ladies' Classic. She won the Sparking Lady C. again, then the JBC Ladies' Classic at the 3rd try - a G1 - and retired at her peak to breed.
2692: Unbeaten in 2, he was 2nd to Saturnalia in the Hopeful S. at 2, but as rivals rose he was 8th in the Satsuki Sho and 18th in the Derby. Against older horses at middle-long trips he finished far back, until the Hakodate Kinen at 4, which he won as 15th of 16 with a brilliant late run; with 13th choice Duomo 2nd, the quinella paid 130,000 yen. Unplaced after, he retired after the Andromeda S. (L) at 6.
2693: The 2018 US Triple Crown winner. Debuting at 3, he won his first 2 by 9.5 and 6.5 lengths, then the G1 Santa Anita Derby. No horse unraced at 2 had won the Kentucky Derby since Apollo in 1882 - "the curse of Apollo" - but he broke it, bursting clear from handy on a sloppy track. He won the Preakness in a tight finish on slop, then dominated the Belmont - an unbeaten Triple Crown. Aiming at the BC Classic, he retired injured: 6 from 6 in about half a year. At stud from 2019, his first foals raced in 2022; by the end of 2024 he had 7 G1 winners incl. Derby winner City of Troy, and in Japan Awesome Result won 3 local graded races. A Santa Anita Derby drug violation later came to light; his disqualification was confirmed in 2024, revising his record to 5 wins from 6.
2694: 4th in the St. Lite Kinen, last in the Kikuka Sho, he restarted in allowances. Winning 3 classes at 4, he was 5th as a longshot in the G2 Sapporo Kinen, then won the Fukushima Kinen as 2nd choice. At 5 he won the Kokura Daishoten, and in autumn beat Derby winner Rey de Oro and others in the All Comers - 3 graded wins.
2695: A dirt miler who won the Mile CS Nambu Hai twice. Winning 4 races at 1600-1700m on dirt, he reached open class late at 3, then won the Oasis S. (L) and Keyaki S. (OP) at 4, and the Procyon S. as 2nd choice behind defending champion Matera Sky. 2nd in the Nambu Hai, at 5 he was 9th in the February S. and 4th in the Kashiwa Kinen, then won the Nambu Hai as 6th choice - his first G1, avenging his defeat. 9th in the Champions C. and February S., short at JRA G1 level, he won the Sakitama Hai and the Nambu Hai again at 6. At 7, 7th in the February S. and 14th going for a 3rd Nambu Hai, he went to stud.
2696: Beaten on debut, he won 7 straight up to the February S. Debuting late in spring at 3, he won a maiden and 5-million race, then fetlock swelling cost a year. Back in summer at 4 with Yutaka Take, he won 3 classes, then the Tokai S. at 1.5, leading with ease. Six straight, he went to the February S., co-favorite with veteran Gold Dream; leading as usual, he won their straight duel by a neck. His streak ended; hampered, he was 15th in the Miyako S., then 3rd in the Champions C. behind 3yo star Chrysoberyl and Gold Dream. At 6, 14th defending the February S. and 9th in the Nambu Hai, he was 3rd again in the Champions C. - "signs of revival," said Take. At 7, 3rd in the Kashiwa Kinen and 4th in the Nambu Hai, he broke superbly and held 4th in a 3rd Champions C. After 2 races at 8, past his best, he retired to stud.
2697: 3rd in the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. and 6th in the Hopeful S., he flopped in spring at 3 (4th Kisaragi Sho, 3rd Mainichi Hai, 9th Arlington C.) and missed the G1s. Restarting, he won 3 classes in a row, then the Fuji S. in autumn at 4 with a powerful finish from midfield. 6th in the Mile CS, at 5 he was 4th in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and 2nd in the Dubai Turf, then 12th in the BC Mile and 6th in the Hong Kong Mile. At 6 he was 3rd in the Dubai Turf; after a 15th in the Yasuda Kinen and heavy defeats in Saudi and Dubai at 7, a tendon injury ended his career, and he went to stud in Brazil.
2698: A long-time middle-to-long distance runner who won his first graded race, the Kyoto Kinen, at 7. Emerging in autumn at 3, he was 12th to Fierement in the Kikuka Sho; at 4, 3rd in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. Slumping from 5, he was 2nd as 17th choice in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai late at 6, then led all the way in the Kyoto Kinen at 7 as 12th choice. Seen as a fluke, he stayed unfancied and unplaced.
2699: A dirt runner at 1200-1600m in Southern Kanto, winning races like the Bloodstone Tokubetsu and April Sho. 7th in his first graded race, the Sakitama Hai, he led to win the Oval Sprint, holding off favored Oken Believe, and won it again the next year; 5th as 3rd choice in the JBC Sprint.
2700: A 2019-2021 dirt star. At 3 he was 3rd to Chrysoberyl in the Japan Dirt Derby; at 4, 4th in the Kawasaki Kinen and JBC Classic, 5th in the Tokyo Daishoten. At 5, after a 4th in the Teio Sho, he won the JBC Classic, leading early and holding off Omega Perfume, Chuwa Wizard and others.
2701: An Oi mare who emerged early at 3, 3rd in the Kanto Oaks and Totsuka Kinen (S1). In December at 4, in her 20th start and 5th JRA-local graded race, she led all the way against JRA stars in the Queen Sho. At 5 she was beaten badly in the TCK Jo-o Hai and Empress Hai, then 6th defending the Beautiful Dreamer C. at Mizusawa, and retired.
2702: Debuting on JRA turf, she kept placing without winning as a maiden, then moved to Kawasaki and won 4 straight. 6th in the Sparking Lady C., she won steadily in Southern Kanto, then at 5 won the Marine C. as 3rd choice in a field of 7, tracking in 3rd and pulling clear. 4th in the G1 JBC Ladies' Classic.
2703: Winner of the 2021 BC Classic and Whitney S., Eclipse Horse of the Year. Bought by the Korea Racing Authority under its K-Nicks program, choosing top prospects by nick patterns and pedigree theory - hence his name. He won the G1 Breeders' Futurity at 2, then went winless at 3. A fracture at 4 meant a long break; back in autumn, he won the BC Dirt Mile. At 5 he won the Pegasus World C. and Whitney S. (4 G1s), then led all the way in the BC Classic as top fancy. Horse of the Year, rated world No. 1 at 129 lbs. After a 2nd in the Pegasus World C. at 6, he retired; at stud in Kentucky from 2023.
2704: A debut winner who was 2nd in the Kyoto 2yo S. and 5th in the Hopeful S. 3rd in the Yayoi Sho for a Satsuki Sho spot, he was 11th there and 6th in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai. Aiming at autumn, he won the Radio Nikkei Sho as 3rd choice, drawing level early from midfield and bursting clear.
2705: Winner of the 2019 Kikuka Sho and, at 5, the Tenno Sho (Spring). He won his debut as favorite and was 3rd in the Kyoto 2yo S. At 3 he won a 5-million race and was 2nd to Velox in the Wakaba S. (L), earning a Satsuki Sho spot, but sore shins ruled out the spring. In autumn he was 3rd to Satsuki winner Saturnalia and Velox in the Kobe Shimbun Hai. With Saturnalia going to the Tenno Sho, Velox was Kikuka favorite and he 3rd choice; Yutaka Take said he was "in by far his best shape." From a handy spot he broke clear - Take became both the youngest and oldest Kikuka Sho-winning jockey. In an Arima Kinen with 11 G1 winners, he was 3rd. Resting long at 4, he ran only in the Japan Cup (6th, in the 3 Triple Crown winners' clash) and Arima Kinen (5th). At 5, 3rd in the Nikkei Sho, he won the Tenno Sho (Spring) as 3rd choice behind Deep Bond and Aristoteles, running on strongly from a handy spot. 11th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn).
2706: Winning 3 classes from late 3 to open class, he won the Kakitsubata Kinen and Sakitama Hai at once - a dirt force. Unplaced in the February S. and JBC Sprint, he won the Kurofune Sho, was 2nd in the Hyogo Gold T. and the Sakitama Hai. At 6 he won the Oval Sprint from a handy spot; after a 10th in the JBC Sprint, he won the Hyogo Gold T. despite gaining 22kg, catching leader Best Macho by a nose. At 7, 2nd in the Summer Champion, he won the Tokyo Hai, then was 7th as 2nd choice in the JBC Sprint. At 8, after placing but not winning, and a 4th in the Kurofune Sho at 9, he retired to stud.
2707: 4th on debut, a sharp closer from midfield, he won a maiden, the Oxalis Sho and Hyogo Junior GP - a dirt talent. 2nd in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun and 4th in the UAE Derby, he won the Nagoya GP in December at 3. Older, 3rd in the Kawasaki Kinen, 2nd in the Mercury C. and Nippon TV Hai, he couldn't win. From 5, occasionally top five; 2nd in the Saga Kinen at 7, he moved to local racing after heavy defeats.
2708: A foreign-bred dirt sprinter. A front-runner at first, he was badly hampered at the start of the Fujinomori S. in October at 3, yet charged from last to win. He won the Autumn Leaf S. (OP), then the Capella S. with another devilish late run, and the Negishi S. at 4. Paired with Nanako Fujita, the first female JRA jockey in 16 years, he drew huge attention: 5th in his first G1, the February S., 2nd in the Tokyo Sprint, 3rd in the Cluster C., then won the Tokyo Hai. A neck 2nd to Bulldog Boss in the JBC Sprint, he won the Capella S. again - the first JRA graded win by a female jockey. At 5, 2nd in the Negishi S. and 3rd in the Summer Champion, he was 6th in the JBC Sprint, winless all year. At 6 in Saudi Arabia he missed the break yet charged to win the Riyadh Dirt Sprint; 5th in the Dubai Golden Shaheen, 3rd in the Summer Champion and 4th in the Tokyo Hai. At 7, 4th defending in Riyadh, he was injured before the Golden Shaheen and retired.
2709: A rare front-running filly in middle-distance dirt races. Leading all the way in the Heijokyo S. in October at 4 to reach open class, 8th in the JBC Ladies' Classic, she led all the way to win the Queen Sho.
2710: Full brother of Blanche Coeur, a star in fillies' JRA-local races. Pulled up lame as favorite on dirt debut, he won a maiden 2 weeks later and the Mochinoki Sho by 4 lengths, then the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun as 5th choice, leading and holding off Dell Mar Louvre by a head. At 3, 3rd in the Hakusan Daishoten; at 4, 3rd in the Saga Kinen. Late at 5 he won 3 straight incl. the Diolite Kinen. After an 8th in the Mercury C. at 6, he died of a heart attack.
2711: Noticed for a sharp debut finish, she won a maiden, then the Fairy S. as 3rd choice from midfield after a duel with Hoh O Catherine. Far back in the Oka Sho and Oaks, she was 5th in the Shion S. and 4th in the Turquoise S. Older, she kept finishing unplaced in fillies' graded races.
2712: Racing mainly at long trips, he reached open class late at 5 - rarely winning but nearly always top three. At once 2nd in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai, 6th in the Nikkei Sho, 4th in the Niigata Daishoten, he won the Meguro Kinen as 3rd choice, charging from the back almost easily. 4th in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai, he was 10th in his first G1, the Japan Cup.
2713: Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Kyodo News Hai, a 2019 classic fancy. 3rd choice in the Satsuki Sho (3rd) and Derby (2nd), he met expectations. Skipping the Kikuka Sho, he beat G1 winners Aerolithe, Indy Champ and Persian Knight in the Mainichi Okan. 2nd choice behind stablemate Danon Premium in the Mile CS, he lacked a kick, 5th. At 4 he won the Nakayama Kinen; Osaka Hai favorite, he led and was caught near the line, 3rd. 7th in the Yasuda Kinen, he was last (12th) as 3rd choice in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). At 5, 8th choice after 7 months off, he won the Yasuda Kinen, holding off hot favorite Gran Alegria by a head - a famous upset. 2nd to 3yo Schnell Meister in the Mainichi Okan, he was 8th in the Hong Kong Mile.
2714: US-bred, by Speightstown, sire of 10+ crops in Japan incl. Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun winner Lieno Tesoro - his first JRA G1 winner. Turning to sprints in summer at 3, she won the Ocean S. at 4; 15th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, she was 2nd to Tower of London in the Sprinters S. At 5, 4th in the Silk Road S., she was 9th choice in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen but beat Tower of London, Gran Alegria and others, leading from a quick break in a 4-horse photo, winning by a nose. 2nd in the Kitakyushu Kinen, she was 4th on dirt in the JBC Sprint.
2715: Winning 2 at 3 incl. the Flower C., a classic hope, she led all the way as 2nd choice. Skipping the Oka Sho for the Oaks, she shared favoritism with Loves Only You and Chrono Genesis but was 9th. 15th in the Shuka Sho off a break, she led all the way to win the Turquoise S., proving her class at a mile. Older she flopped: 16th as 2nd choice in the Nakayama Himba S., 14th in the Victoria Mile, 10th as 3rd choice in the Queen S., 7th and 10th after - unplaced all year. At 5, 11th choice in the Ocean S., she suddenly won, then 8th in the Hakodate Sprint S., 2nd by a neck to Cathedral as 12th choice in the Keisei Hai AH. She retired to breed after the Fukushima Kinen and Nakayama Kinen.
2716: A debut winner who was 3rd in the Flower C. at 3. Building in allowances, she reached open class in spring at 4; fancied but beaten (6th Kokura Kinen, 7th Turquoise S.), she won the Nakayama Himba S. at 5, then was 2nd to Gran Alegria as 10th choice in the Victoria Mile. 9th in the QEII Cup, she was 2nd in the Kokura Daishoten, then retired to breed after a 9th in the Kinko Sho.
2717: He won the Spring S. as 10th choice, breaking well, leading early in the straight and holding off favored Fantasist. Leg trouble ruled out the Satsuki Sho; straight into the Derby, too far, he was 12th. Back at a mile, 7th in the Fuji S. and 17th in the Mile CS. Older his best were 5ths in the May S. (OP) at 4 and Kochi S. (L) at 5; he moved to local racing after the Kochi S. at 6.
2718: A debut winner at 3, he then rested a year and raced little, winning a class at 4 and another at 5, reaching open class at 6. Straight into the March S., he won as 8th choice, charging from the back with the fastest finish. 3rd in the Elm S. and winner of the Brazil C. (L), he was 15th in his first G1, the Champions C.
2719: In open class at 4, he was last in his first graded race, the Keio Hai SC. A year later, much stronger, he won back into open class, was 2nd choice in the Lord Derby CT, raced forward in a hot pace and held on by a neck - stronger than the margin. Far back in the Yasuda Kinen and Mile CS, he was 2nd in the Hanshin C. and Hankyu Hai, then won the Keihan Hai as 3rd choice at 6. In a Hanshin C. against Indy Champ and others his kick misfired, 9th.
2720: He won the NZT early at 3 as 4th choice, leading all the way past Agulhas and other fancies. 9th in the NHK Mile C., he switched to dirt and won the Unicorn S. at once, winning a front-running duel with Due Process. 2nd in the Oval Sprint and 5th in the Miyako S., he was 14th in the Champions C. At 4, 12th in the February S., he won the Kashiwa Kinen as 6th of 7 - a G1 on his 4th try. 4th in the Teio Sho, 7th in the Nambu Hai, 9th in the Miyako S.; at 5, 14th in the February S., then 4th Kashiwa Kinen, 3rd Sakitama Hai. Winless, he moved to local racing after the Kakitsubata Kinen at 6.
2721: Winning 2 at 3 to open class, she was 4th in the Fillies' Revue, missing an Oka Sho spot, then won the Arlington C. as 12th choice, doubted at the trip, by a neck in a blanket finish. 16th in the NHK Mile C., 3rd in the Centaur S., 11th in the Sprinters S. Older, steady in open races (3rd UHB Sho, 5th Auro C.), she led all the way in the Kyoto Himba S. at 5 as 3rd choice, then was 18th in the Victoria Mile.
2722: A late-blooming dirt horse who won his first graded race at 5. Unbeaten in 2, he then fell short, trying graded races only at 5: 3rd in the Nagoya Daishoten, then the Antares S. as 6th choice, breaking clear from a handy spot. 4th in the Heian S., 2nd in the Urawa Kinen; at 6, 5th in his first G1, the Kawasaki Kinen, he won the Diolite Kinen as favorite, then was 2nd in the Antares S. and 3rd in the Elm S., but 13th in the Champions C. At 7, 2nd in the Tokai S., 3rd in the Diolite Kinen and Miyako S., he held 3rd from up front as 14th choice in the Champions C. After poor runs, he moved to local racing after the Antares S. at 8.
2723: Slow away in the Flora S., she still won by a nose, a classic fancy, then closed thrillingly for 4th to Loves Only You in the Oaks. 2nd choice behind Danon Fantasy in the Rose S., she was a close 3rd in a 3-way finish with Beach Samba. Injured, she missed the Shuka Sho and retired.
2724: At 3 she was 2nd in the Flora S., 6th in the Oaks, 9th in the Rose S. and 4th in the Shuka Sho. At 4, 2nd in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and Fuchu Himba S., but 10th in the Victoria Mile and 8th in the QEII Cup. At 5, 3rd in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and Mermaid S., she won the Fuchu Himba S. as 4th choice, charging from the back and just catching Andrasta. 7th in the Japan Cup, 12th in the Arima Kinen; unplaced at 6, she retired to breed after the Turquoise S.
