2725: Stuck in the 10-million class until the end of 3, he surged at 4: 2 classes, then the Niigata Daishoten, the Naruo Kinen as favorite and the Kokura Kinen as favorite - 5 straight that year. Then Australia's G1 Caulfield Cup under Damian Lane, his partner in the Niigata Daishoten and Naruo Kinen: favorite in JRA betting (boosted by fan bets) and 3rd choice with local bookmakers, he ran on to win. Fancied in the Melbourne Cup, he pulled hard and was 6th, ending a 6-race streak.
2726: The 2019 Oaks winner and the first Japanese horse with 3 G1 wins abroad. With Oka Sho winner and sprint queen Gran Alegria and Shuka Sho winner and 3-time Grand Prix winner Chrono Genesis, the trio ruled 2019-2021. She won her debut easily under Lemaire and a 5-million race as favorite under Yasunari Iwata, closing powerfully. Not ready for the Oka Sho, she won the Wasurenagusa Sho (L) the same day easily. In the Oaks, narrowly favored over Chrono Genesis and Contra Check, she tracked them from midfield, burst clear and caught Curren Bouquet d'Or - in a record 0.8s faster than Gentildonna's. Missing the Shuka Sho, she was QEII Cup favorite but 3rd behind older Lucky Lilac and Crocosmia. At 4, 7th in the Victoria Mile, 2nd in the Naruo Kinen, 5th in the Fuchu Himba S., she was a close 3rd to Lucky Lilac in the QEII Cup, then 10th in her first mixed G1, the Arima Kinen. At 5 she won the Kyoto Kinen at short odds, was 3rd in the Dubai Sheema Classic behind Chrono Genesis, then won Hong Kong's QEII Cup, her first G1 abroad. 2nd in the Sapporo Kinen, she won the BC Filly & Mare Turf in America - the first Japanese BC winner - and in her farewell Hong Kong Cup won a duel with fellow Japanese Hishi Iguazu for a 3rd G1 abroad. She, Gran Alegria and Chrono Genesis all retired at the end of 2021; their foals' rivalry is eagerly awaited.
2727: Highly rated, she was 3rd choice stepping up in the Shion S. at 3, but, hot-tempered like her sire Orfevre, finished 13th. Winning a 10-million race, she stalled, then at 4 stepped up for the Mermaid S. and alone found a stunning finish from last to sweep past them all.
2728: A close 2nd on debut, he won a maiden, a 5-million race, the Shoryu S. and Seiryu S. (both OP), then was 2nd in his first graded race, the Unicorn S. Late at 3 he won the Hyogo Gold T., leading alone from a fine start and holding off local chargers Il Ultimone and Sakura Regnum. Older, the odd placing - 4th in the Procyon S. and Galaxy S., 5th and 3rd in listed races - but no wins, and he moved to local racing.
2729: Winning a 16-million race at 5, he was at once 2nd in the Fukushima Minpo Hai (L) and Tanabata Sho. 5th against crop star Rey de Oro in the All Comers, he went to the Fukushima Kinen and, co-favorite with All Comers runner-up Mikki Swallow, beat him - a graded win at last. At 6, 7th as favorite in the Nakayama Kimpai, he won the Tanabata Sho, 4th in the All Comers, 13th in the Japan Cup, and 8th as last choice in the Arima Kinen. Beaten defending the Tanabata Sho at 7, 4th as 8th choice in the Nikkei Sho at 8, he retired after the All Comers.
2730: In open class only in autumn at 5, he was 2nd in the Muromachi S. (OP) and 5th as 10th choice in the Capella S. He won the Polaris S. and Tempozan S. (both OP), was 3rd in the Procyon S., then won the Miyako S. as 7th choice, sweeping early from the back to lead.
2731: From the first crop of Kizuna (at stud from 2015). A neck 2nd on debut, he won a maiden as favorite, then led all the way in the Hakodate 2yo S., his sire's first graded win. 2nd in the Keio Hai 2yo S., 7th in the Asahi Hai FS. A sprinter at 3, he won the Aoi S., then 5th in the Centaur S. and 16th in the Sprinters S. His fiery temper sometimes cost him, so he was gelded late at 3. At 4, 3rd to Contra Check in the Ocean S., he won the Hakodate Sprint S., leading and just holding the late surge. After unplaced runs, 3rd again in the Ocean S., then last (16th) twice, he retired.
2732: From the now-rare Northern Dancer male line, best son of Turtle Bowl. A debut winner, 2nd in the Hakodate 2yo S., he won the Keio Hai 2yo S., was 2nd to Salios in the Asahi Hai FS, and won the Arlington C. at 3. Racing handy for once as 2nd choice in the NHK Mile C., he was 4th; 5th in the Fuji S., then 14th in the Mile CS, his first heavy defeat. At 5, 4th in the Kyoto Kimpai and CBC Sho, 12th in the Sprinters S., he was 2nd in the Keihan Hai.
2733: From grand-dam Shirayuki Hime's white-coated family, the first white horse to win a JRA graded race, and a graded winner on both turf and dirt. A turf maiden winner, 8th in the Ivy S. (OP), he switched to dirt, winning a 5-million race in spring at 3, then won his first graded race, the Leopard S. (G3), as 10th choice, catching favorite Dell Mar Louvre. At 4, 2nd in the Pollux S. and Sobu S. (both OP), he swept from the back to win the Brazil C. (L), and at 5 the Sleipnir S. (OP). Back on turf at 6, 5th as 13th choice in the Nikkei Sho (G2), 15th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he won the Hakodate Kinen (G3) - JRA graded wins on turf and dirt. Over 2 winless years later, at 8, he won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai (G2) as 10th choice under top weight 58.5kg - sheer grit. Injured in the Meguro Kinen (G2) at 9, he retired.
2734: She won her debut with a blistering 32.0 final 600m, by 3.5 lengths as 3rd choice, then the Niigata 2yo S. at 2.1, sweeping past all from midfield. 2nd choice in the Hanshin JF, she lacked a kick, 4th, as longshot Resistencia won brilliantly. Far back in the Oka Sho and Oaks, 18th in the Rose S. and 14th in the Shin'etsu S. (L), she retired to breed.
2735: He won his debut and the Phoenix Sho as favorite from handy spots. In the Kokura 2yo S., with Yusaku Kokubun replacing Ryuji Wada, he was 3rd choice but raced forward and held on - unbeaten in 3. 9th in the Keio Hai 2yo S. and 13th as 13th choice in the Asahi Hai FS. Unplaced at 3 apart from a 5th as last choice in the Tachibana S. (L), and over 1200m after, he moved to local racing at 5.
2736: A debut winner, 4th in the Shinzan Kinen, she was 4th in the Flora S., missing the Oaks, and restarted in allowances. She won a 1-win race easily as favorite in summer and the Shion S. in a tight finish - a graded title and a Shuka Sho spot. 9th choice there, she was forced wide and tired, 10th.
2737: Winless at 3 - 5th Flora S., 16th Oaks, 2nd Shion S., 16th Shuka Sho - she blossomed older: 4th in the Aichi Hai, then the Nakayama Himba S. as 3rd choice behind crop-mates Espoir and Contra Check, and the Fukushima Himba S. Fancied but beaten in the Queen S. and Fuchu Himba S., she was 3rd in the Turquoise S. and Nakayama Himba S. when less fancied. Unplaced from 6, she retired to breed after the Queen S.
2738: A debut winner, then 4th in the Artemis S., 5th in the Fairy S. and 4th in the Elfin S., she dropped to 1200-1400m and won her way up. Back in a graded race in September at 4, the Keisei Hai AH, she was 4th choice with little form at a mile, yet led all the way to win by 3.5 lengths. At 5, 15th in the Hanshin Himba S., she was 4th as 12th choice in the Victoria Mile, 2nd in the Sekiya Kinen, then won the Keisei Hai AH again by a nose in a 3-way finish. 4th in the Fuchu Himba S., she faded from the front to 16th in the Turquoise S. and retired to breed.
2739: Debuting at 3, he won 3 straight to the Principal S. (L), then skipped the Derby to rest. 3rd in the St. Lite Kinen, he was 13th to World Premiere in the Kikuka Sho. At 4, 3rd in the May S. and winner of the Kan'etsu S. (both OP), he won the Epsom C. at 5 as 3rd choice, holding off Satono Flag by a neck. 13th as favorite in the Niigata Kinen and 7th in the Fuji S., he won the Kyoto Kimpai at 6 from the back, then slumped (10th, 6th, 8th).
2740: A new dirt star of 2019 who shot to the top. Full brother of Japan Dirt Derby winner Chrysolite, with siblings like Marialite and Liar Fail. He won his debut and a 5-million race as favorite, the Hyogo Championship at 1.1 and the Japan Dirt Derby at 1.2 for a G1. After the Nippon TV Hai, all eyes were on how the 3yo would fare against Gold Dream and February S. winner Inti in the Champions C. - he raced handy, went toe to toe and held off Gold Dream: dirt champion. At 4 he lost for the first time in the Saudi Cup, then won the Teio Sho and JBC Classic, unbeatable at home. At 1.4 in the Champions C., he lacked his kick and was 4th behind Chuwa Wizard and others he had beaten - his first home defeat. Injured, back in autumn at 5, he was 6th in the Nippon TV Hai and retired with leg trouble.
2741: She came good at 5: open class early that year, then 2nd in the Kurofune Sho and Kakitsubata Kinen. She won the Hokkaido Sprint C. at 2.2, pulling clear from up front, then the Cluster C., then the JBC Ladies' Classic, surging from a forward spot - a G1 on a roll.
2742: She won her debut as 12th choice, placed steadily and reached open class early at 3. 3rd in the Fukuryu S. (OP), she won Kawasaki's Kanto Oaks as 4th choice, leading all the way by 2 lengths, the rest far behind. 3rd in the Breeders' Gold C. - dangerous in fillies' races.
2743: In open class in spring at 5, 10th in the Azuchijo S. (L), 6th in the CBC Sho and 5th in the Chukyo Kinen, he switched to dirt and won Saga's Summer Champion at once, breaking clear with Hizakurige and winning their duel by a nose. 10th as 3rd choice in the Tokyo Hai.
2744: She blossomed after reaching open class late at 4 (4th Brilliant S., 2nd Sleipnir S.), winning the Breeders' Gold C. as 2nd choice from up front. 3rd choice in the Ladies' Prelude, she won a straight duel with favorite Fashionista from midfield. At 6, 2nd in the TCK Jo-o Hai, she won the Empress Hai and retired to breed.
2745: A dirt sprinter who raced until 10 and won the Hokkaido Sprint C. at 10. Winning the 10-million class in January at 5, he struggled for about 3 years in the 16-million class, then moved to Hokkaido racing and won steadily. In the Hokkaido Sprint C., with JRA horses Matera Sky and Suzuka Causeline fancied, he narrowly caught Matera Sky - local pride.
2746: Debuting at 3, he won the Kyoto Shimbun Hai as 11th choice, beating later Derby winner Roger Barows. 11th choice again in the Derby, he closed from the back to 8th. 4th as 4th choice in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, he was 6th in the Kikuka Sho. Older, 3rd in the Naruo Kinen at 4 and 5th in the Kanmonkyo S. (OP) at 6 were his best; he retired at 7.
2747: By imported sire Cape Blanco. 3rd in the Kisaragi Sho, he won the Mainichi Hai as 3rd choice, leading all the way - his sire's first JRA graded win. Overlooked behind Saturnalia in the Satsuki Sho, he was last, then 15th in the Radio Nikkei Sho and 9th in the Cassiopeia S. (L), and failed on dirt too. From 5 he tried jumps, returned to the flat, and moved to local racing in April at 6.
2748: Beaten badly on dirt, he won at Kasamatsu early at 3, switched to turf and won a 5-million race at once, running in the Falcon S. and NZT that spring. A sprinter, he won the Hakodate Sprint S. at 4, leading all the way past later Sprinters S. winner Tower of London and other fancies - Sakura Orion's first graded winner. Unplaced in sprints after, a fracture found after the Centaur S. meant a long break; back in autumn at 5 in the Mainichi Okan, a year off and at a longer trip, he was last, and has struggled since.
2749: 4th as favorite on debut, he won a maiden and a 5-million race, then was 3rd choice behind Vin de Garde and Agulhas in the Kisaragi Sho; tracking in 2nd, he passed leader Lance of Prana and pulled clear. 3rd choice in the NHK Mile C., he was bumped by Gran Alegria in the straight, 4th. Injured before the Derby, he returned only in June at 4 in the Yonago S. (L), placing a few times without winning until January at 7, then became a riding horse.
2750: Unbeaten in 2, 5th in the Hanshin JF, a classic name at 3, she won the Fillies' Revue as 3rd choice - a rare dead heat with No One after a fierce duel. 6th in the Oka Sho, 12th in the NHK Mile C., 13th in the Keisei Hai AH, she turned to 1400m and below: at once 2nd in the Shin'etsu S. (L) and Auro C. (L), and 2nd to Sound Kiara in the Kyoto Himba S. at 4. She won the Auro C. that autumn. Winless in 3 races at 5, she retired after a 7th in the Kyoto Himba S.
2751: Winning his first 2 at Kawasaki easily, a lead hope among 2019 2yo dirt horses, he was 3rd off a break in the Gold Junior, won the Heiwa Sho (S3), then caught JRA leader Iolite by a head in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun - a first G1 for his sire, dirt star Espoir City, in his 3rd crop. At 3 he kept falling short as a fancy (5th Keihin Hai, 3rd Fuyo Sho) and was 12th in the Totsuka Kinen, then dropped in trip to win the Aki no Kura (SP1). At 4, last of 12 in the Kurofune Sho, he placed steadily in local races.
2752: Named after a French ski resort; out of a 3-win JRA mare, by sprint king Lord Kanaloa. Rated for speed before his debut, he won it easily as favorite, then the Shinzan Kinen. 8th as 2nd choice in the Arlington C., 6th in the NHK Mile C., and 13th as 2nd choice in the Cassiopeia S. (L).
2753: Debuting on dirt, he won a 5-million race in summer at 3, then struggled in the 10-million class and switched to turf. Winning it in his 2nd turf race, then the Idaten S. (OP), he won his first graded race, the Ibis Summer Dash, at 1.9. 11th in the 1200m Keeneland C., he was 2nd in the Lumiere Autumn Dash (L). At 5 he won the Idaten S. again, then was 2nd defending the Ibis Summer Dash. At 6, 16th on dirt in the Chiba S. and unplaced in the Idaten S., he was 2nd again in the Ibis Summer Dash. At 7, 10th in it - his first time out of the top two; at 8, 16th in a 5th straight Ibis Summer Dash, he moved to local racing.
2754: Highly rated, he won his debut with Lemaire, then the Keisei Hai as 4th choice, dominant from 2nd. A classic hope, he was 7th as 2nd choice in the Yayoi Sho and 7th in the Satsuki Sho, closing from midfield but unable to catch the leaders. At middle trips he was 2nd in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai late at 3, 3rd in the AJCC at 4, and 2nd to Authority in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai - capable at longer trips too.
2755: He won his first graded race, the Aoba Sho, leading from gate 1 and winning a straight duel with favorite Run for the Roses - a Derby ticket. Leading boldly in a hot-paced Derby, he faded to 15th. Favorite in the St. Lite Kinen, he won easily - a classic name again - but a tendon injury ruled him out of the Kikuka Sho.
2756: Close in his first 3 races, he won his 4th. 5th of 8 in the Kisaragi Sho, he won the Yayoi Sho as 8th of 10, dominating from midfield. Far back in the Satsuki Sho, Derby, St. Lite Kinen and Kikuka Sho, he gradually improved at long trips: 4th in the Stayers S., 2nd in the Diamond S. and 3rd in the Hanshin Daishoten at 4, 8th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), then 5th as 16th choice in the Takarazuka Kinen. After heavy defeats in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai and Stayers S., and at 5 (16th, 6th, 14th), injury meant 1.5 years off; unplaced after returning at 6, he retired in summer at 7.
2757: A filly with a rare record: a dead heat in the 2019 Fillies' Revue. Winning a maiden, she was 12th choice, slipped up the inside from midfield and dueled Pourville to the line; the photo showed a dead heat. Far back in the Oka Sho and Oaks, then unplaced as a sprinter: 8th Sprinters S., 14th Swan S.
2758: Winning his debut and a 5-million race, 2nd in the Falcon S., a 3yo sprint name, he was 10th as 4th choice in the NHK Mile C., then beat older horses in the Chukyo Kinen as 3rd choice, edging clear by a nose in a 4-way finish - the first 3yo winner in 49 years.
2759: 2nd as 4th choice on debut with a sharp late run, he won a maiden at 1.9 by 1 1/4 lengths. 5th choice behind Golconda and Darlington Hall in the Sapporo 2yo S., he burst clear from midfield and won with something in hand. In the classics, 4th in the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen, 9th in the Satsuki Sho, 7th in the Derby, then a fierce battle for 3rd as 14th choice in the Kikuka Sho (5th past the post).
2760: Unable to win a maiden on turf, he switched to dirt and won 3 classes in a row, then was 4th as 3rd choice in his first graded race, the Nagoya Daishoten. At 5, 2nd in the Heian S. and Marine S. (OP), he won the Elm S. as 2nd choice with the fastest finish from midfield. Since: 12th in the Sirius S. and Champions C.
2761: A Mombetsu filly who won the Edelweiss Sho. After a debut win she won a 2yo open race and the Fleur Cup (H3) as heavy favorite, then as 7th choice among local stars in the Edelweiss Sho, drew level early from midfield and pulled clear. Out of form at 3, she revived in autumn: 2nd in the Salvia C. (OP), 3rd in the Rosita Kinen (S1).
2762: Unbeaten in 2, he closed sharply for 5th in the Hopeful S. A classic hope, 3rd in the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen, he skipped the Satsuki Sho for the Aoba Sho, 3rd choice with Filio Allegro and Fly Like a Bird, and won by a neck, breaking clear wide from a handy spot. A fracture ruled out the Derby; back in autumn he won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai, then was 14th in the Arima Kinen. Stronger at 4, he was 2nd as favorite in the Diamond S. after a match race with Grondioz, 10th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), then won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai again and split Derby winners Contrail and Shahryar for 2nd in the Japan Cup. At 5, on his first trip abroad, he led all the way in Saudi Arabia's Neom Turf C., then was 3rd in the Dubai Sheema Classic. Scratched lame from the Takarazuka Kinen with a fracture, he returned at 6 in the Elm S. (12th), suffered a career-ending injury and went to stud.
2763: Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Kyoto 2yo S., a 2019 2yo name. He won his debut as favorite, the Nojigiku S. at 1.1 by 5 lengths, then the Kyoto 2yo S. at 1.5, moving early from midfield and coasting home. Yutaka Take called him "a horse with a big future." At 3 he lost momentum: 4th as hot favorite in the Kyodo News Hai, 13th in the Satsuki Sho, 9th in the Derby, last as 5th choice in the Kobe Shimbun Hai. Older, his best was 2nd in the Miyakooji S. (L) at 4. At 5, after 2 dirt races, he went to France as Do Deuce's companion, raced twice there and retired.
2764: Winning a turf maiden, he struggled in 5-million races, then switched to dirt late at 3 and won 3 classes in a row. 6th in the March S., 4th in the Mercury C., he won the Sirius S. as 6th choice, joining the lead at the 4th turn and winning a duel with Anglaiphen. In G1s he was 7th in the JBC Classic and 5th in the Tokyo Daishoten. The next year, 2nd in the Saga Kinen, he won the Nagoya Daishoten, then was 3rd in the Hakusan Daishoten and 2nd in the Nagoya GP.
2765: Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Asahi Hai FS - seen as Triple Crown winner Contrail's chief rival. He won his debut by 2 lengths, then after 4 months off won the Saudi Arabia Royal C. in race and 2yo course records. Favorite over Keio Hai winner Taisei Vision in the Asahi Hai FS, he raced forward in a hot pace, was joined in the straight, then pulled away by 2.5 lengths. At 3, a classic lead player against Hopeful S. winner Contrail, he was 2nd to the unbeaten Triple Crown winner in the Satsuki Sho and Derby - a worthy rival. Skipping the Kikuka Sho, he won the Mainichi Okan easily as favorite against older horses. 2nd choice in the Mile CS against Gran Alegria, he closed sharply but was 5th. At 4, 5th in the Osaka Hai (Contrail 3rd), 8th in the Yasuda Kinen, 6th in the Mile CS, he was 3rd in the Hong Kong Mile, best of the Japanese. At 5, 3rd in the Yasuda Kinen, he won the Mainichi Okan, his first win in 2 years, then was 14th as 3rd choice in the Mile CS. Withdrawn from the Hong Kong Mile with a leg problem, he retired.
2766: The 2020 NHK Mile C. winner. Debuting in June at 2, 3rd in the Kokura 2yo S., he won the Momiji S. (OP), then was 8th in the Asahi Hai FS. At 3 he led all the way in the Crocus S. (L); favorite in the Falcon S., he was caught by longshot Shine Garnet, 2nd. In the NHK Mile C., with 2yo queen and Oka Sho runner-up Resistencia, Arlington C. winner Taisei Vision and unbeaten Mainichi Hai winner Satono Impresa fancied, he was 9th choice, but tracked in 2nd, passed Resistencia in the straight and held on - his first graded win a G1. 2nd in the Fuji S., he was 15th in the Mile CS. At 4, 3rd in the Silk Road S., he won the Keio Hai SC, but was 14th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and Yasuda Kinen and unplaced in 4 autumn races. At 5, 4th in Saudi Arabia's 1351 Turf Sprint, 5th in the Keio Hai SC, 3rd in the Hanshin C.; unplaced at 6, he moved to Australia in May.
2767: Struggling in turf allowances, he won the 10-million class only in spring at 4, then switched to dirt and won 3 straight: the Aki S. (3-win), Enif S. (L) and Uzumasa S. (OP). 11th as favorite in the Musashino S., he won the Tokai S. as 2nd choice behind Inti, racing handy and taking over. A fracture meant a long break; back in autumn, 4th in the Miyako S., 10th in the Champions C. At 6, 5th as 10th choice in the February S., then unplaced and winless. At 7 he won the Muromachi S. (OP), and moved to local racing after a 5th in the Negishi S. at 8.
2768: She won her debut by 8 lengths - a stunning start; prone to rushing, jockey Yuga Kawada "deliberately started slowly" and waited in midfield. In the Artemis S. she again closed from midfield with a finish from another dimension, at 1.3. Hailed as a "monster," she was 1.8 favorite in the Hanshin JF but closed from last only to 6th. A classic fancy, she was 10th in the Oka Sho and 4th in the Oaks, then won the Rose S., Daring Tact's main rival for the Shuka Sho, but was 13th, and 7th in the QEII Cup. Older she flopped: 7th Nakayama Himba S., 9th Hanshin Himba S., 13th Victoria Mile, 9th Niigata Kinen, 17th Fuchu Himba S. At 5, 4th as 13th choice in the Mermaid S.; she retired to breed after the Aichi Hai at 6.
2769: She won her debut in August at 2 as favorite, was 2nd in the Artemis S., and won the Shinzan Kinen at 3. Straight into the Oka Sho as 3rd choice behind Resistencia and Daring Tact, she was 6th, then 13th in the Oaks and 16th in the Shuka Sho. 3rd in the Fukushima Himba S. when older, then beaten repeatedly, she retired to breed after the Niigata Himba S. (OP) at 5.
2770: A debut winner, always top five, he won his way up by spring at 4. 4th in the Lord Derby CT, he won the Azuchijo S. (L) as favorite, then the Swan S. by a nose in a 3-way finish, charging from behind midfield. At 5, 2nd in the Kyoto Kimpai, 3rd in the Hankyu Hai, 3rd on the same time in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, he won the Hakodate Sprint S. as favorite from 2nd. After a 15th and 13th, a fracture meant a long break; at 7 he was 4th in the Kyoto Kimpai, won the Hankyu Hai, was 4th in the Sprinters S., then won the Swan S. and his farewell Hanshin C. - 5 graded wins. He went to stud in Australia.
2771: Unbeaten in 2, he was 2nd to Contrail in the G1 Hopeful S. In the classics, as Contrail won the Triple Crown, he was 8th, 3rd and 7th, but 2nd in the Spring S. and Kobe Shimbun Hai (G2). 2nd in the AJCC at 4, a tendon injury cost over a year. Back at 5, he won the Naruo Kinen (G3), then was 3rd to Vela Azul in the Japan Cup (G1). At 6 he won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai (G2), 9th in the Osaka Hai, then the tendon injury recurred. 9th in the Epsom C. on return at 7, he has been kept out with leg trouble.
2772: 6th in the Queen C. early at 3, she switched to dirt and won a 5-million race and the Hosu S. (L) at once, then was 2nd in the Kanto Oaks. At 4 she won the TCK Jo-o Hai, taking over from 3rd and winning a long duel with Andes Queen. 2nd in the Ladies' Prelude and JBC Ladies' Classic, at 5 she was 4th, 3rd and 2nd in fillies' graded races, 9th on turf in the Tomoe Sho, and 2nd again in the JBC Ladies' Classic, then retired to breed.
2773: Unbeaten in 2, 9th in the Hanshin JF, she won the Shirayuri S. (L) at 3 but was 15th in the Fillies' Revue and 17th in the Shuka Sho. Older, 6th in the Nakayama Himba S. and Fukushima Himba S., she won the Queen S. as 11th choice, slipping through from midfield past favored Scarlet Color and others.
2774: Winning his 2nd start at 2, he then kept falling short until a 1-win race in summer at 3 - followed by 5 straight: 2-win, 3-win, the Port Island S. (L), then the Challenge C. as 2nd choice behind Gibeon, catching gritty leader Triomphe by a head from midfield. At 4 he was far back in the Kinko Sho and Osaka Hai, his only placing a 2nd in the Capital S. (L). At 5, 16th and 12th, then 5th as 12th choice in the Kyoto Daishoten, far back after; he moved to local racing in May at 6.
2775: Winning a maiden in his 4th start, then a class at 4 and 2 at 5, he won the Cassiopeia S. (L) in his 2nd open race. In graded races, 3rd in the Nakayama Kimpai and Fukushima Kinen at 6, he won the Kokura Daishoten at 7 as 11th choice, beating favorite Bocchelini by a nose in a straight duel, and retired.
2776: A dirt sprinter who won his first graded race, the Hokkaido Sprint C., at 6. Blooming at 4, he won 3 straight - a 5-million race, the Osu Tokubetsu and Naniwa S. - then was 3rd in the Tokyo Sprint. At 5 he won the Keiyo S. (L) and NST Sho (OP). He won the Hokkaido Sprint C. as 3rd choice, then was 2nd in his first mile race, the Nambu Hai. Far back in the Musashino S. and Hyogo Gold T.; at 7, 2nd Chiba S., 6th Tokyo Sprint, 4th Hokkaido Sprint C., 3rd NST Sho, winless. After heavy defeats, he retired to stud after the Reigetsu S. at 8.
2777: From the first crop of Kizuna, hailed as Deep Impact's heir - his 2nd graded winner. Beaten on debut, he led to win a maiden by 5 lengths. 3rd in a 1-win race, he won Hokkaido's top 2yo race, the Hokkaido 2yo Yushun, as 6th choice, leading all the way. At 3 he was 2nd on turf in the Wakaba S. (L), then 17th in the Satsuki Sho, 15th in the Naruo Kinen, 13th back on dirt in the Sirius S., and last (18th) as last choice in the Kikuka Sho. Always far back when older, he retired after the Fukushima Minpo Hai at 5.
2778: A hope from Kizuna's first crop. Winning a maiden and the Saffron Sho at 2, she was 2nd to Resistencia in the Hanshin JF, then beat her in the Tulip Sho at 3. Little fancied in the G1s: 8th as 5th choice in the Oka Sho, 10th as 12th choice in the Oaks. She won the Shion S., then was 7th as 4th choice in the Shuka Sho, and 2nd against older horses in the Hanshin C. At 4, unplaced in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and Victoria Mile, she was 3rd to Shadow Diva in the Fuchu Himba S., then unplaced until retiring to breed after the Nakayama Kinen at 5.
2779: By South Vigorous, a steady source of local graded winners. After 2 defeats he won his 3rd start by 8 lengths, then the Nadeshiko Sho, and his first graded race, the Hyogo Junior GP, leading early and holding on. 5th to local Vacation in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun, he won the Shoryu S. (OP) as favorite at 3 and was 3rd in the Shimotsuki S. At 4 he won the Subaru S. (L), the Kurofune Sho, was 2nd in the Kakitsubata Kinen, won the Teletama Hai Oval Sprint, was 9th in the Musashino S., then won the Hyogo Gold T. At 5 he won the Negishi S. (5th graded win), was 2nd in the February S. and 3rd in the Kashiwa Kinen, 2nd in the Tokyo Hai, then 7th as 2nd choice in the JBC Sprint. Unplaced at 6, he moved to local racing after the Urawa Kinen.
2780: Named after an Argentine city. The 2019 2yo queen, with five 2nds in sprint and mile G1s. Unbeaten in 3, she was 4th choice in the Hanshin JF as all eyes were on unbeaten "monster" Ria Amelia, but led boldly and pulled further clear in the straight with the fastest finish, winning by 5 lengths in a race-record 1:32.7, 0.4s faster than Vodka's 2006 time. Classic favorite at 3, she was 3rd in the Tulip Sho and 2nd to Daring Tact in the Oka Sho, then led early in the NHK Mile C. but was caught by longshot Laudacion, 2nd again. Straight into the Mile CS, she was 8th after a bold lead. Blooming as a sprinter at 4, she won the Hankyu Hai easily, then lost the Takamatsunomiya Kinen by a neck to Danon Smash. She won the Centaur S., was 2nd to younger Pixie Knight in the Sprinters S., and in the Hong Kong Sprint, hampered by another horse's fall, rallied to 2nd. At 5, 6th as favorite in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, 3rd in the Victoria Mile, far back in the Yasuda Kinen and Hong Kong Sprint. At 6, 5th in Saudi Arabia's 1351 Turf Sprint, she retired.
2781: A debut winner, 2nd in the Fantasy S. at 2. In the fillies' classics she was 12th in the Oka Sho, 5th as 14th choice in the Oaks, and 2nd as 10th choice in the Shuka Sho, 1 1/4 lengths behind Daring Tact. At 4 she won the Aichi Hai - no fluke - then was 2nd in the Hanshin Himba S., 3rd in the Victoria Mile and 2nd in the Queen S., but never won again and retired. Out of Oka Sho 3rd So Magic; half-brother So Glittering reached open class and half-brother So Valiant won the Challenge C. - a thriving family; much is hoped from her foals.
2782: A late-blooming dirt horse who won a graded race in autumn at 6. In open class only at 5, he struggled: 5th in the Negishi S., 9th in the February S. Switching to closing tactics, he steadied: 3rd Keyaki S., 1st Akhal-Teke S., 3rd Green Channel C. In the Musashino S. at 6, 9th choice without graded form, he swept from behind midfield to win.
2783: Unbeaten in 2, a graded winner. Under Fukunaga, he won his debut in a match race with Meisho Bosatsu, far clear of 3rd. In the Daily Hai 2yo S., 3rd choice behind Niigata 2yo S. runner-up Pale Ale and Succession, he charged past the field from the back. 3rd choice in the Asahi Hai FS, he closed in vain from the back, 10th to Salios. Throat surgery and a fracture kept him out; he retired in autumn at 3 and went to stud.
2784: The 3rd unbeaten Triple Crown winner, after Deep Impact. With Daring Tact also winning the fillies' Triple Crown unbeaten, 2020 was the "double triple." Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Hopeful S., he was the classic focus: in the Satsuki Sho he beat Asahi Hai FS winner Salios by half a length after a duel, then in the Derby led early in the straight and crushed him. In autumn he won the Kobe Shimbun Hai without the whip. A week after Daring Tact's triumph, under even more pressure, he was shadowed all the way by summer improver Aristoteles in the Kikuka Sho and won a long, grinding duel by a neck - the 8th Triple Crown winner, unbeaten like his sire Deep Impact. His camp and Daring Tact's agreed on a Japan Cup clash of unbeaten Triple Crown winners; 8-G1 champion Almond Eye joined - the race of the century. The senior star won, Contrail 2nd and Daring Tact 3rd, thrilling fans. Older, in the Osaka Hai against sprint queen Gran Alegria, he was 3rd behind runaway longshot Rei Papale. In the Tenno Sho (Autumn) he was 2nd to 3yo Satsuki winner Efforia - ahead of Gran Alegria both times, but doubts arose. In his farewell Japan Cup, billed vs. 3yo Derby winner Shahryar, he won as decisively as in his Triple Crown year - a 5th G1. Retiring to stud as Deep Impact's heir, his first crop is eagerly awaited.
2785: Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Akamatsu Sho, she was 4th in the Fairy S. at 3, then won the Falcon S. against colts as 6th choice, bursting clear from a handy spot and beating favorite Laudacion by 1.5 lengths. In the NHK Mile C. he turned the tables (6th). Unwell, she returned in the Turquoise S. (9th, behind crop-mate Smile Kana). At 4: 5th, 8th, 6th, 6th and 3rd, winless. At 5, 2nd in the Silk Road S., then unplaced; 2nd in the Lapis Lazuli S. (L), she retired to breed after the Silk Road S. at 6.
2786: Winning a maiden and the Mochinoki Sho at 2, she was 10th in the Hyacinth S. (L) and 5th in the Fukuryu S. (OP), then won the Kanto Oaks, bursting clear from a handy spot. 3rd as favorite in the Breeders' Gold C., 4th in the Ladies' Prelude, 5th in the JBC Ladies' Classic. Winless for a while at 4, she won the Ladies' Prelude, leading early and pulling 2.5 lengths clear, then was 4th as 2nd choice in the JBC Ladies' Classic. At 5, 4th in the TCK Jo-o Hai, 3rd, 3rd and 6th behind Shonan Nadeshiko, last in the Sirius S., then 4th as 8th choice in the JBC Ladies' Classic, and retired to breed.
2787: Winning her 2nd start easily, she was 2nd against colts in the Kyoto 2yo S., then won the Queen C. at 3 as 2nd choice, holding on from 2nd. 5th as 7th choice in a wide-open Oka Sho, she was 7th as 4th choice in the Oaks and 14th in the Shuka Sho. After a long break with no races at 4, she returned on dirt in the Uzumasa S. (OP) at 5 (12th), and after 2 more heavy defeats at 6 retired to breed.
2788: Winning his 2nd start, he was 12th in the Asahi Hai FS. Stuck in the 5-million class at 3, he came good at 4, winning 3 classes, then 4th as 11th choice in the Keeneland C. 2nd choice in the Keihan Hai, he closed sharply from midfield to win. A planned trip abroad was cancelled due to the pandemic; after 7 months off, 6th in the Hakodate Sprint S., he won the UHB Sho (OP). 2nd in graded races at 5 and 6 without winning, he raced to 7 and became a lead pony at Sapporo.
2789: She won her debut brilliantly, then kept placing (always top four) in allowances. In her first open race at 4, the G1 Victoria Mile, she was 7th as 15th choice. Blooming at 5, she won 3 graded races in a row - Kyoto Kimpai, Kyoto Himba S., Hanshin Himba S. - then was 2nd to Almond Eye in the Victoria Mile, among the top fillies at a mile. 10th as favorite in the Swan S. and 10th in the Mile CS, 4th in the Hanshin C. At 6, 6th and 11th, 2nd in the Swan S., 8th and 5th, she retired to breed.
2790: 11th in the G1 Hopeful S. at 2, he won the Spring S. at 3, sweeping past Weltreisende and others from midfield - a classic contender. 3rd in the Satsuki Sho behind Contrail and Salios, he was a close 6th in the Derby, doubted at the trip. 3rd in the St. Lite Kinen, 9th in the Kikuka Sho. Favorite against older horses in the December S., he closed fastest from midfield but couldn't catch leader Taurus Gemini, 3rd.
2791: After a 5-million win she ran in the Shuka Sho (10th), then won her way up, reaching open class in summer at 4. Struggling in graded races (6th Queen S., 8th Fuchu Himba S., 9th QEII Cup), she won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai as 8th choice, by a head in a 4-way finish. At 5, 2nd in the Kokura Kinen and 4th in the Niigata Kinen.
2792: His grand-dam Dyna Actress won 5 graded races incl. the Mainichi Okan and Sprinters S. (then G2); his dam Best Location was 2nd in the Kyoto Himba S. Carrying both names, he won the Hankyu Hai at 6. Blooming in autumn at 5, he won the Kanagawa Shimbun Hai, Hibari S. and the Hankyu Hai - 3 straight, and his dam's first graded-winning foal.
2793: Winning his debut at Oi, he then struggled on JRA turf, rising slowly and reaching open class in spring at 5. 10th choice in his first graded race, the Niigata Daishoten, he won by 1.5 lengths. 7th in the Takarazuka Kinen and 6th in the Sapporo Kinen, gritty, he won the Hakodate Kinen at 6, breaking clear from up front. 2nd in the Niigata Kinen, he was 15th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). 5th in the Nakayama Kimpai at 7, he moved to local racing, and in November at 7 a dislocation proved fatal.
2794: A dirt sprinter who won the Kakitsubata Kinen twice. Winning allowances in January at 4, he won his first graded race, the Kurofune Sho, then the Kakitsubata Kinen. At 5 he won the Kakitsubata Kinen and Summer Champion. 3rd going for a 3rd Kakitsubata Kinen at 6, he was 2nd in the Korea Sprint and won the Hyogo Gold T. - 5 graded wins. Winless at 7, but 5th in the JBC Sprint.
2795: He won his debut and a 1-win race as favorite, then the NZT - 3 straight - as 2nd choice in a wide-open field, sweeping past them all from the back. 5th from the back in the NHK Mile C., then last as 2nd choice against older horses in the Keisei Hai AH. Double-figure finishes at 4 and 5; at 6 he tried dirt, 2nd in the Valentine S. (OP), but leg trouble ended his career.
2796: Debuting in January at 3, she won a 2-win race the next January, then stalled in the 3-win class and stepped up for the Mermaid S. Among rivals mostly without graded wins, she was 7th choice, tracked in 2nd and held off the fancies. 3rd choice in the Kokura Kinen, she was 13th.
2797: Unbeaten in 2, 13th in the Unicorn S., he restarted in allowances and won 3 classes from autumn at 4 to spring at 5. Raced little after, he began in open class at 6: he won the Tempozan S. (OP), then the Summer Champion, leading all the way. 4th in the Oval Sprint.
2798: He went to America in spring at 3 for the Kentucky Derby (6th) and Belmont S. (5th), showing talent with sharp late runs. Back home he soon won allowances, was 2nd in the Brilliant S. (L) and Sleipnir S. (OP), then won the Mercury C., Hakusan Daishoten and Nagoya GP, all as favorite. 4th in the Diolite Kinen at 5, he won the Mercury C. again. 4th in the Hakusan Daishoten, a fracture followed and he retired to stud.
2799: The first Japanese graded winner by New Approach, of Galileo's line. A debut winner, 3rd in the Sapporo 2yo S. and Habotan Sho, he won the Kyodo News Hai at 3, breaking clear with Bitter Ender and winning by a nose. 6th in the Satsuki Sho and 13th in the Derby.
2800: Always fancied and steady from his debut, he won the 3-win class in spring at 4, then was 4th in the Niigata Daishoten and 2nd in the Tanabata Sho. 2nd choice in the Niigata Kinen, he saved energy in midfield for the long straight and won by a head in a 3-way finish. 2nd in the Challenge C., unplaced in 4 races at 5, then 4th twice at 6 and far back at 7, he went to stud in Argentina.
2801: By Danon Ballade, of Deep Impact's line - his first graded winner. Racing at middle-long trips on turf, he won only a maiden, then switched to dirt when older and won 3 classes to open class, the BSN Sho (L), then the Nippon TV Hai, dominant from a handy spot. Favorite in the Urawa Kinen, he lost by a nose to Danon Pharaoh. At 5, 6th in the Kawasaki Kinen, then 3rd, 3rd, 13th, 3rd, 2nd and 5th in the Tokyo Daishoten - no win. After over a year off, back at 7 with heavy defeats, he moved to Kochi.
2802: Unbeaten in 2, he was 2nd to Grenadier Guards in the G1 Asahi Hai FS. At 3, 5th in the Kyodo News Hai, he was 3rd to Efforia in the Satsuki Sho and to Shahryar in the Derby, then won the Kobe Shimbun Hai and was a close 4th in the Kikuka Sho - top four in all 3 classics. 3rd choice in a star-studded Arima Kinen, he was 4th. At 4, 2nd in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai, he was last of 5 Japanese (9th) in the Dubai Sheema Classic. A tendon injury meant a long break; back in autumn at 5, he won the Osakajo S. (L) at 6 and was 4th in the Osaka Hai, then 3rd in the Sapporo Kinen, retiring that year.
2803: By spring at 3, 2nd in the Wakagoma S. (L) and Sumire S. (L), still a 1-win horse. Winning 2 in summer, he bloomed; 4th choice in the Kikuka Sho without graded experience, he almost stopped Contrail's Triple Crown, beaten a neck. At 4 he won the AJCC, a spring G1 fancy, but was 4th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and 9th in the Takarazuka Kinen. 2nd in the Kyoto Daishoten, he faded from up front to 9th in the Japan Cup.
2804: Winner of the 1975 Takarazuka Kinen; his dam Eight Crown also won it - the first mother-son double. Debuting in summer at 3 (old age system), injury cost him nearly a year, and he first won in autumn at 4, then 4 straight to the Chukyo Kinen at 5. He won the Kimpai (West) at 6, and at 7 the Chukyo Kinen, Naruo Kinen and Takarazuka Kinen. In 5 Tenno Sho tries his best was 4th; he retired in autumn at 7 with 5 graded wins. His foals included Kabutoyama Kinen winner Cherry Tesco.
2805: Winning a maiden in his 3rd start, 8th in the Daily Hai 2yo S., he was unremarkable at 2. At 3 he was 3rd in the Shinzan Kinen, then won the Kisaragi Sho as 7th of 8, catching gritty Stone Ridge from 3rd. 7th in the Satsuki Sho and 12th in the Derby, he fractured after; injuries kept him out until June at 5. Two defeats, another break, and winless at 6, he retired.
2806: Winning her debut and the Hiiragi Sho, she won the Fairy S. at 3, leading from a fine start and pulling 2.5 lengths clear. 7th in the Tulip Sho, she was 9th choice in the Oka Sho but hung on to 3rd behind Daring Tact and Resistencia. That summer she won the Yonago S. (L) and was 2nd in the Keisei Hai AH - 2nd in the Summer Mile Series. After a 10th and 2nd, she won the Turquoise S. from up front, holding off Andrasta by a nose. At 4, 14th as favorite in the Lord Derby CT, then 15th and 10th - a sharp decline. All double-figure finishes as an older mare, she retired to breed after the Nakayama Himba S. at 5.
2807: A leading Kizuna colt. He won his debut charging from the back, then the Keisei Hai as 7th choice, closing sharply from the back again and sweeping past gritty favorite Sky Groove. 16th in the Satsuki Sho, a tendon injury meant a long break.
2808: 2nd in the Shirayuri S. (L) at 3, outclassed in graded races (9th Kyoto Shimbun Hai, 17th St. Lite Kinen), he matured at 4 and won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai as 2nd choice, pulling clear from a handy spot. 7th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he was 3rd to Chrono Genesis as 12th choice in the Takarazuka Kinen. At 5, 5th in the AJCC, he beat Triple Crown winner Contrail and sprint queen Gran Alegria for 2nd in the Osaka Hai, then 8th, 13th and 13th. Injured in January at 6, he missed a whole year; back at 7, 10th in the Nakayama Kinen, 4th in the Niigata Daishoten, he retired with a tendon injury after the Takarazuka Kinen.
2809: Winning the 3-win class late at 3, she was 2nd in the Silk Road S. at 4, then won the Keeneland C. on her 3rd sprint graded try, 5th choice behind Hakodate Sprint winner Diatonic and Keihan Hai winner Light On Cue, sweeping wide from last. In the Sprinters S. she finished far back for the first time, then 14th and 15th at 5. She was 2nd defending the Keeneland C. and won the Keihan Hai as 10th choice with a brilliant late run. Unplaced in 5 races at 6, she retired to breed after the Silk Road S. at 7.
2810: A late bloomer from the end of 5, he won the 2022 Takamatsunomiya Kinen at 6 - a rarity among sprinters. Winning his debut in autumn at 2, he then struggled, winning 3 classes only from summer to the end of 3. In open class he kept falling short until a 2nd in the Opal S. (L) in autumn at 5, then won the Tanzanite S. (OP). At 6, 3rd in the Silk Road S. and 2nd in the Ocean S., he won the Takamatsunomiya Kinen as 8th choice, charging from last and edging clear of a 5-horse blanket finish by a neck. 3rd to Gendarme in the Sprinters S., 10th in the Hong Kong Sprint. At 7, 4th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, 17th in the Yasuda Kinen and 9th in the Sprinters S., he retired that year.
2811: A late-blooming stayer racing at 2000m+ from his debut. Winning 3 straight in spring at 3, 14th in the St. Lite Kinen, he won the Geishun S. (3-win), then became a long-distance graded regular: 3rd Diamond S., 6th Meguro Kinen. Late at 4 he won the Stayers S. as 7th choice, winning a duel with Tagano Diamante from up front. 9th in the Arima Kinen against the best. At 5 (6th, 13th, 6th), he was withdrawn from the Stayers S. with gait trouble, never returned, and retired to stud at the end of 7.
2812: 6th on debut, he won 3 straight incl. the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen - a classic focus, one of a Big Three with Contrail and Salios in the Satsuki Sho, but faded from midfield to 5th, then 11th as 4th choice in the Derby. 2nd in the St. Lite Kinen and 3rd to Contrail in the Kikuka Sho. Older, 11th AJCC, 7th Kinko Sho, he closed sharply to lose by a neck to Zadar in the Epsom C., then was injured. Back after 1 year 7 months in the Shirafuji S. (L) at 6, he broke down and was pulled up; he went to stud in Argentina.
2813: She won her debut as favorite, then fell short (5th Shiraume Sho, 4th Elfin S.), and won the Fillies' Revue, switching to waiting tactics and closing with a superior kick. 11th choice in an Oka Sho with Daring Tact and Resistencia, she missed the break, 9th. After a year off, 5th in the Hanshin Himba S. at 4 and 7th in the Keio Hai SC, she won her first 1200m race, the Lapis Lazuli S. (L), and retired to breed after the Silk Road S. at 5.
2814: Debuting at 3 with a win, she won the Flower C. as 12th of 14, tracking in 2nd, leading in the straight and holding on. Unbeaten in 2, she was 17th in the Oaks, 12th in the Rose S. and 11th in the Shuka Sho. At 4, 4th in the Aichi Hai, she won the May S. (OP) but no more graded races. She often outran her odds: 2nd as 12th choice in the Nakayama Himba S. at 5, 4th as 11th choice in her farewell Aichi Hai at 6. Retired to breed.
2815: Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Mainichi Hai, charging from last and passing favorite Arjanna with ease. An odd route - NHK Mile C. (13th), then the Derby (4th) - showed his talent. With Salios among the fancied 3yos in the Mainichi Okan, he missed the break, 10th; 2 weeks later, 12th in the Kikuka Sho.
2816: Losing 5 on turf, he switched to dirt in June at 3 and won a maiden and 5-million race - the real start. Winning 2 classes in summer at 4, he placed in open races (3rd Fukushima Minyu C., 1st Pollux S., 2nd Aldebaran S.), then won the March S. as favorite, leading early from 3rd. Struggling in graded races (5th Heian S., 8th Miyako S.), he was 2nd in the Onuma S. (L) and won the Marine S. (OP) at 6, then the Elm S. from up front. At 7 he won the Tokai S. as 7th choice, then faded and moved to Oi in summer.
2817: Placing 2nd, 2nd and 4th on turf, he switched to dirt and won a maiden and 5-million race at once, reaching open class with the Kunpu S. in spring at 4. 3rd as 8th choice in the March S. at 5, he won the Radio Nippon Sho (OP), then the March S. at 6, taking over in the straight from a handy spot. Little else but a 5th in the Elm S.; he retired after the Negishi S. at 7.
2818: The 6th fillies' Triple Crown winner and the only unbeaten one, from new sire Epiphaneia's first crop - a big title at once. She first showed her talent in her 2nd start, the Elfin S. (L): slow away, she alone found an otherworldly kick and won by 4 lengths. Straight into the Oka Sho on rain-soaked ground, she charged from the back past 2yo queen Resistencia and the rest. Oaks favorite at 1.6, she was still near the back at the 4th turn and passed them all in the straight. Straight into the Shuka Sho at 1.4, she moved early and won with ease - an unbeaten Triple Crown in just 5 starts. In the Japan Cup against unbeaten colt Triple Crown winner Contrail and 8-G1 Almond Eye, she was 3rd in a race of the century. At 4, at short odds in the Kinko Sho, she lost by a neck to longshot Gibeon, then was 3rd behind Loves Only You and Glory Vase in Hong Kong's QEII Cup; in May a suspensory injury sidelined her. After a year off she was 6th in the Victoria Mile, 3rd to Titleholder in the Takarazuka Kinen and 4th to Vela Azul in the Japan Cup. Leg trouble led to her retirement in autumn at 6.
2819: 2nd in the Arlington C. and 3rd in the NHK Mile C. at 3, then 2nd in the Kyoto Himba S. and 3rd in the Turquoise S. at 4 without winning, she switched to dirt in summer at 5: she won the NST Sho (OP), 2nd in the Green Channel C. (L), then the Musashino S. with a powerful late run - a graded win on her new surface. 2nd to Lemon Pop in the Negishi S. at 6, a February S. hope, she was injured and retired to breed.
2820: She made her name in the 2020 Oaks, half a length behind later Triple Crown filly Daring Tact. Little noticed, she won the Flora S. by a whisker as 4th choice, then as 7th choice in the Oaks tracked in 2nd and held on almost to the line - a fine ride by Norihiro Yokoyama, standing in for his son Takeshi. 15th in the Shuka Sho, she was 4th as 9th choice in the QEII Cup, best of the 3yos. At 4 she won the Nikkei Sho, 5th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), and the All Comers - a force against males at middle-long trips - but 16th as 3rd choice in the QEII Cup. At 5, after a 16th and 7th, she was 3rd in the Sapporo Kinen and 2nd to Geraldina in her 3rd QEII Cup, then won the Hong Kong Vase - the only winner among 13 Japanese runners, her G1 at last, abroad. At 6, unplaced in Dubai, the Sapporo Kinen and All Comers, she held 4th in the BC Filly & Mare Turf, then retired after a 7th in the Arima Kinen to breed.
2821: At 3, 10th in the Satsuki Sho (G1), he won the Kyoto Shimbun Hai (G2), then improved: 5th in the Derby, 4th in the Kikuka Sho. At 4 he won the Hanshin Daishoten (G2) easily from up front, then was 2nd as favorite to World Premiere in the Tenno Sho (Spring). In France he won the Prix Foy (G2), then was 14th in the Arc (G1), and 2nd in a strong Arima Kinen. At 5 he repeated his record exactly: Hanshin Daishoten win, 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Spring); 4th in the Takarazuka Kinen and 18th in a 2nd Arc. At 6 he was 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Spring) for a 3rd straight year - an odd record. At 7, 3rd in a 4th Tenno Sho (Spring) and 2nd in the Kyoto Daishoten.
2822: At 1600-1800m, 5 wins from 13 by autumn at 5, almost always top three. Reaching open class with the Namba S. in spring at 4, he was 3rd in the Milers C. and Chukyo Kinen at 5, then won the Keisei Hai AH as favorite from up front, by a neck over Mikki Brillante. In the Mile CS, at his best trip, he was unplaced for the first time, 13th.
2823: Winning a maiden in his 5th start, he tried the Mainichi Hai at once (9th of 13), then worked through allowances. Strong at 4, he won 3 classes in a row, then the G2 Meguro Kinen as favorite, charging from the back. 3rd as 2nd choice in the Kyoto Daishoten. After about a year off with a fracture, he won the AJCC at 6. Winless after, 5th in the Swan S., he went to stud after the Hanshin C.
2824: Highly rated from the start: in the QEII Cup at 4, without a graded win, she was fancied alongside Loves Only You, Chrono Genesis and Lucky Lilac, and was 4th. 5th in the Aichi Hai, 2nd in the Mermaid S., she won the All Comers in autumn at 5, charging wide from the back and just catching leader Curren Bouquet d'Or. In the QEII Cup, as Lucky Lilac won again, she closed well for 5th.
2825: He won his debut by 10 lengths, the Hyacinth S. (L) as favorite, and the Unicorn S. as favorite by 5 lengths - unbeaten in 3. 7th as favorite in the G1 Japan Dirt Derby, he won the Sirius S., then was 2nd choice at 3 in the Champions C. but 6th behind Chuwa Wizard and others. Stronger older, he won the February S. as favorite, leading from a handy spot. A dirt star in the making, he was 5th as favorite in the Kashiwa Kinen, 9th on turf in the Hakodate Kinen, and 11th as 4th choice in the Champions C. At 5 he won the February S. again by 2.5 lengths, was 17th on turf in the Yasuda Kinen, and won the Nambu Hai - 3 dirt G1s. At 6, 3rd in the Saudi Cup, 12th in the Dubai World Cup and Yasuda Kinen, he was 5th in the Nambu Hai and retired.
2826: Winning a 1-win race in spring at 3, he was 3rd as 11th choice in his first graded race, the Unicorn S., then won the Leopard S. as 7th choice, blasting to the lead and pulling away as the fancies floundered. 11th in the Musashino S.
2827: 2nd twice, he won a maiden in his 3rd start, then surged: the Sanaebo Sho, the Radio Nikkei Sho as 8th choice by 5 lengths, and the St. Lite Kinen over Satono Flag and Gallo Creek - 4 straight. 3rd choice in the Kikuka Sho, he was 10th. In the Arima Kinen he led as usual but faded after the 4th turn, 13th.
2828: Winning his 3rd start, he was 6th in the Hopeful S. and 9th in the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen. 2nd in the Radio Nikkei Sho, October S. (L) and Kanmonkyo S., he won the October S. in autumn at 4, then the Fukushima Kinen, leading all the way. At 5 he won the Nakayama Kinen, then dead-heated with Lord North in the Dubai Turf - a G1 abroad. 2nd by a neck in the Sapporo Kinen, he set off far clear in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and was caught near the line by Equinox, 2nd - a thrilling run. At 6 he tried dirt abroad and won the Saudi Cup, then was 10th in the Dubai World Cup. In his farewell Japan Cup he led far clear as ever, thrilling the crowd (12th).
2829: Unbeaten in 2 incl. the 2020 Hakodate 2yo S. Winning her debut as favorite from up front, she was 10th choice among debut winners in the Hakodate 2yo S., but held a handy spot and resisted gritty Luce d'Oro and fast-closing Love Kelly - the season's first graded win. 12th in the Keio Hai 2yo S. and Hanshin JF. At 3, 4th in the Marguerite S. (L), then far back as a sprinter; unplaced at 3 and 4, she retired to breed.
2830: A turf sprinter who won the Chukyo Kinen in summer at 5. In open class from autumn at 4, 4th in the Shin'etsu S. (L), then heavy defeats. In the Chukyo Kinen, last choice of 18, he moved up from midfield and won a blanket finish - a shock even to his camp. With longshots 2nd and 3rd, the trifecta paid 3.3 million yen. Occasionally 5th as a longshot after, he retired after the Rokko S. (L) at 7.
2831: It took 20 starts to leave the allowance ranks, but he was top five in 16. In open class early at 5, 4th in the Osakajo S. (L) and 2nd in the Miyakooji S. (L), he was 3rd in his first graded race, the Hakodate Kinen, then won the Fukushima Kinen as 2nd choice, beating favorite Vanqueur Domingo by a neck. At 6, heavy defeats, then 3rd as 12th choice in the Hakodate Kinen. From 7, in listed and open races without success; retired at 8.
2832: A specialist over Niigata's 1000m straight. He won the Hiyoku Tokubetsu and Shunpu S. there, was 10th in the Lumiere Autumn Dash (L), 2nd in the Idaten S. (OP), then won the Ibis Summer Dash as 2nd choice, avenging Idaten winner Lion Boss. Unplaced in the Kitakyushu Kinen, Keihan Hai and on dirt in the Capella S.
2833: A pure sprinter who won the Ibis Summer Dash at 7. Winning a 5-million race early at 3, then a class at 4 and the 3-win class in summer at 5, she was a close 3rd in the Ibis Summer Dash at 5. Unplaced after, she won it at the 3rd try at 7 as 7th choice. Meant to race on, she retired with leg trouble to breed.
2834: Winning through the classes with 4 wins from 6, always top three, she raced in graded races from spring at 4: 3rd in the Sekiya Kinen, 2nd in the Turquoise S., then the Chukyo Kinen at 5 as favorite, breaking clear from a handy spot. 8th in the Sekiya Kinen, 2nd to Shadow Diva in the Fuchu Himba S. and to Miss New York in the Turquoise S. Injured before the Kyoto Kimpai at 6, she retired to breed.
2835: Six straight 2nds in the 1-win class, then wins up to the 3-win class, he stepped up for the Kokura Kinen as 10th choice behind Rambling Alley and Kikuka runner-up Satono Luks, sat 6th and slipped up the rail to win. Winless after at middle-long trips, he moved to local racing in April at 7.
2836: By Irish sire Gleneagles, of Galileo's line - the only graded winner among his 5 runners in Japan as of 2022. 3rd on debut, he won a maiden by 4 lengths, then the Niigata 2yo S., racing forward and bursting clear down the middle of the long straight. A longshot fancy in the Asahi Hai FS, he faded from a handy spot, 13th. At 3, 10th in the Falcon S., 13th in the NHK Mile C.; at 4, 5th in the Rakuyo S. at best.
2837: Heir to the white coat of grand-dam Shirayuki Hime and dam Buchiko, the first white horse to win a turf G1. She won a 7-runner debut easily from 2nd, then the Sapporo 2yo S. as 2nd choice, holding off Uberleben by a neck - the first JRA turf graded win by a white horse - and the Artemis S. easily as favorite. Favorite in the Hanshin JF, with a possible world-first G1 for a white horse at stake, she was boxed in at the top of the straight, split the pack and won a duel with Satono Reinas by a nose. At 3, a real classic contender, she went straight to the Oka Sho as co-favorite with Satono Reinas and beat her. Closely marked as Oaks favorite, she was 8th, then beat older stars Loves Only You and Blast Onepiece in the Sapporo Kinen. 10th as favorite in the Shuka Sho, she tried dirt in the Champions C. (12th). At 4, 3rd in the February S. on dirt, she won the Victoria Mile from up front for a 3rd G1, 2nd in the Fuchu Himba S., 3rd in the Mile CS. At 5 she lost the Victoria Mile by a head, then was 7th as 2nd choice in the Yasuda Kinen and retired.
2838: The 2021 Oaks winner. A debut winner, 2nd to Sodashi in the Sapporo 2yo S., 3rd to her from the back in the Hanshin JF. 3rd as favorite in the Flower C., she switched her aim to the Oaks; 3rd in the Flora S., but rated, she was 3rd choice behind Sodashi and later Shuka Sho winner Akaitorino Musume, and charged clear from the back - the 82nd Oaks winner. Straight into the Shuka Sho as 5th choice, she was 13th, then 6th in the Japan Cup with a sharp finish. At 4, 5th in the Kyoto Kinen and Dubai Sheema Classic, then 11th, 8th and 10th. 3rd in the AJCC at 5, she retired with a tendon injury.
2839: He won his debut easily, was 3rd to Sodashi in the Sapporo 2yo S., 6th in the Kyoto 2yo S. and 4th in the Asahi Hai FS. At 3 he gave Naho Furukawa her first JRA win, then won the NZT, leading and pulling away. In the NHK Mile C. he was pulled up after his rider fell; 15th in the Derby, then far back in autumn. At 4 he led all the way in Dubai's Godolphin Mile as next-to-last choice, then was 4th in England's Sussex S. and 7th in France's Jacques le Marois. 3rd in the Musashino S., at 5 he won Saudi Arabia's 1351 Turf Sprint and was 4th in the Godolphin Mile again, then 3rd in the Sakitama Hai and Korea Sprint, but 7th in the JBC Sprint and 15th in the Mile CS.
2840: In open class from spring at 5, he was 3rd in his first graded race, the Niigata Kinen, and 3rd to Salios in the Mainichi Okan, then won the Niigata Daishoten at 6, closing from the back as usual. 4th to Efforia in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and to Contrail in the Japan Cup - G1-capable. At 7: 3rd Kyoto Kinen, 7th Kinko Sho, 3rd Naruo Kinen, 5th Hakodate Kinen, 8th Niigata Kinen, 4th Challenge C. - no win. He raced until the Tanabata Sho at 8 without another.
2842: A 2020 debut crop colt who won the Keio Hai 2yo S. Beaten a head as favorite on debut, he won a maiden by a huge margin, then was hot favorite in the Kokura 2yo S., 2nd to Meikei Yell. In the Keio Hai 2yo S. he broke clear from up front and held on by a neck. He led far clear in the Asahi Hai FS but faded 200m out, 10th. At 3, 3rd in the Falcon S., 5th as favorite in the Aoi S., 12th in the Ibis Summer Dash. At 4, 16th on dirt in the Keiyo S.; apart from a 5th in the Kitakyushu Kinen, rarely top five.
2843: The first Kumamoto-bred to win a JRA graded race; her name means "it's fine, it's fine" in Kyushu dialect. Unbeaten in 3, 5th in the Fantasy S., she was 5th to Sodashi as 10th choice in the Hanshin JF. 2nd in the Fillies' Revue at 3, she was 17th in the Oka Sho, then 2nd in the Aoi S. and 5th in the CBC Sho before winning the Kitakyushu Kinen in her native Kyushu. A fracture in training before the Sprinters S. ended her career; she retired to breed.
2844: Winning his 2nd start and the Nojigiku S. (OP), he was 2nd to Red Bel Orbe in the Daily Hai 2yo S. 9th in the Asahi Hai FS, he won the Arlington C. at 3, tracking in 2nd and leading in the straight. 9th in the NHK Mile C., he was 3rd in the Swan S., held 5th from the front in the Mile CS, 2nd in the Hanshin C. and Milers C. at 4. Often far back after, his only good run was 3rd in the Hankyu Hai at 5.
2846: A filly who closes sharply from the back. Debuting at 3, unbeaten in 2 incl. the Sweet Pea S. (L), she was 2nd choice behind Daring Tact in the Oaks but 11th; in the Rose S. she charged from last for 4th to Ria Amelia. Stronger older, she won the Hatsune S. (3-win) and the Hanshin Himba S. 8th as 4th choice in the Victoria Mile, then 16th and 8th in autumn. At 5, 3rd in the Aichi Hai and Hanshin Himba S., 15th in the Victoria Mile; a tendon injury followed and she retired to breed.
2847: Winning his 2nd turf start, then far back in 5-million races, he switched to dirt and won 2 in a row, then the Ou S. and Shiwasu S. (L) late at 3. 2nd choice in his first graded race, the Saga Kinen, he tracked in 2nd, led early and outdueled favorite Lord Gorasso - 3 straight. 3rd in the Nagoya Daishoten, he slumped, won the Sobu S. (OP) at 5, and moved to local racing at 7.
2848: Stuck in the 2-win class after 9 turf races to summer at 3, he switched to dirt and won the Myokenzan Tokubetsu and Kadomatsu S., reaching open class early at 4. Losing the Yamato S., he won the Chiba S. (OP) by a street, then led all the way in his first graded race, the Tokyo Sprint, and won the Tokyo Hai. 8th as favorite in the JBC Sprint, he won the Capella S. (G3). Winless at 5 (best 4th Cluster C.), at 6 he won the Yamato S. and was 3rd in the Cluster C. and Capella S. Moving to Oi in summer at 7, he beat JRA visitors in the Tokyo Sprint at 8 and won Funabashi's Kamui Yukara Sprint (OP).
2849: Named after a huge nebula in Orion. Winning a maiden and 1-win race, he was favorite with Lemaire in his first graded race, the Hyogo Championship, and won a straight duel with Danon Pharaoh from 3rd. 3rd choice in the G1 Japan Dirt Derby, he was 8th as the fancies collapsed. Beaten badly when older, he moved to local racing in February at 5.
2850: She was 3rd to later Triple Crown filly Daring Tact as 13th choice in the Oaks. Fancied in autumn, she was 6th in the Shion S. and 9th in the Shuka Sho, then kept finishing unplaced until the Mermaid S. at 5: 10th choice at 14.6 in a wide-open race, she won from a handy spot. 3rd to Vela Azul in the Kyoto Daishoten, 16th in the QEII Cup, 6th as 15th choice in the Arima Kinen. At 6, 6th in the Kyoto Kinen, 2nd in the Mermaid S., then nothing; she retired to breed after the Challenge C.
2851: Winning 2 classes at 4, he raced in mile-to-middle graded races (3rd Epsom C., 4th Hakodate Kinen) and won open races like the Tomoe Sho, December S. (L) and Kochi S. (L). 5th as 13th choice to Danon Kingly in the Yasuda Kinen at 5, he won the Tanabata Sho that summer, tracking in 2nd and outdueling leader Rosamour by a neck. Unplaced in the Sapporo Kinen, Mainichi Okan and all graded races at 6-7, he retired after the Tanabata Sho at 7 and became a lead pony.
2852: By American Pharoah, US Triple Crown and BC Classic winner and a hot sire; a leading runner of his first crop in Japan. Winning a maiden and 1-win race, he was 2nd in the Hyogo Championship, then won the Japan Dirt Derby. With fellow American Pharoah son Cafe Pharoah hot favorite, he was 6th choice at 40.6, but tracked in 2nd and wore down gritty Daimei Corrida. 5th against older horses in the JBC Classic, he won the Urawa Kinen. At 4, 3rd in the Kawasaki Kinen, he won the Diolite Kinen, but was 9th in the Teio Sho, 7th in the JBC Classic and 16th in the Champions C. - and suspended for rearing in the gate. At 5, 4th in the Diolite Kinen, then heavy defeats; after a 13th in the March S. at 6, he moved to local racing.
2853: By Pas de Trois, a 3-time sprint graded winner - his first graded-winning foal. Debuting late in summer at 3 and winless, he moved to Funabashi, won 3, returned to the JRA and won 3 more classes. 3rd in the Capella S. at 4, he won the Keiyo S. (L) at 5, then the Capella S., breaking clear from up front past Mozu Superflare and Ryuno Yukina. At 6 he won Saudi Arabia's Riyadh Dirt Sprint, then the Hokkaido Sprint C. and JBC Sprint - a G1. At 7, 5th in both Riyadh and the Hokkaido Sprint C., he was pulled up after his rider fell in the JBC Sprint, and retired.
2854: A mare who, with Yuga Kawada, won her first 6 incl. the Osaka Hai. Debuting at 3, she won 4 straight through the classes, then the Challenge C. in her first open race, at 1.6 against older horses, leading all the way. 4th choice in the Osaka Hai against Triple Crown winner Contrail and mile queen Gran Alegria, she led and pulled away - rivaling Contrail and Daring Tact as best of her crop. 3rd to Chrono Genesis in the Takarazuka Kinen, 4th in the All Comers, she pulled throughout and tired as favorite in the QEII Cup, 6th. At 5, 2nd in the Kinko Sho, she led mid-straight in the Osaka Hai but was caught by 8th choice Potager, 2nd. After 3 more poor runs, she retired to breed after a 9th in the Hong Kong Cup.
2855: Winning the 2-win class in spring at 4, she flopped in turf graded races, then switched to dirt and won the Sakurajima S. at once, then the Ladies' Prelude as favorite, sweeping wide at the 4th turn and pulling away without the whip. 3rd at 1.3 in the JBC Ladies' Classic. At 5 she won the TCK Jo-o Hai and Empress Hai, was 8th in the Teio Sho, won the Breeders' Gold C., then in America won a fierce duel with Dunbar Road in the BC Distaff - the first Japanese winner of a dirt G1 abroad. After a 6th in her farewell Saudi Cup, she retired to breed.
2856: He won 4 straight from summer at 3: a maiden, 1-win race, Kyushu Sports Hai and Shiori S. Struggling in open class, he won the Procyon S. in his 4th try as 9th choice, from a handy spot by 2.5 lengths. In autumn at 4 he won the Hakusan Daishoten and Urawa Kinen.
2857: Debuting in spring at 3, he passed the allowance ranks by the end of 4 and won the Osakajo S. (L) at 5. Short in graded races (6th Niigata Daishoten, 5th Naruo Kinen), he won the Nakayama Kimpai at 7 from a handy spot by 2.5 lengths, then the Niigata Daishoten. Unplaced in the Sapporo Kinen, Kyoto Daishoten, Tenno Sho (Autumn), and on dirt in the Champions C. and Tokyo Daishoten, he retired after the AJCC at 8 to become a riding horse.
2858: Beaten a head on debut, he won a maiden easily, leading at the 4th turn and pulling away. At 1.3 in the Daily Hai 2yo S. he beat 2nd choice Hoh O Amazon by a head - 2 straight record times. Favorite in the Asahi Hai FS, he was 3rd. Straight into the Satsuki Sho, 8th from up front, he fractured. Back in spring at 4, rarely top five, he won the Kokura Nikkei OP in summer.
2859: A Just a Way colt after Velox, sold for 100 million yen at the Select Sale. He won his debut impressively, then the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. at 1.7 from a handy spot - a precious graded win for his sire amid a battle of new sires like Maurice, Duramente and Kizuna. Favorite in the Hopeful S., he won unbeaten in 3 after Saturnalia (2018) and Contrail (2019) - trainer Takayuki Yasuda's first middle-distance turf G1 for a sprint-famed stable. Classic favorite, he was 3rd at short odds in the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen and 15th in the Satsuki Sho, then fractured. Back in autumn, 4th in the Fuji S., 3rd in the Mile CS behind Gran Alegria and Schnell Meister. At 4, 7th and 6th in spring, 3rd in the Sekiya Kinen and Mainichi Okan, 2nd to Serifos in the Mile CS and in the Hong Kong Cup, best of the Japanese. At 5, 11th in the Nakayama Kinen, 3rd as a longshot in the Osaka Hai, 5th of 7 in Hong Kong's QEII Cup, 13th in the Takarazuka Kinen, 5th in the Mile CS - erratic. After a 12th in the Hong Kong Mile he retired to stud.
2841: By Deep Impact's son Mikki Isle; from his first crop (debuting 2020), his first graded winner. She won her debut as favorite, the Kokura 2yo S. after a duel with Mont Reve from midfield, and the Fantasy S. from up front - unbeaten in 3. 3rd choice in the Hanshin JF, she closed from the back for 4th. At 3 she dead-heated with Elizabeth Tower in the Tulip Sho at 1.6, but Yutaka Take flagged her temper, which left her last (18th) in the Oka Sho. Turning to sprints, she closed sharply for 4th in the Sprinters S. At 4 she won the Silk Road S. and Keio Hai SC, and the Centaur S. from up front by 2.5 lengths, but was 14th as favorite in the Sprinters S. and 5th as 2nd choice in the Hong Kong Sprint. At 5, pushed to favoritism in a wide-open Takamatsunomiya Kinen, she was 12th, then 15th in the Yasuda Kinen; 5th in the Sprinters S., she was last in the BC Filly & Mare Sprint.
2845: The first JRA graded winner by imported sire Makfi. Winning her debut and the Canna S. (OP), 3rd to Gold Chalice in the Chukyo 2yo S., she was 5th in the Marguerite S. (L) and 3rd in the Aoi S. at 3, then won the Ibis Summer Dash as favorite over Lion Boss and Mont Reve with the fastest finish. 8th in the Keihan Hai; at 4, 10th, 6th and 6th defending the Ibis Summer Dash. After a year off, she won it again on her return at 5 as 9th choice - 2 years after her first. 13th in the Sprinters S. and last on her dirt debut in the Capella S., she retired to breed.
2860: Winner of the 2021 Kikuka Sho, and older the Tenno Sho (Spring) and Takarazuka Kinen - a ruler of 2021-2022. He won his debut as favorite, then was 2nd to Danon the Kid in the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. and 4th in the Hopeful S. At 3 he won the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen, his sire Duramente's first graded winner. 2nd to Efforia in the Satsuki Sho, 6th from the front to Shahryar in the Derby, 13th as favorite in the St. Lite Kinen. In a Kikuka Sho without either classic winner, 4th choice, he led and pulled further clear - a classic title. From the wide outside draw he held on for 5th in the Arima Kinen. At 4 he won the Nikkei Sho at short odds, the Tenno Sho (Spring) by 7 lengths, and the Takarazuka Kinen over crop rival Efforia - best in training. 11th in the Arc, he was 9th to new star Equinox in the Arima Kinen. At 5 he won the Nikkei Sho, but was pulled up lame defending the Tenno Sho (Spring). 2nd in the All Comers, he held 5th from 2nd in the Japan Cup, then led and held 3rd in his farewell Arima Kinen, retiring to stud.
2861: Much noticed from his debut, he won a dirt debut at 1.7, then the Yamaboushi Sho by 7 lengths as 3rd choice, leading all the way. At 1.9 in the Hyogo Junior GP he led again and held on by half a length. Favorite in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun, hoping to give sire Mikki Isle a first G1, he was 7th. At 3, 2nd in the Shoryu S. (OP), unplaced in the Tango S. and NST Sho, he won the Muromachi S. (OP) from up front. At 4, sprinting in open races, he won the Tennozan S. and Osaka Sports Hai (both OP).
2862: 2021 JRA Horse of the Year, winner of the Satsuki Sho, and at 3 the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen. By Epiphaneia, sire of Triple Crown filly Daring Tact the year before, much noticed, he won his debut as favorite and the Hyakunichiso Tokubetsu. At 3 he crushed later Derby winner Shahryar and others in the Kyodo News Hai, then won the Satsuki Sho from up front, 2nd choice behind Danon the Kid - unbeaten in 4. Derby favorite at 1.7, he led in the straight but was caught by Shahryar by a nose - his first defeat. Skipping the Kikuka Sho, he beat Triple Crown winner Contrail and sprint queen Gran Alegria in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), the first 3yo winner in 19 years since Symboli Kris S. Top of the fan vote in the Arima Kinen, against Chrono Genesis bidding for a 4th straight Grand Prix, he swept wide and ran them down - the Tenno Sho (Autumn)-Arima double at 3 like his grandsire Symboli Kris S, "best in training." Older he lost his shine: 9th as hot favorite in the Osaka Hai, 6th as favorite in the Takarazuka Kinen, 5th as 5th choice in the Arima Kinen. Pulled up in the Kyoto Kinen at 5 - checks found nothing - he retired as a precaution. First stud fee: 3 million yen.
2863: Unbeaten in 2, 3rd to Danon the Kid in the G1 Hopeful S., 2nd in the Kisaragi Sho, he went straight to the classics: 5th as 11th choice in the Satsuki Sho, 7th in the Derby. Injured in autumn, back at 4, he won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai (G2), outdueling crop-mate and favorite Stella Veloce. A tendon injury cost 2 years; back in spring at 6, 3rd in the Kinko Sho and Niigata Daishoten, he won the Naruo Kinen. At 7 he won the Kyoto Kinen, 3rd in the Osaka Hai and All Comers - still going strong.
2864: By Deep Impact out of Apapane - both Triple Crown winners. In the 4th year of this mating came a star: the 2021 Shuka Sho winner. 7th on debut, she won a maiden and the Akamatsu Sho, then the Queen C. at 3 - 3 straight. 4th to Sodashi in the Oka Sho, 2nd choice in the Oaks, she was 2nd to Uberleben as Sodashi sank. Straight into the Shuka Sho, 4th choice behind Sodashi and improvers Fine Rouge and Andvaranaut, she won from up front - a G1. In the QEII Cup, billed vs. older Rei Papale, both faltered; she was 7th. Scratched at the gate with a leg problem before the Hanshin Himba S. at 4, she retired to breed.
2865: A Hokkaido mare who debuted at Mombetsu and won the Edelweiss Sho. Beaten a head on debut, she won a maiden by 4 lengths, then 3 straight as favorite, and the Edelweiss Sho as hot favorite against JRA horses for the first time, by 4 lengths from a handy spot. At 3 she won the Toritsuki Tokubetsu (Mombetsu) and Hayate Sprint (Morioka), then was last on her turf debut in the JRA's Keeneland C. Back home, she has lost badly.
2866: A Hokkaido horse, first winner of the JBC 2yo Yushun, new in 2020. At Mombetsu, with JRA horses Taisei Again and Luce d'Oro fancied, he was 6th choice, broke clear from a handy spot and held off local Transcendence. Last-to-10th in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun. At 3 he swept Hokkaido's local Triple Crown - Hokuto Hai, Hokkai Yushun and Okan Sho - then was 4th in Morioka's Derby Grand Prix. He later moved to Kawasaki and Sonoda, winning several local stakes there.
2867: A hope from Rulership's next crops after Kiseki. 2nd to Danon the Kid on debut, he won a maiden by 8 lengths. After a 3rd in the Hagi S. (L), he won the Kyoto 2yo S. as 3rd choice, creeping up from the back through the turns and winning a duel with Lagom. At 3, returning in May, he won the Aoba Sho after a duel with Kingston Boy, then was 10th to Shahryar in the Derby and 8th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai. After a long break, back at 4, he has been unplaced.
2868: A debut winner, 2nd in the Ivy S. (L) and Kyoto 2yo S., he won the Kisaragi Sho at 3, holding off Yoho Lake from up front. 13th in the Satsuki Sho, 12th in the Derby and Niigata Kinen, he won the Andromeda S. (L), then was 13th and 9th. Switched to dirt at 4, he won the Azuma Kofuji S. (OP), was 2nd in the Hakusan Daishoten and Urawa Kinen, 3rd in the Nagoya GP. Back on turf at 5 (9th, 4th), he retired.
2869: The 2021 Derby winner; full brother of 2017 Satsuki Sho winner Al Ain. A debut winner at 2, he was 3rd to later Satsuki winner Efforia in the Kyodo News Hai, then won the Mainichi Hai (G3). In the Derby, 4th choice behind Efforia and Oka Sho runner-up Satono Reinas, he tracked Efforia from midfield and caught him by a nose. Favorite in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, 4th on heavy ground, he skipped the Kikuka Sho for the Japan Cup and was 3rd to Triple Crown winner Contrail - a worthy flag-bearer. At 4 he won the Dubai Sheema Classic (G1) by a neck, then was 4th of 5 in England's Prince of Wales's S. and 5th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), then closed sharply for 2nd to Vela Azul in the Japan Cup. At 5, 5th in Dubai, 11th in the Sapporo Kinen, 3rd in the BC Turf, 5th in the Arima Kinen. At 6, 2nd in Dubai, 3rd in the BC Turf, and a nose 2nd to Regaleira in the Arima Kinen, then retired. Only 7 of 74 mares conceived in his first stud year, and retirement was considered, but tests found his fertility normal and he stays at stud.
2870: Unbeaten in 2, outclassed at 3 (13th Aoba Sho, 10th St. Lite Kinen) but 3rd from the front in the Radio Nikkei Sho, he restarted, winning the 2-win class in autumn at 3 and the 3-win class in spring at 4. Back in graded company, he won the Epsom C. from up front. At 5 he won the AJCC; at 6, 3rd in Hong Kong's QEII Cup (G1), then the Sapporo Kinen (G2) - 3 graded wins.
2871: Full brother of 2015 Tenno Sho winner Lovely Day. Much noticed, always fancied, he rose through allowances at 3-4, then 2nd in the Kokura Nikkei OP and Cassiopeia S. (L). In his first graded race, the Chunichi Shimbun Hai late at 4, 2nd choice close behind classic star Velox, he swept from midfield to win. At 5, 2nd in the Kokura Daishoten, 5th and 4th after. At 6, stepping up in trip, 3rd in the AJCC, 2nd in the Nikkei Sho, he won the Meguro Kinen; 2nd in the Kyoto Daishoten, outclassed in the Japan Cup (17th) and Arima Kinen (11th). At 7, 2nd in the Nikkei Sho, he won the Naruo Kinen, then 2nd in the Kyoto Daishoten and Challenge C., and at 8 2nd in the AJCC and Naruo Kinen.
2872: A blueblood by European great Frankel out of fast BC Filly & Mare Sprint winner Wavell Avenue. Ducking in on left-handed tracks in his first 2 starts, he was transformed going right-handed at Hanshin 1400m, winning in 1:20.4, 0.3s off the 2yo course record. 7th choice in the Asahi Hai FS, he sat 3rd as Mont Reve set a hot pace 5+ lengths clear, spurted before the 4th turn, caught him 200m out and held on in a Hanshin 1600m 2yo record 1:32.3 - a fine, bold ride by Kawada on fast ground. At 3, a mile hope, he was 2nd in the Falcon S., 3rd in the NHK Mile C. and Keisei Hai AH, then 13th in the Mile CS as crop-mates Schnell Meister and Danon the Kid held their own. He charged wide to win the Hanshin C., his first win in a year. At 4, 12th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and 19th in England's Platinum Jubilee S., then 2nd in the Hanshin C. At 5, 7th as hot favorite in the Hankyu Hai, 5th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, a fracture; 6th in the Swan S., 2nd in his farewell Hanshin C., and to stud.
2873: Won the 2021 Sprinters S. at 3, showcasing his crop's strength. He won his debut as favorite, then the Shinzan Kinen at 3 as 4th choice, leading all the way. 4th as 2nd choice in the Arlington C. and 12th in the NHK Mile C., both fading from the front, he focused on sprints: 2nd to Fast Force in the CBC Sho, 2nd by a neck to Resistencia in the Centaur S. In the Sprinters S., 3rd choice behind Takamatsunomiya and Hong Kong Sprint winner Danon Smash and Resistencia, he broke clear from a handy spot and pulled away from Resistencia for a G1. In the Hong Kong Sprint he was brought down in another horse's fall and pulled up; the injury kept him out all of 4. Back at 5, 13th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, then unplaced, he retired after a 15th in the Hanshin C.
2874: A leading 2021 3yo filly. She won the Fairy S. early at 3, then was 3rd to Sodashi as 8th choice in the Oka Sho. 4th choice in the Oaks, she was 11th. She won the Shion S., then was 2nd choice behind Sodashi in the Shuka Sho and closed sharply from the back for 2nd to Akaitorino Musume. At 4, 2nd in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai, she was 2nd to Sodashi in the Victoria Mile - a crop 1-2 - then 5th in the Yasuda Kinen, retiring to breed.
2875: Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Keisei Hai, leading at the 4th turn from a handy spot and pulling away. After 3 months off he was 6th in the Satsuki Sho and 8th in the Derby; 9th as 3rd choice in the St. Lite Kinen, 15th as 14th choice in the Kikuka Sho. At 4, 3rd in the Shirafuji S. (L) at 2000m, he dropped to miles: 5th in the Kochi S. (L), 4th in the Lord Derby CT, 3rd in the Kan'etsu S. (OP).
2876: Out of 2006 Oka Sho winner Kiss to Heaven, whose foals had disappointed until he won the Lord Derby CT (G3). 2nd in the Keisei Hai and NZT at 3, he kept falling short, then unplaced in 3 listed races late at 3 and at 4. Out of favor at 11th choice in the Lord Derby CT, he closed from the back with an otherworldly kick to win. 3rd in the Keio Hai SC, 5th in the Epsom C., then a long slump, until he charged to 2nd as 14th choice in the Keisei Hai AH at 6.
2877: A Funabashi horse who won the Kawasaki Kinen and Kashiwa Kinen. Blooming late at 3, he was 2nd to Omega Perfume in his first G1, the Tokyo Daishoten, late at 4. At 5 he beat Omega Perfume in the Kawasaki Kinen, won the Keisei Hai Grand Milers, then the Kashiwa Kinen - 3 straight, 2 G1s. The local hope was 7th to T O Keynes in the Champions C. The next year, 5th Kawasaki Kinen, 4th Kashiwa Kinen, 10th Tokyo Daishoten - out of rhythm.
2878: A foreign-bred son of British sire Kingman; 2021 NHK Mile C. winner. Unbeaten in 2, he was 2nd to Titleholder in the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen, then skipped the Satsuki Sho for the NHK Mile C. 2nd choice behind 2yo champion Grenadier Guards, he won a duel with Songline by a nose from midfield - his first graded win a G1. 4th choice against older stars in the Yasuda Kinen, he held 3rd behind Danon Kingly and Gran Alegria. He beat Danon Kingly in the Mainichi Okan, then was 2nd to Gran Alegria, bidding to repeat, in the Mile CS - a fine 3yo flag-bearer.
