At 4, 8th in the Dubai Turf, he lost the Yasuda Kinen by a neck to Songline, then was 9th in the Sprinters S., 5th in the Mile CS and 9th in the Hong Kong Mile. At 5 he won the Milers C., 3rd in the Yasuda Kinen for a 3rd year, 3rd in the Mainichi Okan, then 7th as favorite in the Mile CS and retired.
2879: A debut winner at 2, he then struggled long in allowances, winning a 1-win race late at 3 and a 2-win race in January at 4. At 5 he stepped up to win the Nikkei Shinshun Hai - unplaced only 3 times in 16. 10th in the Hanshin Daishoten, he retired.
2880: Debuting in Hokkaido with 2 wins, he raced in the JRA: 1st in the Suzuran Sho (OP), 2nd in the Fukushima 2yo S. Far back in the Kyodo News Hai and Arlington C. at 3, he moved to the JRA that autumn and raced in dirt sprints. Winning the Hatsuharu S. in January at 5 to open class, at 6 he won the January S. and Yamato S. (both OP), then the Tokyo Sprint - 3 straight - and the Cluster C. 2nd in the Tokyo Hai, 5th in the JBC Sprint. At 7, 2nd in the Tokyo Sprint, Cluster C. and JBC Sprint - no win. At 8 he won the Tokyo Sprint again, then placed without winning, and after a 4th in the Capella S. moved to local racing.
2881: 15th on his turf debut, he won easily on dirt next time and was always top five on dirt after. At 3 he won a 1-win race, was 2nd in the Fukuryu S. (OP), won a 2-win race, then the Leopard S. as favorite by 3 lengths. 5th as 2nd choice in the Miyako S., 10th in the Shiwasu S. (L), he then rested about a year.
2882: A debut winner, 5th in the Artemis S., then 10th in the Fairy S. and 5th in the Flower C., she won the Flora S. as 5th choice, breaking clear from a handy spot by a length. In the Oaks she led and faded, 14th; 11th in the Rose S., 15th in the Shuka Sho. At 4 only a 4th in the Kan'etsu S. (OP); kept in training at 5 but never ran, she retired to breed in September.
2883: Winning a 1-win race in her 9th start, she won the Hosu S. (L), then the Kanto Oaks as favorite, breaking clear and beating Cerasus Via by 2 lengths. A close 3rd in the Japan Dirt Derby, 3rd in the Ladies' Prelude, 10th in the Queen Sho. At 4, 2nd by a nose in the Marine S. and by a neck in the Elm S., then nearly a year off; 13th on return at 5, she retired to breed.
2884: Always top three in allowances, he reached open class early at 4 and won the Coral S. (L) and Muromachi S. (OP). 2nd in the Capella S., he won the Negishi S. at 5, then was 4th in the February S. and 2nd in Dubai's Golden Shaheen, and won the JBC Sprint easily as favorite - a G1. At 6, 6th in the February S., 2nd in the Golden Shaheen again, he won the Tokyo Hai but was 4th as favorite defending the JBC Sprint. At 7, the same route: February S. 2nd, Golden Shaheen 6th; 3rd in the Musashino S.
2885: From Leondeux's first crop, he gave his sire a quick graded win in the Hyogo Championship. Winning a maiden in his 4th start and a 1-win race, he was 2nd choice well behind hot favorite God Selection, but outdueled him by half a length. 5th in the Japan Dirt Derby and 15th in the Mile CS (Nambu Hai). After 11 months off, 15th in the Uzumasa S. and 8th in the Galaxy S. at 4.
2886: Winning a maiden and the Yukiusagi Sho in spring at 3, she won the Aoi S. as 13th choice, leading early and holding off Yokayoka by a nose. 3rd choice in the Keeneland C., she won by a head in a blanket finish - 4 straight. 16th as 2nd choice in the Keihan Hai; 4th in the Hakodate Sprint S. at 4, then all double-figure finishes, she retired to breed.
2887: A flagship son of Sea The Stars with 6 G1s, mainly European miles. Debuting late in June at 3, he won 4 straight incl. a graded race, then the Prix du Moulin in September, his first G1, and beat favorite Palace Pier by a neck in the Queen Elizabeth II S. At 4 he won the Lockinge S., Queen Anne S. and Sussex S., then stepped up to the International S. (about 2060m) and won by 6 lengths - 10 from 10. In his farewell Champion S. he lacked his usual kick, 4th, his only defeat. Highly prized, he went to stud in 2023.
2888: 5th in the Hanshin JF (G1) and 3rd in the Oka Sho (G1), a classic name until spring at 3, she then turned to sprints, winning the Hakodate Sprint S. (G3), and at 4 the Silk Road S. and Keeneland C. (G3). In G1s, 2nd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and 3rd in the Sprinters S. At 5, again 2nd and 3rd, just short of a G1; she won the Hanshin C. (G2), a 5th sprint graded win. At 6, curiously, the same: 2nd in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, 3rd in the Sprinters S. - 3 years running.
2889: Half-sister of 2019 3yo filly star Shigeru Pink Diamond. She won her debut easily, then was 17th in the Hanshin JF. At 3 she won the Fillies' Revue, catching Yokayoka from midfield, then was 16th in the Oka Sho. As a sprinter, 4th in the Kitakyushu Kinen, 5th in the Keihan Hai, 4th in the Kyoto Himba S., she won the Kurama S. (OP). Unplaced in graded races after, she retired to breed after finishing last in the Michinoku S. (OP) at 5.
2890: A late-blooming sprinter who won the 2023 Takamatsunomiya Kinen at 7. His only graded win before was the CBC Sho, and he had flopped in every G1 - then came the race of his life. Losing his first 6, he was deregistered in summer at 3 and moved to Hokkaido racing, won 3, and returned to the JRA in summer at 4. As a sprinter he won a 1-win race and the Seibu Sponichi Sho at once, then the CBC Sho at 5 off a break as 8th choice, leading all the way, and was 2nd to Yokayoka in the Kitakyushu Kinen - Summer Sprint champion. Then 15th in the Sprinters S., 7th in the Hanshin C., 9th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen at 6. At 7 he was 2nd as 10th choice in the Silk Road S., then won the Takamatsunomiya Kinen as 12th choice, breaking clear from a handy spot as the leaders collapsed in a hot pace - a superb ride by Taisei Danno. He retired to stud.
2891: A 2021-2022 dirt star with 3 G1s: Teio Sho, Champions C., JBC Classic. Winning a 1-win race early at 3 and 2 more classes in autumn, he was 2nd in the Betelgeuse S. (L), then 6th but only 0.2s behind Omega Perfume in the Tokyo Daishoten a week later. At 4 he won the Nagoyajo S. (OP), the Antares S. and the Teio Sho by 3 lengths - 3 straight and a G1. Favorite in the JBC Classic, slow away, 4th. Favorite again in the Champions C. over Chuwa Wizard and Inti, he won by 6 lengths from a handy spot. At 5, 8th in the Saudi Cup, he won the Heian S. and JBC Classic, then was 4th at 1.5 defending the Champions C. At 6, no G1 win but always close: 2nd Kawasaki Kinen, 4th Dubai World Cup, 3rd Teio Sho and JBC Classic, 4th Champions C. - his farewell before stud.
2892: Winning a maiden in spring at 3 and a 1-win race in summer, she blossomed in autumn, stepping up to win the Rose S. as 4th choice from a handy spot. 3rd choice in the Shuka Sho behind Sodashi and Fine Rouge, she drew level in the straight and was 3rd behind Akaitorino Musume and Fine Rouge. At 4, 2nd in the Hanshin Himba S., 3rd in the Fuchu Himba S., but 14th in the Victoria Mile and 17th in the QEII Cup.
2893: Winless in 13 dirt starts, he switched to turf and won a 1-win race in his 3rd try, then another and the Sarakurayama Tokubetsu - 3 straight. Unable to win the 3-win class, he stepped up for the Kokura Kinen in summer at 4 and, 6th of 9, charged thrillingly from last to win. After a 4th as 14th choice in the Niigata Daishoten at 5, he switched to jumps after the Kokura Kinen at 6.
2894: Beaten badly at first, he won a maiden in his 8th start, then was unplaced in almost every race but a 1-win victory in June at 4. Late that year he won the 2-win class, the Wakashio S. early at 5, then the Tokyo Shimbun Hai - 3 straight. 13th after a slow start in the Yasuda Kinen, he was 2nd in the Sekiya Kinen and 5th in the Keisei Hai AH. At 6 he won the New Year S. (L), 3rd in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai, 2nd in the Nakayama Kinen; 16th in the Yasuda Kinen, he stepped up to 2000m and won the Niigata Kinen. 6th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 8th in the Japan Cup. At 7 he won the Niigata Daishoten, then 9th in the Naruo Kinen and 16th in the Takarazuka Kinen.
2895: 3rd on debut, she won a maiden easily, then was 2nd to Fine Rouge as 8th choice in the Fairy S. at 3, and won the Flower C. as 5th choice, breaking clear early. Losing her sparkle, 9th to Sodashi in the Oka Sho, she missed the Oaks unwell, then was 13th in the Shion S. and 16th in the Shuka Sho after a slow start. At 4, 5th in the Kan'etsu S. (OP), then 2nd to stablemate Hoh O Emeuse in the Niigata Himba S. (OP) - a 1-2 for one owner.
2896: A great mare who won 6 G1s in a row in 2021-2022, ending with an Arc at 5. A debut winner, she won only 1 of 3 at 2; at 3, 2nd in her first G1, the Yorkshire Oaks, but just 1 listed win from 4. Blooming at 4, she won a listed race, the Lancashire Oaks, then the Grosser Preis von Berlin and 2 more German G1s - unbeaten in 5, 3 G1s. At 5 she won the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud and Yorkshire Oaks - 5 straight G1s - and went to the Arc as 2nd choice against Japan's Titleholder and Irish Champion winner Luxembourg. Racing 4th-5th on rain-soaked ground, she passed Titleholder 300m out and held off French Derby winner Vadeni and defending champion Torquator Tasso - 6 straight G1s, and the first 5yo mare to win the Arc in 85 years. A Japan Cup farewell was rumored, to Japanese fans' delight, but injury in training ended her career; she retired to breed.
2897: Rated the best gelding in US history: 34 wins from 57, 14 G1s, racing until 8, and 8th in The Blood-Horse's top 100 US racehorses of the 20th century. As crop-mate Secretariat drew the spotlight, he bloomed from autumn at 3. His first G1, the Widener H. at 4, was followed by the Woodward S., Jockey Club Gold C. and more - Horse of the Year. He won from 7 furlongs (Vosburgh H.) to 12 (Woodward S.) and even 16 (Jockey Club Gold C.) - truly versatile. Carrying huge weights from then on, he still won the Brooklyn H. and Suburban H., Horse of the Year 3 years running to 6, and won the Woodward S. 4 years in a row (4-7). He died in 1997 at 27; the G1 Forego S. has honored him since 2001.
2898: Winner of the 1976 Tenno Sho (Autumn). Last of 8 in the Yayoi Sho at 4 (old age system), he raced mostly in allowances, nearly always top three, rising slowly and blooming at 6. He won the Kimpai (East) over Arima Kinen winner Ishino Arashi, was 2nd in the Nakayama Kinen and 3rd in the Keio Hai SH, and won the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai. That autumn, after an open win, he won the Tenno Sho (Autumn), a Big Eight race, breaking clear from midfield by 1 3/4 lengths over Harbor Young. In the Arima Kinen, behind 4yos Tosho Boy and Ten Point, he was 3rd, best of the older horses. At 7 he won the Nakayama Kinen and Argentina Kyowakoku Hai, retiring after a 4th in the Takarazuka Kinen. At stud just 3 years; no notable foals.
2899: Dam of Tenno Sho (Autumn) winners Fujino Perseus and Three Giants. She won only a maiden in 7 starts, retiring in March at 4 (old age system) to breed at once. She had 11 foals by 22. Her first, Western Pearl, won 3 and produced graded winner Higashi Majorca. Her 2nd, Fujino Perseus, won the 1975 Tenno Sho (Autumn), Takarazuka Kinen and Takamatsunomiya Hai (4 graded wins); her 4th, Three Giants, won the 1979 Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Diamond S. - only the 3rd brothers to win the Tenno Sho, raising her standing. No other stars; daughters like Western Young and Sengoku Rose bred on without notable grandchildren.
2900: Winner of the 1975 Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 1976 Takarazuka Kinen. In allowances through 4 (old age system), he won the Tokyo Shimbun Hai at 5 and became a force: 2nd in the Argentina Kyowakoku Hai and Nihon Keizai Sho, 2 open wins, then the Tenno Sho (Autumn) as 2nd choice by 1 3/4 lengths over Colonel Symboli. Arima Kinen favorite, he was caught by longshot Ishino Arashi, 2nd, but at 6, after the Diamond S., won the Takarazuka Kinen as favorite over Ishino Arashi and others. He also won the Takamatsunomiya Hai, then was 6th in America's Washington DC International. 8th behind 4yos Tosho Boy and Ten Point in the Arima Kinen, he retired. No notable foals.
2901: One of Ireland's greatest stayers, winning 5 G1s in the 1970s incl. 3 Gold Cups, dominant at 3000m+. Skipping the classics at 3, he won the Prix de l'Esperance (G3, 3000m), then the Grand Prix de Paris (then 3100m), his first G1, and was 11th to Allez France in the Arc. At 4 he won the 4000m Gold Cup; at 5 the Prix du Cadran and Gold Cup, both 4000m - king of the stayers. At 6, 2nd in the Prix Jean Prat and Cadran, he won a 3rd straight Gold Cup and retired. At stud he passed on too much stamina, perhaps, and sired no stars.
2902: Dam of Kaburaya O, who won the Satsuki Sho and Derby with astonishing front-running, and QEII Cup winner Miss Kaburaya - full siblings by Pharamond, the best offspring of both mare and sire. She won 6 of 32, debuting at 4 (old age system), winning her 6th start and 5 allowances by the end of 5, then retired after 2 heavy defeats over jumps. Her 2nd foal Kaburaya O won the 1975 Satsuki Sho and Derby; bred to Pharamond again that year, she produced her 4th foal, Miss Kaburaya. Miss Kaburaya failed as a broodmare, ending the line. Others incl. Derby runner My Horse (4 wins) and Silver Kaburaya (3 wins).
2903: Dam of 1975 2-classic filly Tesco Gaby. Her 6th dam was Keen Dra, a foundation mare imported by Koiwai Farm in the Meiji era - a line with fewer stars than others, of which she was the most notable. She won only a maiden in 25 starts, retiring at 5 (old age system). Her 2nd foal Tesco Gaby won the Oka Sho and Oaks, making her name - a star from an unproven mating, as sire Tesco Boy was then new. Tesco Gaby was put down at 5, ending that line. Of 13 other foals, the best was Todoroki Hiryu, an Oi star who won the Tokyo Daishoten and Tokyo Hai.
2904: Winner of the 1975 Oka Sho and Oaks, a shock to Japanese racing with her blazing speed - called "the greatest filly ever." She ran away with her debut, the 3yo S. (old age system) and her first graded race, the Keisei Hai 3yo S., then won the Keisei Hai at 4 and sought tougher rivals in the Tokyo 4yo S. (now Kyodo News Hai), losing by a neck to later Satsuki and Derby winner Kaburaya O - impressive in defeat. After an easy Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu as hot favorite, she led in the Oka Sho and kept drawing away to win by a huge margin - unheard of in the race. 3rd in the 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, perhaps tired, she led to win the Oaks by 8 lengths, still a JRA record margin. Injuries followed, and in January at 6 she died of a heart attack, leaving no foals - a great pity.
2905: Dam of Green Grass; herself winner of 2 graded races, the Tanabata Sho and Fukushima Daishoten. In allowances until summer at 4 (old age system), she was 2nd in her first graded race, the Fukushima Daishoten. Blooming at 5, she won it as favorite, then the Tanabata Sho as 2nd choice, beating Hakusen Sho by a head, but lost the Fukushima Kinen to him by a head. Strong in summer local races, she was called a "summer girl"; winless after, she placed in local graded races until autumn at 6. Her 3rd foal Green Grass formed the "TTG Big Three" with Tosho Boy and Ten Point, raising her standing; she also produced Queen S. winner Hazama First (by Barbare).
2906: Winner of the 1976 Oka Sho and Oaks, following Tesco Gaby as a 2-classic filly. Early to shine, she won 3 open races at 3 (old age system), champion 3yo filly. At 4 she won the Queen C., then the Oka Sho as joint favorite with Squash Solon, charging wide with a superior finish despite a slow start, and the Oaks as favorite, breaking clear from a handy spot - top of her crop. 4th in the All Comers and 4th to Diamante in the QEII Cup, she missed a 3rd crown, but held her own against older horses with Tosho Boy and Ten Point, 5th in the Arima Kinen. Older she faded: far back as 2nd choice in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and Nakayama Himba S., she retired winless after a 6th in the Kabutoyama Kinen. No notable foals.
2907: Known as the dam of Ten Point, she won the 1966 Oka Sho. 12th on debut, she won 3 allowances, then the Oka Sho as 4th choice, beating Hiroyoshi and Mejiro Bosatsu by a neck after a fierce duel. 14th in the 4yo Himba Tokubetsu and 7th in the Oaks, she raced in open and local races, winning the Kokura Kinen and 6 open races, racing until the end of 7 (old age system). As a broodmare she produced JRA Hall of Famer Ten Point and 1982 champion jumper King's Point. Her origins are famous too: her dam Kumowaka was caught in an outbreak and nearly put down, escaped to Hokkaido, cleared her name in court, and was re-registered as "Okataka" - and Wakakumo was born.
2908: Winner of the 1977 Oka Sho and QEII Cup. Debuting at 4 (old age system), she won 3 straight: her debut, the Wakaba Sho and the Oka Sho as favorite by 3 lengths over Fine Nissei. Unwell, she was 14th in the Oaks, but after a 3rd in the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu won the QEII Cup, dispelling doubts about the trip, and the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu - champion 4yo filly. At 5 she won the Milers C. and Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu, and lost the Arima Kinen by a length to Kane Minobu. At 6, 3rd in the Chukyo Kinen, 2nd in the Milers C., 12th of 13 in the Takarazuka Kinen, she won the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu again and retired after a 9th in the Arima Kinen. No notable foals.
2909: The 1979 Satsuki Sho winner. Debuting at 3 (old age system), winning his 2nd start, the Rindo Sho and an open race, he won the Asahi Hai 3yo S. as 6th choice behind imported Kentucky Fair, champion 3yo colt. At 4, 2nd in the Tokyo 4yo S. (now Kyodo News Hai) and 5th in the Spring S., he was 3rd choice in the Satsuki Sho and held off Katsurano Haiseiko. In the Derby Katsurano Haiseiko turned the tables; he closed for 4th. After the Keio Hai AH and St. Lite Kinen, he was hot favorite in a Kikuka Sho without the Derby winner, but moved too soon and was 3rd. Pulled up injured in the Arima Kinen, he retired. No notable foals.
2910: The 1980 Kikuka Sho winner. Winning his 3rd start and the Shiragiku Sho, he was 2nd in the Hanshin 3yo S. (old age system). At 4, 3rd in an open race, 10th in the Derby, he improved in autumn: Kobe Shimbun Hai 1st, Kyoto Shimbun Hai 2nd, then the Kikuka Sho as 5th choice by a neck over favorite Monte Prince. Injuries limited him after; he retired at 7. His best foal was Tomino Goran, a Niigata local star.
2911: Legend for beating 2 US Triple Crown winners, Seattle Slew and Affirmed, in the 1978 Jockey Club Gold C. Originally French, he won the Coronation C. and Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud. When disease broke out in France, his connections, planning US stud duty, sent him to America before a travel ban. Losing at first at 4, at 5 he won 6 G1s on any surface - the turf Hollywood Invitational H., the dirt Hollywood Gold C. - above all that Jockey Club Gold C., a duel of 2 Triple Crown winners which he won after a fierce fight. Retired at 6, he disappointed at stud, went to Sweden, and after his owner's bankruptcy was slaughtered. The shock led to the Exceller Fund and other groups to protect retired racehorses.
2912: A gelding who ruled Australian sprints from 1977 to 1983. Sprints were then low-status; his success, it's said, built their prestige today. Dominant from 3 at sprint-mile trips, he was Australian Horse of the Year. At 4, with the new grading system, he won the Futurity S. and George Ryder S., now G1s. Despite injuries he raced until 7, winning the G2 William Reid S. 5 years running. With few G1s then, he won only 4, but by today's grading it would be 20+. His success is said to have paved the way for later sprint stars like Black Caviar. The Freeway S., which he won twice, became the Manikato S., still a sprint G1.
2913: A legend of Australian racing: 30 wins from 41 from 1979 to 1982, 14 G1s, the first in Australia to earn A$1 million. Gelded after a heavy debut defeat, he won 6 straight; after some near-misses, he won 11 in a row from late at 3, from 1200m sprints to 3200m - versatile. He won the Cox Plate in October at 4 and was unbeaten for a year, 8 straight, until winning it again at 5. In the Melbourne Cup, Oceania's biggest race, leg trouble left him 20th. After a long break, back in August at 6, he won a 3rd Cox Plate, the first ever. Leg trouble recurred; after 3 years of trying to return, he retired at 9 as a pensioner.
2914: Winner of 4 graded races incl. the 1972 All Comers and 1974 Kimpai (East); with 76 starts, the JRA record for graded-race runs - "the working horse." Winning allowances in autumn at 4 (old age system), he won his first graded race, the All Comers, then raced 11-14 times a year, winning the Kimpai (East) and Meguro Kinen (Autumn) at 6 and the Aichi Hai at 7. Winless in 19 starts at 8, he retired after a 5th in the Aichi Hai. With partbred blood on his dam's side there was no stud demand, and he became a lead pony at Tokyo.
2915: Dam of 1977 Kikuka Sho winner Presto Toko and 5-time graded winner Noboru Toko. Her first foal Noboru Toko won the Sprinters S., winning her early praise, but unexplained cycle problems then left her barren for years. Told "a change of scene may help," she was sent to a small Hokkaido farm, where a cheap imported sire, Gustav, stood nearby - "cheap, so we can try again and again." She conceived at once, and Presto Toko was born - virtually Gustav's only notable foal. After that she conceived almost every year, producing 9 foals until 1986, at 23 (old age system).
2916: Winner of graded races incl. the Sprinters S., Fukushima Kinen and Tanabata Sho; tough, with 68 JRA starts until 8 (old age system). 2nd in the Niigata 3yo S. and Keisei Hai 3yo S. at 3, he flopped in the classics at 4 but won the Sprinters S. One win at 5, then at 6 the Kokura Daishoten, Sekiya Kinen and Fukushima Kinen; at 7 the Tanabata Sho. He retired after a 7th in the Fukushima Minpo Hai in October at 8. Few foals; he died at 16.
2917: The 1974 Oaks winner. Only just past the 2-million class before the Oaks, she drew attention as jockey Isao Shimada sought a 3rd straight Oaks, and won as 9th of 26. In autumn she won the Queen S. and Victoria C. (forerunner of the QEII Cup), champion 4yo filly (old age system). Older, she was 3rd to Fujino Perseus in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Takarazuka Kinen against top males. Few foals, none beyond allowance level.
2918: 5th on debut, he won a maiden and 2-million race, then 2 open races at 4 (old age system). 5th in the Satsuki Sho and 14th in the Derby, he turned to sprints, 2nd in the Lord Derby CT and CBC Sho. After a year off injured, at 6 he won 4 straight: an open race, Yasuda Kinen, BSN Hai and Sekiya Kinen, then was 2nd to Nippo King under 60kg in the Kumohata Kinen. He raced until 8. No notable foals.
2919: Winner of the 1975 Arima Kinen. First winning in March at 4 (old age system), he won 2 allowances and was 5th to Kaburaya O in the Derby. In autumn he won the St. Lite Kinen and an open race, then was 4th as favorite to Kokusai Prince in the Kikuka Sho. In an Arima Kinen with Fujino Perseus, Kitano Kachidoki and others, he won - then a rare feat for a 4yo. Older, 2nd in the Meguro Kinen and 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Spring), but only 1 open win. Few foals.
2921: Winner of the 1979 Tenno Sho (Spring), a force in the TTG (Tosho Boy, Ten Point, Green Grass) crop. Missing the classics at 4 (old age system), he emerged with the Meguro Kinen in February at 5, won the Keio Hai AH and was 4th to Hokuto Boy in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). At 6 he won the AJCC and Meguro Kinen, was 3rd to Green Grass in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and to Tenmei in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), then won the Tenno Sho (Spring) at 7 as 4th choice. Winless after, he retired at 9. No notable foals.
2922: Of the TTG (Tosho Boy, Ten Point, Green Grass) crop, a sprint star. 9th in the Derby and 13th in the Kikuka Sho at 4 (old age system), he won the St. Lite Kinen, then turned to shorter trips: the Kumohata Kinen (a December Nakayama 1800m handicap until 1980) late at 4, the Keio Hai SH at 5, and at 6 a 1400m open race and the Yasuda Kinen. He retired after a 5th in the Kumohata Kinen. No notable foals; his half-sister Itto won the Takamatsunomiya Hai and Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu.
2920: A 1975 classic fancy: 2nd choice each time, he was 2nd in the Satsuki Sho, 6th in the Derby and 5th in the Kikuka Sho - no crown, but wins in the Spring S., Asahi Challenge C. and Hanshin Daishoten showed his class. From late at 4 (old age system) to spring at 5 he won 6 straight incl. the Nihon Keizai Shinshun Hai and Sankei Osaka Hai, then was 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and Takarazuka Kinen, 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 2nd in the Hanshin Daishoten. From 6, 1 open win; 11th in his farewell Tenno Sho. His best foal: Shinshun 4yo Himba S. winner Juji Lady.
2923: A foreign-bred blueblood (Gallant Man x Northern Dancer) who won the 1979 Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system) unbeaten. Favorite every time, he beat Takeden and Sakura Shori easily. Foreign-bred horses then couldn't run in Japan's classics, so at 4 he aimed at Europe's, but fell ill and never raced there; he came home and rested long. Back in spring at 5, after an open race he won the New Zealand T. (an open race then, unlike today's), but was injured soon after and died, leaving no line.
2924: Unbeaten in 4, 2nd in the Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system), he won the Keisei Hai and Spring S. at 4 and was Satsuki Sho favorite, but 9th, then 13th in the Derby and 6th in the Kikuka Sho. Slumping at 5, winning only the Tanigawadake S. at 6, he won an open race and the Yasuda Kinen at 7. At stud he sired steady open-class horses like March S. winner Takeden Victory and Hopeful S. winner Takeden Junior.
2926: A 1-win horse struggling through 4 (old age system), he was transformed at 5: 3 straight wins, a 2nd, then 2 more, straight into open class. He won the Aichi Hai late that year, then the Kimpai (West) and Chunichi Shimbun Hai at 6, and was a head 2nd to Katsurano Haiseiko in a strong Milers C. with Nichido Arashi. Retired that autumn; no notable foals.
2927: Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Fuchu 3yo S. (old age system), 3rd to Bingo Garoo in the Asahi Hai 3yo S., she won the Queen C. and Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, the classic favorite - but was crushed by longshot Horsemen Tesco in the Oka Sho, 2nd, then 11th in the Oaks. Turning to sprints, she was 2nd in the Sekiya Kinen and Sprinters S., then at 5 won the Keio Hai SH and Sekiya Kinen. A head 2nd to Sakura God in the Sprinters S. again. As a broodmare she produced Dynamic Bird, 3rd in the Nakayama Kinen.
2928: Winner of the 1980 Takarazuka Kinen; only twice out of the top three in 18 starts. Unbeaten in 2 at 3 (old age system), at 4 he was 2nd in the Kisaragi Sho, 3rd in the Mainichi Hai, won the NHK Hai and was 3rd to Katsurano Haiseiko in the Derby. Falling short after (4th Takamatsunomiya Hai and Kobe Shimbun Hai), he won an open race at 5, was 6th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), then won the Takarazuka Kinen as favorite. He died after 2 crops at stud, with no stars.
2929: Racing in allowances at 3 (old age system), top four in all 8, at 4 he was 3rd in the Shinzan Kinen and won the Kisaragi Sho over Teruten Ryu and others. A classic force, 3rd to Bingo Garoo in the Satsuki Sho and 5th to Katsurano Haiseiko in the Derby, he won the Takamatsunomiya Hai and Kobe Shimbun Hai, then was 2nd in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai and injured. Back after about 2 years, 6th - his first time out of the top five - he retired. No notable foals.
2930: One of Shinzan's best sons. Debuting at 3 (old age system), he won the Fukushima 3yo S., then was 5th to Tokuzakura in the Asahi Hai 3yo S. At 4, 23rd to Long Ace in the Derby, he won the Nihon Tanpa Sho (now Radio Nikkei Sho). 7th in the Kikuka Sho, he won the CBC Sho in record time. He won the Tokyo Shimbun Hai at 5 and Keio Hai AH at 6, racing until the Kabutoyama Kinen in November at 8. No notable foals.
2931: Winner of the 1967 Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen, better known for his inconsistency: losing when fancied, winning when not. At 4 (old age system) his jockey Yamaoka was banned for life over a race-fixing scandal, tarnishing his image. Unpopular, he won the Kabutoyama Kinen that autumn. At 5, 2nd in the AJCC, he was 4th as favorite in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai, then 3rd as 9th choice in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and 6th as favorite in the Yasuda Kinen - mocked as "the horse who reads the papers." At 6, unplaced as favorite in the Stayers S. and Meguro Kinen (Autumn), he won the Tenno Sho (Autumn) as 8th choice, then the Arima Kinen as 4th choice by 6 lengths. So erratic that, despite 2 Big Eight wins, he wasn't Horse of the Year. At 7 he won 5 open races in 14 starts but flopped as favorite in every graded race, mocking fans to the end. At stud he did steadily, siring Sankei Osaka Hai winner Gold Eagle.
2932: Winner of 5 graded races 1973-1977 incl. the Aichi Hai and Milers C. In the 1973 Aichi Hai he won easily in a record 1:59.9 - the first sub-2-minute 2000m. Leg trouble limited him to 27 starts until 8 (old age system), with 14 wins. No star foals, but his son Milky Way remarkably competed in Olympic equestrian events.
2933: Racing until 9 (old age system), he won the Chukyo Kinen, Nakayama Kinen and Keio Hai SH: 20 wins from 47 - no JRA horse has won 20+ since (as of 2021). In open class from 5, he won 3 straight to the Chukyo Kinen, the Lord Derby CT at 6, the Nakayama Kinen, Keio Hai SH and Kinko Sho at 7, and was 4th to Tosho Boy in the Arima Kinen. He won the Hakodate Kinen at 8 and retired after the Arima Kinen at 9. Few winners at stud.
2934: Needing 23 starts to win allowances through 4 (old age system), he bloomed at 5: 2nd in the Meguro Kinen and Diamond S., then the Keio Hai SH and Argentina Kyowakoku Hai, the All Comers and Meguro Kinen - Tenno Sho (Autumn) favorite, 4th to Fujino Perseus. Winless after, but often top five in graded races; he retired after a 7th in the Meguro Kinen in February at 7.
2935: A debut winner, 5th in the Hanshin 3yo S. (old age system), at 4 he was 7th in the Satsuki Sho, 4th in the Derby and 5th in the Kikuka Sho, winning the Asahi Challenge C. before it. Often fancied but beaten after, pulled up after a fall in the Tenno Sho (Spring) at 5, he won the Kimpai (West) and Chunichi Shimbun Hai at 6 and was 2nd in the Chukyo Kinen. He retired after a 7th in the Keihan Hai.
2936: The 1975 Kikuka Sho winner. Struggling in allowances until spring at 4 (old age system), he bloomed by summer, winning 2 classes, then 3rd in the St. Lite Kinen and winner of the Kyoto Shimbun Hai. With 2-classic winner Kaburaya O absent, he won a wide-open Kikuka Sho. Winless as an older horse, he retired at 8 and did not go to stud.
2937: Tough, with 66 starts until 8 (old age system), he won the Naruo Kinen and Meguro Kinen. Winning 3 straight in spring at 4, he won 2 open races and was 2nd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai. At 5 he won the Naruo Kinen, 4th to Erimo George in the Tenno Sho (Spring), then the Meguro Kinen as 8th choice; beaten badly in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen. Slumping from 6, he won the Sapporo Kinen at 7 and retired in summer at 8 with 10 wins from 66.
2938: Owned by the president of Aichi Toyota and named after the "Crown Eight" car launched in her debut year, 1964. She won the 1966 Takarazuka Kinen, its first female winner. Unbeaten in 4 incl. the Hanshin 3yo S. at 3 (old age system), she was 4th as favorite in the Oka Sho, 16th in the Oaks and 17th as 15th choice in the Kikuka Sho. 2nd in the Aichi Hai, then steady, she won the Naruo Kinen at 5, then the Takarazuka Kinen as 4th of 8, leading early and winning by 3.5 lengths in record time. She retired in January at 6. Her first foal Naoki won the Takarazuka Kinen too - a mother-son double - and her 4th, Crown Pirado, was 2nd in both Tenno Sho - a great broodmare.
2939: Winning a maiden at 4 (old age system) and 3 straight in autumn, he was 6th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai and 4th in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, 2nd to Erimo George in the Kyoto Kinen, then won the Keihan Hai in a blanket finish. He won the Kimpai (West) at 5, and at 6 an open race and the Kyoto Kinen. 17th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he retired.
2940: Winner of the 1976 QEII Cup. 4th in the Flower C. and 2nd in the 4yo Himba S. in spring at 4 (old age system), she missed the classics and bloomed in autumn: 3rd in the Queen S., 1st in the Keiyo Tokubetsu, then the QEII Cup, beating 2-classic filly Teitania - the first running under that name, formerly the Victoria C. Older she won the Fukushima Kinen, 3rd in the Nakayama Himba S. and Keio Hai AH. Of 11 foals, none starred.
2925: The 1978 Satsuki Sho winner. A debut winner, pulled up after his rider fell in the Hakodate 3yo S. (old age system), 2nd in the Keisei Hai 3yo S. and 4th in the Asahi Hai 3yo S. At 4, 2nd in the Tokyo 4yo S. (now Kyodo News Hai), he won the Yayoi Sho and the Satsuki Sho, holding off Inter Gushiken and Sakura Shori. 10th in the Derby, perhaps too far, he was 3rd in the Hakodate Kinen, then died of a twisted gut 10 days later.
2941: Winner of 3 graded races incl. the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and All Comers; 2nd to Green Grass in the Tenno Sho (Spring) at 6 (old age system). Tough: 56 starts until 8, 17 of them at 5. In open class from late at 4, he won the Tokyo Shimbun Hai at 5, then after a 2nd in the Mainichi Okan, the All Comers. At 6, after the Diamond S., he was 2nd to Green Grass in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and 4th to Erimo George in the Takarazuka Kinen. Winless after, he retired in autumn at 8.
2942: Unbeaten in 4 incl. the Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system): his debut by 6 lengths, the Rindo Sho by 2.5, an open race by 7, then the Asahi Hai 3yo S. as 6th choice without graded form, beating favored Spirit Swaps and others. At 4 he was 4th to Tosho Boy in the Satsuki Sho, 18th in the Derby, then turned to sprints, winning an open race and the UHB Hai, 2nd in the Sprinters S. at 5. At stud for 8 years; no notable foals.
2943: Steady, never out of the top five from his debut, he won 5 straight at 4 (old age system) from allowances to the Kitakyushu Kinen and Kokura Kinen, then was 3rd to Tosho Boy in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai and 16th in the Kikuka Sho. At a mile to middle trips he was 2nd in the Kokura Daishoten, Swan S. and Hankyu Hai at 5, 2nd in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai and Chukyo Kinen at 6, and won the Kokura Daishoten - a 3rd graded win. He retired at 7; his only unplaced runs came at 3000m, in the Kikuka Sho and Hanshin Daishoten.
2944: Debuting at 4 (old age system), he won allowances in summer, then was 5th in the Hakodate Kinen and 3rd in the Fukushima Kinen, and won the Nakayama Kinen in March at 5. In autumn, 2nd in the All Comers and 3rd in the Meguro Kinen, he was 4th to Kane Minobu in the Arima Kinen. At 6 he won 3 straight - Nakayama Kinen, an open race, Argentina Kyowakoku Hai - and at 7 the AJCC. No notable foals.
2945: Unbeaten in 2 at 3 (old age system), she then struggled in allowances, until a 2nd in the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu late at 4. At 5 she won the Hankyu Hai and Kinko Sho, at 6 the Chunichi Shimbun Hai and Kitakyushu Kinen. 2nd in the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu and 3rd in the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu, she retired in spring at 7. Her best foal was Flight Suzuka, 2nd in the Spring S., who ran in the Satsuki Sho and Derby.
2946: No Big Eight win, but he won the Yasuda Kinen and All Comers and was champion sprinter in 1966 at 5 (old age system). His sire Hishi Masaru (1955) left only 2 crops; he was the only one to succeed him. In allowances through 4, he bloomed older: 2 open wins, then the Yasuda Kinen, and that autumn the All Comers. 8th in the Arima Kinen, perhaps too far. At 6 he won the Keio Hai SH, 2nd in the Yasuda Kinen and Nakayama Kinen. With heavier weights, he won only 2 open races after, retiring in autumn at 7. At stud he sired Hishi Speed, 3-time graded winner incl. the Tokyo 4yo S. (now Kyodo News Hai) - 3 generations of home-bred sires - but Hishi Speed failed at stud and the line ended.
2947: A 1977 classic fancy. At 4 (old age system) he won the Keisei Hai and Tokyo 4yo S. (now Kyodo News Hai) and was Satsuki Sho favorite, but was 7th, then 13th in the Derby. His real misfortune was crop-mate Maruzensky, "the monster," who overshadowed the classic horses: in the Fuchu 3yo S., Asahi Hai 3yo S. and Tanchori S. at 4, he was 2nd to Maruzensky each time, crushed. He retired early, in autumn at 4, and had little success at stud.
2948: Debuting at 4 (old age system), she was 3rd in the Flower C. and 4th in the 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, then 23rd in the Oaks. Then she won 4 straight to the Sprinters S. - a gifted sprinter - and won it again at 5. 4th going for a 3rd win at 6, she retired. Her foals incl. Yasuda Kinen runner Main Dish.
2949: Unbeaten in 2, 7th in the Hanshin 3yo S. (old age system), he won the Cyclamen Sho to reach open class. At 4 he won an open race and the CBC Sho; at 5 the Chunichi Shimbun Hai, Swan S. and CBC Sho again. He retired after a 12th in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai at 6. No notable foals.
2950: The year Maruzensky won the Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system) by a street, he won the Hanshin 3yo S., western 3yo champion. At 4 he won the Kisaragi Sho, a classic name, but was 16th in the Satsuki Sho, 5th in the Derby and 6th in the Kikuka Sho. At 5 he won the Kyoto Daishoten and Meguro Kinen (Autumn), then was 4th as favorite in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) - a strong stayer. Winless after, he retired in January at 8.
2951: Winning allowances at 4 (old age system), 12th in the Kikuka Sho, he grew at 5 and won the Kyoto Kinen in autumn, then the Aichi Hai and Kimpai (West) at 6. In autumn he won the Kyoto Kinen again, then closed from the back for 5th as Pretty Cast ran away with the Tenno Sho (Autumn). He collapsed of a heart attack in training at 7 and died.
2952: Winning the Wakaba Sho in spring at 4 (old age system), she was last of 21 in the Oaks, then improved in allowances, blooming late at 4. After an open win, she won the BSN Hai at 5 and was 2nd to Sunny Flower in the Himba Tokyo Times Hai (now Fuchu Himba S.). At 6, 2nd in the Nakayama Himba S. and Yasuda Kinen, she won the Sprinters S. and retired at 7. She produced foals for 16 years; no stars, but MG White raced steadily at Kasamatsu.
2953: Debuting late at 3 (old age system), she won 3 straight allowances at 4 and was 6th of 21 in the Oka Sho. After about a year off, back in spring at 5, she ran 1st, 2nd, 1st, then won the Sprinters S. and the Himba Tokyo Times Hai (now Fuchu Himba S.) - champion older mare. She raced until autumn at 6. A modest broodmare, but a fast mare: 6 wins and 2 2nds from 11 at a mile or less.
2954: Winner of the 1979 Tenno Sho (Autumn); half-brother of Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Takarazuka Kinen winner Fujino Perseus. Winning late at 3 (old age system), he struggled in allowances until spring at 5, then stepped up to win the Diamond S. and bloomed: 3rd in the Mainichi Okan and Meguro Kinen, then the Tenno Sho (Autumn) after a tight finish with Mejiro Phantom. Injured soon after, he never returned, and was put down 2 years later at 7.
2955: The 1978 Oaks winner. Unbeaten in 2 at 3 (old age system), she then kept finishing unplaced, losing favor, until spring at 4: 2nd in the Flower C., 3rd in the 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, and into the Oaks. 5th choice, she held off favorites Hirono Ski and Sanem Joo in the straight. Unplaced in every race after, she retired in spring at 5. No notable foals, but 16 of them carry her blood.
2956: Of the Flory Scup line that shaped Japanese racing, she produced 2-classic winner Kitano Kachidoki, QEII Cup winner Lead Swallow, and Nihon Pillow Evert, dam of Nihon Pillow Winner - a great broodmare. Badly injured as a youngster, she never raced and went straight to breeding. Her first foal died soon after, and she stopped conceiving; near culling, she was sent to her owner's son's farm and turned out wild on the hills to regain her vigor - it worked. Her 3rd foal Kitano Kachidoki won the 1974 Satsuki Sho and Kikuka Sho, her 5th Nihon Pillow Evert later produced Nihon Pillow Winner, and her 6th Lead Swallow won the 1978 QEII Cup - a great dynasty. Her line lives on: 5 generations from her 4th foal Tokuno Perseus came Meisho Muramumo, 2021 Leopard S. winner.
2957: Winner of the 1978 QEII Cup. A debut winner at 3 (old age system), she struggled in allowances until the Nanohana Sho at 4, then was 4th to Oyama Tesco in the Oka Sho and 5th to Five Hope in the Oaks. After the Katsuragawa Tokubetsu, she was QEII Cup favorite and closed sharply from midfield to win. Older she won the Hankyu Hai, 2nd in the Kokura Daishoten and 3rd in the Swan S. Few foals, none notable.
2958: Beaten in his debut and a maiden at 3 (old age system), he was 2nd in the Kokura 3yo S. while still a maiden, then won one, was 3rd to later Tenno Sho winner Nichido Taro in the Momiji Sho, and won the Kyoto 3yo S. 2nd choice in the Hanshin 3yo S., he won as unbeaten hot favorite Bold Acan sank - western 3yo champion. He retired after a 2nd in an open race early at 4.
2959: The 1979 Kikuka Sho winner. At 4 (old age system) he won the Mainichi Hai but was 9th in the Spring S. and 11th in the Satsuki Sho. After a 6th and 8th in autumn, he was a head 2nd to Tenmei in the Kyoto Daishoten, then won the Kikuka Sho easily over favorite Bingo Garoo and others. Injured for over 2 years, he moved to local racing, winning at Obihiro and Hakodate - a Kikuka winner's pride. He left only 1 crop at stud before becoming a pensioner.
2960: Full sister of Kaburaya O; winner of the 1979 QEII Cup. Debuting at 4 (old age system), she won her debut and the 4yo Himba S., rested until autumn, was 2nd in the UHB Hai and Sapphire S., 6th in the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu - her only unplaced run so far - then as 2nd choice ran down favorite Agnes Lady to win the QEII Cup, last leg of the fillies' Triple Crown. 2nd in the Kimpai (East) at 5, unplaced after, she retired that spring. Only 6 foals, none notable.
2961: Much noticed from his debut, he won it and the Kaede Sho but flopped otherwise, 6th as 2nd choice in the Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system). At 4 he was transformed: an open race, the Tokyo 4yo S. (now Kyodo News Hai), Yayoi Sho and Spring S. - 4 straight - then Satsuki Sho favorite, 4th to Bingo Garoo, and 8th to Katsurano Haiseiko in the Derby. At stud for 15 years, with some success.
2962: Winner of the 1979 Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system), champion 3yo colt - in his 9th start, after 2nds in the Hakodate 3yo S., Keisei Hai 3yo S. and Fuchu 3yo S. At 4 he won the Tokyo 4yo S. (now Kyodo News Hai), then rested long; back in autumn, 4th in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, 14th in the Kikuka Sho. Winless after, he retired late at 5.
2963: A home-bred sire who held his own in the import-dominated 1960s, siring Big Eight winners like Yamano O and Sea Ace. He won the 1953 Kikuka Sho and 1954 Tenno Sho (Spring). 2nd and 3rd to Bostonian in the Satsuki Sho and Derby, he bloomed in autumn and denied Bostonian the Triple Crown in the Kikuka Sho, winning by 3.5 lengths. In 1954 he won all 5 starts incl. the Tenno Sho (Spring), named the first-ever Horse of the Year. His first crop gave Takarazuka Kinen winner Caesar, his 3rd Satsuki winner Yamano O; later Oka Sho winner Sea Ace and many graded winners - a leading sire. His blood lives on through dams too: Mistarumae, 3rd dam of Yamanin Zephyr, and Fushimi Ace, 5th dam of Water Navillera.
2964: The 1963 Oaks winner, named for owner Ito's initials, read as letters. Winning late at 3 (old age system) and once at 4, she was 6th of 25 in the Oka Sho and 3rd in the 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, then won the Oaks as 4th choice, surging clear as favorite Milford sank. In Hokkaido she won an open race and was 2nd in the Hakodate Kinen, then 2nd to later Kikuka winner Great Yoruka in the St. Lite Kinen, retiring after 1 race at 5. Of 9 foals, her 6th, Itei Shiro, won the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu and was 4th in the Oaks; via her 2nd, Itei Grace, came Arima Kinen winner Hikari Duel and later Kokura Kinen winner Hokusei Amber.
2965: The 1961 Oka Sho winner. 2nd on debut and then 2 wins at 3 (old age system), last in 2 races early at 4, she won the Kisaragi Sho, then 2nd in an open race, the Oka Sho as 2nd choice of 28 by 5 lengths. 16th as 2nd choice in the Oaks, she won an open race and the Kobe Hai (now Kobe Shimbun Hai), then the Kinko Sho (before graded status) and Osaka Hai at 5 - 4 graded wins - and retired. Breeding at once, she had 9 foals in 12 years, incl. Kyoto Kinen winner Nihon Pillow Homare, Sapporo Kinen winner Erimo Marchis, and Ace Cosmo, 2nd in the Kyoto Daishoten and Victoria C.
2966: Unbeaten in 7 with 2 graded wins - the 3rd unbeaten graded winner after Kurifuji (11 from 11, 1943-44) and Tokino Minoru (10 from 10, 1950-51). He won his debut by 8 lengths in record time, the Hakodate 3yo S. (old age system) by 9 in record time, and the Hokkaido 3yo S. (now Sapporo 2yo S.) easily from last after a slow start, without the whip - "Tokino Minoru reborn," the top classic hope. A fracture in training cost nearly 2 years; back in summer at 5 he won 3 easily, aiming at the Tenno Sho and Arima Kinen, then periostitis struck. He won on return at 6, but it recurred and he retired. With partbred blood on his dam's side, he was classed partbred and neglected at stud, yet sired graded winners like Aichi Hai winner Hard Lark.
2967: The 1959 Derby winner, beating fancied Meitai and Will Deal on heavy ground. Debuting in November at 3 (old age system), winless that year, he won early at 4, then an allowance and an open race; too late for the Satsuki Sho, he was 3rd in the NHK Hai. 3rd choice behind Satsuki 1-2 Will Deal and Meitai, he relished the rain-soaked going and won easily - the race of his life. Winless that year after (6th Kikuka Sho, 5th Arima Kinen), older he won the Tokyo Hai (now Tokyo Shimbun Hai) and an open race, retiring in January at 6. He sired Kyoto 4yo Tokubetsu winner Meisei Hikari.
2968: Winner of the 1967 Satsuki Sho and 1968 Arima Kinen. At 3 (old age system) he won 5 of 6 incl. the Hokkaido 3yo S. (now Sapporo 2yo S.). 6th in the Spring S. at 4, he won the Satsuki Sho, breaking clear early from a handy spot by 2.5 lengths. 5th as Derby favorite, he won the Hakodate Kinen, was 2nd in the Kyoto Hai (now Kyoto Shimbun Hai) and Kikuka Sho - the real thing. At 5 he won the Hakodate Kinen again; 9th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he won the Arima Kinen dominantly - a 2nd Big Eight win. At 6, 2 open wins, 2nd in the British Fair Commemorative (now Sprinters S.), then 6th and 15th; after 4 defeats at 7 he retired. He sired Kabutoyama Kinen winner Ryu Fubuki.
2969: The 1966 Satsuki Sho winner. Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Hanshin 3yo S. (old age system), champion 3yo colt, he won an open race at 4 - 4 straight - then 2nd in the Yayoi Sho and 4th in the Spring S. 2nd choice in the Satsuki Sho, he beat favorite and Spring S. winner Shogun by half a length. Then he faded: 5th in the NHK Hai, 20th as 2nd choice in the Derby, 5th and 17th in autumn. At 5 he won 3 open races and the Hankyu Hai, and after a 4th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) at 6 retired - beaten badly at long trips, but never out of the top five at 2000m or less. He sired Sekiya Kinen winner Suzu Hope.
2970: In 1974 she became the 3rd winner of the US fillies' Triple Tiara. Her owner sponsored tennis star Chris Evert, hence the name. At 2 she won 4 of 5, 2nd only in the G1 Frizette S. At 3 she won the Acorn S. (G1), the Mother Goose S. narrowly, and the CCA Oaks by 3.5 lengths - the Triple Tiara. She then beat Hollywood Oaks winner Miss Musket in a match race, Eclipse champion 3yo filly. At 4 she won the La Canada S., then flopped as favorite in the Santa Margarita H. and retired. Her daughter Six Crowns produced successful sire Chief's Crown, and her line flourished.
2971: The 2021 2yo queen and a 2022 3yo filly fancy. 3rd to later 6-G1 Equinox on debut, she won a maiden, then the Artemis S. as 7th choice with a fine late run. 3rd choice in the Hanshin JF, she sat ideally in midfield and closed with a superior kick - 3 straight, a G1, 2yo queen. A classic lead player, she was 3rd to Namur in the Tulip Sho and just missed in the Oka Sho, 4th to Stars on Earth. Oaks favorite, liked for the longer trip, she never quickened from the back, 12th. 4th to Stunning Rose in the Shion S., she then had a tendon injury; unwilling to push her, her camp announced her retirement in autumn at 4.
2972: A 2021 dirt name who won the JBC 2yo Yushun. He won his debut under Lemaire, breaking clear from up front, then at Mombetsu was 3rd choice behind local fancies Nudge and Scharfsinn in the JBC 2yo Yushun, closing powerfully from the back to beat Nudge by 1.5 lengths. 9th in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun, a fracture cost 3 months; since, 12th in all 3 races.
2973: Debuting in June at 2, he won from up front by 2 lengths. 5th as favorite in the Clover Sho from midfield, he raced forward again to win the Keio Hai 2yo S. as 8th choice - impressive. A fracture followed; back in the Arlington C. in spring at 3, he was 3rd to Danon Scorpion, then 6th in the NHK Mile C. In Europe he was 11th in the July C. and Prix Maurice de Gheest. Back home, 6th, a length behind, in the Capital S. (L).
2974: Offered at 140 million yen in all (3.5 million x 40 shares), the hope of the Kunieda stable for a first Derby. He won his debut at 1.1, then the Saudi Arabia Royal C. - a fine start. But he was 12th as favorite in the Hopeful S., 8th in the Mainichi Hai at 3, 14th on dirt in the Japan Dirt Derby, and last (18th) in the Capital S. (L).
2975: Unbeaten in 3, he was favorite in the Asahi Hai FS (G1) but 2nd to Do Deuce. Taking the mile route at 3, 4th in the NHK Mile C. and Yasuda Kinen (G1), he grew in autumn, beating NHK winner Danon Scorpion and others in the Fuji S. (G2). In the Mile CS (G1), 6th choice behind Schnell Meister and Sodashi, the first white G1 winner, he charged from the back with a stunning finish - his G1 at last. At 4, 5th in the Dubai Turf, 2nd to Songline in the Yasuda Kinen, then 8th in the Mile CS and 7th in the Hong Kong Mile. At 5, 2nd in the Milers C. (G2), 5th in the Yasuda Kinen, 6th in the Mile CS; he retired that year.
2976: A 2022 3yo miler who won the NHK Mile C. Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Hagi S. (L), he was 3rd to Do Deuce in the Asahi Hai FS. 7th in the Kyodo News Hai at 3, he won the Arlington C. as favorite, closing sharply from the back. In the NHK Mile C., 4th choice behind Asahi Hai runner-up Serifos and Junior C. winner Industria, he led mid-straight from midfield and held off Matenro Orion - 3yo mile king. 3rd in the Fuji S., he was 4th choice as the leading 3yo in the Mile CS but 11th as fellow 3yo Serifos won, then 6th in the Hong Kong Mile.
2977: A classic hope at 3, he was 5th as 3rd choice in the Spring S. (G2) and 9th as favorite in the Radio Nikkei Sho (G3), then restarted in allowances. Winning 2 classes at 4, he won the Nakayama Kimpai (G3) early at 5 and the Nakayama Kinen (G2) - 4 straight. In the Tenno Sho (Autumn), billed as Efforia vs. Contrail vs. Gran Alegria, he held 5th. In the Hong Kong Cup he dueled side by side with seasoned traveler Loves Only You, losing by a head. At 6 he ran only twice, but was 2nd in the Takarazuka Kinen. At 7, 7th in the Osaka Hai, 9th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he was 3rd in the Hong Kong Cup, best of the Japanese. At 8 he was 5th in Hong Kong's QEII Cup and retired.
2978: Winning 2 classes at 4, he won the Fukushima Minyu C. (L) and Betelgeuse S. (L) that autumn, then the Tokai S. at 5 as 2nd choice, breaking clear from up front as hot favorite Inti collapsed - 3 straight. 13th in the February S., he won the Heian S., then 7th, 12th and 6th. At 6, 2nd in the Tokai S. and 3rd in the Sirius S., little else; after unplaced runs at 7 he moved to local racing.
2979: A foreign-bred son of First Samurai. On dirt until the Kannazuki S. in autumn at 4, he switched to turf and won the Kitakyushu Tankyori S. (OP). 5th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and Hakodate Sprint S., he won the Silk Road S. at 6 - First Samurai's first graded winner in Japan - then was 3rd to Pixie Knight as 10th choice in the Sprinters S. After 2 unplaced runs and a year off, he moved to local racing at 8 and retired winless after 3 races there.
2980: Debuting at 3, he won his debut, a 5-million race and the Shinanogawa Tokubetsu, then was 13th to Fierement in his first graded race, the Kikuka Sho. Injured for nearly 2 years, back in June at 5 he won the Rokusha S., was 5th in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai, and won the Diamond S. at 6. 4th as favorite in the Meguro Kinen, he died of colic while resting.
2981: She won her debut late at 2 with a fierce finish, then was 9th as favorite in the Elfin S. (L). In the Tulip Sho, 3rd choice, she dead-heated with favorite Meikei Yell after a fierce straight duel. 13th in the Oka Sho, 6th as favorite in the Sweet Pea S. (L), then next-to-last on dirt in the Queen Sho. She never returned from a break and retired to breed.
2982: Winning a maiden in his 3rd start, he was 2nd to later Sprinters S. winner Pixie Knight as 8th choice in the Shinzan Kinen, then won the Falcon S. by a head in a match race with 2yo champion Grenadier Guards. 10th in the NHK Mile C., 2nd in the Port Island S. (L) and 4th in the Swan S., then mostly unplaced; after a 12th in the Seikan S. at 5, he moved to local racing.
2983: After a debut win as hot favorite, he was 2nd to later Satsuki winner Efforia in a Kyodo News Hai with later Derby winner Shahryar, then won the Spring S. In the G1s, 9th as 4th choice in the Satsuki Sho, 14th in the Derby, 10th to Titleholder in the Kikuka Sho. At 4, 13th and 14th.
2984: Winning 3 allowances from late at 3, she won her first graded race, the Lord Derby CT, as 3rd choice - 4 straight. 3rd choice in the Victoria Mile, she was 14th, then won the Queen S. at Hakodate; 11th as 4th choice in the QEII Cup. At 5, 5th in the Nakayama Himba S., beaten badly in the Victoria Mile, she won the Queen S. again - strong at G3 level - and retired after a 12th in the QEII Cup.
2985: Highly rated but 3rd, 3rd and 4th, he won a maiden in his 4th start late at 2, then the Yukiyanagi Sho and the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, closing fastest from the back. 11th in the Derby, 2nd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, he was Kikuka Sho favorite but never fired from the back, 13th. All double-figure finishes at 4.
2986: A stayer who won a 1-win and 2-win race at 2600m and a 3-win race at 2200m. 15th in the Nikkei Sho, she won the Meguro Kinen easily, then was 2nd to Win Marilyn in the All Comers; a QEII Cup fancy, 10th, then 11th in the Arima Kinen. At 5, 12th in the Nikkei Sho, 3rd in the Meguro Kinen and All Comers, then double-figure finishes; she retired to breed after the Diamond S. at 6.
2987: Debuting at 3 with a win, 5th in the Arlington C. and Kobe Shimbun Hai, he restarted in the 3-win class and entered a long tunnel. After a long break from summer at 4, he came good in spring at 5: the Yahiko S., then the Naruo Kinen, and 2nd to Chrono Genesis as 7th choice in the Takarazuka Kinen. Another long break; back at 6, 16th, 12th and 13th, then he led all the way in the Fukushima Kinen as 10th choice - another shock. Then 16th in the Japan Cup, 7th in the Kyoto Kinen at 7, 5th in Australia's Queen Elizabeth S., 15th in the Takarazuka Kinen, 12th in the Hakodate Kinen, and to stud after the Chunichi Shimbun Hai.
2988: Winning a maiden in his 5th start and a 1-win race, he was 3rd in the Tango S. (OP), then won the Unicorn S. as 7th choice with a brilliant late run from midfield. Favorite in the Japan Dirt Derby, he was a close 4th; 11th in the Musashino S. Unplaced in 5 more, he switched to jumps in autumn at 4.
2989: A maiden until her 10th start in July at 3, she then won a 1-win race the next week and a 2-win race in December. At 4 she stepped up to win the Mermaid S. as 10th choice, leading all the way and holding off Clavel and Shadow Diva by a neck. 9th in the Queen S., 15th in the QEII Cup, unplaced in 4 races at 5 and 13th in the AJCC at 6; retired to breed.
2990: A debut winner, 4th to Gratias in the Keisei Hai from a handy spot, he missed the break in a 1-win race and won from last - and became a closer. 4th in the Principal S. (L), he won the Radio Nikkei Sho by 2.5 lengths with a brilliant late run. 16th in the Kikuka Sho, perhaps too far. At 4, 4th in the Kokura Daishoten, he won the Metropolitan S. (L), but an open fracture in training before the Epsom C. proved fatal.
2991: A 2021 debut filly, her crop's first graded winner. 2nd to Pomeranze on debut, she won a maiden as favorite from up front, then the Hakodate 2yo S. as 3rd choice, swinging wide from a handy spot and beating Kaika no Kiseki by 1 1/4 lengths. Leg trouble followed; 17th in the Hanshin JF, then 6th and 18th, and she retired to breed.
2992: A debut winner, 2nd in the Momiji S. (OP), 12th to Resistencia in the Hanshin JF, she raced just once at 3 and restarted in spring at 4: a 1-win race, the Suma Tokubetsu and Yonago S. (L) - 3 straight. 5th in the Chukyo Kinen, she won the Sekiya Kinen as 4th choice from up front. 12th in the Mile CS. At 5 she won the Kyoto Himba S. and lost the Takamatsunomiya Kinen by a neck to Naran Fleg, then faded (10th Yasuda Kinen, 8th Mile CS).
2993: A debut winner who ran in the Unicorn S. at 3, he won through the classes to open class in spring at 4, then the Sannomiya S. (OP). 6th in the Procyon S., he won the Sirius S. as 4th choice, holding off Westerlund by a head from a handy spot. 15th in the Champions C.; at 5, 4th in the Tokai S., then slumped, until he won the Miyako S. as 11th choice by a head over Omega Perfume and Hagino Alegrias - a big upset.
2994: A debut winner, rested nearly 6 months, 2nd in a 1-win race, she won the Anemone S. (L) and chose the NHK Mile C. over the Oka Sho (7th to Schnell Meister), then 7th in the Shuka Sho. At 4, 8th in the Aichi Hai, she won the Fukushima Himba S., charging from the back to win a blanket finish by a neck. 7th on her dirt debut in the JBC Ladies' Classic.
2995: A middle-distance horse who won the Osaka Hai at 5 in 2022. Noticed from his debut, he was remarkably steady: 4 wins and 3 2nds from 7 through allowances. At 4 he won the Shirafuji S. (L), then 3rd in the Kinko Sho, 2nd in the Niigata Daishoten, 3rd in the Mainichi Okan; 6th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), his first time unplaced. At 5, 5th in the AJCC, 4th in the Kinko Sho, he won the Osaka Hai as 8th choice without a graded win, beating Efforia, Rei Papale and others - a G1 for Contrail's crop. 11th in the Takarazuka Kinen, 6th in the Mainichi Okan, 13th to Equinox as 8th choice in the Tenno Sho (Autumn).
2996: Winning a maiden at 2, he restarted after a long break at 4 and passed the allowance ranks by summer at 5, then was 2nd to Sunrise Nova as 11th choice in his first graded race, the Musashino S. At 6, 2nd in the Kashiwa Kinen and 3rd in the Nambu Hai, he won the Musashino S. as 3rd choice in a wide-open field, surging from midfield. At 7, 2nd as 5th choice in the Kashiwa Kinen; at 8, 8th and 5th, he moved to local racing.
2997: A miler who, older, won 2 Yasuda Kinen and a Victoria Mile. Winning a maiden in autumn at 2 and the Kobai S. (L), she went straight to the Oka Sho (15th), then lost the NHK Mile C. by a nose to Schnell Meister. 3rd in the Sekiya Kinen, she won the Fuji S. as favorite from midfield, holding off Satono Wizard. At 4 she won Saudi Arabia's 1351 Turf Sprint; 5th as 2nd choice in the Victoria Mile, she won the Yasuda Kinen as 4th choice at 8.2, beating crop star Schnell Meister by a neck from midfield. 5th in the Centaur S.; at 5, 10th defending in Saudi Arabia, she ran down fancied Stars on Earth and Sodashi in the Victoria Mile and won the Yasuda Kinen again - 3 G1s. 2nd in the Mainichi Okan and 5th in the BC Mile, she retired as champion older mare and champion miler.
2998: Passing the allowance ranks only in January at 5 with the Buzen S., she won the Marine C. in her first open race. 6th as favorite in the Sparking Lady C., 2nd to Reine Blanche in the Ladies' Prelude, she won the JBC Ladies' Classic as favorite, bursting clear from midfield by 2.5 lengths over Madras Check. At 6 she won the TCK Jo-o Hai, then was 14th against males in the February S. and retired to breed.
2999: The 2022 Satsuki Sho winner. His sire Drefong, an American of Storm Cat's line, went to stud in Japan; from his first crop (debuting 2021), he was the first G1 winner. Unbeaten in 2, he was 5th to Do Deuce in the Asahi Hai FS (G1) and 2nd in the Kyodo News Hai at 3. 5th choice in the Satsuki Sho, he moved up from a handy spot at the 4th turn and pulled away from favorites Equinox and Danon Beluga - a classic, and his sire's first G1. Then 7th in the Derby, 9th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 6th in the Hong Kong Cup. At 4 on dirt: 4th in the Saudi Cup, then 11th, 9th, 15th. Back on turf at 5: 3rd Nakayama Kinen, 5th Osaka Hai, 2nd Sapporo Kinen, 5th in the BC Mile. At 6 in Australia, 18th and 13th; a fracture ended his career.
3000: A 2022 3yo filly name. She led all the way on debut, won the Saffron Sho from 2nd, then the Fantasy S. as 2nd choice, holding off favorite Namura Clair - a graded win for brothers Yutaka Take and trainer Koshiro Take. 4th choice in the Hanshin JF despite being an unbeaten graded winner, she held 3rd. At 3, 5th in the Tulip Sho, she lost the Oka Sho by a nose to Stars on Earth, then 13th in the Oaks, 10th as favorite in the Queen S. and 12th in the Shuka Sho. Still beaten at 4, she retired to breed after the Keeneland C.
3001: A long-serving sprinter from 2022 to 2025. 6th in the Asahi Hai FS (G1) at 2 and 8th in the NHK Mile C. (G1) at 3, he struggled at a mile, then turned to sprints and won the Keihan Hai (G3) as favorite, from a handy spot with a superior finish. At 4, 3rd in the Hakodate Sprint S. and Keeneland C., he won the Keihan Hai again. At 5 he won the Ocean S. (G3) and Centaur S. (G2), and lost the Sprinters S. (G1) by a neck to Lugal. At 6 he won the Keio Hai SC (G2), a 5th graded win, then was 10th in the Sprinters S. and 11th in the Mile CS, and his retirement was announced.
3002: Winner of 5 G1s incl. the 2022 Derby - with crop-mate Equinox, one of the best of his era. Debuting in September at 2, unbeaten in 3, he won the Asahi Hai FS (G1). Classic favorite, 3rd to Geoglyph in the Satsuki Sho, he beat Equinox in the Derby - top of his crop. In the Arc he couldn't show his best, 19th. At 4 he was scratched in Dubai with a leg problem, then well beaten by Equinox in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Japan Cup - a slump. With Equinox retired, he won the Arima Kinen for a 3rd G1, back on top: reunited with Yutaka Take, back from injury, he raced at the back, crept forward from 600m out, was 2nd into the straight and passed Titleholder with the fastest finish - a masterful ride. At 5, 5th in the Dubai Turf and 6th in the Takarazuka Kinen, he won the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Japan Cup in autumn - best in training. Bidding for the autumn triple in the Arima Kinen, he was withdrawn lame and retired. Will his foals inherit his rare talent?
3003: Named after a god of Ghana's Ashanti people. Unbeaten in 2, 11th of 15 in the Hopeful S., he won the Keisei Hai early at 3 as 6th choice, closing brilliantly from behind. 6th in the Satsuki Sho, 8th in the Derby, then 4th in the Fukushima Kinen, best of the 3yos.
3004: 2nd on debut, he won a maiden and a 1-win race, then was 4th in the Daily Hai 2yo S. and 8th in the Asahi Hai FS. At 3, 2nd in the Crocus S. (L), he won the Falcon S. as 2nd choice, closing sharply from midfield - the first graded win for his sire Isla Bonita's first crop. 15th in the NHK Mile C., then double-figure finishes (15th Hakodate Sprint S., 12th Keihan Hai).
3005: A long-serving middle-to-long distance star from 2022 to 2025, winner of the 2023 Tenno Sho (Spring). Unbeaten in 2, 2nd in the Hopeful S. (G1). At 3 he went straight to the classics: 9th in the Satsuki Sho and Derby, then won the Kobe Shimbun Hai (G2) and was 3rd in the Kikuka Sho. At 4, after the Hanshin Daishoten (G2), he was 2nd choice behind defending champion Titleholder in the Tenno Sho (Spring); when Titleholder was pulled up lame, he broke clear from a handy spot for a G1. Then 3rd in the Takarazuka Kinen, 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 4th in the Arima Kinen - a G1 regular. At 5, 4th in the Dubai Sheema Classic, top five in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), Japan Cup and Arima Kinen. At 6, 3rd in the Takarazuka Kinen and Tenno Sho (Autumn), 5th in the Japan Cup; his camp announced his retirement, and after a 7th in his farewell Arima Kinen he left amid much affection. His stud career is eagerly awaited.
3006: Winning a maiden at 3, he stepped up to finish 2nd in the Spring S., but faded to last (16th) in the Satsuki Sho and 12th in the Radio Nikkei Sho. In autumn he won the St. Lite Kinen as 9th choice, sweeping wide. 9th in the Kikuka Sho after a sharp late run from last. 4th in the AJCC, then unplaced; he has been resting.
3007: One of Sinister Minister's runners, increasingly prominent on dirt. He won a heavy-ground debut from up front, the Oxalis Sho with a fast 35.9 finish, then the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun as favorite, breaking clear early and winning by 2.5 lengths - 3 straight. At 3, 4th in the Hyogo Championship, he won the Shimotsuki S. (OP) and was 2nd in the Subaru S. (L). At 4, 4th in the February S., he won the Oval Sprint and Musashino S. in autumn.
3008: A 2021 2yo dirt star who won 3 straight incl. Sonoda's Hyogo Junior GP. 6th on a turf debut, he won his 2nd dirt race and the Nadeshiko Sho, then in the Hyogo Junior GP, co-favorite with fellow JRA runner Combustion, won their match race by a neck. 4th in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun, he tried the Saudi Derby at 3, bidding for a 3rd straight Japanese win after Full Flat and Pink Kamehameha, but was 2nd. Unplaced in the UAE Derby, 2nd in the Unicorn S., 3rd in the Korea Cup. At 4, 3rd in the Subaru S. (L), 2nd in the Onuma S. (L), he won the Elm S.
3009: Racing 8 times at 2, he won the Fukushima 2yo S. (OP) and was 2nd in the Chukyo 2yo S. (OP). At 3, 15th in the Falcon S. (G3), he won the Tachibana S. (L) and the Aoi S. (G3) as favorite by 2.5 lengths. 2nd to Vento Voce in the Keeneland C. and by a neck to Gendarme in the Sprinters S. (G1). At 4, 2nd in the Keio Hai SC, then poor until he beat G1 winner Grenadier Guards in the Hanshin C. (G2), his first win in 1.5 years. At 5 he won the Hankyu Hai (G3) and Keio Hai SC, 5th in the Sprinters S. and 3rd in the Mile CS. At 6, 2nd in Saudi Arabia's 1351 Turf Sprint, 5th in the Yasuda Kinen, 4th in the Swan S. - steady.
3010: Debuting in July at 2, he won his 3rd start and was 2nd to Geoglyph in the Sapporo 2yo S., but 10th in the Hopeful S. At 3, 4th to Matenro Leo in the Kisaragi Sho, he won the Kyoto Shimbun Hai as 8th choice with a fine late run. 12th in the Derby, 10th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, 9th in the Kikuka Sho.
3011: Winning a maiden at 3, he was 4th as 8th choice in the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen, then won the Rishiri and Moiwayama Tokubetsu. 2nd to Asama no Itazura in the St. Lite Kinen, he missed the Kikuka Sho unwell, then won the Challenge C. by 3.5 lengths. A fracture at 4 meant a long break; 13th as 2nd choice on return in the All Comers, he won the Challenge C. again by 1 3/4 lengths.
3012: A Funabashi horse who won the 2021 Japan Dirt Derby. Winning in his 9th start, he won 3 straight, then in the Japan Dirt Derby, 12th of 13, led all the way and held off the fancies by a head. 6th as favorite in the Totsuka Kinen, 5th in the Derby Grand Prix, 13th in the Tokyo Daishoten, and unplaced at 4.
3013: A Hokkaido filly who debuted in 2021. Running 2nd, 2nd, 1st, 2nd, 1st, she won the Lily C., then the Edelweiss Sho as 3rd choice in her first graded race, waiting in midfield in a hot pace and catching gritty Historic Nova by a neck. 7th in the JBC 2yo Yushun, her first 1800m race, she won the Tokyo 2yo Yushun Himba by 4 lengths as 5th choice. At 3, racing in Southern Kanto stakes, she won 4 of 4 apart from a 3rd in the Kanto Oaks - a bright future.
3014: An Irish filly by Deep Impact who won the 2021 Oaks, Irish Oaks and Yorkshire Oaks - Cartier champion 3yo filly - but was put down after a fracture the next year. With 1 win from 7 at 2, she won the Musidora S. at 3, then the Oaks by a record 16 lengths; Dettori said, "I've won many classics, but never one so easy." She won the Irish Oaks by 8.5 and the Yorkshire Oaks by 4, top of Europe's 3yo fillies. In autumn, 2nd in the Prix Vermeille, 6th in the Arc and 3rd in the British Champions Fillies & Mares S. Early at 4 she fractured her pelvis in her stall and, despite treatment, was put down.
3015: Winning her debut in October at 2, she rested, then was hampered and 10th in the Fairy S. at 3. In the Flora S., 5th choice, she broke clear from a handy spot - a perfect win. 9th in the Oaks, 13th straight into the Shuka Sho.
3016: She won her debut by 3 lengths despite a slow start, then after a break was 2nd choice behind later 2-classic filly Stars on Earth in the Queen C. in February at 3, and beat her by a neck - a classic hope. 11th in the Oka Sho, 5th in the Oaks, 9th straight into the Shuka Sho.
3017: Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Kyodo News Hai (G3), he was 2nd choice behind Do Deuce in the Satsuki Sho (G1), 4th, then 4th as Derby favorite. Skipping the Kikuka Sho, he was 3rd to fellow 3yo Equinox in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 5th in the Japan Cup, best of the 3yos. At 4, 2nd in the Dubai Turf, 4th in the Sapporo Kinen and Tenno Sho (Autumn), then 6th in the Japan Cup, his first time unplaced. At 5, 3rd in the Dubai Turf, then 14th and 9th.
3018: A 2022 3yo filly star who won the Shuka Sho (G1). From King Kamehameha's final crop, she completed graded winners in all 14 of his crops. Early on she placed in graded races (5th Niigata 2yo S., 3rd Saudi Arabia Royal C., 5th Daily Hai 2yo S.). At 3 she won the Flower C. (G3), skipped the Oka Sho, and was 2nd to Stars on Earth as 10th choice in the Oaks, holding on from up front. She won the Shion S. (G3), then was 3rd choice behind 2-classic filly Stars on Earth and Namur in the Shuka Sho; racing forward as usual, she broke clear and held them off - a G1. 14th in the QEII Cup, 12th in the Victoria Mile at 4; after a long injury break, 8th in the Osaka Hai and 9th in the Victoria Mile at 5, then she won the QEII Cup from a handy spot - a 2nd G1.
3019: Winning a maiden in his 5th start, 13th in the Aoba Sho, he won a 1-win race and was 4th to World Premiere as 16th choice in the Kikuka Sho. Restarting in allowances, he won the 2-win class only at 5, then 15th stepping up in the Tenno Sho (Spring), and won the Stayers S. that December - a true stayer. At 6: 11th, 12th, 5th, 7th, then 3rd defending the Stayers S. Meant to race on, he retired injured and became a riding horse.
3020: A legendary US sprinter, 6th in The Blood-Horse's top 100 US racehorses of the 20th century: 18 wins from 22, still hailed as the greatest sprinter ever for his raw speed. Winning easily from his debut, at 3 he beat crop-mate and later dual classic winner Damascus. Their rivalry was fierce: he faded from the front to 3rd in the Woodward S., beat Damascus in the Suburban H. at 4, then faded to 2nd in the Brooklyn H. In the Washington Park H. that summer he ran a dirt mile in an astonishing 1:32.2 - then a world record on any surface, still the world dirt record. Horse of the Year, he retired the next year after a record 1:20.2 for 7 furlongs in the Vosburgh H. Champion sire in 1971, his male line is gone, but he lives on as Fappiano's broodmare sire.
3021: Unbeaten in 2, favorite in the Hanshin JF (G1), she was 4th to Circle of Life. At 3 she won the Tulip Sho (G2) as favorite, a classic focus, but was 10th as Oka Sho favorite. 3rd in the Oaks, she lost the Shuka Sho by half a length to Stunning Rose and was 5th in the QEII Cup, 2nd-best 3yo. At 4, 7th in the Victoria Mile, 16th in the Yasuda Kinen, she won the Fuji S. (G2), then the Mile CS as 5th choice, finding a finish from another dimension at the back and sweeping past them all - a G1. 3rd in the Hong Kong Mile, 2nd in the Dubai Turf and Yasuda Kinen at 5. In the Mile CS she felt something in a leg, was eased home last, and retired.
3022: Debuting at 3, he won a maiden and 1-win race quickly, then kept placing until the 3-win class in autumn at 4. 4th in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai, at 5 he was 2nd in the Naruo Kinen and 3rd in the Tanabata Sho, then won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai as 8th choice, leading all the way; with longshots 2nd and 3rd, the trifecta paid 2.36 million yen. Winless in graded races at 6, he switched to jumps in December.
3023: Winner of the 2021 QEII Cup. With 19 starts, no graded win and no G1 runs, she was 10th choice - a stunning win, trifecta 3.39 million yen. Winning her 2nd start at 2, she needed 8 more for a 1-win race, then improved at 4, winning 2 more classes. 7th in her first open race, the Fuchu Himba S., she ran in the QEII Cup, where crop-mate and Osaka Hai winner Rei Papale, Shuka Sho winner Akaitorino Musume and All Comers 1-2 Win Marilyn and Win Kitos were fancied. Modest in results but nearly always fastest home, she unleashed her otherworldly kick as the fancies moved early and faded, and won easily. Winless after, apart from a 3rd in the Kinko Sho and 4th in the QEII Cup at 5, she retired after a 15th in the Arima Kinen.
3024: Winner of 6 G1s in 2022-2023 incl. the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen - best in the world, and the first crop of Kitasan Black, sending his sire's fame sky-high. Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S., he went straight to the classics: 2nd to Geoglyph in the Satsuki Sho and to Do Deuce in the Derby. In autumn he beat older horses incl. previous Derby winner Shahryar in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), then was Arima Kinen favorite over champion Titleholder and won easily from midfield. At 4 he romped in the Dubai Sheema Classic, earning the world's top rating, won the Takarazuka Kinen by a neck, and the Tenno Sho (Autumn) in a stunning record 1:55.2. In his farewell Japan Cup, billed vs. 3yo Triple Crown filly Liberty Island, the two broke clear but he drew away to win by 4 lengths - 6 G1s. His first stud fee: 20 million yen. Can he surpass his sire?
3025: A sharp closer. 5th in her first graded race, the Shion S., and 5th as stablemate Daring Tact won the fillies' Triple Crown in the Shuka Sho, she then struggled in graded races. Hampered and 12th in the Fuchu Himba S. under a new rider, she won the Turquoise S. with a stunning finish from wide. At 5, 3rd in the Nakayama Kinen, 10th in the Victoria Mile, 4th in the Chukyo Kinen and Keisei Hai AH, she won the Turquoise S. again by a neck, closing wide. At 6, mostly unplaced, but 3rd in the Keisei Hai AH.
3026: A top dirt horse from 2022 to 2025. Debuting in April at 3, he passed the allowance ranks by spring at 4, then won his first graded race, the Miyako S. (G3). At 5 he won the March S. (G3), then became a JRA-local G1 regular, winning the Teio Sho (JpnI) over T O Keynes, Omega Perfume and Chuwa Wizard; 5th in the JBC Classic, 3rd in the Tokyo Daishoten. At 6, 3rd in the February S. (G1), he won the Kashiwa Kinen and Teio Sho - top of the dirt world. Winless at 7 (best 2nd in the JBC Classic), at 8 he won the Kawasaki Kinen for a 4th G1-level win, 2nd in the JBC Classic, and retired after a 4th in the Champions C.
3027: From Leondeux's 2nd crop, his first JRA graded winner. 2nd on debut to hot favorite Today Is the Day, he won a maiden from midfield, then the Kyoto 2yo S. as 5th choice, avenging Today Is the Day with a brilliant late run from the back. At 3, 4th in the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen, 7th to Geoglyph in the Satsuki Sho, 16th in the Derby. After a long break he retired without racing again.
3028: A US-bred son of More Than Ready. After 3 near-misses he led to win his 4th start easily, then the Chukyo 2yo S. from the front. At 3 he won the Marguerite S. (L) and NZT - 3 straight - leading and holding off favorite Matenro Orion by a head. Slow away in the NHK Mile C., he closed from last for 7th.
3029: Winning his 2nd start, 2nd in the Kyoto 2yo S., talented early, at 3 he was 4th in the Shinzan Kinen and 3rd in the Kyodo News Hai, then won the Spring S. as 5th choice, leading from a fine start and holding off Arrival by a nose. Double-figure finishes in all 3 classics (11th, 10th, 13th).
3030: Winning his debut in spring at 3 and a 1-win race in autumn, he won 2 more classes in spring at 4. At 5 he won the Aso S. and Radio Nippon Sho (both OP), then the Saga Kinen at 6. Steady in graded races, he won the Hakusan Daishoten that autumn.
3031: A mare who blossomed at 5, winning 4 dirt graded races in a row incl. the Kashiwa Kinen. After a 1-win race in spring at 3, she struggled in the 2-win class until spring at 4, then quickly reached open class. At 5, 2nd in her first graded race, the TCK Jo-o Hai, she won the Empress Hai, then the Marine C., Kashiwa Kinen and Sparking Lady C. - 4 straight. Favorite in the Ladies' Prelude, JBC Ladies' Classic and Queen Sho, she was 3rd each time. 6th in the Tokyo Daishoten, 15th in the February S. at 6, then retired.
3032: After a turf maiden win she switched to dirt, doing best on heavy and bad going. Unable to break through in open races, she moved to local racing: 4th in the Ladies' Prelude, then helped by rain-soaked bad ground, she won the Queen Sho - her first graded title. Moving to Kawasaki in Southern Kanto, she won no more and retired to breed.
3033: Beaten by a record margin on debut at Sapporo, then 7 2nds and a 3rd in 9 more starts, he moved to Sonoda, won 2 straight and quickly returned to the JRA. 12th in his first graded race, the Heian S., he improved as distances grew and won the Nagoya GP as favorite that December - his first graded title. At 5, 3rd in the Kawasaki Kinen, then out of contention; he moved to local racing in June at 6.
3034: An explosive closer fancied for the 2022 classics. 5th on debut, he won a maiden by 7 lengths, was 2nd in the Hagi S. (L), then won the Hopeful S. (G1) as 2nd choice, breaking clear from up front in record time. Classic favorite at 3, he went straight to the Satsuki Sho as 4th choice and was 13th. 8th choice in the Derby, he closed from the back for 6th, about 6 lengths behind Do Deuce. In autumn, 8th in the Argentine Republic Hai, he won a blanket finish in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai (G3). Placed 3 times in graded races at 4 without a win. At 5, 2nd in Saudi Arabia's Neom Turf C. (G2), then 15th in the Osaka Hai, 10th in the All Comers and 8th in Bahrain's International T.
3035: 2nd on debut, he won a 1-win race stepping up that December. At 3 he won the Shinzan Kinen, holding off a charging Solitario. Favorite in the NZT, he couldn't catch front-runner Jungle Rock, 2nd; in the NHK Mile C. he was 2nd again, a neck behind Danon Scorpion. 17th in the Derby; unplaced in the Swan S. and Mile CS.
3036: A great US horse with huge influence on today's pedigrees. His son Raise a Native founded the dominant Mr. Prospector line; he also sired Diesis's grandsire Etan, Oguri Cap's sire Dancing Cap, Sea-Bird's sire Dan Cupid, Dancer's Image, Kauai King and more. As broodmare sire of Northern Dancer, his blood runs in most horses today. A rare champion on the track: 21 wins from 22, his only loss a 2nd in the Kentucky Derby. Unbeaten in 9 at 2 incl. the Futurity S., then top 2yo race; at 3 he won the Preakness and Belmont; at 4 he won 3 incl. the Metropolitan H., Horse of the Year, and retired. A huge grey who often won from up front almost unnoticed, he stood out on black-and-white TV and was called "The Gray Ghost."
3037: Nearly 80% of today's Thoroughbreds descend from Phalaris; of other lines, the most notable is Ribot's. It produced sires like His Majesty, Graustark and Tom Rolfe; His Majesty's line flourished through Pleasant Colony. In Japan, descendant Tap Dance City won the Japan Cup and Takarazuka Kinen.
