With Nearco, Ribot was breeder Federico Tesio's greatest horse, winning the 1955 and 1956 Arc - unbeaten in 16. He also won the Gran Premio del Jockey Club at 3, and the King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S. and Gran Premio di Milano at 4. His 2nd Arc was won by a record 6 lengths - film suggests 8.5 - a legendary monster.
3038: A tragic champion filly who won the US Filly Triple Crown unbeaten in 10, then broke down fatally. 35th in The Blood-Horse's top 100 of the 20th century, the highest for a filly. Dominant from her debut, Eclipse champion 2yo filly, she won the Acorn S. by 8 lengths and Mother Goose S. by 13, and the 2400m CCA Oaks by 2 3/4 - the Triple Crown. Then came a match race vs. Kentucky Derby winner Foolish Pleasure; she was favored but broke down mid-race and was put down. Still named champion 3yo filly, she entered the Hall of Fame the next year. Famously, Mr. Okada, who cared for her as a foal, returned to Japan and named his club "Thoroughbred Club Ruffian" after her.
3039: The 1959 Satsuki Sho winner, bred from English parents and raced in Japan as an in-utero import. Winning his debut easily in December at 3 (old age system), he won 2 more early at 4, was 2nd in the Spring S., then won the Satsuki Sho by 4 lengths in record time - a Big Eight win. He took the NHK Hai in record time too, but was 15th in the Derby as 2nd choice on bad ground. In autumn he won the Kyoto Hai (now Kyoto Shimbun Hai) and, skipping the Kikuka Sho, the Kumohata Kinen - Horse of the Year. At 5 he won the Osaka Hai, but was 4th to Kuripero in the Tenno Sho (Spring), 3rd to Otemon in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), and scratched injured before the Arima Kinen. Back at 6, he ran once and retired. At stud he sired Takarazuka Kinen winner Date Horai and Kikuka Sho winner Date Tenryu.
3040: The 1958 Satsuki Sho winner. At 3 (old age system) he won just a maiden from 5. At 4 he won 2 dirt races and an open race, then another, and entered the Satsuki Sho as 8th choice, behind Katsura Shuho (7 of 10, never out of the top 2) and in-form Southern Kanto import Daigo Homare. He beat them by a neck in record time - a huge upset. 4th choice in the Derby, he was a good 3rd behind those two. After 2 summer races at Chukyo he rested; back at 5 he won once, then was 7th of 8 in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and retired. He left few foals at stud.
3041: Winner of the 1975 Tenno Sho (Spring). At 4 (old age system) he ran in the classics: 4th Satsuki Sho, 2nd Derby, 3rd Kikuka Sho; that summer he won the Nihon Tanpa Sho (now Radio Nikkei Sho). Winless for a while at 5, he won the All Comers, then at 6 beat favored Kitano Kachidoki in the Tenno Sho (Spring) - a Big Eight win. He retired after the autumn Meguro Kinen; little success at stud.
3042: After years in allowances, he blossomed in 1965 at 6 (old age system), winning 6 straight incl. the Tenno Sho (Spring) - a famous late bloomer. Debuting in July at 3, he first won at 4 and stayed in allowances to the end of 5. A move to local racing was mooted, but trainer Fujimoto refused. 2nd stepping up in the autumn Meguro Kinen, he surged: winning an allowance at year-end, at 6 he won the Kimpai, AJCC, Keio Hai Spring H. and Swan S. - 4 graded races in a row - then the Tenno Sho (Spring) by 7 lengths on bad ground. A clash with Triple Crown winner Shinzan was hoped for, but Shinzan was scratched unwell; Shinzan's groom later said, "Asahoko then would have been even with Shinzan at his best." Fading after, 2 losses and a long rest, he won 2 open races at 7 and retired. At stud he got few mares and little success.
3043: The 1969 Derby winner - a race famous for incidents. Satsuki Sho winner Wild Moa was out with a fracture, so 3rd-placed Takatsubaki became favorite, but unseated his rider just after the start, causing uproar. In the straight, Dai Shinboru Guard, Minoru and Hakuei Ho fought it out, when Dai Shinboru Guard's groom broke past officials onto the track, waving the horse's hood and yelling "That's my horse!" Dai Shinboru Guard edged ahead to win by a neck. His only other graded win was the Diamond S. at 5 (old age system), but he was 3rd in the Arima Kinen at 4 and in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen at 6, thrilling fans in big races. At stud for 14 years, mostly with local runners, he sired no graded winner.
3044: The 1968 Derby winner, leading all the way to beat the much-touted big three, Takeshiba O, Asaka O and Mahchis. Raised by Country Farm and trainer Tameo Toyama on a "train them hard to make them strong" ethos, he ran 10 times at 2 (old age 3). Without a graded win, he won 3 open races by spring at 4 and was in the top 5 every time except a 6th in the Satsuki Sho. 9th choice in the Derby, he led boldly and, as the big three watched each other, won by 5 lengths. He won the Asahi Challenge C. and Kyoto Hai (now Kyoto Shimbun Hai), then was 6th in the Kikuka Sho, only his 2nd unplaced run. 9 wins from 30 by spring at 5. He is the only Derby winner to run 18 times before the Derby. Little success at stud.
3045: The 1967 Derby winner. Beaten twice at 3 (old age system), he transformed at 4: a maiden by 6 lengths, then an allowance and open race, and the Yayoi Sho - suddenly a classic lead. After another open win he was Satsuki Sho favorite, but a strike delayed the race 2 weeks, upset his preparation, and he was 7th. 5th choice in the Derby, he showed his class: a thunderstorm just before the race caused chaos and a furious pace, and he waited calmly at the back to win. A fracture found right after ended his career. He was donated to Malaysia as a stallion and died there.
3046: The 1962 Derby winner. He won his 2nd start, a newcomer race, in record time, and an open race in record time too - fast from age 3 (old age system). Winning 3 open races by spring at 4, he was 4th choice in the Satsuki Sho but 11th of 16. 6th choice in the Derby, he fought it out with Satsuki Sho winner Yamano O and 11th choice Korehisa, and won by 3/4 length. Poor in autumn: 2 open losses, 17th in the Kikuka Sho, 10th in the Arima Kinen. At 5, 3rd in the AJCC and Nihon Keizaisho, but won only 2 open races, and retired that year. Unremarkable at stud, he stopped covering at 12.
3047: A Southern Kanto star who moved to the JRA and won the 1958 Derby - the 2nd local-bred Derby winner after Golden Wave 4 years earlier. Dominant in Southern Kanto, favorite every time, he won 8 of 8, incl. the Zen-Nihon 3yo Yushun (old age system) by 7 lengths in record time. Moving to the JRA at 4, 2nd in his first open race, he won 3 straight incl. the Yayoi Sho and Spring S., proving himself on JRA turf. 3rd to Taisei Hope in the Satsuki Sho, he won the NHK Hai, then beat Katsura Shuho by a nose in the Derby - a Big Eight win. In autumn he won just 1 open race, last in the St. Lite Kinen and Kikuka Sho, winless to the end of 5, and retired. No graded winners at stud.
3048: An in-utero import by Bois Roussel who, at stud, sired many graded winners incl. Kikuka Sho winner Great Yoruka and Tenno Sho winner Asahoko - a homebred sire holding his own in an era of imported stallions. He also won the 1957 Derby. Slow to win at 3 (old age system), he blossomed at 4, winning 3 straight incl. the Spring S., then an open race. On soft going in the Satsuki Sho he was 2nd to mudlark Kazuyoshi, but beat him in the Derby; in-utero imports could then still run in the classics. Tendon trouble followed; back at 5, he won 2 open races and retired. From his first crop came spring Meguro Kinen winner Asa Ryu, then Big Eight winners Great Yoruka and Asahoko; twice a top-10 sire.
3049: The 1955 Derby winner. The JRA had been founded the previous September, taking over from state-run racing, and he won its first Derby. Unremarkable early, he won his 2nd start but was 7th in the Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system). At 4 he won 2 allowances and was 10th in the Satsuki Sho, then won an open race by a wide margin and, as 10th choice, won the Derby by 8 lengths - his first graded win. 5 more open wins followed; 2nd to Meiji Hikari in the Kikuka Sho, he was Horse of the Year. Unbeaten in 4 at 5 incl. the Diamond S. and Tokyo Hai (now Tokyo Shimbun Hai), he retired with 14 wins from 22. At stud he sired Kyoto Hai winner King Speed and Oi star Aoi Raiko.
3050: The 1954 Derby winner. State racing passed to the JRA that September, so he won the last state-run Derby. He first raced in Southern Kanto as Nentakara, winning 6 of 8 at 3 (old age system) incl. the Zen-Nihon 3yo Yushun. Moving to state racing at 4 and renamed Golden Wave, he won 3 straight, was 7th in the Satsuki Sho, then won the Derby by 3 lengths as 12th choice. He also won the Nakayama 4yo S. (now Radio Nikkei Sho), but was 7th of 9 in the Kikuka Sho. Older, he won only 2 open races; back in Southern Kanto in spring at 6, he ran 3 times and retired. At stud he sired spring Nakayama Daishogai winner Golden Oza.
3051: Winner of 3 graded races incl. the 1973 Takarazuka Kinen, he broke down in the Takamatsunomiya Hai and was destroyed. Blossoming in autumn at 4 (old age system), he won 3 straight incl. the Hanshin Daishoten; at 5 he won the spring Kyoto Kinen and Takarazuka Kinen. After his fatal fracture, it emerged he had been sent to a slaughterhouse instead of being euthanized - a scandal that reportedly led to today's rule of euthanasia as standard.
3052: A late bloomer who won the 1971 Tenno Sho (Spring) at 5 (old age system). He won a maiden only in February at 4, then 2 allowances; 3rd in the Spring S., 5th in the Satsuki Sho, 18th in the Derby. Stronger in autumn: 2nd St. Lite Kinen, 3rd Kyoto Hai (now Kyoto Shimbun Hai), 4th Kikuka Sho. At 5 he won the spring Meguro Kinen, then the Tenno Sho (Spring) on swamp-like ground, outfighting Okura - his first Big Eight win - and the Takarazuka Kinen with Mejiro Asama 2nd: 3 straight. He won the Hakodate Kinen under 62kg. At 6 he was only the 2nd Japan-trained horse in the Arc, 18th, and 7th in the Washington DC International. Winless after, he retired at the end of 7. His best foal was Anglo-Arab star Light Oscar.
3053: Winner of the 1964 Tenno Sho (Spring) and Takarazuka Kinen at 6 (old age system) - the first to win both in one year. Emerging midway through 4, 2nd in the Kobe Hai (now Kobe Shimbun Hai), 3rd in the Kikuka Sho, he began a fierce rivalry with fast-improving Ryu Forel. After a fracture at 5, back in autumn he was 2nd to Ryu Forel in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), then won the Hanshin Daishoten. At 6 he beat 2-classic winner Meizui in the Tenno Sho (Spring) - a Big Eight win - and Ryu Forel in the Takarazuka Kinen, top older horse. After 6 straight wins, he was 5th to Yamato Kyodai in the Arima Kinen, who also took Horse of the Year. At 7, peak Shinzan beat him in the Takarazuka Kinen and Arima Kinen, and he retired. At stud he sired Maruichi King, winner of 5 Southern Kanto graded races.
3054: The 1971 Kikuka Sho winner. Winning a maiden at 4 (old age system), he quickly won an allowance and the Mainichi Hai. 10th in the Satsuki Sho, 8th in the Derby, he improved, winning an open race in summer, then the Kobe Hai (now Kobe Shimbun Hai) and Kyoto Shimbun Hai in autumn. Kikuka Sho favorite, he led early in a slow pace and held on to win. Older, leg trouble limited him to the Chunichi Shimbun Hai at 5 and Sankei Osaka Hai at 6.
3055: One of the 1968 big three with Takeshiba O and Mahchis: 3rd in the Satsuki Sho and Derby, then winner of the Kikuka Sho. Called "the Young Prince" for his blue blood and beauty, he was 2nd on debut, then won 2 straight; in his first clash with Takeshiba O, the Asahi Hai 3yo S., he was 3rd. At 4 (old age system) he beat both rivals in the Yayoi Sho, but was 3rd behind them in the Spring S. and Satsuki Sho, and 3rd in the Derby, ahead of Mahchis but caught out by Tanino Hallo Moa - no spring title. In autumn he won the St. Lite Kinen, was 2nd in the Kyoto Hai, and with Takeshiba O abroad, beat Mahchis in a two-horse duel in the Kikuka Sho - a Big Eight win. 6th as Arima Kinen favorite, his first time unplaced, he was Horse of the Year. At 5 he won the AJCC; in another big-three clash in the Tenno Sho (Spring), 2nd to Takeshiba O but ahead of Mahchis. After a long break he lost 4 straight at 6 and retired. At stud for 10 years in Aomori, a declining breeding area, he had few foals and no stars.
3056: Winner of the 1969 Tenno Sho (Autumn). Debuting at 4 (old age system), he won easily and steadily climbed through allowances by summer; stepping up in the NHK Hai, he was 11th as 10th choice. Stronger at 5, he won the autumn Meguro Kinen and was 4th to Nit Eight in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). At 6, 6th in the Kimpai (East), 7th in the AJCC, he won the Argentine JCC, then placed without winning (4th Nihon Keizaisho, 5th Sapporo Kinen, 3rd Stayers S.). 5th choice in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he broke clear by 2 lengths as fancied Mahchis and Ryuzuki faded - a Big Eight title. 4th to Speed Symboli in the Arima Kinen, he retired after a 9th in the AJCC at 7. 8 years at stud, no stars.
3057: The 1967 Kikuka Sho winner, who added the 1968 Tenno Sho (Autumn). His big blaze and wild temper earned him the nickname "White-faced Rogue Monk." After a debut win he struggled, taking his 2nd win the day before the Derby. Too late for the spring classics, he won 2 open races and was 2nd in the St. Lite Kinen. 9th choice in the Kikuka Sho, in the shadow of stablemate Satsuki Sho winner Ryuzuki, he beat him by 1.5 lengths - a Big Eight win. Erratic at 5 (old age system) with 1 open win from 9, he won the Tenno Sho (Autumn) as 6th choice, in record time. At 6 he won 1 open race and retired after a 5th in the Arima Kinen. No notable foals.
3058: A Southern Kanto horse who moved to the JRA and won the 1961 Tenno Sho (Autumn), sharing a fierce rivalry with fellow Southern Kanto import Onslaught. At 3 (old age system) he won 2 of 11; Onslaught was far above him, beating him all 4 times. Moving to the JRA in spring at 4, he was 10th to Kodama in the Derby. He blossomed at 5, winning the Tokyo Hai (forerunner of the Tokyo Shimbun Hai) and Tokyo Kinen in spring, then the autumn Meguro Kinen and the Tenno Sho (Autumn), beating Onslaught into 2nd; 2nd to Homareboshi in the Arima Kinen, ahead of Onslaught. At 6, 10th in the Washington DC International, then 2nd to Onslaught in the Arima Kinen. 4th defending the AJCC at 7, he retired. Few foals in an era unkind to homebred sires; he later became a lead pony at Hakodate.
3059: A poor sire, but a racehorse who won the 1954 Satsuki Sho and Kikuka Sho and the next year's Tenno Sho (Autumn) - 3 Big Eight wins. Tiny, reportedly in the 380kg range, he blazed from the front and was called "the Brown Bullet Train." Racing first under his foal name Tamasan, he won 8 of 8 at 3 (old age system); renamed Dainana Hoshu at 4, he won 3 straight to the Satsuki Sho. His 11 straight wins from debut still tie the JRA record. 4th to Golden Wave in the Derby, he won the Kikuka Sho easily for 2 classics - champion 4yo colt. At 5 he won 6 of 7 incl. the Tenno Sho (Autumn), champion older horse. Worsening leg trouble ended his career after an 11th in the Nakayama Grand Prix (now Arima Kinen) at 6. At stud, only a few local graded winners.
3060: The 1968 Satsuki Sho winner, battling versatile Takeshiba O and Kikuka Sho winner Asaka O in the classics. At 3 (old age system) he won 3 of 4, then the Hanshin 3yo S. as Kansai's juvenile champion. At 4 he won the Kisaragi Sho; 3rd behind Asaka O and Takeshiba O in the Yayoi Sho, he beat both in the Spring S. and again in the Satsuki Sho - a Big Eight win. He won the NHK Hai, but in the Derby the three fought it out and outsider Tanino Hallo Moa stole it; he was 4th. He won the Sapporo Kinen and Hollywood Turf Club Sho (now Kyoto Daishoten); with Takeshiba O abroad, he was 3rd in the Kikuka Sho behind Asaka O and Date Horai. Older, he won the Sapporo Kinen and autumn Meguro Kinen, but was 5th in both Tenno Sho and 10th in the Arima Kinen. He retired after an open win at 6. No notable foals; he stood until 21.
3061: Rival of stablemate 2-classic winner Meizui in the 1963 classics, he won the final crown, the Kikuka Sho, as Meizui ran off and faded. Early on he won 4 straight from his 3rd start incl. the Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system). At 4 he beat Meizui in the Tokyo Kinen (forerunner of the Yayoi Sho), but was 2nd to him in the Spring S., Satsuki Sho and Derby. In autumn he won the St. Lite Kinen, then the Kikuka Sho, as Triple Crown certainty Meizui went too fast and stopped - a stable Triple Crown. 7th in the Arima Kinen, he rested with leg trouble. Back in autumn at 6 he won an open race; at 7 he won the Keio Hai Spring H. and was 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). Racing mostly at local tracks from 8, with an open win at Niigata, he retired early at 9. No notable foals.
3062: A fierce rival of crop-mate Hakuchikara, winner of the 1956 Kikuka Sho and 1957 Tenno Sho (Spring), he tragically died of acute pneumonia in 1958 at 6 (old age system) while still racing at the top. Debuting in August at 3, he beat Hakuchikara in the Asahi Hai 3yo S., champion 3yo colt. At 4, 2nd to outsider Hekiraku in the Satsuki Sho and to Hakuchikara in the Derby, he beat both in the Kikuka Sho for his title. Top of the fan vote for the Nakayama Grand Prix (now Arima Kinen), he was 2nd to older champion Meiji Hikari. At 5, 5th to Hakuchikara in the spring Meguro Kinen, he won the Tenno Sho (Spring) in record time, beat Hakuchikara in the All Comers and was 2nd to him in the autumn Meguro Kinen. At 6 he died of pneumonia after a summer break. Hakuchikara entered the JRA Hall of Fame; Kitano O did not, but is remembered as a great rival.
3063: A late bloomer who won the 1973 Arima Kinen at 5 (old age system). 13th in the Derby at 4, he restarted in allowances and moved up in summer at 5. After near-misses (3rd Mainichi Okan, 2nd autumn Meguro Kinen, 4th Tenno Sho (Autumn)), he won the Arima Kinen as 10th choice, slipping away as Haiseiko, Tanino Chikara and other fancies watched each other. He won the Naruo Kinen at 6 and AJCC at 7, proving it no fluke, and retired after the AJCC.
3064: A Southern Kanto star who moved to the JRA and won the Tenno Sho (Spring) and Arima Kinen, in a fierce rivalry with fellow import Takamagahara. Debuting at Oi, he won 7 straight, incl. the Zen-Nihon 3yo Yushun (old age system) by 15 lengths. At 4 he kept placing, then regained form to win the Aki no Kura (now Tokyo Daishoten). Moving to the JRA midway through 5, he won quickly, but Takamagahara, who had moved first, beat him: 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 3rd in the Arima Kinen. At 6 he won the Tenno Sho (Spring), beat Takamagahara in the Nihon Keizaisho, then won the Arima Kinen easily with Takamagahara 2nd - settling the rivalry, Horse of the Year. He retired the next year; in an era unkind to homebred sires, he left few foals.
3065: Winner of the 1958 Tenno Sho (Spring) and Arima Kinen. A half-brother to Derby winner O Kitsu, 2 years older, he was hyped from debut and won a newcomer race as favorite. Poor in spring at 4 (old age system) - 5th NHK Hai, 11th Derby - he won the Nakayama 4yo S. (now Radio Nikkei Sho) and Hakodate Kinen in summer, then was 2nd to Rhapsody in the Kikuka Sho and to Hakuchikara in the Arima Kinen. At 5 he won the Kimpai, the Tenno Sho (Spring) as 2nd choice, and the Arima Kinen by 4 lengths - Horse of the Year. Injured in the US at 6, he lost a year; back at 7 he lost 3 and came home. Getting few mares as a homebred sire, he returned to racing at 10 in Hokkaido as Onward Kei, winning 2 of 5, then went back to stud and sired Asahi Hai 3yo S. winner Onward Guy and Stayers S. winner Ziegar.
3066: Winner of the 1956 Derby and the 1957 Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen. He then went abroad - a big undertaking then - and won a US graded race, a first for a Japan-trained horse. Debuting in autumn at 3 (old age system), he won 5 straight, then was 2nd to Kitano O in the Asahi Hai 3yo S., starting their rivalry. At 4 he beat Kitano O in the Derby but trailed him in the Satsuki Sho, Kikuka Sho and Nakayama Grand Prix (now Arima Kinen). At 5 he beat Kitano O in both Meguro Kinen, then won the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen - Horse of the Year, top in name and fact. At 6 he sought a new challenge in the US; winless at first as he adjusted, he won the Washington's Birthday H. at 7 in his 11th US start - the first overseas graded win for a Japan-trained horse, a landmark for Japanese racing. 1 win from 17 in the US, he retired. Little used at stud in Japan, he was donated to India for his later years.
3067: Winner of the 1955 Kikuka Sho and the 1956 Tenno Sho (Spring) and Nakayama Grand Prix (now Arima Kinen). Hoped to succeed great homebred sire Kumohata, he sired only a few graded winners. Debuting in October at 3 (old age system), he won 4 straight incl. the Asahi Hai 3yo S. Classic favorite, he missed the spring through injury, then returned to win the Kikuka Sho by 10 lengths. At 5 he won the Tenno Sho (Spring), showing he was number one. The all-star Nakayama Grand Prix began that year; 2nd in the fan vote, in a field where 8 of 12 were Big Eight winners, he won by 3.5 lengths. After it he retired with the first-ever retirement ceremony in Japanese racing. Unanimous Horse of the Year, he entered the JRA Hall of Fame in 1990.
3068: One of the best from the final crop of English import Theft. A poor sire, he lives on through dams such as Asama Yuri, Mejiro McQueen's third dam. On the track he won the Satsuki Sho and Derby; a sure Triple Crown winner, the first since St Lite, he was beaten into 2nd in the Kikuka Sho by Hakuryo, whom he had always beaten. Older, he won the Hanshin Kinen in record time, but was 2nd to Hakuryo again in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and retired that year. Hoped to succeed his sire, he had few good foals, far behind Hakuryo, who sired top horses like Caesar and Yamano O. Still, through Asama Yuri's thriving female line, his name is firmly in Japanese racing history.
3069: A mare who ran in 4 straight QEII Cups (G1) from 2022 to 2025, always near the top. At 3 she won the Fairy S. (G3), catching later 2-classic filly Stars on Earth, but was beaten badly in all 3 classics (16th, 11th, 10th). 12th choice in the QEII Cup, she closed sharply from the back to dead-heat for 2nd with Win Marilyn. At 4, 4th in the Nikkei Sho, 3rd in the Fuchu Himba S., 4th in the QEII Cup. At 5 never in the top 5, best 6th in the QEII Cup. At 6, after a close 4th in the Ireland T., she was 3rd as 9th choice in the QEII Cup - the race's true regular.
3071: Foundation mare of one of Mejiro Farm's main female lines, with stars like Mejiro Gekko, Mejiro Dober and Mejiro Monterey, central to the farm's success. Winning 7 straight from her 2nd start, she beat leading colts in the Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system). At 4, 3rd in the Oka Sho and 2nd in the Oaks, no classic, but she won the 4yo Himba Tokubetsu and Hakodate Kinen, and retired in spring at 5. Her first foal was Yayoi Sho and Spring S. winner Mejiro Gekko; her daughters Mejiro Kannon, Mejiro Nagasaki and Mejiro Quincy spread her line. Mejiro Nagasaki's granddaughter Mejiro Dober won 4 G1s, and her descendants Shonan Lagoon and Hoo Ixel carry Mejiro Bosatsu's blood today.
3072: The 1965 Oaks winner, by Solonaway, then fighting for the sire title; with his Oka Sho winner Hatsuyuki and Derby winner Keystone, his crop swept the scene. She broke down fatally in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) at 5 (old age system). Winning 3 straight from her 2nd start, she was 3rd to Eight Crown in the Hanshin 3yo S. At 4, 2nd and 1st in open races, she was 12th in the Oka Sho, her first heavy loss. 4th in the 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, she rallied in the Oaks: with Hatsuyuki out, as 4th choice she won a tight finish. She also won the Nihon Tanpa Sho (now Radio Nikkei Sho). In autumn, 2nd in the Queen S., 12th in the St. Lite Kinen, but champion 4yo filly. At 5 she won only an open race; 4th in the autumn Meguro Kinen, she was pulled up in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and put down.
3073: The 1972 Oka Sho winner, who also won that year's Victoria C. (forerunner of the QEII Cup) - only 4 wins from 32, but 2 big ones. Winless in 6 at 3 (old age system), she won her 2nd start at 4, needing 4 more to pass the next class. Stepping up, 4th in the Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, she earned an Oka Sho place; 8th choice on her thin record, she closed from the back to win - a classic. Not entered for the Oaks, she rested; back in autumn she was unplaced in the Sapphire S., Kobe Shimbun Hai and Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu, 5th choice in the Victoria C. She led early and held on by a neck. Then 12 straight losses, retiring at the end of 5. As a broodmare, only 2 open winners.
3074: A 1973 4yo filly star (old age system), winner of the Oka Sho and Victoria C. (forerunner of the QEII Cup), 2nd in the Oaks. After a 4th on debut she was never out of the top 3, with 3 wins by January at 4. She beat classic favorite Kishu Laurel in the Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, then, as Oka Sho favorite, beat her again - a Big Eight win. 2nd to Nasuno Chigusa in the Oaks. 8th in the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu, her first time unplaced, she avenged Oaks winner Nasuno Chigusa in the Victoria C. - top of her crop. The only filly in the Arima Kinen, she was a fine 2nd. Older, she declined, losing 7 straight without a top-5, and retired. Of her 11 foals, Espal was 4th in the QEII Cup.
3075: Debuting in September at 2, she won a maiden in January at 3, then quickly a 1-win race. 4th choice in her first graded race, the Kanto Oaks, she sat 2nd, led in the straight and won easily, then won the Breeders' Gold C. the same way - 3 straight. In autumn, 2nd in the JBC Ladies' Classic and Queen Sho; at 4 she won the TCK Jo-o Hai and Empress Hai, then 2nd again in the JBC Ladies' Classic. At 5, 2nd in the Kawasaki Kinen and 4th in the Teio Sho, then 2nd in the JBC Ladies' Classic for a 3rd straight year - a rare record.
3076: Winning his debut, 6th in the Hopeful S., at 3 he won the Kisaragi Sho. Sharing favoritism with Strong Will and Dantes View, he ran last of the three, unleashed a powerful finish and just caught leader Dantes View. Then 10th in the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen, 12th in the Satsuki Sho, 13th in the Derby. In autumn he won the Andromeda S. (L) and was 2nd in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai.
3077: Beaten badly on a turf debut, she was steady on dirt, unplaced only once, and reached the 3-win class in autumn at 4. Placing in graded races (4th Miyako S., 3rd Queen Sho), she won the Ladies' Prelude in autumn at 5 as 2nd choice, catching favorite Shonan Nadeshiko. 5th in the JBC Ladies' Classic.
3078: He won his debut in July at 2 by 2 lengths from up front, then the Kokura 2yo S. stunningly: very slow away and alone at the back, he caught the field at the 4th turn, then surged past them all as if they were standing still. Favorite in the Keio Hai 2yo S., he was 14th.
3079: A closer with a sharp finish from the back. 4th on debut in a tight finish, she won a maiden easily from up front, then the Sapporo 2yo S. as favorite, catching Do Eyes from midfield to win by a length. In the Hanshin JF she flew from last but was 6th. A classic hope at 3, she was 15th as Tulip Sho favorite and 14th in the Oka Sho. Then, 15th choice in the Oaks, she closed sharply from the back for 3rd. She won the Queen S. as favorite in summer and was 4th in the Shuka Sho - a fine revival.
3080: The 2022 champion 2yo, unbeaten in 3 incl. the Asahi Hai FS. He led on debut and drew away easily, then as 2nd choice in the Saudi Arabia Royal C., sat 2nd, surged from 200m out after runaway leader Granite, and won by 1 1/4 lengths. In the Asahi Hai FS he led in the straight and held off Danon Touchdown by a neck - a G1 already. Expected to lead the milers at 3, he was 7th as hot NZT favorite, then 12th in the NHK Mile C., 18th in the Yasuda Kinen, 13th in the Centaur S., 12th in the Sprinters S. - his juvenile sparkle gone.
3081: He shot to fame winning the 2022 Unicorn S. (G3), a huge upset with a 620,000 yen trifecta. In his first graded race after a 1-win race, 7th choice, he raced forward and won a scramble by a neck, with 9th choice Sekifu 2nd and 8th choice Battle Cry 3rd. 2nd in the Japan Dirt Derby, 3rd in the JBC Classic, he won the Nagoya GP - a top dirt horse. Winless from 4, he won the Elm S. (G3) in summer at 5.
3082: Debuting in August at 2, she won a maiden only in June at 3, her 10th start, and spent nearly 2 years in allowances, reaching the 3-win class at 5. Unfancied in her first graded race, she won the Hanshin Himba S. Last (18th) in the Victoria Mile, then unplaced (12th Queen S., 12th Keeneland C., 12th Sprinters S., 16th Swan S., 14th Galaxy S.); after a 5th in the Kyoto Himba S. she retired to breed.
3070: A great mare who founded one of Japan's leading female lines. With half-sisters Tetsuno Homare and Kamiyamato she forms the Craig Dhu Lochi family; the branch through prolific Star Roch is called the "Star Roch line." Her own foals were poor, but later generations include Hard Barge, Sakura Yutaka O, Sakura Star O and Winning Ticket. Unsold at auction, allotted as a lottery horse, she drew little attention, but defied that: 3rd in the Oka Sho, she won the Oaks as 9th choice with a brilliant late run - the first lottery horse to win a Big Eight race. Without further graded wins, she won open and handicap races and was invited into the Arima Kinen; against 2-classic winner Kodama and other Big Eight winners, she led all the way to win as 9th choice. Perhaps paying for it, she lost 5 straight at 5, then won the Keio Hai Autumn H.; dislocating a joint in the Mainichi Okan, she was pulled up and retired.
3083: Winning a maiden in his 3rd start in November at 2, he struggled at the 1-win level, then at 3, 5th choice of 7 in the Shirayuri S. (L), led all the way into open class. He won the Radio Nikkei Sho, then was 3rd as 3rd choice against older horses in the Niigata Kinen. In the Kikuka Sho he was 15th, over 20 lengths behind Ask Victor More.
3084: Winning on debut at 3, she then kept missing, taking a 1-win race only in her 11th start; at 4 she won 2 more classes, reaching open class at 5. In her first open race, the Aichi Hai, 7th choice, she closed from the back to win. A regular fancy in graded races, she placed often (5th Fukushima Himba S., 4th Queen S., 2nd Challenge C.). At 6, 2nd in the Hakodate Kinen, winless; after a 4th in the Queen S. she retired to breed.
3085: The 2022 Kikuka Sho winner, a star from Deep Impact's second-to-last crop, giving his sire a record 5th Kikuka Sho and 24th classic G1. 3rd on debut behind later Satsuki Sho winner Geoglyph, he won a maiden, then at 3 a 1-win race and the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen, beating favorite Do Deuce by a neck. Not yet top-rated, he was 5th in the Satsuki Sho and 3rd in the Derby. 2nd in the St. Lite Kinen, he faced St. Lite winner Gaia Force in the Kikuka Sho with the spring leaders absent; as Gaia Force faded, he held on from the front by a nose - a classic, and Deep Impact's 12th straight crop with a classic winner. At 4 he slumped: 9th as Nikkei Sho favorite, 11th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) and Takarazuka Kinen. Resting that summer, he died of multiple organ failure from heatstroke.
3086: After a long struggle on turf, he switched to dirt at 5 and won 3 straight incl. the Champions C. Winning his 2nd start and 6th to Salios in the Asahi Hai FS, he showed early talent, but at 3 won only a 1-win race, passing 2 more classes in spring at 4. In open class he struggled (6th Kanetsu S., 11th Port Island S., 7th Capital S.), then on dirt at 5: 2nd in the July S. (L), his first open win in the BSN Sho (L), and the Sirius S. In the Champions C., 3rd choice behind hot favorite and defending champion T O Keynes, he split the field from midfield, beat the champion and caught gritty Crown Pride for a G1. At 6 he tried the dirt G1 circuit - 7th Saudi Cup, 15th Dubai World Cup, 7th Teio Sho - and retired.
3087: First with the JRA, he moved to Oi after a heavy loss in a 1-win race at 3; winless there, he moved to Hyogo that summer. Racing mainly in sprints, he climbed steadily and was 3rd in the Hyogo Gold Trophy. At 4 he won the Kurofune Sho, beating JRA stars Raptas and Helios, then the Kakitsubata Kinen. 4th in the Mile CS Nambu Hai, 5th in the JBC Sprint. At 5 he won the Sakitama Hai, was 2nd in the Mile CS Nambu Hai and won the JBC Sprint easily - a G1 horse. At 6, 5th in the Dubai Golden Shaheen (G1), 2nd in the Sakitama Hai, now a G1, and 4th defending the JBC Sprint.
3088: Without an open win in 36 JRA starts, he moved to Funabashi in spring at 8 and won the Nippon TV Hai - a long-awaited graded win. Winning his 2nd start at 2, he passed classes steadily at 3 and 4, but won the 3-win class only in autumn at 6. Best 5th in 6 open races, he moved to Funabashi, won his 2nd start there, then the Nippon TV Hai as 7th choice, closing sharply from midfield.
3089: Winner of the 2022 Oka Sho (G1) and Oaks (G1); favorite in the Shuka Sho (G1), she was 3rd, just missing the Triple Crown. Debuting in August at 2, she won her 2nd start, then 3rd in a 1-win race. At 3, 2nd in the Fairy S. and Queen C.; without a graded win, she was 7th choice in the Oka Sho but beat Water Navillera by a nose in a fierce duel, then won the Oaks with a superior finish from midfield - top of her crop. After injury she went straight to the Shuka Sho as favorite; slightly slow away, she closed brilliantly from the back for 3rd. At 4 she lost a duel with Jack d'Or by a nose in the Osaka Hai, 3rd as Victoria Mile favorite behind Songline, 3rd in the Japan Cup close behind Equinox and Liberty Island, and 2nd to Do Deuce in the Arima Kinen - winless but top class. At 5, 8th in the Dubai Sheema Classic and 7th in the Japan Cup, her sparkle faded.
3090: A star at last from 7-time G1 winner Gentildonna, she won the 2022 QEII Cup. Noticed early, she won her 3rd start and was 7th to Sodashi in the Hanshin JF. 10th in the Elfin S. (L) at 3, she skipped the classics, then won 3 straight classes from summer; 2nd choice in the Challenge C., 4th to Sovereign Valiant. At 4, near-misses (4th Kyoto Kinen, 2nd Naruo Kinen, 3rd Kokura Kinen), then she won the All Comers as 5th choice from a handy spot. 4th choice in the QEII Cup behind Triple Crown filly Daring Tact and Shuka Sho 1-2 Stunning Rose and Namur, she closed sharply from the back to win by 1 3/4 lengths. 3rd in the Arima Kinen as 3yo star Equinox rose, best of the older horses. At 5, 6th in the Osaka Hai and QEII Cup (HK), then 4th, 0.2 sec behind Equinox in the Takarazuka Kinen. 5th as 2nd choice defending the QEII Cup, 4th in the Hong Kong Vase, she retired to breed.
3091: After an easy debut win, 2 straight 2nds; 4th in the Spring S. still a maiden winner, he was 10th in the Satsuki Sho. Restarting in allowances, he won 3 straight, then the Tokyo Shimbun Hai early at 4 - 4 straight. 8th as Yasuda Kinen favorite in a blanket finish, 11th as 3rd choice in the Sekiya Kinen, he won the Kyoto Kimpai at 5, then 8th in the Nakayama Kinen and 10th in the Yasuda Kinen - inconsistent.
3092: Winner of the 2024 Tenno Sho (Spring) (G1). Winning a maiden in spring at 3, he was 4th as 15th choice in the Aoba Sho (G2), then won 3 straight classes by year-end and the Diamond S. (G3) at 4 in commanding style - 4 straight. 3rd to Titleholder in the Tenno Sho (Spring). In autumn, 5th All Comers, 6th Argentine Republic Hai, 14th Japan Cup. After about a year off, back in autumn at 5, 2nd in the Stayers S. At 6 he won the Diamond S. and Hanshin Daishoten, then the Tenno Sho (Spring) as favorite, breaking clear from a handy spot - 3 straight and a G1.
3093: 11th on debut, then always top 3, winning the 2-win class in summer at 3; 7th in the Kikuka Sho. At 4 he won the 3-win class, then the Kokura Daishoten as favorite, closing sharply from midfield. 3rd in the Osaka Hai, just behind Potager, then 14th in the Takarazuka Kinen.
3094: Winning a maiden late at 2, she missed 3 with a fracture, then won 3 classes at 4. 12th in her first graded race, the Turquoise S.; beaten in graded races at 5, she won the Nakayama Himba S. as 15th choice with a superb late run. Then 2nd in the Fukushima Himba S. and 3rd in the Keisei Hai AH, but 16th in the Victoria Mile and 11th in the QEII Cup.
3095: A 2000m specialist who won the 2023 Osaka Hai (G1). Debuting late at 2 and winning his 3rd start, he won 3 straight classes from autumn at 3, then the Shirafuji S. (L) and Kinko Sho (G2) - 5 straight - favored over G1 winners Rei Papale and Akaitoi, leading all the way. 5th as 2nd choice in the Osaka Hai, he won the Sapporo Kinen (G2) and was 4th to Equinox in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). 7th as 2nd choice in the Hong Kong Cup. At 5, straight into the Osaka Hai, he led throughout and won a 3-way photo by a nose - a G1, and the oldest-ever G1-winning ride for Yutaka Take. 5th in his first mile race, the Yasuda Kinen, then 6th Sapporo Kinen, 11th Tenno Sho (Autumn). Tendon trouble at 6 meant a long rest.
3096: 4th as favorite on debut, she struggled in maidens, 2nd 3 times in a row, winning only in her 6th start. 2nd choice in the Fillies' Revue, she caught hot favorite Namura Clair to win her first graded race. 9th in the Oka Sho; in sprints that autumn, 8th in the Swan S.
3097: After an easy debut win and a break, he won a 1-win race at 3, then the Mainichi Hai - 3 straight unbeaten - leading from a fine start and holding on by 3/4 length. Last (18th) in the Derby; 5th Kokura Kinen, 4th Fuji S., 9th in the Mile CS.
3098: Winner of the 2024 Mile CS (G1). Winless for long at middle distances, he switched to the mile late at 3 and won 3 straight classes, then his first graded race, the Milers C. (G2). 13th in the Yasuda Kinen; 2nd in the Fuji S., 4th in the Mile CS. At 5, 3rd in the Milers C., he won the Keisei Hai AH (G3), lost the Mile CS by a neck to Namur and was 4th in the Hong Kong Mile. At 6 he won the Milers C. again, 3rd in the Yasuda Kinen, 2nd in the Fuji S., then won his 3rd Mile CS try with a brilliant late run - a G1. 2nd in the Hong Kong Mile with a big late surge. At 7 he won the Dubai Turf (G1) in the UAE, 3rd in the Yasuda Kinen; 2nd by half a length in the Hong Kong Mile, he then retired.
3099: Debuting at 3, he won a 2400m maiden in his 3rd start, then the Aoba Sho (G2) in his first graded race as 4th choice, catching 2nd choice Lord Rezel from a handy spot. 5th to Do Deuce in the Derby, holding on well. 8th as 2nd choice in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, 7th in the Kikuka Sho. At 4, 3rd in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai and Kyoto Kinen, 6th in the Takarazuka Kinen, then he won the Kyoto Daishoten (G2). At 5 he won the Kyoto Kinen (G2), 6th in the Osaka Hai, 4th in the Takarazuka Kinen, 11th in the Hong Kong Vase.
3100: A sprinter who won the CBC Sho at 3 in 2022, the 3rd JRA graded win by a female jockey, for rookie Seina Imamura. 13th in the Fillies' Revue and 11th in the Aoi S. in spring, she won a 2-win race, then the CBC Sho, leading all the way. Unplaced after (7th Kitakyushu Kinen, 15th Sprinters S., 6th Keihan Hai) and at 4, she stunned fans leading all the way in the Centaur S. as 14th choice - jockey Kyosuke Tomita's first graded win in his 7th year.
3101: Debuting at 3 and winning his 4th start, he climbed 3 classes by the end of 4. At 5, 9th in the AJCC and 7th in the Kyoto Kinen, then after 5 months off he won the Tanabata Sho as 6th choice, breaking clear early from midfield by 2.5 lengths. 14th in the Niigata Kinen, 3rd in the Challenge C., 2nd in the AJCC at 6, then he won the Kokura Kinen in commanding style.
3102: Winning a maiden at 3, he passed the 2-win class by January at 4, then needed 12 tries until the Shirakawago S. in autumn at 5 for open class. 2nd in his first open race, the Brazil C. (L); at 6 he won the Procyon S. as 4th choice, breaking clear from a handy spot and holding on by half a length as the fancies collapsed.
3103: Struggling on dirt at 2, he switched to turf at 3 and quickly won 2 classes; the 3-win class took longer, but from summer at 4 he raced in graded and listed races. At 5, 4th in the Kochi S. (L), 2nd in the Tanigawadake S. (L), he won the Chukyo Kinen as 6th choice, leading as he likes and holding off outsider Cathedral by half a length. 5th in the Keisei Hai AH.
3104: A dirt miler who won the Elm S. in summer at 5. Nearly always among the top 3 choices, he never missed the top 5. Reaching open class in autumn at 4, he won the Marine S. (OP) at 5, then the Elm S. in his first graded race with a superb late run. Before the Nippon TV Hai he thrashed in the gate, was hurt and scratched; then 15th in the Musashino S. and 13th in the Antares S. at 6, and he retired.
3105: Winning his 2nd start, he won a 1-win race early at 3 and the 2-win class in spring, then the Leopard S. as 7th choice, waiting in midfield and winning a 3-way duel with fancied Taisei Drefong and Hapi. 3rd to K. I. Purple in the Hakusan Daishoten, 7th as 5th choice in the JBC Classic (G1).
3106: A late-blooming sprinter who won the 2025 Sprinters S. (G1) at 8. At 3 he was 4th to Contrail as 17th choice in the Satsuki Sho, 17th in the Derby. Climbing steadily, he reached the 3-win class at 4; at 5 he won the Tanigawadake S. (L), Yonago S. (L) and Sekiya Kinen (G3) - 3 straight - sharing favoritism with younger G1 winner Danon the Kid and beating him and outsider Shuri by 3/4 length. 12th in the Mile CS. At 6 he won the Tokyo Shimbun Hai (G3), then went abroad: 6th in Dubai's Godolphin Mile, 5th in the Mainichi Okan, 11th in the BC Mile. Turning to sprints at 7: 4th Takamatsunomiya Kinen, 2nd Keihan Hai. At 8, 2nd in the UAE's Al Quoz Sprint (G1), then he won the Sprinters S. - a G1 at last.
3107: Winning a maiden late at 2, 7th in the Shinzan Kinen and 4th in the Elfin S. (L), she skipped the classics, quickly won 2 classes and took the Niigata Himba S. (OP) in autumn. At 4, 2nd to Ruby Casablanca in the Aichi Hai and to Win Mighty in the Mermaid S., she won the Kokura Kinen in commanding style. 7th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). Winless at 5 but often top 5 (3rd Aichi Hai, 5th Osaka Hai and Naruo Kinen, 4th Kokura Kinen and All Comers).
3108: Winning her 2nd start, she was 10th to Resistencia in the Hanshin JF. Turning to sprints, she won a 1-win race at 3 and 2 classes at 4. 10th in the Kitakyushu Kinen and 12th in the Centaur S., at 5 she pulled off a huge upset in the Kitakyushu Kinen: 16th choice at 164-1, she broke clear easily from a handy spot and held off fancied Namura Clair and Taisei Vision.
3109: Debuting at 3, he won a newcomer race and 2 classes, then rested about a year; back in summer at 4 he won the 3-win class into open class. At 5 he won the Shunrai S. (L), then 7th in the Hakodate Sprint S., 9th in the Ibis Summer Dash, before winning the Keeneland C. as 6th choice with a brilliant late run. 11th in the Sprinters S. At 6 he won the Ocean S., then 8th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen.
3110: A noted 3yo filly of 2022. After an easy win in the Wasurenagusa Sho (L), she was 2nd choice behind Circle of Life in the Oaks, but 7th. In autumn she won the Rose S. as favorite, holding off Sariela from a handy spot. 4th choice in the Shuka Sho, she was 5th. At 4 she won the Aichi Hai as favorite, but 4th as favorite in the Nakayama Himba S. and 13th in the QEII Cup, her last race; she retired to breed.
3111: 2nd on debut in autumn at 2 to later Derby winner Do Deuce. After a fracture, back in March at 3 he won a maiden, then in autumn a 1-win race and the St. Lite Kinen (G2). 8th as Kikuka Sho favorite. Turning to the mile at 4: 2nd Milers C., 4th Yasuda Kinen, 5th All Comers, 5th Tenno Sho (Autumn). At 5 he tried dirt, 2nd in the February S. (G1), but after 15th in the Champions C. and 7th in the February S. at 6, he focused on turf, won the Fuji S. (G2), and was 2nd in both the Yasuda Kinen and Mile CS.
3112: Still a 1-win runner at 3, she ran well (4th Tulip Sho, 2nd Wasurenagusa Sho (L)). Climbing to the 2-win class, she was 5th as 12th choice in the QEII Cup in autumn at 4. At 5 she won the 3-win class, then the Fuchu Himba S. as 12th choice, flying past as if the rest were standing still and catching hot favorite Sodashi. 10th to Geraldina in her 2nd QEII Cup, 4th as 13th choice in the Arima Kinen. At 6 she struggled (10th Hanshin Himba S., 15th Victoria Mile, 5th Queen S., 7th Sapporo Kinen, 9th Fuchu Himba S., 8th QEII Cup), then was 3rd as 9th choice in her last race, the Challenge C., and retired to breed.
3114: Beaten badly twice, he improved and won a maiden in spring at 3 in his 5th start, then a 1-win race that autumn and the 2-win class in January at 4; slower in the 3-win class, he reached open class that autumn. In the Argentine Republic Hai, 6th choice, he broke clear from up front and held off favorite T O Royal to win easily. At 5, 3rd in the Hanshin Daishoten, 4th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), 12th in the Takarazuka Kinen; in Australia, 8th in the Caulfield Cup and 16th in the Melbourne Cup.
3115: He won 3 straight from spring to autumn at 3, then needed 1.5 years in the 3-win class, reaching open class in spring at 5. 3rd in his first graded race, the Stayers S., and 3rd in the Hanshin Daishoten at 6. In the Tenno Sho (Spring) he unseated his rider at the start but ran the full 3200m riderless, crossing 2nd behind Titleholder - a talking point. That autumn he won the Stayers S., breaking clear coolly from midfield by 3/4 length. At 7 he won Saudi Arabia's 3000m Red Sea Turf H., then was 3rd to Justin Palace in the Tenno Sho (Spring), making amends for the year before.
3116: A dirt star from 2022 to 2025, winning the Kashiwa Kinen (JpnI) twice. Debuting in March at 3, he reached open class in about a year, then won the Tokyo Sprint (JpnIII), Summer Champion (JpnIII) and Oval Sprint (JpnIII); 3rd in the Mile CS Nambu Hai (JpnI) and 5th in the Champions C. (G1). At 5 he won the Kurofune Sho (JpnIII), 4th in the Kashiwa Kinen. After a winless spell, at 6 he won the Kurofune Sho again and the Kashiwa Kinen - a G1 horse. At 7 he won both again, then the Sakitama Hai (JpnI) - better than ever.
3117: Debuting at 3, he won a newcomer race easily as hot favorite. 9th in the Hyacinth S. (L), he won a 1-win race easily, then in his first graded race, the Hyogo Championship, as 3rd choice, broke clear from a handy spot and drew away by 8 lengths - in a class of his own. 3rd as Japan Dirt Derby favorite, then 5th in the Hakusan Daishoten and 12th in the Miyako S.
3118: Winner of the 2022 Japan Dirt Derby, champion 3yo on dirt. Winning his 3rd start and a 1-win race, he was 2nd to Delicada in the Fukuryu S. (OP) and 2nd, 8 lengths behind Blitz Fang, in the Hyogo Championship. In the Japan Dirt Derby he beat Blitz Fang and Unicorn S. winner Peisha Es - top of the 3yo dirt world. Mostly in G1-level races, 2nd in the Tokyo Daishoten. At 4, mostly unplaced, but 2nd in the JBC Classic and 4th in the Tokyo Daishoten. At 5, poor in G1-level races, he won the Saga Kinen and Nagoya GP.
3113: Struggling on dirt, he switched to turf in spring at 5 and was transformed, rising to win the Japan Cup. Leg trouble delayed his debut to spring at 3; he won his 5th start and a 1-win race in January at 4, then hit a wall, never top 2 in 8 tries. On turf he won the Awaji Tokubetsu (2-win) at once and the 3-win class, then in his first graded race, the Kyoto Daishoten, as 2nd choice, caught favorite Boccherini. In the Japan Cup, 3rd choice behind previous Derby winner Shahryar and 3yo Danon Beluga, 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he came out best in the straight duel - a G1. 10th as 4th choice in the Arima Kinen; at 6, 13th in the Dubai World Cup, 8th Takarazuka Kinen, 7th defending the Japan Cup. Meant to race on, he was found to have tendon trouble and retired to stud.
3119: 3rd on a turf debut in autumn at 2, he won a dirt maiden easily, then after 8 months off won a 1-win race by 9 lengths in summer at 3, 2 more classes by year-end and the Sobu S. (OP) at 4 - 3 straight. 15th in his first graded race, the Antares S., he won the Mercury C. Then 15th Sirius S., 14th Champions C., but he won the Saga Kinen at 5, and stayed steady (3rd Nagoya Daishoten, 4th Mercury C.).
3120: After 4 turf races without a win, he switched to dirt, won a maiden easily and a 1-win race in spring at 3. Stuck for a while, he won 2 classes in spring at 4 into open class, then the Rinku S. (OP), Matsukaze Tsuki S. (OP) and the Cluster C., sitting 2nd, leading early and drawing clear. 3rd in the Tokyo Hai.
3121: 4th on debut, she won a maiden by a mile, then was never out of the top 2. At 3 she won 3 straight classes, then the JBC Ladies' Classic as 3rd choice, breaking clear from a handy spot and holding off Grand Bridge by a neck - 4 straight, her first graded win a G1.
3122: A tough campaigner from 2, he won the Urawa Kinen in autumn at 4 in his 28th start. A maiden took 9 tries, the next classes 4, 6 and 6 more, reaching open class in autumn at 4. 4th in the Sirius S. and JBC Classic, he won the Urawa Kinen easily.
3123: Winning his debut by 8 lengths, at 3 he won a 1-win race, the Shoryu S. (OP) and Tango S. (OP). Favorite in the Unicorn S. (G3), he was 6th, his first time unplaced, as longshots Peisha Es, Sekifu and Battle Cry took the top 3. 2nd in the Oval Sprint, he won the Capella S. (G3) as 2nd choice with a finish from another dimension from the back, by 4 lengths. At 4, 3rd in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh Dirt Sprint (G3), 5th in the Dubai Golden Shaheen (G1); he won the Cluster C., the Korea Sprint (G3) and was 2nd in the JBC Sprint. At 5 he won the Riyadh Dirt Sprint, 4th in the Dubai Golden Shaheen, won the Korea Sprint again, then 11th in the BC Sprint (G1).
3124: Blossoming at 5 with the 3-win class and Sleipnir S. (OP), she placed in graded races (2nd Mercury C., 3rd Breeders' Gold C., 2nd Ladies' Prelude), 6th in the JBC Ladies' Classic, then won the Queen Sho, pushing to the lead, kicking early and staying clear. At 6, near-misses (4th Kawasaki Kinen, 3rd Empress Hai, 2nd Dioright Kinen), then she won the Breeders' Gold C.; favorite defending the Queen Sho, she was caught in the straight, 2nd.
3125: Blossoming in autumn at 5, he won 3 G1-level races in a row: the Tokyo Daishoten, Kawasaki Kinen and Dubai World Cup. Winning his 7th start in spring at 3, he took 2 years to pass the 3-win class. In open class from autumn at 5, he won the Brazil C. (L) and Canopus S. (OP), then the Tokyo Daishoten as 2nd choice, sweeping past from wide - his first graded win a G1. At 6 he beat champion T O Keynes in the Kawasaki Kinen, then won the Dubai World Cup, the 2nd Japanese winner after Victoire Pisa. He won the Nippon TV Hai, was 5th in the BC Classic, and won the Tokyo Daishoten again. At 7, 2nd in the world's richest race, the Saudi Cup, and in the Dubai World Cup - winless but Japan's top earner; 10th in the BC Classic. At 8, 3rd Saudi Cup, 6th in his 3rd Dubai World Cup, and he retired. That autumn Forever Young, 4 years younger, passed his earnings, leaving him 2nd all-time.
3126: A filly unbeaten in 2 incl. the Hakodate 2yo S., the 2022 crop's first graded winner. She drew clear from up front on debut, then beat fancied colts Supremo Flavor and Michela Dorata in the Hakodate 2yo S. 2nd to Livala in the Fantasy S., she was 7th choice and 10th in the Hanshin JF.
3127: He won a 1000m dirt debut easily. 3rd closing too late in the turf Hakodate 2yo S., he won a 1-win race on dirt, then the Hyogo Junior GP: with hot favorite Toledo pulled up, 2nd choice Omatsuri Otoko moved up from a handy spot to join the lead at the 4th turn and drew away fast - exceptional. 2nd by a head to Derma Sotogake in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun.
3128: 4th on debut, she beat hot favorite Baroque Dance by a nose in a maiden, then the Niigata 2yo S. as 4th choice: slow away and last, still at the back at the 4th turn, she slipped up the rail in Niigata's long straight and won by half a length. 14th as 8th choice in the Hanshin JF. At 3 she won the Fairy S. as 11th choice in a close finish, then was 12th, 15th and 12th in the fillies' classics.
3129: A filly from Kitasan Black's 2nd crop, quickly a graded winner, unbeaten in 2 incl. the Artemis S. (G3). 4th choice in the Hanshin JF (G1), she was 11th, swamped by later Triple Crown filly Liberty Island; at 3, 11th Oka Sho, 4th Oaks, 11th Shuka Sho. At 4, 5th Kyoto Kinen and Mermaid S.; 2nd as 12th choice in the QEII Cup, she then won the Challenge C. (G3).
3130: Winner of the 2023 fillies' Triple Crown, only the 7th ever, dubbed "the Monster" for her dominance. From Duramente's 3rd crop, after Titleholder and Stars on Earth - a G1 winner in 3 straight crops. Winning her debut easily, 2nd in the Artemis S., she won the Hanshin JF from midfield - champion 2yo filly. At 3 she went straight to the Oka Sho and won with an eye-opening finish from the back, then the Oaks by 6 lengths from a handy spot, and the Shuka Sho direct, breaking clear early and brushing off Masked Diva - a dominant Triple Crown. Skipping the QEII Cup, she took on champion Equinox in the Japan Cup; outclassed, she was still a strong 2nd. At 4, 3rd in the Dubai Sheema Classic, a puzzling 13th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), then 2nd to Hong Kong champion Romantic Warrior in the Hong Kong Cup. At 5, 8th in the Dubai Turf, then she broke down in Hong Kong's QEII Cup and was put down.
3131: Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Keio Hai 2yo S. (G2), which he won as 10th choice; with 11th choice From Dusk 2nd and 5th choice Speed of Light 3rd, the trifecta paid 2.22 million yen. 7th in the Asahi Hai FS. At 3 he won the Arlington C. (G3) and was 3rd in the NHK Mile C.; in Australia he won the 1500m Golden Eagle. At 4, double-figure finishes in Australia's Doncaster Mile and Hong Kong's Champions Mile; 3rd in the Keeneland C., but 11th Sprinters S., 12th Mile CS.
3132: 3rd on debut in a close finish, she beat favorite Haru Orb by a neck in a maiden, then led all the way in the Fantasy S. as 10th choice of 12, drawing clear in the straight and holding off a charging Bouton d'Or by 1 1/4 lengths. Seen as a fluke, she was 9th choice in the Hanshin JF and last (18th).
3133: 2nd on debut, he won a maiden as favorite, then the Daily Hai 2yo S. in style: leading from a fine start as usual, he kicked in the straight and held off favorite Danon Touchdown. From new sire Real Steel's first crop, he gave his sire a graded title at once.
3134: 3rd on debut unable to catch the 2 leaders, he won a maiden easily from 2nd, then the Kyoto 2yo S. as 5th choice, with Kazuhiro Sasaki's blueblood Grand Vinos hot favorite. Leading from a fine start, he held the lead and fended off Top Knife by a head.
3135: From imported sire Mind Your Biscuits' first crop, his first graded winner. Debuting in August at 2 and winning her 2nd start, she ran in Mombetsu's Edelweiss Sho as 4th choice, waited in midfield, kicked from a perfect spot at the 4th turn and flew 2.5 lengths clear. Facing colts for the first time, 4th to Omatsuri Otoko in the Hyogo Junior GP.
3136: 2nd on debut, over 4 sec behind Yamanin Ours, then 10th, he won a maiden and ran in Mombetsu's JBC 2yo Yushun as 9th choice of 13. Moving early from midfield, he led at the 4th turn and drew away to win easily - Hokko Tarumae's 2nd JRA-local graded winner after Blitz Fang. At 3, 5th in the Hyacinth S. (L), 12th in the UAE Derby, then 6th in the Japan Dirt Derby and 7th in the Hakusan Daishoten.
3137: From imported sire Mind Your Biscuits' first crop, he won the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun, giving his sire a G1 at once. After 6th, 4th and 3rd, he won a maiden easily from 2nd and a 1-win race in a tight finish. In the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun he waited in midfield, moved wide at the 4th turn and beat Omatsuri Otoko, rallying on the rail, by a head - his first graded win a G1. At 3 he raced abroad: 3rd in the Saudi Derby (G3), he won the UAE Derby (G2), then 6th in the Kentucky Derby (G1) and 2nd to White Abarrio in the BC Classic. At 4, 5th Saudi Cup, 6th Dubai World Cup, 13th BC Classic.
3138: By 2-classic winner Duramente out of a half-sister to Satono Diamond, with Triple Crown winner Orfevre as broodmare sire - a blueblood. Hyped from debut, he won only his 3rd start, 4th in the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S., and was 14th choice in the Hopeful S. Racing forward with 7th choice Top Knife, the two finished almost level; he won the photo by a nose - a G1. With 6th choice Kings Rain 3rd, the trifecta paid 2.46 million yen. At 3, 2nd in the UAE Derby (G2); then he unseated his rider in the Derby, 10th in the Takarazuka Kinen, 8th in the St. Lite Kinen. Switching to dirt, he was 3rd to Lemon Pop in the Champions C. and to Ushba Tesoro in the Tokyo Daishoten - a new path. At 4, 12th in the February S., 5th in the Dubai World Cup, 2nd in the Elm S. and 3rd again in the Champions C. - winless but consistent.
3139: By top US sire Tapit, he raced just 6 times yet became his sire's best, stunning racing in 2021-2022 with crushing wins. Injured in training, he debuted in spring at 3 and won in hand by over 10 lengths, then won again by a wide margin, then a G1 by 11.5 lengths eased down. Injured again at 4, he returned in June's Metropolitan H. at 1.4-1 favorite against stars incl. the previous BC Sprint winner; slow away, he pushed up to 2nd and won easily. In the Pacific Classic S. against older horses he won by over 19 lengths, by far the race record. Favorite at 1.5-1 in the BC Classic, he sat 2nd as usual, swept past before the straight and won. Unbeaten in 6, he retired to stud. 6 wins by a total of 71 lengths shocked the world; Timeform rated him 143, 5th best ever.
3140: He won his debut with a stunning finish from last, then the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. as 5th choice of 11, waiting at the back, slipping up the inside on the far turn and edging clear of a scramble by a neck. From Just a Way's 5th crop, his first graded winner since Danon the Kid 2 years earlier.
3141: A US turf horse who was 2019 Eclipse Horse of the Year. Debuting late, in February at 3, he won 4 straight incl. a graded race, then went lame and needed surgery. Back after nearly a year in December at 4, he won an allowance, then the Pegasus World Cup Turf at 5 for his first G1, a G2, and 3 straight G1s: the Turf Classic S., Manhattan S. and Arlington Million. Favorite in the BC Turf, he caught leader United by a head, and retired - unbeaten in 6 that year with 5 G1s, the first turf Horse of the Year in 6 years in dirt-dominated America. Bought early by the Shadai group, he went to stud in Japan, hoped to fill the gap left by Deep Impact and King Kamehameha.
3142: A Hong Kong superstar who emerged as Beauty Generation, 3 years older, departed. From 4 to early 6 he won 16 straight incl. 5 G1s, and kept winning after - Hong Kong Horse of the Year 3 years running. Emerging at 4 with 4 straight wins incl. a graded race, he swept the Hong Kong Classic Mile, Classic Cup and Derby - the local Triple Crown. At 5 he beat 8-time G1 winner Beauty Generation 3 times running (Celebration C., Sha Tin T., Hong Kong Mile), his first G1 and a changing of the guard, then won the Stewards' C., Hong Kong Gold C. and Champions Mile - Horse of the Year. At 6 he won the Hong Kong Mile for 16 straight; 2nd in the Stewards' C. ended the run, but he won the Champions Mile, Horse of the Year again. At 7, 2nd by a neck bidding for a 3rd Hong Kong Mile, he again won the Stewards' C., Gold C. and Champions Mile - 9 G1s - and passed Australia's Winx as the world's top earner. At 8 he won a 3rd Hong Kong Mile, then 4th bidding for a 4th Champions Mile, and retired to Northern Horse Park in Hokkaido.
3143: Winner of the 2023 Nakayama Kimpai. Unbeaten in 2, 3rd to Killer Ability in the Hopeful S. At 3, 11th in the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen and 8th in the Satsuki Sho. Restarting in summer, he quickly won 2 classes into open class, then the Nakayama Kimpai at 4, winning a blanket finish by a nose.
3144: Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Shinzan Kinen, a 2023 fillies' classic hope. She won her debut as favorite in November at 2, then the Shinzan Kinen at 3, slightly slow away but closing superbly. Straight to the Oka Sho as 2nd choice, she found nothing, 8th; 17th in the Oaks, 9th in the Queen S.
3145: He won 5 straight from autumn at 5 into 6 incl. the Tokai S. and Antares S. Winning his debut in March at 3, he broke a bone; back that December, another fracture; back in August at 4, another. Sound at last in autumn at 5, he won 3 allowances, then the Tokai S. at 6 and the Antares S. as hot favorite. 5th in the Teio Sho.
3146: Winner of the 2023 Kisaragi Sho after 3 straight wins, a classic contender. 2nd on debut, he won a maiden and a 1-win race at 3, then the Kisaragi Sho as favorite, holding on from up front. 9th from the back in the Satsuki Sho, 10th in the Derby, both without finding a kick.
3147: A leading filly in the 2023 fillies' classics. Winning her 2nd start, she won the Queen C. at 3 by a neck in a tight finish. As Liberty Island swept the Triple Crown, she was 4th, 2nd and 3rd in the 3 classics, then 3rd in the QEII Cup, best of the 3yos. 9th in the Arima Kinen.
3148: A noted runner in the 2023 classics. Unbeaten in 2, 4th in the Hopeful S., he won the Kyodo News Hai at 3, breaking clear from up front. Straight to the Satsuki Sho as favorite, he closed sharply for 3rd; 8th as 3rd choice in the Derby. 3rd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, then 9th in the Kikuka Sho.
3149: A stayer who won the 2023 Diamond S. Debuting in October at 2, he won his 4th start in May at 3; stuck in the 1-win class, he won easily at 2400m, then the 2-win class and Manyo S. (OP). In the Diamond S., 2nd choice, he closed brilliantly from midfield. Aimed at the Tenno Sho (Spring) and Takarazuka Kinen, he was injured and rested long.
3150: A miler who finally won the Kyoto Himba S. at 5. Winning her debut at 2, 14th in the Fillies' Revue at 3, she climbed steadily to the 3-win class by February at 4 and won the Capital S. (L) that December. After the Kyoto Himba S., 14th in the Victoria Mile, 9th as Sekiya Kinen favorite, then 2nd in the Swan S. and 7th in the Hanshin C.
3151: The dirt king of 2023-2024, the first Japanese graded and G1 winner for Lemon Drop Kid. In open class from spring at 4, he won the Negishi S. (G3) at 5, then the February S. (G1) as favorite. 10th in the Dubai Golden Shaheen in his first sprint, he won the Mile CS Nambu Hai by a huge margin as hot favorite, then the Champions C. at a new distance - both JRA dirt G1s in one year. At 6, 12th in the Saudi Cup, he won the Sakitama Hai and Mile CS Nambu Hai, then the Champions C. as favorite in his final race, retiring as the dirt king.
3152: A middle-distance horse who finally won a graded race, the 2023 Kokura Daishoten, at 7. Winning his debut easily late at 2, he climbed 3 classes by spring at 4. In middle-distance graded races, 3rd in the Challenge C. at 4 and 2nd in the Kokura Kinen at 6; at 7 he beat Cathedral by a nose in the Kokura Daishoten. 16th in the Osaka Hai, 4th in the Kyoto Daishoten.
3153: A 2023 sprinter who won the Hankyu Hai. Winning 3 straight allowances from summer at 3, he won his first graded race, the Hankyu Hai, at 4 as 2nd choice, holding off Daddy's Vivid by a neck. 7th in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, 5th in Hong Kong's Chairman's Sprint Prize, 2nd in the Centaur S., 7th as 2nd choice in the Sprinters S., 3rd in the Hanshin C.
3154: Winning her debut in November at 2 and a 1-win race at 3, she won the Tulip Sho (G2) as 7th choice, leading all the way. Leading boldly in the Oka Sho, she faded to 13th. Turning to sprints, she won the Aoi S. (G3), then 10th Kitakyushu Kinen, 16th Sprinters S. At 4, 3rd as 16th choice in the Kitakyushu Kinen, she won the Ibis Summer Dash (G3).
3155: She won the Nakayama Himba S. at 5 in 2023, then was 4th in the Arc - the first Japanese horse in the top 5 for years. Winning a 1-win race in spring at 3, she was 9th in the Oaks and 11th in the Shuka Sho, then raced mainly in the 3-win class, reaching open class at 5. In the Nakayama Himba S. she closed sharply from midfield to win. 10th choice in the Takarazuka Kinen, she was a superb 2nd, a neck behind champion Equinox; in the Arc her sharp late run earned 4th, amazing fans. After a 12th in the Arima Kinen a fracture was found and she retired.
3156: Winner of the 2023 Fillies' Revue. A sharp closer, she won her debut, 5th in a 1-win race, 3rd in the Elfin S. (L), then won the Fillies' Revue, breaking clear from a handy spot and holding on. 7th in the Oka Sho, 11th in the NHK Mile C.; turning to sprints, 2nd in the Opal S. (L), closing from the back.
3157: Winning his debut in spring at 3, he was 3rd to Shahryar in the Mainichi Hai (G3), then won 3 straight allowances; at 4 he was Chunichi Shimbun Hai favorite, 4th. At 5 he won the Kinko Sho (G2), was 2nd in Hong Kong's QEII Cup (G1), and won the Sapporo Kinen (G2). 3rd choice in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he closed from the back for 3rd behind Equinox. At 6 he won the Kinko Sho again, 2nd again in the QEII Cup, and 2nd in Australia's Cox Plate (G1). At 7, 2nd in the QEII Cup for a 3rd straight year; a leg problem then ended his career.
3158: Winner of the 2023 Flower C. Winning a maiden in her 3rd start at 2 and a 1-win race at 3, she ran in the Flower C. as 2nd choice; slow away and last, she flew home in the straight to win. 10th in the Oka Sho, 13th in the Oaks, but 7th in the Shuka Sho with her trademark late run from last.
3159: Winner of the 2023 Falcon S., the first graded winner for imported sire Declaration of War. Winning his debut in July at 2, 9th in the Niigata 2yo S., he tried dirt and was beaten badly, then back on turf won a 1-win race. 8th choice in the Falcon S., he beat favorite Carlo Veloce by a nose in a straight duel. 10th in the NHK Mile C., 9th in the Aoi S., 12th in the Swan S.
3160: Winner of the 2024 and 2025 Osaka Hai (G1). Unbeaten in 3 incl. the Spring S. (G2), he was 10th as 3rd choice in the Satsuki Sho, then a close 4th in the Derby, same time as the winner. In autumn he won the Challenge C. (G3). At 4, 2nd in the Kyoto Kinen (G2), he won the Osaka Hai as 2nd choice, tracking the leader and winning a tight finish by a neck. 3rd in the Takarazuka Kinen, 6th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 4th in the Arima Kinen - always near the top in G1s. At 5 he won the Osaka Hai again with champion's poise. Takarazuka Kinen favorite, he couldn't catch front-runner Meisho Tabaru, 2nd. 2nd to Romantic Warrior in the Hong Kong Cup, he then retired.
3161: Winner of the 2023 Mainichi Hai. Winning his 2nd start, 6th in the Kyodo News Hai still a maiden winner, he won the Mainichi Hai as 5th choice, edging a 3-way battle by half a length from midfield. 7th in the Derby after fading from up front; 10th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, 12th in the Kikuka Sho.
3162: A steady dirt horse who won the 2023 March S. at 7. Quick through the early classes, he ran in the Leopard S. at 3, then rested long. Back at 5 he won the 2-win class, the 3-win class in spring at 6 and the Sannomiya S. (OP). 5th in the Musashino S., 3rd in the Tokai S. at 7, he won the March S. 3rd in the Kashiwa Kinen (G1), he retired with tendon trouble.
3163: He won the 2023 Lord Derby CT at 4. At 3, unbeaten in 2, 5th in the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen and NHK Mile C. Winning the 3-win class that December, he raced in mile graded races at 4: 7th in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai, then won the Lord Derby CT with a brilliant late run. Then 7th Epsom C., 7th Keisei Hai AH, 8th Swan S.
3164: A leading 2023 3yo miler, winner of the NZT. 3rd and 5th, he won a maiden easily and a 1-win race, then was 2nd choice in his first graded race, the NZT; pulling hard up front, he held them off in the straight to win. 9th as 2nd choice in the NHK Mile C.; 8th Mainichi Okan, 10th Mile CS.
3165: Winner of the 2023 Hanshin Himba S. at 4. Through a 1-win race by January at 3, 4th in the Tulip Sho, she got loose before the Oaks and was withdrawn. 2nd in the Shion S., 7th in the Shuka Sho. At 4, as 6th choice in the Hanshin Himba S., she broke clear from up front - a perfect win. 5th in the Victoria Mile, holding on from up front.
3166: Winner of the 2023 Satsuki Sho (G1), from Kitasan Black's 2nd crop after Equinox. Winning his debut in November at 2, he won the Keisei Hai (G3) at 3, bursting clear from midfield. Straight to the Satsuki Sho as 2nd choice, he raced last and found a finish of his own to win the first classic. Hot Derby favorite, he closed well from a handy spot but missed leader Tastiera by a neck. 2nd in the St. Lite Kinen, Kikuka Sho favorite over Derby winner Tastiera, he waited in midfield but couldn't catch front-runner Durezza or Tastiera, 3rd. 8th in the Arima Kinen, 7th in the Osaka Hai at 4, then 2nd in the Takarazuka Kinen. 7th Tenno Sho (Autumn), 14th Japan Cup; at 5, 10th Osaka Hai, 6th Takarazuka Kinen, 14th Tenno Sho (Autumn), and he retired.
3167: Back from about a year off, she won the 2023 Fukushima Himba S. as an outsider - a first graded win at 5. At 3, 13th in the Oaks and 6th in the Shuka Sho, she stunned fans with a 2nd to Akaitoi in the QEII Cup. At 4, 11th Kinko Sho, 8th Osaka Hai, 5th Niigata Daishoten. Injured, she rested a year, then as 8th choice in the Fukushima Himba S. closed well from midfield to win a tight finish by a nose. 9th in the Victoria Mile; another injury followed and she retired to breed.
3168: Winner of the 2023 Flora S. Winning her 2nd start at 2, 2nd in the Fuyo S. (OP), at 3 she was 4th in her first graded race, the Flower C. 7th choice in the Flora S., she led all the way, holding off favorite Soda Zzling. 4th choice in the Oaks, 11th.
3169: Winner of the 2023 Aoba Sho, fancied for the Derby, but he died of acute heart failure in the race - a tragic end. 2nd on debut, he won a maiden and a 1-win race, then the Aoba Sho as hot favorite with the field's fastest finish from midfield. 2nd choice behind Satsuki Sho winner Sol Oriens in the Derby, he slowed alarmingly in the straight, collapsed after the line and died.
3170: Winning a maiden late at 2 and a 1-win race at 3, he won the Kyoto Shimbun Hai (G2) as favorite, edging clear of a blanket finish by a neck. 11th in the Derby. He won the Kobe Shimbun Hai (G2), then 10th as 3rd choice in the Kikuka Sho. At 4, 3rd in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai and Qatar's Amir T. (G3), 4th Meguro Kinen, 5th Kyoto Daishoten.
3171: Winner of the 2023 NHK Mile C. as 9th choice. A miler from 2, he won a mile debut easily and a 1-win race from the front. At 3, 6th in the 2000m Keisei Hai after fading from the lead, then 3rd to Eeyan as 7th choice in the NZT - made for the mile. In a wide-open NHK Mile C. with 5 horses closely fancied, he was 9th choice, but closed sharply from the back, broke clear and held off outsider Umbrail - two longshots 1-2, a big payout. 14th against older horses in the Yasuda Kinen.
3172: Winner of the 2023 Keio Hai Spring C. Debuting late at 2 and winning his 2nd start, 6th in the Kyodo News Hai, he climbed 3 classes steadily by January at 4. 7th in the Lord Derby CT, he won the Keio Hai Spring C. with a fine late run. 6th in the Yasuda Kinen; 2nd in the Fuji S., 9th in the Mile CS.
3173: A late bloomer who won the 2023 Dioright Kinen and Heian S. at 5. Early on he raced on turf, 4th in the Kyoto 2yo S., but stalled in allowances and switched to dirt late at 3. He won 4 straight incl. the Nagoya Jo S. (OP), then was 2nd in the Antares S. 12th in the turf Takarazuka Kinen and 12th as 2nd choice in the Champions C. At 5 he won the Dioright Kinen by 9 lengths and the Heian S., breaking clear from up front. 2nd in Korea's Korea C., then beaten in the Champions C. and Tokyo Daishoten - still blocked at G1 level.
3174: The 2023 Derby winner, top 2 in all 3 classics - best of his crop. Winning his debut in November at 2, 4th in the Kyodo News Hai, he won the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen in classic style from up front. 5th choice in the Satsuki Sho, he broke clear and looked the winner until Sol Oriens swooped, 2nd. 4th choice in the Derby, he turned the tables on hot favorite Sol Oriens, breaking clear and holding him off by a neck. Straight to the Kikuka Sho as 2nd choice behind Sol Oriens, he couldn't catch front-runner Durezza, 2nd. 6th in the Arima Kinen; at 4, 11th as Osaka Hai favorite, 7th Tenno Sho (Spring), then 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 3rd in the Hong Kong Cup. At 5 he won Hong Kong's QEII Cup (G1), his first overseas G1; then 8th as 2nd choice in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 7th Japan Cup, 6th Arima Kinen, and he retired.
3175: A consistent middle/long-distance runner who finally won a graded race, the 2023 Meguro Kinen, at 6. First winning in spring at 3, he climbed the classes by January at 4, then placed often: 2nd Meguro Kinen, 2nd Challenge C., 3rd Nikkei Sho at 5, 4th Tenno Sho (Spring). At 6 he won the Meguro Kinen as 4th choice, beating Diastima by a head. 3rd in the Argentine Republic Hai, 16th in the Arima Kinen - no G1 title yet.
3176: A miler who won the 2023 Epsom C. Debuting at 3, always top 3 in allowances, he reached the 3-win class by spring at 4, then was 2nd to Salios in the Mainichi Okan. At 5, 4th in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and 2nd in the Lord Derby CT, he won the Epsom C. with a sharp late run. In autumn, 3rd as an outsider in the Mile CS.
3177: A speedy filly who improved with age and won the 2023 Hakodate Sprint S. At 2 she won her debut and a 1-win race, 10th in the Hanshin JF. 7th in the Fillies' Revue at 3, she focused on sprints, won 2 of 3 allowances, and was 2nd in the Shunrai S. (L) at 4. In the Hakodate Sprint S. she closed brilliantly from the back. 10th in the Sprinters S.
3178: A noted 2023 3yo on dirt. Debuting in August at 2 with 2 straight wins, 3rd in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun (JpnI). At 3 he won the Hyacinth S. (L), 4th in the UAE Derby (G2), then the Unicorn S. (G3) as favorite. Winless for a while (3rd in the Green Channel C. (L) twice, 3rd Musashino S.), he won the Onuma S. (L) in summer at 5, his first win in about 2 years, then the Elm S. (G3).
3179: Winner of the 2023 Mermaid S. At 3 she won a newcomer race and a 1-win race, at 4 the 2-win class, and after a break the 3-win class at year-end. At 5, 2nd in her first graded race, the Fukushima Himba S., she won the Mermaid S. as favorite, breaking clear from midfield. 11th in the QEII Cup.
3180: A filly who won the 2023 CBC Sho and Kitakyushu Kinen, champion of the Summer Sprint Series. Tried early in graded races (12th Keio Hai 2yo S., 18th Arlington C., 14th Aoi S.), she rested long, restarted at 4 and quickly reached the 3-win class. 16th in the Hakodate Sprint S., she won the CBC Sho, then led all the way in the Kitakyushu Kinen to top the series. 4th in the Sprinters S. (G1); unplaced in the BC Turf Sprint and Hong Kong Sprint.
3181: At 3 he won the Principal S. (L), but was 11th in the Derby and 17th in the Kikuka Sho. After a long rest, back in spring at 4 he won the 3-win class, was 2nd as 2nd choice in the Niigata Daishoten (G3), then won the Tanabata Sho (G3), breaking clear powerfully from a handy spot. Tendon trouble meant another long break; back in autumn at 5, at 6 he won the Epsom C. (G3), and though unplaced in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Japan Cup, he was in fine health.
3182: Racing on turf too until spring at 3, he focused on dirt after a 12th in the Arlington C. Winning the 3-win class early at 4, 4th in the Coral S. (L), he won the Kyoto Grand OP (OP), then the Procyon S. (G3), and the Tokyo Hai in autumn. At 5, 9th in the February S. (G1), 2nd in the Dubai Golden Shaheen (G1), he won the Cluster C.; 9th in the BC Sprint.
3183: Debuting in 2023, he won the Hakodate 2yo S. He won a 1000m dirt debut as favorite from up front, then as 10th choice in the turf Hakodate 2yo S. surged from a handy spot and passed gritty Nanao by a length. 11th in the Keio Hai 2yo S. after a break, then 3rd in the Hyogo Junior GP - suited to dirt.
3184: Winner of the 2023 Chukyo Kinen. Winning his debut easily in October at 2, he kept missing until passing allowances at 4. 4th in the Rokko S. (L), 12th in the Yonago S. (L), 8th choice in the Chukyo Kinen, he led from the start and never tired - a first graded win, and 2nd in the Summer Mile Series. Last (16th) in the Mile CS.
3185: Winning the 2-win class in June at 3, she stepped up in August to the Leopard S. (G3), sat 2nd throughout, broke clear and held off Omega Guinness by a neck. 3rd in the Ladies' Prelude (JpnII), 6th in the JBC Ladies' Classic (JpnI), she won the Queen Sho (JpnIII) from up front. At 4, with the dirt race calendar overhauled, she oddly ran in the Queen Sho again in January, 4th, then won the Hyogo Jo-o Hai (JpnIII). 4th JBC Ladies' Classic; at 5, 3rd Hyogo Jo-o Hai, 2nd Sparking Lady C. (JpnIII), then she won the Breeders' Gold C. (JpnIII).
3186: Winner of the 2023 Sekiya Kinen. A miler from debut, 15th in the NZT in spring at 3, he took nearly 2 years to pass allowances. At 5, 4th in the Keio Hai Spring C., he won the Sekiya Kinen, closing sharply from midfield to catch leader Divina. 7th as Swan S. favorite.
3187: Winner of the 2023 Sapporo 2yo S. Debuting at Hakodate in July, he was caught after leading, 2nd, then led all the way in a maiden. 3rd choice in the Sapporo 2yo S. behind debut winners Gaia Mente and Gamble Room, he led as usual and drew away in the straight - a precious graded title for his sire Declaration of War.
3188: Winner of the 2023 Niigata Kinen. Winning a 1-win race at 3, 2nd in the Mainichi Hai, he was 15th choice in the Derby but held 5th from up front. 2nd choice against older horses in the Niigata Kinen, he won in classic style from up front. 15th in the Kikuka Sho, finding nothing from midfield.
3189: Debuting in 2023, he won the Kokura 2yo S. 2nd on debut, closing from the back but missing leader Kurino Hallelujah, he won a maiden easily, then the Kokura 2yo S. as 5th choice, surging from the back to just catch Miltenberg. 10th as 3rd choice in the Keio Hai 2yo S.
3190: Winner of the 2023 Shion S. Unbeaten in 2 from June at 2, 12th as 2nd choice in the Hanshin JF. At 3, 3rd Queen C., 4th NZT, 6th NHK Mile C. - steady at a mile. She won the Shion S. with a brilliant run from the back, then was 5th in the Shuka Sho, closing again.
3191: Debuting at 3, she won a newcomer race and a 1-win race in June, then stepped up to win the Rose S. (G2) as 7th choice, breaking clear from midfield. 3rd choice in the Shuka Sho, she closed from the back with the fastest finish, a length behind Liberty Island in 2nd. At 4 she won the Hanshin Himba S. (G2) and was 3rd in the Victoria Mile, but tendon trouble that autumn ended her career; she retired to breed.
3192: A middle-distance graded winner incl. the 2023 St. Lite Kinen. Winning a 1-win race in spring at 3, 3rd in the Radio Nikkei Sho, he won the St. Lite Kinen (G2). 8th in the Hong Kong Vase, 11th in the Niigata Daishoten at 4, he bounced back to win the Epsom C. (G3), then the All Comers (G2) as hot 1.5-1 favorite. Unplaced for a while after, he won the Mainichi Okan (G2) in autumn at 5.
3193: At 3 he won a maiden and 1-win race and was 3rd in the St. Lite Kinen. At 4 he won 2 more classes, the Hakodate Kinen (G3) as favorite, then the All Comers (G2), surging from a handy spot past favorite Titleholder. At 5, 2nd Osaka Hai, 5th Takarazuka Kinen, then a close 2nd in the BC Turf. At 6, 6th in Australia's Queen Elizabeth S. and 5th in the Hong Kong Cup.
3194: Racing only on dirt from his 2nd start, he reached open class in autumn at 3, then was injured and rested long. Back after 1 year 8 months, 4th in the Akhal-Teke S. (OP), he won the Uzumasa S. (OP) and was 2nd in his first graded race, the Miyako S. At 6, 2nd in the Tokai S., he won the Nagoya Daishoten; 4th in the Teio Sho, he won the Sirius S. (G3) and was 6th in the Champions C.
