At 7, 3rd in the Dioright Kinen and Antares S., he won the Sirius S. again and improved to 4th in the Champions C.
3195: A mare who blossomed at 4 in 2023 and won the Sprinters S. (G1) - her first graded win a G1. Debuting in June at 2, 3rd to Water Navillera in the Fantasy S., 2nd in the Elfin S. (L) at 3, she restarted in allowances and won 3 straight from summer to autumn. 5th in the Turquoise S., 9th in the Hanshin Himba S. at 4, she won the Azuchijo S. (L), was 2nd in the Kitakyushu Kinen, then won the Sprinters S. At 5, 8th Takamatsunomiya Kinen, 4th defending the Sprinters S. At 6 she won the Ocean S. (G3), 3rd Takamatsunomiya Kinen, 6th Sprinters S., and 2nd in the JBC Sprint - top class on dirt too.
3196: A notable 2yo of 2023. Leading from the start on debut in June, he won easily. In the Saudi Arabia Royal C. he raced last, then surged in the straight as if the rest were standing still, winning by 2 lengths. 4 winners in the race's first 8 runnings became G1 winners, so hopes are high.
3197: A miler who finally won a graded race, the 2023 Fuchu Himba S., at 5. Debuting late in May at 3, she climbed allowances by spring at 4, then struggled in mile graded races (11th Victoria Mile, 13th Sekiya Kinen, 10th Kyoto Himba S.). At 5 she was 4th to Songline in the Victoria Mile, transformed, 2nd in the Chukyo Kinen and Sekiya Kinen, then led all the way in the Fuchu Himba S. Unplaced in the QEII Cup and Hong Kong Mile.
3198: The 2023 Kikuka Sho winner. Still in allowances in spring, he surged in summer and won 5 straight to the Kikuka Sho (G1). 3rd on debut in September at 2, he won a maiden, rested with leg trouble, and won the Yamabuki Sho (1-win) in April at 3, the Hong Kong Jockey Club T. (2-win) in June and Nihonkai S. (3-win) in August. In his first graded race, the Kikuka Sho, he was 4th choice behind Satsuki Sho winner Sol Oriens and Derby winner Tastiera. Leading from a fine start, he settled 3rd, broke clear in the straight and won easily - 5 straight, his first graded win a G1. At 4, 2nd as hot Kinko Sho favorite, well behind Prognosis, 15th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), 5th in England's International S. 7th choice in the Japan Cup, he was 2nd, a neck behind Do Deuce. At 5, 3rd in the Dubai Sheema Classic, 9th Takarazuka Kinen, 8th Kyoto Daishoten, then scratched lame from the Japan Cup.
3199: Winner of the 2024 Oaks (G1) and Shuka Sho (G1). Just beaten by Bond Girl on debut, she won a maiden by 6 lengths at 1.1-1, then the Artemis S. (G3) as 1.5-1 favorite, breaking clear from 3rd. Rested with a leg issue, she went straight to the classics: 13th in the Oka Sho under a new rider, then she won the Oaks, closing strongly from the back. Straight to the Shuka Sho, it was a showdown with Oka Sho winner Stellenbosch, both seeking a 2nd classic; racing ahead of her, she never let her close and won by 1 3/4 lengths. 4th to Do Deuce in the Japan Cup against older horses and males. At 4, 6th in the Dubai Sheema Classic, then to the mile: 2nd in the new Shirasagi S. (G3, formerly the Yonago S. (L)), 7th Mainichi Okan, 10th Mile CS.
3200: A miler who won the Swan S. at 6 for his first graded win. 9th in the Asahi Hai FS at 2, 3rd in the NZT and 7th in the NHK Mile C. at 3, he restarted in allowances, reaching open class in autumn at 5. At 6, 4th Chukyo Kinen, 2nd Keisei Hai AH, he won the Swan S. as 10th choice. 8th in the Hanshin C.
3201: Winner of the 2023 Keio Hai 2yo S., from new sire Suave Richard's first crop - his first graded winner. 3rd to Bond Girl on debut, she won a maiden easily and the Dahlia Sho (OP) from midfield, then beat the colts in the Keio Hai 2yo S. 2nd choice in the Hanshin JF, she closed well from a handy spot but couldn't catch Ascoli Piceno, 3rd.
3202: Winner of the 2023 Fantasy S. as 15th choice. From Fine Needle's 2nd crop, she has her sprint-champion sire's speed. Bought for about 4.5 million yen at auction, she was 4th choice on debut, but won easily from up front, then in the Fantasy S. was the only early leader to hold on, winning by half a length - a shock. 7th choice in the Hanshin JF, she faded badly to 16th.
3203: Winner of the 2023 Argentine Republic Hai (G2). Nearly always top 3, he debuted at 3 and climbed allowances by spring at 4. 4th in his first graded race, the Meguro Kinen (G2), 3rd in the All Comers, he won the Argentine Republic Hai as favorite with the fastest finish from the back. 2nd in the Hong Kong Vase, best of the Japanese. At 5, 2nd in Qatar's Amir T. (G3); tendon trouble then ended his career.
3204: A new dirt star of 2023, unbeaten in 5 incl. the Miyako S. (G3), then 2nd choice as champion Lemon Pop's main rival in the Champions C., but 10th, finding nothing from the back. At 4 he won the Dioright Kinen (JpnII) easily, then 5th as Kawasaki Kinen favorite, 8th as 2nd choice in the Teio Sho, 12th as 8th choice in the Champions C. At 5 he won the Dioright Kinen again, then was poor again.
3205: Winner of the 2025 Yasuda Kinen (G1) and Mile CS (G1); with the Asahi Hai FS (G1) and NHK Mile C. (G1), he completed the grand slam of mile G1s open to colts. Unbeaten in 3 at 2 incl. the Asahi Hai FS. At 3, 2nd in the Kyodo News Hai, 3rd in the Satsuki Sho, then he won the NHK Mile C., leading in the straight and pulling 2.5 lengths clear. 13th in the Hong Kong Mile, he went straight to the Yasuda Kinen at 4 and won, again unchallenged after breaking clear. 2nd in the Fuji S., he was hot 1.8-1 favorite in the Mile CS and won by 1 3/4 lengths from up front - the undisputed champion miler.
3206: Winner of the 2023 QEII Cup (G1). Without a classic run, she beat the battle-hardened older mares as the 3yo leader. A close 2nd on debut in August at 2, she fractured a bone and rested long; back at 3 she won a maiden easily, then fractured again, missing the spring. Back in late June, she won a 1-win race, then as hot favorite in the Rose S. closed from the back but missed Masked Diva, 2nd. Skipping the Shuka Sho to freshen, she ran in the QEII Cup; with Triple Crown filly Liberty Island going to the Japan Cup, she was favorite, facing older mares incl. defending champion Geraldina. From a handy spot she broke clear and held off Rouge Eveil for a G1. A leg problem kept her out until the Fuchu Himba S. at 4, which she won easily; favorite in the Mile CS, 4th to Soul Rush. Winless after, best a 4th in the Yasuda Kinen at 5, she retired after a 6th in the Japan Cup.
3207: A mare who won her first graded race, the 2023 Fukushima Kinen, at 6. She climbed steadily: 1-win class in summer at 3, 2-win in spring at 4, 3-win in spring at 5. Winless in graded races (6th Fukushima Himba S., 16th Mermaid S., 7th QEII Cup), she was 3rd in the Mermaid S. and Tanabata Sho in summer at 6, then blossomed in the Fukushima Kinen, closing sharply from the back and outfighting Dandyism. 10th in the Arima Kinen, she retired to breed.
3208: Winner of the 2023 Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. Debuting in June, he led all the way and won by 9 lengths, then was 3rd to Gonbade Qabus in the Saudi Arabia Royal C., closing from midfield. 4th choice in the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S., he broke clear from a handy spot and won by 1.5 lengths.
3209: A leading member of the 2024 classic crop. A French-bred by Siyouni of the Nureyev line, his sire's first graded winner in Japan. Unbeaten in 2 from November at 2 incl. the Kyoto 2yo S. (G3), 2nd to Regaleira in the Hopeful S. (G1). At 3, 2nd in the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen, 5th in the Satsuki Sho, 3rd in the Derby. In Europe, 3rd in the Irish Champion S., then 12th in the Arc. Back home, 2nd to Do Deuce in the Japan Cup, best of the 3yos. At 4 he won Saudi Arabia's Neom Turf C. (G2), then 7th Dubai Sheema Classic, 6th Irish Champion S., 8th Japan Cup, 14th Arima Kinen.
3210: Debuting at 3, he was nearly always top 3 until passing allowances in January at 4. In middle-distance graded races he struggled (7th Kinko Sho, 7th Niigata Daishoten, 6th Epsom C.), then won the October S. (L) and the Chunichi Shimbun Hai (G3) as 2nd choice, holding on from up front. At 5, 10th in the Kinko Sho, he won the Niigata Daishoten; 4th in the Mainichi Okan.
3211: Winner of the 2023 Capella S. On turf from debut, he won the 2-win class in summer at 4, then lost badly and switched to dirt at 5, quickly winning the 3-win class and Keiyo S. (L). 15th in the turf Hakodate Sprint S., back on dirt 5th in the Muromachi S. (OP), he led all the way in the Capella S.
3212: Champion 2yo filly of 2023 and winner of the 2025 Victoria Mile (G1). Unbeaten in her debut and the Niigata 2yo S. (G3), she was 3rd choice in a wide-open Hanshin JF; from midfield she split the field and held off 5th choice Stellenbosch inside and 2nd choice Corazon Beat outside by a neck. At 3, straight to the Oka Sho as favorite, 2nd to Stellenbosch; favorite in the NHK Mile C., 2nd to Jantar Mantar. She won the Keisei Hai AH (G3) as hot favorite, proving it no fluke. Racing abroad, 12th in Australia's Golden Eagle; at 4 she won Saudi Arabia's 1351 Turf Sprint (G2), then the Victoria Mile as favorite. In France she was favorite for the Prix Jacques le Marois (G1), 6th.
3213: A filly who won Funabashi's Marine C. at 4 in 2023. Winning her debut in October at 2, a 1-win race in August at 3, she won 2 more classes early at 4, then the Marine C. as hot favorite by 5 lengths from up front. She retired after it: 5 wins from 8, top 2 every time except a 9th on turf.
3214: Unplaced on turf early, he switched to dirt in summer at 3 and won 4 straight into open class. At 4 he won his first graded race, the Kakitsubata Kinen (JpnIII), in a tight finish, the Mercury C. (JpnIII) easily, and the Hakusan Daishoten (JpnIII) - 3 straight. In G1s: 5th JBC Classic, 2nd Champions C., 2nd Tokyo Daishoten. At 5, 4th Dubai World Cup, 2nd Teio Sho, then he won the JBC Classic - a G1-level win. In the Champions C. he was 2nd by a nose to champion Lemon Pop. At 6, 4th Saudi Cup, 7th Dubai World Cup; he won the Mile CS Nambu Hai (JpnI), then was 2nd in the Champions C. for a 3rd straight year.
3215: Winning his debut easily in August at 2, he led all the way in a 1-win race at 3, won the Fukuryu S. (OP), then led throughout in the Hyogo Championship, winning by 6 lengths. 3rd to Mick Fire in the Japan Dirt Derby, 2nd in the Urawa Kinen. At 4 he won the Heian S. (G3), then 14th in the Miyako S. and 10th in the Champions C.
3216: He won his first graded race, the Hokkaido Sprint C., at 6. Mostly at 1800m early without winning, he switched to sprints in spring at 4, climbed allowances fast and won the Tempozan S. (OP) at 5. At 6, 2nd in the Tokyo Sprint, he won the Hokkaido Sprint C. from up front. 9th in the JBC Sprint.
3217: Winner of the 2023 Kanto Oaks. Winning her debut by 5 lengths, then a 4th, she won a 1-win race in spring at 3. Only 3rd choice at Kawasaki's 2100m Kanto Oaks, having run only at a mile, she raced forward and held them off in the straight. 2nd in the Breeders' Gold C., 3rd in the Queen Sho.
3218: Winner of the 2023 Sparking Lady C. Talented early, 2nd in the Hyogo Junior GP at 2, she passed allowances in summer at 3 and turned to graded races at 4: 2nd in the Sparking Lady C. and the Marine C. at 5, then she won the Sparking Lady C. in a tight finish, avenging the year before. 3rd to Lemon Pop in the Mile CS Nambu Hai.
3219: An Oi horse who won the 2023 Southern Kanto Triple Crown: Haneda Hai, Tokyo Derby and Japan Dirt Derby. Unbeaten in 3 at 2, at 3 he won the Haneda Hai and Tokyo Derby by 6 lengths each, then beat the JRA runners in the Japan Dirt Derby - an unbeaten Triple Crown, only the 2nd after Toshin Blizzard 22 years earlier. With the 2024 overhaul of dirt racing (a 3yo dirt Triple Crown open to JRA horses), he was the last Southern Kanto Triple Crown winner. He won Morioka's Derby Grand Prix at 1.1-1 - 7 straight. Against older horses: 8th Tokyo Daishoten, 7th February S. at 4, 5th Kashiwa Kinen, 4th Mile CS Nambu Hai, then 13th in the Champions C., his first double-figure finish.
3220: Winner of the 2023 Summer Champion and Hyogo Gold Trophy. Debuting late in June at 3, he won 4 straight from his 2nd start through the classes. Unplaced in open races (10th Keiyo S., 6th Echigo S., 9th Cluster C.), he tried leading in the Summer Champion and never tired. After 3.5 months off, 20kg heavier, he won the Hyogo Gold Trophy, tracking the leader and taking over in the straight.
3221: Passing allowances at 4, she was 4th in her first graded race, the Empress Hai, won the Meitetsu Hai (L), then the Ladies' Prelude as 6th choice, catching hot favorite Grand Bridge. 3rd in the JBC Ladies' Classic, 9th in the Champions C. At 5 she won the Queen Sho and Sparking Lady C., then improved to 7th in the Champions C.
3222: Debuting in Hokkaido in 2023, she won the local Edelweiss Sho. After an easy debut win came 5th, 5th, 6th, 7th, then 2nd in the Blossom C. In the Edelweiss Sho, 10th choice of 14, she saved ground at the back and swept past them all in the straight.
3223: Winner of the 2023 JBC Ladies' Classic. Racing on turf at first, she ran in the Radio Nikkei Sho and Rose S. at 3, then 3rd in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai and 2nd in the Aichi Hai at 5, still winless. Switching to dirt that summer, she won the BSN Sho (L) at once, was 2nd in the Sirius S., then as JBC Ladies' Classic favorite led early and drew away. At 6, 3rd in the Kawasaki Kinen, a close 2nd in the Ladies' Prelude, then 7th defending the JBC Ladies' Classic, her last race.
3224: A dirt name of 2023-2024. Debuting at 3, he reached open class in February at 4, was 3rd in the Antares S. (G3), won the Sannomiya S. and Aso S. (OP), then the JBC Classic as 4th choice, surging clear from a handy spot past Meisho Hario and T O Keynes - a G1-level win. 5th Tokyo Daishoten, 5th February S. at 5, 4th Kashiwa Kinen, then he won the Teio Sho from up front for a 2nd G1-level win.
3225: A horse who rose to the top of the dirt world in 2024, Real Steel's first G1 winner, from his 2nd crop. Unbeaten in 3 at 2 incl. the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun (JpnI), at 3 he won the Saudi Derby (G3) and UAE Derby (G2), was 3rd in the Kentucky Derby, won the Japan Dirt Classic (JpnI), 3rd in the BC Classic, and won the Tokyo Daishoten - a star at home and abroad. At 4 he won the Saudi Cup (G1), 3rd in the Dubai World Cup, won the Nippon TV Hai (JpnII), then the BC Classic - the first Japan-trained winner. His earnings passed a record 2.9 billion yen by end-2025. Without a JRA start that year, he was the first dirt horse to be JRA Horse of the Year, also champion older colt and champion dirt horse.
3226: Debuting in 2023, he won the Hyogo Junior GP. 4th as favorite on a turf debut, he switched to dirt and won a maiden and the Platanus Sho (1-win). In the Hyogo Junior GP, a two-horse duel with Satono Phoenix, they broke clear and he won the long battle by a nose. 2nd, well behind Forever Young, in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun.
3227: Debuting with the JRA in May at 3, winless in 3, he moved to Nagoya, won 2 straight, then returned to the JRA and passed allowances in autumn at 4. In open class at 5 he won the Brilliant S. (L), then the Urawa Kinen as 5th choice, moving early from the back, leading in the straight and drawing clear. He won the Nagoya GP, breaking the course record by over a second. At 6, 4th Kawasaki Kinen, 3rd Teio Sho, then he won the Hakusan Daishoten. Moving to Oi at 7, he stalled, then won Korea's Korea Cup (G3) and beat the JRA runners in the Tokyo Daishoten (G1) - a G1 horse.
3228: An Oi horse who, at 3 in 2023, went to the US and was 2nd in the Santa Anita Derby. Unbeaten in 4 at 2 incl. the local Haiseiko Kinen, 2nd in the Kumotori Sho at 3, he lost the Santa Anita Derby by a nose, then became the first local-racing horse to run in the Kentucky Derby, 12th. Back home, 2nd in the Kuroshio Hai, Totsuka Kinen and Derby Grand Prix - so close.
3229: A globetrotter who raced in the UAE, US, Saudi Arabia and Korea, winning the UAE Derby (G2) and Korea C. (G3). Unbeaten in 2 from October at 2, he announced an overseas campaign and won the UAE Derby. 13th in the Kentucky Derby, back home he was 2nd in the JBC Classic and Champions C. At 4, 5th in the Saudi Cup and Dubai World Cup, 2nd in the Teio Sho, he won the Korea C. Unplaced for a while, he won the Mercury C. at 5 and the Korea C. again.
3230: The 1948 US Triple Crown winner, who set many milestones incl. the first $1 million in earnings and 16 straight wins. 3rd in The Blood-Horse's top 100 of the 20th century, behind Man o' War and Secretariat. He won the Kentucky Derby by 3.5 lengths, the Preakness by 5.5 and the Belmont by 8. 19 wins from 20 that year; almost unanimous Horse of the Year and champion 3yo. Seen as the greatest since Man o' War ("Big Red"), he was nicknamed "Big Cy." Injury cost him the next year; back at 5, he won his return for 16 straight, then often missed. Racing on for the first $1 million, at 6 he won 3 straight incl. the Hollywood Gold C., passed $1 million and retired. At stud his first crop included Preakness winner Fabius, but he fell short of his sire Bull Lea, and his male line faded.
3231: A great sire who founded the Tom Fool line through Buckpasser and Tim Tam. His male descendants (Buckaroo, Egg Toss, and Japan's imports Meiwa Passer and Silver Charm) are minor, but Buckpasser's huge success as a broodmare sire spread his blood worldwide; horses out of Buckpasser mares include Maruzensky, Woodman, Miswaki and Seeking the Gold. A top racehorse too: in 1951 at 2 he won 5 of 7 with 2 seconds, US champion 2yo. Unwell, he missed the classics at 3, winning 6 from summer but no title. At 4 he shone again, winning all 10 starts from a handicap opener, incl. the New York Handicap Triple (Metropolitan H., Suburban H., Brooklyn H.) - only the 2nd ever - and was Horse of the Year over dominant 3yo dual classic winner Native Dancer.
3232: Hyperion's best son, who himself sired St Crespin and Vienna (sire of Vaguely Noble) - a key link keeping the Hampton line alive. His name, meaning the halo of a saint or icon, nods to his sire Hyperion (a god) and dam Angelola (angel). English-bred and raised, he ran in the English classics: 5th in the 2000 Guineas, 2nd in the Derby, 3rd in the St Leger, unplaced but talented, also 2nd in the King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S. He blossomed at 4, winning 4 straight to the King George and retired after it. Temperamental, before the King George he went wild and threw his rider, then started slowly. At stud his first crop included Arc winner St Crespin; he was champion sire in Britain and Ireland in 1960 and 1961. Vienna, from his 2nd crop, was modest on the track but sired Vaguely Noble, spreading Aureole's blood worldwide.
3233: A great sire who influenced pedigrees worldwide through Hail to Reason and Sir Gaylord. Hail to Reason sired Halo (sire of Sunday Silence and others) and Roberto (sire of Brian's Time and others), so in Japan it's hard to find a horse without them. Sir Gaylord sired Sir Ivor and Habitat, forming the Japanese line Habitat - Steel Heart - Nihon Pillow Winner. Though he founded an empire, he sired only 25 stakes winners and was not then seen as special; Hail to Reason and Sir Gaylord made him a great ancestor. He was a fine racehorse too: at 2 he won 3 incl. the Saratoga Special S., joint top of the US Free Handicap; unbeaten in 3 at 3, he fractured just before the Kentucky Derby and retired.
3234: One of Nasrullah's best sons, he sired Never Beat and Die Hard, whose imports made an era in Japan. American-bred, he raced in England and won the Derby and St Leger - Nasrullah's flagbearer in Europe. At stud in England, he was champion sire in 1962 with Derby winner Larkspur. Even his modest runners were exported for their blood; in Japan Never Beat, Die Hard and Cipriani did very well. Never Beat sired Mahchis, Lupinus, Riki Eikan and more, was champion sire 3 times, and sparked a "Never Say Die line boom." But in England his male line had nearly died out by the 1980s, and in Japan it faded with the rise of Northern Taste and others. Today it survives only in female lines.
3235: One of Nasrullah's leading sons. His best son, Tesco Boy, was a huge success in Japan, founding the great "Princely Gift line." A mid-level English sprinter, he was hoped to succeed Nasrullah at stud and steadily sired early-maturing sprinters. Tesco Boy, imported to Japan, sired Kitano Kachidoki, Tosho Boy, Sakura Yutaka O and many more, making his name. Then nearly all his sons, like Faberge, So Blessed and Sun Prince, were imported, so his male line died out elsewhere and developed uniquely in Japan; in the 1970s Tesco Boy was champion sire year after year. It faded with Northern Taste's arrival, and only Tesco Boy's line survives, carried on by Sakura Bakushin O, Air Jihad and others.
3236: A Nasrullah son who excelled both racing and at stud. Debuting in the US in 1954, he won 6 of 8 with 2 seconds, champion 2yo. At 3, 2nd to Swaps in the Kentucky Derby, he won the Preakness and Belmont and was Horse of the Year. Winning 22 of 30 incl. 2 Jockey Club Gold Cups, he retired to stud in autumn at 4 with US record earnings, later passed by Round Table. At stud he sired New York Filly Triple Crown winner Shuvee and many stars - 77 stakes winners. His best were mostly fillies, notably Gold Digger, dam of Mr. Prospector, and Bramalea, dam of Roberto. His male line struggled, but Good Manners, exported to Argentina, became champion sire there and carries it on.
3237: An American-bred 1955 Kentucky Derby winner, whose rivalry with crop-mate Nashua, winner of the Preakness and Belmont, was a sensation. Unremarkable at 2, at 3 he won 4 straight to the Kentucky Derby, beating favored Nashua. Back home in California he kept winning, and a rematch with Nashua was demanded; in their summer match race Nashua won by 6.5 lengths and took Horse of the Year. At 4 he won 8 of 10 and was Horse of the Year over Nashua, then retired to stud that autumn. In The Blood-Horse's top 100 of the 20th century he ranked 20th, above Nashua's 24th. At stud he sired Kentucky Derby winner Chateaugay and Hall of Famer Affectionately; Chateaugay, imported to Japan, sired Asahi Hai 3yo S. winner Hokuto Flag and is broodmare sire of Tamamo Cross and Mery Nice.
3238: A key sire keeping the Herod line alive today, spreading this minor line worldwide through Luthier and Lorenzaccio. French-bred and raised, he excelled at a mile, winning the Poule d'Essai des Poulains and Prix Jacques le Marois. Racing until 5, he retired to stud in France. His first crop included Oaks and Prix Vermeille winner Monade, and from his 7th came Luthier and Lorenzaccio, both successful sires. Luthier sired Sagace, No Lute and others, champion sire in France 4 times; another son, Dandy Lute, went to Japan and sired Bizen Nishiki. Lorenzaccio sired Ahonoora, leading on to Indian Ridge and Dr Devious. That line still carries Klairon's blood today.
3239: A hugely successful Nasrullah son who founded the Bold Ruler line, dominant in the US. His best include US Triple Crown winner Secretariat, Bold Lad, Bold Bidder, Lamb Chop and Gamely; he was US champion sire 8 times between 1963 and 1973. From his son Boldnesian's line came Seattle Slew and A.P. Indy, great sires who built the Bold Ruler empire. A top racehorse too, he won 23 of 32 incl. the Preakness and Trenton H. In 1957 at 3 he was US Horse of the Year over strong crop-mates Gallant Man and Round Table. 19th in The Blood-Horse's top 100 of the 20th century.
3240: One of the US "golden crop" of 1957 classic horses, battling Bold Ruler and Gallant Man. 3rd in the Kentucky Derby, he then won 11 straight incl. the Hollywood Gold C., forming the "big three" with Preakness winner Bold Ruler and Belmont winner Gallant Man. Beaten by them head to head, at 4 he won 14 of 20 and was Horse of the Year. Racing until 5, he retired with world-record earnings of $1.74 million. Versatile on turf and dirt, he set 16 track records. At stud he was US champion sire in 1972; sons Bold Lick and Targowice, imported to Japan, sired Kyoei Promise and Let's Go Tarquin. His male line faded, but as broodmare sire of Caerleon and in Seattle Slew's pedigree, his blood lives on.
3241: One of the US "golden crop" of 1957 classic horses with Bold Ruler and Round Table. Blossoming at 3, he had the Kentucky Derby won in a big-three showdown, but his jockey misjudged the finish line and he lost by a nose. He made amends in the Belmont, winning by 8 lengths in record time. Favorite in an autumn rematch of just the big three, he was 2nd, 2 1/4 lengths behind Bold Ruler, who took Horse of the Year. He raced until autumn at 4. At stud he trailed Bold Ruler and Round Table but sired 52 stakes winners; in Japan in the 1970s his foals included 2-time Sprinters S. winner Meiwa Kimiko and Asahi Hai 3yo S. winner Gallant Dancer.
3242: The first Irish-trained winner of the St Leger; at 4 in 1958 he won the King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S. and the Arc, British Horse of the Year. A modest sprinter early at 3 with just a maiden win, he won the 12f Trigo S. that spring, was judged a stayer, ran 2nd in the Derby and won the Irish Derby by 4 lengths. That autumn he won the St Leger. At 4 he won the Coronation C. and Eclipse S. easily, the King George by 3 lengths and the Arc - 4 straight. 3rd in his farewell Washington DC International, he was Horse of the Year with Timeform's top rating of 136. At stud he was 2nd and 3rd on the British-Irish sire list in 1967-1968; his best include Derby and King George winner Royal Palace, Irish Oaks winner Ancasta and Japan's Asahi Challenge C. winner Ballymoss Nisei.
3243: The sire of the great Northern Dancer, and also of Nonoalco and Icecapade, founding the powerful Nearctic line. A Canadian racehorse, he was champion 2yo in Canada; quieter at 3, at 4 he focused on the mile and won 9 of 18, Canadian Horse of the Year. He retired after racing at 5. His first crop produced his masterpiece, Northern Dancer, who reshaped world pedigrees and raised Nearctic's fame. Icecapade, from his 9th crop, sired Wild Again, whose line thrives; Nonoalco, from his 11th, succeeded at stud and, imported to Japan, sired Daiyusaku and Kashima Wing. Through dams, Nonoalco also produced Hishi Amazon and Admire Moon, so Nearctic's blood spreads without Northern Dancer too.
3244: A 1950s US horse who thrilled fans with incredible stretch runs, winning from dozens of lengths back - an American legend. He won his debut from behind, and that December the Golden Gate Futurity after making up 27 lengths. At 3 he won a 6.5f sprint after trailing by 41 lengths. His style drew a record 61,123 fans to the Santa Anita Derby; racing last as usual, he surged after 5 furlongs and swept past everyone from 28 lengths back to win easily. In the classics his kick deserted him: 12th in the Kentucky Derby, 8th in the Preakness. Battling poor health, he raced until 4 and retired. A poor sire with just 4 stakes winners.
3245: The 1958 US dual classic winner. Winning 8 straight incl. the Kentucky Derby and Preakness, he was 2nd, 6 lengths behind Cavan, in the Belmont with the Triple Crown at stake. Debuting in autumn at 2, he first won at 3; after 2 allowances, a stakes win in the Everglades S. began a winning run: Flamingo S., Fountain of Youth S., Florida Derby, an allowance, then the Derby Trial S. In the Kentucky Derby he held off sensation Silky Sullivan, then won the Preakness as favorite. Bidding to be the first Triple Crown winner since Citation 10 years earlier, he fractured during the Belmont and was 2nd, and retired. At stud he sired Hall of Fame filly Tosmah and, as broodmare sire, Known Fact and Davona Dale - strongest through dams.
3246: The 1959 Prix du Jockey Club winner, who as a sire made history with Grey Dawn, Sea Hawk and Coined Silver. Emerging at 3, he won 3 straight to the French Derby and beat older horses in the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud, but broke down in the Arc, 10th, and retired. At stud he quickly sired Grey Dawn and Sea Hawk, 2nd on the French sire list in 1966. Grey Dawn sired Morning Frolic; Sea Hawk, imported to Japan, sired Monte Prince, Monte Fast, Winners Circle and Ines Fujin. Herbager later moved to the US, where Big Spruce sired 43 stakes winners. His male line eventually faded, but he appears as broodmare sire of Rainbow Quest and Devil's Bag.
3247: Winner of the 1959 Belmont S. and US Horse of the Year, known as the sire of the great Damascus. He struggled early, first winning a maiden in his 8th start. Improved at 3, a Kentucky Derby contender, he lost by a nose to Tomy Lee, was 2nd to Royal Orbit in the Preakness, and won the Belmont. With 8 wins that year incl. the Travers S. and Jockey Club Gold C., he was Horse of the Year. At 4 he won the Suburban H. and Woodward S., but was injured and 3rd in the Man o' War S., and retired. Only 13 stakes winners at stud, but one was the historic Damascus, whose son Private Account carried on the line.
3248: A sire son of Grey Sovereign. His best include 1000 Guineas and Sussex S. winner Humble Duty and Eclipse S. winner Wolver Hollow, who was champion sire in Britain and Ireland in 1976. Another son, Spanish Express, succeeded in Japan, siring Asahi Hai 3yo S. winner Arrow Express, whose foals included Oka Sho winner Titania and Oaks winner Noano Hakobune; only Lead Wonder followed at stud, and the male line has faded. Sovereign Path himself won 8 of 25, incl. 3 stakes such as the Queen Elizabeth II S.
3249: Winner of the 1959 Santa Anita Derby and US champion 3yo filly that year, one of Triple Crown winner Citation's best. Unbeaten in 2, she won 3 more at 3, the last, the Santa Susana S., by 10.5 lengths. Encouraged, her camp ran her against colts in the Santa Anita Derby as favorite; she won by 2.5 lengths, only the 2nd filly winner, the first in 20 years. Aiming to be a filly Kentucky Derby winner, she was 5th to Tomy Lee, but later beat him in the Cinema H. and was named champion 3yo filly. She raced until 4. As a broodmare she produced Demoiselle S. winner Inca Queen and Silver Coin, dam of sire Coined Silver.
3250: A great sire who founded the worldwide Hail to Reason line through Halo and Roberto. Halo, ordinary on the track, sired Sunday Silence; Roberto won the Derby and sired Real Shadai, Brian's Time and more. In Japan today it is hard to find a horse without his blood. Brilliant on the track, at 2 he beat later dual classic winner Carry Back 3 times; injured in September at 2, he retired early, but won 7 stakes in that short time, champion 2yo. At stud his first crop included Belmont winner Hail to All and Derby winner Straight Deal (run at Newmarket); he was US champion sire in 1970. With Horse of the Year Personality, then Halo and Roberto, he built a great empire.
3251: The 1961 US dual classic winner. At 2 he couldn't beat crop-mate Hail to Reason, but with Hail to Reason retired early, he was classic favorite at 3, winning the Kentucky Derby as favorite and the Preakness easily. Injured in the Belmont, he was 7th, 15 lengths behind. Champion 3yo, though Horse of the Year went to older star Kelso. At 4 he beat Kelso in the Metropolitan H. and Monmouth H. In autumn he became the first Kentucky Derby winner to try the Arc, a big story, but was 10th. Retired to stud, he surprisingly returned to racing after the next breeding season and won twice, then retired for good that autumn. No stars at stud, but 12 stakes winners.
3252: A sharp closer who dominated French racing in 1963. A closer already at 3, he kept placing: 3rd in the French Derby, 2nd in the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud, 6th to Soltikoff in the Arc. At 4 he stepped up, winning the Prix Boiard, Prix Ganay, Coronation C. and Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud - 4 straight - beating Val de Loir and Arc winner Soltikoff to top the older horses. In the Arc he made amends with a brilliant late run. French champion older horse, he retired that year. At stud his best was Zamazaan, later champion sire in New Zealand, whose son Beau Zam stood in Japan, but the male line faded.
3253: An American filly star from 1961 to 1963, honored 3 years running: champion 2yo filly in 1961, champion 3yo filly the next year, and champion handicap mare the year after. Emerging in summer at 2, she won 6 straight stakes by year-end. At 3 she won the Kentucky Oaks easily - some said she could have won the Kentucky Derby. Winning the Acorn S. and Mother Goose S., 2nd in the CCA Oaks, she just missed the New York Filly Triple Crown, then won the Beldame S. in record time - top of her crop. At 4 she won 4 handicaps by summer; injured in autumn, she was still champion handicap mare and retired to breed. Barren at 5, she oddly raced once more, then produced 6 foals incl. Juvenile S. winner Cicada's Pride.
3254: An American mare who blossomed with age; at 5 she was the first female champion sprinter. Racing mainly at Aqueduct in Queens, New York, she was called "The Queen of Queens." She debuted with 6 straight wins at 2, then stalled at 3, but from summer at 4 won 6 straight to year-end. Her peak was at 5: she won the Toboggan H. easily, the first filly winner in 55 years; beat previous champion handicap mare Old Hat easily in the Top Flight H.; and won the Vagrancy H. under 137 lb (about 62.1kg), sealing champion sprinter and champion handicap mare (shared with Old Hat). She retired that year. As a broodmare she produced 1970 US Horse of the Year Personality, later a sire in Japan.
3255: From Nasrullah's final crop, one of his sire sons, he founded the powerful Never Bend line through Mill Reef, Riverman and Bravest Roman. A fine racehorse, he won 7 of 10 at 2, US champion 2yo. At 3, 2nd in the Kentucky Derby, 3rd in the Preakness, he won 5 stakes and retired at the end of 3. At stud he sired European great Mill Reef, becoming champion sire in Britain and Ireland; Mill Reef succeeded at stud with Mill George and Magnitude. Riverman sired Irish River and Riverlea, and Bravest Roman sired Calista Glory and Meisho Homura, spreading Never Bend's blood worldwide.
3256: Known as the sire of the great Mr. Prospector. A brilliant speedster, he retired injured after 4 wins from 4 at 2, setting or equalling track records in 3; US champion 2yo. At stud from 3, he sired Exclusive Native in his first crop, then dual classic winner Majestic Prince and English champion 2yo Crowned Prince, and in his 6th crop Mr. Prospector, who reshaped world pedigrees. Mr. Prospector and Alydar, from his 11th crop, both succeeded at stud, spreading Raise a Native's blood worldwide. In Japan, in-utero import Nifty Niece won the Centaur S.
3257: An American filly star of 1963-1964, out of great mare Cosmah and half-sister to Halo, sire of Sunday Silence. Debuting at 2 in 1963, she won 7 straight - 7 of 8 that year, Daily Racing Form champion 2yo filly. At 3 she won the Arlington Classic S., the first filly winner in 17 years, and beat veteran Old Hat in the Maskette H., winning 10 of 14 - US champion 3yo filly and DRF champion handicap mare. She won 3 more at 4 and 3 at 5, a long career. Rarely in foal, she left only 4 foals, 1 stakes winner, and could not carry on the great female line of her granddam Almahmoud and dam Cosmah.
3258: A sire son left in America by legendary Ribot, hugely successful racing and at stud - called Ribot's best heir. Inconsistent at 2, he blossomed at 3: after 3 straight wins, 3rd in the Kentucky Derby, he won the Preakness, beating favored Lucky Debonair. In autumn he did the unusual for a US classic winner and ran in the Arc; on his first trip abroad and first turf start, he was a fine 6th to Sea-Bird in a field of 20 called the strongest ever. 9 wins from 13, US champion 3yo. He raced until autumn at 4. At stud he sired Hoist the Flag, Run the Gantlet, Bowl Game and more; Hoist the Flag sired Alleged, carrying on the line.
3259: An Argentine great, unbeaten in 6 incl. the Argentine Triple Crown, then the Gran Premio Carlos Pellegrini against older horses - an unbeaten quadruple crown. Moving to the US, he won the Coronado H. and an exhibition race, but was hampered and 2nd in the Citation H., his first loss; a fracture found after ended his career. At stud he sired 3-time Eclipse Horse of the Year Forego, plus Thatch, Formidable, Posse and more, successful sires who carried his line. His daughter Special, dam of Nureyev and granddam of Sadler's Wells, spread his blood worldwide through dams.
3260: The 1967 Preakness and Belmont winner. With Buckpasser and Dr. Fager he formed a big three, and their 1967 Woodward S. clash is legendary. Winning 3 of 4 from autumn at 2, he was classic favorite at 3; worked up in the Kentucky Derby, he was 3rd to outsider Proud Clarion, then won the Preakness and Belmont as favorite. That autumn came the Woodward: older superstar Buckpasser, crop-mate Dr. Fager from a separate path, and Damascus - the clash of the century. He beat both by 10 lengths, a legend; Horse of the Year. At 4 he won 6, but Horse of the Year went to Dr. Fager at his peak, and he retired to stud. Hugely successful, he sired Private Account, Desert Wine, Ogygian and more - a rare carrier of the Teddy male line.
3261: The 1967 2000 Guineas and Derby winner, one of Ballymoss's best. Debuting in autumn at 2, unplaced first, he won 2 straight, then the 2000 Guineas and Derby at 3 - 4 straight. Aimed at the Triple Crown in the St Leger, his preparation failed; 3rd to Reform in the Champion S. instead. At 4 he improved, winning the Coronation S., Coronation C., Prince of Wales's S. and Eclipse S., then the King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S. as hot favorite - Britain's best older horse. Injury then ended his career. Not a great sire, but his best was Oaks and St Leger winner Dunfermline.
3262: A brilliant American filly by Bold Ruler, honored 3 years running: champion 3yo filly, then champion handicap mare at 4 and 5. Debuting late at 3, she had only a maiden win by spring. That summer she won the Princess S., then the Test S. and Alabama S.; though she missed after, no one stood out and she was champion 3yo filly. At 4 she won the Santa Maria H., Santa Margarita H. and Wilshire H., and was a close 2nd to peak Dr. Fager against males in the Californian S. 7 wins from 14, champion handicap mare; at 5, 5 from 13, champion again, and she retired. She died young with just 2 foals, but one, Cellini, won England's Dewhurst S.
3263: Winner of the 1968 2000 Guineas and Derby, plus the Champion S. and America's Washington DC International - Sir Gaylord's best, a success racing and at stud. Winning 3 of 4 at 2, at 3 he won the 2000 Guineas Trial, 2000 Guineas and Derby. Then a surprise 2nd in the Irish Derby, 3rd to previous dual classic winner Royal Palace in the Eclipse S., 2nd to Vaguely Noble in the Arc, before winning the Champion S. In the Washington DC International he beat previous winner Fort Marcy and Japan's Takeshiba O. He retired to stud in the US, siring 94 stakes winners incl. Arc winner Ivanjica, and was champion broodmare sire in Britain and Ireland in 1983.
3264: In 1968 she became the first winner of the New York Filly Triple Crown, said to be as good as famed US fillies Ruffian and Go for Wand. Very small, she was rated low early and won just 2 of 15 by the end of 2. At 3 she was transformed: an allowance, the Prioress S. and La Troienne S., then the Kentucky Oaks as favorite by 4.5 lengths. In the Triple Crown she won the Acorn S. by 6, Mother Goose S. by 10 and CCA Oaks by 12 - rivals gave up, saying no one could beat her. 2 more wins; undisputed champion 3yo filly. At 4, handicap weights bore down on her small frame; she won her opener narrowly, then broke down in the Santa Margarita H. Surgery saved her at first, but laminitis followed and she was put down.
3265: The 1968 Arc winner. As favorite, he crushed dual classic winner Sir Ivor, Irish Derby winner Ribero, German Triple Crown winner Luciano and French Oaks winner Roseliere - a performance compared to Sea-Bird's. Winning 2 of 4 at 2 in England, he moved to France at 3 under a new owner. Not entered for the classics, he aimed at the Arc, winning the Prix de Guiche, Prix du Lys and Prix de Chantilly. In a stacked Arc he beat Sir Ivor by 3 lengths, earning a Timeform rating of 140. He retired after it. A great sire too, with champion mare Dahlia, Exceller, Empery and more, he was champion sire in Britain and Ireland in 1973 and 1974. Gay Mecene and Mississipian, imported to Japan as sires, are also among his best.
3266: One of the most successful of the Herod line, he spread it worldwide through Arc winner Sagace, Yawa, No Lute and many more. Racing in France, he won the Prix Jacques le Marois and Prix Lupin; the French Derby and Arc were a bit far for him. He shone at stud: top first-season sire in 1973, he went on to be French champion sire 4 times. Sagace sired BC Classic winner Arcangues, and Dandy Lute, imported to Japan, led to Bizen Nishiki and Daitaku Helios. His male line has faded, but Lorenzaccio, Klairon's other leading son, keeps the Herod line alive.
3267: Raise a Native is best known for Mr. Prospector, but Majestic Prince is also a key sire son carrying his line today. His best include Belmont winner Coastal and Swaps S. winner Majestic Light. Majestic Light, also sire of Nishino Flower, was grandsire of Maria's Mon, whose sons Monarchos and Super Saver succeeded at stud, building a branch second only to the Mr. Prospector line. A fine racehorse, he won the 1969 Kentucky Derby and Preakness unbeaten, but racing with a leg problem in the Belmont he was 2nd to Arts and Letters, just missing the Triple Crown.
3268: A 1969 US classic star who won the Belmont S. Battling rival Majestic Prince, he lost the first 2 classics but won the last. Modest at 2 (2 of 6), he improved at 3, winning the Everglades S. and Blue Grass S. 2nd by a neck to Majestic Prince in the Kentucky Derby and by a head in the Preakness, he won the Belmont, denying Majestic Prince an unbeaten Triple Crown. With his rival retired injured, he dominated, winning the Jim Dandy S., Travers S., Woodward S. and Jockey Club Gold C. - Horse of the Year. Injured in spring at 4, he retired. At stud he sired Preakness winner Codex.
3269: A Chilean horse who moved to the US and was 1972 Eclipse champion turf horse. Good on turf and dirt, he was hugely popular in his California base; "cougar" means puma, so he was nicknamed "Big Cat." In Chile he won 5 of 12 by the end of 3 (late June, being southern-born). Moving to the US at 4, he won on both surfaces; in 1972, late 5 into early 6, he won 4 of 9 with 3 seconds and 2 thirds - champion turf horse. In 1973 he won 3 incl. the Santa Anita H. and Century H., and retired. At stud he sired 24 stakes winners incl. Kentucky Derby winner Gato Del Sol. His male line faded, but he is broodmare sire of sire Charlot.
3270: A standout from the rare Himyar line, he succeeded racing and at stud, keeping that line alive. Winning a maiden at 2, he improved at 3, winning the Derby Trial S., then, skipping the Kentucky Derby, the Withers S. and Arlington Classic S. at a mile. At 4 he won 4 of 5 incl. the Los Angeles H. and Autumn Days H. At 5 he peaked: after a 2nd, he won 6 straight handicaps incl. the San Carlos H. and San Pasqual H., the Santa Anita H. over Cougar in his first try at 10f, and the Hollywood Gold C. under 134 lb (60.5kg). Horse of the Year, he retired at year-end. At stud he sired later North American champion sire Broad Brush, French Derby winner Youth and 54 stakes winners in all.
3271: Dr. Fager's half-sister, who ruled US sprinting in 1969-1970, champion sprinter twice - a match for her brother. Watched from debut, she won 2 at 2, then shone at 3: the Jasmine S., Prioress S., and the Comely S. over later New York Filly Triple Crown winner Shuvee. Skipping the Triple Crown for sprints, she won the Miss Woodford S., Test S. and Fall Highweight H., then the Vosburgh H. over Shuvee and top older mare Gamely - champion sprinter. At 4 she won the Correction H., Hempstead H. and Regret H., then the Fall Highweight H. under 140 lb and the Interborough H. under 142 lb - astonishing strength. Champion handicap mare went to Shuvee, but she retired as champion sprinter again. A fine broodmare: 4 of her 5 foals won stakes; one, Great Above, sired Holy Bull, carrying on Ta Wee's blood.
3272: In 1969 she became the 2nd winner of the New York Filly Triple Crown. Behind contemporaries Gamely, Ta Wee and Gallant Bloom, she raced long and set the North American earnings record for a mare. Struggling early, she won her 7th start in August at 2, then the Frizette S. and Selima S. Triple Crown favorite at 3, she won the Acorn S. by 3/4 length, Mother Goose S. by 2.5 and CCA Oaks by 3 - the 2nd ever. She also won the Alabama S. and Ladies H., but lost twice to Ta Wee and 3 times to Gallant Bloom, who took the titles.
3273: Sir Gaylord's best son, a great European miler who sired many speedsters like himself, founding the Habitat line. Timid, he was slow to train and first raced in April at 3. Winning his 3rd start, he went straight into Britain's top mile race, the Lockinge S., and beat the stars as an outsider. 2nd in the St. James's Palace S., he won the Prix Quincey and Wills Mile, then the Prix du Moulin de Longchamp easily in his final race. At stud his first crop included Habat, making him top first-season sire in Britain and Ireland; 3 times champion 2yo sire, he produced many precocious sprinters. Steel Heart, from his 2nd crop, was imported to Japan and sired Nihon Pillow Winner, continuing to Yamanin Zephyr.
3274: Gallant Man's best foal, US champion 3yo filly of 1969, unbeaten in 8 that year, ahead of rival Shuvee. Inconsistent early, she found form in autumn at 2, winning 4 of 5 to year-end incl. the Matron S. and Gardenia S. At 3 she was even better, winning 8 straight from the spring Liberty Belle H., beating Shuvee in the Delaware Oaks and Gazelle H. and older star Gamely in the Matchmaker S. - undisputed champion 3yo filly. At 4 she won her first 2, then was 3rd against males in the Nassau County H. and 7th in the Suburban H., and retired. Of her 6 foals, none stood out.
3275: The strongest branch of Grey Sovereign's Fortino line comes through Caro. Racing mainly in France, he won the Poule d'Essai des Poulains, Prix d'Ispahan and Prix Ganay, and was 4th to Mill Reef in the Arc. His 2nd crop included French Derby winner Crystal Palace and French Oaks winner Madelia, making him French champion sire. Cozzene, Golden Pheasant, Winning Colors and more followed - 77 stakes winners in all. Crystal Palace, Cozzene and Golden Pheasant succeeded at stud, carrying his line today. A fine broodmare sire too: Tayasu Tsuyoshi, Maria's Mon, Mendez and others.
3276: The first US mare to earn $1 million. Graded races began in 1973, when she was 4, and she won 8 G1s through 6. She blossomed late at 2, winning the Villager S. by 8 lengths, then 6 straight at 3 to the Kentucky Oaks. In the New York Filly Triple Crown she won the Acorn S. but was 2nd in the Mother Goose S. and 3rd in the CCA Oaks. 3 more wins made her champion 3yo filly. At 4, with grading introduced, she won 4 G1s incl. the Santa Margarita Invitational H. and Santa Barbara H. - Eclipse champion older mare. A fracture at 5 threatened her career, but famed vet Dr. Copelan operated and she returned; at 6 she won 4 more G1s incl. the Matchmaker S. and Beldame S., champion older mare again, and retired. Of her 11 foals, a colt named Copelan after the vet won the Hopeful S. and went to stud.
3277: The 1972 US dual classic winner. He won the Kentucky Derby as favorite, struggled on sloppy ground for 4th in the Preakness, then won the Belmont easily. Winning his 2nd start, he took 5 straight incl. the Flash S. and Futurity S., the first Eclipse champion 2yo colt. At 3 he won the Hibiscus S. and Blue Grass S., then 2 classics, and the Hollywood Derby - best of his crop. Then 5 losses against older horses; champion 3yo went to crop-mate Key to the Mint. At 4 he beat Key to the Mint in the Brooklyn H. and met that year's Triple Crown winner, stablemate Secretariat, in the Marlboro C. Invitational H.; 2nd, but strong in defeat. He retired that year; at stud, 29 stakes winners incl. Hopeful S. winner Tap Shoes.
3278: A great sire carrying a main Never Bend branch, founding the Riverman line through Irish River, Riverlea, Rousillon and more. Winning his debut at 2, at 3 he won the Prix de Montenica, the Poule d'Essai des Poulains, the Prix Jean Prat and Prix d'Ispahan - 4 straight - then 3rd in the King George and 2nd in the Champion S., and retired. At stud he quickly sired 7-time G1 winner Irish River and Arc winner Gold River, French champion sire in 1980 and 1981. Rousillon, Riverlea and 9-time G1 winner Triptych, the "Iron Lady," followed. As broodmare sire: El-Harb, Erimo Excel and more.
3279: The leading horse of the Native Dancer branch through Etan, conceived during Etan's one year at stud in Ireland before export to Japan. Nearly all of Etan's line runs through him. Racing in England, he won his first 5 at 2, but lost 3 at 3 and retired. At stud he soon sired G1 winners Kris and Sharpo, champion 2yo sire in Britain and Ireland in 1978; then Diesis and Pebbles, and in the US, Trempolino and Selkirk. Kris, Diesis and Selkirk carried the Etan line on to today.
3280: A dominant US filly of 1973-1974, Eclipse champion 3yo filly and champion older mare, known as the dam of Real Shadai. Modest at 2 (a maiden win from 5), she blossomed at 3, winning 6 straight G1s: Monmouth Oaks, Delaware Oaks, Test S., Alabama S., Gazelle H. and Beldame S. - champion 3yo filly. At 4 she won the Beldame S. and Matchmaker S., and on her first turf start was 2nd in the Washington DC International, ahead of great mare Dahlia - champion older mare. She ran once at 5 and retired. She died at just 12, but her 2nd foal, Real Shadai, was a great sire, raising her name.
3281: Zeddaan's best son and lead sire heir. His son Kampala sired Tony Bin, building the line in Japan. Racing in France, he won the Poule d'Essai des Poulains, Prix Lupin and Prix Jacques le Marois. His first crop included Jacques le Marois winner Kenmare, then G1 winners Shakapour, Bikala and Kalaglow; he sired 21 stakes winners before dying at just 9. Kenmare sired Highest Honor and Kendor. Kampala, from his 2nd crop, was ordinary on the track but sired Tony Bin, the key to the line: imported to Japan, Tony Bin sired Winning Ticket, Sakura Chitose O, Jungle Pocket and more, spreading Kalamoun's blood.
3282: A filly who won her first 12 races at 2 in 1972 - Eclipse champion 2yo filly, and Horse of the Year rival of fellow 2yo Secretariat. Debuting at Canada's Woodbine, she won the My Dear S. in her 3rd start, then the Fleur de Lis S., Colin S. and Schuylerville S. easily, and the Selima S. on sloppy ground by 14 lengths. Unbeaten in 12, she split the Horse of the Year vote with Secretariat, who won the Eclipse; she was Canada's Sovereign Award Horse of the Year. At 3 she faded, winning 2 stakes from 14; at 4, only 5 allowances. After an 8th in the Miss Florida H. she fell ill and died. Still, she was Sovereign champion older mare at 4 and later entered both the Canadian and US Halls of Fame.
3283: The 1975 Kentucky Derby winner, best known for his match race with great filly Ruffian, who broke down fatally in it. Emerging from debut, he won the Dover S. by 10 lengths, then the Sapling S., Hopeful S. and Champagne S. - 3 G1s; unbeaten in 7, undisputed champion 2yo. At 3 he won the Flamingo S. and Wood Memorial, then the Kentucky Derby as favorite; 2nd in the Preakness and Belmont, he was still top of his crop. Meanwhile Ruffian swept the New York Filly Triple Crown, and a match race was arranged; Ruffian broke down and was put down, so he is remembered as her last opponent. Winless after, champion 3yo went to Wajima. At 4 he won 4 incl. the Suburban H. and retired. A fair sire with Marfa, Prayers'n Promises and more; his male line has since declined.
3284: A sire son of Nijinsky who sired Arc winner Suave Dancer and many more, and won the Poule d'Essai des Poulains and Prix Lupin himself. At 2 he won his debut, was 2nd in the Prix de Chenes, then won England's G1 Observer Gold C. At 3 he won the Poule d'Essai des Poulains and Prix Lupin - 3 straight G1s - but was 6th in the Derby and 8th in the Arc, less effective over further, and retired. His first crop included French 1000 Guineas winner Aryenne; with Maximova and Suave Dancer he was French champion sire in 1991. His 2nd-crop son No Attention, in Japan, sired Super Creek, and late son A.P. Preston won Japan's Asahi Hai 3yo S.
3285: A German-bred by German sire Literat out of German mare Surama, the 1977 German Derby winner. Winning his 3rd start and the Union-Rennen (G2), he won the German Derby easily as favorite; also 2nd in the Aral-Pokal (G1). He retired after the Derby with 3 wins from 9. A great sire, with 3-time West German Horse of the Year Acatenango, 2-time Horse of the Year Mondrian, and Platini, 4th to Legacy World in the 13th Japan Cup; 6 times German champion sire. Acatenango, siring Lando, Borgia and more, was champion sire 5 times - a heir every bit his equal.
3286: A filly who won the 1979 Arc. Her International Classification rating of 137 remains the highest ever for a filly even under today's World Thoroughbred Rankings (revised to 132 in 2013). Winning her only start at 2, at 3 she won the Prix Vanteaux, Poule d'Essai des Pouliches and Prix Saint-Alary; a close 2nd in the Prix de Diane, she won the Prix Vermeille, then the Arc, beating hot favorite Troy - rated 137 to his 136. At 4 she won the Prix d'Harcourt, was 2nd in the Prix du Prince d'Orange and 4th in the Arc, then 8th in America's Turf Classic S. She retired to breed in the US; of 7 foals, her 4th, the colt Oregon, went to stud.
3287: Winner of the 1979 Derby and Irish Derby. He also won the King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S., but in the Arc was 3rd, unable to catch filly crop-mate Three Troikas. Debuting in England, he won 2 of 4 at 2. At 3 he won the Classic Trial S. and Predominate S., then as 2nd choice won the Derby by 7 lengths with a surge in the straight, the Irish Derby by 4, and the King George as hot favorite - straight to the top. In autumn he won the Benson & Hedges Gold C.; 3rd to Three Troikas in the Arc, he was British Horse of the Year and retired. Dying at just 7, he left only 4 crops, incl. Irish Oaks winner Helen Street and Prix Vermeille winner Walensee. As broodmare sire of Pilsudski, Fine Motion and Street Cry, his blood lives on widely.
3288: A star British miler of 1979-1980, winner of the Sussex S., with a remarkable 14 wins and 2 seconds from 16. Unbeaten in 4 at 2, he won the Greenham S. at 3 for 5 straight and was 2000 Guineas favorite, but 2nd to outsider Tap On Wood. 3 straight wins incl. the Sussex S. made him Britain's top miler; 3 more in autumn - 7 of 8, International Classification 131. At 4 he won his first 3 for 9 straight, then lost a fierce duel with that year's 2000 Guineas winner Known Fact by a neck in the QEII S., far clear of the rest, and retired. His first crop included Fillies' Triple Crown winner Oh So Sharp, his 2nd Irish 2000 Guineas winner Flash of Steel; champion sire in Britain and Ireland within 2 years. His male line didn't last, but he is in dam lines, e.g. broodmare sire of Neo Universe's dam.
3289: An Irish horse who won the 1980 Eclipse S. and King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S., the best foal left in Ireland by Pitcairn, later a sire in Japan. At 2 and 3 he battled Troy, losing in the Derby and King George - 1 win and 3 losses against him. At 4 in 1980 he won 3 straight to the Eclipse, then the King George - champion older horse. In the Arc he was 3rd, half a length behind 3yo filly Detroit, and retired. At stud he sired St Leger winner Snurge, Grand Prix de Paris winner Sumayr and more. Hoped, like Troy, to carry the then-dominant Fairway line, he had no lasting heirs, and his male line has faded.
3290: A German-bred 1979 German Derby winner, and 3 times German champion sire. Winning 1 of 2 at 2, he won 3 straight to the German 2000 Guineas at 3, lost the Union-Rennen by a short head to rival Nebos, then beat Nebos narrowly in the German Derby. He also won the Aral-Pokal (G1) against older horses and the German St Leger - German Horse of the Year. At 4 he won the Grosser Preis der Stadt Gelsenkirchen, then 4th, 2nd, 5th; Horse of the Year went to Nebos. Racing at 5, he won 3 incl. the Grosser Preis des Jockey Club and retired. Besides 3 sire titles, his best son Monsun spread his blood worldwide as a sire.
3291: A mare who raced in Canada, then the US, winning the Eclipse as champion older mare, and was a hugely successful broodmare, dam of Singspiel and Rahy. At 2 and 3 in Canada she won 4 stakes incl. the Bell Mahone S. and Maple Leaf S. Moving to the US at 4, she won the La Canada S. (G1) in her 3rd start, then the Santa Margarita Invitational H. and Top Flight H. - 3 straight G1s - and against males was a superb 2nd to great Spectacular Bid in the Amory L. Haskell H. Eclipse champion older mare, and in Canada Sovereign Horse of the Year and champion older mare. At 5 she won 3 (Santa Maria H., Dominion Day H., Spinster S.), becoming the first Canadian-bred to earn $1 million, champion older mare again, and retired. As a broodmare she produced world-class sires Singspiel and Rahy, and Grand Opera, sire of Meisei Opera.
3292: A sire son of Damascus keeping the Teddy line alive, sire of BC Distaff winner Personal Ensign, Private Terms, East of the Moon and more. Debuting in the US in May at 3, he won 3 straight; at 4 he won 2 G1s, the Widener H. and Gulfstream Park H. At stud his 2nd crop included 3 G1 winners such as Personal Flag, and his 3rd brought great mare Personal Ensign, unbeaten in 13 incl. the BC Distaff. Then came Inside Information, BC Distaff winner by 13 1/2 lengths, and East of the Moon, out of Miesque, winner of the French fillies' double. With mostly filly stars his male line thinned, but his blood lives on through dams.
3293: In 1979 she became the 5th winner of the New York Filly Triple Crown (Triple Tiara), winning the Mother Goose S. by 10 lengths and the CCA Oaks by 8. Unbeaten in 2 from autumn at 2, at 3 she lost her first 2, then won 3 straight to the Fantasy S., the Kentucky Oaks and Black-Eyed Susan S., then the Acorn S., Mother Goose S. and CCA Oaks, all easily. 3 losses followed, but she was Eclipse champion 3yo filly. Resting early at 4, she returned in July, won the Ballerina S., and retired after a 4th in the Maskette S. Of 12 foals, none stood out.
3294: A sire son of Mr. Prospector from his early, unknown days, who succeeded racing and at stud, raising his sire's name. Debuting in summer at 2, he won 5 straight to May at 3, mostly allowances. Winning the Discovery H. (G3) in autumn at 3, he won the Metropolitan H. at 4, his first G1, and retired that autumn. His first crop included BC Juvenile winner Tasso; his 2nd, G1 winners Cryptoclearance and Tappiano; then Aptostar and Quiet American, and in his 5th crop his biggest star, Unbridled. Many became sires, building a great dynasty from Fappiano.
3295: A filly who ruled European sprinting in 1981, sweeping the top sprint G1s of the day: King's Stand S., July C. and Prix de l'Abbaye de Longchamp. She won a stakes on debut, then 5 straight unbeaten to the Cheveley Park S. (G1) at 2. At 3, 4th in the 1000 Guineas, perhaps too far, she turned to sprints: after the Gus Demmy Memorial S. she won the King's Stand S. and July C. Twice 2nd in G2s, in the Abbaye she beat Sharpo, a year older, by a neck in a thriller, and retired. A fine broodmare: G1 winners Caerwent (Irish National S.) and Marling (Irish 1000 Guineas).
3296: A successful sire son of Northern Dancer; his son Storm Cat spread the line widely, founding the powerful Storm Bird line. Debuting in Ireland in July at 2, he won by 6 lengths as hot favorite, then the Anglesey S., Irish National S. (now Vincent O'Brien S.), Larkspur S. and England's Dewhurst S. (G1) - 5 straight; champion 2yo in Britain and Ireland. At 3 came misfortune: his mane and tail were hacked off in his stable, plus leg trouble and fever. Back in autumn for one race, 5th, he retired. Besides Storm Cat, he sired G1 winners Indian Skimmer, Summer Squall, Balanchine and more; in Japan his son Ski Captain won the Kisaragi Sho. Well served by sire sons, his line is now a main branch.
3297: A filly who made her name in Europe from 1982 to 1984, winning 4 G1s incl. the Oaks, Champion S. and King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S. Winning her 2nd start, she won 2 of 5 at 2. At 3 she won the Masaka S. easily, 2nd in the 1000 Guineas, then the Oaks; in autumn the Sun Chariot S. and the Champion S. by 7 lengths - British champion 3yo filly. At 4 she won the King George over Diamond Shoal and others, then the Prix Foy, but was 4th to All Along, a Japan Cup runner the year before, in the Arc. British champion older mare, she showed, with French and Eclipse Horse of the Year All Along, the best of the fillies. At 5 she won the Coronation C.; without wins in the King George and Arc, she was champion older mare again and retired. Of 10 foals, Zinaad won an English G2 and went to stud.
3298: The core of the Vice Regent branch of Northern Dancer's line, siring Awesome Again, Dehere, Deputy Commander and more. Brilliant on the track, he won 8 of 9 at 2 incl. 2 G1s, the Laurel Futurity and Young America S. - Canada's Sovereign Horse of the Year and champion 2yo, and Eclipse champion 2yo. Hampered by injury from 3, he won just 2 G2s, but shone at stud: early G1 winners included New York Filly Triple Crown winner Open Mind and Eclipse champion 2yo filly Go for Wand, then Dehere, Touch Gold and Awesome Again; North American champion sire in 1997 and 1998. French Deputy, sire of Kurofune in Japan, and foreign-bred Tokyo Daishoten winner Toyo Seattle are also his. Well served by sire sons, his line thrives today.
3299: Raced in Australia until 4, then in France and America. His wins include the Grosser Preis von Baden and Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud, and Japanese fans know him for a 7th to Katsuragi Ace in the 4th Japan Cup. Emerging at 3 in Australia, he won G1s incl. the Rosehill Guineas and AJC Derby - Australian Horse of the Year. At 4 he won Australia's top race, the Cox Plate, and with 13 wins from 26 moved to France. He soon won Germany's Grosser Preis von Baden (G1), then raced the world: 3rd Washington DC International, 4th BC Turf, 7th Japan Cup. He won the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud for a 2nd G1, then moved to the US in 1986, late at 6, winning only a G2 but racing hard until 7. At stud he sired BC Turf winner Fraise.
3300: The 1984 Arc winner. Dying young, he left just 3 crops, but they included BC Classic winner Arcangues and Saganeca, dam of Arc winner Sagamix. Debuting in France in spring at 3, he won his 3rd start and the Prix Niel, then was 11th in the Arc. After that he only twice finished 2nd and won all the rest. At 4 he won the Prix Foy, then the Arc by 2 lengths. At 5 he won the Prix Ganay, Prix d'Ispahan and Prix Foy, then crossed the line first in a 3rd Arc but was demoted to 2nd for interference, and retired. Arcangues and Sagamix did little at stud, so his male line is fading.
3301: Unbeaten in 10, she won the 1983 Kentucky Oaks, then the inaugural BC Distaff the next year easily - a great mare of 1980s US racing. She won her debut in May at 2, then by 18 lengths in her 3rd start and 12 in her 4th, and the Frizette S. (G1) by 8 - unbeatable in the East. 5 more wins by spring at 3 incl. the Kentucky Oaks. 2nd to Ski Goggle in the Acorn S., then a fracture meant a long rest. After a spell of losses she revived in summer at 4 with the Vanity Invitational H. (G1), then the Chula Vista H., an allowance and Spinster S. (G1), and won the first BC Distaff by 7 lengths, her last race. Bred to Danzig in her first year, she raised high hopes but produced no notable foals.
3302: A durable US star from 1983 at 2 to 1988, winning 6 G1s; at 4 he won the BC Sprint, Eclipse champion sprinter. 3 wins from 5 at 2, no stakes. At 3 his first G1, the Swaps S., 5 wins from 12. At 4 he won the San Fernando S. and Charles H. Strub S. (G1s), then the BC Sprint - champion sprinter. At 5 he won the Californian S. and Woodward S. for a 6th G1, 4 wins from 9, no title. Retired to stud, he proved infertile, sired no foals, and after a year off returned to racing at 7, winning 3 incl. the Cabrillo H. (G3), then retired for good. With fertility problems he left just 4 foals in 3 years, but daughter Preciseness produced graded winner Draw Again.
3303: Winner of the 1985 Kentucky Derby in a stunning wire-to-wire display, who stirred controversy by skipping the other classics for the richer Jersey Derby. At 2 he won 5 of 8 incl. the Arlington-Washington Futurity (G1). At 3 he won the Cherry Hill Mile H. and Garden State S., then led throughout at a hot pace to win the Kentucky Derby by 5 1/4 lengths. Hopes of a Triple Crown rose, but his camp went for the Jersey Derby and won $2.6 million. A sound Derby winner skipping the classics was unheard of; reportedly it led to a $5 million Triple Crown bonus. He won the Monmouth H. (G1), then was injured in training and retired. 5 wins from 7 with 2 G1s - few wins, but his brilliance made him Eclipse Horse of the Year. At stud he sired about 30 stakes winners incl. Santa Anita Oaks winner Antespend, many in Brazil.
3304: In 1985 she became the 6th New York Filly Triple Crown winner, ridden by Abigail Fuller, daughter of her breeder-owner - the first female jockey to win a fillies' Triple Crown race. Often slow away at 2, she still won the Selima S. (G1), 4 of 7. At 3 she won her opener by 19 lengths, then the Cherry Blossom H. and Comely S., and the Triple Crown: Acorn S. by 3, Mother Goose S. by 5.5 and CCA Oaks by 2.5 - flawless. 2nd in the Test S., she won the Alabama S. easily for a 5th G1, then was injured in training and retired. Eclipse champion 3yo filly. Of 15 foals, no stars, but colt Jonesboro won 4 graded races.
3305: The 1986 French Derby winner, who as a sire produced Pennekamp and American Post, continuing grandsire Sea-Bird's male line. Debuting in autumn at 2, he won his 2nd start, then the Prix Noailles and Prix Hocquart at 3, and the French Derby as favorite in record time. Back in autumn, he won the Prix Niel easily, then in the Arc swept past from the back into the lead, only to be overtaken by Dancing Brave's devastating run, 2nd, and retired. At stud in the US he sired 2000 Guineas winner Pennekamp and French 1000 Guineas winner Matiara; back in France from 1992 he sired Poulains winner American Post. Also broodmare sire of Harbinger.
3306: A rare carrier of a minor Blenheim branch, and a top racehorse who won the King George VI & Queen Elizabeth Diamond S. and Eclipse S. Debuting in summer at 2, he won only a maiden from 7 by the end of 3. At 4 he blossomed, winning the Brigadier Gerard S., Prince of Wales's S. and Eclipse S. - his first G1. At 5 he won the Prince of Wales's S. and Eclipse S. again, then the King George with an eye-opening run from last. After a break he won the Select S. and ran in the Arc; closing from behind as usual, he was boxed in at the key moment and lost by a neck to Tony Bin. He retired after it. His best son was Derby winner Shaamit, who failed at stud, so the male line is fading.
3307: A US turf star of 1986-1987, winner of the BC Turf, Arlington Million and Turf Classic S. Starting on dirt, he needed 4 tries to win. Switching to turf in his 2nd start at 3, he won an allowance by 7 1/4 lengths, the Cinema H. and Lexington S., then the United Nations H. in record time for his first G1. After a G3 he won the Turf Classic S., then the BC Turf, beating Europe's jewel Dancing Brave and Theatrical - America's top turf horse. 9 straight through the next year's United Nations H.; 2nd in the Bernard Baruch H., he then won the Arlington Million for a 5th G1. A fracture ended his career. His first crop included 4-time G1 winner Bien Bien, raising hopes, but few followed; Bien Bien sired a G1 winner, just keeping the line alive.
3308: A 1986 European sprint star who won the July C., and a hugely successful Danzig sire son. Debuting in England in May at 2, he won 2 sprint stakes from 5. At 3 the 2000 Guineas (English and Irish) and St. James's Palace S. were too far, so he focused on sprints and won the July C. (G1), then the Sprint C. In America he ran in the BC Sprint, last on his first dirt start, and retired. At stud he passed on his speed, siring BC Sprint winner Sheikh Albadou in his first crop, then G1 winners Owington, Cape Cross, Desert Prince and Japan's Takamatsunomiya Kinen winner Shinko Forest. Blessed with sire sons, he is a pillar of the Danzig line.
3309: A sire son of Mr. Prospector who produced Hansel, Hector Protector, Timber Country and many more. Modest on the track, he debuted in Ireland and won 3 straight incl. 2 G3s, then was 5th in the Dewhurst S. (G1) and retired after a 3rd in the Mill Reef S. early at 3. Little was expected at stud, but his first crop produced G1 winners Hansel and Hector Protector, and his stock soared. Timber Country, Bosra Sham, Hawk Wing and Japan's Sprinters S. winner Hishi Akebono followed - over 100 stakes winners. Few of them succeeded at stud, so his sire line has not grown.
3310: A sire son of Mr. Prospector whose own sire sons - Zafonic, Elusive Quality, Grand Slam and more - built a powerful family. Debuting in the US in September at 2, he won only a maiden from 4. At 3 he won 2 G2s; 6th in his target, the Belmont, he won the Dwyer S. by 12.5 lengths for a G1. Winless after, he retired at the end of 3. His 2nd crop included 2000 Guineas winner Zafonic, sending him soaring, followed by G1 winners Da Hoss, Grand Slam, Speightstown and Johar - about 100 stakes winners in all. With Elusive Quality and others succeeding at stud, his line is thriving.
3311: She beat the colts in the 1988 Kentucky Derby, only the 3rd filly to win it after Regret (1915) and Genuine Risk (1980). Unbeaten in 3, 2nd in her first G1, the Las Virgenes S., she won the Santa Anita Oaks by 8 lengths and the Santa Anita Derby against colts by 7.5, and her camp went for the Kentucky Derby, where she beat Forty Niner and the rest. 3rd in the Preakness and 6th in the Belmont, she was 2nd by a nose to Personal Ensign in the BC Distaff - Eclipse champion 3yo filly. At 4, troubled by injury and a breathing problem, she won 2 of 7 without a stakes win and retired. No stars as a broodmare; her best was Golden Colors, a foreign-bred runner-up in Japan's Daily Hai Queen C.
3312: Winner of the 1988 Oaks, Irish Oaks and Yorkshire Oaks - top of Europe's 3yo fillies. Debuting in England in June at 2, she won 4 straight incl. a G3 and G2. At 3, 2nd in the Nell Gwyn S. (G3) and 3rd in the 1000 Guineas, she won the Musidora S. (G3) easily, then the Oaks by 4 lengths, dead-heated with Melodist in the Irish Oaks after a fierce duel, and won the Yorkshire Oaks by 5. 2nd to Minster Son against colts in the St Leger, she ran in the Arc 2 weeks later, 10th to Tony Bin, and retired. Of 9 foals, 3 won; her best was Calando, winner of England's May Hill S. (G3).
3313: An Australian star of 1989-1991, familiar in Japan as winner of the 10th Japan Cup - still the only Australian winner. To the 1988/89 season at 3 he was a mere handicapper. In 1989/90 at 4 he blossomed, winning 5 of 9 incl. 4 G1s. At 5, after 4 straight wins, he won the Japan Cup over Belmez, Kakoi Seeds, Oguri Cap and others. Back home he added another G1 and was Australian Horse of the Year. Injury kept him out long; back late at 6 he had lost his edge, winless until retiring at 7. A gelding, he left no foals, but entered the Australian Racing Hall of Fame in 2004 and is still loved.
3314: He ruled English mile racing in 1989. His career lasted just 6 months, from May to November at 3, but his stunning dominance made him British Horse of the Year. Winning his debut by 10 lengths, he won the Jersey S. (G3) and Criterion S. (G3) easily, the Sussex S. (G1) in record time, and the QEII S. (G1) - unbeatable. In the US, unsettled, he was 6th in the BC Mile and retired. He was Horse of the Year over 2000 Guineas and Derby winner Nashwan. With poor fertility he left under 400 foals, but they included milers like Sussex S. winner Among Men and French 1000 Guineas winner Always Loyal. As broodmare sire: Hong Kong mile champion Good Ba Ba.
3315: In 1989 she became the 7th New York Filly Triple Crown (Triple Tiara) winner. Later imported to Japan as a broodmare, she produced filly Easy Mind by Easy Goer. At 2 she won 2 G1s, the BC Juvenile Fillies and Demoiselle S. - Eclipse champion 2yo filly. At 3 she won 4 straight to the Kentucky Oaks, then the Acorn S. and Mother Goose S.; in the CCA Oaks outsider Nite of Fun crossed first but was disqualified for interference, giving her the win and the Triple Crown by a whisker. She won the Alabama S. for 10 straight, then lost 3 against older mares, but was Eclipse champion 3yo filly. Beaten twice at 4, she retired. Imported to Japan in foal to Easy Goer, she produced Easy Mind, who won the Wasurenagusa Sho (OP) and carried on the female line.
3316: Winner of the 1990 Kentucky Derby and BC Classic, and a sire of many G1 winners incl. Grindstone, Unbridled's Song and Empire Maker - a firm pillar of the Mr. Prospector line. At 3 he won the Florida Derby, his first G1, then the Kentucky Derby over fancied Mister Frisky and Summer Squall. 2nd in the Preakness, 4th in the Belmont, he won the BC Classic in autumn - Eclipse champion 3yo. At 4 he was 3rd to Black Tie Affair in the BC Classic and retired. His first crop included Kentucky Derby winner Grindstone and BC Juvenile winner Unbridled's Song; then Preakness winner Red Bullet and Belmont winner Empire Maker. He died at 14 but left many promising sons.
3317: A Hong Kong gelding of 1990-1994, the first and only Hong Kong Triple Crown winner and 3 times Horse of the Year. Debuting late at 3, he won 6 straight incl. the Hong Kong Derby and Champions & Chater C. - Horse of the Year in 1990/91. In 1991/92 he won the Hong Kong Invitation C., Gold C. and QEII C. - Horse of the Year again. Only 2 wins in 1992/93, 11th in America's Arlington Million. In 1993/94 he swept the Stewards' C., Gold C. and Champions & Chater C. - the Triple Crown - Horse of the Year once more. Winless after, he raced until the 1995/96 season and retired to Australia.
3318: The 1991 Arc winner. His rivalry with crop-mate Generous, winner of the Derby and Irish Derby, drew attention; beaten in the Irish Derby, he got revenge in the Arc. Little noticed at first, he won the Prix Greffulhe (G3) at 3, then the French Derby easily - suddenly a top horse. In the Irish Derby he was outgunned by Generous, 2nd. After a break he won the Irish Champion S., then thoroughly beat Generous in the Arc. He was the new Cartier Award's champion 3yo colt over Generous. At 4, 3rd in the Prix Ganay, then injury ended his career. Dying at 10, he left just 4 crops, incl. G1 winners Compton Admiral and Execute.
3319: A mare who won the Prix de l'Abbaye in 1993 and 1994, Cartier Horse of the Year as a sprinter. Debuting late in August at 3, temperamental, she plodded through handicaps until 4. Trying stakes at 5, she kept placing, then won the King George S. (G3) in summer, the Nunthorpe S. for her first G1, 3rd in the Sprint C., and the Abbaye by 6 lengths - a stunning margin in a sprint. Her brilliance made her Cartier Horse of the Year. At 6 she won 4 stakes but was 8th in the July C. and 10th in the Nunthorpe; then she won the Abbaye again by 5. 14th in the BC Sprint in America. Not Horse of the Year this time, she was Cartier champion sprinter 2 years running, and retired to breed; of 8 foals, none won a stakes.
3320: The first filly to win the Canadian Triple Crown and the first Canadian-bred to win the BC Distaff - a legend in Canada. At 2 she won 3 of 5 and was 3rd in the BC Juvenile Fillies, Sovereign champion 2yo filly. At 3 she swept the fillies' races - Star Shoot S., Selene S., Canadian Oaks - then took on the colts: the Queen's Plate by 8 lengths, the Prince of Wales S. by 2 and the Breeders' S. by 8 - the Triple Crown. She also won the BC Distaff in the US; unbeaten that year, she was Sovereign Horse of the Year and Eclipse champion 3yo filly. Injured at 4, 1 win from 4, she retired. A fine broodmare: Canadian G1 winners Scatter the Gold and Dancethruthedawn, and sire Dance Brightly.
3321: Known as the sire of Satono Crown, also of French Oaks winner Sil Sila and Prix Vermeille winner My Emma. His half-sister Salsabil won the Oaks and Irish Derby. 2nd to Generous in the Derby, he won the St. James's Palace S. for his first G1, then was unplaced in the Eclipse S. and Champion S. and retired. His first crop's Sil Sila and My Emma made him a hot sire; later came Hong Kong Vase winner Indigenous, Sussex S. winner Soviet Song and Irish 1000 Guineas winner Bethrah, and from his final crop (born 2012) Satono Crown, making him known in Japan. He died in 2016.
3322: A key sire carrying the Bold Ruler line in a North America dominated by the Mr. Prospector and Northern Dancer lines, building it steadily with his sire Seattle Slew. Brilliant on the track, he won the Hollywood Futurity (G1) at 2 and the Santa Anita Derby at 3. A minor injury kept him out of the Kentucky Derby and Preakness, but he won the Belmont, then the BC Classic by 2 lengths - Eclipse Horse of the Year - and retired. His first crop had G1 winners Royal Indy and Runup the Colors; he was North American champion sire in 2003 and 2006, siring nearly 150 stakes winners. As broodmare sire: Super Saver, Mystic Guide and more - a great modern sire.
3323: A great US miler who won the BC Mile in 1992 and 1993. Starting on dirt, he won the Gotham S. (G3) early at 3, then stalled. Switched to turf in autumn at 3, he won an allowance by 10 lengths, was 2nd in a G3, and won the BC Mile in record time. At 4 he won 6 of 8 with 2 seconds and won the BC Mile again. At 5 he won the Caesars International H. for a 3rd G1, but bidding for an unprecedented 3rd BC Mile he was unplaced for the first time since his dirt days, and retired without an Eclipse Award. With low fertility he left few foals, but France's Prix Morny winner Orpen succeeded at stud.
3324: Winner of the 1992 Oaks and Irish Oaks, and favorite in that year's 12th Japan Cup - well known to Japanese fans. Debuting late in April at 3, she won 3 straight to the Oaks, then the Irish Oaks and Yorkshire Oaks, and was St Leger favorite over the colts. Favorite in the Arc too, she was headed near the line by Subotica, 2nd. Favorite in the Japan Cup, 6th to Tokai Teio, she was still Cartier Horse of the Year. At 4 she won only the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud from 5, 22nd in the Arc. Moving to the US at 5, she won an allowance, then faded and retired. A poor broodmare, with just one G3-winning filly.
3325: A notable Gone West sire son, whose first crop included G1 winner Xaar; in Japan he sired graded winners Zacharia and Rusel. Debuting in France in 1992, he won 4 straight unbeaten incl. 3 G1s - Prix Morny, Prix de la Salamandre and Dewhurst S. - Cartier champion 2yo colt. At 3, a close 2nd in a listed race, he won the 2000 Guineas by a wide margin in record time. Expected to dominate the miles, he was injured and 7th in the Sussex S., and retired. He was rated 130 in the International Classification. Besides Xaar, he sired Prix de l'Opera winner Zee Zee Top and St. James's Palace S. winner Zafeen.
3326: In 1993 she became the 8th New York Filly Triple Crown (Triple Tiara) winner. Temperamental, she was below par on the road, but unbeatable at home in New York.
