Debuting in July at 2, she won 3 straight incl. a G2; first past the post in the Spinaway S. (G1), she was demoted to 3rd for interference, then won the Matron S. for her first G1. At 3, after a G2 2nd, she won the Acorn S., Mother Goose S. and CCA Oaks, then the Alabama S. and Rare Perfume S. - 5 straight - but was 5th away in the BC Distaff. 5 wins from 7 with 4 G1s, but no Eclipse. At 4 she won 5 straight with 4 G1s; 9th in the BC Distaff, but Eclipse champion older mare. At 5 she won a G3 and retired injured. Bred to Storm Cat, Deputy Minister and others, she produced only one G3 winner.
3327: A great German sire, 4 times champion sire in Germany, siring Shirocco, the first German-bred BC winner, and many more at home and abroad. On the track he battled crop-mate Lando, winner of the 15th Japan Cup; 2-3 head to head, but he was German Horse of the Year at 3 over Lando. Racing until summer at 5, he won 12 of 23 incl. 3 G1s. His first crop included German Derby winner Samum, and he was champion sire by his 4th year. BC Turf winner Shirocco, Manduro, Getaway and over 100 stakes winners followed - far ahead of rival Lando at stud.
3328: She won the 1995 BC Distaff by 13.5 lengths, Eclipse champion older mare that year. Winning her debut at 2, at 3 she won 5 straight incl. 2 G1s, the Ashland S. and Acorn S.; 3rd in the Mother Goose S., she began another winning run. At 4 she won 5 straight incl. the Shuvee H. (G1); after one 2nd, the Ruffian H. and Spinster S. (G1s). In the BC Distaff, billed against stablemate and 8-time G1 winner Heavenly Prize and younger 8-time G1 winner Serena's Song, she left them nowhere, winning by a record 13.5 lengths, and retired. Many of her foals died young, but her daughter Smuggler won the Mother Goose S. and CCA Oaks.
3329: A US filly who won 8 G1s from 1993 to 1995; her BC Distaff at 4 against great stablemate Inside Information was much talked about. Unbeaten from debut to the Frizette S. (G1) at 2, 3rd in the BC Juvenile Fillies. At 3 she won the Alabama S., Gazelle H. and Beldame S. - 3 straight G1s - then lost the BC Distaff by a neck, but was Eclipse champion 3yo filly. At 4 she won 4 straight G1s incl. the Apple Blossom H. and Hempstead H., then in the BC Distaff "clash of great mares" with stablemate Inside Information (5 G1s) and younger Serena's Song (8 G1s), she was 2nd as Inside Information romped. She ran once at 5 and retired. A fine broodmare too: 7 winners incl. Hollywood Derby (G1) winner Good Reward.
3330: A world traveller who won the Japan Cup, Dubai World Cup and Coronation C., and a top sire whose son Moon Ballad also won the Dubai World Cup. To the end of 1995 at 3 he had no stakes win, only G1 2nds in the Grand Prix de Paris and Eclipse S. At 4 he won the Gordon Richards S. (G3), then his first G1, the Canadian International S. in Canada. 2nd in the BC Turf, he came to Japan and won the Japan Cup over Helissio, Pentire, Bubble Gum Fellow and others - Eclipse champion turf male. At 5 he won the Dubai World Cup on his first dirt start, then 2 G1s in England, the Coronation C. and International S.; injured while preparing for the BC Turf, he retired. His first crop's Moon Ballad made it a father-son Dubai World Cup double; later came Papineau, Lahudood, Japan's Yasuda Kinen winner Asakusa Den'en and many more G1 winners.
3331: A US mare who won 11 G1s from 1994 to 1996. Debuting in May at 2 and winning her 3rd start, she won the Oak Leaf S. and Hollywood Starlet S. by year-end. At 3 she won the Las Virgenes S. and Santa Anita Oaks, then 16th against colts in the Kentucky Derby. She won the Black-Eyed Susan S., Mother Goose S., Haskell Invitational H. and Beldame S., and in the BC Distaff, a much-hyped big-three clash with older stars Inside Information and Heavenly Prize, was 5th - still 6 G1s, Eclipse champion 3yo filly. At 5 she won 3 more G1s, the Santa Monica H., Santa Maria H. and Hempstead H., with several G1 2nds, and retired. A great broodmare too: G1 winner Sophisticat and 3 other graded winners.
3332: Winner of 10 Australian G1s from 1995 to 1997 and sire of 11-time G1 winner Lonhro - a hero in Australia. At 2 in 1994/95 he won 3 of 5 with 2 seconds, Australian champion 2yo. At 3 in 1995/96 he beat older horses in the Cox Plate, then won 4 G1s in a single month late in the season - Australian Horse of the Year. At 4 in 1996/97 he ran unplaced more often, but improved to win 4 G1s and retired. His first crop produced Lonhro, who outdid him with 11 G1s; shuttled to France in 1998, he sired Laverock, winner of the Prix d'Ispahan and Gran Premio del Jockey Club.
3333: Sire of Curlin, English Channel and many more - Mr. Prospector's most celebrated sire son. North American champion sire in 2007 and 2008, he smashed the record for a year's progeny earnings. On the track he won 1 G1: debuting in April at 3, 2nd, then 3 straight wins; injured, he rested over a year, returned to win the Salvator Mile H. (G3) and Philip H. Iselin H. (G1), and retired after a 4th in the Woodward S. His first crop included Japan Cup Dirt winner Fleetstreet Dancer; in 2007 Curlin and English Channel won the BC Classic and BC Turf on the same day - his peak. Fabulous Strike, Furthest Land, Lookin at Lucky and many more G1 winners kept him a top sire.
3334: A great European miler who fought Spinning World in 1996, beating him all 4 times they met, and won 2 G1s. Debuting in October at 2, he won 2 straight incl. the Prix Thomas Bryon (G3). At 3 he won the Prix de Fontainebleau (G3), then the Poule d'Essai des Poulains, holding off Spinning World. 2nd by a head to Bijou d'Inde in the St. James's Palace S., he beat Spinning World decisively in the Prix du Moulin. 5th in the QEII S., he retired: 5 wins from 7, unbeaten in France, both losses in England. At stud in Ireland his best was US Citation H. (G1) winner Ashkal Way; little else of note.
3335: The 1996 Arc winner, familiar to Japanese fans as favorite in that year's Japan Cup. Debuting in March at 3, he won 3 straight to the Prix Lupin. 5th in the French Derby, he won the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud and Prix Niel, then led the Arc and drew away, winning by 5 lengths though Olivier Peslier stopped riding. Favorite in the Japan Cup, he was 3rd to Singspiel, but Cartier Horse of the Year. At 4 he won the Prix Ganay and Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud, then 3rd in the King George, 2nd in the Prix du Moulin, 6th defending the Arc, and retired. At stud in Japan he sired 2-time Meguro Kinen winner Pop Rock; shuttled to Australia, G1 winner Helenus. Below expectations, he was sold to Northern Ireland in 2005. As broodmare sire: mile G1 winners Sadamu Patek (Mile CS) and Jour Polaire (Victoria Mile).
3336: A great miler who won 5 mile G1s in 1996-1997, incl. the Prix Jacques le Marois, Prix du Moulin and BC Mile. A sire mostly in Australia, he is also broodmare sire of 2014 Oaks winner Nuovo Record. Unbeaten in 2 at 2 incl. a G3. At 3, 2nd to Ashkalani in the Poulains, he won the Irish 2000 Guineas, then the Prix Jacques le Marois, but was 2nd to Ashkalani again in the Moulin - beaten by him all 4 times they met. At 4 he won the Jacques le Marois and Moulin, then his farewell BC Mile. At stud in the US, he shuttled or was leased to Australia, New Zealand and Japan, later moving to Ireland. His stars include Australians Thorn Park and Special Harmony; in Japan, local runners like Haiseiko Kinen winner Silk Beat.
3337: Winner of the 1996 1000 Guineas and Champion S., Cartier champion 3yo filly. A full sister to Hector Protector, she was noticed before debut; from August at 2 she won 2 straight incl. the Fillies' Mile (G1). At 3 she won the Fred Darling S. (G3) and the 1000 Guineas - 4 straight. After 5 months off injured, she was 2nd in the QEII S., her first loss, then won the Champion S. easily on her first try at 10f - a 3rd G1. Cartier champion 3yo filly, rated 131, the top filly of the 1990s. At 4 she won 2 stakes, then 3rd in the Eclipse S. and 4th in the International S.; leg trouble ended her career. As a broodmare only Canadian G3 winner Rosberg stood out.
3338: From Unbridled's first crop, his leading sire son, siring many G1 winners such as Unbridled Elaine, Thorn Song and Forever Unbridled, extending grandsire Fappiano's line. Winning his debut easily in August at 2, he won the BC Juvenile, his sire's first G1 winner. At 3, twice 2nd in G2s, he won the Florida Derby and Wood Memorial, then was 5th, injured, in the Kentucky Derby. He won a listed race at 4 and retired. His first crop included BC Distaff winner Unbridled Elaine, making him a popular sire; over 100 stakes winners followed. As broodmare sire in Japan: Contrail, Suave Richard and more.
3339: A great Australian middle/long-distance horse of 1997-1998, who won both big races, the Melbourne Cup and Cox Plate, and was Horse of the Year twice. Winning his 3rd start in 1995/96 at 2, he won a G3 in the last race of 1996/97. Still inconsistent at 4 in 1997/98, he stepped up to 2400m and won the Caulfield Cup, his first G1, then the Melbourne Cup; later that season he won the Mercedes Classic, AJC Queen Elizabeth S. and Doomben C. - Australian Horse of the Year. At 5 in 1998/99, racing only in spring, he won 2 G1s, the Yalumba S. and Cox Plate - Horse of the Year again. Leg trouble kept him out nearly 2 years; back at 7 he ran twice below his best and retired. Australian Racing Hall of Fame, 2002.
3340: He won the 1998 BC Classic at 4, unbeaten in 6 that year, then sired 4 BC winners incl. Ghostzapper. Debuting late in May at 3, he won his 2nd start and 3 straight to the Jim Dandy S. (G2), but was well beaten in the Travers S. and Super Derby. Back in May at 4 after a rest, he was transformed: 3 straight incl. the Whitney H. (G1), 2 more stakes, then the BC Classic against what was called the greatest field ever - Skip Away, Silver Charm, Swain and more - pulling 3/4 length clear of a blanket finish. He retired after it. His first crop's Ghostzapper made it a father-son BC Classic double; Round Pond, Ginger Punch and Wilko also won BC races. He sired 15 G1 winners before being pensioned in 2019.
3341: A great European stayer of 1998-2000, full brother to Opera House. Debuting late in July at 3, he won a maiden in his 2nd start. At 4, 3rd in his first stakes, the Henry II S. (G3), he won the 20f Ascot Gold C. for a G1, plus the 14f Irish St Leger (G1) - Cartier champion stayer. At 5 he couldn't repeat in the Gold Cup, but won the Irish St Leger again and 3 G2s - champion stayer again. At 6 he won the Yorkshire C. (G2) and regained the Ascot Gold C. - just 2 runs, 2 wins, champion stayer for a 3rd year - and retired. Used mainly as a jumps sire, with no flat stars.
3342: A great sire of 3 Cartier Horses of the Year: Sea The Stars, Golden Horn and Ouija Board; Sea The Stars has greatly expanded his line. Not much noticed on the track, his main win was the Lockinge S. (G1) as an outsider. Winning his 2nd start at 2, he won just one allowance at 3. At 4, running as pacemaker for stablemate Kahal in the Lockinge, he led throughout and held on to win. Then the Jacques le Marois, QEII S. and BC Mile, all lost; at 5 he won 2 G2s and retired. At stud his first crop had Oaks and Irish Oaks winner Ouija Board, followed by Able One, Behkabad and Arc winners Sea The Stars and Golden Horn; champion sire in Britain and France in 2009 - far more acclaimed than as a racehorse.
3343: A great miler, Hong Kong Horse of the Year in 1999/2000 and 2000/01, and the first Hong Kong-trained winner of the Yasuda Kinen. He ran once at 2, winning on debut. At 3 in 1998/99 he won 4 of 8 incl. the Chairman's Prize (later Chairman's Sprint Prize), his first G1. At 4 in 1999/2000 he blossomed, winning the Hong Kong Sprint, then stunned the crowd winning the Yasuda Kinen in Japan as 10th choice. Just those 2 wins that season, but Horse of the Year. At 5, 2nd to 7-time Australian G1 winner Sunline in the Hong Kong Mile, he won 3 Hong Kong G1s - Stewards' C., Bauhinia Sprint T. and Chairman's Sprint Prize; 9th defending the Yasuda Kinen, he was Horse of the Year again. At 6 he won his opener, then was injured and retired. His name means "fairy" (lively) + "king prawn" (big shrimp), unrelated to Irish sire Fairy King.
3344: A globetrotter who won 6 G1s in England, Ireland, the US and Hong Kong, plus the Dubai Sheema Classic, and was 3rd in the Japan Cup. Unbeaten in 2 from August at 2, he won the Classic Trial S. (G3) at 3, but a heavy loss in the Derby Trial S. ended classic plans. 2 more wins encouraged his camp to try the Arc; 11th, far behind the Montjeu-El Condor Pasa duel. At 4 he blossomed: he won the Dubai Sheema Classic (G3), was 2nd in the Coronation C. and King George, won his first G1, the Man o' War S., in the US, 5th in the BC Turf, 3rd to T M Opera O in the Japan Cup, and won the Hong Kong Cup. At 5 he won the Tattersalls Gold C. and Prince of Wales's S.; 2nd to Galileo in the King George, he beat Galileo in the Irish Champion S., then won the BC Turf and retired. At stud in England, then Japan from his 5th season, he sired only 2 local G1 winners and was pensioned with little success.
3345: A US winner of 5 G1s incl. the 1999 Belmont S. As a sire he produced G1 winners Lemons Forever and Citronnade, and in Japan February S. winner Lemon Pop. Debuting in July at 2 and winning his 2nd start, he won the Futurity S. (G1); 5th in the BC Juvenile. At 3, 9th in the Kentucky Derby, he skipped the Preakness; after a G2 3rd he won the Belmont, beating hot favorite and dual classic winner Charismatic. He won the Travers S.; 6th in the BC Classic. At 4 he won the Brooklyn H. and Suburban H. (G2s), then the Whitney H. and Woodward S. (G1s) - 4 straight; 5th in the Jockey Club Gold C. and BC Classic, but Eclipse champion older male. Retired that year, his 2nd crop had Kentucky Oaks winner Lemons Forever and Gamely S. winner Citronnade; a steady sire, a pillar of the Mr. Prospector line.
3346: A US winner of 5 G1s incl. the 1999 Kentucky Oaks and Alabama S., one of Silver Deputy's best. Debuting in June at 2, she won 3 straight, a G2, then the BC Juvenile Fillies (G1) and a G3 - Eclipse champion 2yo filly. At 3 she kept winning: the Ashland S. (G1) easily, the Kentucky Oaks, and the Black-Eyed Susan S. (G2) for 8 straight. Against colts in the Belmont she was 7th, ending the run. She then won the Alabama S. and Gazelle H. for 5 G1s; 6th in the BC Distaff, but Eclipse champion 3yo filly. At 4 she won a listed race, then lost 4 and retired. No notable foals.
3347: A leading Danehill sire son, who spread the line with Arc winner Rail Link, King George winner Harbinger and many more. Not highly rated as a racehorse, he raced mainly at a mile and just missed at G1 level. Unbeaten in 2, 2nd in the Poulains, then 3rd in the Jacques le Marois and Moulin, 2nd in the Sussex S. and Prix de la Foret - G1 near-misses; he retired with a G2 and 2 G3s. At stud he was transformed: his 2nd crop had Arc winner Rail Link, then G1 winners Zambezi Sun, Harbinger and Dank. French champion sire in 2006, a key builder of the Danehill line with Danehill Dancer.
3348: Winner of the 2000 Derby, Irish Derby and Arc - the first to win both Derbys and the Arc. Debuting in September at 2, he won 2 straight incl. the National S. (G1). At 3, 2nd in a listed race - his only defeat - he won the Derby Trial S. (G3), then the Derby over later Arc winner Sakhee, and the Irish Derby by 9 lengths. After a rest he won the Prix Niel (G2) by 8, then the Arc, beating favored previous winner Montjeu and breaking the jinx that winners of both Derbys can't win the Arc. Cartier Horse of the Year went to crop-mate Giant's Causeway, but he beat him for champion 3yo colt, and retired. At stud he steadily sired stars like Irish Oaks winner Shawanda and Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud winner Youmzain, 3 times Arc runner-up. He died in France in 2018.
3349: In the 2001 US classics he was beaten in the Kentucky Derby, caught in a hot pace, but won the Preakness and Belmont. Debuting in August at 2 and winning his 2nd start, he won the Kentucky C. Juvenile S. (G3); in 3 straight G1s he was 2nd in the Champagne S. and BC Juvenile, then won the Hollywood Futurity. At 3 he won the San Felipe S. and Santa Anita Derby; in the Kentucky Derby he raced forward in a record-fast pace and faded to 5th. He bounced back in the Preakness, won the Belmont by 12 1/4 lengths, then the Haskell Invitational H. and Travers S. - 6 G1s. A BC Classic clash with Europe's best, Galileo, was hoped for, but tendon trouble ended his career. Eclipse Horse of the Year. At stud: Go Between, Coil and Canada's first filly Triple Crown winner Sealy Hill, but below expectations.
3350: A US sprinter who, despite long injury breaks, blossomed at 6 and won the 2004 BC Sprint. At stud he sired many G1 winners incl. Haynesfield, Tamarkuz and Japan's Mozu Superflare. Winning a maiden early at 3 in his 2nd start, he won 3 straight in spring, then a fracture kept him out nearly 2 years. Back in spring at 5, he won an allowance in 2 starts and rested again. At 6 he won a listed race and 3 straight G2s; 3rd in the Vosburgh S., he won the BC Sprint at last - Eclipse champion sprinter - and retired. Like him, his foals are mostly sprinters; in Japan Mozu Superflare and Rieno Tesoro made his name.
3351: Winner of the 2002 Dubai World Cup. 5 wins, 6 seconds and a third from 12 - remarkably consistent - and a great sire of Street Sense and Zenyatta. At 2 he won just a maiden from 5, 2nd in 2 G2s and 3rd in the BC Juvenile. Moving to Dubai at 3, he won the listed UAE 2000 Guineas. At 4 he hit his prime: the Maktoum Challenge R3 (G2), then the Dubai World Cup for his first G1, and the Stephen Foster H. 2nd in the Whitney H., he retired injured. His first crop had Kentucky Derby winner Street Sense and 13-time G1 winner Zenyatta - top first-season sire in North America. Shuttled to Australia, he sired Winx and many G1 winners - a world-class sire. He died at 16 at his peak, but Street Sense carries on his line.
3352: A US sprint filly of 2000-2003 with 26 wins from 35, Eclipse champion 3yo filly with just 1 G1. Debuting in June at 2, she won 6 straight incl. a stakes; 10th in the BC Juvenile Fillies, too far, she won 6 more into 3. In July at 3 she won the Prioress S., then G1; 2nd in the Test S. and BC Sprint - champion 3yo filly. At 4, no G1 but 7 wins incl. 5 stakes. At 5 she won another G2, then retired injured. 25 of her 26 wins were stakes - a North American record for a filly. As a broodmare, 2 graded-placed foals, nothing more.
3353: The 2003 Arc winner, 8 wins from 9, beaten only into 2nd in the Irish Derby - a precious carrier of the now-rare Mill Reef line. Winning his debut in August at 2, he won the Prix des Chenes and Criterium International (G1) - 3 straight. At 3 he won the Prix Greffulhe, Prix Lupin and French Derby unbeaten, then lost a duel with Alamshar in the Irish Derby, his only defeat. After a rest he won the Prix Niel, then the Arc, beating favorite High Chaparral, previous Derby and Irish Derby winner and BC Turf winner - Cartier Horse of the Year - and retired. His first crop had 4 G1 winners incl. 2-time BC Turf winner Conduit and Irish Oaks winner Moonstone; later French Derby winner Reliable Man and Grand Prix de Paris winner Shakeel. An undiagnosed illness stopped him covering in 2016, and he was pensioned.
3354: The 2004 Arc winner, known in Japan as the sire of Kikuka Sho winner Big Week and 3-time Grand Prix winner Chrono Genesis. Unbeaten in 4 at 2 incl. the Criterium International (G1), he won the Prix Jean Prat and Grand Prix de Paris at 3 - 6 straight. Stepping up in trip for the Arc, he was 3rd in the International S. and Prix Niel, then won the Arc as 5th choice - Cartier champion 3yo colt. At 4 he won only the Prix Ganay, but was 2nd in the Tattersalls Gold C. and 3rd in the King George and in the Arc again; 4th in the BC Turf and 8th in the Japan Cup, he retired to stud in Japan. His first crop had Kikuka Sho winner Big Week and Oka Sho runner-up Oken Sakura; later Chrono Genesis cemented his standing.
3355: A European sprint/mile filly of 2003-2005, the first to win both the English and Irish 1000 Guineas, unbeaten at the time. A brilliant front-runner, she won her first 5 at 2 incl. 2 stakes; injured after July, she still stunned enough to be Cartier champion 2yo filly without a G1. At 3 she returned in the 1000 Guineas, her first mile and first G1, and won, then the Irish 1000 Guineas and Coronation S. - 3 straight G1s. She lost 3 against older horses and colts, then won the Sun Chariot S. for a 4th G1. A stellar year, but crop-mate Ouija Board, winner of the Oaks, Irish Oaks and BC Filly & Mare Turf, took the headlines and the Cartier Award. At 4 she won the Matron S., a 5th G1, in 3 starts and retired. As a broodmare, one stakes-winning colt, nothing like her.
3356: A US winner of 7 G1s from 2005 to 2007 incl. 3 straight Hollywood Gold Cups. A cheap horse once sold in a claiming race, he earned a record $5.26 million for a claimer - a dream horse. At 2 he won a maiden in his 5th try. At 3, after 2 allowance wins, he was claimed by new owners. At 4 he blossomed, winning the Californian S., then the Hollywood Gold C. for his first G1. At 5 he won 4 G1s: Santa Anita H., Charles Whittingham Memorial H., Hollywood Gold C. and Pacific Classic S. At 6 he won the Santa Anita H. and Hollywood Gold C. - 7 G1s. He raced until July at 7 and retired injured; a comeback a year later ended in a heavy loss, and he retired for good. He became a lead pony and entered the US Hall of Fame in 2015.
3357: Raced in Germany until 3 in 2005, then in France from 4; in his prime at 5 he won 3 G1s: Prix d'Ispahan, Prince of Wales's S. and Prix Jacques le Marois. Unbeaten in 4 in Germany to autumn at 3, he was 4th in his first G1, Italy's Premio Roma. In France at 4 he won his opener, then kept placing to year-end. At 5 he blossomed: 2 straight wins to the Ispahan, his first G1, then the Prince of Wales's S., Jacques le Marois and Prix Foy - 5 straight. Having won at 2400m, he was aimed at the Arc, but a fracture ended his career. At stud he sired 5 G1 winners incl. Prix Royal-Oak winners Vazirabad and Ireseine and Criterium de Saint-Cloud winner Mandaean.
3358: The 2005 Derby winner, one of Montjeu's best, and sire of great mare Treve, 2-time Arc winner. Unbeaten in 2 at 2 incl. the Racing Post T. (G1). At 3 he won the Dante S., then the Derby by 5 lengths, unbeaten. Hot favorite in the Eclipse S., he was caught by Oratory, 2nd, and 2nd to him again in the Irish Champion S. In the Arc he was 5th to fellow Montjeu son Hurricane Run, and retired. Disappointing at stud at first, he shot to fame when Treve, from his 4th crop, won the French Oaks, Prix Vermeille, Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud and 2 Arcs. With few other stars, his standing is slipping.
3359: The only star and sire son of Dubai Millennium, who died after a single crop. His first crop produced 9 G1 winners incl. Monterosso and Prince Bishop - beyond all hopes. A top racehorse too, he won 3 straight from June at 2 incl. the National S. (G1). At 3, 5th in the 2000 Guineas, he won the Irish 2000 Guineas, was 3rd in the Derby, and won the Prix Jacques le Marois. 2nd in the QEII S., he retired as a precaution after injury. G1 winners came yearly: Tattersalls Gold C. winner Al Kazeem, Hong Kong Cup winner Akeed Mofeed, Australian Srikandi and more. Sire sons are emerging, like Makfi, imported to Japan, sire of All at Once, Sirius Colt and French 2000 Guineas winner Make Believe.
3360: The 2006 Arc winner, well known in Japan for beating Japan's great hope Deep Impact. Debuting late in April at 3, he unseated his rider; 2nd next time, he won his 3rd start, then the Prix du Lys (G3) and Grand Prix de Paris, his first G1. In autumn he won the Prix Niel by half a length, then the Arc, billed as a 3-way clash between favorite Deep Impact, bidding to be the first Japan-trained winner, previous winner Hurricane Run and BC Turf winner Shirocco. He passed Deep Impact, who had broken clear, and held off outsider Pride - 5 straight. 5 wins from 7; Cartier Horse of the Year went to Ouija Board, but he was French Horse of the Year. Injury kept him off the track at 4 and he retired. His best foals were Criterium de Saint-Cloud winner Epiculis and Australian G1 winner Spillway - below hopes. He died in 2022.
3361: Winner of 4 mile G1s in 2008 incl. the 2000 Guineas and Irish 2000 Guineas, in fierce rivalry with crop-mates New Approach (Derby) and Raven's Pass (BC Classic). Debuting in May at 2, he won 2 straight incl. a stakes, 2nd in the Phoenix S. (G1), and 3rd to New Approach in the Futurity S. (G2). At 3 he got revenge, beating New Approach by a nose in the 2000 Guineas and by 1 3/4 lengths in the Irish 2000 Guineas. At a mile he beat Raven's Pass in the St. James's Palace S. and Sussex S. - 4 straight G1s. 4th in France's Prix du Moulin, 2nd to Raven's Pass in the QEII S., and 2nd to him again in his farewell BC Classic, showing he could handle a new trip and surface (synthetic that year). His first crop had G1 winners George Vancouver and Pedro the Great, his next Sudirman - a fine start.
3362: Winner of 6 G1s from 2009 to 2013 incl. 3 straight Coronation Cups, the BC Turf and Dubai Sheema Classic. Unbeaten in 3 from August at 2 incl. the Racing Post T. (G1) - Cartier champion 2yo, a future star. At 3, 6th in the 2000 Guineas, his preparation faltered and he rested to year-end. At 4 he won the Ormonde S. (G3), then the Coronation C. and BC Turf. At 5 he won the Coronation C. again, 3rd in the King George and International S. At 6 he won the Dubai Sheema Classic and a 3rd Coronation C. - 6 G1s. Preparing for the King George he suffered a severe injury; he survived 3 operations, but colic left him beyond help and he was put down.
3363: A US winner of 6 G1s from 2011 to 2013 incl. 2 BC Ladies' Classics, Eclipse champion mare 3 years running. The biggest star left in the US by Empire Maker before his export to Japan; her success made the sale controversial. Winning her debut in October at 2, at 3 she won the Alabama S. and BC Ladies' Classic - Eclipse champion 3yo filly. At 4 she won the Beldame Invitational S. and a 2nd BC Ladies' Classic - champion older mare. At 5 she won the Delaware H. and Personal Ensign H.; bidding for a 3rd in the renamed BC Distaff, she was 4th to Beholder, but champion older mare again. She retired to breed but died at 9, leaving one foal by Galileo, Delta's Royalty, a broodmare since 2021 - will she carry on her dam's blood?
3364: A great Hong Kong sprinter who won 4 sprint G1s from 2014 to 2016, the first foreign-trained winner of the Takamatsunomiya Kinen. New Zealand-bred, he first raced there as Naisoso Warrior, winning 1 of 1, then moved to Hong Kong in the 2012/13 season, late at 4. At 5 he started winning handicaps; at 6 he won the Hong Kong Sprint, his first G1, then in Japan beat Straight Girl and Mikki Isle in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, and Singapore's KrisFlyer International Sprint - 3 G1s. Without a G1 at 7, he raced on at 8 and won the Hong Kong Sprint again. After an 8th in the Centenary Sprint C. (G2), he retired.
3365: A rare successful sire from the now-minor Grey Sovereign line, prized in America as an outcross to the dominant Mr. Prospector and Northern Dancer lines. Winning his debut in August at 2, he won the Champagne S. (G1) and BC Juvenile - near-unanimous Eclipse champion 2yo. At 3, after a 3rd in the Wood Memorial, a leg problem ended classic plans; back, he won the Kelso H. (G2) and retired at 3. His first crop had Kentucky Derby winner Nyquist, making him North America's champion 2yo sire; then Hollywood Derby winners Mo Town and Mo Forza, BC Turf Sprint winner Golden Pal and Belmont winner Mo Donegal - on a roll.
3366: One of Dubawi's best, winner of 4 G1s in 2015-2016 incl. the King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S. and Dubai Sheema Classic. Debuting in July at 2, he won just a maiden from 3. Still missing at 3, he won the Great Voltigeur S. (G2) that summer. At 4 he won the King George, his first G1, then the Prix Foy and, at 5, the Dubai City of Gold, then the Dubai Sheema Classic, the Coronation C. and International S. - 6 straight. Favorite in the Arc, 5th to Found. At 6, 3rd defending the Sheema Classic, he retired. At stud in England from 2018, his foals disappointed and he was switched to jumps breeding.
3367: From Sea The Stars' first crop, one of his best; he won the German Derby by 11 lengths and sired a father-son German Derby winner, Fantastic Moon. Winning his debut by 4 lengths in September at 2, his only start that year, at 3 he won the Fruhjahrs-Preis (G3) and Union-Rennen (G2), then the German Derby as favorite, veering wide at the top of the straight yet still storming clear. Aimed at the Arc, 2nd in the Grosser Preis von Baden, he was found injured and retired. At stud from 2015, his 2nd crop had Coronation S. winner Alpine Star, followed by German Derby winner Fantastic Moon and German Oaks winner Muskoka - a steady sire.
3368: A US winner of 6 G1s incl. the 2015 BC Mile. Debuting in September at 2, she won her 2nd start and a stakes in her 4th - talented early. Beaten at 3, her best a 2nd in the San Clemente H. (G2), winless in 4. At 4 she soared: 3 straight incl. the Just a Game S. (G1), then the First Lady S. and BC Mile against the colts - Eclipse champion turf female. At 5 she won 3 straight incl. the Jenny Wiley S., the Distaff Turf Mile S. (G2), then the Queen Anne S. and Woodbine Mile S. - 8 straight, 6 G1s. 2nd in the First Lady S. and in the BC Mile, she retired, and has bred in Ireland since 2017.
3369: The 2015 Derby and Arc winner, denying great mare Treve a 3rd Arc. Winning his only start at 2, at 3 he won a listed race and 3 straight to the Derby, flying from the back in the straight. Skipping the Irish Derby, he beat older horses in the Eclipse S., then lost the International S. by a neck to filly crop-mate Arabian Queen, his first defeat, but won the Irish Champion S. In the Arc, with favorite Treve bidding for a historic 3rd, he overpowered them all. In his farewell BC Turf he was half a length behind Found, whom he had beaten in the Irish Champion S. Cartier Horse of the Year, he retired to stud.
3370: An Australian sprint gelding with 2 G1s, whose A$16.44 million in earnings were then 2nd only to great mare Winx. At 2 in 2014/15 he won his debut from 2 starts; at 3 he won a listed race and a handicap late in the season. Blossoming at 4 in 2016/17, he won the Regimax S. (G3), was 2nd in The Galaxy (G1), and won the Doomben 10,000 - a G1. At 5 he won 6 straight incl. the new The Everest and the Darley Classic. 2nd in the Black Caviar Lightning and T J Smith S. (both G1). At 6 he won The Everest again but only a G3 besides; at 7, just a G3. 3rd in his farewell T J Smith S., he retired.
3371: Winner of 3 mile G1s in 2015: the 2000 Guineas, Irish 2000 Guineas and St. James's Palace S. Aidan O'Brien called him "the best miler I've had." Debuting in June at 2, he won his 2nd start and 4 straight to the National S. (G1); first past the post in the Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere, he was demoted to 3rd for interference, but with 4 wins from 6 was Cartier champion 2yo colt. At 3 he won the 2000 Guineas easily, the Irish 2000 Guineas in a duel with Endless Drama, and the St. James's Palace S. over Poulains winner Make Believe - top of Europe's 3yo milers. Kept out by ground conditions, he was 6th in the QEII S. in autumn, then last in the BC Classic on his first dirt start at a new trip, and retired. At stud from 2016 he has sired G1 winners Loving Dream and Highland Chief; in Japan, Shock Action won the Niigata 2yo S.
3372: Imported to Japan from the US, at stud from 2018. A son of Storm Bird-line Gio Ponti, he was prized in Japan as free of Sunday Silence blood. His first crop produced Sapporo 2yo S. and Satsuki Sho winner Geoglyph, making him top first-season sire - a sire to watch. He won 3 US sprint G1s in 2016-2017. Debuting in October at 2, he won a maiden in his 2nd start, then 3 straight at 3 incl. the King's Bishop S. (G1), and the BC Sprint - Eclipse champion sprinter. At 4 he unseated his rider in the Bing Crosby S., then won the Forego S. for a 3rd G1. Bidding to repeat in the BC Sprint, he found nothing in the straight, 6th, and retired to stud in Japan.
3373: An Australian sprint star who won 9 G1s incl. 3 straight T J Smith S. Debuting at 3 in 2017/18, he won 7 of 10, mostly handicaps and listed races. At 4 he won the Mitty's McEwen S. for his first stakes, then The Galaxy S. for his first G1. At 5 he won 3 G1s: A J Moir S., Sprint Classic and T J Smith S. At 6, the Black Caviar Lightning and T J Smith S.; at 7, the Sprint Classic, T J Smith S. and England's King's Stand S. - 9 G1s. 3 T J Smith S. in a row; in the Sprint Classic 2 wins and a 2nd in 3 years. At 8 he won only a G2, and retired after a 6th in a G3 at 9.
3374: A British stayer at the top from 2017 to 2022, named after the famous string instruments made by the Stradivari father and sons in Italy. Winning a maiden from 3 at 2, he won the Goodwood C. in summer at 3 for his first G1. At 4 he won all 5 starts incl. the Ascot Gold C. and Goodwood C. At 5 he won 5 more, a 2nd Gold Cup and 3rd Goodwood C., before losing a G2 by a nose - 10 straight ended. At 6 he won a 3rd Gold Cup and 4th Goodwood C., 7th in the Arc - Cartier champion stayer 3 years running. At 7, 4th bidding for a 4th Gold Cup and 2nd in the Prix du Cadran - no G1. At 8, 3rd in the Gold Cup and 2nd in the Goodwood C., then he retired.
3375: A British horse who won G1s in 3 countries in 2018: the UAE, Germany and Australia. Debuting late in April at 3, he was 5th in the Derby and King George, and won the Hampton Court S. (G3). Based in Dubai early at 4, he won the Dubai Turf for his first G1, then Germany's Grosser Dallmayr-Preis, and in Australia the Ladbrokes S. - 3 G1s. In the Cox Plate, Australia's biggest race, he was 2nd to queen Winx. After that hard year he rested until autumn at 5, winning a G2 in 2 runs. At 6 he won 2 G2s in Dubai and was 3rd in Saudi Arabia's new Saudi Cup. In his final year, at 7, he won another G2 in England and retired. Imported to Japan, he has stood at stud since 2022.
3376: The 2020 French Derby winner, who ran in the world's richest race, the Saudi Cup, twice, winning it in 2021, the year before it became an international G1. Debuting in October at 2, he won a maiden in his 3rd start. At 3 he won the listed Newmarket S., then the French Derby, surging from a handy spot. At 4 he won the 2nd Saudi Cup and its huge purse, then the Dubai Sheema Classic; 2nd to Adayar in the King George, he won the International S. by 6 lengths - 3 G1s. At 5, last in the Saudi Cup, now an international G1; then 2nd Eclipse S., 3rd King George, 2nd International S., and after a 4th in the BC Turf he retired to stud in France.
3377: The 2021 Arc winner. As 13th choice of 14, he became only the 3rd German-trained winner. Debuting late in May at 3, he won his 2nd start and was 2nd in the German Derby in his 3rd. In autumn he won the Grosser Preis von Berlin, his first G1. At 4, 2nd defending the Berlin race, he won the Grosser Preis von Baden. The Arc field was stacked - Frankel's Hurricane Lane and Adayar, Shamardal's Tarnawa - and he was ignored, but he surged from midfield to beat all the fancies. At 5, no G1 win, but 2nd in the King George and Grosser Preis von Baden; in the Arc, from a wide draw in 18 of 20, he was 3rd, 3/4 length behind Alpinista. He retired to stud in Germany.
3378: A gelding who ruled Hong Kong racing in the 2020s, winning 4 straight Hong Kong Cups (G1) and 3 straight QEII Cups (G1). At the end of 2024 he passed Hong Kong's Golden Sixty as the world's top earner. Debuting in 2021/22, he won 2 legs of the local Triple Crown, the Classic Mile and Hong Kong Derby, then won the QEII Cup 3 seasons running and the Hong Kong Cup 3 straight from 2022/23. In 2023/24 he became the first Hong Kong-trained Cox Plate winner, then went to Japan for the Yasuda Kinen as favorite over top milers Soul Rush, Serifos and Namur, and won - the first foreign-trained winner in 18 years. He was Hong Kong Horse of the Year that season over 3-time champion Golden Sixty. In 2024/25 his 3rd straight Hong Kong Cup took his earnings to a world-record $22.8 million. 2nd in the Saudi Cup and Dubai Turf, he fractured and rested long, but returned in 2025/26 to win a 4th Hong Kong Cup - still the champion.
3379: Winner of the 2023 Derby and Irish Derby, an Irish-bred son of Deep Impact and the best of his final crop of just 12 worldwide. Debuting in June at 2 and winning his 2nd start, he won the Champions Juvenile S. (G2) and Vertem Futurity T. (G1). At 3, 12th in the 2000 Guineas, he won the Derby with a brilliant late run - a historic first for a son of a Japanese horse - then the Irish Derby as favorite. 10th in the King George, he won the Irish Champion S. for a 4th G1, then the BC Turf in America as favorite, beating Japan's Shahryar. At 4 he won the Prince of Wales's S., 2nd in the Tattersalls Gold C. and Irish Champion S. His last race was the Japan Cup, 8th, and he left the turf with a retirement ceremony in Japan, his sire's homeland.
3380: A Nagoya star who moved to the JRA at 5 (old age system) and won 3 graded races. At Nagoya he won the Shinshun Grand Prix and Tokai King Sho, with 14 wins, 2 seconds and a 3rd from 18. Adapting to turf, he won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai in autumn at 5, then the Hanshin Daishoten and Diamond S., and was 2nd to Tomei in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) at 6. Leg trouble kept him out about a year; 4th in an open race at 7, he rested again, and after a 4th trying jumps at 9 he retired.
3381: The 1975 Southern Kanto Triple Crown winner, only the 2nd after Hikaru Takai. Debuting in September at 3 (old age system), he won 2 straight. At 4, after near-misses, he won the Haneda Hai, then the Tokyo Derby, 3rd in the Tokyo Hai, and the Tokyo Okan Sho - the Triple Crown. Moving to the JRA at 5, he was winless but 2nd in the Tomoe Sho at 6.
3382: He won the 1976 Tokyo Daishoten easily in record time, a lasting memory for Southern Kanto fans. Debuting in November at 3 (old age system), at 4 he ran in the Southern Kanto Triple Crown: 4th Haneda Hai, 5th Tokyo Derby, 2nd Tokyo Okan Sho. He then beat JRA stars in the JRA Invitational and was fancied as a 4yo in the Tokyo Daishoten; leading all the way, he won in 3:08.6, smashing the record by 1.4 sec. He raced until 6. At stud he sired Urawa Oka Sho winner Grace Taizan and Niigata 3yo S. winner Meiner Mut.
3383: A durable Oi horse who raced until 7, winning the Tokyo Daishoten in 1979 at 7. Few wins but always racing: 2 from 9 at 3 (old age system), 3 from 14 at 4, 4 from 11 at 5, none from 6 at 6. At 7, 1 win from 9, then he won a tight finish in his final race, the Tokyo Daishoten - a big title at last. Moving to the JRA at 8, he was unplaced in the Nakayama Kinen and Nikkei Sho, ran once over jumps, and retired.
3384: Winner of the 1977 Tokyo Daishoten. Debuting in September at 3 (old age system), he won 5 straight to January at 4. In the Southern Kanto Triple Crown he was 2nd, 4th and 3rd. Favorite in the Tokyo Daishoten, he beat later winner Ebi Chikara. Older, he won only the Tokyo Hai; moving to the JRA at 6, he was winless and retired.
3385: Battling leg trouble, he raced in Southern Kanto, Nagoya and Hokkaido, and in Hokkaido was called the strongest ever. Debuting at Kawasaki in September at 3 (old age system), he was a Triple Crown hope at 4, but tendon trouble led to heavy losses in the Haneda Hai and Tokyo Derby. In Nagoya leg trouble limited him to 4 runs in 1.5 years. Moving to Hokkaido at 6, he won 9 straight to summer at 7, finally showing his class: 16 wins from 18 there to the end of 8, incl. a Japanese record for 1800m on dirt.
3386: A Tokai-region star with 20 wins from 23 between 1981 and 1983, winner of the Tokai Triple Crown. Winning from autumn at 3 (old age system), he won 10 straight through the Chunichi Sports Hai and Tokai Derby at 4. 2nd in the Gifu Okan Sho, he won the Gifu Kinsho that autumn for the Triple Crown, then 8 straight to spring at 5. At stud he sired JRA Tokai S. winner Gold Proof and Oi Kimpai winner Gold Safe.
3387: Unbeaten in 8 at Oi in 1981-1982, he moved to the JRA and was hailed as "the second Haiseiko." Winning easily from debut at 3 (old age system), he won 8 straight to the Haneda Hai. Injury kept him out of the Tokyo Derby; moving to the JRA in autumn, he crushed Satsuki Sho winner Azuma Hunter in the St. Lite Kinen. Aimed at the Japan Cup, he was plagued by injury, won 1 of 2 more and retired; his only loss was a 2nd to Frost King in an open race. At stud he sired Satsuki Sho winner Doctor Spurt and many local stars.
3388: One of Haiseiko's best, winner of the Haneda Hai and Tokyo Derby in the 1984 Southern Kanto Triple Crown. Winning 9 straight from debut at 3 (old age system), his first loss was a 3rd in the Kuroshio Hai. He beat that race's winner, State Jaguar, in the Haneda Hai and held off Rocky Tiger in the Tokyo Derby, but was 2nd to Rocky Tiger in the Tokyo Okan Sho. Moving to the JRA at 4, 13th in the Yasuda Kinen on his first turf start, he was 2nd in the Sapporo Kinen. At stud he sired Breeders' Gold C. winner Snow Endeavor.
3389: A Hokkaido horse who moved to Southern Kanto and won the Haneda Hai and Tokyo Derby of the 1990 Triple Crown, one of Haiseiko's best. 3rd in the Hokkaido 3yo Yushun (old age system), he moved to Urawa and won 7 of 8 with a 2nd, incl. both races. 4th in the Tokyo Okan Sho, perhaps too far. Back in Hokkaido midway through 5, he won 3 more by 7 and retired.
3390: A star of Utsunomiya, a track that closed in 2006, and winner of the Tochigi Triple Crown. He won 2 quickly at 3 (old age system), then kept missing until spring at 4, when he won the Shimotsuke Satsuki Sho, the Tochigi Derby easily, and the Shimotsuke Kikuka Sho for the Triple Crown. He hit his peak with 7 straight wins late at 6 into 7, but at 8 he was killed in a traffic accident on the way back from training.
3391: An Oi horse who won his first 11 races from 1992 to 1994. Debuting late in July at 4 (old age system), he won 4 of 4 that year and 4 of 4 at 5, then kept winning at 6, 11 straight incl. the Kimpai and After 5 Star Sho. In the Grand Champion 2000 he broke down and was put down.
3392: An Oi horse who won the Haneda Hai and Tokyo Okan Sho of the 1993 Southern Kanto Triple Crown. Debuting in September at 3 (old age system), he won 7 straight to the Haneda Hai. 5th in the Tokyo Derby, he won the Tokyo Okan Sho in autumn. After that he won only the Tokyo City Hai at 6; moving to Hokkaido in autumn at 7, he was winless in 4 and retired.
3393: An Oi horse, unbeaten in 5 to the 1997 Haneda Hai. Injury kept him out of the other legs, and he went on to a turbulent career, incl. a move to Hokkaido and a comeback at 12. After about 1.5 years off, he returned late at 4 (modern ages used, as the system changed during his career) in the Tokyo Daishoten, 10th, then won the Frontier Sprint Hai at 5. Another long break, then 1 run in Hokkaido late at 6, 3 at Oi from January at 7, over 2 years off, and back in Hokkaido from August at 9, winning 3. Retired at 11, he returned at 12, running 5th, 3rd, 3rd, 4th, and retired for good at the end of 13.
3394: A Sonoda horse who won the 2001 Hyogo Triple Crown - the only Thoroughbred to do so since the series was set up. Winning 4 straight late at 2 (modern ages) into 3, he won the Sonoda Derby, Hyogo Championship and Kikusui Sho - 7 straight. JRA horses have won the Hyogo Championship every year since; he is its only local winner. Racing until early at 9 with 12 stakes wins, he retired, but with fertility problems he aimed for a comeback in Hokkaido; scratched with a fever, he moved to Kasamatsu at 10, winning 2, then to Kochi at 11, winning 2 more, and retired.
3395: Southern Kanto dual classic winner of 2005. Debuting at Funabashi, he won 2 straight and was 2nd in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun. At 3 he won 2 more, the Haneda Hai, and the Tokyo Derby by 4 lengths. A Japan Dirt Derby clash with JRA star Kane Hekili was awaited, but injury ruled him out. Back in autumn, he was 8th in the Tokyo Daishoten; after another long rest, 9th in it late at 4. Winless after, he retired after an 11th in the After 5 Star Sho in August at 7.
3396: A great sire who dominated Japanese racing in the 1950s-60s, known as the sire of Shinzan. His foals won 113 JRA graded races, the national record until Sunday Silence. An English horse, he won 2 of 8; unplaced in the 2000 Guineas and Derby, he won the Irish Derby and St. George S. and retired at 3. Unimpressive at stud in Ireland, he was bought in 1955 by Japan's Hidaka breeders' association. His first Japanese crop included Tenno Sho winner Yamanin Moa; the next, 3 classic winners - Shin Tsubame, Sugihime and Hakusho. In the 1960s came 5-crown winner Shinzan, Kikuka Sho winner Daikoter, Tenno Sho winner Yamato Kyodai and more; 7 times Japan's champion sire. In an era unkind to homebred sires, only Shinzan succeeded at stud, and that line ended with Mihoshinzan and Mai Shinzan. Many daughters bred on, so his blood lives on through dams.
3397: Winner of the Satsuki Sho and Kikuka Sho soon after the war, with 21 wins from 31 incl. 10 in record time. As a brother of St Lite he was valued at stud, and held his own in the import era with 10 straight years among the top-10 sires. Dominant to the Satsuki Sho, he was hot Derby favorite but ran off in front and collapsed to 7th - a huge upset. He then won 11 straight incl. the Kikuka Sho and St. Lite Kinen. Burdened by heavy weights, he won only the Sapporo Kinen and Tokyo Hai after, and retired. His first crop had Kikuka Sho winner Kitano O, followed by Derby winner Komatsu Hikari, Tenno Sho winner Tosa O and others - 7 Big Eight winners. Against imported Hindostan and Rising Flame he never topped the list, but was twice 2nd. His foals' 1,135 JRA wins were the homebred-sire record until Fuji Kiseki.
3398: An imported sire star of the 1960s, siring Derby winners Keystone and Teito O and many more; champion sire in 1966. An Irish horse, he won 6 of 9 incl. the Irish 2000 Guineas and Cork & Orrery S. At stud in Ireland for 9 years to 1958, he sired Irish 2000 Guineas winner Lucero and English dual classic filly Sweet Solera. Imported to Japan, he quickly sired graded winners like Solona Onward and Buru Takachiho; his 3rd crop had 3 Big Eight winners - Derby winner Keystone, Oaks winner Verona and Oka Sho winner Hatsuyuki - and the next, Derby winner Teito O. In 1966 he displaced dominant Hindostan as champion sire. In an era unkind to homebred sires, no heir emerged and his line ended.
3399: Winner of the 1950 Satsuki Sho and Derby. Bidding to be the 2nd Triple Crown winner after St Lite, he was 2nd in the Kikuka Sho. Debuting in November at 3 (old age system), he first won in his 8th start, in April at 4. 2 runs later, on his beloved bad ground, he won the Satsuki Sho by 4 lengths as 4th choice; Derby favorite, he broke clear from a handy spot to win. After 2 open wins in autumn, he looked the Kikuka Sho winner from a handy spot, but Satsuki Sho runner-up High Record swooped and beat him by a head. He won 3 of 10 more to autumn at 5 and retired. His best foal was spring Nakayama Daishogai winner Kuroshio.
3400: An imported sire dominant from the late 1950s to early 1960s, rival of Hindostan; together they ruled Japanese racing. An English horse, he won 7 of 25 without a stakes win, 5th in the 2000 Guineas and Derby. At stud in England, he was imported to Japan the year after imports were allowed again. His first crop had graded winners Seiyu and Rising Winner; the next, sire son Hishi Masaru (I). Stars kept coming, and he was champion sire 3 years running from 1958. His foals were mostly sprinters and milers, then thought inferior, so people joked "Hindostan for quality, Rising Flame for quantity." Still, his 1,379 career and 176 single-year JRA wins stood until Northern Taste and Sunday Silence. His line ran through Hishi Masaru to Hishi Masahide and Hishi Speed, then declined; today his name survives mainly in pedigrees like Nihon Pillow Winner's.
3401: Unbeaten, he won the 1951 Satsuki Sho and Derby and was famous even outside racing, but died of tetanus just after the Derby - "the Phantom Horse." Rated low early, he ran unnamed as "Perfect," his farm's name, but after an easy debut win was renamed Tokino Minoru. He won 5 straight to the Asahi Hai 3yo S. and 8 straight by spring at 4 (old age system). Hot Satsuki Sho favorite, he broke the record by over 6 seconds, then won the Derby in record time too - 10 of 10, 7 in record time. Falling ill right after the Derby, he died of tetanus 17 days later. The news spread nationwide, and novelist Nobuko Yoshiya's tribute calling him "the Phantom Horse" became his epithet. Today the 3yo Kyodo News Hai carries the subtitle "Tokino Minoru Kinen."
3402: Winner of the 1952 Oka Sho and Oaks, the first filly to win both. Her name was meant to read "Sweet Sue," but a clerical slip produced this spelling. Winning 4 of her first 5, she was 5th in the Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system). At 4 she won the Oka Sho in record time - a Big Eight title. 8th in the Derby, she won the Yasuda Sho (now Yasuda Kinen), then the Oaks, then held in autumn, as 2nd choice - the fillies' double. 2nd against colts in the Kikuka Sho, and as an older mare she won the Yasuda Sho again. From 6 she raced at Oi, winning at least 9 of 16 on record. As a broodmare, only Golden Beam (4 JRA wins) stood out; she is 4th dam of 1998 February S. winner Gourmet Frontier.
3403: Bought from Ireland by the Shadai group in 1961, he defined an era in Japan, siring Kikuka Sho winner Knit Eight, Oaks winners Shadai Turkin and Hiroyoshi and more - the foundation of Shadai. Racing in France, he won the Poule d'Essai des Poulains, Prix de la Foret and Prix Ganay, and in England as an older horse the Coronation S. and Hardwicke S. At stud in Ireland he sired Irish St Leger winner Barclay. Bought by Shadai at 12, he became a leading sire in Japan, champion sire in 1969 over long-dominant Hindostan. The pillar of a Shadai group with no other top sire, he contributed hugely to its growth. Knit Eight failed at stud and his stars were mostly fillies, so his male line died out.
3404: A leading sire of the 1960s-70s, known as the sire of Haiseiko and Takeshiba O. An English horse, he raced in England and France, winning 7 of 25 without distinction. At stud in England he was little valued and was exported to Japan after a year. His first crop produced graded winners in both JRA and local racing, making him popular at once. His 3rd crop had Yashima National, called the best ever in local racing, his 4th the JRA monster Takeshiba O, and his 9th his masterpiece, Haiseiko; in 1973, Haiseiko's peak, he was champion sire. Displaced by Tesco Boy, he kept siring graded winners and stayed near the top. As broodmare sire: Nihon Pillow Winner, Riesengross, Take no Velvet and more. Takeshiba O and Haiseiko had some success at stud, but the line went no further and has died out.
3405: A late-blooming mare who won the 1959 Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen at 5 (old age system); only she and Tomei have won both as fillies or mares. Slow to start, she won her 4th race, then was 6th in the Oka Sho and 5th in the Oaks at 4. She could win open races but only placed in graded races. Still without a title by summer at 5, she ran in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) as her farewell, broke clear from midfield and held off Otemon by a nose - a shock first graded win. Invited to the Arima Kinen, 9th choice of 12, she won by 4 lengths, and retired to breed. Her foals were steady winners, mostly fillies, and her female line spread widely, producing 2006 dual classic winner Meisho Samson among others.
3406: An imported sire star of the 1970s in Japan, siring Derby winner Cornell Lancer and Tenno Sho winners Aiful and Three Giants; 6th on the sire list in 1976. A top racehorse too: at 3 in Italy he won 4 big races - the Derby Italiano, Gran Premio di Milano, Gran Premio d'Italia and Premio Principe Amedeo; at 4 the Gran Premio del Jockey Club and Premio Presidente della Repubblica - Italy's best. At stud in Italy for about 5 years with few foals, he was exported to Japan in 1964; then the foals he left behind, like Over and Mogadiscio, made him Italy's champion sire. In Japan his first crop had graded winners like Hakuei Ho; his 6th, Cornell Lancer and Aiful; his 10th, Three Giants. He also sired Sakura Sedan, dam of Sakura Toko, Sakura Chiyono O and Sakura Hokuto O.
3407: The 1959 Arc winner, imported to Japan in 1971, who defined an era siring Tenno Sho winner Taite M, Erimo George and more. French-trained, he won his first 2, then 4th in the Derby; he won the Eclipse S. and the Arc from a field of 25, and retired that year to stud in Ireland. His 4th crop had Prix Vermeille winner Casaque Grise and Italian Oaks winner Dolina, his 8th Oaks and Irish Oaks winner Altesse Royale. In Japan, beyond in-utero import Taite M, he sired Tenno Sho winner Erimo George and reached 12th on the 1978 list. As broodmare sire of Magnitude and in Special Week's pedigree, his blood lives on.
3408: Winner of 4 straight Nakayama Daishogai in 1974-1975 (then run in spring and autumn) - the only jumper in the JRA Hall of Fame. Starting on the flat, winless in 6 at 3 (old age system), he won at 4 and the Manyo S. early at 5. His stable's rookie jockey specialized in jumps, and with a granddam who had starred over fences, he was switched to jumps. Climbing steadily at 5, he peaked at 6, winning the spring Nakayama Daishogai, autumn Kyoto Daishogai and autumn Nakayama Daishogai, and at 7 won both races spring and autumn - 11 wins from 12 from late 6 through 7. At 8, weighed down by heavy imposts and injured, he retired that spring. Over jumps: 19 wins from 39, never once falling. He later stood as a riding-horse stallion.
3409: Kochi's idol, famous nationwide for losing all 113 starts. Debuting in November at 2 (modern ages), winless in 3; then 0 from 20 at 3, 18 at 4, 19 at 5, 18 at 6 and 22 at 7. Always losing but never hurt, she ran about 20 times a year, steadily earning appearance money. Her losing streak hit 100 by the end of 7, and media coverage made her a national sensation. At 8, Yutaka Take rode her, and the track set records for attendance and betting. She lost again, but Take, who had said he couldn't understand why a weak horse drew fans, said afterward, "She's definitely a star. I'd ride her again." She retired at 113 straight losses and, never bred, lives at Martha Farm in Chiba.
3410: The undisputed jumps king from 2016 to 2022, winning 9 G1s incl. 5 straight Nakayama Grand Jumps, and champion jumper 5 times in 7 years. To 4 he was ordinary: from 13 starts, only a maiden and 3 open wins. From 5 in 2016 he blossomed, winning 4 of 5 incl. the Nakayama Grand Jump and Nakayama Daishogai. At 6, unbeaten in 4, he won both again, and flat fans began to know him. At 7, after a 3rd straight Grand Jump, he invaded the flat, winning allowances with ease, and ran in the Arima Kinen, 3rd in the fan vote, making a strong move at the top of the straight. At 8 and 9 he won the Grand Jump - 5 straight. 5th at 10, he won the Nakayama Daishogai, and at 11 won the Grand Jump again, retiring with 9 G1s.
3411: A Southern Kanto star who won the Haneda Hai and Tokyo Derby of the 1973 Triple Crown. At 3 (old age system) he won 5 of 8 with a 2nd and 2 thirds, incl. a 2nd in the Zen-Nihon 3yo Yushun. At 4, with Southern Kanto hero Haiseiko gone to the JRA, he filled the gap, winning both classics and great popularity. Preparing for the Tokyo Okan Sho, he broke down in the Sumidagawa Tokubetsu and was put down.
3412: A 1979 Southern Kanto dual classic winner. He won the Haneda Hai, then the Tokyo Derby from a handy spot. Hoped to follow Hatsushiba O as the 4th Triple Crown winner, he was Tokyo Okan Sho favorite but faded from the front, unplaced. He won 3 more at 4 (old age system), none at 5 or 6, and retired.
3413: A 1980 Southern Kanto dual classic winner, rated by many fans among the best ever in local racing. Not yet a graded force at 3 (old age system), he improved greatly at 4: 2 straight wins, 2nd to Tagawa Tetsu O in the Kuroshio Hai, then crushing wins in the Haneda Hai and Tokyo Derby - best of his crop. Leg trouble kept him out of the Tokyo Okan Sho. Back at 5 he lost twice; moving to the JRA at 7, he never won and quietly disappeared.
3414: Winning a maiden in her 3rd start, she won the 1-win class in her 7th, 2-win in her 9th and 3-win in her 11th, reaching open class in autumn at 4. In her first open race, the Turquoise S., she was 3rd with the fastest finish; 9th in the Epsom C. at 5, 4th in the Sekiya Kinen and Fuchu Himba S., then she won the Turquoise S. late at 5. Half-sister to 2012 Flora S. winner Midsummer Fair, full sister to 2020 Shuka Sho 3rd Soft Flute.
3415: Winning a maiden in February at 3, she struggled in the 1-win class (12th twice), passed it early at 4, then alternated wins and losses into open class in autumn at 4. In the Kanagawa Kinen, run for one year only, she raced forward to win - also jockey Hollie Doyle's first graded win in Japan. Her third dam is Rosa Nay, making her one of the famed "Rose family."
3416: A filly who won the Arima Kinen (G1) at 3 in 2024 - the first 3yo filly winner in 64 years, since Star Roch in 1960 - giving her sire Suave Richard a big title from his first crop. Winning her debut in July at 2, 3rd in the Ivy S. (L), she took on the colts in the Hopeful S. (G1), co-favorite with Shin Emperor, and caught him from the back - the first filly winner since it became a G1. At 3 she faced colts again: 6th as Satsuki Sho favorite, 5th as 2nd choice in the Derby. Back with fillies, 5th in the Rose S., then 5th as hot 1.9-1 QEII Cup favorite, unable to catch those who raced forward. Voted into the Arima Kinen, she raced a bit closer, broke clear and outfought Shahryar to win. After a fracture she returned at 4, 11th in the Takarazuka Kinen, then won the All Comers and the QEII Cup as favorite - a true Grand Prix winner. 4th defending the Arima Kinen after a rough trip, she was champion older mare.
3417: Debuting early, in June at 3 (old age system), he won a newcomer race and was 2nd in the Hakodate 3yo S. (now Hakodate 2yo S.). He won 5 of 9 that year incl. the Hokkaido 3yo S. (now Sapporo 2yo S.), unplaced only once. At 4, on the classic path, he was 10th in the Yayoi Sho, 12th in the Satsuki Sho and 25th in the Derby. After about 3 months off he won a Hakodate open race, the new local-racing invitational and the Lord Derby CT - 3 straight to end the year. He won the Tokyo Shimbun Hai at 5, raced until 6 and retired.
3418: A Northern Dancer sire son who didn't found his own line but sired G1 winners like Opening Verse and Palace Music, and Palace Music sired Cigar. His granddam Flaming Page was Nijinsky's dam, and his sire Northern Dancer too - a pedigree very close to Nijinsky's. Unbeaten in 3 from September at 2 incl. the Dewhurst S. (G1). At 3 he won the 2000 Guineas Trial S. (G3), then was 3rd and 2nd in the English and Irish 2000 Guineas, before a storming run: the Derby, then the Irish Derby easily - only the 5th to win both - and the King George VI & Queen Elizabeth Diamond S. as favorite over older horses. With a huge syndicate already formed, he retired as a precaution to stud in America.
3419: US turf champion of 1978 with 12 wins incl. 2 G1s, best son of Minnesota Mac, a rare Himyar-line sire. Debuting in October at 2, he lost both starts; 8th in his first race at 3, he then won 10 straight: a maiden easily, 4 allowances, the Long Branch S. (G3) and Leonard Richards S. (G3), then the Lexington H., Secretariat S. and Lawrence Realization S. (G2s). 3rd in his first G1, the Man o' War S., he won the Canadian International S. and Washington DC International - US turf champion. He retired to stud that year; no notable foals.
3420: A great European sprinter of 1980-1981. Debuting in England in August at 2, he won his 2nd start and 2 more. At 3 he was 2nd in the Poulains (G1), then won the July C. for his first G1, the Sprint C. (G2), the Prix de l'Abbaye, the Challenge S. (G3) and the Prix de la Foret - 4 straight, 3 G1s. At 4, 2nd defending the July C., he won the Prix Maurice de Gheest (G2) in record time, 2 G3s and the 1400m Prix de la Foret again for a 4th G1, and retired. At stud his 2nd-crop Lockton won the Irish National S. (G1), his only G1 winner, but he sired steady runners in Germany and England.
3421: An Irish mare who came to Japan for the 2nd and 3rd Japan Cups, winning the 3rd after a fierce duel with Kyoei Promise. Slow to develop, she won her debut in spring at 3, then not again until spring at 4. After more near-misses she was invited to the Japan Cup, 4th as foreign horses swept the top places. At 5 she blossomed, winning 3 straight middle-distance stakes; 4th in the Eclipse S. (G1), she won the Joe McGrath Memorial S. (now Irish Champion S.), her first G1. Invited again to the Japan Cup as 3rd choice among the favored foreigners, she outfought Kyoei Promise, bidding to be the first Japanese winner - a 2nd G1. At 6, 4th in a summer G2, she retired. As a broodmare, nothing notable; her daughter Sundrine was imported to Japan as a broodmare.
3422: The 1982 Derby winner. Unbeaten in a brief career of 4, he was called by jockey Pat Eddery "the best horse I've ridden." Winning his debut easily in September at 2, he rested; at 3 he won the Ballymoss S. (G2) and Nijinsky S. (G2), a classic fancy. In the Derby he raced at the back, swung wide in the straight and produced an eye-opening finish, breaking a record that had stood half a century. Training problems ended his career after the Derby; just 3 wins that year, yet rated Europe's best at 134. He died young after one crop, which included G1 winner Pixie Erin.
3423: A Mr. Prospector sire son who, despite high hopes, sired few G1 winners but a steady stream of stakes winners. His best was Hollywood Gold C. (G1) winner Marquetry, whose sons Squirtle Squirt and Artax carry on the line. A brilliant racehorse, he was 1982 Eclipse Horse of the Year at 3 for 2 crushing G1 wins. After losing his opener, he won 3 allowances easily, then the Metropolitan H. against older horses by 7 lengths in record time. 5 days later he won the Belmont S. by 14 lengths. He won 2 more stakes, then hurt a leg and was 3rd in the Travers S. (G1), and retired.
3424: A leading sire son of Grey Sovereign-line Caro, siring many G1 winners like Star of Cozzene and Alphabet Soup; North American champion sire in 1996. In Japan he is known through Yasuda Kinen winner Admire Cozzene and Oaks winner Robe Decollete. A top miler, he won the 1985 BC Mile (G1). Debuting in May at 3 on dirt and often just missing, he switched to turf in summer at 4: 2nd United Nations H., 3rd Man o' War S., 3rd BC Mile. At 5 he won the Oceanport H. (G3), then his 2nd BC Mile in record time - Eclipse champion turf male - and retired.
3425: A speedster with his sire Mr. Prospector's pace, winner of the first BC Sprint (G1) in 1984. Sprinting on dirt from his debut at 3, he won his first 4 brilliantly. After 3 losses, at 4 he won 4 straight by 3 lengths (in record time), 7, 3 and 6. Last on his first turf start, a mile, he returned to dirt sprints and won 3 more. Favorite in the inaugural BC Sprint, he led and held on by a nose - his first stakes win a G1. Sadly he then fell gravely ill and died, passing on none of his speed.
3426: The 1984 French Oaks winner, from Northern Dancer's famed crop with Sadler's Wells, El Gran Senor and Secreto. Debuting late in April at 3, she won easily, then was 2nd in the Prix Saint-Alary (G1). 2nd choice in the French Oaks, she beat Saint-Alary winner Grise Mine. Back in autumn, she won the Prix de la Nonette (G3) and Prix Vermeille (G1) over Oaks winner Circus Plume. In the Arc she was 2nd, 2 lengths behind Sagace, ahead of All Along and Sadler's Wells. She retired to breed; no stars of her own, but descendants Shiva and Main Sequence extended her female line.
3427: Winner of the 1985 Eclipse S., Champion S. and BC Turf - hailed as Britain's greatest ever filly for beating the colts. Debuting in England in May at 2, she won her 2nd start, 2 wins from 6. At 3 she won the Nell Gwyn S. (G3) and the 1000 Guineas by 3 lengths, then was 2nd in the Coronation S. (G2) and Champion S. (G1). At 4 she blossomed: in the Eclipse S., Britain's top middle-distance race, she beat Rainbow Quest and others, the first filly to win it; then the Champion S. easily over Derby winner Slip Anchor and previous winner Palace Music; then the BC Turf in America as favorite, on her first US start and first 12f race. British Horse of the Year and Eclipse champion turf female, rated 135 by Timeform, second only to Slip Anchor's 136. Retired to breed, she produced nothing notable; later imported to Japan, she had no success there either.
3428: Winner of the 1984 Kentucky Derby and Belmont S. Debuting in July at 2 and winning his 2nd start, he won the Saratoga Special S. (G2), then the Futurity S. and Young America S. (G1s), but crop-mate Devil's Bag, "the second Secretariat," kept him in 2nd place. At 3 he won the Hutcheson S. (G3) and Florida Derby (G1); with favorite Devil's Bag retired just before, the Kentucky Derby was wide open, and he won by 3 1/4 lengths. Flat in the Preakness, 7th, he won the Belmont by 4 lengths - top of his crop. Just 8 days later he died suddenly. He never went to stud, but was Eclipse champion 3yo and helped his sire Seattle Slew to the North American sire title.
3429: Invincible in (then West) Germany from 1985 to 1987, and 5 times German champion sire. Modest at 2, 1 win from 5, he awoke at 3, winning from the start of the year incl. the German Derby and Aral-Pokal - unbeaten in 6, German Horse of the Year. At 4 he won France's Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud and 3 German G1s - Grosser Preis von Berlin, Aral-Pokal, Grosser Preis von Baden - unbeatable. In an Arc of historic strength with Dancing Brave and Shahrastani, he was 7th, but Horse of the Year again. At 5 he was 3rd in England's Coronation C. and 6th in the King George; he won the Grosser Preis von Baden, Horse of the Year for a 3rd year, and retired. At stud he sired Japan Cup winner Lando, German Derby winner Borgia and many more - still one of Germany's great sires.
3430: An Irish horse who moved to the US at 4 and blossomed; in 1987 at 5 he won 6 G1s incl. the BC Turf - Eclipse champion turf male. Unbeaten in 3 from October at 2, he was 7th in the Derby and 2nd in the Irish Derby, then kept losing. Moved to the US in summer at 4, he was 2nd in the Oak Tree Invitational H. (G1) and BC Turf. At 5 he won the Hialeah Turf C., his first G1, then 4 straight G2s and G1s; 3rd in the Arlington Million, he won the Turf Classic S., Man o' War S. and BC Turf - America's turf champion - and retired. A great sire too, with Zagreb, Royal Anthem and many G1 winners; in Japan, sire of Hishi Amazon and Taiki Eldorado.
3431: A gelding who dominated Australia and New Zealand in 1986-1987, known in Japan from 2 Japan Cup trips. Modest at 2, he improved at 3, winning 7 straight incl. the New Zealand Derby. At 4 he won 3 straight Australian G1s to the Cox Plate; a Japan Cup fancy, an infection ruled him out. He won the Australian C. (G1) back home - Horse of the Year in both countries. Resting much of 5, he won only the Air New Zealand S. (G1). At 6, 3rd in the Cox Plate, he tried the Japan Cup again but, past his peak, was 8th behind the Pay the Butler-Tamamo Cross duel. Winless after, he retired at 7 and later entered New Zealand's racing Hall of Fame.
3432: Winner of the 1986 Derby and Irish Derby - in the Derby he beat Dancing Brave, the only horse to beat him in Europe. Unraced after a 2nd on his only start at 2, at 3 he won the Classic Trial S. (G3) and Dante S. (G2), becoming a Derby fancy. With Dancing Brave hot favorite, he broke clear early from up front and held off Dancing Brave's charge from last by half a length. He won the Irish Derby by 8 lengths as favorite, but was 4th to Dancing Brave in the King George and in the Arc, outclassed. He retired to stud in the US; poor as a sire, he moved to Ireland and Japan, siring only a few graded winners.
3433: A US star of 1986-1987, winner of 3 G1s - Kentucky Derby, Hollywood Gold C. and BC Classic - and Eclipse Horse of the Year, but a poor sire; reports that he was slaughtered in Japan caused outrage. Debuting in September at 2, he won his 4th start, overshadowed by rival Snow Chief. At 3 he struck back in the Kentucky Derby as 9th choice, with a powerful finish for his first G1. 2nd in the Preakness, 3rd in the Belmont; champion 3yo went to 3-time G1 winner Snow Chief. At 4, after near-misses, he won the Hollywood Gold C., then 4 straight incl. the BC Classic - Horse of the Year. Winless in 6 at 5, he retired. Siring few stakes winners, he was imported to Japan in 1994; still unsuccessful, he was disposed of (slaughtered) after his 2002 season, as later investigation revealed.
3434: She won the 1987 French Oaks (G1) easily, beating great filly Miesque, and won 5 G1s in all incl. the Phoenix Champion S. and Champion S. - one of the great mares of the 1980s. First winning in spring at 3, she won 4 straight to the Prix Saint-Alary (G1), then the French Oaks by 4 lengths from English and French 1000 Guineas winner Miesque. After about a year off, at 4 she won the Phoenix Champion S. (now Irish Champion S.) and the Champion S. - only the 2nd to win both. 3rd in the BC Turf in America. At 5 she won the Prix d'Ispahan for a 5th G1, and retired after a 3rd in the Eclipse S. Not a successful broodmare; her colt Manshood, unraced, went to stud on pedigree.
3435: A late bloomer who in 1990 at 5 won 4 US G1s incl. the Metropolitan H. and Hollywood Gold C. Debuting in August at 2 and winning his 2nd start, he then lost for 2 years until autumn at 4. After a 3rd win that December, he took off: 4 straight incl. 2 G2s, the Pimlico Special H. for his first G1, then the Metropolitan H., Hollywood Gold C. and Whitney H. - beating Easy Goer in the Metropolitan and Sunday Silence in the Gold Cup, the best in training. 6th in the Woodward S., he retired injured - Eclipse Horse of the Year. At stud in the US, his farm went bankrupt after one season and he was imported to Japan, siring local graded winners like Onward Meteor and Sakino Tenryu.
3436: Winner of the 1988 Preakness S. and Belmont S.; his Belmont win by 14 3/4 lengths recalled his sire Secretariat. Until early at 3 he was a Louisiana local star, winning 5 of 7 with 2 seconds. Winning the Lexington S. (G2), he went national as a Kentucky Derby contender; 3rd behind Winning Colors and Forty Niner, he beat both in the Preakness, then crushed the Belmont field - best of his crop. Injury then ended his career; Eclipse champion 3yo, he went to stud. Hoped to be Secretariat's heir, he sired just one G1 winner and died at 13. In Japan he is known as the sire of 1993 Rose S. (G2) winner Star Ballerina.
3437: A late bloomer who won the 1991 BC Classic (G1) at 5. Raced hard early - 8 starts at 2, 16 at 3 - without standing out, he won the Sheridan S. (G3) in autumn at 3, then was 8th in the BC Sprint. At 4 he improved, winning 3 G2s and G3s, and was 3rd in the BC Sprint. At 5 he switched from sprints to middle distances in June and won 3 straight stakes, then the Philip H. Iselin H. for his first G1, a G2, and the BC Classic - 6 straight. He retired as Eclipse Horse of the Year. His first crop included 2-time G1 winner Formal Gold, plus Washington Color, a 3-time graded winner in Japan; later imported to Japan, he sired JBC Sprint winner Fujino Wave and many local stars.
3438: A US sprint filly of 1989-1991 with 24 wins from 31, never worse than 4th - a long-time force. At 2 she won 3 of 5. At 3 she won 8 straight incl. the Test S. (G1) and Prioress S. (G2); 2nd by a neck in the BC Sprint, she was still Eclipse champion sprinter. At 4 she won 7 of 9, then in the BC Sprint fought a fierce duel with hot favorite Dayjur, who jumped a shadow from the stands, and she won. At 5 she won 5 of 7, but was injured before the BC Sprint and retired. As a broodmare, 9 winners incl. 2 stakes winners.
3439: An Australian gelding who won 7 G1s from 1990 to 1992 and was 3rd to Golden Pheasant in the 11th Japan Cup. Sprinting early, he won the Royal Sovereign S. (G3) at 3, also 2nd in 3 G1s. At 4 he won the George Main S. (G1) at a mile, plus 2 more mile G1s and 2 sprint G1s - dominant at shorter trips. At 5 he tried middle distances, winning the 2000m Caulfield S. (G1); 12th of 14 in the 2040m Cox Plate, he went further still in the Japan Cup, and as hot favorite Mejiro McQueen faltered, finished 3rd behind Golden Pheasant and Magic Night. After a long rest he won the Warwick S. (G1) at 6 and retired.
3440: A European stayer of the early 1990s, racing mostly at 14f and beyond, winner of the Irish St Leger and Australia's Melbourne Cup. Debuting late in autumn at 4, he won over hurdles too. 5th in his first G1, the Irish St Leger, at 5; after 6th in the Champion Hurdle Challenge T. (G1) at 6, he focused on the flat. That autumn he won the Irish St Leger, then the Melbourne Cup - the first winner from outside Oceania. At 7 he won the Irish St Leger again, 7th as Melbourne Cup favorite. At 8, 4th and 3rd in the same races, and he retired. A gelding, he lived in Ireland until 27.
3441: Winner of the 1990 fillies' double in England, and the first filly in 90 years to win the Irish Derby (G1) - a great mare of 1990s Europe. Winning her debut easily in September at 2, after a 2nd she won the Prix Marcel Boussac (G1). At 3 she won the Fred Darling S. (G3), then the 1000 Guineas as favorite, and the Oaks by 5 lengths. Instead of the Irish Oaks she took on Derby winner Quest for Fame in the Irish Derby and beat him. She won the Prix Vermeille, then was Arc favorite over In the Wings and Belmez, but flat, 10th, and retired. She died at 9, but produced 3 stakes winners.
3442: A mare who debuted in Argentina, then moved to the US and won 10 G1s incl. the BC Distaff. Debuting at 3 in 1990/91, she won a G1 and 2 G2s. Moving to the US in late 1991, she won 2 G2s, then in 1992 5 straight G1s incl. the Santa Maria H., Santa Margarita Invitational H. and Apple Blossom H. After 2 losses she won the BC Distaff easily - 7 wins from 9 with 6 G1s, Eclipse champion older mare. In 1993 she won the Apple Blossom H., Milady H. and Spinster S. - champion older mare again. In 1994 the Santa Margarita Invitational H., a 10th G1. Racing in 1995, she won 1 of 6 and retired. Few foals.
3443: A speedster called "America's best sprinter" in 1990-1991, the first to be Eclipse champion sprinter twice running. Debuting in October at 2, he won 2 of 3. At 3, ignoring the classics, he won 5 straight sprint stakes; 2nd by a neck to that year's Horse of the Year Criminal Type in the Metropolitan H. (G1), he won 3 more incl. the Jerome H. (G1) by 13 lengths - champion sprinter. At 4 he won the Carter H. and Vosburgh S. (G1s); hurt just after the start of his farewell BC Sprint, he was 9th, but champion sprinter again. At stud in the US, and in Japan for 3 years from 1999, he sired no superstar but over 30 stakes winners incl. 2002 Hong Kong Horse of the Year Electronic Unicorn.
3444: A great British sprinter who in 1991 became the first European-trained BC Sprint (G1) winner. First winning at 3, he won the Nunthorpe S. (G1) that summer for his first stakes, then was 2nd in the Sprint C. and Prix de l'Abbaye (both G1). In America, on his first dirt start as 9th choice, he crushed US stars like Housebuster and Pleasant Tap in the BC Sprint - Cartier champion sprinter. At 4 he won the Sprint C. (G1) and King's Stand S. (G2) from 6, then 4th defending the BC Sprint, and retired. No stars at stud, but many winners.
3445: A French horse who blossomed after moving to the US; in 1993 he won 5 G1s and was Eclipse Horse of the Year. He also ran in that year's Japan Cup, famously 2nd after jockey Kent Desormeaux misjudged the finish line. Racing in France to the end of 3, he won 3 of 8 with just a G3. In the US at 4 he won only an allowance from 4. At 5 he emerged: a G2, then 3 straight G1s - San Luis Rey S., San Juan Capistrano H., Eddie Read H. - a G2 2nd, then the Oak Tree Invitational S. and BC Turf, top US turf horse. 2nd to Legacy World in the Japan Cup, he was Horse of the Year and retired after it. At stud in Japan he sired almost no stars.
3446: A durable US mare of 1991-1994 who won 9 G1s, Eclipse champion turf female in 1992 and 1993. Debuting in June at 2, she won 3 of 7 incl. 2 G3s. At 3 she won 2 more G3s and the Matriarch S., her first G1. At 4 she won the Beverly Hills S. and Ramona H., 2 seconds, then the Matriarch again - champion turf female. At 5 she won the Beverly Hills H., Ramona H. and Beverly D. S. - 3 straight G1s; 9th in the BC Mile, she won a 3rd Matriarch - champion again. At 6 she won a 3rd Ramona H. for a 9th G1, and retired after a 2nd in the Beverly D. S. Kidney disease took her early with just 2 foals, but she entered the US Hall of Fame.
3447: Winner of both the 1992 2000 Guineas and Irish 2000 Guineas, with 5 G1s at a mile to 10f. Debuting in July at 2, he won 5 straight to the Middle Park S. (G1), but crop-mate Arazi, Cartier Horse of the Year at 2, took the honors. At 3, beaten in the Greenham S. (G3), he won both 2000 Guineas, then the International S. and Champion S. - 5 G1s. Last in the BC Classic on his first dirt start, he retired to stud in Japan. His 2nd crop had Oaks winner Erimo Excel; graded winners Ibuki Yamano O and Grace Namura followed.
3448: A star miler in Europe and America in 1993-1994; his 1994 BC Mile (G1) made him Cartier Horse of the Year with just one G1 that year. Unbeaten in 2 from October at 2, at 3 he was 2nd in the 2000 Guineas and won the Irish 2000 Guineas. 5th in the Derby and Eclipse S., less effective further, he focused on the mile: 4th Prix du Moulin, 2nd QEII S., 5th BC Mile - winless but suited. At 4 he won the Queen Anne S. (G2), then kept placing, until a 2nd BC Mile try; thoroughly prepared after the year before, he won by 3 lengths and retired. A successful sire with over 80 stakes winners.
3449: Winner of the 1993 German Derby, Grosser Preis von Baden and Grosser Preis des Jockey Club; at 5 in 1995 he won the 15th Japan Cup, beating Narita Brian and Hishi Amazon. Debuting in August at 2, he won 2 listed races from 3. At 3, 5th, 6th and 7th, he won the German Derby as 12th choice, then the Grosser Preis von Baden. At 4 he won the Hansa-Preis (G2), Baden again and the Jockey Club race; 8th in the Arc, but German Horse of the Year. At 5 he won the Gran Premio di Milano and Merck Finck-Bank Preis (G1s), 4th in the Arc, then the Japan Cup, holding off Hishi Amazon's charge - Horse of the Year again. Retired to stud that year, he sired G1 winners Paolini, Intendant and more.
3450: She won the 1993 BC Distaff (G1), Eclipse champion 3yo filly; her fierce duel with runner-up Paseana was The Blood-Horse's "Race of the Year." She began unbeaten in 4 incl. a stakes, then stopped winning, and moved to a California stable in spring at 3. She won the Hollywood Oaks (G1) at once, 4 straight incl. a listed race and G2. Favorite in the BC Distaff, she beat 9-time G1 winner Paseana by a nose after a fierce duel. At 4 she won the Gamely H. for a 3rd G1; 6th defending the BC Distaff, she retired. As a broodmare she produced BC Mile (G1) winner War Chant; her daughter Spinning Wildcat, imported to Japan, produced Danon Smash.
