3451: A durable Australian gelding from 1992 to 1998, winning 8 G1s from 1000m to 2500m. At 2 in 1992/93 he won his 2nd start, then the QTC Sires' Produce S. and Castlemaine S. (G1s around a mile). At 3 he won the Caulfield Guineas and Australian Guineas (mile G1s) and the 2500m Victoria Derby and 2400m AJC Derby. At 4 he won the 1000m Lightning S. (G1). Winless in 4 at 5, but 2nd in the Cox Plate. At 6, mainly sprinting, he won the Lightning S. again, a 1200m G2 and a listed race. Fading at 7, he won the Chirnside S. (G2) and retired at season's end.
3452: A British 10f specialist who won 5 G1s in 1995-1996 incl. 2 Eclipse S. and 2 International S. Debuting late in July at 3, he won his 4th start and 3 straight, then joined Godolphin and won 3 more in Dubai early at 4. In England he won the Eclipse S., his first stakes win a G1, then the International S. Last in the BC Classic on dirt, and last in the Dubai World Cup at 5, he focused on turf, winning the Prix d'Ispahan, Eclipse S. and International S. - 3 straight G1s. 2nd in the Champion S., his only loss at his best trip, he was Cartier champion older horse and retired. At stud he sired G1 winners Cavalryman and Cutlass Bay and many more.
3453: A great miler who won 4 mile G1s in Europe and America in 1995 and was Cartier Horse of the Year over Triple Crown winner Lammtarra. 3rd on debut in September at 2, she then kept winning: the Weld Park S. (G3), Athasi S. (L), and the Irish 1000 Guineas in spring at 3. In England she won the Coronation S. in record time; in France the Prix du Moulin against older horses and colts as favorite. 2nd in the QEII S., her only mile defeat, she bounced back in the BC Mile, breaking clear to win by 2 lengths, 7 more to 3rd, and retired. The Cartier vote split with Lammtarra, but her strong wins in 4 countries carried the day. She left no stars and died at 11.
3454: A star European sprinter of 1996, Cartier champion sprinter. Debuting late in July at 3, he won his 2nd and 3rd starts, then kept losing. At 4 he was transformed: 3 straight incl. the Prix de Saint-Georges (G3), the Prix du Gros-Chene (G2), then the July C. as 2nd choice, leading throughout, and the Prix Maurice de Gheest (G1). In the Abbaye he was caught late by Kistena, 2nd by a neck, ending 6 straight. 6 wins and a 2nd from 7 - champion sprinter - and he retired. His first crop had French Derby winner Anabaa Blue, then G1 winners Goldikova, Yell and many more - a great success.
3455: Winner of the King George VI & Queen Elizabeth Diamond S. in 1997 and 1998, who also ran well in the Dubai World Cup and BC Classic - top class on turf and dirt. Debuting in France in May at 3, he won 5 straight to the Grand Prix de Deauville (G2), then 3rd to Lammtarra in his first G1, the Arc. At 4 he won the Coronation C., then 4th to Helissio in the Arc and 3rd to Pilsudski in the BC Turf. Moving to a British stable at 5, he won the King George over Pilsudski, but was 7th to Peintre Celebre in the Arc. At 6 he won the King George again and the Irish Champion S. - 4 G1s - and on dirt was 2nd in the Dubai World Cup and 3rd in the BC Classic. Cartier champion older horse. At stud only 13 stakes winners - below hopes.
3456: Winner of the 1995 Kentucky Derby and Belmont S., and a successful sire of dual classic winner Point Given; North American champion sire in 2001. Debuting in September at 2, he won 2 of 6 incl. the Remsen S. (G2). At 3 he won the Florida Derby; 4th in the Blue Grass S., he then won the Kentucky Derby, was 3rd in the Preakness and won the Belmont - best of his crop. He won the Travers S. easily for a 4th G1; 5th to 10-race winner Cigar in the Jockey Club Gold C., but Eclipse champion 3yo. His first crop had BC Distaff winner Spain, his 2nd 6-time G1 winner Point Given. Leased to Japan for a year with no stars, though in-utero import Iide Kenshin won the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun.
3457: A miracle horse who won the 1996 BC Mile (G1), spent ages injured, and won it again 2 years later. Unbeaten in 3 from September at 2, he won the Best Turn S. (G3) at 3, 2nd in the Illinois Derby (G2), won the Jersey Derby (G2), then was last in the BC Sprint; 4 wins from 10 with 3 stakes. At 4 he won a G3 and listed race, then the BC Mile on turf over Spinning World and Mark of Esteem - suddenly a star. A leg injury kept him out about 2 years; back in autumn at 6, after an allowance, he won a fierce duel in the BC Mile - an amazing comeback.
3458: Winner of both the Cox Plate and Melbourne Cup in 1996/97, Australian Horse of the Year. At 2 in 1994/95 he won 1 of 4. Emerging at 3, he won the Expressway S. (G2) and soon the Australian C. (G1), but rival Octagonal blocked him: 2nd, 3rd, 2nd in G1s. At 4 he finally beat Octagonal in the Cox Plate, then won the Melbourne Cup by 2 1/4 lengths - only the 4th to win both in a season. Coming to the Japan Cup, he fell ill and was scratched - as his sire Sky Chase had been in 1988. Back home he won the C F Orr S. for a 4th G1 and retired.
3459: Winner of the 1998 French Derby and Irish Derby, Cartier Horse of the Year. Debuting at 3, he won the Prix La Force (G3) in his 3rd start, then the French Derby as 6th choice, outfighting Croco Rouge, and the Irish Derby as favorite by 4.5 lengths - top of his crop. Aimed at the Arc, he was 3rd to Sagamix in the Prix Niel and 8th to Sagamix in the Arc. In a wide-open Cartier vote he still took Horse of the Year and champion 3yo colt. At 4, placings in G1s (2nd Ganay, 3rd Coronation C., 3rd Saint-Cloud) and a win in the Prix Gontaut-Biron (G3), then he retired to stud in Japan. Siring only 2-time graded winner Admire Monarch, he was exported to France after 4 years.
3460: Winner of the 1999 Kentucky Derby and Preakness. Once running in claiming races, he rose to the top and became Eclipse Horse of the Year. Struggling early, he won his 6th start at 2; still losing at 3, he got his 2nd win in a claiming race. Believing in him, his camp ran him in the Kentucky Derby, and he won as 11th choice, stunning everyone; 5th choice in the Preakness, he won by 1.5 lengths. Triple Crown favorite in the Belmont, he was injured in the race, 3rd, and retired. After 3 years at stud he was imported to Japan, siring Wonder Acute, a 3-time dirt G1 winner.
3461: The 2001 Arc winner. Gifted but injured through much of 3 and 4, he romped in the Arc as if making up for lost time. Winning 2 of 3 from August at 2, he won 2 stakes at 3, then was 2nd by a length to Sinndar in the Derby and 4th to Giant's Causeway in the Eclipse S., injured in the race. After a year off, he returned in summer at 4, won a listed race easily, the International S. by 7 lengths, and the Arc by a joint-record 6 lengths. On dirt in the BC Classic he lost by a nose to Tiznow. At 5, 3rd in the Dubai World Cup, then 2nd in a G3, and he retired. At stud: G1 winners Presvis and Sakhee's Secret.
3462: Winner of the 2003 BC Classic and 2004 Dubai World Cup - no Eclipse Award, but for a time the best on dirt. Debuting late in May at 3, he couldn't keep up and was pulled up; after a long rest he first won in February at 4, then climbed through allowances and claimers, winning the Goodwood BC H. (G2) that autumn. At 5 he won the Goodwood again, then the BC Classic for his first G1. At 6 he beat Medaglia d'Oro in a duel in the Dubai World Cup - top of the dirt world. He won the Pacific Classic S., then was 3rd to Ghostzapper in the BC Classic and retired. Few stars at stud, but 2 G1 winners: Shared Account and Whitmore.
3463: He blossomed after moving from England to the US; with 3 straight G1s incl. the Jockey Club Gold C., he was 2003 Eclipse Horse of the Year. Debuting in England in April at 3, he won his 2nd start, then struggled - no future in 7 European turf starts, so he moved to the US. He won 3 straight, the New Orleans H. (G2) in March at 4, then 3 more incl. the Pimlico Special H. (G1). A narrow 2nd in the Stephen Foster H., he won the Suburban H., Woodward S. and Jockey Club Gold C., pulling clear each time - Horse of the Year - and retired. A steady sire with some G1 winners, if short of an ideal heir to A.P. Indy.
3464: An Australian sprinter of 2002-2003 who, at Royal Ascot in 2003, became the first Southern Hemisphere-trained winner of both the King's Stand S. (G2) and Golden Jubilee S. (G1). Debuting in 2001/02 at 2, he won easily, then the Skyline S. (G3) in his 5th start. In G1s he was 3rd, 2nd, 3rd. At 3 he missed 6 more times, then won the Emirates Classic (G2) and Lightning S. (G1). Late that season in England he won the King's Stand S. as 13th choice, and 4 days later the Golden Jubilee S. as 2nd choice. Favorite in the July C. (G1), he was 2nd, then retired to stud. A fine sire, with Golden Jubilee winner Starspangledbanner and many G1 winners.
3465: A durable Hong Kong horse who raced until 9 and won the Yasuda Kinen (G1) at 7 in 2005/06, Hong Kong Horse of the Year. Debuting in England, he won his first 2, then nothing to the end of 3, and moved to Hong Kong. Just 1 win from 7 in 2002/03; in 2003/04 he won the Hong Kong Kimpai, a first sign of progress. From 2004/05 he raced at the top, winning the Stewards' C. and Champions Mile. In 2005/06 he won the Champions Mile again, then in a wide-open Yasuda Kinen beat Asakusa Den'en and others for his first G1 - Horse of the Year. Declining from 2006/07 (winless in 9, then 1 win from 7), he raced until the Hong Kong Cup in December 2008 and retired.
3466: Winner of 4 G1s in 2005 incl. the BC Classic, US Eclipse Horse of the Year. Debuting at 3, he won just a maiden and an allowance from 9. At 4 he improved, placing in stakes, then 2nd by a neck to that year's Horse of the Year Ghostzapper in his first G1, the Woodward S. At 5 he won the Donn H., his first G1, then the Stephen Foster H. and Woodward S., and the BC Classic as favorite - top of the tree, Horse of the Year - and retired. He died after just one crop, which included Woodward S. winner Havre de Grace, a filly.
3467: An Australian sprint mare who won 5 G1s in 2006-2007. Debuting at 3 in 2004/05, she won easily, then after a 2nd won 5 straight. In 2005/06 she won the Winterbottom S. (G2), but was 6th and 11th in G1s. In 2006/07 she won the Manikato S., then the Lightning S., Australia S. and Newmarket H. - top of Australian sprinting. At Royal Ascot she won the King's Stand S. (G2) easily; 15th in the Golden Jubilee S., but Australian Horse of the Year. In 2007/08 she won The Age Classic for a 5th G1, and retired after a 10th in the Hong Kong Sprint.
3468: Winner of the 2005 Poulains and French Derby, now better known as a sire: dual French classic winner Lope de Vega, BC Turf and Prix Vermeille winner Tarnawa and many more G1 winners; in Japan, graded winner Light On Cue. Debuting in July at 2, he won 3 straight to the Dewhurst S. (G1), Cartier champion 2yo. At 3, 9th in the UAE Derby, he won the Poulains, French Derby and St. James's Palace S. - 3 straight G1s - then a fracture ended his career. His 2nd crop had Lope de Vega; then Hong Kong stars Dan Excel and Able Friend, French 1000 Guineas winner Castle Lady and others - over 20 G1 winners. Lope de Vega has succeeded at stud too.
3469: A French filly who won the 2005 Pouliches and French Oaks unbeaten; Cartier champion 2yo filly, then champion 3yo filly. Debuting in May at 2 under Christophe Lemaire, then based in France, she won all 5 incl. 2 G1s, the Prix Morny and Prix Marcel Boussac. At 3 she won the Prix de la Grotte (G3) easily, the Pouliches by 5 lengths, the French Oaks by 3, and the Prix d'Astarte (G1) against older mares. Against colts in the Jacques le Marois, she was 4th to Dubawi - her first defeat - and retired. Her first foal, Eightfold Path, won a US G3.
3470: Winner of the 2005 Preakness and Belmont S. At the time, a girl also named Alex died of childhood cancer at 8; his owners donated to and raised money for a childhood cancer fund, earning a special Eclipse Award. Debuting in June at 2, he won 4 straight to the Hopeful S. (G1). At 3 he won the Arkansas Derby (G2), then was caught by 2 outsiders in the Kentucky Derby, 3rd. He made amends in the Preakness by 4 3/4 lengths and won the Belmont by 7. An injury then ended his career; with only a spring campaign, he was still Eclipse champion 3yo. At stud he sired Texas Red, Afleet Express and other G1 winners.
3471: A US turf horse of 2005-2007 with 6 G1s incl. the BC Turf, which he won on his 3rd try by a record 7 lengths. Always on turf, he won the Virginia Derby (G3) in summer at 3, but was beaten in the Secretariat S., Turf Classic Invitational and BC Turf. At 4 he won the Turf Classic S., United Nations S. and Turf Classic Invitational, then 3rd to Red Rocks in the BC Turf. Unsatisfied, he raced on at 5, winning the United Nations S. and Turf Classic Invitational again, then, on soft ground for the first time, broke clear from a handy spot and drew away in the BC Turf. Eclipse champion turf male, he retired. At stud he sired Arlington Million winner The Pizza Man and more.
3472: Winner of both the 2007 King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S. and Arc; with 4 G1s that year, Cartier Horse of the Year. At 2 he won 2 of 4. At 3, 3rd in the Derby, he won the Irish Derby and Irish Champion S.; on dirt in America he was last, 32 lengths back, in the Jockey Club Gold C., and came home. At 4 he won the Prix Ganay, the King George easily, the Irish Champion S. again, and the Arc, holding off Youmzain by a head. Beaten in the BC Turf and Hong Kong Vase, he retired. A steady sire with multiple stakes winners from his first crop.
3473: At 4 in 2007 she won 3 G1s incl. the BC Distaff, Eclipse champion older mare. Debuting in January at 3, she struggled, first winning in her 4th start; 2 wins from 6. At 4 she won the First Flight H. (G2), then the Go for Wand H. and Ruffian H., and outfought Hystericalady in the BC Distaff - champion older mare. At 5 she won the Ogden Phipps H., Go for Wand H. and Personal Ensign H.; 6th to Zenyatta in the renamed BC Ladies' Classic, she retired. Imported to Japan as a broodmare, she produced stars Rouge Buck and Potager.
3474: A Hong Kong sprint gelding who won the Hong Kong Sprint (G1) in 2007/08 and 2009/10. Debuting at 3 in 2006/07, he won 5 straight; in 2007/08 he won 3 straight to the Hong Kong Sprint. Aimed at Japan's Sprinters S. in 2008/09, he was injured; back, he won Singapore's KrisFlyer International Sprint (G3). In 2009/10 he won a 2nd Hong Kong Sprint, then the Centenary Sprint C. and Chairman's Sprint Prize - Hong Kong Horse of the Year. In 2010/11, 3rd in the Hong Kong Sprint, he won 2 stakes; in 2011/12 at 8, after heavy defeats, he retired.
3475: Winner of the 2006 BC Juvenile (G1) and 2007 Kentucky Derby (G1), and a successful sire in the US and Japan. Debuting in July at 2 and winning his 2nd start, he was 3rd in the Arlington-Washington BC Futurity (G3) and Breeders' Futurity (G1), then won the BC Juvenile by a record 10 lengths - Eclipse champion 2yo. At 3, after 2 preps, he broke clear powerfully in a 20-runner Kentucky Derby. He won the Travers S. for a 3rd G1; 4th in the BC Classic, he retired. His foals include stakes winners every year; in Japan, in-utero import Fleet Street won the Elm S. (G3), and during one season in Japan he sired local graded winners Fashionista and Field Sense.
3476: Winner of the 2008 Derby, Irish Champion S. and Champion S.; Cartier champion 2yo, then champion 3yo colt. Unbeaten in 5 at 2 incl. the National S. and Dewhurst S. (G1s), he was hailed as next year's classic star. At 3, 2nd in the 2000 Guineas and Irish 2000 Guineas, his camp stepped him up in trip 1 week later in the Derby, where he outfought Tartan Bearer. 3rd against older horses in the International S., he won the Irish Champion S. and Champion S., and was champion 3yo colt over 4-time G1 winner Henrythenavigator. At stud he sired Dawn Approach and many more.
3477: A great modern sire, North American champion sire every year since 2019, the best son and heir of Harlan's Holiday. In 2020 his progeny earned a North American record $21,725,335, over double runner-up Uncle Mo. On the track he won 3 of 6 incl. the CashCall Futurity (G1) and drew little attention at stud. But his first crop produced 2-time BC Dirt Mile winner Goldencents, then G1 winners Practical Joke, Authentic and Gamine. His value soared; his fee reached $150,000 when he first topped the list in 2019, yet mares kept flooding in, and his runners dominate stakes. In 2025 2yo stars like Hopeful (G1) winner Ted Noffey and Spinaway S. (G1) winner Tommy Jo kept coming - his reign looks set to continue.
3478: Winner of the 2008 Kentucky Derby and Preakness unbeaten. Hoped to be the first unbeaten Triple Crown winner since Seattle Slew, he was inexplicably pulled up in the Belmont. Brilliant from the start, he won his September debut at 2 by 11 1/4 lengths, an allowance at 3 by 12 3/4, the Florida Derby by 5 and the Kentucky Derby by 4 3/4 - no one could get near him. He won the Preakness by 5 1/4. A Triple Crown seemed certain; he was 1.3-1 Belmont favorite, but faded at the crucial point and was pulled up, a crushing letdown for fans. He won the Haskell Invitational S. (G1) and the turf Monmouth S. (L), then retired as Eclipse champion 3yo. At stud: G1 winner Dortmund and scattered stakes winners - modest.
3479: A US winner of 7 G1s from 2007 to 2011, Eclipse champion turf male in 2009 and 2010 - 12 wins and 10 seconds from 29, only twice unplaced. Unbeaten in 2 from debut, 2 of 3 at 2; at 3 he won 3 stakes incl. the Virginia Derby (G2). At 4 he blossomed, winning 4 straight G1s - Frank E. Kilroe Mile H., Manhattan H., Man o' War S., Arlington Million - and was 2nd to Zenyatta in the BC Classic; champion older male and turf male. At 5 he won the Man o' War S. and Shadwell Turf Mile S., champion turf male again. In 2011 at 6 he won only the Shadwell Turf Mile from 6 G1 tries and retired. His best foal is BC Sprint winner Drefong.
3480: An Australian sprint gelding of 2010-2012 who repeatedly met Black Caviar, unbeaten in 25, finishing 2nd to her 4 times. Debuting at 3 in 2008/09, he won 8 straight into 2009/10, then 3 more in 2010/11 incl. the Manikato S., his first G1. That season his clashes with Black Caviar began: 2nd in the Lightning S., T J Smith S., BTC Cup and the next season's Lightning S. In 2011/12 he won the All Aged S. and Newmarket H. - 3 G1s. After about a year off, he returned in March 2013, winless in 5, then 11th in The Shorts (G2) and 14th in the Premiere S. (G2) at 8, and retired.
3481: An invincible Singapore sprinter of 2008-2012 who also won 2 international G1s, the Dubai Golden Shaheen and KrisFlyer International Sprint, and was 4th to Curren Chan in Japan's Sprinters S. Debuting in October 2008 at 3, he won his first 7, mostly easily. From 2010 he tried international G1s: 2nd in the Golden Shaheen, KrisFlyer and Hong Kong Sprint. In 2011 he won the Golden Shaheen and KrisFlyer, then 4th in the Sprinters S., his first finish outside the top 3. 2nd defending the Golden Shaheen in 2012, he won once at home, then leg trouble kept him out; his retirement was announced at the end of 2016, at 11.
3482: Winner of the 2010 BC Classic (G1), handing 19-race unbeaten favorite Zenyatta her only defeat. Debuting in September at 2, he won his 2nd start, rested 8 months, then won 2 straight, the Fayette S. (G2), Clark H. (G2), and at 4 the William Donald Schaefer S. (G3), Stephen Foster H. and Whitney H. (G1s) - 5 straight. 2nd to Haynesfield in the Jockey Club Gold C., he then beat Zenyatta in the BC Classic, breaking clear and holding off her furious run from wide by a head. He retired after it; Horse of the Year went to Zenyatta, but he was champion older male. At stud: G1 winners such as French Oaks winner Senga and CCA Oaks winner Wet Paint.
3483: A filly who won 3 G1s incl. the Woodward S. in 2011, Eclipse Horse of the Year - the only star, and masterpiece, of Saint Liam, who died after one crop. 1 win from 2 at 2; back from a long rest in May at 3, she won the Cotillion S. (G2), but was 2nd in the Alabama S. and 3rd in the BC Ladies' Classic. At 4 she improved, winning the Azeri S. (G3), Apple Blossom H. (G1) and Obeah S. (G3), then beat the males in the Woodward S. and won the Beldame Invitational S. 4th in the BC Classic, she was still Horse of the Year. At 5 she won a listed race easily, then retired injured. Bred to Tapit and others, her 2017 foal Marvelous Guy was imported to Japan.
3484: A French mare who starred in European sprints and miles from 2011 to 2013, winning 6 G1s incl. 3 straight Prix Maurice de Gheest. Unbeaten in 2 from August at 2, she won the Prix Imprudence (G3) at 3; 7th in England's 1000 Guineas, she won the Maurice de Gheest at home. At 4 she won it again and the Prix du Moulin; 8th of 9 in America's BC Mile. At 5 she won the Maurice de Gheest, Jacques le Marois and Prix de la Foret - 3 straight G1s; 6th in the Hong Kong Mile, but Cartier champion older horse, and she retired. Unbeatable in France with 6 G1s, she lost all 5 starts abroad - yet in one, the Diamond Jubilee S., she was 2nd by a head to Australia's unbeaten Black Caviar, the only horse ever to truly threaten her.
3485: The 2012 Arc winner, famous in Japan for catching hope Orfevre near the line to win by a neck, crushing Japanese fans. To 3 she was unremarkable: 2 wins from 7 and a stakes 2nd. At 4 she won a listed race and the Prix Corrida (G2), then 4th in the Prix de Pomone and 3rd in the Prix Vermeille. Her camp took a bold shot at the Arc, where unbeaten Derby winner Camelot and Japanese Triple Crown winner Orfevre were fancied; she was 12th choice. In the straight Orfevre looked the winner but veered badly, and she pounced to win by a neck - shattering Japan's dream and making her name famous there. 13th in the Japan Cup, far behind the Gentildonna-Orfevre battle, she retired.
3486: Winner of the BC Filly & Mare Sprint (G1) in 2012 and 2013, Eclipse champion female sprinter both years. Debuting late in June at 3, she won 3 straight to the Gardenia S. (G3). At 4 she won the Madison S. (G1), the Humana Distaff S. (G1) by 7 1/4 lengths in record time, and the BC Filly & Mare Sprint by 4.5 - 5 straight. At 5 she won the Masters S. (G2) and the BC Filly & Mare Sprint again, holding the lead to the line by half a length. 4th in the Cigar Mile H. (G1), she won the Hurricane Bertie S. (G3) at 6 and retired.
3487: A gelding who won 5 straight G1s in 2015 incl. the Dubai Turf and QEII S., a miler and Cartier champion older horse. Debuting over a mile in September at 2, he kept losing; stepped up at 3, he won his 5th start at 2400m. After nearly a year off, 6th of 8 in his first stakes, the 3100m Prix Vicomtesse Vigier (G2) at 4, he returned to the mile and was transformed: 5 straight into 5 to the Dubai Turf (G1), then the Prix d'Ispahan, Queen Anne S., Sussex S. and QEII S. Unbeaten in 6 that year, Cartier champion older horse; one more win at 6 made 10 straight, and he retired.
3488: A filly who won the 2014 Oaks (G1) and King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S. (G1) - only the 2nd 3yo filly to win the King George, after Pawneese 38 years earlier. Winning her debut in September at 2, she rested long. Aimed at middle distances at 3, she won the Pretty Polly S. (L) and the Oaks easily. Taking on older horses and colts in the King George, she beat Telescope, Magician and others by 3 lengths. Hot favorite in the Yorkshire Oaks, she lost a duel with Tapestry by half a length; favorite in the Arc too, she was 3rd as Treve won again, and retired to breed.
3489: An Irish mare who won the 2016 Arc (G1). With just 1 G1 that year but 6 G1 seconds, she was Cartier champion older horse. Debuting in August at 2, she won 2 of 3 incl. the Prix Marcel Boussac (G1). At 3 she was 2nd in the Irish 1000 Guineas, Coronation S., Irish Champion S. and Champion S. - so close - then won the BC Turf (G1) in America. At 4 she was 2nd in 5 straight G1s: Tattersalls Gold C., Coronation C., Prince of Wales's S., Yorkshire Oaks and Irish Champion S. 5th choice in the Arc, she won in record time, making up for it all. 2nd in the Champion S. and 3rd in the BC Turf, she retired - 10 G1 seconds in 2 years, a remarkable record. Her foal by War Front, Battleground, won the Vintage S. (G2).
3490: A filly who dominated the 2016 English fillies' classics, from a blueblood family with full sisters Empress Josephine (Irish 1000 Guineas) and Tuesday (Oaks). Debuting early, in June at 2, she won her 2nd start, then the Moyglare Stud S. and Fillies' Mile (G1s) - Cartier champion 2yo filly. At 3 she won the 1000 Guineas easily on her return, lost the Irish 1000 Guineas by a head, and won the Oaks as favorite - best of her crop. She beat older horses in the Pretty Polly S. and Nassau S. (G1s); 3rd in the Irish Champion S., she won the QEII S. against colts. Cartier Horse of the Year and champion 3yo filly. At 4 she won the Mooresbridge S. (G2) easily, then retired injured. Her son Henry Longfellow won the Vincent O'Brien S., his first G1.
3491: Winner of the 2017 BC Classic (G1), Woodward S. (G1) and more, Eclipse Horse of the Year. A fine start at stud too: his first crop includes Preakness winner Early Voting and many others. Unbeaten in 2 from September at 2, he won the Risen Star S. (G2) at 3; 3rd in the Kentucky Derby, 2nd in the BC Dirt Mile, he won the Clark H. (G1) and blossomed. At 4 he won the Razorback H. (G3) easily; 2nd in the Dubai World Cup, he won the Stephen Foster H., Whitney S., Woodward S. and BC Classic - 4 straight G1s - Horse of the Year. He won the Pegasus World Cup (G1) at 5 and retired to stud.
3492: A British sprinter who won 3 sprint G1s in Europe and Dubai in 2019, Cartier champion sprinter. Winning his debut in June at 2, he won the Gimcrack S. (G2) in his 4th start, 2nd in the Middle Park S. and 3rd in the Dewhurst S. At 3 he won 2 G3s but was 3rd in the Commonwealth C. and 4th in the Sprint C. - not quite there. At 4 he won the King's Stand S. (G1), and at 5 he peaked: 2 G2s in Dubai, then the Al Quoz Sprint, and back home the King's Stand S. and Diamond Jubilee S. - top of European sprinting. He retired, champion sprinter on his first-half record alone. His first crop has G1 winners Irish 2000 Guineas winner Rosallion and BC Juvenile Turf Sprint winner Big Evs - a fine start.
3493: From Frankel's first crop, one of his best, winning 4 G1s incl. the Champion S. in 2017 and 2018, and sire of Arc winner Ace Impact. Winning his only start at 2, after 6 months off he won his opener at 3, then 3rd in the Derby and 2nd in the Irish Derby. He won the Great Voltigeur S. (G2), Prix Niel (G2) and Champion S. (G1) - 3 straight. At 4 he won the Prix Ganay and Coronation C. - 5 straight; 2nd in the Prince of Wales's S., he won the Champion S. again for a 4th G1 and retired. His first crop had French Derby and Arc winner Ace Impact, making him France's champion sire in 2023.
3494: The 2018 French Derby winner, an Irish-bred, Irish-trained son of Deep Impact. Winning his debut at Saint-Cloud in September at 2, after 6 months off he was 2nd in the Prix La Force (G3), then won the Prix Greffulhe (G2). 2nd choice in the French Derby, he broke clear in the straight and held on by half a length. 3rd in the Prix Guillaume d'Ornano (G2); 5th in the Irish Champion S. and 9th in the Arc. At 4, 2nd in the Prix Ganay and Prix d'Ispahan, he switched to the mile, 3rd in the Prix Messidor and 6th in the Jacques le Marois, and retired. His 2nd crop has 2-time British Champions Fillies & Mares S. winner Kalpana - spreading Deep Impact's blood in Europe.
3495: Winner of the 2018 2000 Guineas (G1), a Japan-bred, Irish-trained son of Deep Impact - the first Japan-bred winner of an English classic. Winning his debut in August at 2 and the Beresford S. (G2), he won the Racing Post T. (G1) as favorite - next year's top classic hope. Straight to the 2000 Guineas at 3, 2nd choice behind new star Masar, he beat him - unbeaten in 4, a classic. Hot favorite for the Derbys, he was 4th in the Derby and 3rd in the Irish Derby, then 2nd in the Eclipse S., 4th in the International S. and 2nd in the Irish Champion S. Tendon trouble ended his career.
3496: Winner of 4 G1s in 2018 incl. the Eclipse S. and International S., Cartier Horse of the Year. Unbeaten in 3 from August at 2 incl. the Royal Lodge S. (G2), he lost the Racing Post T. by a neck. At 3, 5th in the 2000 Guineas and 3rd in the Derby, then a storming run: the Eclipse S., International S., Irish Champion S. and QEII S. - 4 straight G1s from a mile to 10f. Last in the BC Classic on his first dirt start, but Cartier Horse of the Year and champion 3yo colt. Retired to stud that year, his first crop's Dubai Mile won the Criterium de Saint-Cloud (G1).
3497: Winner of 3 G1s in 2020 incl. the Eclipse S., Cartier Horse of the Year. One of the best by Dubawi, Dubai Millennium's only sire son, he was hyped before his debut. Debuting in September at 2, he won the Autumn S. (G3) in his 3rd start. Injury cost him spring at 3; he won only the Prix du Prince d'Orange (G3) on return. At 4 he won the Grosser Preis von Baden, his first G1, but was 10th in the Arc, his only time unplaced. At 5 he won the Dubai Millennium S. (G3), then the Coronation C., Eclipse S. and International S. - 3 straight G1s. 2nd to Magical in the Irish Champion S., he was Horse of the Year, retired that year, and has stood in Ireland since 2021.
3498: A US mare who won 7 of 8 incl. 3 G1s in 2019, Eclipse champion older mare. Winless from October at 2, she won 3 straight stakes at 3 to the Santa Anita Oaks (G1). Beaten by Monomoy Girl and Eskimo Kisses in the fillies' classics, she won the Cotillion S. (G1), and was 3rd to Monomoy Girl in the BC Distaff. At 4, with rival Monomoy Girl out injured, she ruled: the Apple Blossom H., Ogden Phipps S. and Personal Ensign S. (G1s), her only loss a 2nd in the BC Distaff - champion older mare. At 5 she won the world's richest race, the Saudi Cup, doubling her earnings; 2nd in the Personal Ensign S., she was found to have a fracture and retired.
3499: A US filly who won 7 G1s from 2018 to 2020, Eclipse champion 3yo filly and champion older mare: 14 wins from 17, all 3 losses 2nds. Unbeaten in 3, 2nd in the Golden Rod S. (G2) at 2. At 3 she won the Ashland S., Kentucky Oaks, Acorn S. and CCA Oaks - 4 straight G1s; first past the post in the Cotillion S., she was demoted to 2nd, then won the BC Distaff - undisputed champion. Injured, she missed all of 4. Back in spring at 5 she won 2, then the La Troienne S. and BC Distaff - unbeaten in 4, champion older mare. At 6 she won the Bayakoa S. (G3), lost the Apple Blossom H. by a nose, and retired with a fracture.
3500: A US turf filly who excelled at a mile, Eclipse champion turf female of 2020. Unbeaten in 3 from September at 2 incl. the BC Juvenile Fillies Turf (G1). At 3 she won the Appalachian S. and Lake Placid S. (G2s) and the 9f Queen Elizabeth II Challenge C. (G1). At 4 she won the Jenny Wiley S. and Just a Game S. (G1s), but 4th to Uni in the First Lady S.; Uni, also a 2-time G1 winner, took the Eclipse. At 5 she won the Jenny Wiley S. and Diana S. (G1s), then in her farewell BC Filly & Mare Turf was 2nd by a neck to Audarya - champion turf female at last.
3501: An Australian mare of 2018-2022, a stayer who won 11 G1s incl. the Melbourne Cup and Caulfield Cup. Debuting at 2 in 2017/18, she won the Ethereal S. (G3) in 2018/19, then the Vinery Stud S. and Australian Oaks (G1s). Only the Tancred S. in 2019/20, then a huge 2020/21: the Winx S., Turnbull S., Caulfield Cup, Chipping Norton S. and Ranvet S. - 5 G1s, Australian Horse of the Year. After 3 more G1s in 2021/22 she moved to France for its rich staying races, but best 3rd in the Prix Foy (G2), no G1 impact; her retirement was announced at the end of 2022.
3502: Cartier champion 2yo colt of 2018 and champion 3yo colt of 2019, a central figure in European racing. Winning his debut in August at 2, he won the Solario S. (G3), Champagne S. (G2) and Dewhurst S. (G1) - unbeaten in 4, champion 2yo. Aimed at the 2000 Guineas and Derby at 3, a leg issue held him back; 2nd in the Dante S. (G2) and Irish 2000 Guineas, 3rd in the St. James's Palace S. Dropping to 1400m, he won the Prix Jean Prat (G1), then beat older horses in the Sussex S. (G1). Aimed at the BC Mile, he was found to have a fracture and retired to stud.
3503: A great European miler of 2020-2021, Cartier champion 3yo colt in 2020 and champion older horse in 2021. Watched from debut, he won his first 2 in England from August at 2; at 3 a handicap, then the St. James's Palace S. and Jacques le Marois (G1s) - unbeaten in 5. 3rd in the QEII S., his first loss, but champion 3yo colt. At 4 he won the bet365 Mile (G2), then the Lockinge S., Queen Anne S. and Jacques le Marois - 3 straight mile G1s. 2nd again in the QEII S., he was still champion older horse, and retired to stud in England.
3504: Winner of the 2020 Kentucky Derby (G1) and BC Classic (G1), Eclipse Horse of the Year - a top earner who helped his sire Into Mischief to the North American title. Winning his debut in November at 2, at 3 he won the Sham S. (G3) and San Felipe S. (G2). 2nd in the Santa Anita Derby after a slow start, his first loss, he won the Haskell S. (G1). In a Kentucky Derby moved to autumn by Covid, he beat Belmont winner Tiz the Law (the Belmont, delayed 2 weeks, was run first). 2nd in the Preakness, he won the BC Classic over favorite Tiz the Law again, and retired to stud that year.
3505: A US filly who won 5 G1s in 2020-2021, Eclipse champion female sprinter of 2020. Winning her debut in March at 3, she won 3 straight to the Acorn S. (G1) by 18 3/4 lengths, then the Test S. (G1) by 7. Crossing 3rd in the Kentucky Oaks, she was disqualified for a drug test. She won the BC Filly & Mare Sprint in record time - champion female sprinter. At 4 she won 4 straight incl. the Derby City Distaff S. and Ballerina H. for a 5th G1 - unbeatable in filly sprints - but was 3rd to Ce Ce in her 2nd BC Filly & Mare Sprint, and retired.
3506: Winner of 4 straight G1s in 2021 - Poulains, French Derby, Eclipse S. and Irish Champion S. - Cartier Horse of the Year. Named after St. Mark's Basilica in Venice. French-bred, he debuted in Ireland and won a maiden in his 3rd start; 3rd in the Vincent O'Brien National S. (G1), he won the Dewhurst S. (G1) to end the year. At 3 he won the Poulains, the French Derby as favorite by 1 3/4 lengths, the Eclipse S. as favorite over older horses by 3.5 lengths, and the Irish Champion S., a tight 4-runner race - 5 straight G1s. Cartier Horse of the Year and champion 3yo colt, he retired to stud in Ireland that year.
3507: A European stayer of 2022-2024 who won 8 staying G1s incl. the 19f Ascot Gold C. and 4000m Prix du Cadran; Cartier champion stayer in 2022 and 2024. Unremarkable early - a maiden from 2 at 2, an allowance from 2 at 3 - he blossomed at 4, winning 3 straight to the Ascot Gold C., then the Goodwood C., Irish St Leger and Prix du Cadran - 4 straight staying G1s, champion stayer. Injured at 5, he ran twice, 2nd both times. At 6 he was back, winning the same 4 G1s - unbeaten in 7 - and champion stayer again.
3508: US Eclipse champion female sprinter in 2022 and 2023. A dirt 7f specialist, she won 4 G1s incl. 2 BC Filly & Mare Sprints. Debuting at 3, she first won that autumn, then kept winning: at 4, 5 straight to the Ballerina H., her first G1, then the BC Filly & Mare Sprint - champion female sprinter. At 5 she won the Madison S. for a 3rd G1; 3rd in the Derby City Distaff S. ended 7 straight, but she won the Bed o' Roses S. (G2), then the BC Filly & Mare Sprint again by 2 3/4 lengths, and retired: 9 wins from 12, beaten only twice into 2nd and once into 3rd.
3509: Winner of a 2nd straight BC Dirt Mile (G1) at 5 in 2023, Eclipse Horse of the Year. Named "Cody's Wish" for Cody, a boy in a wheelchair battling a genetic disease, whom the colt adored. Debuting late in June at 3, he needed 4 tries to win, then blossomed at 4: the Westchester S. (G3), the Forego S. for his first G1, and the BC Dirt Mile, outfighting Cyberknife. At 5 he won the Churchill Downs S. and Metropolitan H.; 3rd in the Whitney S., he won the Vosburgh S. (G2), then beat National Treasure by a nose in a fierce duel for a 2nd BC Dirt Mile, his last race. Cody watched it, and passed away soon after, as if at peace.
3510: America's sprint king of 2022-2023, Eclipse champion sprinter both years. Debuting late in September at 3, winless in 2, he first won in his 2nd start at 4, then soared: 4 straight to the Vosburgh S. (G2) easily, then the BC Sprint - champion sprinter. Into 5 he won the Riyadh Dirt Sprint (G3), True North S. (G2) and A G Vanderbilt H. (G1) - 8 straight. 2nd to Gunite in the Forego S., he beat Gunite in the BC Sprint - champion sprinter again - and retired.
3511: A US horse who won the 2024 Dubai World Cup (G1). 5th on debut in October at 2, after 6 months off he won in spring at 3, then just one allowance from 3 more. At 4 he won the Pat O'Brien S. (G2). Moving to Dubai at 5, 7th in the Al Shindagha Sprint (G3), he won the Burj Nahaar (G3). In the Dubai World Cup, with 4 Japanese runners incl. Ushba Tesoro and Derma Sotogake, he was 6th choice in JRA betting, but led from a fine start, quickened on the far turn and drew away, beating Ushba Tesoro by 8.5 lengths for his first G1.
3512: A Hong Kong gelding in short races from 2022 to 2024, winner of the Hong Kong Mile and Queen's Silver Jubilee C. (G1s), plus Dubai's Al Quoz Sprint (G1). Debuting at 3 in 2020/21, he won 2 straight; in 2021/22 he was 2nd in the Classic Mile, won the Classic C. and was 2nd in the Hong Kong Derby. On the mile path, he beat champion Golden Sixty in the 2022/23 Hong Kong Mile for his first G1. Dropping to sprints from 2023/24, he won the Queen's Silver Jubilee C., then the Al Quoz Sprint in Dubai in record time. 2nd in the Chairman's Sprint Prize (G1) and Premier C. (G3), he has been winless since.
3513: Winner of the 2022 Coronation S. and Jacques le Marois (G1s), Cartier champion 3yo filly. Brilliant from her June debut at 2, she won 3 straight to the May Hill S. (G2), then the Fillies' Mile (G1) - champion 2yo filly. At 3 she started late, in June's Coronation S., winning by 4 3/4 lengths; 2nd in the Falmouth S., she won the Jacques le Marois. 6th in the QEII S., still champion 3yo filly. At 4 she was even better, winning the Jacques le Marois, Sun Chariot S. and BC Filly & Mare Turf - 3 straight G1s. At 5, 3rd bidding for a 3rd Jacques le Marois, she has been winless this year.
3514: Winner of 3 G1s incl. the 2023 BC Distaff, Eclipse champion older mare. Winning her debut in April at 3, she kept missing after. At 4 she improved, winning 3 straight, the Shawnee S. (G3), the Delaware H. (G2), then the Personal Ensign S., Spinster S. and BC Distaff - straight to the top, champion older mare. At 5 she won the La Troienne S. (G1) - 4 straight G1s - then lost the Ogden Phipps S. by a head; she won the Molly Pitcher S. (G3), lost the Personal Ensign S. by a head again, and won the Spinster S. easily for a 5th G1.
3515: He swept French racing in 2023, unbeaten in 6 incl. the French Derby and Arc - Cartier Horse of the Year. From the first crop of Frankel's son Cracksman, he gave his sire a big title at once. Irish-bred, he debuted in France at 3 under Cristian Demuro, won easily, then an allowance and the Prix de Suresnes (L). 3rd choice in the French Derby, he swept past hot favorite Big Rock in the straight. Hot favorite in the Prix Guillaume d'Ornano (G2), he won by 3/4 length with ease. Arc favorite at last, he won by 1 3/4 lengths. A Japan Cup clash with Japan's champion Equinox was hoped for, but he retired after the Arc. Cartier Horse of the Year and champion 3yo colt, he went to stud in France.
3516: A filly who won the 2024 Arc (G1). Winning her debut in September at 2, she kept missing at 3: 2nd and 3rd, then 2nd by half a length to Savethelastdance in the Irish Oaks, 4th in the Yorkshire Oaks, 2nd in the Stand C. (L) and by a neck in the British Champions Fillies & Mares. At 4 she found her form, winning 2 straight to the Pretty Polly S. (G1), 2nd in the King George, and the Prix Vermeille. In the Arc she sat 2nd from a fine start, broke clear and never tired, winning by 1 1/4 lengths. She retired to breed after it.
3517: The 2024 Derby winner and Cartier Horse of the Year. Winning his debut in July at 2, he won the Superlative S. (G2) by 6.5 lengths and Dewhurst S. (G1) by 3.5 - in a class of his own; champion 2yo colt. 9th at 3 in the 2000 Guineas on unsuitable ground, he won the Derby easily, beat older horses in the Eclipse S., and won the International S. in record time - 3 straight G1s. For his farewell he tried the BC Classic in America, banking on dirt aptitude from his sire Justify; 2nd choice on his first dirt start, he never got going and was 8th. Still Cartier Horse of the Year, he retired to stud.
3518: A late bloomer who won the 2024 February S. (G1) at 6. Debuting in January at 3 and winning his 3rd start, he won 3 straight through 2 classes, then struggled, passing the 3-win class only in autumn at 4. At 5 he won the Onuma S. (L), but in graded races his best was 4th in the Miyako S. In the February S. at 6, as 11th choice, he edged clear from a handy spot and held on by 1 1/4 lengths - his first graded win a G1. 3rd as 3rd choice in the Kashiwa Kinen, 2nd to Lemon Pop in the Mile CS Nambu Hai and 5th to him in the Champions C. - among the best.
3519: A sprinter in G1s from 2023 to 2025 who won the Takamatsunomiya Kinen (G1) at 5 in 2024 - the first Japanese graded and G1 winner for popular Irish sire Dark Angel. Trying miles and dirt early at 3, he focused on sprints after his first win, climbing 3 classes in 3 straight; at 4 he was 3rd in his first open race, the Silk Road S. (G3). From autumn he ran in 5 straight sprint G1s: 2nd in the Sprinters S., 8th in the Hong Kong Sprint, then won the Takamatsunomiya Kinen at 5 - his first graded win a G1. 11th in Hong Kong's Chairman's Sprint Prize and 12th in the Sprinters S., he was 2nd in the Hanshin C. (G2). At 6, 6th defending the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and 10th in the Yasuda Kinen at a mile; aiming at the Sprinters S., a leg problem ended his career.
3520: The 2024 Oka Sho winner, central to that year's fillies' classics. Winning her debut in July at 2, she needed 2 tries for the 1-win class. In a Hanshin JF where 6 were closely fancied, as 5th choice she had the fastest finish and lost by a neck to Ascoli Piceno. Straight to the Oka Sho at 3, she kicked first this time and held off Ascoli Piceno for the first classic. Oaks favorite, she lost a finishing duel with 2nd choice Cervinia by half a length. Straight to the Shuka Sho, co-favorite with Cervinia, she couldn't catch her and was also passed by outsider Bond Girl, 3rd. 3rd in the Hong Kong Vase. At 4, expected to lead the older mares, she was 13th in the Osaka Hai, 8th in the Victoria Mile and 10th as 6th choice in the QEII Cup - her sparkle gone.
3521: The 2024 Satsuki Sho winner, Kizuna's first G1-winning colt, carrying hopes for grandsire Deep Impact's line. Winning his debut in November at 2, after a break he won the Kyodo News Hai (G3) at 3 from a handy spot. 2nd choice behind G1-winning filly Regaleira in the Satsuki Sho, he broke clear from a handy spot and held on by a neck. Hot Derby favorite, a double seemingly certain, he couldn't catch outsider Danon Decile, who kicked first, 2nd. Aimed at the Tenno Sho (Autumn) instead of the Kikuka Sho, he developed tendon trouble; his retirement was announced suddenly, and he went to stud the next year.
3522: A late-blooming speedster who finally won a graded race, the Victoria Mile (G1), at 6 in 2024, always racing at short trips. Winning her debut in August at 2, 3rd in her first stakes, the Artemis S. (G3), she was talented early, but then spent ages in allowances, passing the 3-win class only in spring at 4. In open class her best from 7 was 2nd in the Shin'etsu S. (L); she won the Toki S. (L) in summer at 5. After 6 months off, 7th in the Kyoto Himba S. and 6th in the Hanshin Himba S. at 6, she was 14th choice at 208-1 in the Victoria Mile, then flew from midfield to win - a stunner, and a first G1 for jockey Tsumura too. 7th in the Centaur S., she was a creditable 4th in America's BC Mile.
3523: The 2024 Derby winner. Debuting in October at 2, he won his 2nd start, then 4th to Shin Emperor in the Kyoto 2yo S. (G3). At 3 he won the Keisei Hai (G3) from a handy spot. Just before the Satsuki Sho start a leg problem was found and he was withdrawn. He made up for it in the Derby: 9th choice behind Satsuki Sho placers Justin Milano and Regaleira, he raced handily, broke clear and beat Justin Milano by 2 lengths - jockey Norihiro Yokoyama became the oldest winner of the Derby and of any JRA G1. Straight to the Kikuka Sho after a break, he faded on the far turn, 6th. In the Arima Kinen he led at a slow pace and held 3rd. At 4 he won the AJCC (G2), then the Dubai Sheema Classic (G1); 5th of 6 in England's International S., back home he was 3rd in both the Japan Cup and Arima Kinen - still a force.
3524: A dogged middle/long-distance horse who won the 2024 Takarazuka Kinen (G1) at 5. Slow to win, he took a maiden in his 9th start in June at 3, then climbed 3 classes by spring at 4. 3rd in his first stakes, the Hakodate Kinen (G3), he won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai (G2) at 5 as favorite. 3rd in the Hanshin Daishoten, in his first G1, the Tenno Sho (Spring), he closed sharply for 2nd to T O Royal. In the Takarazuka Kinen he waited at the back again and swept wide in the straight for his first G1. 11th as Kyoto Daishoten favorite, 12th in the Japan Cup.
3525: Winner of the 2024 Sprinters S. (G1) - also the first G1 for jockey Junya Nishimura. Starting on dirt, he won a maiden in January at 3 in his 4th start, then on turf sprints won the Tachibana S. (L) and was 2nd by half a length to Mozu Meimei in the Aoi S. (G3). Near-misses followed (4th Swan S., 2nd Keihan Hai), then the Silk Road S. (G3) at 4. Favorite in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, he was 10th, then found to have a fracture. Returning straight in the Sprinters S. as 9th choice, he won strongly from up front - a G1 at last. Then 11th Hong Kong Sprint, 7th Takamatsunomiya Kinen at 5, 5th in Hong Kong's Chairman's Sprint Prize, 12th Sprinters S.; still, 2nd in the Keihan Hai and a win in the Hanshin C. (G2) keep him among the top sprinters.
3526: The 2024 Kikuka Sho winner. Ordinary in spring, he blossomed over the summer and became a classic winner in autumn. Winning his debut in August at 2 and the Hyakunichiso Tokubetsu (1-win), he was 2nd to later Derby winner Danon Decile in the Keisei Hai at 3, 4th in the Satsuki Sho from the back, but 11th in the Derby. After a break he won the St. Lite Kinen (G2), closing sharply from midfield. Co-favorite with Danon Decile in the Kikuka Sho, he broke clear from midfield and won by 2.5 lengths. In the Arima Kinen the two 3yos were the top 2 choices; slow away, he was 6th. At 4, 3rd in the Nikkei Sho, then 14th Takarazuka Kinen, 5th Tenno Sho (Autumn), 10th Hong Kong Vase.
3527: Champion 2yo filly of 2024, central to the 2025 3yo fillies' races. Winning her debut in August at 2, she was 2nd by a nose to Magic Sands as 6th choice in the Sapporo 2yo S. (G3). In the Hanshin JF she moved wide at the 4th turn and swept past with a powerful finish. A classic favorite at 3, she went straight to the Oka Sho as narrow 2nd choice behind Erika Express; closing from the back, she was a neck short of Embroidery, 2nd. 2nd choice behind Embroidery in the Oaks, she broke clear from a handy spot, but outsider Come Nyack caught her by a head - 2nd again. Preparing for the Shuka Sho, she developed tendon trouble and faces a long rest.
3528: Debuting in October at 2, he won a maiden in February at 3, then was 4th in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai (G2). He won a 1-win race, then 2 more classes at 4, and the Nakayama Kimpai (G3) at 5 as 5th choice, breaking clear from a handy spot by half a length. Last (16th) in the Osaka Hai, but 3rd in the All Comers (G2).
3529: Quickly through the 1-win class at 2, at 3 he was 7th in the Kyodo News Hai and 5th in the Radio Nikkei Sho (G3s). Back in allowances, he won the 3-win class late at 3, then the Kyoto Kimpai (G3) at 4 as 8th choice, with a razor-sharp finish from midfield. Unplaced since in mile graded races.
3530: Debuting in October at 2, she won her 2nd start, then the Fairy S. (G3) at 3 as 5th choice in a field of graded maidens, edging a 4-way blanket finish by a neck. 11th in the Oka Sho, but 5th as 13th choice in the NHK Mile C.
3531: Winning his debut easily, he took on the Shinzan Kinen (G3) as 3rd choice, closing sharply from midfield to beat favorite Ecoro Bloom by 1 1/4 lengths. Favorite in the Mainichi Hai (G3), he was 2nd to front-running outsider Meisho Tabaru. 12th in the NHK Mile C.; in autumn, 4th in the Swan S. (G2), holding on from up front.
3532: Debuting in February at 3, she won 2 straight, then 14th in the Oaks (G1). Back in allowances, she won 2 classes, then the Aichi Hai (G3) at 4 as favorite, with a brilliant late run from the back. Then 14th in the Osaka Hai and 13th in the Mermaid S. (G3).
3533: After a long spell in allowances, he won his first graded race, the 2024 AJCC (G2), at 6. Debuting at 3, he won a maiden and a 1-win race from 6; winless at 4, he won 2 classes at 5. 3rd in his first open race, the Argentine Republic Hai (G2), he won the AJCC at 6. Then poor (14th Tenno Sho (Spring), 6th Hakodate Kinen, 8th Sapporo Kinen), but 2nd in the Nikkei Sho (G2) at 7 - still capable.
3534: 5th on a turf debut, he switched to dirt and was remarkably steady: 4 wins and a 2nd from 5 through the allowances, then the Negishi S. (G3) early at 4, breaking clear from a handy spot by 2.5 lengths. 2nd in the Keyaki S. (OP), he won the Enif S. (L), then the Musashino S. (G3) as 1.7-1 favorite, holding on from up front.
3535: A miler/10f horse who finally won a graded race, the Tokyo Shimbun Hai (G3), at 7. Winning his debut in October at 2, he reached the 2-win class at 3, then struggled, passing the 3-win class in summer at 5, and was unplaced in graded races. 7th choice in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai at 7, he broke clear from a handy spot to win. Racing on at 8, he won the Kyoto Kimpai.
3536: Unbeaten in 2 incl. the Kisaragi Sho (G3), winning a 4-way blanket finish by a nose as favorite. 13th in the Satsuki Sho and 17th in the Derby, finding nothing from the back, he improved to 5th in the Kikuka Sho after a 6th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai. At 4 he won Saudi Arabia's Red Sea Turf H. (G2), was 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Spring), then in France won the Prix Foy (G2) and was 5th in the Arc, best of the Japanese - a fruitful trip.
3537: Debuting at 3, she was soon 2nd in the Flora S. (G2), but 8th in the Oaks and Rose S. After the 3-win class, she was 4th in the Turquoise S. (G3), then won the Kyoto Himba S. (G3) at 4 as 2nd choice, beating favorite Namura Clair by a neck.
3538: At 3 he won 4 straight from a maiden to the 3-win class. In open class at 4, after near-misses (4th Kochi S. (L), 3rd May S. (OP)), he won the Cepheus S. (OP). At 5 he won the Kokura Daishoten (G3), breaking clear from a handy spot and holding them off. 10th in the Osaka Hai, but 2nd by a neck in the Chukyo Kinen (G3).
3539: After winning his debut in August at 2, he kept placing in allowances, passed the 3-win class in spring at 4 and was 3rd in the Epsom C. (G3). He won the Rigel S. (L), then the Nakayama Kinen (G2) at 5, beating G1 winners Sol Oriens and Geoglyph and previous winner Hishi Iguazu. 5th as an outsider in the Tenno Sho (Autumn).
3540: Debuting in August at 2, she won her 2nd start. In the Hanshin JF, jockey Manami Nagashima's first G1 ride, she was 7th as 9th choice. Ridden by Yutaka Take from the Tulip Sho (G2) at 3, she won it, then closed from last for 4th in the Oka Sho and 6th in the Oaks.
3541: A 2024 classic standout. Debuting early in June at 2, he won a maiden in his 4th start; his next win, stepping up at 3, was the Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen (G2) as 6th choice of 11, breaking clear early from a handy spot - the first graded win for his sire Al Ain's foals. 2nd in the Satsuki Sho and 6th in the Derby, but 14th as 3rd choice in the Kikuka Sho. At 4, 3rd in the AJCC, then 8th Osaka Hai, 12th Tenno Sho (Autumn), 9th Japan Cup; then 2nd as an outsider in the Arima Kinen, a reminder of his class.
3542: Winning her debut in July at 2, she was 15th in the Oka Sho and 18th in the Shuka Sho at 3. At 4 she won the 3-win class, then led all the way in the Nakayama Himba S. (G3). 5th in the Queen S., but 13th in the Victoria Mile and 16th in the QEII Cup.
3543: Talented early: 1st in the Fukushima 2yo S. (OP), 4th in the Chukyo 2yo S. (OP). At 3, 11th choice in the Fillies' Revue (G2), she led all the way, holding off hot favorite Corazon Beat by 3/4 length. 5th in the Oka Sho; sprinting since, 4th Aoi S., 11th Keeneland C.
3544: Winning her only start at 2, at 3 she was 5th in a 1-win race, then won the Flower C. (G3), breaking clear from a handy spot. 14th in the Oaks; in autumn, 2nd in the Shion S. and 6th in the Shuka Sho, closing well from the back, just behind the 4th-place fight.
3545: Unbeaten in 2, 8th as 3rd choice in the Asahi Hai FS. At 3, 7th choice in the Falcon S. (G3), he flew from last with a finish of his own. Unplaced in the NHK Mile C. and Keeneland C., he won the Swan S. (G2) with another late run. At 4, 4th in the UAE's Al Quoz Sprint, 13th in Hong Kong's Chairman's Sprint Prize; 6th as 13th choice in the Sprinters S.
3546: Unbeaten in his debut and the Hiiragi Sho (1-win) at 2, he won the Spring S. (G2) at 3 as favorite, breaking clear from up front. Skipping the Satsuki Sho, he was 9th as 3rd choice in the Derby, swamped. Favorite over older horses in the Mainichi Okan, he won from up front. At 4 he won the Nakayama Kinen (G2), then 7th as Osaka Hai favorite and 12th in the Yasuda Kinen. Switching to dirt, he was 2nd in the Mile CS Nambu Hai, then 11th in the Champions C.
3547: A middle/long-distance horse who won his first graded race, the Nikkei Sho (G2), at 5. Winning the 2-win class late at 3, winless at 4, he passed the 3-win class early at 5, then won the Nikkei Sho, closing from the back with the fastest finish, and the Meguro Kinen (G2). In G1s: 11th Takarazuka Kinen, 10th Japan Cup.
3548: Always on dirt, he won a 1-win race in spring at 3 and was a close 4th in his first stakes, the Unicorn S. (G3). Passing the 3-win class late at 3, he struggled in open class (16th March S., 7th Musashino S.), then won the Pollux S. (OP) at 5 and the March S. (G3) - a graded winner at last.
3549: Unbeaten in 2 and favorite in the Kobe Shimbun Hai (G2), he raced mostly around 2000m but kept missing, and switched to the mile at 5. He won the New Year S. (L), then the Lord Derby CT (G3). 13th in the Yasuda Kinen, then 14th Sekiya Kinen, 16th Fuji S.
3550: Debuting in October at 2, 3rd on debut, he won a maiden by 4 lengths at 1.5-1. 2nd in the Shinzan Kinen (G3) at 3, holding on from up front, he won the NZT (G2) as 3rd choice, edging clear of Bond Girl by 3/4 length. A fracture then sidelined him.
3551: At 2 he won a 2000m maiden and ran in the Kyoto 2yo S. and Hopeful S. Switching to the mile at 3, he won a 1-win race and the Arlington C. (G3) as favorite with a fine late run. 7th in the NHK Mile C., 9th Sekiya Kinen, 7th Keisei Hai AH.
3552: Climbing steadily - 1-win class at 3, 2-win at 4, 3-win at 5 - he turned to graded races at 6. 7th in the Tokai S., he won the Antares S. (G3), closing sharply from midfield. Steady since: 6th Heian S., 5th Miyako S.
3553: Passing the 3-win class early at 4, she was 3rd in the Hanshin Himba S. and Queen S. At 5, favorite by default in a wide-open Fukushima Himba S. (G3), she won. 2nd in the Kokura Kinen, but 9th in the QEII Cup.
3554: She won her debut in August at 2 sweeping wide, then stalled in the 1-win class; stepping up at 3 she won the Flora S. (G2) as 2nd choice by a length from a handy spot. 9th in the Oaks, 12th straight into the Shuka Sho.
3555: Debuting at 3, he won a maiden and a 1-win race, then the Aoba Sho (G2) as 2nd choice, holding off the charge from up front. In the Derby he sat 2nd and led early but was caught, 7th. Preparing for the Arima Kinen after a break, he developed tendon trouble and is resting again.
3556: Raced hard at 2 with 6 starts, incl. a 4th as an outsider in the Asahi Hai FS. At 3, after 2 listed races, he won the Kyoto Shimbun Hai (G2) as 8th choice, staying on from up front. 10th in the Derby; 2nd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, then tendon trouble forced a rest.
3557: A sprint name of 2024-2025: winner of the Takamatsunomiya Kinen (G1), and 2nd in Hong Kong's Chairman's Sprint Prize and England's Queen Elizabeth II Jubilee S. (both G1). Debuting in spring at 3, he won 4 of 5 to the 3-win class by spring at 4, then was injured for about 10 months. Back at 5 he blossomed: the Shunrai S. (L), Hakodate Sprint S. (G3) and Keeneland C. (G3) - 3 straight. 7th as Sprinters S. favorite, 3rd in the Hong Kong Sprint. At 6 he won the Takamatsunomiya Kinen, his first G1, then was 2nd in both overseas G1s. 4th again as Sprinters S. favorite and 9th in Hong Kong, but champion sprinter for his year's work.
3558: Talented early, 3rd in the Artemis S. (G3) at 2, she then kept missing, winning a 1-win race only at 4. After the 2-win class she led all the way in the Mermaid S. (G3), holding a 2-length lead - also jockey Manami Nagashima's first graded win. 4th in America's BC Distaff. At 5, 4th in the Fukushima Himba S., 5th in the Victoria Mile; 10th in a 2nd BC Distaff, her last race.
3559: Winning his 2nd start at 2 and a 1-win race early at 3, he was 6th in his first stakes, the Arlington C., 2nd in the Shirayuri S. (L), then won the Radio Nikkei Sho (G3), sweeping past everyone from last. In autumn, again from last, 2nd to Danon McKinley in the Swan S. and 3rd to Namura Clair in the Hanshin C. Unplaced for a while at 4, he was 2nd in the Sekiya Kinen, then won the Swan S.
3560: Debuting at 2, she won her 3rd start and a 1-win race at 3, then turned to sprints. 2nd in the Marguerite S. (L), she won the Aoi S. (G3), leading and drawing clear, then led all the way in the Kitakyushu Kinen (G3). 13th as Centaur S. favorite, 8th in the Sprinters S. At 4 she won the Ibis Summer Dash (G3) and raced abroad: 5th in the UAE's Al Quoz Sprint, 10th in America's BC Sprint.
3561: Winning a maiden and 1-win race at 2, winless at 3, he climbed slowly: 2-win class at 4, 3-win at 5. 2nd in his first open race, the Metropolitan S. (L), he won the Tanabata Sho (G3) as 2nd choice by 2 lengths with a sharp late run from midfield. 5th in the Niigata Kinen, then tendon trouble ended his career.
3562: He debuted by a huge margin at 2, then at 3 won 3 classes as a 1.2-1.3 favorite every time. Unbeaten in 4, he was hot 1.7-1 favorite in the Procyon S. (G3) and won by 3 lengths from up front - 5 straight. Then 6th in the Nagoya Daishoten (JpnIII) and 10th on turf in the Kokura Daishoten (G3) at 5, before winning the Tokai S. (G3) that summer. (That Tokai S. inherited the old Procyon S. conditions, while the old Tokai S. (G2) became the Procyon S. (G2) that year.)
3563: He won his June debut at 2 by a wide margin, then the Hakodate 2yo S. (G3) as favorite, breaking clear powerfully from a handy spot - a graded win for a 4th straight Kitasan Black crop. Skipping Japan's year-end G1s, he went for the BC Juvenile Turf (G1) in America; with a perfect trip on the rail into the straight, he found nothing, 9th of 12.
3564: At 3, 2nd in the Spring S. (G2), he was 17th in the Satsuki Sho and 6th in the Derby. At 4, 3rd in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai, he won the Tomoe Sho (OP) and Hakodate Kinen (G3). 2nd in the Mainichi Okan, he led and held 3rd to Do Deuce in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). At 5, 2nd in the Kinko Sho and Mainichi Okan - a leading middle-distance runner.
3565: Talented early, 4th in the Asahi Hai FS at 2. He climbed steadily at 3 and 4, winning the Cassiopeia S. (L) in autumn at 4. At 5, 4th in the Kokura Daishoten, he won the Chukyo Kinen (G3) from a handy spot. 11th in the Mile CS, he won the Nakayama Kimpai (G3) at 6.
3566: Winning her 4th start at 2, a 1-win race in spring at 3 and the Sweet Pea S. (L) - 3 straight - she was 12th in the Oaks, then won the Queen S. (G3) by a head in a 5-way finish. 9th in the Shuka Sho, 8th in the Challenge C.
3567: A whirlwind in the 2024 3yo dirt crop. Unbeaten in 2, 3rd in the Unicorn S. (G3), he won the Leopard S. (G3), then was 2nd to Forever Young in the Japan Dirt Classic (JpnI) - suddenly top class. He won the Nagoya Daishoten (JpnIII); 3rd as February S. favorite at 4, he then won the Antares S. (G3), Teio Sho (JpnI) and JBC Classic (JpnI) as hot favorite each time, crushing veterans Meisho Hario and Wilson Tesoro in the JBC Classic - firmly at the top of dirt racing.
3568: Reaching open class in autumn at 4, he was 3rd in the Kyoto Kimpai (G3) at 5. 10th in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and Milers C., he bounced back in the Sekiya Kinen (G3) as 3rd choice, leading all the way for his first graded win.
3569: Winning the 2-win class early at 4, he struggled in the 3-win class (2nd, 3rd, 4th), reaching open class only at 6. He won his first open race, the Fukushima Minpo Hai (L), was 5th in the Niigata Daishoten and Tanabata Sho, then won the Kokura Kinen (G3) with a fine late run from the back.
3570: Debuting at 3, she passed the 3-win class late at 4. 9th in her first stakes, the Kyoto Himba S. (G3), at 5, she kept losing, then won the CBC Sho (G3) as 6th choice, edging clear from 3rd. 2nd in the Keisei Hai AH; late at 6 she won the Turquoise S. (G3).
3571: 2nd choice on her June debut at 2, she broke clear from up front with the fastest finish. 6th choice in the Niigata 2yo S. (G3), she moved up on the far turn, stayed on, and held off Court Alicien by half a length - her sire Bago's first graded winner in 3 years.
3572: A noted 2025 3yo miler. Unbeaten in 2 to the Sapporo 2yo S. (G3), he was 16th as 2nd choice in the Hopeful S. Straight to the Satsuki Sho at 3, he was 6th as 16th choice, then focused on the mile: 3rd choice in the NHK Mile C., his big finish put him in a 3-way photo, a head behind Panja Tower in 2nd. 10th in the Fuji S., 8th in the Mile CS.
3573: At 2 she was 2nd to Liberty Island as an outsider in the Hanshin JF; at 3, 6th in the Oka Sho and 5th in the Oaks - top class. After heavy defeats, she was 3rd in the Nakayama Himba S. at 4, then won the Niigata Kinen (G3) as an outsider, sitting 2nd and holding off Seleccion by a nose. 4th to Stunning Rose in the QEII Cup.
3574: She won her debut from 2nd, drawing clear. The Kokura 2yo S. (G3) that year was run at Chukyo over 1200m due to a schedule change; narrow favorite, she sat 3rd, broke clear and held off Craspedia by 3/4 length. 2nd choice in the Keio Hai 2yo S. (G2), she found nothing, 8th.
3575: Debuting late at 2, she won a newcomer race and a 1-win race early at 3. 4th in the Flora S. (G2) and 9th on dirt in the Kanto Oaks, she won the Shion S. (G2) in autumn, breaking clear from 2nd and holding off Mia Nero by a neck. 5th to Cervinia in the Shuka Sho.
3576: A fancied filly in the 2024 classics. Winning a maiden late at 2, she won the Queen C. (G3) at 3. 8th in the Oka Sho, 4th to Cervinia in the Oaks; in autumn she won the Rose S. (G2). 3rd choice in the Shuka Sho, she stumbled at the start, perhaps hurting a leg, and was last (15th). Still highly rated, at 4 she won the Kinko Sho (G2), then lost the Victoria Mile by a neck to Ascoli Piceno. 9th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn).
3577: Winner of the 2025 Takarazuka Kinen (G1). Winning a maiden late at 2 and a 1-win race at 3, he won the Mainichi Hai (G3) by 6 lengths. 17th as 4th choice in the Satsuki Sho; scratched lame from the Derby. He won the Kobe Shimbun Hai (G2), but burned out fighting for the lead in the Kikuka Sho, 16th. At 4, 11th in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai, 5th in the Dubai Turf, then he won the Takarazuka Kinen as 7th choice, leading all the way and drawing clear - a G1. In the Tenno Sho (Autumn) he led and held 6th, just behind the fight for 2nd.
3578: Favorite on his July debut at 2, he broke clear from a handy spot and beat Hishi Aman by a neck, 5 lengths clear of the rest - a two-horse match. 2nd choice of 7 in the Saudi Arabia Royal C. (G3), he was held up at the back from a fine start, swung wide at the top of the straight and swept past the duelling leaders to win by a length.
3579: An early G1 runner (5th Hopeful S. at 2, 11th Satsuki Sho at 3), but his only open win was the Hagi S. (L) at 2, and he kept just missing until 6. 2nd in the Meguro Kinen (G2) in May at 6, he won the Kyoto Daishoten (G2) as 8th choice of 11, outfighting Deep Bond by a head. 2nd choice in the Stayers S. (G2), he held off Sil Blonde. At 7, 7th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), 12th Takarazuka Kinen; in Australia, 23rd of 24 in the Melbourne Cup.
3580: Last in the Hopeful S. (G1) late at 2, she turned to dirt stakes at 3, winning the Bluebird C. (JpnIII), 2nd in the Haneda Hai (JpnI) and 3rd in the Tokyo Derby (JpnI) of the 3yo dirt Triple Crown. 4th in the Marine C., she won the JBC Ladies' Classic (JpnI), leading all the way and drawing 4 lengths clear. At 4, near-misses (2nd Queen Sho, 3rd Empress Hai), then she won the JBC Ladies' Classic again as 7th choice.
3581: Racing on turf from July at 2, he never contended in 3 starts, then switched to dirt, won a maiden, a 1-win race at 3, and the Kumotori Sho, leading all the way. 8th as 2nd choice in the Haneda Hai; poor since (14th Procyon S., 8th Leopard S.).
3582: Debuting at Mombetsu in June at 2, he won 2 straight, Kawasaki's Kamakura Kinen in October, and was 3rd to Forever Young in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun (JpnI). Moving to Oi at 3, he won the Keihin Hai (JpnII) by 7 lengths, but a fracture ruled him out of the Haneda Hai and Tokyo Derby; back for the Japan Dirt Classic (JpnI), he was 7th. At 4 at Funabashi he won steadily, then was 3rd in the JBC Classic, behind JRA stars Mikki Fight and Meisho Hario but best of the local horses.
3583: After struggling with the JRA, he moved to Kawasaki and blossomed, winning the Kawasaki Kinen (JpnI) at 7. With the JRA he won the 2-win class at 3, the 3-win class and Uzumasa S. (OP) at 4, then stalled and moved to Kawasaki in summer at 5. 5th in the Tokyo Daishoten and Kawasaki Kinen, at 7 he led all the way in the Kawasaki Kinen and won a 3-way finish - his first G1-level win. 4th in Korea's Korea C. (G3), 2nd in the Urawa Kinen (JpnII). At 8 he won Oi's Oi Kinen, then was unplaced in graded races and retired after a 3rd in the Katsushima Okan.
3584: Winner of the 2024 Haneda Hai, first leg of the 3yo dirt Triple Crown. Winning his June debut at 2, 3rd in the Platanus Sho (1-win), he won the Cattleya S. (OP). 2nd in the Kumotori Sho at 3 earned a Haneda Hai place; favorite there, he sat handy, and in a straight duel with front-running Ammo Sierra won by a length - a G1. A leg problem then ruled him out of the later legs and he rested.
3585: Beaten twice on turf, he switched to dirt, won a maiden late at 2, a 1-win race at 3 and the Violet S. (OP), then his first stakes, the Hyogo Championship (JpnII), as favorite under Joao Moreira, leading all the way and winning by 3 lengths. 2nd in the Hokkaido Sprint C., 3rd in Sonoda's Hyogo Gold T. At 4 he won Oi's Tokyo Sprint (JpnIII).
3586: Winning her November debut at 2, she broke a bone and rested long, then came back in June at 3 on a tear: 3 straight to the 3-win class, the Aldebaran S. (OP) at 4, the Empress Hai (JpnII) and Breeders' Gold C. (JpnIII) - unbeaten in 7. Sent to America for the BC Distaff, she was scratched. At 5 she won the Queen Sho (JpnIII); 2nd in the Empress Hai, 3rd in the Breeders' Gold C., she retired after a 3rd in the JBC Ladies' Classic (JpnI).
3587: Winner of the 2024 Tokyo Derby (JpnI). Winning a 1-win race late at 2, he won the Hyacinth S. (L) and Unicorn S. (G3) at 3 - 3 straight - then the Tokyo Derby as favorite by 6 lengths, surging from a handy spot. 4th as 2nd choice in the Japan Dirt Classic. At 4, 6th Saudi Cup, 9th Dubai World Cup, 6th Teio Sho; then 3rd in Korea's Korea C. and in the Champions C. - still a dirt G1 force.
3588: Debuting in August at 2, she won her 2nd start, rested 6 months, and needed 3 tries for the 1-win class at 3. Favorite in her first stakes, the Kanto Oaks, she led throughout and drew away with the fastest finish to win by 7 lengths - also a first graded win for 2nd-year jockey Taguchi. 6th Marine C., 13th Brazil C. (L).
3589: At 2 he placed on both surfaces: 2nd in the JBC 2yo Yushun (JpnIII), 3rd in the Hopeful S. (G1). At 3 he won the Wakakoma S. (L) on turf, but after 9th in the Satsuki Sho and 12th in the Derby he switched to dirt, winning the Kozukata Sho (JpnII), 3rd in the Japan Dirt Classic (JpnI), then the Miyako S. (G3). At 4, 2nd in the February S., 3rd in the Kawasaki Kinen, he won the Nagoya GP (JpnII), then 5th back on turf in the Arima Kinen - truly versatile.
3590: A dirt miler who finally won a graded race, the Oval Sprint, at 7. Stabled in Hokkaido before his debut, he never raced there and moved to Funabashi, winning 13 local races by 5. Trying JRA-local stakes from 6, he was 2nd in the Sakitama Hai and Oval Sprint, then won the Oval Sprint at 7.
3591: Debuting at 3, she won a newcomer race as 13th choice, then 2 classes, and her first stakes, the Marine C. (JpnIII), as 2nd choice, flying past as hot favorite Ammo Sierra faded to win by 5 lengths. In the JBC Ladies' Classic, Ammo Sierra led all the way, and she was 3rd. At 4 she won the Hyogo Jo-o Hai (JpnIII) and Empress Hai (JpnII); 2nd in the Ladies' Prelude, she was 2nd again as Ammo Sierra led throughout in the JBC Ladies' Classic.
3592: Winless on turf early, he switched to dirt, won a 1-win race by the end of 2 and the Shoryu S. (OP) at 3. 2nd in the Hyogo Championship, he won the Hokkaido Sprint C., then the Tokyo Hai, and was a close 2nd in the JBC Sprint - a sprint force.
3593: At 3 he placed in stakes (4th Kyodo News Hai, Arlington C., Kobe Shimbun Hai). Back in allowances, favorite every time but often beaten, he reached open class in spring at 5. 3rd in the Sekiya Kinen, he won the Fuji S. (G2); 5th choice in the Mile CS, he closed too late, 10th.
3594: Ridden by Christophe Lemaire, she was a 1.2-1 favorite on debut and won in commanding style, then the Artemis S. (G3), breaking clear from a handy spot. Favorite in the Hanshin JF, a new star in waiting, she was down 12kg and found nothing, 16th.
3595: Winning her debut in August at 2, she faded from the lead to 3rd as Rindo Sho favorite (1-win), then won the Fantasy S. (G3) on rain-sodden bad ground, edging a 5-way finish by a nose. 17th in the Hanshin JF.
3596: Winner of the 2025 NHK Mile C. (G1), giving his sire Tower of London a G1 from his first crop. Hot favorite on his September debut at 2, he won from a handy spot, then the Keio Hai 2yo S. (G2) as 8th choice, edging Meiner Ticket by a neck in a two-horse duel. 12th as 4th choice in the Asahi Hai FS; 4th as Falcon S. favorite at 3. 9th choice in the NHK Mile C., he won a blanket finish by a head, then the Keeneland C. (G3). In Australia's Golden Eagle he was 5th of 16.
3597: 6th on debut in September at 2, she won a maiden, then the Daily Hai 2yo S. (G2) as favorite, joining the lead at the 4th turn from midfield and holding off Dragon Boost by half a length - a precious graded win for Yuichi Fukunaga's stable in its first year. 11th in the Hanshin JF.
3598: A 2000m stakes regular who finally won the Fukushima Kinen (G3) at 7. At 4 he won 3 straight allowances and the Cepheus S. (OP); his best in stakes were 3rds in the Fukushima Kinen at 4 and 5 and the Kinko Sho at 6. At 7, at his 3rd try, he won the Fukushima Kinen.
3599: The 2025 Derby winner, from Kitasan Black's 4th crop - his 3rd JRA G1 winner after Equinox and Sol Oriens. Unbeaten in 3 at 2 incl. the Hopeful S. (G1), he was the classic favorite. Straight to the Satsuki Sho at 3 as 1.5-1 favorite, he was caught by Museum Mile, 2nd. Derby favorite again, he broke clear and never let anyone get near him. In France he won the Prix du Prince d'Orange (G3), then was the best-fancied of 3 Japanese in the Arc, but faded to 14th. Back home, 2nd choice behind crop-mate and Tenno Sho winner Masquerade Ball, 4th in the Japan Cup.
3600: A 2025 classic standout. Unbeaten in 3 at 2 incl. the Kyoto 2yo S. (G3), all as favorite. A classic contender at 3, 11th in the Satsuki Sho, he was 5th to Croix du Nord in the Derby. He won the Kobe Shimbun Hai (G2) with a brilliant late run, then was 2nd to Energico as 2nd choice in the Kikuka Sho.
3601: Winning his 3rd start, he won 3 sprints straight: the Fukushima 2yo S. (OP), Chukyo 2yo S. (OP) and Marguerite S. (L) at 3. Winless in stakes (3rd Aoi S., 10th Centaur S., 5th Keihan Hai), at 4 he was 2nd in the Ocean S. and 3rd in the Hakodate Sprint S., then won the Keihan Hai (G3) as favorite.
3602: Winning a maiden in his 8th start, he took 1.5 years to clear the allowances, in autumn at 4. In staying stakes: 4th Stayers S., then at 5, 3rd Diamond S., 2nd Hanshin Daishoten, 5th Tenno Sho (Spring). In Australia, 13th in the Caulfield Cup, then 2nd by a nose in the Melbourne Cup.
3603: Winning a newcomer race in September at 2, she won the Edelweiss Sho (JpnIII), leading in the straight and drawing clear. 2nd choice in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun (JpnI), she moved early to lead at the 4th turn and held off Happy Man - the first filly dirt champion in 8 years. At 3, 7th in Saudi Arabia's Saudi Derby (G3), then on her first turf start in the Hakodate Sprint S. (G3) she collapsed in the race with cardiac arrest, ending her short life.
3604: Debuting at Mombetsu with 3 wins and 3 seconds from 6, he was 5th choice of 10 in the JBC 2yo Yushun (JpnIII), but saving ground at the back, kicked from a perfect spot and won by 3 lengths as the leaders faded - a first graded title for his sire Le Vent Se Leve's first crop. 3rd to Myriad Love in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun, 4th in the Keihin Hai at 3, he then swept the Hokkaido Triple Crown - Hokuto Hai, Hokkai Yushun, Okan Sho - all as favorite, only the 8th to do so. 10th in the Japan Dirt Classic (JpnI).
3605: Winning a maiden through the 2-win class at 3 and the 3-win class early at 4, he won his 2nd open race, the Radio Nippon Sho (OP). 2nd as 11th choice in his first stakes, the Miyako S., he won the Urawa Kinen (JpnII), leading at the top of the straight and drawing away. At 5 he won the Heian S. (G3), 2nd in the Teio Sho and 3rd in the Tokyo Daishoten.
3606: Debuting in June at 2, he won a 1200m dirt newcomer race, bursting clear from midfield. 4th in the Yamaboshi Sho (1-win), he won the Hyogo Junior GP as favorite, catching the leader at the 4th turn and pulling away with a superior finish.
3607: At 3 he won the Wakaba S. (L), but was 16th in the Satsuki Sho and 15th in the Derby. On dirt he won the Green Channel C. (L); back on turf from autumn at 5, he won the Andromeda S. (L), then the Chunichi Shimbun Hai (G3) as 3rd choice, leading all the way.
3608: Winning a dirt maiden, she was 13th on turf in the Queen C. (G3), then climbed 3 dirt classes. Favorite in her first dirt stakes, the Capella S. (G3), late at 3, she broke clear from midfield and held off late closers like Kurojishi Joe. At 4, 3rd in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh Dirt Sprint (G2), 5th Tokyo Sprint, 4th Oval Sprint.
3609: Unbeaten in 2, 4th in the Asahi Hai FS - talented early. On dirt from 3, he reached open class in January at 4 and won listed races, but not stakes. 2nd in the Kashiwa Kinen at 6 and 7, he won the JBC Sprint in autumn at 7 - his first graded win a G1.
3610: Debuting in January at 3, she won a newcomer race and raced at a mile, reaching open class with the Hakata S. (3-win) in June at 4. In her first stakes, the Queen S. (G3), she held on for a close 3rd; she won the Cassiopeia S. (L), then the Turquoise S. (G3) under top weight. At 5, 2nd in the Hanshin Himba S., 4th in the Victoria Mile, she won the Queen S. as favorite, then 6th in America's BC Mile; her retirement was then announced.
3611: Winner of the 2024 Asahi Hai FS (G1). Winning his 2nd start, he was 5th choice in the Asahi Hai FS, sat 2nd, led at the 4th turn and drew 2.5 lengths clear with a stunning finish. Top mile hope at 3, he was 1.7-1 NZT favorite but caught by a neck by Immigrant Song; NHK Mile C. favorite, he found nothing, 14th. 6th as 2nd choice in the Swan S.
3612: Rated the greatest sprinter in British racing history: 14 wins and 3 seconds from 17, incl. 2 July Cups and 2 Nunthorpe S. Rivals so feared him that most of his races had just 3 runners. 2nd on his April debut at 2, he won 5 by year-end, 4 easily - Timeform's top 2yo at 133. At 3, after one run, he was 2nd in the 2000 Guineas on his first try at a mile, then focused on sprints, winning 4 straight incl. the King's Stand S. and July C. - Timeform's best again at 138. At 4 he won 4 of 5, repeating in the July C., King George S. and Nunthorpe S., and retired. At stud he sired many sprinters, but mostly fillies, so his male line died out; his name survives in dam lines.
3613: Winner of England's stayers' triple crown (Gold C., Goodwood C., Doncaster C.), called Britain's greatest stayer of the 20th century. Losing his first 3 from October at 2, he won the Classic Trial S. in spring at 3, then took the staying path: the Royal Standard S., Princess of Wales's S. and St. George S. 2nd to Black Tarquin in the St Leger, he then showed his true class: the Jockey Club S. and King George VI S., then at 4 the Ormonde S. and Corporation S., and the stayers' triple crown, the first in 70 years - 7 straight - and retired. A fine sire, with St Leger winner Alcide and Fillies' Triple Crown winner Meld; Alcide's son Remand, imported to Japan, sired Opec Horse, Agnes Lady and more.
3614: Debuting in England, then moving to America, he won the Washington DC International twice - the only horse ever to do so. In England he won 3 of 6, but temperament let him down in the classics: 7th in the 2000 Guineas, 12th in the Derby. Moving to the US in autumn at 3, he gradually blossomed, winning the Suburban H. in summer at 4, the Saratoga H., and the turf Washington DC International. At 5 he won the Widener H., Gulfstream Park H. and Metropolitan H., then the Aqueduct H. and a 2nd Washington DC International - US champion handicap male - and retired. Not a great sire, but 12 stakes winners incl. Arc-winning filly San San; daughter Too Bald produced Capote, carrying his blood on.
3615: Rated among France's best racehorses of the 20th century. Winning his June debut at 2 easily, he swept the Prix Robert Papin, Prix Morny and Grand Criterium, sometimes called France's 2yo triple crown - unbeaten in 4, top-weighted at 63kg in France's Free Handicap. At 3 he won the Prix de Sevres, the Poule d'Essai des Poulains and Prix Lupin; illness kept him out of both Derbys, but back in autumn he won the Prix Royal-Oak, then the Arc easily - unbeaten again, rated 68kg, far above rival Admiral Drake. At 4, after more wins, he got loose in the streets while travelling and was 5th in the Ascot Gold C., his first defeat; 4th in the Arc, he retired. At stud, taken from France to Germany during WWII and returned after the war, he still sired Vieux Manoir, a successful sire, founding the Brantome line.
3616: A legendary 19th-century star of New Zealand and Australia, still called the greatest in Oceania's history. Like his sire Musket, he was named after a gun. Debuting in New Zealand in 1887/88 at 2, he won all 5.
