Racing in Australia from 3, he was Victoria Derby favorite but lost by a head through his jockey's complacency; his owner, who lost heavily, sold him to new Australian owners. He then won at every trip from 8f to 24f, incl. the Melbourne Cup and Sydney Cup, and won 15 straight from 4 into 5. Retiring at the end of 5, his earnings of 29,476 pounds stood as a record for over 20 years. His first crop included Victoria Derby winner Wallace; later moved to England, he sired Derby winner Spearmint, leaving his mark on European racing too.
3617: A speedster of 1948-1949, called America's fastest. At 3 in 1948 he was overshadowed by stablemate and crop-mate Triple Crown winner Citation; 2nd to him in the Kentucky Derby, he focused on sprints, winning 4 incl. the Jerome H. and Phoenix H. - champion sprinter. At 4, with Citation injured, he stepped in at middle distances, winning his first 8 incl. the Gulfstream Park H. in record time - 12 wins from 15. Beaten twice that autumn by dual classic winner Capot, he shared Horse of the Year with him. Declining after, he won 3 more by 6 and retired. Not a successful sire.
3618: Unbeaten in 15 in America in 1907 at 2 and into 3, Horse of the Year both years - the most wins by any unbeaten US champion. Debuting in May at 2, he swept through sprints, winning with ease rather than by margins, 12 of 12 incl. the Futurity S. and Champagne S. Called the greatest 2yo ever, he was Horse of the Year at 2. At 3 leg trouble kept him out about 6 months; aiming at the Belmont, he won the Withers S. a week before, then the Belmont and Tidal S., and retired. At stud in England and America for 23 years, poor fertility left just 81 foals. Not a success, but his son Neddie led to Alsab, and 3 generations on to Ack Ack, keeping his line alive.
3619: The 6th US Triple Crown winner: 16 wins, 4 seconds and a 3rd from 21. He won the Belmont by 25 lengths, the record until Secretariat 30 years later. Often 2nd early from his June debut at 2, he blossomed after summer, winning easily in record times, and took his final 2yo race, the Walden S., by 30 lengths. Unbeaten at 3, he won the Kentucky Derby, the Preakness by 8 lengths at 1.15-1, the Withers S., and the Belmont at 1.05-1 by 25 lengths. He was injured in the Belmont and never raced again. A great sire, with Kentucky Derby winner Count Turf and Belmont winner Counterpoint; his male line has faded, but as broodmare sire of Mr. Prospector's dam, his blood is everywhere.
3620: US champion 2yo colt of 1958. Debuting in April at 2, he won 3 straight to the Juvenile S., an allowance, then the Great American S., Saratoga Special S. and Hopeful S. - 7 straight. 2nd to Intentionally in the Futurity S., he won 3 more by year-end - 10 of 11, champion 2yo. At 3 he faded: inconsistent, 3rd in the Kentucky Derby and 9th in the Preakness, his first heavy loss. Just 3 stakes wins from 18 more to autumn at 4, and he retired. At stud he sired dual classic winner Riva Ridge and many stakes winners; his son First Family, imported to Japan, sired Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen winner Hoyo Boy.
3621: A legendary horse, perhaps France's greatest, and the only French-bred winner of the English Triple Crown. Ordinary at 2 with 1 win from 3, he won the 2000 Guineas as 5th choice in his first race at 3, narrowly, then the Derby as favorite. English racing then reigned supreme, and foreign-breds rarely won its big races; as the first French-bred Derby winner, he sent France into raptures. He won 3 straight in summer incl. the Grand Prix de Paris, then the St Leger easily - the Triple Crown. At 4 he won 5 straight to the Ascot Gold C., waiting last and winning by 40 lengths with an astonishing finish, then the Grand Prix de l'Empereur at home - 6 of 6 that year - and retired. Amid the Franco-Prussian War he failed at stud, but daughter Keepsake's line produced, 4 generations on, Ksar (sire of Tourbillon), so his blood lives on.
3622: A South African star who moved to America and became champion turf horse. Debuting in South Africa in 1966/67, he won 15 of 18 to early 1968/69 at 4, unbeatable at a mile and under; at 3 he won the Guineas triple (Royal Reserve Guineas, Cape Merriwood Guineas, South African Guineas), champion 3yo colt. Moving to the US in 1969, travel and new surroundings delayed his start 6 months, but he won an allowance easily, then the Stars & Stripes H. and Bernard Baruch H., and in autumn the 12f Sunrise H. and Man o' War S. - a stayer too. 2nd to Karabas in the Washington DC International, where Japan's Takeshiba O also ran, he was champion turf horse and retired. At stud he sired Derby winner Henbit and Kentucky Oaks winner Sun and Snow; his male line ended, but he appears in dam lines, e.g. in Ghostzapper's and Transcend's pedigrees.
3623: A 1950 US classic star, winner of the Preakness and Horse of the Year. Winning 6 of 7 at 2, at 3 he won the Wood Memorial, was 2nd to Middleground in the Kentucky Derby, then beat him in the Withers S. and Preakness. 7th to Middleground in the Belmont, he won the American Derby, Jerome H. and Jockey Club Gold C. in autumn, then the Sunset H. - champion 3yo and Horse of the Year with one classic. At 4 his only stakes win was the New York H.; at 5 he added the San Marcos H. and retired. A fair sire with 23 stakes winners; few sons succeeded, so his male line ended, but his blood survives through dams.
3624: A carrier of Man o' War's blood who extended that rare line. His best son, In Reality, led to sires Relaunch, Tiznow and Warning; Warning sired Dikat and, in Japan, G1 winners Carlton Light O and Sunningdale. Through daughter Ta Wee came Holy Bull 2 generations later. A gifted racehorse in the US from 2 to 6, he won 18 of 34, mainly at a mile and under: at 2 the Futurity S. over First Landing; at 3, 5 wins incl. the Withers S. and Jerome H. - US champion sprinter. At 5 and 6 he had great battles with dual classic winner Carry Back, 2 years younger, and won his last race, the Seminole H., by 8 lengths.
3625: US champion 3yo colt of 1962 with 6 wins incl. the Belmont S. His fierce duel with Ridan in the Travers S. is a classic, and the Jaipur S. (then ungraded, now G1) was created in his name in 1984. Winning his debut in July at 2 and the Flash S., then the Hopeful S. and Cowdin S., he won 4 of 7 at 2. Starting in April at 3, he won 2 straight, was 10th in the Preakness, his first heavy loss, then after a win took the Belmont. That summer he beat Ridan by a nose in the Travers, earning champion 3yo over Ridan, winner of the Florida Derby and Arlington Classic. Winless after, he retired after a 4th in the Seminole H. in February at 4. At stud he sired Prix Morny winner Amber Rama, later imported to Japan.
3626: A legend who was US Horse of the Year 5 years running from 1960 at 3. Effective from a mile to 16f, he stayed on top even under heavy weights; 4th in The Blood-Horse's top 100 of the 20th century. Starting after the classics at 3, he won 6 straight stakes, 3 in record time incl. the Jockey Club Gold C. - Horse of the Year without a classic run. At 4 he won the New York Handicap Triple (Metropolitan H., Suburban H., Brooklyn H.), 7 of 9. Unwell until summer at 5, he then won the Stymie H., Woodward S. and Jockey Club Gold C. by 10 lengths in record time - Horse of the Year a 3rd time. At 6 he won 8 straight from the Gulfstream Park H. to the Jockey Club Gold C. At 7 he won a 5th straight Gold C. and, after 3 straight 2nds, the Washington DC International in record time - 5 straight titles. Declining at 8 with 3 wins from 6, he lost the title, ran once at 9 and retired. A gelding, he never bred, but was much loved until his death at 26.
3627: A historic 19th-century Hungarian mare, unbeaten in 54 races across Europe, famous worldwide with countless stories told of her. Debuting in Germany in June at 2, she won all 10, 5 by over 10 lengths. At 3 she won classics incl. the Hungarian 2000 Guineas and Austrian Derby - 17 of 17, already hugely popular. At 4 she won abroad incl. England's Goodwood C. and France's Grand Prix de Deauville; in Germany's Grosser Preis von Baden she dead-heated with Prince Giles, then won the run-off easily - 15 of 15. At 5, her last year, she won all 12 under heavy weights, retiring with a Guinness record 54 unbeaten. A fine broodmare with several classic winners; daughter Budagyongye's line produced, 16 generations later, Derby and Irish Derby winner Camelot.
3628: A French horse who won the Arc in 1921 and 1922. Unusually for Bruleur's slow-maturing stock, he raced well at 2 and won 3 straight to the French Derby in spring at 3. Beaten by England's Lemonora in the Grand Prix de Paris, he won the 2nd-ever Arc in autumn over the English, defending French pride. At 4, hot Arc favorite with no foreign runners, he won easily - the first 2-time winner. 2nd in the Prix Gladiateur, perhaps too far at 6200m, he retired. At stud he sired French Derby winners Tourbillon and Thor, French Oaks winner Ukrania and more. Tourbillon succeeded at stud, siring Clarion and Partholon, whose blood is common in Japan.
3629: An Irish horse who won the 1969 Arc. Debuting in July at 2, he won his 2nd start. At 3 he went to England for the classics, but was 4th in the Derby Trial S. and Queen's Vase. He won the Oxfordshire S. that summer, then lost until the Prix du Cadran at 4, followed by the Ascot Gold C. and Leinster H. - 3 straight staying wins. Dropping back in trip for the Arc, 14th choice, he raced forward on his stamina and held on by 3/4 length, stunning the crowd. He won the November H. and retired. At stud he sired stayers Shafaraz and M-Lolshan; his male line ended, but granddaughter Malt produced Horlicks, spreading his name worldwide.
3630: A historic US champion of 1919-1920: 20 wins from 21, one crushing victory after another, once by 100 lengths. 1st in The Blood-Horse's top 100 of the 20th century. Called "Big Red" for his reddish chestnut coat, he is seen as the greatest in American racing history. At 2 he won 9 of 10, losing only the Sanford Memorial S. by half a length; the winner, Upset, is remembered as "the only horse to beat Man o' War." At 3 he won the Preakness, Withers S., Belmont S., Dwyer S. and more, many in record time - the Belmont by 20 lengths, and the Lawrence Realization S. by 100, setting an unbroken 2:40.8 record. 3 more record wins to year-end - 11 of 11 - and he retired. At stud, though his book was limited and he was champion sire only once, he sired Triple Crown winner War Admiral; War Admiral and War Relic founded his sire line. The War Relic - Intent - In Reality - Relaunch branch still holds its place in America, carrying Man o' War's blood today.
3631: Winner of the 1955 English Fillies' Triple Crown. Debuting in September at 2, she won 1 of 2. Straight to the 1000 Guineas at 3, highly rated, she won as favorite; even more fancied in the Oaks, she won by 6 lengths from Ark Royal, so easily she wasn't even blowing in the winner's photos. After the Coronation S. in summer, she rested for the St Leger; below par with a cold, she raced more patiently and won - the 8th Fillies' Triple Crown, the first in 13 years - and retired. A fine broodmare: Derby winner Charlottown and Mellay, twice champion sire in New Zealand.
3632: A US star of 1961-1964, mainly on turf, winner of 2 United Nations H. and the Washington DC International; champion turf male of 1963 at 4. Emerging at 3, he won 5 handicaps incl. the United Nations H., Trenton H. and Lexington H. At 4 he won the United Nations H. again, the Washington DC International - beating champion Kelso at his peak by half a length - the Kelly-Olympic H., Diamond State H. and more, on turf and dirt. At 5 he won 5 dirt handicaps incl. the Monmouth H., John B. Campbell H. and Widener H., and retired. A fair sire with 21 stakes winners incl. Bushongo and Mongo Queen.
3633: A French horse who won the 1948 2000 Guineas and Sussex S. At 2 he won the Champagne S. and New S. in England; at 3 he won the 2000 Guineas in a stunning record 1:35.8 and the Sussex S. - a famed speedster. He won the 7f Victoria C. at 4 and retired. A successful sire of many stakes winners incl. Milesian and Our Babu. Milesian sired Partholon, imported to Japan, where the line developed uniquely, carrying Tourbillon's line on: Partholon sired Symboli Rudolf, Mejiro Asama and more, leading Japanese racing from the 1970s to the 1990s. The male line has nearly faded, but as Mejiro McQueen is broodmare sire of Orfevre and Gold Ship, My Babu's blood lives on through dams.
3634: Raced in England, then in America from 4, where at 5 he beat Citation 4 times, all in record time. Debuting in England in May at 2, he won his 5th start; at 3 he was 9th in the 2000 Guineas, 3rd in the Derby, 8th in the St Leger. After winning the Great Foal S., he was sold to America. After about a year off, his US career began in autumn at 4; struggling at first on dirt, at 5 he hit form: the Santa Anita H. over Citation in record time, then the San Juan Capistrano H., Forty-Niners H. and Golden Gate H., beating Citation each time. Helped at first by the weights, in the Golden Gate he carried more than Citation and still won - America's best. He added the Hollywood Gold C. in record time and retired as champion handicap male. At stud, 13 stakes winners, but among Nasrullah's many fine sire sons he never stood out.
3635: The 4th English Triple Crown winner, in 1886, unbeaten in 16 - a great British horse. Debuting in October at 2, he won 3 straight incl. the Dewhurst Plate. At 3 he beat fancied Minting in the 2000 Guineas, won the Derby easily as favorite, 2 more races, and the St Leger easily - the first unbeaten Triple Crown. A breathing problem (roaring) then set in, and he retired after 3 runs at 4. At stud his fertility was low; his owner, fearing the roaring was hereditary, sold him to Argentina, then he went to America, siring few foals anywhere. Yet among his early English foals was Orme, whose line produced Teddy, founder of the Teddy line, still alive today.
3636: He ruled English sprinting in 1955 at 3, unbeaten in 8 that year, with Timeform's top rating of any age, 139 - one of Britain's best sprinters. At 2, not yet a star, he raced locally and won the Moulton S. at Newmarket, 4 wins from 7. At 3, under big weights, he won the Tetrarch S., Prince of Wales H. and Stewards' S., then the Festival S. and Gosforth Park C. Rivals so feared him that the July C. drew just 2 opponents; he won easily, then a 2-runner Diadem S. in autumn - 8 of 8 - and retired. At stud in America he sired 20 stakes winners, but was no great success, and his male line has died out.
3637: English champion 2yo of 1967 and a successful sire - the 4th straight generation of English champion sires after great-grandsire Fairway, grandsire Fair Trial and sire Petition, part of the then-dominant Fairway line. At 2 he won 3 straight incl. the Gimcrack S. and Middle Park S.; at 3 the Craven S., St. James's Palace S. and Sussex S., and he retired that year. At stud he sired Derby and Irish Derby winner Troy, Irish Derby winner English Prince and sire Pitcairn; champion sire in Britain and Ireland in 1979. Pitcairn sired Ela-Mana-Mou and others, champion sire too, and in Japan graded winners Kane Kuroshio and Soshin Hoju. No further heirs followed, and the male line has faded.
3638: Winner of the 1959 1000 Guineas and Oaks. Skipping the St Leger, she won the Yorkshire Oaks and Champion S. instead - 6 of 6 that year, rated 134 by Timeform, the best of her crop. At 4 she won the Victor Wild S., then met Derby winner Parthia in the Coronation C. as hot favorite and beat him easily - best of her generation, again rated 134, top older horse. At 5 she won 4 of 6 incl. the Coronation S. and Coronation C., and retired. As a broodmare, barren years and stillbirths left just 3 foals, all failures, but daughter Zahra built a family that produced Arc winner Zarkava 4 generations later.
3639: A legendary Australian speedster of 1929-1932, feared on his US trip as "The Red Terror" for his power and deep chestnut coat. Ordinary at 2 in 1928/29, losing often, he was transformed at 3 over middle and long trips: 4 straight from the Rosehill Guineas, then 9 straight in 1930 incl. the AJC Plate. At 4 in 1930/31 he won 14 straight incl. the Melbourne Cup; at 5, 8 more from the Underwood S. Late at 5, in 1932, he went to Mexico and won the Agua Caliente H. on his first dirt start, stunning North America. Two weeks later he suddenly died of colic and high fever; poisoning was whispered, but the truth is still unknown. His impact was such that, with a single North American start, he ranks 22nd in The Blood-Horse's top 100 of the 20th century.
3640: A great mare of 1903-1906 with 22 wins and 2 seconds from 24, winner of the Fillies' Triple Crown and, against males, the Champion S., Coronation C. and more - and an immensely influential broodmare. From her June debut at 2 she won 15 straight through the Triple Crown; 2nd in France's Prix du Conseil Municipal, she won again from her first start at 4, and retired after a 2nd in the Ascot Gold C. at 5. Winning from sprints to the 19f Jockey Club C., she had both speed and stamina. Her 10 foals did little racing, but 4 daughters bred on, and her female line produced Brigadier Gerard, Northern Taste, Luthier and many more - founder of a worldwide family.
3641: Winner of the 1963 Irish Derby, King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S. and more; a fine sire, known in Japan as broodmare sire of Mill George. Little noticed until spring at 3, he emerged with a 3rd in the Derby, then won the Irish Derby and 4 straight incl. the King George and St Leger - Timeform 137. At 4 he won 2 of 4 and retired after an unplaced Arc. At stud he sired Derby winner Morston, Irish 2000 Guineas winner Ballymore, Gold Cup winner Ragstone and more. Dying at 13, he left few foals, but as broodmare sire of Japan's champion sire Mill George, he greatly influenced Japanese racing.
3642: An English star of 1966-1967 with 11 wins from 14, rated 132 by Timeform, the best 3yo of 1967. Lowly rated and not entered for the classics, he defied that with 5 straight wins at 2 incl. the Granville S., Rous Memorial S. and Clarence House S. - the best 2yo colt. At 3 he won the St. James's S., St. James's Palace S. and Sussex S., then the QEII S. by 10 lengths, and beat dual classic winner Royal Palace in the Champion S. - top of his crop - and retired. At stud: Oaks winner Polygamy, French Derby winner Roi Lear, Grand Prix de Paris winner Valiant Heart and more.
3643: A French winner of the 1963 Derby. A positive drug test afterward put the result on hold, causing a furor in both countries; a later retest proved negative, and he was confirmed as Derby winner. At 2 he won 2 of 5 in France. At 3 he won the Poulains and Prix de Guiche, then went for the Derby, winning by 6 lengths; cleared over 4 months later. In autumn he won the Prix Royal-Oak, France's final classic - Timeform 136. At 4 he won the Prix Ganay and Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud in France and the Coronation C. in England - 3 of 3 - and retired. At stud: Irish Oaks winner Olwyn, Give Thanks, Benson & Hedges Gold C. winner Relkino and more.
3644: A great English sprinter of the 1950s who won 4 sprints twice each - Cork & Orrery S., July C., King George S., Nunthorpe S. - rated 137 by Timeform. Still developing to 3, his big results were a King's Stand S. win and Nunthorpe 2nd. At 4 he blossomed, winning 6 straight incl. those 4 - top of sprinting. At 5, under heavier weights, he won all 4 again, then was 2nd conceding 32 lb in the Portland H., and retired. Not a great sire, but his few stars included sprinters Reet Lass and Village Boy; in Japan he is the third dam sire of miler Material.
3645: France's best 3yo of 1961, who also won England's King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S. and succeeded at stud. Debuting in September at 2, he won his 2nd start, then the Prix de la Salamandre and Grand Criterium - French champion 2yo. At 3, 2nd in his opener, he won the Poulains, Prix Lupin and French Derby - unbeatable at home. In the King George he outfought previous dual classic winner St. Paddy. In autumn he won the Prix Foy, was 2nd in the Arc, and retired. At stud he sired Irish Derby winner Prince Regent and Italian Derby winner Ruysdael; Ruysdael, imported to Japan, sired Tenno Sho winner Tenmei.
3646: The first horse to win both the 2000 Guineas and Irish 2000 Guineas, in 1969. Debuting in June at 2, he won the Imperial S. and Middle Park S., rated 131 in the Free Handicap. At 3, 2nd in the Greenham S., he won the 2000 Guineas by 2.5 lengths, then the Irish 2000 Guineas, and beat Habitat by half a length in an epic St. James's Palace S. Unwell, he rested; 2nd on return in the Peter Hastings S., he was 7th to Habitat in France's Prix du Moulin and retired. His best foal was Take A Reef, a top English 3yo; moved to Australia, he sired nothing notable.
3647: Winner of the 1964 Derby and Irish Derby - only the 2nd to win both, the first in 57 years. Beaten on debut at 2, he won the Irish National S. by 8 lengths, becoming a classic fancy. At 3 he won the Irish 2000 Guineas, then the Derby and Irish Derby, all as favorite. In the King George, outsider Nasram led all the way and he was 2nd; 2nd again in the Arc, lacking a finishing punch, he retired with record earnings for an Anglo-Irish horse of 153,646 pounds. He died at 9 after just 5 crops, which included Irish St Leger winner Reindeer and Irish Oaks winner Santa Tina - a fair success.
3648: The 1970 Arc winner, famed for denying Nijinsky Europe's grand slam. Debuting in August at 2, he won 1 of 4. At 3 he blossomed: 3rd in the Prix Lupin, he won the French Derby. In the Prix Royal-Oak he was promoted to 1st after first-past-the-post Hallez was demoted, but the run itself was a clear defeat, so he was 4th choice in the Arc. Hot favorite at 1.4-1 was unbeaten English Triple Crown winner Nijinsky, seen as a certainty; in a straight duel, he edged ahead by a head - famed as the first horse to beat Nijinsky. He retired after it. At stud: Prix Royal-Oak winner Henri le Balafre, Italian Oaks winner Marmolada and others.
3649: Winner of the 1902 English Fillies' Triple Crown plus the 2000 Guineas, 4th in the Derby - the only horse ever to run in all 5 English classics. Her punishing schedule began at 3: the 1000 Guineas 2 days after the 2000 Guineas; the next month the Oaks 2 days after the Derby, plus 3 more races that month incl. the St. James's Palace S. In autumn she won the St Leger - 4 English classics - and 2 days later was 2nd in the Park Hill S. At 4 she won 5 incl. the Jockey Club S. and Champion S., racing until spring at 5. Her own foals did little, but daughter Maid of the Mist was a fine broodmare, and the family flourished; 6 generations on came Speed Symboli, winner of the Tenno Sho (Spring) and Arima Kinen.
3650: A US horse who won 33 of 89 from 1935 at 2 to 1940 at 7. Unremarkable at first, he improved and finally beat Triple Crown winner War Admiral to become the best - a symbol of hope for Depression-era America, hero of books and films. At 2, raced as a form of training, he ran 35 times, needing 18 to win and winning just 5. At 3, unsettled by a stable change, he started winning, 9 from 23. At 4 he blossomed, winning 7 straight coast to coast under ever-heavier weights, then 3 more - champion handicap male. At 5 the hoped-for clash with War Admiral, a year younger, came in the Pimlico Special match race; he won by 4 lengths - Horse of the Year and the best. Racing until 7, he won his long-sought Santa Anita H. and retired. Not a successful sire, he entered the Hall of Fame in 1958 and ranks 25th in The Blood-Horse's top 100 of the 20th century.
3651: The 1951 French Derby winner and a great sire of Pharamond, Moutiers and many European Oaks winners; French champion sire in 1966, spreading the Prince Rose line worldwide. In Japan his imported sons Pharamond, Moutiers and Diatome sired stars like Kaburaya O, Tanino Moutiers and Kushiro King. His male line has faded, but he lives on as Sea-Bird's broodmare sire. On the track he won 8 of 9 to spring at 3: 2nd in his 3rd start, he won the Grand Criterium; at 3, aiming at 2000m+, he won the Prix de Guiche, Prix Greffulhe and Prix Hocquart, then the French Derby and the long Grand Prix de Paris. Aimed at the Arc, he retired injured.
3652: Unbeaten winner of the 1884 Derby, rated with contemporary St. Simon among the best of the 19th century. At 2 he won 3 minor races. Lowly rated for the Derby on his first run at 3, he dead-heated with Harvester for the win and shot to fame, then won the Gold Vase, Cesarewitch H., Newmarket Free H. and Jockey Club C. - suddenly the best. At 4 he won 4 of 5, his first defeat after 11, incl. the Ascot Gold C. and Jockey Club C. At 5 he met younger Derby and St Leger winner Melton in the Jockey Club C., beating him by 8 lengths for a 3rd straight win, and retired. At stud he sired only a few German classic winners, a stark contrast to great sire St. Simon.
3653: Winner of the 1960 Derby and St Leger, and sire of 6th Japan Cup winner Jupiter Island. Debuting in August at 2, he won his 2nd start. At 3, 6th in the 2000 Guineas, he won the Dante S., then the Derby as 3rd choice by 3 lengths, and the St Leger easily as hot favorite. At 4 he won 4 incl. the Eclipse S. and Jockey Club S.; 2nd in the King George and Champion S., his earnings were 2nd-highest for a British-trained horse, and he retired with 9 wins from 14. At stud: Jupiter Island, Eclipse S. winner Connaught, Irish St Leger winner Parnell and more.
3654: A great 19th-century sire who reshaped the Thoroughbred, his line producing many sires - Prince Rose, Ribot, Bois Roussel, Wild Risk and more - forming the powerful St. Simon line. Unbeatable on the track in England in 1883-1884, he won all 10; not entered for the classics, he won the Ascot Gold C. and Goodwood C. by 20 lengths - in a class of his own. At stud he sired Triple Crown winner Diamond Jubilee, Fillies' Triple Crown winner La Fleche and many more, champion sire in Britain and Ireland 9 times; in 1900 his foals swept all 5 English classics. His male line is declining, but through dams he produced Nearco (inbred to him 5x4x4x5); it is said no horse today lacks his blood.
3655: A US star of 1959-1962 who at 4 in 1961 beat champion Kelso in the Washington DC International - US champion turf male. Blossoming late at 3, he won 5 straight from the Arlington Classic S. to the United Nations H., beating previous Horse of the Year Sword Dancer. At 4, just 2 wins from 15 to September, he then won the Hollywood Gold C., Knickerbocker H. and Washington DC International, beating Kelso, later 5-time Horse of the Year, into 2nd. At 5, 2 wins from 17, and he retired. At stud he steadily sired stakes winners like T. V. Commercial and Quack, US champion sire in 1974.
3656: Winner of the Arc in 1950 and 1951, and French champion sire in 1962 and 1965. Winning his debut at 2, after a run he won 3 straight incl. the Grand Criterium and Prix de la Foret, then the Poulains and Prix Lupin at 3 - 6 straight. 2nd by a short head to Scratch in the French Derby, he won England's Queen Elizabeth S. and the Arc, by then Europe's championship - 5 wins and a 2nd from 6 at 3. At 4 he won the Prix Ganay, Coronation C. and Arc from 4 and retired. At stud: French Derby winner Reliance and King George winner Match; Tanerko became a sire too, and his descendants Relko and Fidion, imported to Japan,, succeeded, Fidion siring Mejiro Durren, Mejiro Thomas and more.
3657: A great English horse of the mid-19th century, 15 wins from 16, winner of the 1849 Derby and St Leger. At 4 he won the Ascot Gold C. by 8 lengths, but was 2nd to Voltigeur in the Doncaster C., his only defeat. Unsatisfied, his camp challenged Voltigeur to a rematch; the next year's match race was billed the race of the century, and he won a fierce duel to gain revenge, then retired. At stud he sired Derby winner Ellington and Oaks winner Brown Duchess; via son Dollar, 8 generations on came Tourbillon, then Partholon, who greatly influenced Japan. As broodmare sire of Galopin, St. Simon's sire, his influence spread worldwide.
3658: Unbeaten in 7 in England at 2 in 1911, mostly by wide margins - called the greatest 2yo in British history. Odd white blotches on his coat earned him the nickname "the Spotted Wonder." His only close call, the National Breeders' S., where he was left badly at the start yet won by a neck, became a legend of his brilliance. Hot classic favorite at 3, he never raced again due to injury. His best foals were 2000 Guineas winner Tetratema and speedy filly Mumtaz Mahal. Disliking stud duty, he sired few foals, yet with them alone was champion sire in 1919. Tetratema succeeded at stud, and via his son Theft came Tokino Minoru and many stars in Japan.
3659: One of Australia's historic greats, winning 10 of 12, mostly sprints, from 1956 to 1960. Debuting at 2 in 1956/57, he won his first 4 incl. the inaugural Golden Slipper S., the top 2yo race; his sire Star Kingdom's foals then won it 5 years running. He also won the AJC Champagne S. and, in 1957/58 at 3, the Canterbury Guineas - races of today's G1 standard. Injured and 4th in the Hill S., he was off for about 2 years; back at 5 in 1959/60 he won 3 straight incl. the Lightning S. and Futurity S., and retired. A successful sire of Golden Slipper winner Eskimo Prince and many more.
3660: A dominant English miler of 1946-1947, rated 144 by Timeform, called the best miler in British racing history. Unbeaten in 4 at 2, all easily, he won an allowance and the 2000 Guineas at 3 by a record 8 lengths; jockey Gordon Richards said he would have won by 20 had he not eased him. A Derby certainty, he was 4th, perhaps over too far, then won the St. James's Palace S. and Knight's Royal S. - unbeaten in 8 at a mile - and retired. At stud in England and America he sired Kentucky Derby winner Tomy Lee and many more; King of the Tudors and Tudor Melody succeeded as sires, and in Japan his line through Tudenham produced Hospitality and Sarno King.
3661: Winner of the 1952 Derby and St Leger. Poor at 2 and little fancied, he improved rapidly at 3: 3 straight wins, then the Derby as favorite, edging Gay Time. Against older horses he won the Eclipse S. by 3 lengths, then the 2nd-ever King George VI & Queen Elizabeth S., again beating Gay Time, and the St Leger easily, a 3rd defeat of Gay Time - 7 of 7 that year. Skipped the 2000 Guineas as too short; many say he would have won the Triple Crown. Retired to stud amid huge expectations, he sired one Irish and one French classic winner, then was sold to America, where he again disappointed.
3662: The 4th US Triple Crown winner, in 1937, known as great rival of hugely popular Seabiscuit. Modest at 2 with 3 wins from 6 incl. one stakes, he blossomed at 3: 2 straight incl. the Chesapeake S. easily, the Kentucky Derby in hand, the Preakness in a tight finish with Derby runner-up Pompoon, and the Belmont in a US record 2:28.6 - an undisputed Triple Crown. On the West Coast, older Seabiscuit was a sensation, and a clash with the East's champion was demanded. It came in autumn at 4; favored after 8 wins from 9 that year, he was beaten 4 lengths - the end of the race of the century. 2 more wins, and he retired in spring at 5. At stud he sired Busher, Blue Peter and many more, North American champion sire in 1945. His sons failed at stud, but as broodmare sire of Buckpasser he influenced the world.
3663: The 1853 English Triple Crown winner - the first ever. 2nd on debut, his only defeat, he won the Glasgow S., then at 3 the 2000 Guineas and Derby as favorite, both in tight finishes. After a rest he won the St Leger easily as hot favorite - the first to sweep all 3. Rivals then avoided him, and he walked over 3 times running. At 4 he won 4 incl. the Ascot Gold C. and retired. At stud he was overshadowed by Stockwell, "the Emperor of Stallions," a year older, but sired Oaks winner Summerside and 2000 Guineas winner The Wizard. His son Australian led, 4 generations on, to Man o' War, and son Solon to Hurry On - later hailed as key to the Matchem line.
3664: Winner of the 1934 Derby and St Leger. Debuting in July at 2, he won his 3rd start, 1 of 3. Aimed at long races at 3, he skipped the 2000 Guineas, won at 12f and 10f, then beat 2000 Guineas winner Colombo, unbeaten in 9 and favorite, in the Derby. 3rd in the Eclipse S., he won the 12f Great Yorkshire S., then the St Leger as hot favorite in a race record 3:01.6. At 4 he won all 4 starts incl. the Coronation C. and Eclipse S., and retired. Dying young of illness, he left few foals; his best was Irish Triple Crown winner Windsor Slipper.
3665: A legendary filly of wartime Japan who won an irregular Triple Crown: the Tokyo Yushun (Derby), Hanshin Yushun Himba (Oaks) and Kyoto 4yo race (Kikuka Sho). Unbeaten in 11 - still the record for an unbeaten top-class horse. Debuting in 1943 at 4 (old age system), she won easily, then by a huge margin from the front, then the Tokyo Yushun by 6 lengths in record time. In autumn she won the Hanshin Yushun Himba by 10, 2 more, and the Kyoto race by a huge margin - no one could live with her. No Kikuka Sho winner before or since has won by such a margin. In 1944, as the war intensified, racing was halted and only betting-free ability trials held without crowds; she won 3 by 5, 10 and 6 lengths and retired, 11 of 11. As a broodmare she produced Kumohata Kinen winner Ichijo and Oaks winner Yamaichi; Ichijo's family later produced 1994 Kisaragi Sho winner Samson Big and 2011 Hyogo star Oe Raijin.
3666: Winner of the 1963 Kentucky Derby and Belmont S., later imported to Japan as a sire of Hokuto Flag, Metro Jumbo and others. His crop had stars Candy Spots and Never Bend, and he was overlooked; even after beating both in the Kentucky Derby he was underrated, 2nd to favorite Candy Spots in the Preakness. Beating Candy Spots in the Belmont, he finally took top billing. He won the Jerome H. that autumn, but no more stakes, and retired at 5. After 7 modest years at stud in the US, in Japan he sired many graded winners incl. Asahi Hai 3yo S. winner Hokuto Flag and autumn Kyoto Kinen winner Metro Jumbo; as broodmare sire of Tamamo Cross and Mery Nice, he spread his blood widely.
3667: A French sprint star of 1965-1966. With brilliant speed he won 5 of 6 sprints at 2, beating older stars in the Abbaye and Prix du Petit Couvert. At 3, beaten in the Poulains and its trial, he won 4 straight incl. middle-distance races like the Prix Jean Prat and Prix d'Ispahan, then the Prix du Moulin, and retired. At stud in Ireland he sired Irish 2000 Guineas winner Sharp Edge and other stakes winners; imported to Japan in his 7th season, he sired graded winners Asaka Silver and Sea Bird Park. Yet he is best known as a broodmare sire: of White Nalby, dam of siblings Oguri Cap and Oguri Roman, and, from his Irish days, Tuna, dam of Arc winner Carroll House.
3668: A sensational US 2yo of 1964, winning the Hopeful S. and Champagne S. easily - 8 wins and 2 seconds from 10. The Jockey Club's Free Handicap rated him 130, above later 2yo Horse of the Year Secretariat's 129. Classic favorite at 3, he was 10th in the Kentucky Derby, anemic, and rested the rest of the year. Back in spring at 4 he won 4 straight incl. the Roseben H. and Metropolitan H.; 6th in the Suburban H. under 135 lb, a fracture was found and he retired. At stud in the US, then France from 11 and Japan from 16, he did better in France and Japan. Note: an Irish-bred by the same sire, 2 years younger, was also named Bold Lad; the owners were sisters, and the name was reportedly reused in his honor.
3669: The 1968 Oka Sho winner. Debuting in September at 3 (old age system), she won a newcomer race and the Daily Hai 3yo S. At 4 she kept missing, 8th in the Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, but in the Oka Sho, from the widest draw of 24, she raced boldly forward and outfought Nittou Yayoi by a head - a Big Eight win. Injury ruled out the Oaks. Back in spring at 5, she was injured again; 14th in an allowance that autumn. At 6 she won the Ikaruga Tokubetsu, then 3 more incl. the Uzushio Tokubetsu and HBC Hai, ran well in stakes, and retired that autumn. No notable foals; she died at 22. Her own line ended, but full sister Miss Tokyo and half-sister Shadai Center carried on the family.
3670: The 1968 Oaks winner, from Never Beat's first crop; with crop-mate Satsuki Sho winner Mahchis, she gave her sire classic titles at once. Debuting in July at 3 (old age system), she won her 3rd start, then 3 straight early at 4. 5th in the Oka Sho, she won the Oaks as 8th choice, holding off Suzu Gerbera. In autumn she won an open race, was 4th in the Mainichi Okan and Himba Tokyo Times Hai (forerunner of the Fuchu Himba S.), ran in the Arima Kinen, and was champion 4yo filly. Winless at 5 but 2nd in the Tanabata Sho and Fukushima Daishoten, she raced until February at 6. Of 7 foals, none stood out.
3671: The 1969 Satsuki Sho winner. With stablemates Minoru, Hakuei Ho and Mejiro Asama, he was one of trainer Ogata's "Four Kings" of that classic crop. Winning his August debut at 3 (old age system) by a huge margin, he won 2 allowances early at 4, the Yayoi Sho in record time over rival Minoru, the Spring S. easily on bad ground, and the Satsuki Sho - 5 straight and a classic. A fracture followed; 2nd on his autumn return, he kept missing from 5: 3rd in the Kumohata Kinen late at 5, a win in the UHB Sho at 7, little else. Retired at 7 to stud, his JRA foals rarely rose above allowances, though local runners like Asahi Teru Hikari did well.
3672: Winner of the 1969 Takarazuka Kinen and many more graded races: Nihon Keizai Shinshun Hai, Sankei Osaka Hai, Asahi Challenge C. Debuting in July at 3 (old age system), he won his 2nd start, his only win that year. At 4 he won 2 allowances and the Mainichi Hai; barred from the Satsuki Sho after a disqualification and scratched from the Derby, he missed the big stage, but was 3rd in the Asahi Challenge C. and Kyoto Hai and 2nd in the Kikuka Sho. At 5 he won the Nihon Keizai Shinshun Hai, Chukyo Daishoten (forerunner of the Takamatsunomiya Kinen) and Sankei Osaka Hai; 4th to Takeshiba O in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he won the Takarazuka Kinen in record time, then the Asahi Challenge C. under top weight 61kg, again in record time. A fracture followed; 2nd in the Milers C. at 6, he retired. His best foal was Teio Sho and Haneda Hai winner Konan Ruby.
3673: The 1970 Oka Sho winner, also of the Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu (old age system) and Sprinters S. - champion sprinter, a speedy filly. Winning her August debut at 3, she struggled in allowances, then surged late at 3 into 4: 3 straight to the Queen C., the Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, and the Oka Sho as favorite by 4 lengths - 5 straight. 14th as Oaks favorite and 11th in the Queen S., she won the Sprinters S., proving it no fluke; champion 4yo filly went to 2-time graded winner Harbor Game, but she was champion sprinter. At 5 she won the Keio Hai Spring H., 3rd in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai, and retired that July. She died at 11 without notable foals.
3674: Winner of the 1970 Tenno Sho (Spring). Emerging early, he won his August debut at 3 (old age system), 3 wins from 7, always top 5, and beat later Oka Sho winner Hide Kotobuki in the Hanshin 3yo S. - top of his crop. A classic contender at 4, he was 16th in the Satsuki Sho, then 4th as 17th choice in the Derby. 2nd against older horses in the Sapporo Kinen, 2nd to Akane Tenryu in the Kikuka Sho, he beat Akane Tenryu in the Tenno Sho (Spring) at 5 - a Big Eight win. Racing until 7, he won 4 open races and was 2nd in the Hakodate Kinen and Sapporo Kinen - 13 wins from 47. No stars at stud; he lived as a pensioner to 35.
3675: The 1970 Oaks winner. Only 3 wins from 26, but one was a Big Eight race. Winning her first 2 from August at 3 (old age system), she then stalled and was little fancied at 4. 5th to Tamami in the Oka Sho, she won the Oaks as 12th choice by 5 lengths: on rain-soaked bad ground, as favorite Tamami floundered to 14th, she alone surged up the rail. The final 3f took nearly 42 seconds - a true mudbath. 2nd in the autumn Kobe Hai, she won no more and retired in autumn at 5. Of 8 foals none starred, but the line via daughter Hamana Jubee to granddaughter Isami Sakura continues.
3676: The 1970 Kikuka Sho winner. His crop was ruled by Satsuki Sho and Derby winner Tanino Moutiers, but he took the final classic, denying him the Triple Crown. Debuting late at 3 (old age system), he climbed through allowances by spring at 4 and joined the classics in the Derby, a close 2nd, half a length behind Tanino Moutiers - suddenly famous. He won the Mainichi Hai; with champion Tanino Moutiers unwell, he was fancied in the Kikuka Sho and seized the chance. 3rd in the Arima Kinen, best of the 4yos. At 5, 2nd in the spring Kyoto Kinen and Milers C., then injuries limited him, and he retired after a 5th in an open race in autumn at 7. Not a success at stud, he died at 11.
3677: The 1971 Oka Sho winner, leading filly of that year's classics and champion 4yo filly (old age system). Debuting in July at 3, she won her 2nd start, then the Salvia Sho over later Oaks winner Kane Himuro, and an open race - 3 wins from 7, nearly always top 3. At 4, after the Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, she was Oka Sho favorite despite worries about bad ground, and won. She won the 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, but was 10th as Oaks favorite, finding nothing. Quiet the rest of that year, she won 3 at 5 incl. the BSN Hai and Niigata Nippo Sho, 2nd in the Fukushima Daishoten, and retired. Few foals, but daughter Nasuno Aroma's line - Magic Morning, Magic Victoria - continues.
3678: The 1971 Oaks winner. Oka Sho winner Nasuno Kaori was the star, but as she struggled on bad ground, this filly won as 10th choice - a huge upset. Debuting in August at 3 (old age system), she won easily, then her 4th start and her first race at 4. Then a slump: 12th Queen C., 18th Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, 15th Oka Sho, 8th in the 4yo Himba Tokubetsu - ignored for the Oaks. On bad ground she flew, with what jockey Okabe called a demon's finish: "She's just brilliant in the mud." 4th in the Victoria C., she won no more and retired in March at 6. As a broodmare she produced 1978 Arima Kinen winner Kane Minobu.
3679: A late bloomer who won the 1972 Tenno Sho (Autumn). Debuting at 4 (old age system), he won a maiden and an allowance from 14; at 5 he won 4 more allowances with 5 seconds. At 6 he won 2 in spring, reached open class, was 4th in the Hankyu Hai and 2nd in the Asahi Challenge C., then won the autumn Kyoto Kinen. As 7th choice in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), while 8th choice Passing Goal ran off in front, he sat patiently at the back and swept past in the straight - a Big Eight win. Winless after, but 2nd in the Hanshin Daishoten, the autumn Kyoto Kinen at 7 and the Nihon Keizai Shinshun Hai at 8, then he retired. No notable foals.
3680: Winner of the 1967 Oaks, and as an older mare the Sankei Osaka Hai, Naruo Kinen and more. At 3 (old age system) she won 4 straight to the Daily Hai 3yo S.; hot favorite in the Hanshin 3yo S., she was 3rd, her first loss, but champion 3yo filly. At 4, 12th in the Oka Sho, she won the Oaks; 15th against colts in the Kikuka Sho, but champion 4yo filly. At 5 she beat males in the Sankei Osaka Hai and Naruo Kinen and won the Yuzuki Tokubetsu by 8 lengths - champion older mare, 3 straight years as top filly. Retired to breed, she left just one foal before dying young.
3681: Winner of the 1968 Sprinters S. Unbeaten in 2 at 3 (old age system), he raced at a mile to middle distances from 4, winning the Fukushima Daishoten in autumn. Unplaced often at 5, he won the Sprinters S. back at a sprint for the first time since 3, then the Sekiya Kinen in autumn. Pulled up in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he left the turf.
3682: Winner of 3 graded races in 1968: the Nakayama Kinen, Yasuda Kinen and Mainichi Okan. Debuting at 4 (old age system), he soon won his way into the Derby (11th) and Kikuka Sho (10th). He won the Kumohata Kinen, then again at 5; at 6, at his peak, he won the Nakayama Kinen, Yasuda Kinen and Mainichi Okan. Over 10 years at stud, no notable foals.
3683: A late-blooming mare who won the 1968 Chukyo Daishoten and CBC Sho. Debuting at 3 (old age system), she was 2nd in the Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu and Oaks at 4 - talented, but winless, until her first open win in the Chukyo Daishoten in summer at 5. She won the CBC Sho that autumn and retired in spring at 6. A broodmare until 22, her foals never rose above allowances.
3684: Winner of the 1968 Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system). With stablemates Wild Moa, Hakuei Ho and Mejiro Asama, he was one of trainer Ogata's "Four Kings," a big classic hope, but was 4th in the Satsuki Sho and 2nd in the Derby. 2nd choice in the Kikuka Sho, he struggled on soft ground, 17th. At 5 he won the Keio Hai Spring H.; with the Tokyo 4yo S. at 4, 3 graded wins. Not a success at stud.
3685: Winner of the 1969 NHK Hai. First winning at 4 (old age system), he won the Renge Sho and Green S. in spring, then the NHK Hai as favorite. 12th to Dai Shinboru Guard in the Derby, he kept losing, 8th in the Kikuka Sho. Rarely racing from 5, he retired after an allowance in January at 6.
3686: A mare who won 3 graded races incl. the 1969 Yasuda Kinen. Winning her debut easily in January at 4 (old age system), she won 3 straight to the 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, then the Queen S. in autumn; last (11th) in the Arima Kinen. Struggling at 5, she won the Yasuda Kinen as 10th choice in record time, and retired that summer. Her only foal never rose above allowances.
3687: A mare with 5 graded wins incl. the 1970 Shorai S. (forerunner of the Takamatsunomiya Hai). Winning 5 of 9 with 3 seconds at 3 (old age system), she won the Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu at 4; 9th in the Oka Sho and 6th in the Oaks, she won the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu that December. At 5 she won the Kimpai (West) and Naruo Kinen, 2nd in the Swan S.; at 6 she won the Shorai S. for a 5th graded win and retired. She left 4 daughters.
3688: Winner of the 1970 Sankei Osaka Hai and 1971 Takamatsunomiya Hai, by English sire Parthia, raising his name in Japan. Winning his debut at 3 (old age system), he climbed allowances at 4 and battled in stakes without winning, then won the Sankei Osaka Hai that spring. At 5 he won the Takamatsunomiya Hai, and retired in spring at 6. His half-brother, a year younger, Shunsaku Ryu, won the spring Kyoto Kinen.
3689: Winner of the 1970 Victoria C. (forerunner of the QEII Cup), created that year as the fillies' final classic; she was its first winner. Debuting late at 3 (old age system), she first won at 4, 16th in the Oka Sho. Climbing through allowances, she beat Oaks winner Jupiq in the autumn Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu, then won the Victoria C. Winless after, she retired in spring at 5. No stars of her own, but via daughter Kunino Kiyoko came grandson Daiyusaku, an Arima Kinen winner.
3690: Winner of 4 graded races incl. the 1970 Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system). After 4 straight 2nds, he won 3 straight to the Asahi Hai 3yo S. A classic contender at 4, he missed the Satsuki Sho, short of work, was 20th in the Derby, then 3rd in the Kikuka Sho. At 5 he won the Hakodate Kinen, 4th in the Arima Kinen; at 6 the AJCC and spring Meguro Kinen. Placed but winless in Big Eight races, he raced steadily until early at 8. No notable foals.
3691: Winner of the 1970 Hanshin 3yo S. (old age system). Winning his 2nd start, he won the Hokkaido 3yo S. (forerunner of the Sapporo 2yo S.) and Hakodate 3yo S., an open race, and the Hanshin 3yo S. - 5 straight. At 4 the classic trips didn't suit him; just 2 open wins. Older, he won the Milers C. and Keihan Hai, strong at a mile to middle distances. He left few foals at stud.
3692: Winner of the 1971 Sankei Osaka Hai. Debuting at 4 (old age system), he reached open class by summer in 13 starts, then tried stakes from autumn, 4th in the CBC Sho - 19 starts that year, a tough campaign. Improving at 5 and 6, he won the Kimpai (West) early at 7, then 3rd in the spring Kyoto Kinen, 2nd in the Chukyo Kinen, and won the Sankei Osaka Hai. 4th to Mejiro Musashi in the Takarazuka Kinen, he retired.
3693: A mare who won the 1971 Yasuda Kinen. Debuting in September at 3 (old age system), she won 1 of 6. At 4, overshadowed by Oka Sho winner Tamami, she was 3rd in the Oka Sho and 2nd in the 4yo Himba Tokubetsu, then won the Queen S. in autumn and beat Tamami in the Himba Tokyo Times Hai (forerunner of the Fuchu Himba S.). At 5 she won the Yasuda Kinen, strong at a mile, and retired at year-end. Her daughters Harbor Never, Harbor Shine and Harbor Freesia carried on the family; a great-grandchild, Arrow September, starred in Southern Kanto.
3694: He beat Arrow Express to win the 1971 Sprinters S. Winning his first 2 from July at 3 (old age system), he then spent ages in allowances until spring at 6. 4th in the Yasuda Kinen, he won the Sprinters S. that autumn - his only graded win, but beating hot favorite Arrow Express left a lasting impression. He won an open race at 7 and retired. No notable foals.
3695: Winner of the 1971 Victoria C. (forerunner of the QEII Cup). Debuting in July at 3 (old age system), she won 2 of 6. At 4 she was a fine 9th as 20th choice in the Oka Sho. After an allowance win that autumn she won the Victoria C., then the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu - 3 straight. At 5, in middle-distance stakes against males, 3rd in the Sankei Osaka Hai and 2nd in the Takarazuka Kinen. Retired that year; her 2 colts did nothing notable.
3696: A filly who won 4 graded races incl. the 1971 Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system). Winning 3 straight to the Keisei Hai 3yo S., then the Asahi Hai 3yo S., she was 4th in the Oka Sho at 4, then won the Himba Tokyo Times Hai (forerunner of the Fuchu Himba S.) and Lord Derby CT in autumn. 14th in the Arima Kinen; winless as an older mare, she retired in spring at 6. 7 foals, some family growth, but her line has since died out.
3697: Winner of the 1971 Hanshin 3yo S. (old age system). Winning his debut easily, then 2 straight to the Hanshin 3yo S., then an open race, the Kisaragi Sho and Keisei Hai at 4 - 5 straight, classic favorite. 2nd in the Spring S. with leg trouble, he was sidelined; back in spring at 6, he ran once and retired. At stud he sired local stars like Zen-Nihon 3yo Yushun winner Shigeno Kamada and Kashiwa Kinen winner Kisarazu Boy.
3698: Winner of 4 graded races incl. the 1972 Sankei Osaka Hai. Winning 3 straight from autumn at 3 (old age system) to the Shinzan Kinen, 3rd in the Mainichi Hai and Spring S., he joined the classics; among the famed "Class of '72" - Land Prince, Long Ace, Taite M - he was a creditable 3rd in the Derby. Older, he won the Kimpai (West), Sankei Osaka Hai and Naruo Kinen. Then just one open win, and he retired in spring at 7.
3699: Winner of the 1972 NHK Hai. Winning his first 3 from late at 3 (old age system), 2nd in his first stakes, the Shinzan Kinen, steady in open races, he won the NHK Hai. In the Derby, no match for the big three Long Ace, Land Prince and Taite M, he was 5th; 6th of 19 in the Kikuka Sho, he retired that year. Nothing notable at stud.
3700: A mare who at 5 (old age system) in 1971 won 3 straight graded races - Tanabata Sho, Fukushima Daishoten, Lord Derby CT - 5 graded wins in all. Debuting in January at 4, she climbed allowances by autumn, 3rd in the Victoria C. (forerunner of the QEII Cup) and 5th in the Himba Tokyo Times Hai. At 5 she blossomed with those 3 wins; at 6 she added the spring Meguro Kinen and Takamatsunomiya Hai - 5 graded wins against males. Of 6 foals, none stood out.
3701: A mare who won the 1972 Yasuda Kinen. At 3 (old age system) she won a newcomer race and an allowance, then 4th as 12th choice in the Asahi Hai 3yo S. Only 2 allowance wins at 4, she blossomed at 5: 2nd in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and spring Meguro Kinen, then the Yasuda Kinen - all 3 on bad ground, earning the nickname "Mud Demon." At 6 she won the Keio Hai Autumn H.; switching to jumps in autumn at 7, she won 1 of 4. Just 2 foals.
3702: Winner of the 1972 Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system). Winning his October debut at 3 easily and an allowance, he won his first stakes, the Asahi Hai 3yo S., as 8th choice of 12; with hot favorite Mammy Blue and the other fancies flopping, 8th and 9th choices (him and Cape Cod) went 1-2 - a big upset. He retired after it, unbeaten in 3. Not a success at stud.
3703: A filly unbeaten in 4 to the 1972 Hanshin 3yo S. (old age system). She won her debut by a huge margin and the Daily Hai 3yo S. by 8 lengths in record time, then the Hanshin 3yo S. as favorite by 5 - champion 3yo filly. Classic favorite at 4, she was 2nd to Nittou Chidori in both the Hanshin 4yo Himba Tokubetsu and Oka Sho. Turning to sprints, 2nd in the Centaur S. At 5 she won 2 open races; set to retire after the autumn Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu, she fell in the race and was put down.
3704: Winner of the 1972 Sapporo Kinen. First winning late at 3 (old age system), he climbed allowances and won an open race at 4, 3rd in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai. At 5, after a 5th in the spring Meguro Kinen, he won the Sapporo Kinen as favorite, beating 4-time graded winner Long One. Only 2 allowance wins at 6, and he retired that year.
3705: An Oi star until 5 (old age system) who moved to the JRA at 6 in 1971 and won that year's Sapporo Kinen. At Oi he was 4th in the Haneda Hai and 5th in the Tokyo Derby; blossoming at 5, he won 6 of 8 incl. the Dioright Kinen and Oi Kinen. With the JRA at 6 he ran 2nd, 1st, 2nd in open races, then won the Sapporo Kinen as favorite. 2nd in the autumn Meguro Kinen, 7th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he retired.
3706: Winner of the 1970 Sapporo Kinen, full brother to the next year's Hanshin 3yo S. winner Hide Hayate. Debuting in August at 3 (old age system), he won his 3rd start, climbed allowances by spring at 4 and won 2 open races. 2nd choice against older horses in the Sapporo Kinen, he won by 3 lengths. Rarely racing after, one open race each at 5 and 6, he retired.
3707: Winner of 3 graded races incl. the 1972 Nakayama Kinen, a half-brother 6 years older than Tosho Boy. Debuting in October at 3 (old age system), he passed allowances in spring at 4; in autumn, 2nd in the Sekiya Kinen and 3rd in the Niigata Kinen. At 5 he won 3 straight to the Sekiya Kinen, then the Kumohata Kinen; at 6 the Nakayama Kinen. 4th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), 6th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he retired that year. Over 10 years at stud, no stars.
3708: Winner of the 1971 Nakayama Kinen. Winning his July debut at 3 (old age system) and the Niigata 3yo S., he was talented early, but his crop had strong rivals like Arrow Express and Tanino Moutiers; winless at 4, best 2nd in the Tokyo 4yo S. (forerunner of the Kyodo News Hai). After allowances at 5, he won the Nakayama Kinen; 2nd in the Argentine JCC (forerunner of the Argentine Republic Hai), he left the turf.
3709: Winner of the 1970 Nakayama Kinen. Winning his November debut at 3 (old age system), 7th in the Asahi Hai 3yo S. and 18th in the Derby at 4, he was 2nd in the Kabutoyama Kinen that autumn, then raced in stakes and won the Nakayama Kinen at 5 as 7th choice. His only later wins were 3 straight allowances at 7, and he retired in spring at 8.
3710: The best Grey Sovereign son to race in Japan, winner of the 1969 Nakayama Kinen. Winning his September debut at 3 (old age system), he won an open race in spring at 4, 13th in the Derby, then improved to 2nd in the Kumohata Kinen. At 5, 2nd in the Keio Hai Spring H., 3rd in the spring Meguro Kinen, he won the Nakayama Kinen. Winless after, he retired in spring at 6. Hoped to carry Grey Sovereign's line, he sired no stars.
3711: Winner of the 1972 Kinko Sho and Asahi Challenge C. At 3 (old age system) he won his 6th start and an allowance. At 4 he won 2 open races but was outclassed in stakes. Often unplaced at 5, he used the lightest weight to win a 7-runner Kinko Sho, then the Asahi Challenge C., another 7-runner field, as 5th choice. At 6, 2nd in the Nihon Keizai Shinshun Hai and Chukyo Kinen, and he retired that year.
3712: Winner of the 1971 Kinko Sho and Hanshin Daishoten. First winning at 4 (old age system), he won 5 straight allowance and open races, then was 4th as 12th choice of 28 in the Derby. He won the Kinko Sho that summer; 2nd in the Kobe Hai, 6th in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai, 2nd in the Kikuka Sho, then after an open win he won the Hanshin Daishoten as favorite. At 5, 3rd in the Swan S., 2nd in the spring Kyoto Kinen; he raced until autumn at 6.
3713: Winner of the 1970 Hakata S. (that year only, the Kinko Sho was run under this name at Kokura). First winning late at 3 (old age system), he won 3 allowances at 4, then the Hakata S. at 5 as 7th choice. Besides an open win, his best in stakes that year was 4th in the Kokura Daishoten. At 6 he won an allowance and the Hakata S. (an open race again), and retired that summer.
3714: Winner of 4 graded races incl. the 1969 Kinko Sho. He blossomed at 5 (old age system): 2nd in the Keio Hai Spring H. and Tanabata Sho, he won the Fukushima Kinen, then the Niigata Kinen. At 6 he won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai, was 2nd in the Chukyo Kinen, and won the Kinko Sho. 13th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) at 7, his first double-figure finish, he retired after a 6th in an open race early at 8.
3715: Winner of the 1969 Hanshin Daishoten. First winning in his 8th start, in June at 4 (old age system), he ran in the Kikuka Sho still an allowance horse and was 3rd as 20th choice, then won the Hanshin Daishoten. Rarely in the top 5 in stakes as an older horse, he switched to jumps at 7 and won 4 straight incl. the spring Hanshin Shogai S., becoming favorite for the spring Nakayama Daishogai - but an unlucky incident in the paddock forced his withdrawal, and hurt, he never won again.
3716: Winner of the 1968 Hanshin Daishoten. Debuting at 4 (old age system), he won easily, then kept missing in allowances. Reaching open class in spring at 5, he was 2nd in the Hakodate Kinen; after 2nds in the Keihan Hai and autumn Kyoto Kinen, he won the Hanshin Daishoten. At 6, 10th in the spring Kyoto Kinen, 6th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), and he retired.
3718: Winner of the 1970 All Comers and 1971 Nihon Keizaisho, owned by Kakuei Tanaka, later Prime Minister. At 4 (old age system), still an allowance horse, he was 19th in the Derby and 10th in the Kikuka Sho. Blossoming at 5, 3rd in the Sprinters S., he won the All Comers, then 4th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 7th in the Arima Kinen. He won the Nihon Keizaisho at 6 in record time, ran once at 7 and retired.
3719: Raced 20 times at 5 (old age system) in 1969, winning 3 graded races: Nihon Keizaisho, Keio Hai Autumn H. and All Comers. His first stakes win was the Keisei Hai early at 4, then 8th Satsuki Sho, 6th Derby, 7th Kikuka Sho - 21 starts that year too. After the 3 wins at 5, he was 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). Winless at 6, but 2nd in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai and spring Kyoto Kinen, he retired that year.
3720: Winner of the 1967 Tanabata Sho and 1968 Nihon Keizaisho. Debuting at 4 (old age system) with 2 straight wins, he was 22nd in the Satsuki Sho and 23rd in the Derby, but 2nd in the Kabutoyama Kinen. At 5 he won 4 open races and the Tanabata Sho; at 6, 2nd in the Sprinters S., he won the Nihon Keizaisho in record time. 2nd in the Diamond S. and Nakayama Kinen at 7, he retired at 8.
3721: Winner of the 1971 All Comers and 1972 Fukushima Kinen. First winning late at 3 (old age system), he battled in allowances, reached open class in autumn at 4, was 5th in the St. Lite Kinen, then won the All Comers as 12th choice of 15. At 5, 4th in the Yasuda Kinen, 3rd in the Tanabata Sho, he won the Fukushima Kinen. In the Tenno Sho (Autumn) he broke down and was put down.
3722: A mare who won 4 graded races incl. the 1968 All Comers. 5th in the Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system), 2nd in the Oka Sho and 3rd in the Oaks at 4, she won the Keio Hai Autumn H. at 5, then the All Comers. 11th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn); at 6 she won the Himba Tokyo Times Hai (forerunner of the Fuchu Himba S.), at 7 the Kimpai (East), and retired. Over 18 years at stud she produced 8 daughters, all bred on, greatly expanding her family.
3723: Winner of the 1972 Mainichi Okan. Winning his debut at 3 (old age system) and 2 allowances at 4, he was 4th in the Satsuki Sho; 19th in the Derby, too far. 4th in the Kabutoyama Kinen, he won a 1800m open race at 5, his best trip, then the Mainichi Okan as 4th choice. 3rd in the All Comers, he left the turf.
3724: Winner of the 1971 Niigata Kinen and Mainichi Okan. Struggling long in allowances at 3 and 4 (old age system), he reached open class in his 19th start in autumn at 4, but was 16th and 11th in stakes. At 5 he matured, always top 3: 3rd in the Sekiya Kinen, then the Niigata Kinen and Mainichi Okan as a fancy. Unplaced in the Sprinters S. and All Comers, he retired.
3725: Winner of 4 graded races incl. the 1970 Mainichi Okan. 12th in the Satsuki Sho and 7th in the Derby at 4 (old age system), he improved in autumn: the Keio Hai Autumn H. as 5th choice, then the Mainichi Okan and St. Lite Kinen - 3 straight - and later the Lord Derby CT. Just one open win from 5, but 2nd in the AJCC and Nihon Keizaisho.
3726: Winner of the 1971 autumn Kyoto Kinen and 1972 Hollywood Turf Club Sho (forerunner of the Kyoto Daishoten). Winning his debut in summer at 4 (old age system), he won 6 of 9 allowances to spring at 6, never worse than 5th. 4th in his first stakes, the Kinko Sho, he won the autumn Kyoto Kinen. At 7, 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Spring), 4th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), he won the Hollywood Turf Club Sho in record time and retired.
3727: Winner of the 1970 Naruo Kinen and Hollywood Turf Club Sho (forerunner of the Kyoto Daishoten). Passing allowances in autumn at 4 (old age system), he was 6th of 21 in the Kikuka Sho and 6th in the Tenno Sho (Spring) at 5. He won the Naruo Kinen (then 2400m), then the Hollywood Turf Club Sho, and after an open win at 6 left the turf.
3728: Winner of 3 graded races incl. the 1969 Hollywood Turf Club Sho (forerunner of the Kyoto Daishoten), and 3 times 2nd and once 3rd in the Tenno Sho - so close. A classic contender at 4 (old age system), 3rd in the Satsuki Sho, 8th in the Derby, he was scratched ill from the Kikuka Sho, then won the autumn Kyoto Kinen and Hanshin Daishoten. At 5 he was 2nd as Tenno Sho (Autumn) favorite; at 6 he won the Hollywood Turf Club Sho, 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 6th in the Arima Kinen; at 7, 2nd in both Tenno Sho. After a 2nd in the Diamond S. at 8 he retired.
3729: Winner of the 1968 AJCC and Stayers S. Emerging in autumn at 4 (old age system), 3rd in the All Comers, 5th in the Arima Kinen, he won an open race and the AJCC early at 5, then the spring Stayers S. 5th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and 2nd in the Arima Kinen - a fine stayer. Winless at 6, best 2nd in the CBC Sho and Aichi Hai, he retired at year-end.
3730: Winner of the 1972 spring Kyoto Kinen. After near-misses in allowances at 3 and 4 (old age system), he reached open class at 5 and at once was 2nd in the Naruo Kinen and 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Spring). Almost always top 5, he won the spring Kyoto Kinen at 6 - his only open win, but a familiar contender in graded races.
3731: Winner of 4 graded races incl. the 1971 spring Kyoto Kinen. After a long apprenticeship - 9 starts to win, then allowance struggles until late at 4 (old age system) - he blossomed at 5, winning the spring Meguro Kinen easily as 14th choice, then the Stayers S. At 6 he won the Nihon Keizai Shinshun Hai and spring Kyoto Kinen, and was a close 2nd to Tomei in the Arima Kinen. At 7 he broke down in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and was put down.
3732: Winner of the 1970 autumn Kyoto Kinen. Debuting at 4 (old age system), he won a maiden and 3 allowances. At 5 he placed in stakes (2nd Nihon Keizai Shinshun Hai, 3rd Kitakyushu Kinen and Kokura Kinen), then won 2 allowances and the autumn Kyoto Kinen - 3 straight. Out of contention after, he retired in summer at 6.
3733: Winner of the 1970 spring Kyoto Kinen. Winning 3 straight allowances at 4 (old age system), he was 18th in the Satsuki Sho and 22nd in the Derby, then rested. Back at 5, 4th in the Swan S., he won the spring Kyoto Kinen, crushing fancied crop-mate Kinsen O and others. Poor in stakes after, he won one allowance at 6 and left the turf.
3734: Winner of the 1969 autumn Kyoto Kinen. He ran in the Kyoto Kinen 5 times, spring and autumn, from 5 to 7 (old age system): 7th in spring at 5, he won that autumn over younger Kinsen O and others; 3rd in spring and 6th in autumn at 6; last (10th) in autumn at 7. He was also 2nd in the Asahi Challenge C. and Hollywood Turf Club Sho.
3735: Winner of 3 graded races incl. the 1968 autumn Kyoto Kinen. He won 4 straight from late at 3 (old age system) to the Kisaragi Sho, was 2nd in the NHK Hai and 3rd in the Derby, then won the Hollywood Turf Club Sho in record time. At 5, 5th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), 3rd in the Takarazuka Kinen, he won the autumn Kyoto Kinen. 2nd in the spring Kyoto Kinen at 6, he retired after an 11th in the Swan S.
3717: Winner of 3 graded races incl. the 1972 Nihon Keizaisho. Winning his debut at 3 (old age system), 3rd in the Hokkaido 3yo S. (forerunner of the Sapporo 2yo S.), 2nd in the Asahi Hai 3yo S., he was noticed early. Struggling at 4, he won 2 allowances and the Kabutoyama Kinen. At 5 he won the Nihon Keizaisho and autumn Meguro Kinen; in Big Eight races, 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and, at 6, 2nd in the Tenno Sho (Spring). He retired after a 6th in the Takarazuka Kinen.
3736: Winner of the 1968 spring Kyoto Kinen. Climbing through allowances at 3 and 4 (old age system), he was 6th in his first stakes, the Nihon Keizai Shinshun Hai, early at 5, then after an open race won the spring Kyoto Kinen as 5th choice of 7, a length clear of Yama Pit. 2nd to Yama Pit in the Sankei Osaka Hai, 4th in the Takarazuka Kinen, he rarely raced after and retired at 7.
3737: Winner of the 1972 Stayers S. Debuting in October at 3 (old age system), he first won in his 12th start in May at 4, then spent ages in allowances until autumn at 5. 10th in his first open race, the Aichi Hai, he blossomed in the Stayers S., winning by 3.5 lengths as 4th choice. 8th in the AJCC at 6, he left the turf.
3738: Winner of the 1969 Stayers S. First winning at 4 (old age system), he raced long in allowances and stepped up to be 3rd in the Niigata Kinen in summer at 5, then won the Stayers S. in record time on soft ground. 11th in both the Tenno Sho (Autumn) and Arima Kinen.
3739: Winner of the 1972 Keio Hai Spring H. Winning his first 2 from October at 3 (old age system), he struggled in allowances to the end of 4, then improved at 5: 3rd in his first stakes, the spring Meguro Kinen, he won the Keio Hai Spring H. 2nd in the Argentine JCC (forerunner of the Argentine Republic Hai), 4th in the Nihon Keizaisho. From 6 just 2 allowance wins; switching to jumps at 8, he was beaten badly and retired.
3740: Winner of the 1966 Asahi Hai 3yo S. (old age system), champion 3yo colt, and a big classic hope. Unwell, he was 8th in the Satsuki Sho and 10th in the Derby; he won the St. Lite Kinen in autumn but missed the Kikuka Sho, unwell again. At 5 he won 4 open races, 2nd in the Sapporo Kinen and All Comers, 4th in the Arima Kinen. At 6 he won the Keio Hai Spring H., a 3rd graded win, and retired in spring at 7.
3741: Winner of the 1968 Keio Hai Spring H. At 4 (old age system), 3rd in the St. Lite Kinen, he was 14th in the Kikuka Sho; 12th in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai at 5, he was overlooked in the Keio Hai Spring H. but beat favorite Hakusensho. 2nd in the spring Meguro Kinen, 4th in the Diamond S. Then just 2 open wins; switching to jumps at 7, he won 1 and was 2nd 3 times from 4, and retired.
3742: A filly who won the 1972 Swan S. At 4 (old age system) she was 5th in the Oka Sho, 8th in the Oaks, 18th in the Victoria C. (forerunner of the QEII Cup). Then 2 allowance wins late at 4, an open race early at 5, and the Swan S. - 4 straight. Unplaced after in the Sankei Osaka Hai, Milers C. and others, she retired at the end of 5.
3743: Winner of the 1971 Swan S. and 1972 Hankyu Hai, a homebred from Bamboo Farm's early days who helped build it. Reaching open class late at 4 (old age system), 4th in the Kimpai (West) at 5, he won the Swan S., then after 2 open wins and near-misses, the Hankyu Hai at 6. He won 3 straight open miles late at 6 into 7 - a standout around a mile.
3744: A local star at Nagoya and Kasamatsu in 1967 at 3 (old age system), he moved to the JRA at 4 and won 3 graded races. At 4 he won the Kobe Hai, 3rd in the autumn Kyoto Kinen, 2nd in the Hanshin Daishoten. At 5 he won the Swan S. and Centaur S., 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Spring). Winless in stakes from 6 but with 3 open wins, he switched to jumps in spring at 8, winning 1 of 2.
3745: Winner of 4 graded races incl. the 1966 Hanshin Daishoten, and a fair sire who stood out in an era unkind to homebreds. Always top 3 until autumn at 4 (old age system), first unplaced in the Kikuka Sho, he won the Hanshin Daishoten. At 5 he won the Sankei Osaka Hai, 3rd in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 2nd in the Arima Kinen. At 6 he won the Nihon Keizai Shinshun Hai and Swan S. and retired. At stud: Hanshin 3yo S. winner Ryu Kiko and later sire Andre Amon among others.
3746: Winner of the 1972 Nihon Keizai Shinshun Hai. Through allowances by the end of 4 (old age system), at 5 he was in the top 5 in all 7 graded races without winning. At 6 he won the Nihon Keizai Shinshun Hai as favorite; often unplaced after (15th Tenno Sho (Spring)), he retired at 7 without another win.
3747: Winner of the 1970 Nihon Keizai Shinshun Hai at 5 (old age system). Ignored in the classics at 4, 16th choice or longer, he still ran 13th, 7th and 7th. 2nd in the autumn Kyoto Kinen and Kimpai (West), he won the Nihon Keizai Shinshun Hai. Only 2 allowance wins after, but he raced until spring at 8 - 51 starts, a tough career.
3748: Winner of the 1970 autumn Meguro Kinen. Debuting at 4 (old age system), he spent 34 races in allowances until autumn at 5, then still an allowance horse was 2nd in the autumn Meguro Kinen and 4th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn). At 6 he won the autumn Meguro Kinen as 8th choice by half a length over Mejiro Asama, Makino Hope and others. 3 more runs to 7, and he retired.
3749: Winner of the 1972 Argentine JCC (forerunner of the Argentine Republic Hai) - his only graded win, but his razor-sharp finish thrilled fans. At 4 (old age system), as dual classic winner Hikaru Imai stole the headlines, he showed promise with a 5th in the Derby. At 5, after an allowance win, he produced the run of his life in the Argentine JCC, sweeping past Tosho Pit, Banrai and others to win in record time. Winless after and fragile, he rarely raced and retired at 7.
3750: Winner of 3 graded races incl. the 1970 Argentine JCC (forerunner of the Argentine Republic Hai). In allowances until summer at 4 (old age system), he won his first stakes, the Tanabata Sho, easily in record time, then the Fukushima Daishoten. At 5, 2nd in the Diamond S., 4th in the Nakayama Kinen, he beat fancied Speed Symboli by a nose in the Argentine JCC. Winless after, he retired at 6.
3751: A mare of 1970-1973 who raced mainly in the then-rare fillies' graded races. 3rd in her first stakes, the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu, at 4 (old age system), 2nd in the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu; at 5, 2nd in the Kyoto race in the same time as the winner, she won the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu. At 6, 4th in the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu and 2nd in the Kimpai (West), and she retired.
3752: Winner of fillies' stakes the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu and Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu in 1969. Debuting at 4 (old age system), she won her 6th start, climbed allowances by autumn, was 13th in the Keihan Hai, then won the Kyoto Himba Tokubetsu and beat Tomei in the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu. Winless at 5, but 2nd against males in the Naruo Kinen and autumn Kyoto Kinen; after a 2nd in the Hanshin Himba Tokubetsu she retired.
3753: A French horse, 2025 Cartier Horse of the Year, who also won the Japan Cup (G1) - the first foreign-trained winner in 20 years, since Alkaased in 2005. At 2 he won 1 of 2. At 3 he won the Prix Noailles (G3), Prix Hocquart (G3) and King Edward VII S. (G2), but was 2nd in the International S. and Champion S. At 4, after 2nds in the Dubai Sheema Classic and Coronation C., he won the Grand Prix de Saint-Cloud at home, his first G1, then the King George and Champion S. in England - Cartier Horse of the Year. In Japan, as Europe's best, he drew huge interest and won the Japan Cup by a head after a fierce duel with Japan's leading Masquerade Ball.
3754: Hong Kong's dominant sprinter of 2024-2025: 4 sprint G1s in 2024/25 incl. the Hong Kong Sprint, Horse of the Year. Debuting at 3 in 2023/24, he won, ran 2nd twice, then won 4 straight to the Sha Tin Vase (G3). In 2024/25 he won all 8 incl. 4 G1s - Hong Kong Sprint, Centenary Sprint C., Queen's Silver Jubilee C., Chairman's Sprint Prize. In 2025/26 he won The Everest (G1) in Australia and the Jockey Club Sprint (G2) at home, then a 2nd Hong Kong Sprint in December, extending his winning run.
3755: A 2025 dirt star, winner of the February S. (G1). Debuting late at 2, he steadily climbed the classes, 4 wins from 6 by spring at 4, then won his first open race, the Keyaki S. (OP), as 2nd choice. 6th in the Cluster C., he won the Negishi S. (G3) at 5 by 4 lengths. In the February S., 2nd choice under visiting jockey Rachel King, he surged from a handy spot and held off Sunrise Zipang - the first JRA flat G1 won by a female jockey. 3rd as 1.5-1 Kashiwa Kinen favorite, 11th in the Sakitama Hai, he bounced back with a 2nd in the Musashino S.
3756: Central to the 2025 3yo fillies' races, winner of the Oka Sho (G1) and Shuka Sho (G1), from Admire Mars's first crop. At 2 she won 2 of 4. At 3 she won the Queen C. (G3) as 3rd choice; 3rd choice in the Oka Sho behind Erika Express and Arma Veloce, she beat Arma Veloce by a neck. Oaks favorite, she pulled hard and was 9th. Straight to the Shuka Sho, billed against Oaks winner Come Nyack; as Come Nyack faded, she dueled front-running Erika Express and caught her by half a length. 11th in the Hong Kong Mile, but champion 3yo filly.
3757: The 2025 Satsuki Sho winner. Active early, 2nd as 2nd choice in the Asahi Hai FS at 2. At 3, 4th as Yayoi Sho favorite, he was 3rd choice in the Satsuki Sho and swept past hot favorite Croix du Nord from midfield for his first G1. 2nd choice in the Derby, he closed from the back for 6th. He won the St. Lite Kinen, then skipped the Kikuka Sho for the Tenno Sho (Autumn), 3rd choice as fellow 3yo Masquerade Ball was favorite; both waited at the back and surged, and he was 2nd by 3/4 length - showing the 3yos' strength. In the Arima Kinen he beat veterans Danon Decile and Regaleira decisively - champion 3yo colt.
3758: Winner of the 2025 Tenno Sho (Spring) (G1). Racing mainly at long trips, he won a 1-win race by spring at 3, 8th in his first stakes, the Aoba Sho. He won 2 more classes, then was 2nd to Urban Chic in the Kikuka Sho, moving early from the back. At 4 he won the Diamond S. (G3) as 1.9-1 favorite, leading at the 4th turn and drawing away. Favorite in the Tenno Sho (Spring), he broke clear from a handy spot and held off Byzantine Dream's charge by a head - a G1, top of the stayers.
3759: The 2025 Oaks winner. Winning her August debut at 2, she was 6th as favorite in the Artemis S. At 3, 4th in the Elfin S. (L), she won the Flora S. as 7th choice with a sharp late run in race-record time. In the Oaks, 4th choice behind the big three - Oka Sho winner Embroidery, champion 2yo Arma Veloce and Oka Sho 3rd Links Tip - she closed powerfully from the back and caught Arma Veloce by a head. She won the Rose S. easily; Shuka Sho favorite, billed against Embroidery, both seeking a 2nd classic, she found nothing and faded to 16th.
3760: The 2025 Kikuka Sho winner. Winning his October debut at 2 and the Saintpaulia Sho (1-win) at 3, he won his first stakes, the Aoba Sho (G2), as favorite with a powerful late run from the back - unbeaten in 3, a Derby contender. Unwell, he skipped the Derby; against older horses in the Niigata Kinen he was 2nd to Shirankedo. Straight to the Kikuka Sho, with both the Satsuki Sho winner Museum Mile and Derby winner Croix du Nord absent, he was narrow favorite over Kobe Shimbun Hai winner Eri King; moving early from the back on the 3rd turn, he took the lead and won decisively - a G1.
3761: A leader of the 2025 3yo crop, winner of the Tenno Sho (Autumn) (G1). Unbeaten in 2, 11th as 4th choice in the Hopeful S. at 2, he won the Kyodo News Hai (G3) at 3 as favorite. 3rd to Museum Mile in the Satsuki Sho, charging from the back; 2nd in the Derby, 3/4 length behind Croix du Nord. Skipping the Kikuka Sho, he was favorite over older horses in the Tenno Sho (Autumn), and beat Satsuki Sho winner Museum Mile by 3/4 length, both closing from midfield. Favorite in the Japan Cup, he lost a fierce duel with French star Calandagan by a head.
3762: Winner of the 2025 Champions C. (G1), only the 2nd filly or mare to win it, after Sanbista in 2015. Debuting late, in summer at 3, she won 4 straight from a maiden to the 3-win class, then her first open race, the Sannomiya S. (OP) - 5 straight. 2nd in her first stakes, the Breeders' Gold C., her first defeat, she won the Miyako S. (G3) as 2nd choice, leading early and holding off Simon Zanadu by a neck. In the Champions C., with top 3yo Narukami hot favorite, she was 3rd choice; saving ground on the rail, she kicked in the straight and beat 2-time runner-up Wilson Tesoro by a nose - a G1.
3763: Champion 2yo filly of 2025. 5th on debut closing from the back, she then raced forward and won a maiden by 7 lengths. Hot 1.7-1 favorite in the Chukyo 2yo S. (G3), she and Candide drew far clear in a match race, and she lost by a neck. The Hanshin JF had no graded winners; 2nd choice behind unbeaten Alankar, she waited in midfield and held off fast-closing Gallaborg by 1 1/4 lengths - her first stakes win a G1.
3764: A 2025 3yo filly star. Winning her October debut at 2, she won the Fairy S. (G3) at 3 easily and went unbeaten to the Oka Sho as favorite, but led and faded to 5th. 10th in the Oaks, 11th in the Keisei Hai AH, she then led and held on for 2nd in the Shuka Sho, gritty in the final classic. 12th as 5th choice in the QEII Cup.
3765: Winner of the 2025 Shinzan Kinen (G3). Watched from debut, he won with ease in October at 2, then the Shinzan Kinen at 3 with a powerful finish from midfield, beating favorite Arte Veloce. 7th as Mainichi Hai favorite; hoped to give his sire Kizuna a father-son Derby, he was 10th.
3766: Winner of the 2025 Keisei Hai (G3) as 11th choice; with longshots also 2nd and 3rd, the trifecta paid 1.72 million yen. Debuting in August at 2, he placed often before winning his 4th start, then at 3 won the Keisei Hai with a brilliant late run from the back. Carrying the hopes of a small breeder and trainer Chiba in his 2nd year, he was 13th in the Satsuki Sho and 16th in the Derby.
3767: Winner of the 2025 Nikkei Shinshun Hai (G2). Unbeaten in 3 from his January debut at 3, 4th in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, then 2 more wins - plenty of promise. 2nd in the Chunichi Shimbun Hai at 4, he won the Nikkei Shinshun Hai at 5. 4th choice in his first G1, the Osaka Hai, he was 2nd, a length behind Bellagio Opera. 3rd choice in the Takarazuka Kinen, he found nothing from the back, 8th.
3768: First winner of the Kokura Himba S. (G3), created in 2025 to replace the Aichi Hai (G3).
