Winning her July debut at 2, she spent ages in allowances, reaching open class in summer at 4; 2nd at once in the Fukushima Kinen (G3), she dead-heated with Scintillation in the Kokura Himba S. for her first graded win. 2nd in the Fukushima Himba S., 3rd in the Queen S., but 9th in the QEII Cup.
3769: Co-winner, in a dead heat with Fair Erlung, of the first Kokura Himba S. (G3), created in 2025 to replace the Aichi Hai (G3). Early on she was 6th in the Artemis S. at 2 and 3rd in the Flower C. at 3. After a long break she returned at 4 and climbed the allowances; reaching open class in summer at 5, she was 2nd in the Fuchu Himba S. (G2), then won the Kokura Himba S. at 6.
3770: A dirt horse throughout, who won his first graded race, the Procyon S. (G2), at 5 in 2025. On debut at 2 he beat later Sprinters S. winner Lugal and later dirt graded winner Out Range. Climbing steadily, he reached open class in spring at 4, then lost heavily in stakes until winning the Betelgeuse S. (L) late at 4 and the Procyon S. early at 5.
3771: A sprinter who blossomed at 5 in 2025. 5th on a mile debut late at 2, he won his 3rd start at a sprint and stuck to sprints, winning 2 classes at 3 and the 3-win class at 4, then the Carbuncle S. (OP) at 5. In his first stakes, the Silk Road S. (G3), 9th choice, he closed sharply from midfield to win - also jockey Kawamata's first JRA graded win. 5th as 8th choice in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen; 12th in Hong Kong's Chairman's Sprint Prize.
3772: A miler who won the 2025 Tokyo Shimbun Hai (G3). As an outsider early at 3 he was 3rd in the Shinzan Kinen and 2nd in the Kisaragi Sho. 16th in the Satsuki Sho and 8th in the NHK Mile C., he won the 3-win class and Capital S. (L), 2nd in the Kyoto Kimpai at 4, then won the Tokyo Shimbun Hai with a brilliant late run from the back. 9th in the Yasuda Kinen, he was 3rd as 15th choice at 130-1 in the Mile CS.
3773: A fancied 3yo of 2025. Winning his September debut at 2 easily, 2nd in the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. (G2), he won the Kisaragi Sho (G3) at 3 as favorite - a classic contender. 5th as 2nd choice in the Satsuki Sho, 4th in the Derby - no crown, but a presence. Skipping the Kikuka Sho, he was favorite over older horses in the Mainichi Okan, 3rd in a tight finish.
3774: A sprinter who won the 2025 Centaur S. (G2) and Hankyu Hai (G3). Clearing allowances with 2 straight wins at 4, 4th in the Kitakyushu Kinen, 6th in the CBC Sho, he won the Hankyu Hai early at 5 as 7th choice with a fine late run. Unplaced in the Takamatsunomiya Kinen and Sprinters S., he won the Centaur S. in autumn.
3775: Winner of the 2025 Tulip Sho (G2). Unbeaten in 2 from August at 2, 14th in the Hanshin JF, she won the Tulip Sho at 3 as 9th choice, beating Water Gerbera by a nose. 15th in the Oka Sho, 4th in her first dirt race, the Kanto Oaks, and 7th as 17th choice in the Shuka Sho - glimpses of talent.
3776: Winner of the 2025 Nakayama Himba S. (G3) and Niigata Kinen (G3). A leg problem at 2 meant a long rest; starting in summer at 3, she won a maiden at once and was 3rd in the Shion S. At 4 she won 3 and was 2nd twice from 5 through the allowances, then at 5 beat outsider Ho Elite by a head in the Nakayama Himba S. 3rd in the Victoria Mile, closing from last; she won the Niigata Kinen and was 4th in the Tenno Sho (Autumn) - G1 class.
3777: A noted 2025 3yo filly. Winning her 2nd start at 2, she was 3rd in the Artemis S. and 4th in the Hanshin JF. At 3, 9th in the Queen C., she won the Fillies' Revue (G2), but was 10th in the Oka Sho and 16th in the NHK Mile C. Turning to sprints, 5th in the Centaur S.
3778: Winner of the 2025 Yayoi Sho Deep Impact Kinen (G2). Debuting in September at 2 and winning his 2nd start, he was 3rd in the Hopeful S. at 303-1, 17th choice, moving early from the back - a shock. Still doubted as 7th choice in the Yayoi Sho, he won and proved himself. Double-figure finishes in the Satsuki Sho and Derby.
3779: Winner of the 2025 Spring S. (G2). Leading all the way on debut, he was 2nd to later Tenno Sho winner Masquerade Ball in the Ivy S. (L), then 13th as 3rd choice in the Hopeful S. 2nd choice in the Spring S. at 3, he won from up front. Last (18th) in the Satsuki Sho, a leg problem then forced a rest.
3780: Winner of the 2025 Flower C. (G3). In her 2nd start, a 3yo maiden, she won by 5 lengths as 10th choice; still a maiden winner in the Flower C., 5th choice, she broke clear strongly from up front. Then 16th in the Oaks, 10th as 3rd choice in the Queen S., 17th as 15th choice in the Shuka Sho.
3781: A 2025 stayer of note: winner of the Hanshin Daishoten (G2) and 4th as 2nd choice in the Tenno Sho (Spring). Winning his October debut at 2 and the Sumire S. (L) at 3, he was 12th in the Satsuki Sho but 4th as 15th choice in the Derby. After a break, at 4, 2nd in the 3-win class, he won the Hanshin Daishoten by 6 lengths. In the Tenno Sho (Spring) he faded from up front but held 4th. 2nd in the Kyoto Daishoten, 15th in the Japan Cup.
3782: A filly who won the 2025 Aichi Hai (G3) at 4. At 3, 13th in the Tulip Sho and 6th in the Oka Sho, she turned to sprints and reached open class that autumn. 10th in the Turquoise S. and Yodo Tankyori S. (L), she won the Aichi Hai as 10th choice with a razor-sharp finish from the back. 2nd as 12th choice in the Swan S. - full of surprises.
3783: Winner of the 2025 Nikkei Sho (G2). Winning his October debut at 2, he then spent a long, long time in allowances: 2 classes late at 3, the 3-win class late at 4, reaching open class at 5. 3rd at once in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai (G2), he won the Nikkei Sho, holding off Chuck Nate and others. 5th in the Tenno Sho (Spring), leading and holding on.
3784: Unbeaten in 3 to the 2025 Mainichi Hai (G3), from Saturnalia's first crop - his first graded winner. Winning his September debut at 2 and the Junior C. (L) at 3 as favorite, he was 2nd choice in the Mainichi Hai and swept wide from the back to win. 4th choice in the Derby, he found nothing, 14th.
3785: Winner of the 2025 March S. (G3). Debuting at 3, he was 3rd in his first stakes, the Unicorn S. Climbing allowances, he was 6th as March S. favorite at 4; at 5 he won the Aldebaran S. (OP) and then the March S., finishing strongly. 5th in the Sirius S.; late in the year he won the Shiwasu S. (L), a 3rd open win.
3786: Winner of the 2025 Lord Derby CT (G3). Unbeaten in 2, he was 6th in the Yayoi Sho and 11th in the Aoba Sho, then dropped to the mile and won 2 classes into open class. At 4 he won the New Year S. (L), then the Lord Derby CT as hot favorite, finishing well from midfield to win a tight one. 17th in the Yasuda Kinen; trying dirt from summer, 3rd in the Perseus S. (OP).
3787: Winner of the 2025 Churchill Downs C. (G3), formerly the Arlington C., renamed when its partner track changed from Arlington Park to Churchill Downs. 3rd as 9th choice in the Asahi Hai FS late at 2, 3rd in the Kisaragi Sho at 3, he won the Churchill Downs C. as 2nd choice, holding off favorite Arte Veloce. 5th in the NHK Mile C., fading from up front; 3rd in the Swan S., then he won the Rigel S. (L).
3788: Winner of the 2025 NZT (G2). Winning his 2nd start, he lost 2 close calls in a 1-win race, then stepped up as 2nd choice in the NZT and caught favorite Admire Zoom with a sharp late run from the back. 11th as 2nd choice in the NHK Mile C.
3789: Winner of the 2025 Hanshin Himba S. (G2). Noticed early - 2nd in the Artemis S., favorite in the Hanshin JF at 2 - she was 13th in the Oaks at 3. Back in allowances, still in the 3-win class at 4, she won the Hanshin Himba S., holding on from up front in a 3-way photo. 13th in the Victoria Mile, 7th in the QEII Cup.
3790: Winner of the 2025 Fukushima Himba S. (G3). She won 3 straight at 3 from a maiden through the 2-win class, then after a 2nd the 3-win class at 4. Favorite in her first stakes, the Fukushima Himba S., she moved early from midfield and won by 2 lengths. 7th in the Victoria Mile and Ireland T. (G2), then she retired.
3791: True to his name, a long-serving runner who won the Kokura Daishoten (G3) and Milers C. (G2) at 7 in 2025. Starting on dirt and stuck in the 2-win class, he switched to turf in spring at 4, won 2 straight into open class, and ran in mile-to-2000m stakes. He won the December S. (L) late at 5, was 2nd in the Kokura Daishoten at 6, then at 7 won it, and the Milers C. too. In G1s: 13th Yasuda Kinen, 15th Mile CS.
3792: A 2025 3yo dirt star. Winning his 2nd start at 2 and a 1-win race easily at 3, he won the Unicorn S. (G3) as 3rd choice, holding off hot favorite Clay King by 3/4 length. 3rd choice in the Tokyo Derby (JpnI), he was 5th, behind fancied JRA runners Natural Rise and Clay King and 2 local horses.
3793: From Saturnalia's first crop, winner of the 2025 Kyoto Shimbun Hai (G2), giving his sire a graded title. Debuting in November at 2 and winning his 2nd start, 4th in the Kisaragi Sho, he won the Kyoto Shimbun Hai as 5th choice in commanding style from up front. 3rd in the Derby; 2nd in the Kobe Shimbun Hai, but 14th as 3rd choice in the Kikuka Sho.
3794: Winner of the 2025 Niigata Daishoten (G3). Always in good company - 6th in the Hopeful S. at 2, 3rd in the Yayoi Sho and 14th in the Satsuki Sho at 3 - he turned to middle distances: 2nd in the Radio Nikkei Sho, then at 4 the Fukushima Minpo Hai (L) and the Niigata Daishoten as 8th choice, leading all the way. 5th in the Fukushima Kinen.
3795: Winner of the 2025 Aoi S. (G3). Winning her July debut at 2 and a 1-win race at 3, 6th in the Marguerite S. (L), she was 15th choice of 16 in the Aoi S., but surged from midfield and alone broke clear of a blanket finish - a trifecta of 1.89 million yen. 3rd in the Kitakyushu Kinen.
3796: A stayer who won his first stakes, the 2025 Meguro Kinen (G2). Unbeaten in 2, 4th in the Kyoto Shimbun Hai at 3, he won the 2-win class, then was 3rd to Urban Chic in the Kikuka Sho. At 4 he won the Osaka-Hamburg Cup (OP) as favorite, then the Meguro Kinen as favorite after a duel with Ho Elite. 4th in the Kyoto Daishoten; in the Japan Cup, jockey Kawada was unseated just after the start, and the riderless horse crossed the line first - a curious scene.
3797: A filly who won the 2025 Hakodate Sprint S. (G3). Winning just a dirt maiden early, she switched to turf in summer at 3 and quickly climbed to open class. At 4, after near-misses in sprint stakes (4th Silk Road S., 3rd Aichi Hai), she won the Hakodate Sprint S., breaking clear with June Blair and winning the photo by a nose. 16th as 9th choice in the Sprinters S.
3798: First winner of the Fuchu Himba S. (G3), created in 2025 when the Mermaid S. was renamed and moved (the old Fuchu Himba S. became the Ireland T.). Winning her 2nd start, at 3 she was 2nd in the Tulip Sho and 3rd in the Rose S. At 4, 12th in the Nakayama Himba S. and 10th in the Fukushima Himba S., she won the Miyako Oji S. (L), then the Fuchu Himba S. 6th in the QEII Cup.
3799: Winner of the new Shirasagi S. (G3) in 2025, formerly the Yonago S. (L), upgraded and renamed. Passing allowances in autumn at 3, he ran well in listed miles; 3rd in the Lord Derby CT in spring at 4, he won the Shirasagi S., closing sharply from the back and outfighting favorite Cervinia. 5th in the Chukyo Kinen, he was 2025 Summer Mile Series champion.
3800: Winner of the 2025 Radio Nikkei Sho (G3). Slow to win, taking his 5th start, 2nd in a 1-win race, he stepped up in the Radio Nikkei Sho as 4th choice, close behind the top fancies, and edged clear of a scramble by half a length. 3rd to Energico as 13th choice in the Kikuka Sho.
3801: Winner of the 2025 Hakodate Kinen (G3); with 5ths in the Sapporo Kinen and Niigata Kinen, he was 2025 Summer 2000 Series champion. Winning his 2nd start, he won 3 straight classes late at 3 into open class. At 4, in staying stakes, 4th in the Nikkei Shinshun Hai and 5th in the Hanshin Daishoten, then he won the Hakodate Kinen as an outsider.
3802: Winner of the 2025 Kitakyushu Kinen (G3). Debuting at 3, he never won a maiden before they ended, and first won stepping up in a 2-win race in his 9th start. Sprinting since, he won 2 allowances at 4, then the Kitakyushu Kinen as favorite, breaking clear from the back. 15th in the Sprinters S.
3803: Winner of the 2025 Tanabata Sho (G3). He won 3 straight from debut through the 2-win class, then spent about a year placing, before winning the Sunshine S. (3-win) at 5. 2nd choice in his first stakes, the Tanabata Sho, he led throughout and held off favorite Durador by a head - 2 straight.
3804: A filly who won the 2025 Kokura Kinen (G3). At 3, 4th in the Queen C. and Flora S., 16th in the Oaks. Restarting in allowances, she won the 1-win class in summer at 4 and 2-win in spring at 5, then stepped up in the Kokura Kinen as 9th choice and won from a handy spot. 5th in the Challenge C.
3805: Winner of the 2025 Hakodate 2yo S. (G3). First with Hokkaido local racing, he won his 2nd start, then moved to the JRA. 9th choice of 12 in the Hakodate 2yo S., ridden by visiting Australian jockey Rachel King, he led all the way - Fine Needle's 4th straight crop with a graded winner, after A Shin Fencer, Culture Day and Aboukir Bay.
3806: A mare who won her first stakes, the 2025 Sekiya Kinen (G3), at 6. Slowly climbing - 1-win class at 3, 2-win in autumn at 4, 3-win early at 6 - she was 2nd in her first open race, the Fuchu Himba S. (G3), then won the Sekiya Kinen as favorite in record time with an eye-opening finish from the back. 3rd in the Ireland T. (G2).
3807: A dirt horse who won his first stakes, the 2025 Leopard S. (G3). Winning his October debut at 2 and a 1-win race early at 3, he was 3rd in the UAE Derby (G2), 2nd-best Japan-trained. Still a 1-win horse, he won the Leopard S., holding on from up front. 11th in the Japan Dirt Classic (JpnI).
3808: Winner of the 2025 CBC Sho (G3). Starting in dirt sprints, he reached open class by November at 3 with 4 wins from 6. 7th in his first stakes, the Capella S., he won the Keiyo S. (L) at 4 as favorite. Switching to turf, 4th in the Hakodate Sprint S., he won the CBC Sho - his first graded win, on turf. 6th in America's BC Turf Sprint (G1).
3809: A 2025 3yo filly star - no G1, but she won the Chukyo Kinen (G3) that summer. 2nd in the Queen C. at 3, she was 4th to Embroidery in the Oka Sho, 7th in the NHK Mile C., then won the Chukyo Kinen as 5th choice. 10th in the Shuka Sho, 9th back at a mile in the Capital S. (L).
3810: Winner of the 2025 Sapporo Kinen (G2) at his 3rd attempt, having run in it 3 years in a row. Prominent early, 2nd in the Kyoto 2yo S. and Hopeful S. at 2. At 3, 2nd in the Yayoi Sho, he was 7th in the Satsuki Sho, 14th in the Derby and Kikuka Sho, but 2nd in the Sapporo Kinen. Poor at 4, best 3rd in the Andromeda S. (L); at 5, 11th Epsom C., 10th Hakodate Kinen, then he won the Sapporo Kinen as 10th choice.
3811: From the first crop of Irish import Poetic Flare, winner of the 2025 Niigata 2yo S. (G3) - a graded title for his sire at once. Hot favorite on debut, he won by 7 lengths, then as hot favorite in the Niigata 2yo S. sat 2nd, led early in the straight and won by 4.
3812: Winner of the 2025 Hyogo Championship (JpnII). Beaten badly on a turf debut in June at 2, he switched to dirt and won a maiden and 1-win race, then the Shoryu S. (OP) as 2nd choice. Hot favorite in the Hyogo Championship, he broke clear from up front and drew away. 2nd in Mombetsu's Hokkaido Sprint C., 2nd in the Green Channel C. (L).
3813: Dominant on dirt among 2025 3yos, winner of the Haneda Hai (JpnI) and Tokyo Derby (JpnI). Unbeaten in 2, 4th in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun, he improved at 3: the Keihin Hai (JpnII) easily, the Haneda Hai at 1.3-1 easily, and the Tokyo Derby as favorite, leading all the way. A Triple Crown seemed certain in the Japan Dirt Classic, but he couldn't catch front-running Narukami, 2nd.
3814: A filly who won the 2025 Kanto Oaks (JpnII). Debuting at 3, she won her 2nd start and a 1-win race, then the Kanto Oaks at Kawasaki as 1.6-1 favorite, moving early from a handy spot and drawing away by 5 lengths. Hot favorite in Funabashi's Marine C., she was 2nd to front-running Proud Frere.
3815: A mare who won the 2025 Sparking Lady C. (JpnIII). Unbeaten in 2 at 3, 2nd choice in the Kanto Oaks, she faded from the lead to 7th. After allowances, she returned to stakes at 5: 5th in the Queen Sho, won the local Shirasagi Sho, then the Sparking Lady C., leading early and holding on. 4th in the Ladies' Prelude.
3816: Winner of Morioka's Mercury C. (JpnIII) in 2025. Debuting in July at 2, he struggled, finally winning a maiden in his 10th start in spring at 3. He took about a year to reach open class, then was 2nd in the Sleipnir S. (OP) at 4, and won the Mercury C. as favorite, flying from the back to catch leader Crown Pride.
3817: He won his first stakes, Morioka's Cluster C. (JpnIII), at 6 in 2025. Winning 3 straight from a maiden through the 2-win class at 3, the 3-win class in spring at 4, he won the Fujimori S. (OP), Ritto S. (L), Nagatsuki S. (OP) and Minazuki S. (OP), then the Cluster C. as favorite, leading throughout and holding off outsider Candid Drive. 3rd in the Tokyo Hai and JBC Sprint.
3818: Winner of 3 straight dirt stakes in 2025: Hokkaido Sprint C. (JpnIII), Summer Champion (JpnIII) and Tokyo Hai (JpnII). In spring at 3 he won a 1-win race and the Violet S. (OP), 4th in the Hyogo Championship. That summer he won at Mombetsu, then at Saga caught favorite Emperor Wakea, then at Oi broke clear from a handy spot. 2nd to T O Elvis in the JRA's Capella S. (G3).
3819: Winner of the 2025 Bluebird C. (JpnIII). Beaten badly in 2 turf races, he won a dirt maiden by a wide margin and a 1-win race by 5 lengths. Back on turf, 12th in the Junior C. (L), he returned to dirt and won the Bluebird C. as 2nd choice. A fracture then sidelined him.
3820: A steady dirt runner who finally won a stakes, the Saga Kinen (JpnIII), at 7. Through the 3-win class in spring at 4, he hit a wall in open class, then blossomed at 5, winning the Aldebaran S. (OP), 3rd in the Dioright Kinen, 2nd in the Hakusan Daishoten. At 7 he led all the way in the Saga Kinen, then was 5th to Meisho Hario in the Kawasaki Kinen (JpnI).
3821: A noted 2025 3yo on dirt, winner of the Kumotori Sho (JpnIII). Winning his August debut at 2 as hot favorite and a 1-win race with a razor-sharp finish, at 3 he won the Kumotori Sho, the Triple Crown trial - unbeaten in 3. 2nd choice in the Haneda Hai, he faded from up front to 3rd; 6th as 6th choice in the Leopard S.
3822: Winner of the 2025 Kakitsubata Kinen (JpnIII). Winning his 2nd start, he steadily climbed the classes by autumn at 4, then won his first open race, the Shimotsuki S. (OP), as favorite. At 5, 2nd in the Negishi S. (G3), he won the Kakitsubata Kinen as favorite, then was 4th to Shamal in the Kashiwa Kinen and 5th in the Musashino S.
3823: Raced boldly abroad at 3 in 2025: 2nd in the UAE's Mahab Al Shimaal (G3) and 4th in America's BC Sprint (G1). On dirt from debut, he won his 4th start and a 1-win race, then the turf Chukyo 2yo S. (OP) as favorite. At 3, 2nd in the Mahab Al Shimaal, 6th in the Dubai Golden Shaheen, then 4th in the BC Sprint - a Japan-trained force.
3824: He went to the UAE in 2025 and won the UAE Derby (G2). Winning his 4th start from October at 2, he ran once in open class (4th Hyacinth S.) then went abroad, winning a tight UAE Derby over fellow Japanese Don in the Mood and others. In the Kentucky Derby he was 19th; back home, 9th in the Japan Dirt Classic and 14th in the Musashino S.
3825: He went to France at 3 in 2025 and won the Prix Guillaume d'Ornano (G2). Winning his November debut at 2, 3rd in the Yayoi Sho at 3, he was 8th to Museum Mile in the Satsuki Sho, then headed for France aiming at the Arc. He won his first race there, the d'Ornano; in the Arc, with fellow Japanese Croix du Nord and Byzantine Dream, he was 16th.
3826: First winner of the Chukyo 2yo S. (G3), created in 2025 when the Kokura 2yo S. was renamed and moved. He won his debut from midfield with a sharp finish, then the Chukyo 2yo S. as 6th choice, closing from the back to catch favorite Star Anise. 8th as 3rd choice in the Daily Hai 2yo S.
3827: A mare who won her first stakes, the Keisei Hai AH (G3), at 7 in 2025. Always at a mile to 2000m, she reached the 2-win class at 3, then went 23 races without winning until the 3-win class in spring at 7. Unplaced in open races, she produced the run of her life as 13th choice in the Keisei Hai AH; with 11th choice Drop of Light 2nd, even the quinella-place paid a fortune.
3828: Debuting in 2025, he won the Sapporo 2yo S. (G3). Sold for 210 million yen (pre-tax) as a foal at the Select Sale, he lived up to it. A 1.3-1 favorite on debut, he won by 7 lengths from up front; favorite in the Sapporo 2yo S., he flew from the back as if the rest were standing still and caught gritty leader Zine King.
3829: A filly who won the 2025 Shion S. (G2). Winning a maiden in spring at 3, 3rd in the Sweet Pea S. (L) still a 1-win horse, she was 14th choice at 188-1 in the Oaks, yet held 8th, best of the early pace. She won the Shion S. as 7th choice, leading all the way, but was 11th in the Shuka Sho and 14th in the QEII Cup.
3830: Winner of the 2025 Challenge C. (G3). Racing at longer trips, he climbed to the 3-win class by late at 3. In open class at 4 he was 9th in the Tokyo Shimbun Hai, 3rd in the Osakajo S. (L), 6th in the Niigata Daishoten, then won the Challenge C., closing from the back with the fastest finish to catch favorite Grand Vinos.
3831: A dirt stakes horse who won the Sirius S. (G3) and Urawa Kinen (JpnII) at 6 in 2025. Through the 2-win class in summer at 3 and 3-win in autumn at 4, he struggled in open class (6th Miyako S., 9th Antares S.), winning the Canopus S. (OP) in autumn at 5. At 6, 4th in the Procyon S., 5th in the March S., he won the Sirius S. and Urawa Kinen back to back.
3832: Winner of the 2025 Kyoto Daishoten (G2). At 3, unplaced in the Satsuki Sho and Derby, he was 5th in the Kikuka Sho. At 5, 5th in the Kinko Sho, 14th in the Tenno Sho (Spring). From 6 in middle-distance stakes he placed often (2nd Challenge C., 3rd Kokura Kinen), then at 7 won the Kyoto Daishoten, catching gritty leader Sunrise Earth by half a length.
3833: Debuting in 2025, he won the Saudi Arabia Royal C. (G3), from Mozu Ascot's 2nd crop - a graded winner in 2 straight crops after Faust Lasen. On debut, under visiting jockey Rachel King, he won easily from midfield. In the Saudi Arabia Royal C. he missed the break, then from last in the straight produced a finish from another dimension, sweeping past them all.
3834: First winner of the Ireland T. (G2), created in 2025 from the old Fuchu Himba S. (G2). At 3 she was 11th in the Oaks but 4th as 13th choice in the Shuka Sho. At 4, still in the 3-win class, she was 3rd in the Hanshin Himba S. and in the new Fuchu Himba S. (G3, inheriting the old Mermaid S. conditions), then won the Ireland T. with a fine late run from midfield. 16th in the Mile CS, fading in the straight.
3835: A filly who won the 2025 Artemis S. (G3). 2nd choice on debut, she won a tight finish from midfield; 2nd choice again in the Artemis S., she raced forward, broke clear early and won easily. A Hanshin JF fancy, she was then found to have tendon trouble and retired to breed.
3836: A filly who debuted in 2025 and won the Fantasy S. (G3), Saturnalia's first graded winner from his 2nd crop, after Shohei and Fandom a year earlier. She beat Albanne by half a length in a duel on debut, was 3rd in the Niigata 2yo S. (G3), then won another tight one in the Fantasy S. A fracture then forced a rest.
3837: Winner of the 2025 Keio Hai 2yo S. (G2), the first graded winner from the 3rd crop of imported sire Bricks and Mortar, hailed as "the second Sunday Silence." Beaten twice at 1200m, he won at 1400m, a better trip, then was 2nd in the Momiji S. (OP). In the 1400m Keio Hai 2yo S., hot 1.8-1 favorite, he sat 2nd and drew 3 lengths clear. In the Asahi Hai FS he held on from up front for 2nd - a presence for the classics.
3838: A gelding who won the Argentine Republic Hai (G2) at 7 in 2025 - his first stakes start and first stakes win. Debuting at 3, he won his 3rd start, then struggled: 1-win class in autumn at 4, 2-win in summer at 5, 3-win in spring at 7 - open class at last in his 33rd start. After the Sapporo Nikkei Sho (L) he won the Tancho S. (OP), then led all the way in the Argentine Republic Hai as 9th choice.
3839: A noted 2025 3yo on dirt who beat spring dual classic winner Natural Rise decisively in the Japan Dirt Classic (JpnI) - best of his crop. Winning his debut by a huge margin, beaten in a 1-win race, he won 3 straight to Morioka's Kozukata Sho (JpnII), then led all the way in the Japan Dirt Classic, 3 lengths clear of Natural Rise and 9 more to 3rd. Favorite over older horses in the Champions C., he found nothing, 13th; 6th in the Tokyo Daishoten.
3840: Winner of the 2025 Hakusan Daishoten (JpnIII), the first Japanese graded winner for US sire Khozan. Almost always top 2 from 2, he reached the 3-win class in spring at 4 in his 8th start, then won the BSN Sho (L) in his 2nd open race. 3rd choice in his first stakes, the Hakusan Daishoten, he led as he likes and won by a length.
3841: A Funabashi filly who beat the JRA runners in the 2025 Marine C. (JpnIII). Unbeaten in 2, she won Southern Kanto stakes like the Tokyo 2yo Yushun Himba and Jungfrau Sho by spring at 3. 3rd in June's Kanto Oaks (JpnII); in the Marine C. she led all the way, leaving fancied Memoria Cafe and others behind. 14th in the JBC Ladies' Classic (JpnI).
3842: A mare who switched from turf to dirt at 5 in 2025 and won the Ladies' Prelude (JpnII). Racing mainly at a mile on turf, she reached the 3-win class in autumn at 4; 2nd in her first stakes, the Turquoise S., then 4th in the Nakayama Himba S. and Hanshin Himba S. Switching to dirt in autumn at 5, she won the Ladies' Prelude at once. 9th as 3rd choice in the JBC Ladies' Classic.
3843: Debuting in Hokkaido in 2025, she won the Edelweiss Sho (JpnIII). Leading all the way on debut, she won the Lily C. by 5 lengths and Fleur C. by 4, then as 1.3-1 favorite in the Edelweiss Sho, sat 2nd, led early and beat JRA runners like Tokai Ma Cherie by 1.5 lengths - unbeaten in 4.
3844: Winner of the 2025 Oval Sprint (JpnIII). Winning his debut in February at 3, after a 3rd he won 3 straight classes, then the Autumn Leaf S. (OP) and was 3rd in his first stakes, the Negishi S. Always top 5 after, he won the Oval Sprint at 5 as favorite, then 4th in the Musashino S.
3845: He debuted with the JRA, moved to Oi, and won the JBC Sprint (JpnI) at 6 in 2025. With the JRA he passed the 3-win class in summer at 4, then went 0 for 10 in open races; after a 15th in the Minazuki S. (OP) at 6 he moved to Oi. He won 2 local stakes at once, then led all the way in the JBC Sprint, beating fancied JRA runners - his first graded win a JpnI.
3846: A filly who won the 2025 JBC 2yo Yushun (JpnIII). Winning her October debut as 8th choice, she was 6th choice in the JBC 2yo Yushun but closed well from midfield to catch gritty leader Fleur d'Or by a neck. In the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun (JpnI), though the only stakes winner in the field, she was 4th choice; closing sharply from midfield, she was 2nd, a neck behind Pyromancer.
3847: Winner of the 2025 Musashino S. (G3). Winning his 3rd start, he won 4 straight: a 1-win race, the Hyacinth S. (L) and Fukuryu S. (OP), then ran in America's Kentucky Derby, 12th. In autumn, 3rd in the Japan Dirt Classic, he won the Musashino S. 6th choice in the Champions C., close behind the fancies, he was 15th.
3848: Winner of the 2025 Daily Hai 2yo S. (G2). Favorite on debut with Ryusei Sakai, he swept past with a finish from another dimension. Favorite again in the Daily Hai 2yo S. with Sakai, he closed from the back and beat Cavalerizzo by a head in a 2yo course record 1:33.1. Favorite in the Asahi Hai FS, he was 3rd.
3849: A filly who won the 2025 Fukushima Kinen (G3). Winning her 2nd start, 5th in the Fairy S. early at 3, she struggled in allowances, then won 3 classes in a row at 4 into open class. 2nd choice in the Fukushima Kinen, she sat 2nd, led early and held them off.
3850: Winner of the 2025 Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. (G2). 2nd on debut, closing too late, he won a maiden at 1.1-1, then as 3rd choice in the Tokyo Sports Hai 2yo S. moved early from midfield to lead and held off Zoroastro by a head - 2 straight, a contender in his crop.
3851: Winner of the 2025 Kyoto 2yo S. (G3), from Saturnalia's 2nd crop; with Festival Hill, his sire had graded winners in 2 straight crops. 5th choice on debut, he sat 2nd and held off Timeless Flare and others. 9th choice in the Kyoto 2yo S., he waited at the back and swept wide to win.
3852: A long-serving sprinter who won his first stakes, the Keihan Hai (G3), at 6 in 2025. Starting at a mile on turf and often missing, he switched to dirt late at 3, quickly reached the 3-win class and ran in open sprints, but rarely won. Back on turf in spring at 6, he won the Seikan S. (OP); 7th in the Keeneland C., he won the Keihan Hai as 7th choice with a sharp late run.
3853: A filly who won the 2025 Hyogo Junior GP (JpnII). Debuting early in June at 2, she won her 2nd start, 7th in the Hakodate 2yo S. (G3). Switching to dirt, she was 2nd in Mombetsu's Edelweiss Sho, then at Sonoda as 3rd choice waited at the back, moved early to join the leaders, and won with a powerful finish.
3854: Winner of the 2025 Stayers S. (G2), only the 2nd filly or mare to win it, the first since Sheenan Lady in 1986, 39 years earlier. At 3, 2nd in the Flower C., she was 10th in both the Oaks and Shuka Sho. At 4 she won the 3-win class, then placed against males in staying stakes (2nd Meguro Kinen, 5th All Comers), and won the Stayers S. as 2nd choice from up front.
3855: A dirt sprinter who won the 2025 Capella S. (G3). Debuting in September at 2, he won his 2nd start, then 3 straight classes at 3, all as favorite, the 3-win class by 4 lengths. Favorite in his first open race, the Capella S., he unleashed a finish of his own from midfield and won a sprint by 5 lengths.
3856: Winner of the 2025 Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun (JpnI). Debuting in October at 2, he led nearly all the way to win easily, then the Mochinoki Sho (1-win) from a handy spot by half a length. 2nd choice in the Zen-Nihon 2yo Yushun, he sat 2nd, outfought favorite Best Green in the straight, and held off Tamamo Freesia by a neck.
3857: From the first crop of World Premiere, winner of the Kikuka Sho and Tenno Sho (Spring). On debut, in pouring rain under Kohei Matsuyama, he won by 3 lengths. 7th choice in the Hopeful S. (G1), he swung wide from midfield, losing ground, yet produced an eye-opening finish - 2 straight. Not champion 2yo, but a big step toward the classics. He is named Lovcen after a mountain in Montenegro, in the Balkans.
3858: Debuting on dirt in February at 3, he won his 2nd start, then climbed steadily to open class in spring at 4. That autumn he won the Brazil C. (L) as 9th choice, then the Nagoya Daishoten (JpnIII), beating strong rivals Kazu Tanger and Derma Sotogake - a graded winner.
3859: Named Cavalerizzo, Italian for horseman. Winning his summer debut at Chukyo by 5 lengths, he emerged as a classic hope; in the Daily Hai 2yo S. (G2) he lost a duel with highly rated Admire Quads by a head. Meeting Admire Quads again in the Asahi Hai FS (G1), driven by Italy's Cristian Demuro, he swept past front-running Diamond Knot in the straight to win, with Admire Quads 3rd - top of his crop.
